questions.question: Where is the MBMS RAB Establishment Indication procedure described, and what makes the RNC initiate it?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS RAB Establishment Indication procedure is described in TS 25.346 clause 8.2.14 and TS 25.413 clause 8.42.2. The RNC initiates it when it has not yet established the MBMS RAB for a particular MBMS/Multicast service and either decides to establish the Iu bearer after a UE linking (via Iu or Iur) or channel type reconfiguration in another RNC, or is informed that a given UE joined that Multicast Service.

questions.question: When the RNC asks the core network to release an MBMS RAB, what should the CN release and what must it keep, and which message tells the RNC the release failed?
questions.reference_answer: On reception of the MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message, the CN should initiate the release of all MBMS resources related to the Iu connection, but without releasing the Iu signalling connection. The MBMS RAB RELEASE FAILURE message tells the RNC that the release failed, informing it of the reason with an appropriate cause value if the CN node is not capable of correctly processing the request.

questions.question: The MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message appears in both M2AP and M3AP. Which node sends it in each case, and what condition triggers it?
questions.reference_answer: In M2AP (TS 36.443), the eNB sends the MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message to the MCE when it is not capable of correctly processing the request, e.g. the MBMS resources could not be established at all in any cell. In M3AP (TS 36.444), the MCE sends the MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message to the MME, either when the E-UTRAN cannot accommodate the requested configuration for any involved MBSFN area (MBSFN transmission) or cell (SC-PTM), or when the MBMS Cell List IE in the MBMS SESSION START REQUEST includes no cell controlled by an eNB with which the MCE has a connection.

questions.question: Which node sends the RADIO LINK RESTORE INDICATION over NBAP and which over RNSAP, and what algorithm decides when it is sent?
questions.reference_answer: Over NBAP (TS 25.433), the Node B sends the RADIO LINK RESTORE INDICATION message to the CRNC. Over RNSAP (TS 25.423), the DRNC sends it to the SRNC. In both cases it is sent as indicated by the UL (Uu) synchronisation detection algorithm defined in TS 25.214 and TS 25.224, which uses the minimum value of the parameter N_INSYNC_IND configured in the cells supporting the radio links of the RL Set.

questions.question: In which clause is the RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message defined, and what must the NG-RAN node do when it carries a Time to Wait IE?
questions.reference_answer: The RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.7.2.3. When the message carries a Time to Wait IE, the NG-RAN node shall wait at least for the indicated time before reinitiating the RAN Configuration Update procedure towards the same AMF.

questions.question: Which clause specifies what the NG-RAN node may do when it receives neither a RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE nor a RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.7.2.4 (Abnormal Conditions) specifies that if the NG-RAN node, after initiating the RAN Configuration Update procedure, receives neither a RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE nor a RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message, it may reinitiate a further RAN Configuration Update procedure towards the same AMF, provided the content of the new RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE message is identical to the content of the previously unacknowledged one.

questions.question: Tell me where the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT FAILURE INDICATION message is defined, and which node sends it to which peer in each.
questions.reference_answer: The DEDICATED MEASUREMENT FAILURE INDICATION message is defined in TS 25.423 clause 8.3.14.2, where it is sent from the DRNC to the SRNC, and in TS 25.433 clause 8.3.11.2, where it is sent from the Node B to the CRNC (over the Communication Control Port assigned to the Node B Communication Context). In both cases it informs the peer that a previously requested (dedicated) measurement can no longer be reported because it has been locally terminated.

questions.question: Which specification defines the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT INITIATION FAILURE message, and which IE must it echo from the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST?
questions.reference_answer: The DEDICATED MEASUREMENT INITIATION FAILURE message is defined in TS 25.423 clause 8.3.11.3. It must echo the same Measurement ID IE that was used in the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST message, and must include the Cause IE set to an appropriate value.

questions.question: What is the Nnef_ECSAddress_Create service operation used for, which inputs are mandatory, and which are optional?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Create is used for the NF consumer to request creation of ECS Address Configuration Information. The only mandatory (Required) input is ECS Address Configuration Information; the optional inputs are AF-service-identifier, AF Transaction Id, DNN, and S-NSSAI.

questions.question: Where is the Nnef_ECSAddress_Create service operation described, and which NF invokes it to provide ECS Address Configuration Information via the NEF in the VPLMN?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Create is described in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.2 and used (invoked) in TS 23.548 clause 6.5.2.6.2. The AF invokes the Nnef_ECSAddress_Create/Update/Delete service operation to provide ECS Address Configuration Information to the NEF in the VPLMN.

questions.question: What does Nnef_ECSAddress_Notify carry to the NF consumer, and which inputs are required?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Notify carries subscribed event information — e.g. updated ECS Address Configuration Information — to the NF Consumer; per TS 29.591 it enables the NEF to notify the NF service consumer about subscribed ECS Address Configuration Information. Its required inputs are Event ID, Notification Correlation ID, and ECS Address Configuration Information.

questions.question: Which clause defines the Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe service operation, and what optional input narrows the subscription?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe is defined in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.5. The optional input that narrows the subscription is a list of (DNN, S-NSSAI).

questions.question: Tell me where the V-SMF supporting HR-SBO is described as using the Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe service operation towards the NEF in the VPLMN.
questions.reference_answer: This is described in TS 23.548 clause 6.5.2.6.3, where the SMF (V-SMF supporting HR-SBO) subscribes to ECS Address Configuration Information Change Notification from the NEF in the VPLMN by sending the Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe message, optionally indicating that the current status shall be notified immediately and/or the (list of) DNN and/or S-NSSAI it subscribes for.

questions.question: In which clauses are the Nausf_SoRProtection and Nausf_UPUProtection services described, and which NF provides them?
questions.reference_answer: Nausf_SoRProtection is described in TS 29.509 clause 6.2 and TS 23.502 clause 5.2.10.3; Nausf_UPUProtection is described in TS 29.509 clause 6.3 and TS 23.502 clause 5.2.10.4. Both services are provided by the AUSF: Nausf_SoRProtection protects Steering of Roaming information for the requester NF, and Nausf_UPUProtection protects the UE Parameters Update for the requester NF.

questions.question: Which specifications define the MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message is defined in TS 36.443 (M2AP), where it is sent by the eNB to the MCE, and in TS 36.444 (M3AP), where it is sent by the MCE to the MME.

questions.question: In which specifications is the RADIO LINK RESTORE INDICATION message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The RADIO LINK RESTORE INDICATION message is defined in TS 25.433 (NBAP), where it is sent by the Node B to the CRNC, and in TS 25.423 (RNSAP), where it is sent by the DRNC to the SRNC.

questions.question: Tell me where the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT FAILURE INDICATION message is defined, and which node sends it in each.
questions.reference_answer: The DEDICATED MEASUREMENT FAILURE INDICATION message is defined in TS 25.433 clause 8.3.11.2, where it is sent by the Node B to the CRNC, and in TS 25.423 clause 8.3.14.2, where it is sent by the DRNC to the SRNC.

questions.question: Where is the MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message is defined in TS 25.413 clause 8.43.2 and TS 25.346 clause 8.2.15. In both, it is the RNC that sends the MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message towards/to the CN.

questions.question: In which specifications is the MBMS RAB ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS RAB ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message is defined in TS 25.346 clause 8.2.14 and TS 25.413 clause 8.42.2. In both, it is the RNC that sends the MBMS RAB ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message to the CN.

questions.question: Tell me where the RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message is defined, and which node sends it.
questions.reference_answer: The RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.7.2.3. It is sent by the AMF (to the NG-RAN node) when the AMF cannot accept the update.

questions.question: Which specification defines the RAN PAGING REQUEST message, and which node sends it?
questions.reference_answer: The RAN PAGING REQUEST message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.3.14.2. It is sent by the AMF to the NG-RAN node.

questions.question: In which specification is the MBMS RAB RELEASE FAILURE message defined, and in which direction is it sent?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS RAB RELEASE FAILURE message is defined in TS 25.413 clause 9.1.76. It is sent in the direction CN → RNC, as an unsuccessful response to the MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message.

questions.question: Which specification defines the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT INITIATION FAILURE message, and which node sends it?
questions.reference_answer: The DEDICATED MEASUREMENT INITIATION FAILURE message is defined in TS 25.423 clause 8.3.11.3. It is sent by the DRNC (to the SRNC), when the requested measurement cannot be initiated for one of the RL/RLS.

questions.question: Where is the Nnef_ECSAddress_Create service operation described, and which NF invokes it?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Create is described in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.2. It is invoked by the AF, which invokes the Nnef_ECSAddress_Create/Update/Delete service operation to provide ECS Address Configuration Information to the NEF.

questions.question: Tell me where the Nnef_ECSAddress_Notify service operation is described, and which NF invokes it.
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Notify is described in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.7 and in TS 29.591 clause 4.5.2.4.1. It is invoked by the NEF, which notifies subscribed event information such as updated ECS Address Configuration Information to the NF service consumer.

questions.question: In which specifications is the Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe service operation described, and which NF invokes it?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe is described in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.5 and in TS 29.591 clause 4.5.2.1. It is invoked by an NF service consumer to explicitly subscribe to notification of changes of ECS Address Configuration Information.

questions.question: Which NF invokes Nnef_ECSAddress_Unsubscribe, and what does the operation do?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Unsubscribe is invoked by an NF service consumer. It is used by the NF service consumer to explicitly unsubscribe from the notification of ECS Address Configuration Information.

questions.question: Which specifications list the Nausf_UEAuthentication, Nausf_SoRProtection and Nausf_UPUProtection services together, and which NF offers them?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.509 clause 5.1 and TS 23.501 clause 7.2.7 list Nausf_UEAuthentication, Nausf_SoRProtection and Nausf_UPUProtection together; both specify that these services are offered by the AUSF (to NF service consumers such as the AMF).

questions.question: Where is the MBMS SESSION START REQUEST message defined for M2AP, and what is its successful outcome message?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS SESSION START REQUEST message is defined for M2AP in TS 36.443 clause 8.1 (Table 2: Class 1 procedures, MBMS Session Start elementary procedure). Its successful outcome message is MBMS SESSION START RESPONSE.

questions.question: How does the MBMS RAB Release procedure over Iu differ between what the RNC requests and what the CN is expected to release?
questions.reference_answer: The RNC requests release via the MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message sent to the CN, and at reception the CN should initiate release of all MBMS resources related to the Iu connection without releasing the Iu signalling connection. The RNC itself, on reception of MBMS RAB RELEASE, initiates release of the related MBMS RAB resources.

questions.question: Which specifications define the MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message, and which node is informed by it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message is defined in TS 36.443 clause 8.2.3 (M2AP), where it informs the MCE if the eNB cannot correctly process the request, and in TS 36.444 clause 8.2.3 (M3AP), where it informs the MME if the MCE cannot accommodate the requested configuration or the MBMS Cell List includes no cell controlled by the eNB connected to the MCE.

questions.question: Where is the RADIO LINK RESTORE INDICATION message defined, and which node sends it to which peer in each?
questions.reference_answer: The RADIO LINK RESTORE INDICATION message is defined in TS 25.433 clause 8.3.13.2 (NBAP), where the Node B sends it to the CRNC, and in TS 25.423 clause 8.3.10.2 (RNSAP), where the DRNC sends it to the SRNC.

questions.question: Which specifications define the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT FAILURE INDICATION message on the Iub and Iur interfaces, and which node reports it to whom in each?
questions.reference_answer: The DEDICATED MEASUREMENT FAILURE INDICATION message is defined for the Iub interface in TS 25.433 clause 8.3.11.2, where the Node B sends it to the CRNC, and for the Iur interface in TS 25.423 clause 8.3.14.2, where the DRNC sends it to the SRNC. In both cases it informs the receiving node that a previously requested measurement can no longer be reported because it has been locally terminated.

questions.question: How does the Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe operation relate to Nnef_ECSAddress_Notify, and which NF plays which role in each?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe is used by an NF consumer to explicitly subscribe to notification of changes of ECS Address Configuration Information, while Nnef_ECSAddress_Notify is used by the NEF to provide that subscribed event information (e.g. updated ECS Address Configuration Information) back to the NF consumer. Thus the NF consumer is the requester/subscriber and the NEF is the provider/notifier.

questions.question: Tell me where the Nnef_ECSAddress_Create and Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe service operations are described for provisioning ECS Address Configuration Information in the VPLMN.
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Create (used to provision ECS Address Configuration Information from the AF via NEF in the VPLMN to the UDR) is described in TS 23.548 clause 6.5.2.6.2, and Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe (used by the SMF in the VPLMN to subscribe to ECS Address Configuration Information Change Notification from the NEF) is described in TS 23.548 clause 6.5.2.6.3.

questions.question: In which clauses are the RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message and the abnormal condition where no RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE arrives defined, and what does the NG-RAN node do in each case?
questions.reference_answer: The RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.7.2.3 (Unsuccessful Operation): if the AMF cannot accept the update it responds with this message and an appropriate cause value. The abnormal condition of receiving neither RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE nor RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE is defined in clause 8.7.2.4: the NG-RAN node may reinitiate the RAN Configuration Update procedure toward the same AMF, provided the new message content is identical to the previously unacknowledged one.

questions.question: Which node initiates the MBMS RAB Establishment Indication and which initiates the MBMS RAB Release Request, and do they run over the same interface?
questions.reference_answer: Both are initiated by the RNC toward the CN: MBMS RAB Establishment Indication uses the MBMS RAB ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message, and MBMS RAB Release Request uses the MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message. Yes, both run over the same interface, the Iu (Iu signalling connection).

questions.question: For the MBMS RAB Release procedure, which message reports success and which reports failure, and which node sends each?
questions.reference_answer: Success is reported by the RNC sending the MBMS RAB RELEASE REQUEST message to the CN (successful operation). Failure is reported by the CN sending the MBMS RAB RELEASE FAILURE message to the RNC, informing it of the reason for the unsuccessful operation with an appropriate cause value.

questions.question: When a context setup toward the RAN fails, which specifications define the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message, and which node reports the failure in each?
questions.reference_answer: The INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.3.1.3/8.3.1.4 (NGAP), reported by the NG-RAN node when it cannot establish an NG UE context, and in TS 36.413 clause 8.3.1.3 (S1AP), reported by the eNB when it cannot establish an S1 UE context or even one non-GBR bearer.

questions.question: Where is the ACCESS AND MOBILITY INDICATION message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The ACCESS AND MOBILITY INDICATION message is defined in TS 38.423 clause 8.4.12.2 (Xn), sent by NG-RAN node1 to NG-RAN node2; in TS 38.473 clause 8.11.1.2 (F1), sent from the gNB-CU to the gNB-DU; and in TS 36.423 clause 8.3.16.2 (X2), sent by the eNB to the en-gNB or by eNB1 to eNB2.

questions.question: After a public warning system restarts, which specifications define the PWS RESTART INDICATION message and which node raises it?
questions.reference_answer: The PWS RESTART INDICATION message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.9.3.2 (NGAP), sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF, and in TS 36.413 clause 8.12.3.2 (S1AP), sent by the eNB to the MME. The message definition also appears in ts_29_168_4.3.4.2.7 (PWS RESTART INDICATION; Direction: MME, PWS-IWF → CBC).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The PWS RESTART INDICATION message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.9.3.2 (NGAP), sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF, and in TS 36.413 clause 8.12.3.2 (S1AP), sent by the eNB to the MME.

questions.question: Tell me where the HANDOVER FROM UTRAN FAILURE message is defined, and which node sends it in each.
questions.reference_answer: The HANDOVER FROM UTRAN FAILURE message is defined in TS 43.130 clause 7.2.6.3.2, sent by the MS/UE to the SRNS, and in TS 25.331 clauses 8.3.7.8/8.3.7.8a, sent by the UE (e.g. in response to an unsupported HANDOVER FROM UTRAN COMMAND configuration or when received while in CELL_FACH).

questions.question: When an information exchange between RAN nodes cannot proceed, which specifications define the INFORMATION EXCHANGE FAILURE INDICATION message and who sends it?
questions.reference_answer: The INFORMATION EXCHANGE FAILURE INDICATION message is defined in TS 25.453 clause 8.6.2, sent from the SAS to the RNC; in TS 25.423 clause 8.5.9.2, sent from RNC2 to RNC1; and in TS 25.433 clause 8.2.29.2, sent from the Node B to the CRNC.

questions.question: In which specifications is the INFORMATION EXCHANGE TERMINATION REQUEST message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The INFORMATION EXCHANGE TERMINATION REQUEST message is defined in TS 25.433 clause 8.2.28.2, sent from the CRNC to the Node B; in TS 25.453 clause 8.5.2, sent to the SAS; and in TS 25.423 clause 8.5.8.2, sent from RNC1 to RNC2.

questions.question: Which specifications define the RESOURCE STATUS RESPONSE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The RESOURCE STATUS RESPONSE message is defined in TS 38.473 clause 8.2.10.4 (F1, sent by gNB-DU to gNB-CU), TS 37.483 clause 8.2.9.2/8.2.9.4 (E1, sent by gNB-CU-UP to gNB-CU-CP), TS 38.423 clause 8.4.10.4 (Xn, sent by NG-RAN node2 to NG-RAN node1), and TS 36.423 clause 8.3.7.2 (X2, sent by eNB2 to eNB1).

questions.question: If the warning system itself fails rather than restarts, which specifications define the PWS FAILURE INDICATION message and which node emits it?
questions.reference_answer: The PWS FAILURE INDICATION message is defined in TS 38.413 clause 8.9.4.2 (NGAP), sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF; TS 36.413 clause 8.12.4.2 (S1AP), sent by the eNB to the MME; and TS 29.168 clause 4.3.3F.2/4.3.4.2.8 (SBc-AP), sent by the MME or PWS-IWF to the CBC.

questions.question: For transferring information directly between core and RAN nodes, which specifications define the DIRECT INFORMATION TRANSFER message and which node initiates it?
questions.reference_answer: DIRECT INFORMATION TRANSFER (and the eNB-specific variant) is defined in TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.14 (eNB-initiated, eNB to MME), TS 25.413 clause 8.34.2.1/8.34.2.2 (RNSAP-style Iu, initiated either from the RNC to the CN or from the CN to the RNC), and TS 23.924 clause 5.6.3.1.6 (initiated from the RNC to the CN, or from the CN to the RNC).

questions.question: Which specifications describe the BSSMAP HANDOVER REQUEST message, covering both the PS handover request procedure on the Gb interface and the case where the message is carried inside the user data field of a Connection Request?
questions.reference_answer: The BSSMAP HANDOVER REQUEST message, including the PS handover request procedure on the Gb interface (TS 48.018 clause 8a.5, where the target BSS matches its CS Indication IE against the BSSMAP HANDOVER REQUEST message) and the case where it is carried inside the user data field of a Connection Request message, is described in TS 48.006 clause 9.1.2.

questions.question: The MEASUREMENT REQUEST message is used by the LMF towards NG-RAN nodes over NRPPa, and a MEASUREMENT RESPONSE is returned. In which clauses are these two NRPPa messages described?
questions.reference_answer: Both messages are described in TS 38.455 clause 8.5.1.2 (Successful Operation): the LMF sends MEASUREMENT REQUEST to the NG-RAN node, and the NG-RAN node returns MEASUREMENT RESPONSE.

questions.question: Where does the corpus describe the NGAP HANDOVER REQUEST message carrying the UE's 5G security capabilities to the target gNB, and which security clauses reference it in the context of N2 handover and NAS algorithm selection?
questions.reference_answer: The corpus describes the NGAP HANDOVER REQUEST message carrying the UE's 5G security capabilities to the target gNB in TS 33.501 clause 6.7.3.2 (N2-handover) and clause 6.7.3.6 (algorithm negotiation for unauthenticated UEs in LSM). The security clauses that reference it in the context of N2 handover and NAS algorithm selection are TS 33.501 clause 6.9.4.4 (AS key re-keying), clause 6.9.2.3.3 (N2-Handover, NASC/NH/NCC handling), and TS 33.512 clause 4.2.2.4.2 (NAS protection algorithm selection in AMF change test case).

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the BSSMAP HANDOVER FAILURE message?
questions.reference_answer: The BSSMAP HANDOVER FAILURE message is defined/described in TS 48.008 clause 3.1.5.3.2 (Handover Failure), clause 3.1.5a.4 (Inter System Handover Failure), and clause 3.1.5c.2.1 (Internal Handover failure), plus TS 48.006 clause 9.1.2 which describes it being carried in the user data field of the SCCP Connection Refused message.

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the ETWS PRIMARY NOTIFICATION WITH SECURITY message?
questions.reference_answer: The ETWS PRIMARY NOTIFICATION WITH SECURITY message is described in TS 33.969 clause 6.2.2.3 (warning message format in ETWS, UTRAN delivery of the ETWS Primary Notification) and clause A.1.4 (distribution of the signature algorithm identifier in UMTS), and in TS 25.331 clause 8.5.10 (listed as an RRC message exempted from integrity protection) and clause 10.1.1 (listed as an RRC message with non-critical extensions only, clause 10.2.12a).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses of the MCPTT and MCVideo stage-3 specifications that define the handling of the GROUP CALL ACCEPT message, including the Message type coding tables that assign it a value.
questions.reference_answer: GROUP CALL ACCEPT handling is defined in TS 24.379 clause 10.2.2.4.3.3 (MCPTT stage-3, generation of GROUP CALL ACCEPT on receiving a GROUP CALL ANNOUNCEMENT) and TS 24.281 clause 9.3.2.4.3.4 (MCVideo stage-3, equivalent handling). The Message type coding tables assigning it a value are TS 24.379 clause 15.2.2 (MCPTT) and TS 24.281 clause 17.2.2 (MCVideo), where GROUP CALL ACCEPT is coded as bits 10001011. The message definition also appears in ts_24_281_17.1.4.1 (Message definition; Direction: UE to other UEs), ts_24_379_15.1.4.1 (Message definition; Direction: UE to other UEs).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: GROUP CALL ACCEPT handling is defined in TS 24.379 clause 10.2.2.4.3.3 (MCPTT stage-3, generation of GROUP CALL ACCEPT on receiving a GROUP CALL ANNOUNCEMENT) and TS 24.281 clause 9.3.2.4.3.4 (MCVideo stage-3, equivalent handling). The Message type coding tables assigning it a value are TS 24.379 clause 15.2.2 (MCPTT) and TS 24.281 clause 17.2.2 (MCVideo), where GROUP CALL ACCEPT is coded as bits 10001011.

questions.question: The HS-DSCH CAPACITY REQUEST control frame is sent per priority group to indicate user buffer size. In which frame-protocol specifications is its payload structure defined, one where the CRNC sends it and one where the SRNC sends it?
questions.reference_answer: The HS-DSCH CAPACITY REQUEST control frame payload structure is defined in TS 25.435 clause 6.3.3.10 (Iub frame protocol, NBAP), where it is sent by the CRNC, and in TS 25.425 clause 6.3.3.5 (Iur frame protocol, RNSAP), where it is sent by the SRNC.

questions.question: Where is the MBMS MODIFICATION REQUEST message specified — both the clause that lists the contents the UE shall set and the clauses on frequency selection and service prioritisation that trigger it?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS MODIFICATION REQUEST message content the UE shall set is defined in TS 25.331 clause 8.7.6.2a. It is triggered by the frequency selection procedure (clause 8.5.27, when the UE in CELL_DCH must move to a preferred frequency), the service prioritisation procedure (clause 8.5.26, to terminate p-t-p services inhibiting a prioritised MBMS service), and the initiation conditions in clause 8.7.6.2 (entering CELL_DCH, completing RRC connection setup, or a change in MBMS Selected Services).

questions.question: Which specifications define the ueIpv4Addr attribute, and what does it identify in each?
questions.reference_answer: The ueIpv4Addr attribute is defined in: TS 29.122 clause 5.14.2.1.2 (AsSessionWithQoSSubscription) as the IPv4 address of the UE; TS 29.514 clause 5.6.2.40 (PduSessionTsnBridge) as the identifier of the PDU session's UE IPv4 address for the reported UP node information; TS 29.556 clause 6.1.6.2.2 (DnsContextCreateData) as the UE IPv4 address; TS 29.558 clause 8.5.5.2.2 (SessionWithQoS) as the IPv4 address of the UE; TS 29.564 clause 6.1.6.2.3 (NotificationItem) as the IPv4 address of the UE for which the notification is generated; and TS 29.571 clause 5.4.4.10 (N3gaLocation) as the UE/N5CW device's local IPv4 address used to reach the N3IWF, TNGF, TWIF, or ePDG.

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the NGAP UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message?
questions.reference_answer: The NGAP UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message is described in TS 28.552 clause 5.1.1.6.1.9 (number of failed legacy handover executions), clause 5.1.1.6.8.9 (number of failed DAPS handover executions), and clause 5.1.1.6.1.13 (number of failed handover executions per beam pair) as a performance-measurement trigger event, and in TS 23.700-05 clause 6.12.3.2 as the message the CN sends to the source IAB-donor-CU to trigger release of resources on the source path during IAB-node mobility.

questions.question: The PDN MODIFICATION INDICATION message is used in the WLAN Control Protocol. Which clauses define the message itself, its abnormal cases in the UE, and the NBIFOM scenarios that carry it over trusted WLAN using MCM?
questions.reference_answer: The PDN MODIFICATION INDICATION message itself is defined in TS 24.244 clause 7.12.1 (message content table). Its abnormal cases in the UE are defined in TS 24.244 clause 5.7.5 (T3586 expiry, unknown PDN connection ID, collision with TWAG-initiated PDN disconnection). The NBIFOM scenarios carrying it over trusted WLAN using MCM are TS 24.161 clause 5.5.1.4 (UE-initiated IP flow mapping), clause 5.3.1.4 (UE-initiated IP flow mobility), clause 5.7.1.4 (access stratum indication), and clause 5.6.1.4 (change in usability of trusted WLAN using MCM).

questions.question: Where is the PMFP TDR REQUEST message used to resume traffic duplication over an access of an MA PDU session described, including the message-type coding table and the PMFP timer table?
questions.reference_answer: The PMFP TDR REQUEST message is described in TS 24.193: the message-type coding table is in clause 6.2.2.1 (Table 6.2.2.1-1, value bits 00001111), the traffic duplication resume procedure (initiation and completion) is in clauses 5.4.11.2 and 5.4.11.3, and the PMFP timer table is in clause 7.2 (Table 7.2-2, timer T208, started on transmission of PMFP TDR REQUEST and stopped on receipt of the matching PMFP TDR RESPONSE). The message definition also appears in ts_24_193_6.2.1.16.1 (Message definition; Direction: UPF to UE), ts_24_193_6.2.1.17.1 (Message definition; Direction: UE to UPF).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The PMFP TDR REQUEST message is described in TS 24.193: the message-type coding table is in clause 6.2.2.1 (Table 6.2.2.1-1, value bits 00001111), the traffic duplication resume procedure (initiation and completion) is in clauses 5.4.11.2 and 5.4.11.3, and the PMFP timer table is in clause 7.2 (Table 7.2-2, timer T208, started on transmission of PMFP TDR REQUEST and stopped on receipt of the matching PMFP TDR RESPONSE).

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the PMFP TDS REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: The PMFP TDS REQUEST message is defined or described in TS 24.193 clause 6.2.2.1 (message type coding table), clause 5.4.10.2 (traffic duplication suspend procedure initiation, sent by the UPF), clause 5.4.10.3 (traffic duplication suspend procedure completion, received by the UE), and clause 7.2 (PMFP timer table, timer T207); it is also mentioned in TS 29.244 clause 5.20.6 as sent by the UPF to the UE to suspend traffic duplication. The message definition also appears in ts_24_193_6.2.1.14.1 (Message definition; Direction: UPF to UE), ts_24_193_6.2.1.15.1 (Message definition; Direction: UE to UPF).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The PMFP TDS REQUEST message is defined or described in TS 24.193 clause 6.2.2.1 (message type coding table), clause 5.4.10.2 (traffic duplication suspend procedure initiation, sent by the UPF), clause 5.4.10.3 (traffic duplication suspend procedure completion, received by the UE), and clause 7.2 (PMFP timer table, timer T207); it is also mentioned in TS 29.244 clause 5.20.6 as sent by the UPF to the UE to suspend traffic duplication.

questions.question: In which clauses are the BSSMAP HANDOVER COMMAND message from MSC to BSS carrying the target channel, and the radio-interface HANDOVER COMMAND the old BSS then sends to the MS, described?
questions.reference_answer: The BSSMAP HANDOVER COMMAND message from MSC to BSS carrying the target channel is described in TS 48.008 clause 3.2.1.11 (message contents). The radio-interface HANDOVER COMMAND that the old BSS then sends to the MS is described in TS 48.008 clause 3.1.5.3.1 (Operation of the procedure).

questions.question: The UTRAN MOBILITY INFORMATION FAILURE message is sent on the uplink DCCH using AM RLC. Which clauses specify when the UE transmits it, and which SRNS relocation clauses involve the UTRAN MOBILITY INFORMATION message?
questions.reference_answer: The UE transmits UTRAN MOBILITY INFORMATION FAILURE on the uplink DCCH using AM RLC in TS 25.331 clause 8.3.3.5 (cell re-selection case), clause 8.3.3.6 (invalid UTRAN MOBILITY INFORMATION message / protocol error), and clause 8.3.3.5a (incompatible simultaneous security reconfiguration). The SRNS relocation clauses involving the UTRAN MOBILITY INFORMATION message are TS 25.303 clause 6.4.8.1 (lossless radio bearers) and clause 6.4.8.3 (seamless radio bearers), where it is used by the target RNC on SRB#1 to trigger Case I relocation.

questions.question: Which clauses describe the Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Update service operation that lets the AMF update the NSSF with the S-NSSAIs it supports per TA?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Update service operation is described in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.16.3.2 (definition: enables the AMF to update the NSSF with the S-NSSAIs it supports per TA and get availability/NSI IDs per TA), TS 29.531 clause 5.2.2.2.2 (referencing it in the context of Nnssf_NSSelection's Get operation for target AMF Set discovery), and TS 23.700-41 clause 6.24.3.1 (the AMF provides per-S-NSSAI and per-TA timing information to the NSSF using this service operation).

questions.question: Where in the corpus is the Nnwdaf_MLModelProvision_Unsubscribe service operation defined and used, covering both the stage-2 ML model subscribe/unsubscribe procedure and the stage-3 HTTP DELETE realisation?
questions.reference_answer: Nnwdaf_MLModelProvision_Unsubscribe is defined at stage-2 in TS 23.288 clause 6.2A.1 (ML Model Subscribe/Unsubscribe, used by an NWDAF service consumer to cancel a subscription for trained ML Model(s)) and TS 29.552 clause 5.6.2 (ML Model Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Notify procedure). Its stage-3 HTTP DELETE realisation is defined in TS 29.520 clause 4.5.2.1 (operation table) and clause 4.5.2.3.2 (Unsubscribe from event notifications: HTTP DELETE to the Individual NWDAF ML Model Provision Subscription resource, returning 204 No Content).

questions.question: Where is the Nadrf_DataManagement_StorageSubscriptionRemoval service operation specified?
questions.reference_answer: The Nadrf_DataManagement_StorageSubscriptionRemoval service operation is specified in TS 29.575 clause 4.2.2.1 (operation table), clause 4.2.2.4.2 (HTTP POST to the request-storage-sub-removal resource), and clause 5.1.9 (OAuth2 scope covering it), and referenced in TS 29.552 clause 5.9.3 as the operation an NF service consumer (DCCF/NWDAF) invokes to remove its storage subscription from the ADRF.

questions.question: The Nadrf_MLModelManagement_Delete service operation removes stored ML models from the ADRF. Which clauses define it, both by storage transaction identifier and by unique ML model identifier?
questions.reference_answer: The Nadrf_MLModelManagement_Delete service operation is defined by storage transaction identifier in TS 29.575 clause 4.3.2.4.2 (HTTP DELETE to the mlmodel-store-records/{storeTransId} resource) and by unique ML model identifier in TS 29.575 clause 4.3.2.4.3 (HTTP POST to the remove-stored-mlmodel resource with a list of model identifiers). It is also defined at stage-2 in TS 23.288 clause 10.3.3 (service operation description, inputs of either a Storage Transaction Identifier or one or more unique ML Model identifiers).

questions.question: Which documents specify the notifFlag attribute, and what does setting it control?
questions.reference_answer: The notifFlag attribute is specified in TS 29.503 (ReportingOptions, clause 6.4.6.2.6), TS 29.508 (NsmfEventExposure, clause 5.6.2.2), TS 29.518 (AmfEventMode, clause 6.2.6.2.6), TS 29.523 (ReportingInformation, clause 5.6.2.4), TS 29.536 (SACEventSubscription, clause 6.2.6.2.2), and TS 29.564 (UpfEventMode, clause 6.1.6.2.12). In each it indicates the notification flag used to mute/unmute notifications and to retrieve events stored during a period of muted notifications.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus describe the Ndcaf_DataReporting_Report service operation, and which entity invokes it towards the Data Collection AF?
questions.reference_answer: The Ndcaf_DataReporting_Report service operation is described in TS 24.549 clause 7.3.2.1 (operation table) and TS 26.532 clauses 4.2.6, 4.2.7 and 4.3.3 (indirect data reporting, reporting by Application Server, and direct data reporting). It is invoked towards the Data Collection AF by the Direct Data Collection Client, the Application Server, or the Indirect Data Collection Client, depending on the reporting path.

questions.question: Which documents specify the Nnef_ASTI_Delete service operation?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_ASTI_Delete service operation is specified in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.28.4 (service operation definition) and referenced in TS 23.700-25 clause 6.14.3.2, where the AF invokes Nnef_ASTI_Delete on the NEF to remove an existing 5G access stratum time distribution request.

questions.question: Which clauses describe the Nnef_ChargeableParty_Create request sent by the AF to the NEF to become the chargeable party for a session?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_ChargeableParty_Create request sent by the AF to the NEF is described in TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.4 (Set a chargeable party at AF session setup, step 1) and TS 23.700-80 clause 6.12.2 (step 2, enhanced charging for Application AI/ML traffic), where the AF requests to become the chargeable party for the session.

questions.question: The Nnef_MBSGroupMsgDelivery_Delete service operation cancels a previously submitted group message. Where is it specified in the stage-2 and stage-3 documents?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_MBSGroupMsgDelivery_Delete is specified at stage-3 in TS 29.522 clause 4.4.29.7.4 (Procedure for MBS Group Message Delivery Deletion, AF sends HTTP DELETE to the NEF) and at stage-2 in TS 23.247 clause 7.5.3 (Cancellation of previously submitted Group message: AF sends the Nnef_MBSGroupMsgDelivery_Delete Request to the NEF, which coordinates with the MBSF/MBSTF to cancel the delivery).

questions.question: In which clauses is the Nnrf_NFDiscovery_NFDiscover service operation specified?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnrf_NFDiscovery_NFDiscover service operation is referenced in TS 29.552 clause 5.8.2.3 (consumer discovery of an NWDAF containing AnLF or MTLF via NRF) and TS 23.700-17 clause 6.14.1 (UE discovery of the AN NRF, reusing this service operation as defined in TS 23.502).

questions.question: Where is the Npcf_EventExposure_Unsubscribe service operation described, including the table of Npcf_EventExposure service operations and the AF request termination flow?
questions.reference_answer: The Npcf_EventExposure_Unsubscribe service operation is described in TS 29.523 clause 4.2.1 (Table 4.2.1-1, Npcf_EventExposure service operations, used by an NF service consumer to unsubscribe from event notifications) and in TS 29.513 clause 5.2.2.2.2.5 (AF Request termination of application detection exposure: the AF sends Npcf_EventExposure_Unsubscribe via HTTP DELETE to the Individual Policy Control Events Subscription resource).

questions.question: Which clauses use the Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSM Context request from the AMF to the SMF in the XR media rate-adaptation and QoS notification control flows?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-60 clause 6.6.3.1 (Non-GBR QoS Notification Control Report) and clause 6.48.3.1 (Rate Adaptation Notification) both use the Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext request from the AMF to the SMF, carrying the changed available mean bitrate or the rate adaptation request respectively.

questions.question: Where is the Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify service operation specified, both in the table of Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization service operations and in the operation definition itself?
questions.reference_answer: Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify is specified in TS 29.565 clause 5.2.2.1 (Table 5.2.2.1-1, Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization service operations: allows the TSCTSF to notify the NF service consumer of the capability of time synchronization service) and in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.27.2.8 (operation definition: forwards the notification for the time synchronization configuration, invoked by the TSCTSF when it detects an event corresponding to a subscription).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Nucmf_Provisioning_Create service operation used to create a UCMF dictionary entry for a Manufacturer-assigned UE Radio Capability ID.
questions.reference_answer: Nucmf_Provisioning_Create is defined in TS 29.675 clause 4.2.1 (Table 4.2.1-1, Nucmf_Provisioning service operations: used by an NF service consumer to create a UE radio capability provisioning resource for Manufacturer-assigned UE Radio Capability IDs) and in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.18.2.1 (operation definition: the consumer creates a UCMF dictionary entry for a Manufacturer-assigned UE Radio Capability ID, providing the radio access capability set(s) and the related UE model IMEI/TAC values).

questions.question: The Nucmf_Provisioning_Update service operation updates the list of IMEI/TAC values a UCMF dictionary entry applies to. Where is it specified?
questions.reference_answer: Nucmf_Provisioning_Update is specified in TS 29.675 clause 4.2.1 (Table 4.2.1-1, Nucmf_Provisioning service operations: used by an NF service consumer to modify a UE radio capability provisioning resource) and in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.18.2.3 (operation definition: the consumer updates the list of IMEI/TAC values a UCMF dictionary entry applies to, by adding or removing IMEI/TAC values for the given UE Radio Capability ID).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the domainNames attribute, and say what it identifies in each API.
questions.reference_answer: The domainNames attribute is defined in: TS 26.510 clause 11.2.2.1 (createMediaDelivery input parameters), identifying a set of FQDNs of Media AS endpoints supporting the media delivery session at reference point M4; TS 29.122 clause 5.11.2.1.4 (type Pfd), TS 29.520 clause 5.1.6.2.107 (type SuggestedPfdInfo), and TS 29.551 clause 5.6.2.5 (type PfdContent), in all three identifying an FQDN or regular expression as a domain name matching criteria for the PFD; and TS 29.558 clause 8.6.5.2.14 (type TrafficFilterInfo), identifying domain name(s) matching criteria for the traffic flow.

questions.question: Where are the Nudm_MT_ProvideUeInfo and Nudm_MT_ProvideLocationInfo service operations defined, and which NF consumes them?
questions.reference_answer: The Nudm_MT_ProvideUeInfo and Nudm_MT_ProvideLocationInfo service operations are defined in TS 29.503 clause 5.8.2.1 (Introduction to the Nudm_MT service). They are consumed by the HSS: ProvideUeInfo is used to request terminating access domain selection information, user state and/or 5GSRVCCInfo, and ProvideLocationInfo is used to request the UE's location information in the 5GC.

questions.question: The Transport Layer Address information element carries an IP address for user-plane transport. In which specifications is it defined or used as part of a GTP Tunnel Endpoint IE?
questions.reference_answer: The Transport Layer Address IE is defined in TS 25.413 clause 9.2.2.1 (RANAP) as an IP address for user-plane transport, and appears as an optional element in TS 25.423 clause 9.1.35 (RNSAP) and TS 25.433 clause 9.2.1.108 (NBAP) tables. It is used as part of a GTP Tunnel Endpoint IE in TS 36.423 clause 9.2.1 (X2AP, X2/S1 user plane transport) and TS 36.463 clause 9.2.22 (Xw-AP, Xw user plane transport between eNB and WT), both defining the GTP Tunnel Endpoint IE as containing a Transport Layer Address and a GTP Tunnel Endpoint Identifier.

questions.question: Which clauses define the Uncertainty semi-major information element, whose uncertainty r is derived from the uncertainty code k by r = 10 x (1.1^k - 1), across the UTRAN, E-UTRAN and NG-RAN access point position IEs?
questions.reference_answer: The Uncertainty semi-major IE is defined across TS 25.331 clause 10.3.8.4c (Ellipsoid point with Altitude and uncertainty ellipsoid, UTRAN) and clause 10.3.8.4e (Ellipsoid point with uncertainty Ellipse, UTRAN), TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.68A (Uncertainty Ellipse, RNSAP), TS 36.455 clause 9.2.8 (E-UTRAN Access Point Position), and TS 38.455 clause 9.2.10 and TS 38.473 clause 9.3.1.174 (both NG-RAN Access Point Position).

questions.question: Tell me where the 'Uncertainty' and 'Orientation' simple data types used to describe a location estimate are defined, in the SEAL, LCS and lawful-interception specifications.
questions.reference_answer: The 'Uncertainty' and 'Orientation' simple data types are defined in TS 24.546 Annex C.1.4.3 (SEAL, Table C.1.4.3-2: Uncertainty is a number with minimum value 0; Orientation is an integer from 0 to 180), TS 29.572 clause 6.1.6.3.2 (LCS, Table 6.1.6.3.2-1: Uncertainty is a float value in meters with minimum 0; Orientation is an integer angle in degrees from 0 to 180), and TS 33.128 clause 7.3.3.2.1 (lawful interception, Table 7.3.3.2.1-1: Uncertainty is deprecated and always set to 0, INTEGER (0..127); Orientation is an integer angle in degrees from 0 to 180, encoded per TS 29.572).

questions.question: Which documents specify the resourceType attribute, and in which data-type definition table does it appear in each?
questions.reference_answer: The resourceType attribute is specified in TS 28.104 clause 8.5.17.2/8.5.19.2 (ResourceUsage data type), TS 29.486 clause 6.7.6.2.4 (AppplicationQosRequirement type), TS 29.512 clause 5.6.2.16 (QosCharacteristics type), TS 29.537 clause 6.1.6.2.9 (MbsQosChar type), and TS 29.571 clause 5.5.4.3 (Dynamic5Qi type).

questions.question: Where is the Capacity Value information element indicating the amount of resources available relative to the total RAN resources defined, across X2AP, XnAP, F1AP and the Xw case?
questions.reference_answer: The Capacity Value IE is defined in TS 36.423 clause 9.2.47 (X2AP, amount of resources available relative to total E-UTRAN resources) and clause 9.2.166 (NR Capacity Value, per cell/SSB area relative to total en-gNB resources), TS 38.423 clause 9.2.2.54 (XnAP, relative to total NG-RAN resources), and TS 38.473 clause 9.3.1.133 (F1AP, relative to total gNB-DU resources). For the Xw case, TS 36.463 clause 9.2.26 reuses the same 'Capacity Value' field inside the 'Available Channel Utilization' IE, indicating the amount of WLAN channel utilization time available for LWA services.

questions.question: The Charging Id field appears in bearer/session context tables and in charging information structures. Which clauses list it, covering the GGSN, S-GW and P-GW contexts as well as the PS and 5G data connectivity charging tables?
questions.reference_answer: The Charging Id field is listed in TS 23.060 clause 13.3 (GGSN PDP Context table), TS 23.401 clause 5.7.3 (S-GW EPS bearer context table) and clause 5.7.4 (P-GW context table), TS 32.251 Annex E.3.4 (service information used for PS charging), and TS 32.255 Annex C.3.2.1 (definition of 5G data connectivity charging information).

questions.question: Where is the Complete Almanac Provided field, indicating whether the RNC provided almanac for the full GPS constellation, defined together with the GPS/GANSS almanac IEs?
questions.reference_answer: The Complete Almanac Provided field is defined together with the GPS/GANSS almanac IEs in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.89 (UE positioning GPS almanac) and clause 10.3.7.89a (UE positioning GANSS almanac), and also appears in the corresponding NBAP/RNSAP/PCAP almanac IEs in TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.30G (GPS Almanac), TS 25.433 clause 9.2.1.31F (GPS Almanac), and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.9 (GPS Almanac and Satellite Health). It is a boolean field indicating whether the RNC provided almanac for the full GPS/GANSS constellation (TRUE meaning complete almanac is provided).

questions.question: In which specification clauses is the "DBDS Reference Time" information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: The DBDS Reference Time IE is defined in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.92e (UE positioning DBDS corrections), TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.157 (DBDS Corrections, RNSAP), TS 25.433 clause 9.2.1.127 (DBDS Corrections, NBAP), and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.161 (DBDS Correction Information, PCAP).

questions.question: The 'Encryption supported' information element appears in ad hoc group communication request information flows. Which mission-critical specifications include it in their ad hoc group request tables?
questions.reference_answer: The 'Encryption supported' IE appears in the ad hoc group request tables of TS 23.281 clause 7.19.2.1 (MCVideo ad hoc group call request), TS 23.282 clause 7.17.2.1 (MCData ad hoc group data session request), TS 23.379 clause 10.19.2.1 (MCPTT ad hoc group call request), and TS 23.700-76 clause 7.1.2.1 (generic MC service ad hoc group communication request).

questions.question: Which specifications define the EnhDataMgmt supported feature, and what does it indicate in each?
questions.reference_answer: The EnhDataMgmt feature is defined in TS 29.508 clause 5.8 (Nsmf_EventExposure API), TS 29.517 clause 5.8 (Naf_EventExposure API), TS 29.520 clause 5.3.8 (Nnwdaf-relevant API), TS 29.574 clause 5.1.8 (Ndccf_DataManagement API), TS 29.575 clause 5.1.8 (Nadrf_DataManagement API), and TS 29.591 clause 5.1.8 (Nnef_EventExposure API). In all of these it indicates support of enhanced data management mechanisms; TS 29.520/29.574 additionally note this includes support of pending notification, muting and storage handling, while TS 29.508/29.517/29.591 note that supporting this feature also requires support of the EneNA feature.

questions.question: Which clauses use the GANSS Time ID parameter, covering both the UE positioning GANSS reference time IE and the TUTRAN-GANSS measurement value/threshold information IEs?
questions.reference_answer: The GANSS Time ID parameter is used in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.96o (UE positioning GANSS reference time IE) and, for the TUTRAN-GANSS measurement value/threshold information IEs, in TS 25.423 clause 9.1.43 and clause 9.2.1.114 (RNSAP), TS 25.433 clause 9.1.18 and clause 9.2.1.99 (NBAP), and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.124 (GANSS Reference Time, PCAP).

questions.question: The 'List of service area identifier' information element accompanies TMGI information. In which MBMS bearer announcement and V2X user service description tables does it appear?
questions.reference_answer: The 'List of service area identifier' IE appears in the MBMS bearer announcement tables of TS 23.280 clause 10.7.2.1 (MC service server to MC service client), TS 23.434 clause 14.3.2.3 (NRM server to NRM client), and TS 23.700-79 clause 7.8.2.1 (MC GW MBMS bearer announcement), and in the V2X user service description tables of TS 23.285 clause 4.4.7.2 (User Service Description for V2X Communication) and clause 4.4.7.3 (User Service Description for V2X Application Server Discovery). It also appears in ts_23_479_5.8.3.1 (MC MBMS bearer registration request).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The 'List of service area identifier' IE appears in the MBMS bearer announcement tables of TS 23.280 clause 10.7.2.1 (MC service server to MC service client), TS 23.434 clause 14.3.2.3 (NRM server to NRM client), and TS 23.700-79 clause 7.8.2.1 (MC GW MBMS bearer announcement), and in the V2X user service description tables of TS 23.285 clause 4.4.7.2 (User Service Description for V2X Communication) and clause 4.4.7.3 (User Service Description for V2X Application Server Discovery).

questions.question: In which specification clauses is the "Message structure" information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: The Message Structure IE is defined in TS 25.413 clause 9.2.1.42 (RANAP), TS 25.419 clause 9.2.20 (SABP), TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.39A (RNSAP), and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.23 (PCAP).

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus specify the QoS-Information Diameter AVP among the AVPs re-used from Gx or other Diameter applications by the SGmb, S15, S9a and S9a* reference points?
questions.reference_answer: The QoS-Information Diameter AVP re-used from Gx or other Diameter applications is specified in TS 29.061 clause 20.5 (SGmb re-used AVPs, containing the QoS required for the MBMS bearer service), TS 29.212 Annex E.6.4.1 (S15 re-used AVPs, containing QoS information for a CS service resource), and TS 29.215 Annex A.7.4.1 (S9a re-used AVPs) and Annex A.8.4.1 (S9a* re-used AVPs), both defining the QoS information that can be accepted by the BPCF.

questions.question: In which specification clauses is the "WLAN Measurement Configuration Name List" information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: The WLAN Measurement Configuration Name List IE is defined in TS 36.413 clause 9.2.1.138 (S1AP), TS 36.423 clause 9.2.135 (X2AP), TS 38.413 clause 9.3.1.178 (NGAP), and TS 38.423 clause 9.2.3.135 (XnAP).

questions.question: Which clauses define the Week Number field as an almanac reference week or GANSS time-model parameter, in both the UTRAN RRC positioning IEs and the RNSAP/NBAP/PCAP GANSS Time Model IEs?
questions.reference_answer: The Week Number field is defined in ts_25_331_10.3.7.89a (UE positioning GANSS almanac, as the almanac reference week) and ts_25_331_10.3.7.97a (UE positioning GANSS time model, as the reference week of the GANSS Time Model). In RNSAP, NBAP, and PCAP it is defined in the GANSS Time Model IE at ts_25_423_9.2.1.110, ts_25_433_9.2.1.96, and ts_25_453_9.2.2.125 respectively.

questions.question: The asTimeDisParam attribute carries the 5G access stratum time distribution parameters. In which data type definition tables does it appear?
questions.reference_answer: The asTimeDisParam attribute (type AsTimeDistributionParam) appears in Type PolicyAssociation (ts_29_507_5.6.2.2) and Type PolicyUpdate (ts_29_507_5.6.2.5). It also appears as AfAsTimeDistributionParam in Type AccessTimeDistributionData (ts_29_522_5.22.4.3.2 and ts_29_565_6.3.6.2.2), and as AsTimeDistributionParam in Type AppAmContextData (ts_29_534_5.6.2.2) and Type AppAmContextUpdateData (ts_29_534_5.6.2.3).

questions.question: The communicationDurationTime attribute indicates how long the UE will normally stay in CM-CONNECTED for data transmission. Which data types and lawful-interception records include it?
questions.reference_answer: The communicationDurationTime attribute (type DurationSec) appears in Type CpParameterSet (ts_29_122_5.10.2.2.2), Type CnAssistedRanPara (ts_29_502_6.1.6.2.48), Type ExpectedUeBehaviourData (ts_29_503_6.1.6.2.49), and Type ExpectedUeBehaviour (ts_29_503_6.5.6.2.8, as DurationSecRm). It is also included in the lawful-interception records for Expected UE behaviour update (ts_33_128_7.7.5.1.2) and Communication pattern update (ts_33_128_7.8.5.1.2).

questions.question: In which specification clauses is the "dnaiChgType" information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: The "dnaiChgType" information element (type DnaiChangeType) is defined in Type EventSubscription (ts_29_508_5.6.2.4), Type UpPathChgEvent (ts_29_512_5.6.2.20), Type EventNotification (ts_29_522_5.4.3.3.4), Type AcrMgntEventSubsc (ts_29_558_8.6.5.2.3), and Type UpPathChangeInfo (ts_29_558_8.6.5.2.9). It also appears in ts_29_508_5.6.2.5 (Type EventNotification), ts_29_519_6.4.2.2 (Type TrafficInfluData), ts_29_522_5.4.3.3.2 (Type: TrafficInfluSub).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The "dnaiChgType" information element (type DnaiChangeType) is defined in Type EventSubscription (ts_29_508_5.6.2.4), Type UpPathChgEvent (ts_29_512_5.6.2.20), Type EventNotification (ts_29_522_5.4.3.3.4), Type AcrMgntEventSubsc (ts_29_558_8.6.5.2.3), and Type UpPathChangeInfo (ts_29_558_8.6.5.2.9).

questions.question: For a consumer choosing how notifications are delivered, where is the notifMethod attribute defined and what values does each specification allow?
questions.reference_answer: The notifMethod attribute is defined in Type NsmfEventExposure (ts_29_508_5.6.2.2, type NotificationMethod, default "ON_EVENT_DETECTION"), Type AfEventSubscription (ts_29_514_5.6.2.10, type AfNotifMethod, default "EVENT_DETECTION"), Type TimeSyncExposureSubsc (ts_29_522_5.15.4.3.2 and ts_29_565_6.1.6.2.2, type NotificationMethod, default "ON_EVENT_DETECTION"), Type ReportingInformation (ts_29_523_5.6.2.4, type NotificationMethod, default "ON_EVENT_DETECTION"), and Type AmEventData (ts_29_534_5.6.2.8, type NotificationMethod, default "ON_EVENT_DETECTION").

questions.question: Where is the formatInstruct attribute defined, and in which data type is it defined in each?
questions.reference_answer: The formatInstruct attribute (type FormattingInstruction) is defined in Type NnwdafDataManagementSubsc (ts_29_520_5.3.6.2.2), Type RoamingDataSub (ts_29_520_5.7.6.2.2), Type NdccfAnalyticsSubscription (ts_29_574_5.1.6.2.2), Type NdccfDataSubscription (ts_29_574_5.1.6.2.3), Type NadrfDataStoreSubscription (ts_29_575_5.1.6.2.3), and Type MessageConfiguration (ts_29_576_5.1.6.2.3).

questions.question: Which documents specify the lcsQosClass attribute, and in which data type is it defined in each?
questions.reference_answer: The lcsQosClass attribute (type LcsQosClass) is defined in Type RangingSlPosQos (ts_29_503_6.1.6.2.102), Type LocUpdateData (ts_29_515_6.1.5.2.5 and ts_29_522_5.13.3.3.2), Type LocUpdateNotification (ts_29_515_6.1.5.2.9), and Type LocationQoS (ts_29_572_6.1.6.2.13).

questions.question: In which specification clauses is the "notificationURI" information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: The "notificationURI" information element (type Uri) is defined in the Operation Definition callback URI variables table of ts_29_520_5.1.5.2.2, Type NnwdafEventsSubscription (ts_29_520_5.1.6.2.2), Type TopicListSubscription (ts_29_538_8.3.5.2.2), Type NadrfDataRetrievalSubscription (ts_29_575_5.1.6.2.4), and Type MessageConfiguration (ts_29_576_5.1.6.2.3). It also appears in ts_29_538_8.3.4.2.2 (Target URI), ts_29_575_5.1.5.2.2 (Target URI), ts_29_576_5.2.5.2.2 (Target URI).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The "notificationURI" information element (type Uri) is defined in the Operation Definition callback URI variables table of ts_29_520_5.1.5.2.2, Type NnwdafEventsSubscription (ts_29_520_5.1.6.2.2), Type TopicListSubscription (ts_29_538_8.3.5.2.2), Type NadrfDataRetrievalSubscription (ts_29_575_5.1.6.2.4), and Type MessageConfiguration (ts_29_576_5.1.6.2.3).

questions.question: Which clauses define the 2dRelativeLocation and 3dRelativeLocation attributes of the location data and event notification data types?
questions.reference_answer: The 2dRelativeLocation and 3dRelativeLocation attributes (types 2DRelativeLocation and 3DRelativeLocation) are defined together in Type LocationData (ts_29_515_6.1.5.2.3 and ts_29_572_6.1.6.2.3) and Type EventNotifyData (ts_29_515_6.1.5.2.6 and ts_29_572_6.1.6.2.34), and also in Type ProvidePosInfo (ts_29_518_6.4.6.2.3) and Type NotifiedPosInfo (ts_29_518_6.4.6.2.4).

questions.question: The stationaryIndication attribute identifies whether the UE is stationary or mobile. Which data types define it in the SMF, UDM and communication-pattern provisioning specifications?
questions.reference_answer: The stationaryIndication attribute (type StationaryIndication) is defined in Type CnAssistedRanPara (ts_29_502_6.1.6.2.48, SMF-related), Type ExpectedUeBehaviourData (ts_29_503_6.1.6.2.49, UDM-related) and Type ExpectedUeBehaviour (ts_29_503_6.5.6.2.8, as StationaryIndicationRm, nullable), and Type CpParameterSet (ts_29_122_5.10.2.2.2, communication-pattern provisioning).

questions.question: Which data type definitions carry the steeringContainer attribute used for steering of roaming information?
questions.reference_answer: The steeringContainer attribute (type SteeringContainer) used for steering of roaming is carried in Type SorInfo (ts_29_503_6.1.6.2.26 and ts_29_509_6.2.6.2.2) and Type SorInformation (ts_29_550_6.1.6.2.2). Type ExtendedSteeringContainer (ts_29_544_6.1.6.2.3) also carries a steeringContainer attribute, but as an array(SteeringInfo).

questions.question: The 'UE identifier' information element identifies the hosting UE by GPSI or identity token in PIN and edge-enabling flows. Which information-flow tables include it?
questions.reference_answer: The 'UE identifier' (identifying the hosting UE by GPSI or identity token) appears in the PIN client profile information flow (ts_23_542_8.2.2.3 and ts_23_700-78_7.7.2.4), the PIN discovery request (ts_23_542_8.5.7.3.2), the ACR request (ts_23_558_8.8.4.4), the EELManagedACR service request (ts_23_558_8.8.4.15), and the traffic influence solution information flow (ts_23_700-98_7.22.2.1).

questions.question: The Uncertainty Altitude field is part of an ellipsoid point with altitude and uncertainty ellipsoid - in which clauses is it defined, in the UTRAN RRC IE and the E-UTRAN / NG-RAN access point position IEs?
questions.reference_answer: In the UTRAN RRC IE, Uncertainty Altitude is defined in clause ts_25_331_10.3.8.4c (Ellipsoid point with Altitude and uncertainty ellipsoid) as Integer(0..127). In E-UTRAN/NG-RAN it is defined in ts_36_455_9.2.8 (E-UTRAN Access Point Position), ts_38_455_9.2.10 (NG-RAN Access Point Position), and ts_38_473_9.3.1.174 (NG-RAN Access Point Position), all as INTEGER(0..127) mapped via h=45x(1.025^k-1).

questions.question: The 'Event Time Stamps' information element appears in converged charging message structures. Which charging specifications include it in their Charging Data Request or CHF CDR tables?
questions.reference_answer: The 'Event Time Stamps' IE appears in ts_28_826_6.4.5 (Common IE), ts_32_260_6.4.1b.2 (IMS converged charging CHF CDR data), ts_32_270_6.2a.1.2.1, ts_32_274_6.2a.1.2.1, and ts_32_277_6.2a.1.2.1 (Charging Data Request message in each), and ts_32_277_6.2a.3.2 (5G ProSe converged charging CHF CDR data). It also appears in ts_32_290_7 (Message contents).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The 'Event Time Stamps' IE appears in ts_28_826_6.4.5 (Common IE), ts_32_260_6.4.1b.2 (IMS converged charging CHF CDR data), ts_32_270_6.2a.1.2.1, ts_32_274_6.2a.1.2.1, and ts_32_277_6.2a.1.2.1 (Charging Data Request message in each), and ts_32_277_6.2a.3.2 (5G ProSe converged charging CHF CDR data).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the 'External Identifier' information element in the SCEF control-plane data transfer, exposure function API and SMS charging information structures.
questions.reference_answer: The 'External Identifier' IE is defined in ts_32_253_6.1.3.2 (SCEF Control Plane data transfer charging data CPDT-SCE-CDR) and ts_32_253_6.3.1.2 (Definition of the CP data transfer Information), ts_32_254_6.1.3.2 (Exposure Function API charging data EA-SCE-CDR) and ts_32_254_6.3.1.2 (Definition of the Exposure Function API Information), and ts_32_274_6.1.3.6 (SC-SMO-T4 CDR content) and ts_32_274_6.3.1.2 (Definition of the SMS Information).

questions.question: The Node Functionality information element is reused across several charging interfaces - in which specifications is it defined, and what roles can it name?
questions.reference_answer: The Node Functionality IE is defined in ts_32_251_6.3.1.1 (PS charging, naming SGW, ePDG, TWAG, PGW, TDF, or HSGW), ts_32_251_6.3.1.1a (SMS over MME Charging, naming MME), ts_32_253_6.3.1.1 (CP data transfer charging, naming SCEF, IWK-SCEF, MME), ts_32_254_6.3.1.1 (Exposure Function API charging), ts_32_260_6.3.1.2 (IMS Information, general node function), and ts_32_276_6.3.1.1 (VCS charging, naming "Proxy-Function").

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the Monitoring state information element, and in which information flow table does it appear in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Monitoring state IE, used to control if the client is actively monitoring the MBMS bearer/reception quality, is defined in the MBMS bearer announcement flow (ts_23_280_10.7.2.1 and ts_23_434_14.3.2.3), the MBMS user service announcement flow (ts_23_282_7.3.5.2.1), the MC GW MBMS bearer announcement flow (ts_23_700-79_7.8.2.1), and referenced in the Introduction clause of MCData/protocol procedures (ts_24_581_9.3.3.1).

questions.question: Which clauses describe the DISTRIBUTION SETUP REQUEST message that an NG-RAN node sends to the AMF for an MBS session, and which stage-3 clause lists it as an NGAP IE carried in N2 MBS session management information?
questions.reference_answer: The NG-RAN node initiates the Distribution Setup procedure by sending the DISTRIBUTION SETUP REQUEST message to the AMF, as described in ts_38_413_8.18.1.2. Stage-3 clause ts_29_532_6.2.6.5.2 (N2 MBS Session Management Information) lists the MBS Distribution Setup Request Transfer IE, related to this message, among the NGAP IEs carried in N2 MBS Session Management Information per TS 38.413 clause 9.3.5.

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the DISTRIBUTION RELEASE REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: The DISTRIBUTION RELEASE REQUEST message is described in ts_38_413_8.18.2.2 (Successful Operation of the Distribution Release procedure, sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF) and referenced in ts_29_532_6.2.6.5.2 (N2 MBS Session Management Information), which lists the MBS Distribution Release Request Transfer IE as the NGAP IE carrying this message.

questions.question: Which clauses describe the IURH SETUP REQUEST message, covering both the Iurh setup procedures between HNBs via the HNB-GW and the abnormal conditions when the first message on a TNL association is not an Iurh Setup message?
questions.reference_answer: The IURH SETUP REQUEST message is described in ts_25_467_5.9.4 (Iurh Setup between the HNB and HNB-GW for HNB-RNC connectivity, sent by the HNB to the HNB-GW) and ts_25_467_5.9.3 (Iurh Setup for Iurh connectivity between HNBs via the HNB-GW). The abnormal conditions when the first message on a TNL association is not an Iurh Setup message are covered in ts_25_471_8.2.2.3 (Abnormal Conditions).

questions.question: In which clauses is the 'Clock Frequency Stability' element of the Clock Quality Acceptance Criteria and RAN Timing Synchronisation Status Information IEs defined, in NGAP, XnAP and F1AP?
questions.reference_answer: In NGAP, Clock Frequency Stability is defined within the Clock Quality Acceptance Criteria IE (ts_38_413_9.3.1.251) and the RAN Timing Synchronisation Status Information IE (ts_38_413_9.3.1.252). In XnAP it is defined within Clock Quality Acceptance Criteria (ts_38_423_9.2.3.190), and in F1AP within RAN Timing Synchronisation Status Information (ts_38_473_9.3.1.298). In all cases it is a BIT STRING(SIZE(16)) indicating the offsetScaledLogVariance as specified in TS 23.501.

questions.question: Tell me where the SMS BROADCAST COMMAND message sent to a BTS for cell broadcast is described, in both the BSC-BTS layer 3 specification and the cell broadcast service architecture.
questions.reference_answer: In the BSC-BTS layer 3 specification, the SMS BROADCAST COMMAND message is described in ts_48_058_5.6 (Short Message Cell Broadcast), where the BSC requests broadcast of a complete Cell Broadcast message in a single message and the BTS handles segmentation. In the cell broadcast service architecture it is described in ts_23_041_9.1.1 and ts_23_041_6, where the BSC sends 1 SMS BROADCAST COMMAND message (or a sequence of 4 SMS BROADCAST REQUEST messages) to transfer CBS information to the BTS.

questions.question: Which clauses define the 'Disposition association' information element identifying the original MCData transaction in data disposition notification flows?
questions.reference_answer: The 'Disposition association' IE, which identifies the original MCData transaction, is defined in ts_23_180_10.6.1.2.2 (IOPS MCData data disposition notification), ts_23_282_7.4.2.1.9 (MCData data disposition notification, server-client), ts_23_282_7.4.2.1.9A (MCData aggregated data disposition notification), ts_23_282_7.5.3.2.3 (MCData download completed report), and ts_23_283_10.8.2.3 and ts_23_283_10.8.2.6 (IWF MCData data disposition notification(s)). It also appears in ts_23_282_7.4.2.1.2 (MCData data disposition notification).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The 'Disposition association' IE, which identifies the original MCData transaction, is defined in ts_23_180_10.6.1.2.2 (IOPS MCData data disposition notification), ts_23_282_7.4.2.1.9 (MCData data disposition notification, server-client), ts_23_282_7.4.2.1.9A (MCData aggregated data disposition notification), ts_23_282_7.5.3.2.3 (MCData download completed report), and ts_23_283_10.8.2.3 and ts_23_283_10.8.2.6 (IWF MCData data disposition notification(s)).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that describe the WRITE-REPLACE WARNING INDICATION message reporting Broadcast Scheduled Area Lists back to the CBC or CBCF, including the NG-RAN variant.
questions.reference_answer: The WRITE-REPLACE WARNING INDICATION message, reporting the Broadcast Scheduled Area List back to the CBC, is described in ts_29_168_4.3.4.2.5 (sent by MME/PWS-IWF to CBC) and ts_23_041_9.2.20. The NG-RAN variant, WRITE-REPLACE-WARNING-INDICATION-NG-RAN, sent by the AMF to the CBCF with the Broadcast Scheduled Area List NG-RAN, is described in ts_23_041_9.2.30.

questions.question: The UTDOA INFORMATION RESPONSE message is returned by the eNB to the E-SMLC. Which LPPa clauses specify the UTDOA Information Exchange procedure and the elementary-procedure table that lists it?
questions.reference_answer: The UTDOA Information Exchange procedure, in which the eNB replies to the E-SMLC with the UTDOA INFORMATION RESPONSE message, is specified in ts_36_455_8.2.6.2 (Successful Operation). It is listed as a Class 1 Elementary Procedure (Initiating Message UTDOA INFORMATION REQUEST, Successful Outcome UTDOA INFORMATION RESPONSE, Unsuccessful Outcome UTDOA INFORMATION FAILURE) in the elementary-procedure table ts_36_455_8.1.

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the X2AP HANDOVER REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: The X2AP HANDOVER REQUEST message is referenced in ts_36_300_10.5.1.2 (RRC_CONNECTED, as the message the source eNB/HeNB sends to the target HeNB including CSG membership status) and in ts_32_425_4.2.1.9/4.2.1.10, which define the E-RAB establishment measurements triggered on receipt of an X2AP HANDOVER REQUEST (or transmission of the X2AP HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE).

questions.question: Which specifications define the sampRatio attribute, and what values can it take?
questions.reference_answer: The sampRatio attribute (type SamplingRatio) is defined in Type NsmfEventExposure (ts_29_508_5.6.2.2), Type AmfEventMode (ts_29_518_6.2.6.2.6), Type EventReportingRequirement (ts_29_520_5.1.6.2.7, as percentage of sampling 1%...100% among impacted UEs), Type ReportingInformation (ts_29_523_5.6.2.4), and Type UpfEventMode (ts_29_564_6.1.6.2.12). In each it indicates the ratio of a random subset of target UEs (or PDU sessions, for UpfEventMode) to which event reports relate, applicable to events targeting a group of UEs or any UE.

questions.question: Where is the SGNB MODIFICATION REQUEST REJECT message specified — the unsuccessful operation of the MeNB initiated SgNB Modification Preparation procedure, its abnormal conditions, and the stage-2 description of that procedure?
questions.reference_answer: The SGNB MODIFICATION REQUEST REJECT message is specified in ts_36_423_8.7.6.3 (Unsuccessful Operation), sent by the en-gNB to the MeNB when it does not admit any modification requested by the MeNB or when the SGNB MODIFICATION REQUEST message's MeNB to SgNB Container IE lacks required information. Its abnormal conditions (e.g. duplicate E-RAB IDs, mismatched security algorithms) are in ts_36_423_8.7.6.4. The stage-2 description of the MeNB initiated SgNB Modification Preparation procedure is in ts_36_300_20.2.2.22.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus describe the SENB MODIFICATION REQUEST REJECT message returned when the SeNB does not admit a requested modification, and the corresponding stage-2 procedure description?
questions.reference_answer: The SENB MODIFICATION REQUEST REJECT message, sent by the SeNB to the MeNB when it does not admit a requested modification, is described in ts_36_423_8.6.3.3 (Unsuccessful Operation) and its abnormal conditions (e.g. duplicate E-RAB IDs, mismatched encryption algorithms) in ts_36_423_8.6.3.4. The corresponding stage-2 procedure, MeNB initiated SeNB Modification Preparation, is described in ts_36_300_20.2.2.2c.

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the S-NODE CHANGE CONFIRM message?
questions.reference_answer: The S-NODE CHANGE CONFIRM message is described in ts_38_423_8.3.5.2 (Successful Operation, sent by the M-NG-RAN node to the S-NG-RAN node when it can perform the requested change) and its abnormal conditions in ts_38_423_8.3.5.4 (e.g. timer TXnDCoverall expiry, missing PDU Session Resource Change Confirm Info). It is also referenced in ts_28_552_5.1.1.6.10 as the XnAP message that triggers the S-SN to communicate CPC configuration to the UE in the inter-SN CPC preparation time measurement.

questions.question: Which chunks in the corpus define or describe the PACKET POLLING REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: The PACKET POLLING REQUEST message is described in ts_43_246_7.2 (Mobile Station tasks, where a broadcast/multicast-receive-mode MS shall respond to it when addressed by TLLI), and in ts_43_059_9.5.2.2.2 and ts_43_059_9.5.2.2.1, where it is used in the Packet polling procedure to cause the MS to transmit for U-TDOA location purposes, with the BSS indicating a PACKET CONTROL ACKNOWLEDGEMENT response via the TYPE OF ACK information element.

questions.question: Where is the MEDIA FAILURE message described in the MCPTT and MCVideo stage-3 specifications when the media session declared in the SDP body of a PRIVATE CALL SETUP REQUEST cannot be established?
questions.reference_answer: In the MCVideo stage-3 specification, the MEDIA FAILURE reason (set in the Reason IE of the PRIVATE CALL REJECT message) is described in ts_24_281_10.3.2.4.3.1 (Unable to establish media), when the media session declared in the SDP body of a PRIVATE CALL SETUP REQUEST cannot be established. In the MCPTT stage-3 specification it is described equivalently in ts_24_379_11.2.2.4.3.1 (Unable to establish media), and ts_24_379_11.2.3.4.5.6 describes the related emergency private call handling when the media session can be established.

questions.question: Where is the MANAGE UE POLICY COMMAND COMPLETE message described, in the URSP update flows initiated by the PCF and in the UE abnormal cases for UE policy delivery?
questions.reference_answer: The MANAGE UE POLICY COMMAND COMPLETE message is described in the URSP update procedures initiated by the PCF: ts_23_700-85_6.16.2.3.2 (PCF-UE processes the MANAGE UE POLICY COMMAND COMPLETE UPDP message received via Npcf_UEPolicyControl_Update) and ts_23_700-85_6.16.2.2 (the UE generates the UPDP message MANAGE UE POLICY COMMAND COMPLETE after processing the UE Policy Container). In the UE abnormal cases for UE policy delivery, ts_24_501_D.2.1.6 covers transmission failure of this message and retransmission of the MANAGE UE POLICY COMMAND COMPLETE (or REJECT) message upon receiving a duplicate MANAGE UE POLICY COMMAND with the same PTI.

questions.question: Which clauses define the '5G ProSe Direct Communication' entry of the 5G ProSe Authorized IE, indicating whether the UE is authorized for 5G ProSe direct communication, across NGAP, XnAP and F1AP?
questions.reference_answer: The '5G ProSe Direct Communication' entry of the 5G ProSe Authorized IE is defined in ts_38_413_9.3.1.233 (NGAP), ts_38_423_9.2.3.159 (XnAP), and ts_38_473_9.3.1.268 (F1AP). In each, it is an optional ENUMERATED(authorized, not authorized, ...) field indicating whether the UE is authorized for 5G ProSe Direct Communication.

questions.question: Tell me where the 'Last E-UTRAN PLMN Identity' element is defined, in the RANAP COMMON ID and source-to-target container and in the NGAP/XnAP Mobility Restriction List.
questions.reference_answer: The 'Last E-UTRAN PLMN Identity' element is defined in the RANAP COMMON ID message (ts_25_413_9.1.24) as an optional field indicating the E-UTRAN PLMN ID where the UE formerly requested CS Fallback to UTRAN. It also appears via reference in the Source RNC to Target RNC Transparent Container (ts_25_413_9.2.1.28). In NGAP and XnAP it is defined within the Mobility Restriction List IE (ts_38_413_9.3.1.85 and ts_38_423_9.2.3.53). It also appears in ts_25_413_9.1.7 (IU RELEASE COMMAND).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: The 'Last E-UTRAN PLMN Identity' element is defined in the RANAP COMMON ID message (ts_25_413_9.1.24) as an optional field indicating the E-UTRAN PLMN ID where the UE formerly requested CS Fallback to UTRAN. It also appears via reference in the Source RNC to Target RNC Transparent Container (ts_25_413_9.2.1.28). In NGAP and XnAP it is defined within the Mobility Restriction List IE (ts_38_413_9.3.1.85 and ts_38_423_9.2.3.53).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the 'CHOICE Transaction ID Length' element of the Transaction ID IE used to associate all messages belonging to the same procedure, in RNSAP, NBAP and PCAP.
questions.reference_answer: The 'CHOICE Transaction ID Length' element of the Transaction ID IE is defined in ts_25_423_9.2.1.59 (RNSAP), ts_25_433_9.2.1.62 (NBAP), and ts_25_453_9.2.2.28 (PCAP). In each, it offers a Short (INTEGER 0..127) or Long (INTEGER 0..32767) encoding, interpreted only by its integer value, not the encoding type.

questions.question: The 'CHOICE ssb-PositionsInBurst' element indicates the time domain positions of transmitted SS blocks in a half frame. In which interface specifications is the SSB Positions In Burst IE defined?
questions.reference_answer: The SSB Positions In Burst IE, with its CHOICE ssb-PositionsInBurst element (ShortBitmap SIZE(4), MediumBitmap SIZE(8), or LongBitmap SIZE(64)), is defined in ts_36_423_9.2.169 (X2AP), ts_38_423_9.2.2.64 (XnAP), and ts_38_473_9.3.1.138 (F1AP).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the ServiceExperience attribute, and say what each one exposes it for.
