questions.question: For lawful interception of PTC services, where is the GroupCharacteristics parameter defined?
questions.reference_answer: The GroupCharacteristics parameter for lawful interception of PTC services is defined in TS 33.108, clauses 17.2.13 (PTC Group Advertisement), 17.3.3 (Group Call Cancel), 17.3.4 (Group Call Response), and 17.3.6 (MCPTT Imminent Peril Group Call).

questions.question: Where is the Support of MAC-i/is information element of the UTRAN RRC signalling defined?
questions.reference_answer: The Support of MAC-i/is information element is defined in TS 25.331, appearing in the RRC messages CELL UPDATE (clause 10.2.7), CELL UPDATE FDD (clause 10.2.7a), URA UPDATE (clause 10.2.60), and in the UE radio access capability type (clause 10.3.3.42).

questions.question: Tell me where the TDM Termination information element used in the IMS-CS interworking is described.
questions.reference_answer: The TDM Termination information element used in IMS-CS interworking is described in TS 23.205, clauses 16.2.53 (Continuity Check Tone), 16.2.54 (Continuity Check Verify), and 16.2.55 (Continuity Check Response), and in TS 29.163, clauses 9.3.2.9 (Continuity check), 9.3.2.10 (Continuity check verify), and 9.3.2.11 (Continuity check response).

questions.question: In which clauses is the ageOfLocationInfo attribute defined?
questions.reference_answer: The ageOfLocationInfo attribute is defined in TS 29.122, clause 5.3.2.3.5 (Type: LocationInfo), and in TS 33.128, clauses 7.3.3.2.6 (Type: NRLocation), 7.3.3.2.7 (Type: N3GALocation), and 7.3.3.2.9 (Type: GERALocation).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the ecsServerAddr attribute used to provision an edge configuration server address.
questions.reference_answer: The ecsServerAddr attribute is defined in TS 29.503, clause 6.5.6.2.21 (Type: EcsAddrConfigInfo); TS 29.519, clause 6.4.2.23 (Type EcsAddrData); and TS 29.522, clauses 5.7.2.3.13 (Type: ECSAddrParams), 5.16.2.3.2 (Type: EcsAddressProvision), 5.36.5.3.2 (Type: EcsAddrInfo), and 5.36.5.3.4 (Type: EcsAddrInfoPatch).

questions.question: Which specifications define the eapMessage attribute in the UE authentication APIs?
questions.reference_answer: The eapMessage attribute in the UE authentication APIs is defined in TS 29.526, clauses 6.1.6.2.3 (Type: SliceAuthContext), 6.1.6.2.4 (Type: SliceAuthConfirmationData), 6.2.6.2.3 (Type: AuthContext), and 6.2.6.2.5 (Type: AuthConfirmationResponse).

questions.question: For MBS service information, where is the mbsServInfo attribute defined?
questions.reference_answer: The mbsServInfo attribute is defined in TS 29.537, clauses 6.1.6.2.2 (Type: MbsPolicyCtxtData), 6.1.6.2.11 (Type: MbsPolicyCtxtDataUpdate), 6.2.6.2.2 (Type: MbsAppSessionCtxt), and 6.2.6.2.3 (Type: MbsAppSessionCtxtPatch); it also appears in TS 29.571, clause 5.9.4.6, and TS 29.580, clause 6.2.6.2.3.

questions.question: Where is the resynchronizationInfo attribute used in authentication resynchronisation specified?
questions.reference_answer: The resynchronizationInfo attribute is specified in TS 29.503, clauses 6.3.6.2.10 (Type: HssAuthenticationInfoRequest) and 6.3.6.2.15 (Type: GbaAuthenticationInfoRequest); TS 29.509, clause 6.1.6.2.2 (Type: AuthenticationInfo); and TS 29.562, clause 6.3.6.2.2 (Type: SipAuthenticationInfoRequest). It contains RAND and AUTS used for authentication resynchronisation.

questions.question: Where is the BAP Address information element of the IAB architecture defined?
questions.reference_answer: The BAP Address IE is defined in TS 38.423 clause 9.2.2.89 (BAP Address, X2AP/Xn), and it also appears as an IE (clause 9.3.1.111) in the F1AP messages of TS 38.473: F1 SETUP REQUEST (9.2.1.4), F1 SETUP RESPONSE (9.2.1.5), GNB-DU CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE (9.2.1.8), and GNB-CU CONFIGURATION UPDATE (9.2.1.10).

questions.question: Tell me where the LCS to GCS Translation information element is described.
questions.reference_answer: The LCS to GCS Translation IE is defined in TS 38.455 clause 9.2.69, and it appears as a field within UL Angle of Arrival (9.2.38), UL-AoA assistance information (9.2.66), and Z-AoA (9.2.67) of TS 38.455. It is also defined as clause 9.3.1.241 of TS 38.473, appearing within UL-AoA Assistance Information (9.3.1.238) and Zenith Angle of Arrival Information (9.3.1.239).

questions.question: In which clauses is the NR A2X UE PC5 Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: The NR A2X UE PC5 Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE is defined as an optional IE (referencing the NR UE Sidelink Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate type, clause 9.3.1.148) in three TS 38.413 (NGAP) message definitions: UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST (9.2.2.7), PATH SWITCH REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE (9.2.3.9), and UE Context Information – Retrieve UE Context Response (9.2.1.13).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Available fast MCG recovery via SRB3 information element.
questions.reference_answer: The Available fast MCG recovery via SRB3 IE is defined in TS 36.423 (X2AP), appearing in the SGNB ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message (clause 9.1.4.2) and the SGNB MODIFICATION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message (clause 9.1.4.6).

questions.question: For NG-RAN positioning, where is the Ranging and Sidelink Positioning Service Information information element specified?
questions.reference_answer: The Ranging and Sidelink Positioning Service Information IE is defined in TS 38.413 (NGAP), appearing in INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST (9.2.2.1), UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST (9.2.2.7), HANDOVER REQUEST (9.2.3.4), and PATH SWITCH REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE (9.2.3.9), and it also appears in TS 38.473 (F1AP) in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message (9.2.2.1).

questions.question: Which documents specify the Redundant UL NG-U UP TNL Information information element?
questions.reference_answer: The Redundant UL NG-U UP TNL Information element (as UL NG-U UP TNL Information / Additional/Redundant NG-U UP TNL Information) is defined in TS 38.413, within the PDU Session Resource Setup Request Transfer (9.3.4.1), PDU Session Resource Modify Request Transfer (9.3.4.3), PDU Session Resource Modify Confirm Transfer (9.3.4.7), and Path Switch Request Acknowledge Transfer (9.3.4.9) IEs.

questions.question: Where is the RAN UE NGAP ID information element referenced in the 5GS procedures and in the 5G performance measurements?
questions.reference_answer: The RAN UE NGAP ID is referenced in the Namf_Communication_UEContextTransfer service operation of TS 23.502 (5.2.2.2.2), in the 5G registration charging information of TS 32.256 (6.2.1.2) and N2 connection charging information (6.2.1.3), in the UE Context Reference at Source IE of TS 36.413 (9.2.1.144), and in the HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message of TS 38.413 (9.2.3.5).

questions.question: Tell me where the RLC configuration information element of the LTE and NR RRC ASN.1 is defined.
questions.reference_answer: The RLC configuration IE is defined in TS 36.331 within the STCH configuration (9.1.1.6), and in TS 38.331 within the SCCH configuration (9.1.1.4), the STCH configuration (9.1.1.5), and the MTCH configuration for MBS broadcast (9.1.1.7).

questions.question: In which clauses is the EAS discovery filters information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: The EAS discovery filters IE is defined in TS 23.700-98 clause 8.5.3.2 (EAS discovery request), and it is also referenced in the EAS discovery subscription request table of TS 23.558 clause 8.5.3.4 and discussed in the RedEEC solution description of TS 23.700-98 clause 7.18.2.

questions.question: Where is the Application Group ID information element of the edge enabler architecture specified?
questions.reference_answer: The Application Group ID IE of the edge enabler architecture (TS 23.558) is defined/referenced in: Application Group profile (8.2.11), Retrieve EES request (8.8.4.6), Announce common EAS request (8.19.3.2, as part of the announcing procedure), EAS information get request (8.20.3.2), and Common EAS information store request (8.20.3.4).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Ad hoc group ID information element in the mission-critical common functional architecture.
questions.reference_answer: The Ad hoc group ID IE, in TS 23.280 (mission-critical common functional architecture), is defined in the Ad hoc group emergency alert request (10.10.3.2.2), Ad hoc group emergency alert response (10.10.3.2.3), Ad hoc group emergency alert cancel response (10.10.3.2.5), and Ad hoc group emergency alert participants list notification (10.10.3.2.6).

questions.question: For MCVideo, where is the Ambient viewing type information element defined?
questions.reference_answer: For MCVideo (TS 23.281), the Ambient viewing type IE is defined in the Ambient viewing call request (7.6.2.1), Ambient viewing call response (7.6.2.2), Ambient viewing call release response (7.6.2.4), and Ambient viewing call release notification (7.6.2.5).

questions.question: Which specifications define the Identity of the multicast/broadcast resource information element?
questions.reference_answer: The Identity of the multicast/broadcast resource IE is defined in TS 23.434, within the Multicast/broadcast resource response (14.3.2.41), Multicast/broadcast resource update request (14.3.2.42), Multicast/broadcast resource delete request (14.3.2.44), and Multicast/broadcast resource delete response (14.3.2.45).

questions.question: Where is the Data Collection Event ID information element of the ADAE flows specified?
questions.reference_answer: The Data Collection Event ID IE of the ADAE flows is defined in TS 23.436, within the Data collection subscription request (8.2.4.4), Data Notification (8.2.4.6), Network slice data retrieval request (8.7.4.5), Network slice data retrieval response (8.7.4.6), and Edge data collection subscription request (8.8.3.4).

questions.question: Tell me where the Notification Target URI information element of the SEAL service flows is described.
questions.reference_answer: The Notification Target URI/address IE of the SEAL service flows is described in TS 23.255 within the Subscribe real-time UAV status information request (7.5.3.2, as Notification URI), and in TS 23.434 within the Location area monitoring subscription request (9.3.2.14), Location area monitoring subscription modify request (9.3.2.17), and VAL service area subscription request (9.3.2.42).

questions.question: Where is the Acct-Session-Id RADIUS attribute used towards the AAA server defined?
questions.reference_answer: The Acct-Session-Id RADIUS attribute used towards the AAA server is defined in TS 29.061, within the Accounting-Request Interim-Update message (16.4.8) and the Disconnect-Request message (16.4.9).

questions.question: In which clauses is the Extended SRNC-ID information element of RNSAP defined?
questions.reference_answer: The Extended SRNC-ID IE of RNSAP (TS 25.423) is defined at clause 9.1.70 (ENHANCED RELOCATION REQUEST, referencing the Extended RNC-ID type at 9.2.1.50a) and referenced/used, with the plain SRNC-ID, in the FDD Message (9.1.3.1), TDD Message (9.1.3.2), and DOWNLINK SIGNALLING TRANSFER REQUEST (9.1.25).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the PSCell Information field of the charging records.
questions.reference_answer: The PSCell Information field of the charging records is defined in TS 32.251 within the PS Information structure (6.3.1.2), and in TS 32.256 within the Location Reporting charging information structure (6.2.1.4).

questions.question: Where is the Reference Time information element defined across the UTRAN RRC, PCAP and F1AP specifications?
questions.reference_answer: The Reference Time IE is referenced as part of the Additional GPS Assistance Data types requested, in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.88a (UE positioning GPS Additional Assistance Data Request) and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.128 (Additional GPS Assistance Data Required); it is separately defined as its own IE, carrying the ReferenceTimeInfo from TS 38.331, in TS 38.473 clause 9.3.1.149 (F1AP Reference Time).

questions.question: Which documents specify the Time Since Failure information element?
questions.reference_answer: The Time Since Failure IE is defined in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.132a (Connection Establishment Failure Report), and appears (as a field within the HO Report) in TS 38.413 clause 9.3.3.39 (HO Report) and TS 38.423 clause 9.1.3.17 (HANDOVER REPORT message).

questions.question: Which specifications enumerate the transport protocols an NF may use, and what options do they list?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.128 (7.3.3.2.33), TS 29.558 (8.1.5.3.5), TS 29.571 (5.4.3.38), and TS 29.510 (6.1.6.3.5) each define a TransportProtocol enumeration. TS 33.128 lists UDP and TCP; TS 29.558 lists QUIC, TCP, and TCP_TLS; TS 29.571 lists "UDP" and "TCP"; TS 29.510 lists only "TCP".

questions.question: Which specifications define the Cause enumeration, and what kinds of failure does each list?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.222 (8.5.4.3.3) defines a Cause enumeration for CAPIF authorization revocation with values OVERLIMIT_USAGE, UNEXPECTED_REASON, AUTHORIZATION_ISSUE, and OTHER_REASON. TS 29.502 (6.1.6.3.8) defines a Cause enumeration for SMF/PDU session release causes with a large set of values such as REL_DUE_TO_HO, EPS_FALLBACK, HO_FAILURE, REL_DUE_TO_SLICE_NOT_AVAILABLE, and many others. TS 24.543 (A.2.6.3) defines a Cause enumeration for VAL/SEALDD errors with values VAL CLIENT ERROR, SEALDD POLICY MISMATCH, and OTHER.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Cause information element and its coded values in legacy signalling?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.008 clause 10.5.4.11 defines the Cause information element for CC/MM signalling, coded per Q.931-derived classes (normal event, resource unavailable, service/option not available or not implemented, invalid message, protocol error, interworking) with values such as 1 Unassigned number, 16 Normal call clearing, 17 User busy, 31 Normal unspecified, 41 Temporary failure, 96 Invalid mandatory information, 111 Protocol error unspecified, and 127 Interworking unspecified. TS 24.011 clause 8.2.5.4 defines the RP-Cause element for SMS (RP-ERROR) with cause values such as 1 Unassigned number, 8 Operator determined barring, 21 Short message transfer rejected, 38 Network out of order, 41 Temporary failure, 81 Invalid short message transfer reference value, and 127 Interworking unspecified. TS 29.273 also defines two related Diameter cause AVPs: the IMEI-Check-In-VPLMN-Result (5.2.3.35) with values 0 Successful and 1 Illegal_ME, and the TWAN-S2a-Failure-Cause (5.2.3.31) with values such as 26 Insufficient resources, 27 Unknown APN, 29 User authentication failed, 38 Network failure, 50/51 PDN type IPv4/IPv6 only allowed, and 113 Multiple accesses to a PDN connection not allowed.

questions.question: Which documents specify the Event enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.122 (5.2.1.3.3) defines the Event enumeration for SCEF-reported events: SESSION_TERMINATION, LOSS_OF_BEARER, RECOVERY_OF_BEARER, RELEASE_OF_BEARER, USAGE_REPORT, FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION, SUCCESSFUL_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION. TS 29.522 (5.11.2.4.3) defines an Event enumeration for AF-provisioned service parameter outcomes: SUCCESS_UE_POL_DEL_SP and UNSUCCESS_UE_POL_DEL_SP. TS 29.580 (6.2.6.3.4) defines an Event enumeration for MBS User Data Ingest Session status events, including USER_DATA_ING_SESS_STARTING/STARTED/TERMINATED, DIST_SESS_STARTING/STARTED/TERMINATED/SERV_MNGT_FAILURE/POL_CRTL_FAILURE, DATA_INGEST_FAILURE, DELIVERY_STARTED, SESSION_STARTED/RELEASED/TERMINATED, DIST_SESS_ACTIVATED/EST_FAILURE, and USER_SER_AD.

questions.question: When a session or subscription ends, which specifications define the TerminationCause values?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.572 (6.1.6.3.20) defines TerminationCause with values TERMINATION_BY_UE, TERMINATION_BY_NETWORK, and NORMAL_TERMINATION. TS 29.514 (5.6.3.10) defines TerminationCause for the PCF's deletion of an Individual Application Session Context with values ALL_SDF_DEACTIVATION, PDU_SESSION_TERMINATION, PS_TO_CS_HO, INSUFFICIENT_SERVER_RESOURCES, INSUFFICIENT_QOS_FLOW_RESOURCES, and SPONSORED_DATA_CONNECTIVITY_DISALLOWED. TS 29.594 (5.6.3.3) defines TerminationCause for CHF subscription termination with the value REMOVED_SUBSCRIBER.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Priority enumeration, and say what each value means.
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.538 clause 8.2.5.3.5 defines Priority with HIGH, MIDDLE, and LOW (message sending priority). TS 29.435 clause 6.14.6.3.4 defines Priority as fault prioritization with CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, and IGNORE. TS 29.122 clause 5.7.2.2.4 defines Priority as a device trigger priority indication with NO_PRIORITY (no priority) and PRIORITY (has priority).

questions.question: After an authentication run completes, where are the AuthResult values defined?
questions.reference_answer: AuthResult values are defined in TS 29.509 (6.1.6.3.4): AUTHENTICATION_SUCCESS, AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE, AUTHENTICATION_ONGOING; in TS 29.256 (6.1.6.3.3): AUTH_SUCCESS and AUTH_FAIL for UAV authentication or C2 Authorization; and in TS 29.255 (5.1.6.3.3): AUTH_SUCCESS and AUTH_FAIL for UUAA or C2 authorization.

questions.question: The PduSessionStatus values report the state of a PDU session - in which specifications are they defined, and what states can a PDU session be in?
questions.reference_answer: PduSessionStatus is defined in TS 29.514 (5.6.3.24) with values ESTABLISHED and TERMINATED, in TS 29.519 (7.3.3.3) with values "ACTIVE" and "RELEASED", and in TS 29.508 (5.6.3.8) with values ACTIVATED and DEACTIVATED.

questions.question: Which documents specify the charging TriggerType values, and what kinds of trigger do they cover?
questions.reference_answer: Charging TriggerType values are specified in TS 32.291, twice: clause 6.2.5.3.5 covers CDR-level triggers such as FINAL, ABNORMAL_RELEASE, QOS_CHANGE, VOLUME_LIMIT, TIME_LIMIT, PLMN_CHANGE, HANDOVER_START/COMPLETE/CANCEL, and ATSSS access-change triggers; clause 6.1.6.3.6 covers Common/SMF/IMS/NSACF/MB-SMF triggers grouped by category, e.g. QUOTA_THRESHOLD, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, FORCED_REAUTHORISATION (Common Trigger), OTHER_QUOTA_TYPE, ECGI_CHANGE, VSMF_CHANGE, JOIN_MULTICAST (SMF Trigger), SIP_INVITE, SIP_BYE_MESSAGE (IMS Trigger), NSAC_THRESHOLD_INITIAL, NSAC_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED (NSACF Triggers), and MBS_CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED_WITH_NG-RAN (MB-SMF Trigger). TS 29.435 (6.2.6.3.4) defines a separate TriggerType with NETWORK_SLICE_LOAD, NETWORK_SLICE_PERFORMANCE, and QOE.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the ResultCode values, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: ResultCode values are defined in TS 29.558 (8.6.5.3.8) with ACCEPTED and REJECTED (for the ACT); and in TS 32.291, twice: clause 6.1.6.3.14 with SUCCESS, END_USER_SERVICE_DENIED, QUOTA_MANAGEMENT_NOT_APPLICABLE, QUOTA_LIMIT_REACHED, END_USER_SERVICE_REJECTED, RATING_FAILED, and QUOTA_MANAGEMENT (rating-group level charging results), and clause 6.2.5.3.6 with SUCCESS (the CHF opens or updates a CDR).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the MsgType values, and say what each value means.
questions.reference_answer: MsgType is defined in TS 29.486 (6.11.6.3.5) with values VAM, CAM, DENM, BSM, and CPM (V2X message types); and twice in TS 26.930: clause D.3.3 with values "bearer" and "basic" (authentication type), and clause D.3.1 with values "request" and "response" (message direction).

questions.question: A gNB-CU-CP has suspended a UE and later needs the context brought back to active state over NG. Which specifications define the UE CONTEXT RESUME REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The UE CONTEXT RESUME REQUEST message is defined in TS 38.413 (NGAP), sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF, and in TS 36.413 (S1AP), sent by the eNB to the MME; TS 29.502 clause 6.1.6.4.3 also references the related N2 SM Information IEs carried over NGAP.

questions.question: Which specifications define the UE CONTEXT RESUME FAILURE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The UE CONTEXT RESUME FAILURE message is defined in TS 38.413 (NGAP), sent by the AMF to the NG-RAN node when it cannot resume a PDU session; and in TS 36.413 (S1AP), sent by the MME to the eNB when it cannot resume an E-RAB (also described in TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.27 as sent by the MME).

questions.question: Before a UE is moved to a suspended state the core network must be told to keep its context. Which specifications define the UE CONTEXT SUSPEND REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The UE CONTEXT SUSPEND REQUEST message is defined in TS 38.413 (NGAP), sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF, and in TS 36.413 (S1AP), sent by the eNB to the MME; TS 29.502 clause 6.1.6.4.3 also references the related N2 SM Information IEs carried over NGAP.

questions.question: An MME wants to know whether the eNB and the UE have compatible radio capabilities for a voice service before it commits to it. Which specifications define the UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message is defined in TS 36.413 (S1AP), sent by the MME to the eNB, and in TS 25.413 (RANAP), sent by the SGSN to the RNC; TS 23.401 clause 5.11.2 also describes the related UE Radio Capability handling procedure over S1.

questions.question: When an eNB first brings up its TNL association towards the MME the two nodes exchange configuration data that is then kept for the life of the association. Which specifications define the S1 SETUP RESPONSE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The S1 SETUP RESPONSE message is defined in TS 36.413 (S1AP), sent by the MME to the eNB (also described in TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.8 and referenced by TS 33.128 for lawful-interception IEs derived from it, e.g. S1Information and MMEServedGUMMEIList/MMEServedGUMMEI).

questions.question: In which specifications is the E-RAB RELEASE COMMAND message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The E-RAB RELEASE COMMAND message is defined in TS 36.413 (S1AP), sent by the MME to the eNB (also described in TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.4.3); it is additionally referenced as a triggering event in the TS 32.425 performance measurement definitions for released/attempted E-RABs.

questions.question: Which specifications define the RAB RELEASE REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The RAB RELEASE REQUEST message is defined in TS 25.413 (RANAP) clause 8.3.2, sent by the RNC to the CN; it is also referenced (as a RANAP message relayed on the E-interface, sent 3G_MSC-I to 3G_MSC-A) in TS 29.108 clause 6, and cited in the TS 32.452 and TS 32.405 performance measurement clauses covering RAB Release Request.

questions.question: A Home NodeB has just come up and needs service from the HNB-GW before it can carry any traffic. Which specifications define the HNB REGISTER ACCEPT message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The HNB REGISTER ACCEPT message is defined in TS 25.469 (HNBAP) clause 8.2.2, sent by the HNB-GW to the HNB in response to the HNB's HNB REGISTER REQUEST (procedure also described in TS 25.467 clause 5.2.2, with the measurement overview in TS 32.452 clause 4.1.3.1).

questions.question: The HNB-GW performs access control and finds the Home NodeB is not allowed to register. Which specifications define the HNB REGISTER REJECT message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The HNB REGISTER REJECT message is defined in TS 25.469 (HNBAP) clause 8.2.3, sent by the HNB-GW to the HNB when the HNB cannot be registered (procedure also described in TS 25.467 clause 5.2.2, with the measurement overview in TS 32.452 clause 4.1.3.1).

questions.question: The gNB-CU-UP observes that a bearer has gone quiet and must tell the control plane so the UE can be released. Which specifications define the BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVITY NOTIFICATION message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVITY NOTIFICATION message is defined in TS 37.483 (E1AP), sent by the gNB-CU-UP to the gNB-CU-CP; the related state-transition procedure is also described in TS 38.401 clause 8.9.6.1, where the gNB-CU-UP sends it with inactivity monitoring results.

questions.question: A gNB-CU-CP needs an existing bearer context on the user plane node torn down. Which specifications define the BEARER CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The BEARER CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message is defined in TS 37.483 (E1AP) clause 8.3.5.2, sent by the gNB-CU-UP to the gNB-CU-CP; the related procedure is also described in TS 38.401 clause 8.9.3.2 as the gNB-CU-UP initiated bearer context release over F1-U.

questions.question: The AMF has to change the MBS service area of an ongoing broadcast session in the radio network. Which specifications define the BROADCAST SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The BROADCAST SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message is defined in TS 38.413 (NGAP) clause 8.17.2.2, sent by the AMF to the NG-RAN node; TS 29.518 clause 6.5.6.4.2.2 also references the related MBS Session Setup or Modification Request Transfer N2 IE (9.3.5.3) carried in this message.

questions.question: Which documents specify the BROADCAST SESSION MODIFICATION FAILURE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The BROADCAST SESSION MODIFICATION FAILURE message is defined in TS 38.413 (NGAP) clause 8.17.2.3, sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF when it fails to update the requested modification; TS 29.518 clause 6.5.6.4.2.2 also references the related MBS Session Setup or Modification Failure Transfer N2 IE (9.3.5.6) carried in this message.

questions.question: An AF wants to read back the 5G access stratum time distribution configuration it created at the TSCTSF. Which specifications describe the Ntsctsf_ASTI_Get service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.565 clause 5.4.2.1 lists Ntsctsf_ASTI_Get as allowing the NF service consumer (e.g. AF, NEF) to query the status of the 5G access stratum time distribution configuration, and clause 5.4.2.5.1 states it is used to retrieve the status of access stratum time distribution for a list of UEs. TS 23.502 clause 5.2.27.4.5 defines it as authorizing the request and querying the status of the access stratum time distribution, with required input a list of UE identities (GPSI or SUPI) and outputs an execution result plus optionally the ASTI status (active/inactive). TS 29.522 clause 4.4.24.3 and TS 29.513 clause 5.5.11.4 describe how the AF invokes the corresponding Nnef_ASTI_Get operation (via the NEF's "retrieve" custom HTTP POST operation), which the NEF maps onto Ntsctsf_ASTI_Get towards the TSCTSF.

questions.question: A CHF is asked to open a charging record for a session where only offline charging applies. Which specifications describe the Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Create service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.290 clause 6.5.2 defines Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Create as providing charging capabilities before service delivery: it opens a CDR in the CHF based on information from the NF Consumer (known consumers SMF, IMS-Node), requiring a subscriber identifier plus service identification or rating group, and returning a result indication. TS 32.291 clause 5.3.2.1 lists it as the operation for "Initial report of service usage", mapped to Charging Data Request/Response [Initial]; clause 5.3.2.2 describes the procedure: the NF (CTF) sends a Create request to the CHF to start charging, and on success the CHF returns "201 Created" with a Location header for the created resource; clause 6.2.3.1 describes the corresponding "Offline Only Charging Data" resource created by a POST to the Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging API.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that describe the Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Update service operation, and say what each one states about it.
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.290 clause 6.5.3 defines Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Update as providing charging capabilities during service delivery: if trigger conditions occur it may update the CDR or produce an interim CDR (known NF Consumer SMF), requiring a subscriber identifier (except for emergency sessions), session identifier and reporting reason, and returning a result indication. TS 32.291 clause 5.3.2.3 describes the procedure: the NF (CTF) sends an Update request to the CHF identifying the "Offline Only Charging Data" resource via {OfflineChargingDataRef} and includes the used service unit; on success a "200 OK" is returned. TS 32.291 clause 5.3.2.1 lists it as the operation for "Intermediate report of service usage", mapped to Charging Data Request/Response [Update]; clause 6.2.3.1 describes the corresponding "Individual Offline Only Charging Data" resource updated via the "update" custom POST operation.

questions.question: A UE has asked that its location be reported to an application function outside the operator network. Which specifications describe the Nnef_Location_LocationUpdateNotify service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.21.2 defines Nnef_Location_LocationUpdateNotify as providing UE location information to the consumer NF, requiring the AF identity, UE identifier (GPSI), the event causing the location estimate (5GC-MO-LR), the location estimate, its age, accuracy indication, and LCS QoS class, and returning a success/failure indication. TS 23.273 clause 8.5 states that for the 5GC-MO-LR procedure, if the UE requests to report its location to an AF, this is supported by the Nnef_Location_LocationUpdateNotify service operation (defined in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.21). TS 23.273 clause 6.2 describes the 5GC-MO-LR procedure in which the UE requests its location be sent to an LCS client or AF. TS 33.128 clause 7.7.2.1.1 states the IRI-POI in the NEF sends a SeparatedLocationReporting xIRI when it receives updated UE location information via the Nnef_Location_LocationUpdateNotify service operation destined for an external AF.

questions.question: An AF has to withdraw packet flow descriptions it previously provisioned for an application identifier. Which specifications describe the Nnef_PFDManagement_Delete service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.3.8 defines Nnef_PFDManagement_Delete: the consumer requests PFD management to delete the PFDs, with a required Transaction Reference ID input and no defined outputs. TS 28.552 clause 5.9.2.3.1 defines the measurement "Number of PFD deletion requests" (PFD.DeleteReq) triggered on receipt of an Nnef_PFDManagement_Delete Request by the NEF from the AF, and clause 5.9.2.3.2 defines "Number of successful PFD deletions" (PFD.DeleteSucc) triggered on transmission of an Nnef_PFDManagement_Delete Response indicating success. TS 23.700-81 clause 6.9.1 discusses PFD management context (AF providing PFDs per application ID to NEF/PFDF, distributed to SMFs/UPFs) without describing the Delete operation specifically.

questions.question: Which specifications describe the Nnef_PFDManagement_Subscribe service operation, and which consumer invokes it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.3.3 defines Nnef_PFDManagement_Subscribe: provided by the NEF (PFDF) for NF consumers to explicitly subscribe to notification of PFD changes for an Application Identifier, requiring the Application Identifier(s) as input. It is invoked by the NWDAF in TS 29.552 clause 5.7.17 and TS 23.288 clause 6.16.4 (the NWDAF subscribes to PFD notifications from the NEF(PFDF) to obtain PFD determination analytics), and by the SMF in TS 23.502 clause 4.18.3.2 (the SMF subscribes to PFD notifications from the NEF(PFDF) as a pre-requisite to receiving push notifications). TS 23.502 clause 4.18.2.1 also notes that SMFs subscribe to the PFD management service using Nnef_PFDManagement_Subscribe to receive PFDs provisioned by the AF.

questions.question: An SMS-SC has to hand a mobile-originated short message to the NEF for onward delivery. Which specifications describe the Nnef_SMService_MoForwardSm service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.541 clause 5.1 lists Nnef_SMService_MoForwardSm as a service operation of the Nnef_SMService service, with the SMS-SC as the example consumer. TS 23.540 clause 6.8.2.2 and TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.29.2 both define it identically: it transmits an MO SMS message from the consumer NF to the NEF, requiring SMS payload, Application port ID, SUPI, and the destination SME address (long/short code of the AF), and returning the SMS message transmission result. TS 23.540 clause 5.2.4 describes the MSISDN-less MO SMS procedure: the SMS-SC forwards the MO SM to the NEF by invoking Nnef_SMService_MoForwardSm, and the NEF responds with success/failure via the same operation's response.

questions.question: An AF has subscribed to learn whether time synchronization service is available for a group of UEs, and the capability then changes. Which specifications describe the Nnef_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.25.8 defines Nnef_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify: when the NEF receives a change notification from the TSCTSF, it forwards the notification to the subscribed AF via this operation (known consumer AF), per the parameters of clause 5.2.27.2.8, returning an operation execution result. TS 29.513 clause 5.5.11.3 states the Nnef_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify service operation indicates the list of UE identities per User-plane Node ID matching the requested time synchronization capabilities, following a prior Nnef_TimeSynchronization_CapsSubscribe. TS 23.502 clause 4.15.9.3.1 and TS 23.700-25 clause 6.14.3.1 both describe that the AF may receive a time synchronization service status update via the Nnef_TimeSynchronization_UpdateNotify/CapsNotify service operation, e.g. when a PTP port is activated/deactivated due to failure, degradation or improvement. TS 23.502 clause 4.15.9.2 and TS 29.513 clause 5.5.11.2 describe the broader exposure-of-UE-availability procedure in which capability notifications are generated.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus describe the Nnef_TimeSynchronization_ConfigDelete service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.25.4 defines Nnef_TimeSynchronization_ConfigDelete: the consumer requests deletion of the time synchronization configuration and deactivation of the corresponding service, for which the NEF authorizes the request and invokes the corresponding operation with the TSCTSF, returning an execution result indication. TS 23.502 clause 4.15.9.3.4 describes the deactivation procedure: the AF invokes Nnef_TimeSynchronization_ConfigDelete providing the PTP instance reference, the NEF invokes Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_ConfigDelete with the TSCTSF (which may also invoke it itself when UEs move outside the spatial validity condition), and the NEF/TSCTSF then respond. TS 23.502 clause 4.15.9.3.1 and TS 23.700-25 clause 6.14.3.1 both state the AF may deactivate the time synchronization service using Nnef_TimeSynchronization_ConfigDelete, which deletes the corresponding configuration. TS 23.502 clause 4.15.9.3.3 describes the related ConfigUpdate (modification) procedure. TS 29.513 clause 5.5.11.3 notes the AF may subscribe to status reports via ConfigCreate/ConfigUpdate and does not itself detail ConfigDelete beyond this context.

questions.question: An edge application has relocated and the NEF must inform the AF that subscribed to traffic influence. Which specifications describe the Nnef_TrafficInfluence_AppRelocationInfo service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.7.6 defines Nnef_TrafficInfluence_AppRelocationInfo: it forwards the acknowledgement to the notification of a UP path management event report to the SMF, requiring Notification Correlation Information and a cause code (positive/negative response), with optional N6 traffic routing information, an indication that uplink buffering should start, and EAS IP replacement information; clause 4.3.6.3 gives further usage details, e.g. for the uplink-buffering indication. TS 23.548 clause 6.3.3.2 describes that the AF may include Source and Target EAS IP address(es)/port(s) in the Nnef_TrafficInfluence_Create/Update or Nnef_TrafficInfluence_AppRelocationInfo request to support EAS IP replacement. TS 29.513 clause 5.5.3.3 describes the related Nnef_TrafficInfluence_Create/Update/Delete operations for AF traffic-influence requests without detailing AppRelocationInfo specifically.

questions.question: An NF service consumer wants to look up the UE parameters an AF previously provisioned in the UDM, such as Expected UE Behaviour. Which specifications describe the Nudm_ParameterProvision_Get service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.3.6.5 defines Nudm_ParameterProvision_Get: the consumer gets UE-related information (e.g. Expected UE Behaviour, Network Configuration parameters), requiring GPSI, AF Identifier and the requested information type, and returning the requested data plus an execution result indication. TS 28.552 clause 5.6.9.4.1 defines the measurement "Number of parameter getting requests" (PPV.GetReq) on receipt of an Nudm_ParameterProvision_Get request by the UDM from a consumer NF (e.g. NEF); clause 5.6.9.4.2 defines "Number of successful parameter gettings" (PPV.GetSucc) on a successful response; clause 5.6.9.4.3 defines "Number of failed parameter gettings" (PPV.GetFail.Cause) on a failed response. TS 33.893 clauses 6.3.2 and 6.3.3 discuss (as an alternative solution, not adopted) using Nudm_ParameterProvision_Get together with Namf_Location_ProvideLocationInfo for Ranging/SL Positioning authorization, noting this combination is not part of the defined SA2 LCS architecture.

questions.question: The PCF is asked to authorise policy for an MBS application session on behalf of an AF or MBSF. Which specifications describe the Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Create service operation, and what does each say about it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.2.3.2 defines Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Create: it authorizes the request and optionally determines/installs MBS Policy Control Data, requiring the MBS Session ID, with optional DNN, S-NSSAI, MBS Service Information, and a request-for-location-dependent-session flag; it returns success (application session context) or failure (with reason), and optionally an Area Session Policy ID or the acceptable MBS Service Information on failure. TS 29.537 clause 5.3.2.2.1 states this operation enables an NF service consumer (e.g. AF, NEF, MBSF) to request creation of an MBS Application Session Context at the PCF for MBS policy authorization of a multicast/broadcast session, supporting the MBS Application Session Context Establishment procedure; clause 5.3.2.1 lists it in the Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization service table as initiated by an NF service consumer (e.g. NEF, MBSF, AF). TS 29.513 clause 5.7.2 and TS 23.247 clause 7.1.1.3 describe the broader MBS Policy Association / MBS Session Creation with PCC procedures in which the AF/NEF/MBSF interacts with the PCF for MBS policy authorization.

questions.question: Tell me where the Nsmsf_SMService_Deactivate service operation is described, and which consumer invokes it in each.
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.9.2.3 defines Nsmsf_SMService_Deactivate: it removes SMS service authorization from the SMSF for a given service user, or (with Access Type included) removes connectivity for SMS over the affected Access Type, requiring SUPI (optionally Access Type), and returning the SMS service deactivation result. TS 23.502 clause 4.13.3.2 describes it being invoked by the AMF, during SMS-over-NAS deregistration, to trigger release of the UE Context for SMS on the SMSF for the impacted Access Type(s). TS 29.524 clause 4.1 notes that no HTTP-to-5GMM-cause mapping is required for the Nsmsf_SMService_Deactivate operation (among others) as described in TS 29.540.

questions.question: Which specifications define the DAPS Indicator information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The DAPS Indicator IE is defined identically (as "DAPS Request Information") in TS 36.413 (9.2.1.155), TS 36.423 (9.2.154), TS 37.483 (9.3.1.91), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.188), and TS 38.423 (9.2.1.33). In each it is a Mandatory IE coded as ENUMERATED (DAPS HO required, ...), indicating that DAPS Handover (DAPS HO) is requested for the concerned E-RAB (in TS 36.413/36.423) or DRB (in TS 37.483/38.413/38.423).

questions.question: Where is the Integrity Protection Indication information element defined, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Integrity Protection Indication IE is defined within the Security Indication IE in TS 36.413 (9.2.1.163), TS 36.423 (9.2.181), TS 37.483 (9.3.1.23), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.27), and TS 38.423 (9.2.3.52). In each it is Mandatory and coded as ENUMERATED (required, preferred, not needed, ...), indicating whether UP integrity protection shall/should/shall not apply for the concerned E-RAB (TS 36.413/36.423), PDU Session Resource or E-RAB depending on CP-UP separation (TS 37.483), or PDU session (TS 38.413/38.423). TS 37.483, TS 38.413 and TS 38.423 additionally pair it with a Confidentiality Protection Indication IE and a conditional Maximum Integrity Protected Data Rate IE (present if Integrity Protection Indication is "required" or "preferred").

questions.question: A QoS flow is delay critical and the network needs to state how many packets it may lose before the service breaks. Which specifications define the Packet Loss Rate information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Packet Loss Rate IE is defined in TS 36.413 (9.2.1.130), TS 36.423 (9.2.124), TS 37.483 (9.3.1.46), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.79), and TS 38.423 (9.2.3.11). In each it is Mandatory and coded as INTEGER(0..1000) (with a trailing extension marker in the 37.483/38.413/38.423 versions), representing the ratio of lost packets per number of packets sent, expressed in tenths of a percent.

questions.question: The RAN wants to know the terminal model without being able to identify the individual handset. Which specifications define the Masked IMEISV information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Masked IMEISV IE is defined in TS 36.413 (9.2.3.38), TS 36.423 (9.2.69), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.54), TS 38.423 (9.2.3.32), and TS 38.473 (9.3.1.55). In each it is Mandatory and coded as BIT STRING (SIZE(64)), holding the IMEISV value (as defined in TS 23.003) with the last 4 digits of the SNR masked by setting the corresponding bits to 1 (the first to fourth bits correspond to the first digit, the fifth to eighth to the second digit, and so on), so the RAN can identify the terminal model without identifying the individual Mobile Equipment.

questions.question: Which documents specify the Delay Critical information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Delay Critical IE, part of the Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE, is defined in TS 37.473 (9.3.1.36), TS 37.483 (9.3.1.28), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.18), TS 38.423 (9.2.3.9), and TS 38.473 (9.3.1.47). In each it is Conditional (present if GBR QoS Flow Information is present in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE, condition ifGBRflow) and coded as ENUMERATED (delay critical, non-delay critical, ...), indicating whether the GBR QoS flow is delay critical as specified in TS 23.501; when set to "delay critical" the accompanying Maximum Data Burst Volume IE must also be included.

questions.question: A guaranteed bit rate flow is being set up and the target node must be told the bit rate it has to reserve in the downlink. Which specifications define the Guaranteed Flow Bit Rate Downlink information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Guaranteed Flow Bit Rate Downlink IE, part of the GBR QoS Flow Information IE, is defined in TS 37.473 (9.3.1.35), TS 37.483 (9.3.1.30), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.10), TS 38.423 (9.2.3.6), and TS 38.473 (9.3.1.46). In each it is Mandatory and typed as Bit Rate, representing the guaranteed bit rate (provided there is data to deliver) in the downlink, as detailed in TS 23.501.

questions.question: Tell me where the GBR QoS Flow Information information element is defined, and how it is coded in each.
questions.reference_answer: The GBR QoS Flow Information IE, referenced from the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE, is defined in TS 37.473 (9.3.1.34, referencing GBR QoS Flow Information at 9.3.1.35), TS 37.483 (9.3.1.26, referencing 9.3.1.30), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.12, referencing 9.3.1.10), TS 38.423 (9.2.3.5, referencing 9.2.3.6), and TS 38.473 (9.3.1.45, referencing 9.3.1.46). In each specification it is Optional within QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters, and shall be present only for GBR QoS Flows (ignored otherwise); its own content (Maximum/Guaranteed Flow Bit Rate Downlink/Uplink, plus Maximum Packet Loss Rate Downlink/Uplink and, depending on spec, Notification Control or Alternative QoS Parameters Set List) is typed with the Bit Rate and Packet Loss Rate IE types as detailed in TS 23.501.

questions.question: A TSC QoS flow can tolerate a bounded gap in successfully delivered messages before the application fails. Which specifications define the Survival Time information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Survival Time IE is defined in TS 37.483 (9.3.1.103), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.221), TS 38.423 (9.2.3.152), and TS 38.473 (9.3.1.231). In each it is Mandatory and coded as INTEGER(0..1920000, ...), expressed in units of 1 microsecond, indicating the Survival Time of a TSC QoS flow as defined in TS 23.501.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Battery Indication information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Battery Indication IE, part of the (Subscription Based) UE Differentiation Information IE, is defined in TS 36.413 (9.2.1.140), TS 36.423 (9.2.136), and TS 38.413 (9.3.1.144). In each it is Optional and coded as ENUMERATED (battery powered, battery powered not rechargeable or replaceable, not battery powered, ...): "battery powered" means the UE has a rechargeable/replaceable battery, "battery powered not rechargeable or replaceable" means the battery cannot be recharged or replaced, and "not battery powered" means the UE is not battery powered. TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.3 defines it at the service level as one of the Expected UE Behaviour parameters, identifying power-consumption criticality for the UE with the same three categories, without ASN.1-style coding.

questions.question: For UE differentiation towards an MTC device, where is the Traffic Profile attribute inside the UE Differentiation Information defined and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Traffic Profile attribute of the UE Differentiation Information is defined as a table row inside the Subscription Based UE Differentiation Information IE in TS 36.413 (9.2.1.140) and TS 36.423 (9.2.136), coded as ENUMERATED(single packet, dual packets, multiple packets, …); and inside the UE Differentiation Information IE in TS 38.413 (9.3.1.144), coded the same way as ENUMERATED (single packet, dual packets, multiple packets, …). “Single packet” indicates single packet transmission (UL or DL), “dual packets” indicates dual packet transmission (UL with subsequent DL, or DL with subsequent UL), and “multiple packets” indicates multiple packets transmission.

questions.question: M7 measurement collection has to be configured with the same period whether it is set over S1, X2, NG, Xn or F1. Which specifications define the M7 Collection Period information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The M7 Collection Period IE is defined inside the M7 Configuration IE in TS 36.413 (9.2.1.102), TS 36.423 (9.2.88), TS 38.413 (9.3.1.175), TS 38.423 (9.2.3.132), and TS 38.473 (9.3.1.154). In all five specifications it is coded identically as a Mandatory INTEGER (1..60, …) with unit minutes.

questions.question: An MBMS bearer service is only to be delivered inside a defined geographical region. Which specifications define the MBMS Service Area information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS Service Area IE is defined in TS 25.413 (9.2.3.41), TS 36.443 (9.2.3.6), and TS 36.444 (9.2.3.6). In all three it is coded as a Mandatory OCTET STRING consisting of a list of one or several MBMS Service Area Identities, with the value part coded per the MBMS Service Area AVP defined in TS 29.061.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the MBMS Session Identity information element, and how is it coded in each?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS Session Identity IE is defined in TS 25.413 (9.2.3.38), TS 36.443 (9.2.3.4), and TS 36.444 (9.2.3.4). In all three it is coded as a Mandatory OCTET STRING (SIZE (1)), coded the same way as the MBMS Session Identity IE defined in TS 29.061, and identifies the session of an MBMS Bearer Service so the UE can recognise repetitions of that session; it is transparent to RAN.

questions.question: A CAPIF API provider has to advertise how much compute its edge deployment still has spare. Which specifications define the Available Compute information element, and how is it described in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Available Compute information element appears as part of the Service KPIs structure in TS 23.222 (8.3.2.1, Table 8.3.2.1-2), TS 23.558 (8.2.5, Table 8.2.5-1) as part of EAS Service KPIs, and TS 28.538 (5.2.2, Table 5.2.2-1) as part of Edge Application Server Service KPIs. In all three it is an optional (O) element described as "The maximum compute resource available for the API Invoker/AC/Application Client".

questions.question: A PCF has to tell the AMF exactly which events should cause the policy association to be re-evaluated, such as a tracking area change or the UE entering a presence reporting area. Which specifications define the RequestTrigger enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The RequestTrigger enumeration is defined in TS 29.525 (5.6.3.3) and TS 29.507 (5.6.3.3). TS 29.525 lists (among others): LOC_CH, PRA_CH, UE_POLICY, PLMN_CH, CON_STATE_CH, GROUP_ID_LIST_CHG, UE_CAP_CH, SAT_CATEGORY_CHG. TS 29.507 lists (among others): LOC_CH, PRA_CH, SERV_AREA_CH, RFSP_CH, ALLOWED_NSSAI_CH, UE_AMBR_CH, SMF_SELECT_CH, ACCESS_TYPE_CH, UE_SLICE_MBR_CH, NWDAF_DATA_CH, TARGET_NSSAI, SLICE_REPLACE_MGMT, FEAT_RENEG, PARTIALLY_ALLOWED_NSSAI_CH, SNSSAIS_PARTIALLY_REJECTED_CH, REJECTED_SNSSAIS_CH, PENDING_NSSAI_CH.

questions.question: An NF service consumer retrieving subscription data from the UDM must name which data set it wants, for example access and mobility data or SMS subscription data. Which specifications define the DataSetName enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The DataSetName enumeration is defined in TS 29.562 (6.2.6.3.3), for the IMS User Profile, with values "CHARGING_DATA", "IFC_DATA", "TRACE_DATA", "PRIORITY_DATA"; and in TS 29.503 (6.1.6.3.3), with values "AM", "SMF_SEL", "UEC_SMF", "UEC_SMSF", "SMS_SUB", "SM", "TRACE", "SMS_MNG", "LCS_PRIVACY", "LCS_MO", "LCS_SUB", "UEC_AMF", "V2X", "LCS_BCA", "PROSE", "UC", "MBS", "A2X", "RANGINGSL_PRIVACY".

questions.question: An LCS client must declare which geographic area shapes it can interpret before the LMF returns a position. Which specifications define the SupportedGADShapes enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The SupportedGADShapes enumeration is defined in TS 24.546 (C.1.4.5.1) with values POINT, POINT_UNCERTAINTY_CIRCLE, POINT_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSE, POLYGON, POINT_ALTITUDE, POINT_ALTITUDE_UNCERTAINTY, ELLIPSOID_ARC, LOCAL_2D_POINT_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSE, LOCAL_3D_POINT_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSOID; and in TS 29.572 (6.1.6.3.4) with the same nine values plus "DISTANCE_DIRECTION", "RELATIVE_2D_LOCATION_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSE", and "RELATIVE_3D_LOCATION_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSOID".

questions.question: Which specifications define the HttpMethod enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The HttpMethod enumeration is defined in TS 29.571 (5.2.3.4) and TS 29.573 (6.1.5.3.4). Both list the same nine values: "GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "OPTIONS", "HEAD", "CONNECT", "TRACE".

questions.question: The UDM has to tell an old AMF why the UE is being deregistered there, for instance because a new AMF now serves the UE after an initial registration. Which specifications define the DeregistrationReason enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The DeregistrationReason enumeration is defined in TS 29.503 (6.2.6.3.3) with values "UE_INITIAL_REGISTRATION", "UE_REGISTRATION_AREA_CHANGE", "SUBSCRIPTION_WITHDRAWN", "5GS_TO_EPS_MOBILITY", "5GS_TO_EPS_MOBILITY_UE_INITIAL_REGISTRATION", "REREGISTRATION_REQUIRED", "SMF_CONTEXT_TRANSFERRED", "DUPLICATE_PDU_SESSION", "PDU_SESSION_REACTIVATION_REQUIRED", "DISASTER_CONDITION_TERMINATED", "OPERATOR_DETERMINED_BARRING", "DUPLICATE_PDU_SESSION_EPDG"; and in TS 29.563 (6.3.6.3.3) with values "UE_INITIAL_AND_SINGLE_REGISTRATION", "UE_INITIAL_AND_DUAL_REGISTRATION", "EPS_TO_5GS_MOBILITY", "EPS_TO_5GS_MOBILITY_WITHOUT_N26_IWK".

questions.question: Analytics output has to classify the terminal behind a session as a smartphone, a dongle, a WLAN router or an IoT device. Which specifications define the DeviceType enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The DeviceType enumeration is defined in TS 29.520 (5.1.6.3.31) with values MOBILE_PHONE, SMART_PHONE, TABLET, DONGLE, MODEM, WLAN_ROUTER, IOT_DEVICE, WEARABLE, MOBILE_TEST_PLATFORM, UNDEFINED; and in TS 24.558 (6.2.5.3.4), with a different meaning (device resource constraint), with values CONSTRAINED_UE and NORMAL_UE.

questions.question: An AF describing a media component to the PCF must say whether it carries audio, video, data, control or text. Which specifications define the MediaType enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The MediaType enumeration is defined in TS 29.514 (5.6.3.3) with values AUDIO, VIDEO, DATA, APPLICATION, CONTROL, TEXT, MESSAGE, OTHER; and in TS 29.175 (6.1.6.3.4) with values "DC" (data channel), "AUDIO", "VIDEO".

questions.question: A monitoring event subscription is refused because the AF is not allowed to monitor that event type or the subscriber lacks the subscription. Which specifications define the FailedCause enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The FailedCause enumeration is defined in TS 29.503 (6.4.6.3.12) with values "AF_NOT_ALLOWED", "MTC_PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED", "MONITORING_NOT_ALLOWED", "UNSUPPORTED_MONITORING_EVENT_TYPE", "UNSUPPORTED_MONITORING_REPORT_OPTIONS", "UNSPECIFIED"; and in TS 29.563 (6.4.6.3.5) with the same values except it omits "AF_NOT_ALLOWED": "MTC_PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED", "MONITORING_NOT_ALLOWED", "UNSUPPORTED_MONITORING_EVENT_TYPE", "UNSUPPORTED_MONITORING_REPORT_OPTIONS", "UNSPECIFIED".

questions.question: An AF provisioning expected UE behaviour must state whether the device does a single uplink packet transmission or a dual transmission. Which specifications define the TrafficProfile enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The TrafficProfile enumeration is defined in TS 29.122 (5.10.2.3.7) and TS 29.571 (5.4.3.25). Both list the same five values: SINGLE_TRANS_UL (uplink single packet transmission), SINGLE_TRANS_DL (downlink single packet transmission), DUAL_TRANS_UL_FIRST (dual packet transmission, uplink first then downlink), DUAL_TRANS_DL_FIRST (dual packet transmission, downlink first then uplink), and MULTI_TRANS (multiple packet transmission).

questions.question: Which documents specify the AuthType enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The AuthType enumeration is defined in TS 29.509 (6.1.6.3.3) with values 5G_AKA, EAP_AKA_PRIME, EAP_TLS, EAP_TTLS; and in TS 29.503 (6.3.6.3.3) with values "EAP_AKA_PRIME", "5G_AKA", "EAP_TLS", "NONE", "EAP_TTLS".

questions.question: An LCS request has to state how precise a position fix the client needs before the LMF chooses a positioning method. Which specifications define the LocationAccuracy enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The LocationAccuracy enumeration is defined in TS 29.503 (6.4.6.3.4) with values "CELL_LEVEL", "RAN_NODE_LEVEL", "TA_LEVEL", "N3IWF_LEVEL", "UE_IP", "UE_PORT"; and in TS 29.563 (6.4.6.3.4) with only three values: "CELL_LEVEL", "RAN_NODE_LEVEL", "TA_LEVEL".

questions.question: In which specifications is the RedirectAddressType enumeration defined, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The RedirectAddressType enumeration is defined in TS 29.512 (5.6.3.12) with values IPV4_ADDR, IPV6_ADDR, URL, SIP_URI; and in TS 32.291 (6.1.6.3.8) with values IPV4, IPV6, URL, URI.

questions.question: The core network must report whether the UE is inside or outside a presence reporting area, or that the state is unknown. Which specifications define the PresenceState enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The PresenceState enumeration is defined in TS 29.571 (5.4.3.20) with values "IN_AREA", "OUT_OF_AREA", "UNKNOWN", "INACTIVE"; and in TS 33.128 (7.3.3.2.69), where it is derived from the TS 29.571 type, with the corresponding values inArea(1), outOfArea(2), unknown(3), inactive(4).

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the MeasurementType enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The MeasurementType enumeration is defined in TS 29.571 (5.6.3.23) for 5GC UE level measurements trace, with values including "GTP_DELAYDLPSAUPFUEMEAN_SNSSAI_QFI", "GTP_DELAYULPSAUPFUEMEANEXCD1_SNSSAI_QFI", "GTP_DELAYDLPSAUPFUEMEANINCD1_SNSSAI_QFI", "GTP_DELAYULPSAUPFNGRANMEAN_SNSSAI_QFI", "GTP_DELAYDLPSAUPFNGRANMEAN_SNSSAI_QFI"; and in TS 29.564 (6.1.6.3.5) with values "VOLUME_MEASUREMENT", "THROUGHPUT_MEASUREMENT", "APPLICATION_RELATED_INFO".

questions.question: An AM policy association is being torn down and the PCF has to give the reason, for example that the UE is deregistered or the policy is no longer applicable. Which specifications define the PolicyAssociationReleaseCause enumeration, and what values does each list?
questions.reference_answer: The PolicyAssociationReleaseCause enumeration is defined in TS 29.525 (5.6.3.4) with values UNSPECIFIED (unspecified reasons), UE_SUBSCRIPTION (the subscription of UE has changed, e.g. was removed), and INSUFFICIENT_RES (the server is overloaded and needs to abort the policy association); and in TS 29.507 (5.6.3.4) with the same three values UNSPECIFIED, UE_SUBSCRIPTION, and INSUFFICIENT_RES, worded for terminating the session instead of the policy association.

questions.question: A random access attempt on the CCCH can be turned down rather than granted a channel. Which specifications define the IMMEDIATE ASSIGNMENT REJECT message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The IMMEDIATE ASSIGNMENT REJECT message is defined in TS 48.058, where it is one of three immediate assign message types (IMMEDIATE ASSIGNMENT, IMMEDIATE ASSIGNMENT EXTENDED, IMMEDIATE ASSIGNMENT REJECT) carried in the Full Imm. Assign Info IE (9.3.35) of the IMMEDIATE ASSIGN COMMAND message sent from the BSC to the BTS (8.5.6); the BTS then transmits the message as received, or builds it from the contents of two or more IMMEDIATE ASSIGN COMMAND messages (5.7), for transmission on the downlink CCCH to the mobile station.

questions.question: A Node B detects that a radio link it was maintaining has broken down and must report the loss upward. Which specifications define the RADIO LINK FAILURE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The RADIO LINK FAILURE message is sent by the Node B, as described in TS 25.433 (8.3.3.3, 8.3.14.3), which initiates/triggers the Radio Link Failure procedure and rejects the procedure using the RADIO LINK FAILURE message (e.g. with cause value "Invalid CM Settings") when reconfiguration or compressed-mode conditions are not met. TS 52.402 (B.2.1.20, B.2.1.27) separately defines measurements (nbrOfLostRadioLinksTCH, nbrOfLostRadioLinksSDCCH) counting local end releases at the BTS due to a "RADIO LINK FAILURE", but that is a measurement definition, not the message definition.

questions.question: The MSC needs to learn how much spare capacity a particular cell still has before it commits traffic to it. Which specifications define the RESOURCE INDICATION message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The RESOURCE INDICATION message is defined in TS 48.008 (3.2.1.18), where it is sent from the BSS to the MSC in response to a RESOURCE REQUEST message, including an explicit indication of the cell concerned; and in TS 23.924 (5.6.3.2.5), where it is likewise sent from the BSS to the MSC in response to a resource request message, and on receipt the SNSF node broadcasts it to all MSC Servers.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the RESOURCE REQUEST message, and say which node sends it in each.
questions.reference_answer: The RESOURCE REQUEST message is defined in TS 48.008 (message list at 3.2, individual definition at 3.2.1.17) and in TS 23.924 (5.6.3.2.5). In both, it is sent from the MSC to the BSS, requesting the current spare and optionally the total accessible resource on a particular cell; per TS 23.924, on receipt the SNSF node transfers this message to the destination BSC.

questions.question: Where is the NSSAI DELETE RESPONSE message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The NSSAI DELETE RESPONSE message is defined in TS 38.509 (5.7.1) and TS 38.508-1 (4.7A.6, 4.9.35). In both, it is sent from the UE to the SS (network) — in TS 38.508-1 specifically embedded in an RRC ULInformationTransfer message — confirming deletion of the requested NSSAI information after receiving a NSSAI DELETE REQUEST message.

questions.question: An eNB and a relay node have to agree which handover path to take, and the serving MME identity travels with the request. Which specifications define the S1 HANDOVER REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The S1 HANDOVER REQUEST message is discussed in TS 36.300 (4.7.6.6, 4.6.2), where the DeNB/HeNB GW forwards or informs about it during handover to/from an RN, and in TS 33.401 (7.2.4a/J.1.2, 7.2.8.4.3), which specifies it is sent by the target MME to the target eNB, carrying the {NH, NCC} pair and (for unauthenticated UEs in LSM) the UE EPS security capabilities restricted to EIA0/EEA0.

questions.question: The SYSTEM TO E-UTRAN HANDOVER COMMAND message crosses an inter-system boundary - in which specifications is it defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The INTER SYSTEM TO E-UTRAN HANDOVER COMMAND message is referenced in TS 45.010 (6.13a) as received by the MS from GSM per TS 44.018, and in TS 48.008 (3.1.5a.3), where the old BSS sends an intersystem handover command radio interface message (e.g. INTER SYSTEM TO UTRAN HANDOVER COMMAND or INTER SYSTEM TO E-UTRAN HANDOVER COMMAND) to the MS after receiving the BSSMAP HANDOVER COMMAND from the MSC; TS 36.523-1 test cases confirm the UE receives this message when performing GERAN-to-E-UTRA handover.

questions.question: The NEF has just been told by the UDR that an AF changed its traffic influence request, and it must pass that on to whoever subscribed. Which specifications define the Nnef_TrafficInfluenceData_Notify service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_TrafficInfluenceData_Notify service operation is defined in TS 29.591 (4.4.2.1, 4.4.2.4.1) and TS 23.502 (5.2.6.35.4). It is initiated by the NEF to notify the NF service consumer about subscribed Traffic Influence Data, specifically when the NEF receives AF traffic influence request information from UDR. Per TS 23.502, required inputs are Notification Correlation ID, Data Set Identifier, Target of Event Reporting, and AF traffic influence request information; required output is Result Indication.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Nnef_TrafficInfluenceData_Subscribe service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_TrafficInfluenceData_Subscribe service operation is defined in TS 29.591 (4.4.2.1, 4.4.2.2.2) and TS 23.502 (5.2.6.35.2). It is used by an NF service consumer (e.g. SMF) to explicitly subscribe to notification of Traffic Influence Data; the request carries the notification URI, notification correlation identifier, DNN and/or S-NSSAI identifications, and optionally target UE identification(s), any-UE indication, HPLMN identification, UE address(es), and reporting requirements. Per TS 23.502, required inputs are Data Set Identifier, Data Subset Identifier, Data Key(s), Notification Target Address, and Event Reporting Information; on acceptance the required output is a Subscription Correlation ID.

questions.question: After a device trigger has been pushed towards a UE, the delivery outcome has to be reported back to the requesting application. Which specifications define the Nnef_Trigger_DeliveryNotify service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_Trigger_DeliveryNotify service operation is defined in TS 23.502 (5.2.6.5.3), where the NEF reports the status (failure or success) of the trigger delivery to the consumer, carrying Transaction Reference ID and Delivery Report as required inputs; it is also referenced in TS 33.128 (7.7.3.1.5) and TS 28.552 (5.9.1.4), which describe the NEF sending it to the AF with the GPSI of the target UE and a delivery result value (e.g. SUCCESS, UNKNOWN, FAILURE, TRIGGERED, EXPIRED, UNCONFIRMED, REPLACED, TERMINATE).

questions.question: A visited NRF that only knows one configured address needs to discover the full set of NRF service instances and their endpoints. Which specifications define the Nnrf_Bootstrapping_Get service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnrf_Bootstrapping_Get service operation is defined in TS 23.502 (5.2.7.5.2, 4.17.13) and TS 29.510 (5.5.2.1). It is sent by an NF service consumer (e.g. a visited NRF/v-NRF) to the configured address of the Bootstrapping Service instance with no required inputs; the NRF responds with the NRF service instances and their endpoint addresses (required output), optionally also NF Set ID, NRF instance ID, OAuth2 requirement for authorization, and NRF status, and can additionally indicate hPLMN authorization capability (per TS 33.875, 6.24.2).

questions.question: An AF no longer wants the access and mobility policy authorization it previously asked the PCF for. Which specifications define the Npcf_AMPolicyAuthorization_Unsubscribe service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Npcf_AMPolicyAuthorization_Unsubscribe service operation is defined in TS 29.534 (4.2.1, 4.2.6.1, 5.3.1) and TS 23.502 (5.2.5.8.7). It allows an NF service consumer (e.g. AF, NEF, TSCTSF) to remove an existing subscription to event(s) for an AF application AM context, invoked via HTTP DELETE to the AM Policy Events Subscription sub-resource. Per TS 23.502, the required input is Subscription Correlation ID, and the required output is Success or Failure.

questions.question: The PCF learns from the NWDAF that network performance in the area of interest has dropped below the operator criteria and has to warn the consumer of the background data transfer policy. Which specifications define the Npcf_BDTPolicyControl_Notify service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Npcf_BDTPolicyControl_Notify service operation is defined in TS 29.554 (4.2.1, 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.2) and TS 23.502 (5.2.5.5.4). It is initiated by the PCF to send a BDT (background data transfer) warning notification to the NF service consumer when network performance in the area of interest, as learned from the NWDAF, drops below the criteria set by the operator. Per TS 23.502, the required input is the Background data transfer reference ID, with optional inputs Network Area Information, Time window, and list of candidate Background Data Transfer policies; there are no required or optional outputs.

questions.question: An MB-SMF is tearing down a multicast session and wants the associated policy association and its resources removed. Which specifications define the Npcf_MBSPolicyControl_Delete service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Npcf_MBSPolicyControl_Delete service operation is defined in TS 29.537 (5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.4.1) and TS 23.247 (9.2.2.4). It is invoked by the NF service consumer (e.g. MB-SMF) to request deletion of an existing MBS Policy Association and its associated resources (via HTTP DELETE to the Individual MBS Policy resource). Per TS 23.247, the required input is the MBS Policy Association ID, and the required output is Success or Failure.

questions.question: Which documents specify the Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageUnsubscribe service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageUnsubscribe service operation is referenced in TS 29.513 (5.6.3.1.1, 5.6.3.1.2, 5.6.3.1.3, 5.6.3.2.1), which points to its full definition in TS 29.518 [32] (not itself in gold). It is invoked by the PCF towards the AMF, sent as an HTTP DELETE to the URI of the N1N2 Individual Subscription resource, to unsubscribe from notifications of the N1 message for UE Policy Delivery Result, during UE Policy Association termination (both non-roaming and roaming cases).

questions.question: An interworking deployment keeps subscriber data in an HSS rather than a UDM, and a consumer still needs to be told when subscription events occur. Which specifications define the Nhss_EventExposure_Subscribe service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nhss_EventExposure_Subscribe service operation is referenced in TS 29.505 (5.2.19E.1, 5.2.31B.1, 5.4.2.30) and TS 23.632 (5.6.2), which point to its full definition in TS 29.562 [20] (not itself in gold). It is invoked by the UDM to subscribe to a monitoring event at the HSS for interworking deployments where subscriber data is kept in HSS rather than UDM; the HSS returns a Subscription Id (allocated by the HSS) in the HTTP Location header of the response, which the UDM stores in the UDR.

questions.question: An NEF is provisioning influence on access and mobility handling on behalf of an application function for the first time. Which specifications define the Nnef_AMInfluence_Create service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_AMInfluence_Create service operation is defined in TS 23.502 (5.2.6.23.2) and referenced in TS 29.513 (5.5.10.3) and TS 23.502 (4.15.6.9.3). It is invoked by the AF to the NEF (HTTP POST to the AM Influence Subscription resource) to provide a new request to influence access and mobility management policies for one or multiple UEs. Required input is AF Transaction Id; optional inputs include list of (DNN, S-NSSAI) pairs, Target (GPSI, External Group Identifier(s), any UE, or any inbound roaming UEs by PLMN ID), throughput/service coverage requirements, policy duration, list of External Application Identifiers, and subscribed event(s); the required output is an operation execution result indication. The NEF authorizes the request, maps GPSI to SUPI (and External to Internal Group Identifier), and stores the AM influence data in the UDR.

questions.question: Group message delivery over MBS has been attempted and the application needs to know how it went. Which specifications define the Nnef_MBSGroupMsgDelivery_StatusNotify service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_MBSGroupMsgDelivery_StatusNotify service operation is defined in TS 23.247 (9.4.4.4) and TS 29.522 (4.4.29.7.5). It is used by the NEF to notify a previously subscribed AF/NF service consumer of the status of a previously submitted MBS Group Message Delivery, sent as an HTTP POST to the AF's notification URI. Per TS 23.247, required inputs are Status Information and Notification Endpoint; there are no required or optional outputs (the AF replies with HTTP 204 No Content).

questions.question: Tell me where the Nnef_NIDDConfiguration_Create service operation is defined, and what it carries.
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_NIDDConfiguration_Create service operation is defined in TS 23.502 (5.2.6.13.2, 4.25.3). It is invoked by the consumer (typically the AF) to request NIDD Configuration between the NF consumer and the NEF to support Non-IP Data Delivery via the NEF. Required inputs are GPSI or External Group Identifier, AF Identifier, T8 Destination Address, and MTC Provider Information; optional inputs are Reliable Data Service Configuration, Requested Action, TLTRI, and NIDD Duration. Required outputs are TLTRI, Reliable Data Service Indication, Maximum Packet Size, and Cause; optional output is NIDD Duration.

questions.question: A primary NSACF has recalculated how many registered UEs a slice may hold locally and must push the new figure to the other NSACFs. Which specifications define the Nnsacf_NSAC_LocalNumberUpdate service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnsacf_NSAC_LocalNumberUpdate service operation is defined in TS 23.502 (5.2.21.2.6, 4.2.11.6) and referenced in TS 23.501 (5.15.11.2.2, 5.15.11.1.2). It is invoked by the Primary NSACF towards NSACF(s) to update the local maximum number of registered UEs and/or PDU sessions of a network slice at any time, based on current registered UE/PDU session numbers and operator policy. Required inputs are S-NSSAI and the updated local number(s); the required output is a result indication.

questions.question: A consumer has stopped using an ML model and no longer wants its accuracy tracked by the NWDAF that trained it. Which specifications define the Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Deregister service operation, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Deregister service operation is defined in TS 29.520 (4.7.2.1, 4.7.2.3.1, 4.7.2.3.2) and TS 23.288 (7.9.6). It is invoked by the NF service consumer (i.e. NWDAF containing AnLF) towards the NWDAF containing MTLF, via an HTTP DELETE request to the Individual NWDAF ML model monitoring registration resource, to delete a registration of the use or monitoring capability of the analytics accuracy of an ML Model — e.g. when the consumer is no longer using or monitoring that accuracy. Per TS 23.288, the required input is the ML Model monitoring registration ID, with optional inputs a termination indication, termination cause, and the NWDAF containing AnLF NF ID of the target NWDAF (if the cause is analytics transfer); there are no required or optional outputs.

questions.question: Which specifications define the GBR QoS Information information element, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The GBR QoS Information IE is defined in TS 36.423 (Table for E-RAB Level QoS Parameters, 9.2.9), TS 36.463 (E-RAB Level QoS Parameters, 9.2.19), TS 37.473 (E-UTRAN QoS, 9.3.1.19), TS 37.483 (E-UTRAN QoS, 9.3.1.17), and TS 38.473 (E-UTRAN QoS, 9.3.1.19). In each, it is an optional field referenced by its own sub-clause (9.2.10 in TS 36.423; 9.2.21 in TS 36.463; 9.3.1.21 in TS 37.473; 9.3.1.19 in TS 37.483; 9.3.1.21 in TS 38.473) that applies to GBR bearers only and is ignored otherwise.

questions.question: In which specifications is the Local Home Network ID information element defined, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Local Home Network ID IE (also called LHN ID) is defined in TS 25.413 (Table in clause 9.2.1.123, identifying the LHN ID of the RNC), TS 36.413 (Table in clause 9.2.1.92, identifying the LHN ID of the eNB), and TS 36.423 (Table in clause 9.2.83, identifying the LHN ID of the eNB). In all three, it is coded as a Mandatory OCTET STRING (SIZE(32..256)).

questions.question: Tell me where the MBS Session ID IE is defined, and in which table it is specified in each.
questions.reference_answer: The MBS Session ID field/IE is defined in the MBS subchannel control specific data fields table of TS 24.380 (Table 8.6.3.1-1, Field ID 001), TS 24.581 (Table 9.5.3.1-1, Field ID 001), and TS 24.582 (Table 11A.2.3.1-1, Field ID 001); it also appears as an information element in the MBS Session Charging Information structure of TS 32.279 (Table 6.2.1.2-1, category M).

questions.question: Two MBS sessions can carry byte-identical user data, and the RAN has to be told they belong together without interpreting the contents. Which specifications define the Associated Session ID IE, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Associated Session ID IE is defined in TS 37.483 (Table for clause 9.3.3.38), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.262), and TS 38.473 (Table for clause 9.3.1.309). In all three it is a Mandatory OCTET STRING coded as the AssociatedSessionId defined in TS 29.571, used to associate MBS Session IDs providing identical user data; the receiving node (gNB-CU-UP, gNB, gNB-DU respectively) does not interpret its content.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Expected Activity Period information element, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Expected Activity Period IE is defined within the Expected UE Activity Behaviour IE in TS 36.413 (Table for clause 9.2.1.97), TS 36.423 (Table for clause 9.2.71), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.94), and TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.3.82). In all four, it is an Optional INTEGER (1..30|40|50|60|80|100|120|150|180|181, ...) where value 181 means the expected activity time is longer than 180 seconds, and other values indicate the expected activity time in seconds.

questions.question: Which documents specify the Expected HO Interval IE, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Expected HO Interval IE is defined within the Expected UE Behaviour IE in TS 36.413 (Table for clause 9.2.1.96), TS 36.423 (Table for clause 9.2.70), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.93), and TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.3.81). In all four, it is an Optional ENUMERATED (sec15, sec30, sec60, sec90, sec120, sec180, long-time, ...) indicating the expected time interval between inter-eNB/inter-NG-RAN-node handovers; 'long-time' means the interval is expected to be longer than 180 seconds.

questions.question: The NR Encryption Algorithms information element is carried over several RAN interfaces - in which specifications is it defined, and in which table is it specified in each?
