questions.reference_answer: The NR Encryption Algorithms IE is defined within the (NR) UE Security Capabilities IE in TS 36.413 (Table for clause 9.2.1.127), TS 36.423 (Table for clause 9.2.107), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.86), and TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.3.49). In all four, it is a Mandatory BIT STRING (SIZE(16, ...)) bitmap where the all-zero value means the UE supports no other NR algorithm than NEA0, and successive bits indicate support for 128-NEA1, 128-NEA2, 128-NEA3, with remaining bits mapped from octets of the UE (Additional) Security Capability IE.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the NR Integrity Protection Algorithms IE, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The NR Integrity Protection Algorithms IE is defined within the (NR) UE Security Capabilities IE in TS 36.413 (Table for clause 9.2.1.127), TS 36.423 (Table for clause 9.2.107), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.86), and TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.3.49). In all four, it is a Mandatory BIT STRING (SIZE(16, ...)) bitmap where the all-zero value means the UE supports no other NR algorithm than NIA0, and successive bits indicate support for 128-NIA1, 128-NIA2, 128-NIA3, with remaining bits mapped from octets of the UE (Additional) Security Capability IE.

questions.question: A location estimate can be delivered as a street address rather than as coordinates, encoded as a PIDF-LO document. Which specifications define the Civic Address IE, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Civic Address IE is defined in TS 25.413 (Table for clause 9.2.3.59) and TS 29.171 (Table 7.4.32-1). In both, it is an Optional OCTET STRING containing a UTF-8 encoded PIDF-LO XML document as defined in IETF RFC 4119, restricted to a civic address using the namespaces "urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:pidf:geopriv10:civicAddr" (RFC 5139) and "...civicAddr:ext" (RFC 6848).

questions.question: Which specifications define the DL TNL Available Capacity information element, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The DL TNL Available Capacity IE is defined within the TNL (Available) Capacity Indicator IE in TS 36.423 (Table for clause 9.2.161), TS 37.483 (Table for clause 9.3.1.72), TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.2.49), and TS 38.473 (Table for clause 9.3.1.128). In all four, it is a Mandatory INTEGER (0..100, ...) indicating the available downlink transport-network capacity as a percentage, where value 100 corresponds to the (maximum) offered capacity.

questions.question: For RAN load reporting between nodes, where is the Composite Available Capacity Downlink IE defined and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Composite Available Capacity Downlink IE is defined within the (NR/E-UTRAN) Composite Available Capacity Group IE in TS 36.423 (Table for clause 9.2.44, Composite Available Capacity Group, and Table for clause 9.2.163, NR Composite Available Capacity Group), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.196, E-UTRAN Composite Available Capacity Group), TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.2.51, Composite Available Capacity Group), and TS 38.473 (Table for clause 9.3.1.130, Composite Available Capacity Group). In each, it is a Mandatory field of type Composite Available Capacity referencing the corresponding sub-IE clause (e.g. 9.2.45 in TS 36.423, 9.3.1.197 in TS 38.413, 9.2.2.52 in TS 38.423, 9.3.1.131 in TS 38.473), giving the overall available resource level for the Downlink.

questions.question: In which specifications is the HO Cause Value information element defined, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The HO Cause Value IE is defined within the Last Visited (UTRAN/E-UTRAN/NG-RAN) Cell Information IE in TS 25.413 (Table for clause 9.2.1.83), TS 36.413 (Table for clause 9.2.1.43a), TS 36.423 (Table for clause 9.2.40), and TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.97). In all four, it is an Optional field of type Cause referencing the corresponding Cause sub-clause (9.2.1.4 in TS 25.413, 9.2.1.3 in TS 36.413, 9.2.6 in TS 36.423, 9.3.1.2 in TS 38.413), indicating the cause for the (outgoing) handover/relocation.

questions.question: Which documents specify the N6 Jitter Lower Bound information element, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The N6 Jitter Lower Bound IE is defined within the N6 Jitter Information IE in TS 37.483 (Table for clause 9.3.1.144), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.265), TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.3.204), and TS 38.473 (Table for clause 9.3.1.320). In all four, it is a Mandatory INTEGER (-127..127, ...) indicating the lower bound of the N6 jitter, in units of 0.5 ms.

questions.question: Which specifications define the M6 Report Amount information element, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The M6 Report Amount IE is defined within the M6 Configuration IE in TS 37.483 (Table for clause 9.3.1.87), TS 38.413 (Table for clause 9.3.1.174), TS 38.423 (Table for clause 9.2.3.131), and TS 38.473 (Table for clause 9.3.1.153). In all four, it is an Optional ENUMERATED (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, infinity, ...) indicating the number of reports.

questions.question: Every service based interface implementation has to agree on which HTTP headers it must be able to process, whatever the payload. Which specifications define the Content-Encoding header field, and in which table is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Content-Encoding HTTP header field is defined as a mandatory-to-support standard header in TS 29.500 (Table 5.2.2.2-1, request headers, per IETF RFC 9110) and in TS 29.573 (Table 4.3.2.2-2, response headers on the N32 interface, per IETF RFC 9110). It may be used to indicate the content encodings (e.g. gzip) applied to the resource/response body beyond those inherent in the media type.

questions.question: A location request can ask for where the UE is now, or settle for the last position the network happened to record. Which specifications enumerate the values of LocationType, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The LocationType enumeration is defined in TS 29.518 (6.4.6.3.3) with values "CURRENT_LOCATION" (current location of the target UE required), "CURRENT_OR_LAST_KNOWN_LOCATION" (current or last known location required), "NOTIFICATION_VERIFICATION_ONLY" (notification/verification required but no location estimate), and "DEFERRED_LOCATION" (deferred location request); and in TS 29.122 (5.3.2.4.5) with values CURRENT_LOCATION (SCS/AS requests notification for current location), LAST_KNOWN_LOCATION (notification for last known location), CURRENT_OR_LAST_KNOWN_LOCATION (AF requests current or last known location), and INITIAL_LOCATION (AF requests the initial location).

questions.question: An application tells the core whether its traffic only ever flows towards the device, only away from it, or both. Which specifications enumerate the values of ScheduledCommunicationType, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The ScheduledCommunicationType enumeration is defined in TS 29.571 (5.4.3.23) with values "DOWNLINK_ONLY", "UPLINK_ONLY", and "BIDIRECTIONAL"; and in TS 29.122 (5.10.2.3.8A) with values DOWNLINK, UPLINK, and BIDIRECTIONAL — in both cases meaning downlink only, uplink only, and bi-directional traffic respectively.

questions.question: Analytics about congestion have to distinguish whether the strain is on signalling or on the traffic itself. Which specifications enumerate the values of CongestionType, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The CongestionType enumeration is defined in TS 29.520 (5.1.6.3.8) with values USER_PLANE, CONTROL_PLANE, and USER_AND_CONTROL_PLANE (congestion analytics type is User Plane, Control Plane, or both); and in TS 29.122 (5.9.2.3.3), with a different meaning (abstracted congestion status), with values HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW.

questions.question: Which specifications enumerate the values of PositioningMode, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The PositioningMode enumeration is defined in TS 29.572 (6.1.6.3.7) with values "UE_BASED" (UE-based mode), "UE_ASSISTED" (UE-assisted mode), and "CONVENTIONAL" (Conventional mode); and in TS 33.128 (7.3.3.2.53), derived from the TS 29.572 type, with the corresponding values uEBased(1), uEAssisted(2), and conventional(3).

questions.question: A positioning result has to state plainly whether the accuracy the requester asked for was actually achieved. Which specifications enumerate the values of AccuracyFulfilmentIndicator, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The AccuracyFulfilmentIndicator enumeration is defined in TS 29.572 (6.1.6.3.12) with values "REQUESTED_ACCURACY_FULFILLED" (requested accuracy is fulfilled) and "REQUESTED_ACCURACY_NOT_FULFILLED" (requested accuracy is not fulfilled); and in TS 33.128 (7.3.3.2.51), derived from the TS 29.572 type, with the corresponding values requestedAccuracyFulfilled(1) and requestedAccuracyNotFulfilled(2).

questions.question: Subscription data can be watched for a change in the handset behind an IMSI, and the operator may or may not care about a bare software version bump. Which specifications enumerate the values of AssociationType, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The AssociationType enumeration is defined in TS 29.503 (6.4.6.3.6) with values "IMEI_CHANGE" (report if the IMSI-IMEI association changed; a bare Software Version change alone is not reported) and "IMEISV_CHANGE" (report if the IMSI-IMEI or IMSI-SV association, or both, changed, including when only the SV changed); and in TS 29.122 (5.3.2.4.6), with values IMEI (detect change of IMSI-IMEI association) and IMEISV (detect change of IMSI-IMEISV association).

questions.question: Session continuity can break down because the UE moved between two standalone non-public networks, or because no home-routed agreement exists. Which specifications enumerate the values of ReleaseCause, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The ReleaseCause enumeration is defined in TS 29.518 (6.1.6.3.25) with values "SNPN_SNPN_MOBILITY" (PDU Session continuity cannot be supported between networks due to SNPN-SNPN mobility), "NO_HR_AGREEMENT" (continuity cannot be supported due to inter-PLMN mobility where no HR agreement exists), and "UNSPECIFIED" (unspecified reasons); and in TS 29.541 (6.1.6.3.5), with a different meaning (cause for release of the SM Context in the NEF), with the value "PDU_SESSION_RELEASED" (the SM Context is released because the corresponding PDU Session is released).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the values of PolicyType, and say what each value means.
questions.reference_answer: The PolicyType enumeration is defined in TS 29.549 (7.4.1.4.3.6) with values LOWEST_COST (policy guidance considers lowest cost) and HIGH_THROUGHPUT_WITH_COST (policy guidance considers highest throughput); and in TS 29.435 (6.3.6.3.3), with a different meaning (network slice/UE session policy type), with values MAX_NUM_PDU_SESS (maximum number of PDU Sessions), MAX_NUM_UE (maximum number of UEs), SLICE_LOAD_PREDICTION (network slice load prediction), TIME_PERIOD_AND_AVG_QOS (time period and average QoS per UE), and TIME_PERIOD_AND_MIN_QOS (time period and minimum QoS per UE).

questions.question: A PCF request can be rejected because the PCC rules it carried could not be installed at all, in which case retrying is pointless. Which specifications enumerate the values of FailureCause, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The FailureCause enumeration is defined in TS 29.512 (5.6.3.14) with values PCC_RULE_EVENT (some PCC rules cannot be installed/activated; request should not be retried), PCC_QOS_FLOW_EVENT (some PCC rules cannot be enforced/modified now but might succeed later), RULE_PERMANENT_ERROR (PCC and/or session rules cannot be installed/activated; do not retry), RULE_TEMPORARY_ERROR (PCC and/or session rules cannot be enforced/modified now but might succeed later), and POL_DEC_ERROR (policy decisions cannot be provisioned in the NF service consumer); and in TS 29.515 (6.1.5.3.7), with a different meaning (positioning failure cause), with values "POSITIONING_DENIED", "UNSUPPORTED_BY_UE", "NOT_REGISTED_UE", and "UNSPECIFIED".

questions.question: A UE that is not expected to move at all can be handled differently from one that roams, so its stationarity has to be stated. Which specifications enumerate the values of StationaryIndication, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: The StationaryIndication enumeration is defined in TS 29.571 (5.4.3.21) and TS 29.122 (5.10.2.3.4). Both list the same two values: STATIONARY (identifies the UE is stationary) and MOBILE (identifies the UE is mobile).

questions.question: Admission control for a slice can be applied strictly at every request or relaxed to a periodic reconciliation. Which specifications enumerate the values of NsacAdmissionMode, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.536 and TS 29.503 enumerate NsacAdmissionMode. Both define "VPLMN_ADMISSION" (VPLMN NSAC admission mode) and "VPLMN_WITH_HPLMN_ASSISTANCE" (VPLMN with HPLMN assistance NSAC admission mode); TS 29.503 additionally defines "HPLMN_ADMISSION" (HPLMN NSAC admission mode).

questions.question: Whether a subscriber reached the core over 3GPP radio or over an untrusted non-3GPP path changes how the session is treated. Which specifications enumerate the values of AccessType, and what does each value mean?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.128 and TS 29.571 enumerate AccessType. TS 33.128 defines threeGPPAccess(1) (3GPP access), nonThreeGPPAccess(2) (Non-3GPP access), and threeGPPandNonThreeGPPAccess(3) (3GPP and Non-3GPP access); TS 29.571 defines "3GPP_ACCESS" (3GPP access) and "NON_3GPP_ACCESS" (Non-3GPP access).

questions.question: When several NF service consumers each hand the NEF a set of IPv4 addresses, the same attribute has to mean the same thing in every API. Which specifications define the ipv4Addrs attribute, and in which type is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: ipv4Addrs is defined in: TS 29.122 in type UpLocRepAddrAfRm; TS 29.503 in type PcscfAddress; TS 29.520 in type AddressList; TS 29.558 in type EndPoint; and TS 29.591 in type TrafficInfluDataSub.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the precedence attribute, and in which type is it specified in each?
questions.reference_answer: The precedence attribute is defined in: TS 29.502 in type TrafficInfluenceData; TS 29.512 in types PccRule and UeInitiatedResourceRequest; TS 29.522 in type RouteSelectionParameterSet; TS 29.537 in type MbsPccRule; and TS 29.556 in type DnsRule.

questions.question: Where is the sNssaiList attribute defined, and which data type carries it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The sNssaiList attribute is defined in: TS 29.503 in type DataRestorationNotification; TS 29.504 in type DataRestorationNotification; TS 29.510 in type PlmnSnssai; TS 29.531 in type RestrictedSnssai; and TS 29.571 in type SnssaiDnnItem.

questions.question: An RNC has asked a GSM BSS to reserve radio resources for a relocation, and the BSS answers once the preparation is finished. Which specifications define the ENHANCED RELOCATION RESOURCE RESPONSE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 43.130 and TS 25.423 define the ENHANCED RELOCATION RESOURCE RESPONSE message. In TS 43.130 (Iur-g) it is sent by the TBSS to the SRNS in response to the ENHANCED RELOCATION RESOURCE REQUEST. In TS 25.423 (RNSAP) it is sent by the BSS to the RNC as the successful outcome of the Enhanced Relocation Resource Allocation procedure.

questions.question: A mobile station requests a channel and the very first layer-3 message it piggybacks already carries its identity, so the BSS can pass it straight to the MSC. Which specifications define the IMMEDIATE SETUP message, and in which interface direction does it travel?
questions.reference_answer: TS 48.006 and TS 48.008 define the IMMEDIATE SETUP message as one of the initial Layer 3 messages an MS sends (piggybacked on the SABM frame) to the BSS, which the BSS forwards to the MSC in a COMPLETE LAYER 3 INFORMATION / COMPLETE L3 INFORMATION message. TS 27.007 also lists IMMEDIATE SETUP 2 as a value of the <message> parameter for the +COTDI AT command.

questions.question: Which specifications define the NR SIDELINK PACKET COUNTER REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.509 and TS 38.508-1 define the UE TEST LOOP NR SIDELINK PACKET COUNTER REQUEST message (also referred to as NR SIDELINK COUNTER REQUEST/NR SIDELINK PACKET COUNTER REQUEST). It is sent by the network side (SS/NR-SS acting as the network, i.e. the NR-NW) to the UE to request the UE to report its NR sidelink PSCCH/STCH/PSSCH packet counters.

questions.question: A GPRS mobile station contends for uplink resources on the PRACH with a one-phase or single-block access cause. Which specifications define the PACKET CHANNEL REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 52.402, TS 43.246, and TS 43.051 define the PACKET CHANNEL REQUEST message. It is sent by the mobile station (MS) on the PRACH, e.g. with a one-phase or single-block access establishment cause (including "Single Block MBMS Access"), to the BSS/BSC/network to request uplink packet channel resources.

questions.question: The network offers to activate a PDP context and the MS turns it down with a cause such as 'insufficient resources'. Which specifications define the REQUEST PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION REJECT message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.008, TS 24.007, and TS 31.111 define the REQUEST PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION REJECT message. In all cases it is sent by the MS to the network, rejecting a network-requested PDP context activation (e.g. REQUEST PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION message) with a cause such as insufficient resources (#26), activation rejected unspecified (#31), feature not supported (#40), or a protocol error (#95-111).

questions.question: A peer RAN node cannot bring up any of the cells or SSB beams it was asked to switch on, so it answers with a cause value instead. Which specifications define the CELL ACTIVATION FAILURE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 (XnAP) and TS 36.423 (X2AP) define the CELL ACTIVATION FAILURE message. In TS 38.423 it is sent by the NG-RAN node2 to NG-RAN node1 when it cannot activate any of the requested cells or SSB beams; in TS 36.423 it is sent by eNB2 to eNB1 when it cannot activate any of the requested cells, each with an appropriate cause value.

questions.question: A CRNC needs a Node B to shift its cell timing using a frame adjustment value carried over the Node B Control Port. Which specifications define the CELL SYNCHRONISATION ADJUSTMENT REQUEST message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.433 (NBAP) defines the CELL SYNCHRONISATION ADJUSTMENT REQUEST message, sent by the CRNC to the Node B over the Node B Control Port to instruct it to adjust its SFN/frame timing (e.g. via the Frame Adjustment Value IE). TS 25.402 also describes this message as being sent by the RNC to the cells to update their timing during the synchronisation procedure.

questions.question: Which documents specify the DATA FORWARDING ADDRESS INDICATION message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 (X2AP) defines the DATA FORWARDING ADDRESS INDICATION message. It is sent by the new eNB to the old eNB to indicate forwarding addresses for E-RABs; in Conditional Handover/Dual Connectivity/EN-DC scenarios it is also sent MeNB to en-gNB or MeNB to SeNB.

questions.question: A BSS asks an SMLC for a location estimate for a target MS, and the same message is reused to carry a TA Layer 3 BSSLAP APDU. Which specifications define the BSSMAP-LE PERFORM LOCATION REQUEST message, and over which interface?
questions.reference_answer: TS 49.031 defines the BSSMAP-LE PERFORM LOCATION REQUEST message, sent from the BSS to the SMLC over the Lb interface to request a location estimate for a target MS (also used to carry the TA Layer 3 BSSLAP APDU, per TS 48.071).

questions.question: A cell broadcast entity has ordered an ongoing CBS broadcast to be stopped, and the radio-side node confirms once every service area or cell has ceased broadcasting. Which specifications define the KILL COMPLETE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 48.049 (CBSP) and TS 25.419 (SABP) define the KILL COMPLETE message. In TS 48.049 it is sent by the BSC to the CBC indicating a successful Kill procedure, once broadcasting has stopped in the cells listed in the Cell List IE / Number of Broadcasts Completed List IE. In TS 25.419 it is sent by the RNC to the CN once all indicated Service Areas have successfully stopped the CBS broadcast.

questions.question: Tell me where the LOAD QUERY COMPLETE message is defined, and which node sends it in each.
questions.reference_answer: TS 48.049 (CBSP) and TS 25.419 (SABP) define the LOAD QUERY COMPLETE message. In TS 48.049 it is sent by the BSC to the CBC in response to a LOAD QUERY message, reporting the CBCH radio resource load. In TS 25.419 it is sent by the RNC to the CN, reporting the available bandwidth of the Service Area(s).

questions.question: Where is the MESSAGE STATUS QUERY COMPLETE message defined, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 48.049 (CBSP) and TS 25.419 (SABP) define the MESSAGE STATUS QUERY COMPLETE message. In TS 48.049 it is sent by the BSC to the CBC, reporting the number of broadcasts completed per cell. In TS 25.419 it is sent by the RNC to the CN, reporting the number of broadcasts completed per Service Area.

questions.question: Which specifications define the MCE CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.444 (M3AP) and TS 36.443 (M2AP) define the MCE CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message. In TS 36.444 it is sent by the MME to the MCE when the MME cannot accept the update. In TS 36.443 it is sent by the eNB to the MCE when the eNB cannot accept the update. Both may include a Time To Wait IE.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the POSITIONING ACTIVATION FAILURE message, and say which node sends it in each.
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.455 (NRPPa) and TS 38.473 (F1AP) define the POSITIONING ACTIVATION FAILURE message. In TS 38.455 it is sent by the NG-RAN node when it is unable to activate (or trigger aperiodic) UL SRS transmission in the UE. In TS 38.473 it is sent by the gNB-DU for the same reason.

questions.question: An NF instance is about to shut down gracefully and wants the NRF to stop advertising it. Which service operation does it invoke, and which specifications define that operation?
questions.reference_answer: It invokes the Nnrf_NFManagement_NFDeregister service operation, defined in TS 23.502 (clause 5.2.7.2.4, NF Service Deregistration procedure). TS 23.700-62 and TS 23.228 also describe its use (e.g. UPF or P-CSCF deregistering from the NRF).

questions.question: A consumer needs to add, modify or delete terminations and medias inside an already established media context on the MF. Which specifications define the Nmf_MRM_Update service operation, and which NF consumes it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.228 defines the Nmf_MRM_Update service operation (used by a consumer NF to add, modify, or delete terminations and/or media streams within an existing media resource context on the MF); TS 29.176 also specifies it, describing its use for updating existing media resources within a media context on the MF.

questions.question: The MB-SMF has to tell subscribed consumers that the state of an MBS session, or of the part of it inside one service area, has changed. Which specifications define the Nnef_MBSSession_StatusNotify service operation, and what are its required inputs?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 defines the Nnef_MBSSession_StatusNotify service operation, used by the MB-SMF (via NEF/MBSF) to notify subscribed NF service consumers of events related to an MBS session or, for a location-dependent session, the part within a service area. Its required inputs are Status Information and MBS Session ID (Area Session ID is optional).

questions.question: A consumer that had been receiving PFD change notifications no longer wants them. Which specifications define the Nnef_PFDmanagement_Unsubscribe service operation, and which resource does it act on?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.551 defines the Nnef_PFDmanagement_Unsubscribe service operation, used by an NF service consumer to unsubscribe from PFD change event notifications. It acts on the "Individual PFD subscription" resource (/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}), deleting the subscription via HTTP DELETE.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Nnef_UCMFProvisioning_Delete service operation, and which NF invokes it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_UCMFProvisioning_Delete service operation, invoked by the consumer (e.g. an AF) via the NEF to delete a UCMF dictionary entry for a Manufacturer-assigned UE Radio Capability ID, by providing the UE Radio Capability ID(s) or IMEI/TAC value(s) to be deleted.

questions.question: An AMF wants to be told whenever the S-NSSAI availability per tracking area changes because another AMF updated it. Which specifications define the Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Subscribe service operation?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 defines the Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Subscribe service operation, which lets an NF service consumer (e.g. AMF) subscribe to notifications of changes in NSSAI availability information (S-NSSAIs and restricted S-NSSAIs per TA) when updated by another AMF.

questions.question: An RE-NWDAF has collected data about roaming UEs and must push it to the consumer that subscribed. Which specifications define the Nnwdaf_RoamingData_Notify service operation, and which NF initiates it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.520 and TS 23.288 define the Nnwdaf_RoamingData_Notify service operation, which is initiated by the RE-NWDAF to notify the NF service consumer about the subscribed data of roaming UEs.

questions.question: A consumer already holding a TSC application session context wants to add event subscriptions to it without recreating the context. Which specifications define the Ntsctsf_QoSandTSCAssistance_Subscribe service operation?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.565 and TS 23.502 define the Ntsctsf_QoSandTSCAssistance_Subscribe service operation, which lets an NF service consumer create (via HTTP PUT) or modify a subscription to events for an existing TSC application session context without recreating it.

questions.question: Where is the Nudr_DM_Delete service operation defined, and which NF invokes it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 (clause 5.2.12.2.4) defines the Nudr_DM_Delete service operation, invoked by an NF service consumer to delete user data (e.g. an application data record) stored in the UDR.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Nupf_EventExposure_Unsubscribe service operation, and which NF invokes it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 and TS 23.700-62 define the Nupf_EventExposure_Unsubscribe service operation. It is invoked by the NF consumer (or the SMF on behalf of another NF) to unsubscribe from an event notification at the UPF.

questions.question: When the schedule of active periods ends, the MBSF has to tell the MBSTF to deactivate the distribution sessions it is carrying. Which specifications define the Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession_Update service operation?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.502 defines the Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession_Update service operation, used e.g. by the MBSF to update an existing MBS Distribution Session (such as updating its state to DEACTIVATING) at the end of its scheduled active period.

questions.question: A consumer NF has a UE Radio Capability ID and a coding format, and needs the actual UE Radio Access Capability and the UE Radio Capability for Paging behind it. Which specifications define the Nucmf_UECapabilityManagement_Resolve service operation, and which HTTP method carries it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.673 and TS 23.502 define the Nucmf_UECapabilityManagement_Resolve service operation, which lets a consumer NF obtain the UE Radio Access Capability and UE Radio Capability for Paging for a given UE Radio Capability ID and Coding Format. It is carried by the HTTP GET method.

questions.question: An AF needs previously allocated TMGIs released again through the NEF. Which specifications define the Nnef_MBSTMGI_Deallocate service operation, and what does the request body carry?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.522 and TS 23.247 define the Nnef_MBSTMGI_Deallocate (stage-3 Nnef_MBSTMGI_Deallocation) service operation. The request body (TmgiDeallocRequest) carries the "afId" attribute (identifier of the requesting AF) and the "tmgis" attribute (the list of MBS TMGI(s) to be deallocated).

questions.question: Which documents specify the Nnef_IPTVconfiguration_Create service operation, and which NF invokes it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.316 and TS 29.513 specify the Nnef_IPTVconfiguration_Create service operation, which is invoked by the AF (via the NEF) to request IPTV configuration information for a UE or group of UEs.

questions.question: Tell me where the Nucmf_UECapabilityManagement_Notify service operation is defined, and which NF invokes it.
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 (clause 5.2.18.3.5) defines the Nucmf_UECapabilityManagement_Notify service operation, invoked by the producer NF (UCMF) to notify a subscribed consumer NF about changes in the UCMF.

questions.question: An assistance-data message has to carry the instant in BDS system time, taken modulo 3600 seconds, at which the ionospheric grid information is valid. Which specifications define the BDS Reference Time information element, and what value range does it take?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.331, TS 25.423, TS 25.433, and TS 25.453 define the BDS Reference Time IE (within the BDS Ionospheric Grid Model IE). It is an INTEGER ranging from 0 to 3570 in steps of 30 (seconds), indicating the time in BDS system time, modulo 3600 s, at which the BDS Ionospheric Grid Information is valid.

questions.question: MDT configuration needs to name the specific Bluetooth beacons the UE should look for when the Bluetooth Measurement Configuration is set to Setup. Which specifications define the Bluetooth Measurement Configuration Name List information element?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413, TS 36.423, TS 38.413, and TS 38.423 define the Bluetooth Measurement Configuration Name List information element, present when the Bluetooth Measurement Configuration IE is set to "Setup", containing up to maxnoofBluetoothName (4) Bluetooth Measurement Configuration Name items.

questions.question: A CHF rejects part of a charging data request and has to point at exactly which element caused the rejection. Which specifications define the Failed Parameter information element in the Charging Data Response, and what category does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.255, TS 32.276, TS 32.277, and TS 32.279 define the Failed Parameter information element in the Charging Data Response (and analogous Debit/Reserve Units Response) message, described in TS 32.290/TS 32.299. It carries category "OC" (Optional Conditional).

questions.question: A node describing a neighbour cell's PRACH resources must state which Zadoff-Chu root sequence that cell uses. Which specifications define the RootSequenceIndex information element, and what integer range does it span?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423, TS 37.473, TS 38.423, and TS 38.473 define the RootSequenceIndex information element (within the PRACH Configuration / E-UTRA PRACH Configuration IE). It is an INTEGER ranging from 0 to 837.

questions.question: During handover the target node must be given the NCC value that lets it derive the next hop key for AS security. Which specifications define the Next Hop Chaining Count information element, and what is its integer range?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413, TS 36.423, and TS 38.413 (and TS 38.423, which defines the containing AS Security Information IE) define the Next Hop Chaining Count (NCC) information element. It is an INTEGER ranging from 0 to 7.

questions.question: XR traffic needs a per-PDU-Set error target rather than a per-packet one when QoS is applied to a flow. Which specifications define the PDU Set Error Rate information element, and which IE type does it reuse?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.483, TS 38.413, TS 38.423, and TS 38.473 define the PDU Set Error Rate information element (within PDU Set QoS Information), applied to a QoS flow as specified in TS 23.501. It reuses the Packet Error Rate IE type.

questions.question: An MDT configuration must be updated with the modified list of PLMNs that are allowed to collect MDT data, up to a maximum of 16. Which specifications define the MDT PLMN Modification List information element?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.483, TS 38.413, TS 38.423, and TS 38.473 define the MDT PLMN Modification List information element, which provides the modified list of PLMN(s) allowed for MDT, containing 0 to maxnoofMDTPLMNs (16) PLMN Identity entries (an empty list means no PLMN is allowed for MDT).

questions.question: Which specifications define the Paging Priority information element, and what values does it take?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413, TS 38.413, TS 38.423, and TS 38.473 define the Paging Priority information element. It is an ENUMERATED type with values PrioLevel1 through PrioLevel8, where a lower value codepoint indicates higher priority.

questions.question: A DRB is set up to carry only one direction of a QoS flow, and the peer node has to be told which direction that is. Which specifications define the QoS Flow Mapping Indication information element, and what enumerated values does it use?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.473, TS 37.483, TS 38.423, and TS 38.473 define the QoS Flow Mapping Indication information element. It is an ENUMERATED type with values "ul" and "dl", indicating that only the uplink or only the downlink of a QoS flow is mapped to the DRB (for MBS, applied to an MRB and always set to "dl").

questions.question: Where is the Reporting Amount information element defined, and what values does it take?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.413 and TS 25.453 define a Reporting Amount IE (within Periodic Location Info) as an INTEGER(1..8639999,...) indicating the amount of periodic reports. TS 38.455 and TS 38.473 define a Reporting Amount IE (within UE Reporting Information) as ENUMERATED(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64), where value 0 represents an infinite number of periodic reports.

questions.question: Subscription data in the HLR/HSS has to record how long an extended idle-mode DRX cycle the subscriber is allowed. Which specifications define the Extended idle mode DRX cycle length information element?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.060, TS 23.401, and TS 23.502 define the Extended idle mode DRX cycle length as a subscription data field in the HLR/HSS (and UDM), indicating a subscribed extended idle mode DRX cycle length value for the subscriber.

questions.question: When a QoS flow can no longer meet its primary parameters, the node reports which entry of the alternative list it is currently meeting. Which specifications define the Alternative QoS Parameters Set Index information element, and what integer range does it use?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413, TS 38.423, and TS 38.473 define the Alternative QoS Parameters Set Index information element. It is an INTEGER ranging from 1 to 8, indicating the index of the item within the Alternative QoS Parameters Set List IE corresponding to the currently fulfilled alternative QoS parameters set.

questions.question: A target node has to answer whether it accepted a dual active protocol stack handover for the bearer concerned. Which specifications define the DAPS Response Indicator information element, and what enumerated values does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413, TS 36.423, and TS 38.413 define the DAPS Response Indicator information element (within DAPS Response Information). It is an ENUMERATED type with values "DAPS HO accepted" and "DAPS HO not accepted".

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the Common Network Instance information element, and how is its OCTET STRING encoded?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.483, TS 38.413, and TS 38.423 define the Common Network Instance information element, used by the NG-RAN node to select a particular transport network resource in a format common with 5GC. Its OCTET STRING is encoded as the Network Instance field of the Network Instance IE specified in TS 29.244.

questions.question: The IAB Authorized information element tells a node whether IAB operation is allowed - in which specifications is it defined, and what enumerated values does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413, TS 36.423, and TS 38.413 define the IAB Authorized information element. It is an ENUMERATED type with values "authorized" and "not authorized", indicating the IAB-node's authorization status.

questions.question: A lawful-interception record and a 5GC data model both have to say whether the UE came in over 3GPP or non-3GPP access. Which specifications enumerate the values of AccessType, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.128 and TS 29.571 enumerate AccessType. TS 33.128 defines threeGPPAccess(1) (3GPP access), nonThreeGPPAccess(2) (Non-3GPP access), and threeGPPandNonThreeGPPAccess(3) (3GPP and Non-3GPP access); TS 29.571 defines "3GPP_ACCESS" (3GPP access) and "NON_3GPP_ACCESS" (Non-3GPP access).

questions.question: An LMF reports back a location estimate and must state whether the accuracy the client asked for was actually met. Which specifications enumerate the values of AccuracyFulfilmentIndicator, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.572 and TS 33.128 enumerate AccuracyFulfilmentIndicator. TS 29.572 defines "REQUESTED_ACCURACY_FULFILLED" and "REQUESTED_ACCURACY_NOT_FULFILLED"; TS 33.128 defines the equivalent requestedAccuracyFulfilled(1) and requestedAccuracyNotFulfilled(2), both indicating whether the requested accuracy was fulfilled or not.

questions.question: An event subscription has to distinguish a change in the IMSI-to-IMEI binding from one where only the software version moved. Which specifications enumerate the values of AssociationType, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.503 and TS 29.122 enumerate AssociationType. TS 29.503 defines "IMEI_CHANGE" (report only if the IMSI-IMEI association changed, not if only the SV changed) and "IMEISV_CHANGE" (report if the IMSI-IMEI or SV association, or both, changed). TS 29.122 defines the equivalent values IMEI and IMEISV for detecting the change of IMSI-IMEI/IMEISV association.

questions.question: Analytics about congestion must say whether the congestion sits on the user plane, the control plane, or both. Which specifications enumerate the values of CongestionType, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.520 enumerates CongestionType with USER_PLANE, CONTROL_PLANE, and USER_AND_CONTROL_PLANE. TS 29.122 also defines an enumeration named CongestionType, but with different values (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) representing congestion status level rather than plane.

questions.question: A group message can be pushed over unicast, over EPS MBMS multicast, or over 5GS MBS in either multicast or broadcast form. Which specifications enumerate the values of DeliveryMode, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.549 and TS 24.548 enumerate DeliveryMode. TS 29.549 defines UNICAST (unicast delivery), MULTICAST (EPS MBMS multicast delivery), MBS_MULTICAST (5GS MBS multicast delivery), and MBS_BROADCAST (5GS MBS broadcast delivery); TS 24.548 defines BROADCAST and MULTICAST delivery modes.

questions.question: A PDU session record has to say whether the DNN was matched against an explicitly subscribed DNN or fell back on a wildcard subscription. Which specifications enumerate the values of DnnSelectionMode, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.291 and TS 29.502 enumerate DnnSelectionMode: "VERIFIED" (DNN authorized based on the explicitly subscribed DNN, subscription verified), "UE_DNN_NOT_VERIFIED" (UE-provided DNN authorized via wildcard subscription, not verified), and "NW_DNN_NOT_VERIFIED" (network-provided DNN authorized via wildcard subscription, not verified).

questions.question: An SMF has to tell the PCF why provisioned PCC rules could not be installed, and whether it is worth retrying. Which specifications enumerate the values of FailureCause, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.512 enumerates FailureCause for PCC/session rule installation failures, including PCC_RULE_EVENT and RULE_PERMANENT_ERROR (rule cannot be installed/activated, request failed and should not be retried) and PCC_QOS_FLOW_EVENT and RULE_TEMPORARY_ERROR (rule cannot currently be enforced/modified, but may succeed if retried later), among other values such as POL_DEC_ERROR. TS 29.515 also defines an enumeration named FailureCause, but for positioning failure causes ("POSITIONING_DENIED", "UNSUPPORTED_BY_UE", "NOT_REGISTED_UE", "UNSPECIFIED"), unrelated to PCC rules.

questions.question: A data-retrieval request fails and the answer must distinguish an unknown user from an unknown stream from data that simply is not available. Which specifications enumerate the values of FailureReason, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.549 enumerates FailureReason with USER_NOT_FOUND (user not found), STREAM_NOT_FOUND (stream not found), DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE (requested data not available), and OTHER_REASON. TS 29.573 also defines an enumeration named FailureReason, but with unrelated values about invalid JSON pointers/HTTP headers ("INVALID_JSON_POINTER", "INVALID_INDEX_TO_ENCRYPTED_BLOCK", "INVALID_HTTP_HEADER").

questions.question: A location request may want the current position, or the last known one, or only a notification with no estimate produced at all. Which specifications enumerate the values of LocationType, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.518 and TS 29.122 enumerate LocationType. TS 29.518 defines "CURRENT_LOCATION", "CURRENT_OR_LAST_KNOWN_LOCATION", "NOTIFICATION_VERIFICATION_ONLY" (notification/verification only, no location estimate), and "DEFERRED_LOCATION"; TS 29.122 defines CURRENT_LOCATION, LAST_KNOWN_LOCATION, CURRENT_OR_LAST_KNOWN_LOCATION, and INITIAL_LOCATION.

questions.question: A subscription to NWDAF events can either be reported at a fixed repetition period or only when a threshold is crossed. Which specifications enumerate the values of NotificationMethod, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.520 and TS 29.508 enumerate NotificationMethod. TS 29.520 defines PERIODIC (repetitionPeriod-based) and THRESHOLD (upon threshold exceeded); TS 29.508 defines PERIODIC, ONE_TIME, and ON_EVENT_DETECTION.

questions.question: Network slice admission control in a visited network can run on its own or with help from the home network, and the applied mode must be signalled. Which specifications enumerate the values of NsacAdmissionMode, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.536 and TS 29.503 enumerate NsacAdmissionMode. Both define "VPLMN_ADMISSION" (VPLMN NSAC admission mode) and "VPLMN_WITH_HPLMN_ASSISTANCE" (VPLMN with HPLMN assistance NSAC admission mode); TS 29.503 additionally defines "HPLMN_ADMISSION" (HPLMN NSAC admission mode).

questions.question: A UE's location is worked out either by the UE itself, with the UE only assisting, or by the conventional network method. Which specifications enumerate the values of PositioningMode, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.128 and TS 29.572 enumerate PositioningMode. TS 33.128 defines uEBased(1), uEAssisted(2), and conventional(3); TS 29.572 defines the equivalent "UE_BASED", "UE_ASSISTED", and "CONVENTIONAL".

questions.question: Which specifications enumerate the values of ScheduledCommunicationType, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.571 and TS 29.122 enumerate ScheduledCommunicationType. TS 29.571 defines "DOWNLINK_ONLY", "UPLINK_ONLY", and "BIDIRECTIONAL"; TS 29.122 defines the equivalent DOWNLINK, UPLINK, and BIDIRECTIONAL.

questions.question: Tell me where the values of StationaryIndication are defined, and what they are.
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.571 and TS 29.122 define StationaryIndication, with values "STATIONARY" (UE is stationary) and "MOBILE" (UE is mobile).

questions.question: In which specifications are the values of TermCause defined, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.520 and TS 29.574 define TermCause. TS 29.520 defines USER_CONSENT_REVOKED, NWDAF_OVERLOAD, and UE_LEFT_AREA; TS 29.574 defines USER_CONSENT_REVOKED, DCCF_OVERLOAD, OUT_OF_SERVING_AREA, and OTHER.

questions.question: An MC server has to be handed the rule or label that tells it who should be pulled into an ad hoc group call, for instance everyone inside a given area. Which specifications define the Criteria for determining the participants information element?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.280, TS 23.281, TS 23.282, TS 23.379, and TS 23.700-76 define the Criteria for determining the participants information element, used in ad hoc group (emergency alert/call/data session) request/get-userlist information flows to carry the criteria or label the MC server uses to determine participants, e.g. location-based criteria to invite participants in a given area.

questions.question: A URSP rule needs a number that fixes the order in which the UE evaluates it against the other rules. Which specifications define the Route Selection Descriptor Precedence information element?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.503, TS 23.700-33, TS 23.700-48, and TS 23.700-85 define the Route Selection Descriptor Precedence information element, which determines the order in which the Route Selection Descriptors of a URSP rule are to be applied.

questions.question: An index pointing at a specific RRM configuration has to travel with the subscription from the HSS down into the BSS or the RAN. Which specifications define the RFSP Index information element?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.060, TS 23.401, TS 23.502, and TS 23.503 define the RFSP Index information element: an index to a specific RRM configuration, held as subscription/context data in the HLR/HSS/UDM and carried down to the BSS (GERAN), RNC (UTRAN), E-UTRAN, or NG-RAN; TS 23.503 also describes it as PCF-provided access and mobility policy information delivered to the AMF.

questions.question: An MC client is being pushed out of an ongoing ad hoc group call and the server may explain why. Which specifications define the Reason to leave information element?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.281, TS 23.282, TS 23.379, and TS 23.700-76 define the Reason to leave information element, carried in the ad hoc group call/data session leave request from the MC service server to the MC service client to explain why the client is being asked to leave the ongoing ad hoc group communication.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Reestablishment Indication information element, and what values does it take?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423, TS 37.473, TS 38.423, and TS 38.473 define the Reestablishment Indication information element (within the RLC Status IE). It is an ENUMERATED type with the single value "reestablished", indicating that the RLC has been re-established following a change of radio status.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND message, and say which node sends it in each.
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.473 (F1AP) defines the SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND message, sent by the gNB-CU to the gNB-DU. TS 37.473 (W1AP) also lists System Information Delivery / SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND as a Class 2 elementary procedure.

questions.question: A peer UE turns down a PC5 unicast link modification with a cause such as 'lack of resources for PC5 unicast link'. Which specifications define the DIRECT LINK MODIFICATION REJECT message, and in which direction does it travel?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.587 defines the DIRECT LINK MODIFICATION REJECT message. It travels from the (target) UE to the peer UE, sent when the target UE cannot accept a PC5 unicast link modification request, e.g. with cause #5 "lack of resources for PC5 unicast link".

questions.question: An MCData user asks to see the list of group communications that were deferred for later retrieval. Which specifications define the DEFERRED DATA REQUEST message, and does the IWF support it?
questions.reference_answer: The DEFERRED DATA REQUEST message is defined in TS 29.582 and TS 24.282. The IWF does not support the DEFERRED DATA REQUEST message.

questions.question: A DRNS or a Node B has dropped HS-DSCH PDUs and reports the drop events upward, identifying the dropped PDUs directly. Which specifications define the HS-DSCH PDU DROP INDICATION control frame, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The HS-DSCH PDU DROP INDICATION control frame is defined in TS 25.425 and TS 25.435. In TS 25.425 it is sent by the DRNS to report PDU drop events to the SRNC, and in TS 25.435 it is sent by the Node B to report PDU drop events to the CRNC.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus define the Nnef_DNAIMapping_Unsubscribe service operation, and which NF invokes it?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_DNAIMapping_Unsubscribe service operation is defined in TS 29.591 (clauses 4.6.2.1 and 4.6.2.3.1) and TS 23.502 (clause 5.2.6.34.3). It is invoked by an NF service consumer (e.g. NWDAF) to explicitly unsubscribe from notification of DNAI Mapping information.

questions.question: An untrusted AF asks, through the NEF, for access and mobility policy to be authorized for one UE identified by GPSI, which the NEF then translates to SUPI. Which specifications define the Nnef_AMPolicyAuthorization_Create service operation?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_AMPolicyAuthorization_Create service operation is defined in TS 29.513 and TS 23.502.

questions.question: Which documents specify the values of PolicyType, and what are they?
questions.reference_answer: The PolicyType enumeration values are specified in TS 29.549 (LOWEST_COST, HIGH_THROUGHPUT_WITH_COST) and TS 29.435 (MAX_NUM_PDU_SESS, MAX_NUM_UE, SLICE_LOAD_PREDICTION, TIME_PERIOD_AND_AVG_QOS, TIME_PERIOD_AND_MIN_QOS).

questions.question: Which service operation lets an AF authorize a ProSe discovery request, and for a "restricted" discovery type which identifier is the required input?
questions.reference_answer: The Naf_ProSe_DiscoveryAuthorization service operation lets an AF authorize a ProSe discovery request. For a "restricted" discovery type, the required input is the RPAUID.

questions.question: For the Nnef_EASDeployment_Update service operation, what is the only required input and what is returned as the required output?
questions.reference_answer: For Nnef_EASDeployment_Update, the only required input is EAS Deployment Information, and the required output is a Result Indication.

questions.question: Which information elements are required in the Page MS via SGSN and Search for MS via SGSN messages, and which of them are optional?
questions.reference_answer: Both Page MS via SGSN and Search for MS via SGSN require the IMSI (mandatory) as the only required information element. The optional information elements in both are eMLPP priority, TMSI, and Channel type.

questions.question: In the Nudm_SDM_ModifySubscription service operation, which two inputs are mandatory and which inputs are optional?
questions.reference_answer: In Nudm_SDM_ModifySubscription, the two mandatory inputs are Subscription Correlation ID and SUPI. The optional inputs are Expiry time and Monitored resource URIs.

questions.question: Which service operation does an NF consumer use to explicitly unsubscribe from Nnef_AMPolicyAuthorization events, and what input does it need?
questions.reference_answer: An NF consumer uses the Nnef_AMPolicyAuthorization_Unsubscribe service operation to explicitly unsubscribe from Nnef_AMPolicyAuthorization events, and it requires the Subscription Correlation ID as required input.

questions.question: For Nnef_ServiceParameter_Get, what is the required input Service Descriptor made of, and what does the operation return as required outputs?
questions.reference_answer: For Nnef_ServiceParameter_Get, the required input Service Descriptor is made of the combination of DNN and S-NSSAI, an AF-Service-Identifier, or an External Application Identifier. The required outputs are the Transaction Reference ID, an operation execution result indication, and the requested data.

questions.question: In which messages is the Subscriber state information element reported, and what states can it indicate?
questions.reference_answer: The Subscriber state information element is reported in the Obtain Subscriber Info ack and Provide Subscriber Info ack messages. It can indicate that the MS is busy (engaged on a circuit-switched call), network determined not reachable (IMSI detached or roaming in a prohibited location area), or assumed idle.

questions.question: Which service operation does the USS invoke towards the NEF to revoke an existing C2 connection between a UAV and its UAV-C, and what does the request include?
questions.reference_answer: The USS invokes the Nnef_AFsessionWithQoS_Revoke service operation towards the NEF to revoke an existing C2 connection. The request includes the USS identity/AF identifier and the Transaction Reference ID.

questions.question: What is the enumeration N32fErrorType used for, and which value indicates that the integrity check on the modifications block of an N32-f message failed?
questions.reference_answer: The N32fErrorType enumeration indicates the reason an N32-f message-related procedure failed (e.g. integrity check failure, deciphering failure, context not found). The value "INTEGRITY_CHECK_ON_MODIFICATIONS_FAILED" indicates that the integrity check verification on the modifications block of the received N32-f message failed.

questions.question: In the NefEvent enumeration, which value indicates a subscribed event about UE communication information and what is its applicability?
questions.reference_answer: In the NefEvent enumeration, the value UE_COMM indicates that the subscribed/notified event is UE communication information, and its applicability is UeCommunication.

questions.question: Which information elements does the Deflected-to number appear in for the Call Deflection supplementary service, and when is the Deflected-to subaddress present?
questions.reference_answer: The Deflected-to number appears in the CD Request and Process Call Waiting negative response information elements as a mandatory field. The Deflected-to subaddress is conditional and shall be present if it was entered by the served subscriber; otherwise it shall be absent.

questions.question: The EventNotifyDataType enumeration lists the types of location event notification - which values cover entering, leaving and being inside an area?
questions.reference_answer: In the EventNotifyDataType enumeration, "ENTERING_INTO_AREA" covers entering an area, "LEAVING_FROM_AREA" covers leaving an area, and "BEING_INSIDE_AREA" covers being inside an area.

questions.question: Which messages carry the ISDN bearer capability and ISDN low layer compatibility information elements, and under what condition are they present?
questions.reference_answer: The ISDN bearer capability and ISDN low layer compatibility information elements are carried in the Complete Call and Process Call Waiting messages. They are conditional and shall be present for an MT call (Complete Call) or for the waiting call (Process Call Waiting) if received in the Provide Roaming Number; otherwise they shall be absent.

questions.question: In the PolicyControlRequestTrigger enumeration, what do the values AC_TY_CH and UE_MAC_CH indicate?
questions.reference_answer: In the PolicyControlRequestTrigger enumeration, AC_TY_CH indicates Access Type Change, also indicating the addition or removal of Access Type for an MA PDU session; UE_MAC_CH indicates that a new UE MAC address is detected or a used UE MAC address is inactive for a specific period.

questions.question: Which clause defines the DataSetId enumeration, and what do the values A_PFD and A_AFQOS stand for?
questions.reference_answer: The DataSetId enumeration is defined in clause 6.1.6.3.8 of TS 29.510. "A_PFD" stands for the ApplicationData subset Packet Flow Descriptions, and "A_AFQOS" stands for the ApplicationData subset AF Requested QoS Data.

questions.question: Which enumeration value names the provisioned data set for LCS Broadcast Assistance Subscription Data, and which one covers Operator Determined Barring?
questions.reference_answer: In the ProvisionedDataSetName enumeration, "LCS_BCA" names the LCS Broadcast Assistance Subscription Data set, and "ODB" covers Operator Determined Barring Subscription Data.

questions.question: In the EventId enumeration used by NWDAF analytics exposure, which value represents E2E data volume transfer time analytics and which represents NF load information?
questions.reference_answer: In the EventId enumeration, "E2E_DATA_VOL_TRANS_TIME" represents the analytics of E2E data volume transfer time, and "NF_LOAD" represents the analytics of NF Load information.

questions.question: The UserPlaneEvent enumeration reports user plane events - which values distinguish a successful from a failed resource allocation?
questions.reference_answer: In the UserPlaneEvent enumeration, "FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION" indicates the resource allocation failed, and "SUCCESSFUL_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION" indicates the resource allocation is successful.

questions.question: Which service operation lets an NF consumer fetch GBA User Security Settings from the HSS, and which Zh message does it map to?
questions.reference_answer: The Nhss_GbaSDM_Get service operation lets an NF consumer fetch GBA User Security Settings from the HSS. It maps to the Zh interface message used when the BSF retrieves the AV and user profile from the HSS.

questions.question: What are the possible values of the N32Purpose enumeration, and which two of them are allowed only for test traffic?
questions.reference_answer: The N32Purpose enumeration values are ROAMING, INTER_PLMN_MOBILITY, SMS_INTERCONNECT, ROAMING_TEST, INTER_PLMN_MOBILITY_TEST, SMS_INTERCONNECT_TEST, SNPN_INTERCONNECT, SNPN_INTERCONNECT_TEST, DISASTER_ROAMING, DISASTER_ROAMING_TEST, DATA_ANALYTICS_EXCHANGE, and DATA_ANALYTICS_EXCHANGE_TEST. DATA_ANALYTICS_EXCHANGE and DATA_ANALYTICS_EXCHANGE_TEST are not restricted to test traffic; the values allowed only for test traffic are ROAMING_TEST, INTER_PLMN_MOBILITY_TEST, SMS_INTERCONNECT_TEST, SNPN_INTERCONNECT_TEST, and DISASTER_ROAMING_TEST.

questions.question: In the N1N2MessageTransferCause enumeration, which cause value is used when the AMF has stored the N1/N2 message due to Asynchronous Transfer?
questions.reference_answer: In the N1N2MessageTransferCause enumeration, the cause value "WAITING_FOR_ASYNCHRONOUS_TRANSFER" represents the case where the AMF has stored the N1/N2 message due to Asynchronous Transfer.

questions.question: Which enumerations define the MDT report interval for LTE and for NR, and which interval values does the NR one add on top of the LTE one?
questions.reference_answer: The MDT report interval for LTE is defined by the ReportIntervalMdt enumeration and for NR by the ReportIntervalNrMdt enumeration. The NR enumeration adds the interval values "20480" (20480 ms) and "40960" (40960 ms) on top of the LTE one.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Nnef_MBSSession_StatusSubscribe service operation, and what are its required inputs?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_MBSSession_StatusSubscribe service operation is defined in TS 23.247 and TS 29.522. Its required inputs are Status Information and MBS Session ID.

questions.question: Which service operation allows the AMF to forward MO Small Data received in a NAS procedure to the SMF, and which inputs does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Nsmf_PDUSession_SendMOData service operation allows the AMF to forward MO Small Data received in a NAS procedure to the SMF. Its required inputs are the SM Context ID and the N1 container received from the UE, with optional inputs AN type and MO Exception Data Counter.

questions.question: What does the Nnsacf_NSAC_QuotaUpdate service operation update in the VPLMN NSACF, and which three inputs are required?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnsacf_NSAC_QuotaUpdate service operation updates the NSACF at the VPLMN with the maximum number of Registered UEs to be enforced and/or the maximum number of LBO PDU sessions to be admitted. Its three required inputs are S-NSSAI (the mapped S-NSSAI in HPLMN), PLMN ID (the serving PLMN of the UE), and Requested Quota attribute type.

questions.question: Which service operation between the S-CSCF and the HSS carries the Authentication Scheme as required Authentication Data, and what does it return?
questions.reference_answer: The Nhss_ImsUEAuthenticate_Get service operation between the S-CSCF and the HSS carries the Authentication Scheme as required Authentication Data input. It returns a Result Indication as required output, with User Identity and Authentication Data (e.g. AV) as optional outputs.

questions.question: Which service operation does the S-CSCF use to retrieve restoration data from the HSS, and is the Private Identity a required or optional input?
questions.reference_answer: The S-CSCF uses the Nhss_ImsUECM_RestorationInfoGet service operation to retrieve restoration data from the HSS. The Private Identity is an optional input; the required input is the Public Identity.

questions.question: Which message does the S-NG-RAN node send when it cannot accept any of the bearers during S-NG-RAN node Addition Preparation, and what does it include?
questions.reference_answer: When the S-NG-RAN node cannot accept any of the bearers during S-NG-RAN node Addition Preparation, it sends the S-NODE ADDITION REQUEST REJECT message with an appropriate cause value to the M-NG-RAN node. If the CHO Information SN Addition IE and the PCell ID IE were included in the S-NODE ADDITION REQUEST message, the S-NG-RAN node shall, if supported, include the PCell ID IE in the S-NODE ADDITION REQUEST REJECT message.

questions.question: When does the UE send the WLCP BEARER RELEASE REJECT message to the TWAG, and which information elements does that message carry?
questions.reference_answer: The UE sends the WLCP BEARER RELEASE REJECT message to the TWAG to reject release of a WLCP bearer for the given PDN connection, upon receipt of a WLCP BEARER RELEASE REQUEST message it does not accept. The message carries the WLCP bearer identity and a Cause IE indicating the reason for rejection (mandatory), plus optional Protocol configuration options.

questions.question: Which message does a target UE send when the sidelink positioning privacy check is unsuccessful, and what must it include?
questions.reference_answer: When the sidelink positioning privacy check is unsuccessful, the target UE sends the SIDELINK POSITIONING PRIVACY CHECK REJECT message. It must include the procedure transaction ID received in the SIDELINK POSITIONING PRIVACY CHECK REQUEST message and the info of denied UE(s) against which the privacy check was unsuccessful.

questions.question: In which clauses are the WT ADDITION REQUEST REJECT message and the abnormal conditions for the WT ADDITION REQUEST message during WT Addition Preparation defined?
questions.reference_answer: The WT ADDITION REQUEST REJECT message is defined in clause 8.8.3 (Unsuccessful Operation) of TS 36.463, and the abnormal conditions for the WT ADDITION REQUEST message during WT Addition Preparation are defined in clause 8.8.4 (Abnormal Conditions) of TS 36.463.

questions.question: Which message reports the outcome of an E-RAB MODIFICATION INDICATION, in which direction is it sent and which lists does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The E-RAB MODIFICATION CONFIRM message reports the outcome of an E-RAB MODIFICATION INDICATION. It is sent in the direction MME to eNB, and it carries the E-RAB Modify List, E-RAB Failed to Modify List, and E-RAB To Be Released List.

questions.question: Which clauses define the CELL SETUP FAILURE message and the abnormal conditions of the Cell Setup procedure, and which cause value applies if the cell is already Enabled or Disabled?
questions.reference_answer: The CELL SETUP FAILURE message is defined in clause 8.2.12.3 (Unsuccessful Operation) of TS 25.433, and the abnormal conditions of the Cell Setup procedure are defined in clause 8.2.12.4 (Abnormal Conditions) of TS 25.433. If the cell is already Enabled or Disabled when the CELL SETUP REQUEST message is received, the Cause IE is set to "Message not compatible with receiver state".

questions.question: Which message confirms an E1 RELEASE REQUEST between the gNB-CU-CP and the gNB-CU-UP, and which information elements does it contain?
questions.reference_answer: The E1 RELEASE RESPONSE message confirms an E1 RELEASE REQUEST between the gNB-CU-CP and the gNB-CU-UP. It contains the Message Type, Transaction ID (both mandatory), and an optional Criticality Diagnostics IE.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Location number information element, and say under what condition it is present in the compound Location information element.
questions.reference_answer: The Location number information element is defined in TS 23.018 clause 8.3.5.1 and TS 23.078 clause 11.3.2.1.2. Within the compound Location information element it shall be present if the VLR can derive it from the stored service area identity (UMTS), cell global identity (GSM), or location area identity; otherwise it shall be absent.

questions.question: An RNC needs to release the relocation resources it had reserved at a BSS over the Iur-g interface. Which specifications describe the ENHANCED RELOCATION RESOURCE RELEASE COMMAND message, and which node sends it to which?
questions.reference_answer: The ENHANCED RELOCATION RESOURCE RELEASE COMMAND message is described in TS 25.423 and TS 43.130. It is sent by the RNC to the BSS.

questions.question: When a TBSS cannot reserve the radio resources asked for by the SRNS, it answers with the ENHANCED RELOCATION RESOURCE FAILURE message. Which specifications define that message and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The ENHANCED RELOCATION RESOURCE FAILURE message is defined in TS 43.130 and TS 25.423. It is sent by the TBSS/BSS to the SRNS/RNC with an appropriate Cause value when the TBSS cannot reserve the requested radio resources.

questions.question: Which documents specify the Xn FAILURE INDICATION message that an NG-RAN node sends after receiving an RLF Report from a UE, and how is it used to pass RLF information from the gNB-CU to the gNB-DU?
questions.reference_answer: The Xn FAILURE INDICATION message is defined in TS 38.423 and TS 38.401. NG-RAN node2 sends the FAILURE INDICATION message (including the UE RLF Report Container IE) to NG-RAN node1 via Xn after receiving an RLF Report from a UE, and the gNB1-CU then forwards the RLF Report to the gNB1-DU using the F1: Access and Mobility Indication message.

questions.question: Where is the Nnef_ParameterProvision_Delete service operation defined, what inputs does it require, and which NEF measurement counters count its requests and failures?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_ParameterProvision_Delete service operation is defined in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.4.4. Its required inputs are AF Identifier and Transaction Reference ID. The NEF measurement counter EPP.NbrDelReq counts requests, and EPP.NbrDelFail.cause counts failures.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Nnef_ServiceParameter_Update service operation used by a consumer to update service specific parameters in the UDR via the NEF, and which measurement counter name is incremented on a successful update?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_ServiceParameter_Update service operation is defined in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.11.3. The measurement counter SPP.NbrUpdateSucc is incremented on a successful update.

questions.question: Which parts of the corpus describe the Nnef_PFDmanagement_Subscribe service operation that lets a consumer subscribe to PFD change notifications, and which NEF counter records a successful PFD subscribe?
questions.reference_answer: The Nnef_PFDmanagement_Subscribe service operation is described in TS 29.551 clause 4.2.3.1. The NEF counter PFD.SubscribeSucc records a successful PFD subscribe.

questions.question: The Requested SRS Transmission Characteristics IE carries the SRS Frequency together with the Number Of Periodic Transmissions. Which specifications define this IE, and what does the value 0 for the number of periodic transmissions mean?
questions.reference_answer: The Requested SRS Transmission Characteristics IE is defined in TS 38.455 and TS 38.473. A value of '0' for the Number Of Periodic Transmissions represents an infinite number of periodic SRS transmissions.

questions.question: In which specifications is the SRS Port Index information element defined, and what choice of reference signal does the enclosing SRS Resource type IE offer?
questions.reference_answer: The SRS Port Index information element is defined in TS 38.455 and TS 38.473. The enclosing SRS Resource type IE offers a CHOICE Reference Signal between SRS (with SRS Resource ID) and Positioning SRS (with Positioning SRS Resource ID).

questions.question: Tell me where the SRB Failed to be Setup List in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE message is defined, and in which direction that message is sent in F1AP and in W1AP.
questions.reference_answer: The SRB Failed to be Setup List is defined in TS 37.473 clause 9.2.2.8 (UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE), and does not appear in the F1AP version of that message (TS 38.473 clause 9.2.2.8). In F1AP, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE is sent gNB-DU to gNB-CU; in W1AP, it is sent ng-eNB-DU to ng-eNB-CU.

questions.question: Which specifications define the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT and PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT messages sent by the SMF to the UE, and what does the UE do on a mandatory IE error in a 5GSM message?
questions.reference_answer: The PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT and PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT messages are defined in TS 24.501. On a mandatory IE error in a 5GSM message, if the message is a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST, the network returns a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message with 5GSM cause #96 "invalid mandatory information"; if it is a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST, the network returns a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT message with the same 5GSM cause #96.

questions.question: What condition governs the E-AGCH DRX Offset value when the E-AGCH DRX information type indicates "Same as HS-SCCH"?
questions.reference_answer: When the CHOICE E-AGCH DRX information type indicates "Same as HS-SCCH", the E-AGCH DRX Offset (and the E-AGCH DRX cycle) are the same as the HS-SCCH DRX Cycle and Offset, and the E-AGCH DRX Offset field itself is not separately signalled; only when "E-AGCH DRX parameters" is chosen instead is the E-AGCH DRX Offset explicitly given as an Integer (0..63) in units of subframes.

questions.question: What sub-elements make up the Call Barring SS Data, and when must the Password and Wrong Password Attempts Counter be sent inside it?
questions.reference_answer: Call Barring SS Data contains an SS Code (only sent for the code being modified), a Call Barring Feature List, a Password, a Wrong Password Attempts Counter, and a Notification-to-CSE Flag. In the Any Time Modification acknowledgement, the Password and Wrong Password Attempts Counter shall each be sent only if it was modified.

questions.question: What does Nnef_MBSTMGI_ExpiryNotify communicate to a subscribed AF, and how does the AF acknowledge it?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_MBSTMGI_ExpiryNotify is used by the NEF to notify an already-subscribed AF that the timer for one or more previously allocated MBS TMGI(s) has expired, carried in the "tmgis" attribute of the ExpiryNotif data structure. The AF acknowledges successful reception with an HTTP "204 No Content" status code; on failure it responds with an appropriate error status code.

questions.question: What triggers an AMF to invoke Nausf_UEAuthetication_Authenticate as part of counter-wraparound handling, and what parameters does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: When the UDM has previously received a "Counterupu Reaching Max value" or "CounterSoR Reaching Max value" indication from the AUSF during a UPU/SoR procedure, the UDM sends the AMF a notification with the SUPI and a "re-authentication required" flag set to true. Based on this, the AMF starts the primary re-authentication procedure by invoking Nausf_UEAuthetication_Authenticate Request carrying the SUPI and SN-Name.

questions.question: When an NSACF cannot locally admit a new PDU session entry against the S-NSSAI's maximum count, what does it do, and what does the Primary NSACF return in its Nnsacf_NSAC_NumOfPDUsUpdate response?
questions.reference_answer: If admitting a new PDU session entry would exceed the local maximum PDU session number, the NSACF discovers (if not done before) and delegates the request to the Primary NSACF by invoking Nnsacf_NSAC_NumOfPDUsUpdate with the S-NSSAI. The Primary NSACF checks the global maximum PDU session number and returns either a newly allocated local maximum PDU sessions number or an indication to reject the request to update the local maximum.

questions.question: What is Ndccf_DataManagemen_Transfer used for, and which two entities are described as supporting it during DCCF relocation?
questions.reference_answer: Ndccf_DataManagemen_Transfer is used to inform a target DCCF of handover preparation and handover of data subscriptions during DCCF relocation. Both the DCCF (which supports the UE(s) data subscription transfer procedure) and the Data Consumer (which supports subscription renewal with the target DCCF instance) support this service operation.

questions.question: What does invoking Nmbsf_MBSUserServie_Retrieve accomplish at the MBSF?
questions.reference_answer: Nmbsf_MBSUserServie_Retrieve is used by an NF service consumer to retrieve the properties of an existing MBS User Service at the MBSF, supporting the MBS User Service Retrieval procedure.

questions.question: Which entity can determine that a location QoS is applicable to EPS during 5GS-to-EPS location service continuity, and how is that information communicated to the LMF if the AMF does the processing?
questions.reference_answer: Either the AMF or the LMF can determine the EPS-applicable location QoS when the UE's supported access type includes EUTRAN and the required LCS QoS class is "multiple QoS class". If the AMF performs this determination, it notifies the LMF of the resulting information via the Nlmf_Location_DermineLocation Request message; otherwise, the LMF performs the same determination itself.

questions.question: What must an NF consumer supply to request that the UDM deregister a UE's serving AMF via Nudm_UECM_AMFDeregistration?
questions.reference_answer: The NF consumer must provide the SUPI and a deregistration reason as required inputs to Nudm_UECM_AMFDeregistration, which requests the UDM to initiate deregistration of the AMF serving that UE, if any; the UDM returns a Result Indication.

questions.question: In 5GS-to-EPS idle mode mobility with N26 and data forwarding, when is the Buffered DL Data Waiting indication included in the Nsmf_PDUSession_Response, and what does the AMF do with it?
questions.reference_answer: The (V-)SMF includes the Buffered DL Data Waiting indication in the Nsmf_PDUSession_Response if the Extended buffering timer is running in the (V-)SMF. The AMF then forwards this Buffered DL Data Waiting indication to the MME.

questions.question: In enhanced ML model provisioning, what does an NWDAF containing AnLF do when it receives a "degraded" indication in an Nnwdaf_MLModelProvisioning_Notify request, and what happens once re-training clears that indication?
questions.reference_answer: Upon receiving the Nnwdaf_MLModelProvisioning_Notify request containing the ML model's "degraded" status, the NWDAF containing AnLF (the ML Model Provisioning service consumer) determines, based on that indication, whether it still wants to download the model. Once the NWDAF containing MTLF finishes re-training and the model is no longer degraded, it clears the "degraded" indication and sends a new Nnwdaf_MLModelProvisioning_Notify request with the updated ML Model Information, which the consumer acknowledges.

questions.question: What kind of resource does Nucmf_Provisioning_Create let an NF service consumer create, and for which identifiers is it used?
questions.reference_answer: Nucmf_Provisioning_Create is used by an NF service consumer to create a UE radio capability provisioning resource specifically for Manufacturer-assigned UE Radio Capability IDs.

questions.question: What must an NF consumer provide to delete a Member UE selection assistance subscription via Nnef_MemberUESelectionAssistance_Unsubscribe?
questions.reference_answer: The NF consumer must provide the Subscription Correlation ID as the required input to Nnef_MemberUESelectionAssistance_Unsubscribe, which deletes an already-created subscription for Member UE selection assistance information at the NEF, returning an operation execution result indication.

questions.question: What does Nnef_ECSAddress_Unsubscribe let an NF consumer stop receiving, and what single identifier does it require?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Unsubscribe lets an NF consumer explicitly unsubscribe from notifications of changes to ECS Address Configuration Information, requiring only the Subscription Correlation ID (the reference of the subscription) as input, and returns a Result Indication.

questions.question: Which specifications define the E-CID MEASUREMENT INITIATION FAILURE message, and which node sends it and under what condition?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 38.473 clause 8.13.12.3 (Unsuccessful Operation), the gNB-DU sends the E-CID MEASUREMENT INITIATION FAILURE message when it is unable to initiate at least one of the requested E-CID measurements. TS 38.305 clause 8.3.4.3.1 (LMF-initiated Position Measurement) describes the same failure being reported by the NG-RAN node to the LMF when it cannot initiate the requested E-CID measurements. TS 36.455 clause 8.2.1.3 (Unsuccessful Operation) has the eNB send the equivalent LPPa message to the E-SMLC for the same reason. TS 36.305 clause 8.3.4.3.1 (E-SMLC-initiated Position Measurement) confirms the eNodeB reports the failure to the E-SMLC when unable to initiate the requested measurements.
