questions.question: Where is the OTDOA INFORMATION FAILURE message defined across the corpus, and which node initiates the exchange?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.305 clause 8.2.3.2.2.1 (LMF-initiated assistance data delivery) shows the LMF sending an NRPPa OTDOA INFORMATION REQUEST to the NG-RAN node, with a failure returned when the requested OTDOA assistance data cannot be provided. TS 36.305 clause 8.2.3.2.2.2 (E-SMLC-initiated assistance data delivery) mirrors this for E-UTRAN: the E-SMLC requests OTDOA assistance data from the eNodeB via LPPa, with OTDOA INFORMATION FAILURE returned analogously.

questions.question: Which specifications define the PROSE DIRECT LINK RELEASE ACCEPT message, and which node sends it and to whom?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38_523-1 clause 12.3.1.1.20 exercises sidelink relay reselection test purposes involving ProSe direct link procedures. TS 38.508-1 clause 4.7C.3 (Contents of ProSe PC5 signalling messages) lists the ProSe PC5 signalling message table this message belongs to. TS 24.554 clause 10.3.5.1 (Message definition) states the message is sent by the UE to another peer UE to indicate that the link release request is accepted.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the E8 TERMINAL RESPONSE message, and say what triggers the ME to send it.
questions.reference_answer: TS 51.010-4 clause 27.22.4.28.4 (Method of Test) verifies the ME sends this TERMINAL RESPONSE after executing the BIP OPEN CHANNEL proactive command related to E8 test conditions. TS 31.124 clause 27.22.7.10.4 (Method of test) runs the equivalent USIM-side test, checking the ME's TERMINAL RESPONSE after the corresponding proactive command sequence.

questions.question: Where is the C7 TERMINAL RESPONSE message defined across the corpus, and what triggers the ME to send it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 51.010-4 clause 27.22.4.30.4 (Method of test) verifies the ME sends this TERMINAL RESPONSE after receiving a C7-class proactive command. TS 31.124 clause 27.22.4.30.1 (SEND DATA normal) tests the ME sending the equivalent TERMINAL RESPONSE after processing the SEND DATA proactive command.

questions.question: In which specifications does the ME NORMAL ENDING OF COMMAND message appear, and which node sends it and to whom?
questions.reference_answer: TS 51.010-4 clause 27.22.1.4.2 (Procedure) shows the SIM sending NORMAL ENDING OF COMMAND 1.1A to the ME as part of the PROFILE DOWNLOAD sequence. TS 31.124 clause 27.22.1.4.2 (Procedure) shows the UICC sending NORMAL ENDING OF COMMAND 1.1 to the ME after TERMINAL PROFILE is processed. TS 31.117 clause 10.3.1.4.2 (Procedure) repeats the same UICC-to-ME NORMAL ENDING OF COMMAND response in its PROFILE DOWNLOAD sequence.

questions.question: Which specifications define the RELOCATION PREPARATION FAILURE message, and which node sends it and to whom?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.405 clause 4.11.2.1.3 counts failed relocation preparations based on receipt of the RANAP RELOCATION PREPARATION FAILURE message sent from the PS CN (source side) to the source RNC. TS 25.413 clause 9.2.1.49 (Cell Load Information) notes the Cell Load Information IE's meaning differs depending on whether it is carried in a RELOCATION PREPARATION FAILURE or a RELOCATION COMMAND message. TS 29.060 clause 15 (Mapping of BSSGP and RANAP causes) provides the cause-value mapping tables relevant to this inter-RAT PS Handover failure signalling.

questions.question: Which clauses specify the REROUTE NAS REQUEST message, and which node sends it and for what purpose?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.6.5.3 (Abnormal Conditions) has the NG-RAN node treat the procedure as failed if the S-NSSAI totals in the REROUTE NAS REQUEST message's NSSAI IEs are inconsistent. TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.6 (NAS transport procedures) lists Reroute NAS Request as one of the S1 NAS transport procedures. TS 36.413 clause 8.6.2.5 (Reroute NAS Request) specifies that the MME initiates the procedure by sending REROUTE NAS REQUEST to the eNB, requesting it reroute the INITIAL UE MESSAGE to the MME indicated by the MME Group ID IE.

questions.question: Which specifications define the E-CID MEASUREMENT REPORT message, and which node sends it and what it contains?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.128 clause 6.3.2.2.8 (Positioning info transfer) references LPPa exchanges (per TS 36.455) between the E-SMLC and eNB via the MME, including this measurement report, for lawful-interception purposes. TS 36.455 clause 8.2.3.2 (Successful Operation) specifies the eNB initiates the procedure by sending E-CID MEASUREMENT REPORT, which carries the measurement results per the configuration in the corresponding E-CID MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the MODIFY PDP CONTEXT REQUEST message, and say which entities are involved.
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.161 clause 5.7.1.1 (Access stratum indication via GERAN or UTRAN) uses MODIFY PDP CONTEXT REQUEST as part of NBIFOM access-stratum indication signalling between UE and network. TS 24.229 clause B.2.2.1C (P-CSCF restoration procedure) has the UE act on P-CSCF address(es) received in the Protocol Configuration Options IE of a MODIFY PDP CONTEXT REQUEST message. TS 24.007 clause 6.5.1.18 (SMREG-PDP-MODIFY-REQ) defines this as the primitive requesting an MS-initiated PDP context modification, identified via the NSAPI.

questions.question: Which clauses specify the MULTICAST SESSION UPDATE REQUEST message, and which node sends it and to whom?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.18.5.2 (Successful Operation) has the AMF initiate the Multicast Session Update procedure by sending MULTICAST SESSION UPDATE REQUEST to the NG-RAN node. TS 29.518 clause 6.6.6.4.2.2 (NGAP IEs) lists the Multicast Session Update Request Transfer as the N2 Information content associated with this NGAP message per TS 38.413.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the MBMS SESSION STOP REQUEST message, and say which node sends it and to whom.
questions.reference_answer: TS 43.246 clause 6.1.3 (MBMS channel release) has the SGSN send MBMS SESSION STOP REQUEST to the GERAN, which acknowledges with MBMS SESSION STOP RESPONSE and releases the session's radio resources. TS 36.444 clause 8.1 (Elementary procedures) lists MBMS SESSION STOP REQUEST as the initiating message of the M3AP MBMS Session Stop elementary procedure.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Alert indicator information element in emergency group call requests, and what does it indicate in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Alert indicator IE is defined in the MCVideo emergency group call request (ts_23_281, clause 7.1.2.2.18), the IWF emergency group call request (ts_23_283, clause 10.6.1.1), and the MCPTT emergency group call request (ts_23_379, clause 10.6.2.2.1); in all three it indicates whether an emergency alert is to be sent. A related mapping also appears in the LI parameter table for PTC communications (ts_33_108, clause 17.1.5).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the E-RAB Maximum Bit Rate Uplink information element, and say what it represents in each.
questions.reference_answer: E-RAB Maximum Bit Rate Uplink is defined inside the GBR QoS Information IE in ts_36_423 (clause 9.2.10), ts_37_473 (clause 9.3.1.21), ts_37_483 (clause 9.3.1.19), and ts_38_473 (clause 9.3.1.21). In every case it is a mandatory Bit Rate field giving the maximum bit rate in the uplink direction (from E-UTRAN/access to core) for a GBR E-RAB.

questions.question: Where is the SIPTO L-GW Transport Layer Address information element defined across the S1/Iu interface messages, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: SIPTO L-GW Transport Layer Address is carried in the INITIAL UE MESSAGE of ts_25_413 (clause 9.1.33) and ts_36_413 (clause 9.1.7.1), and in the SENB ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE of ts_36_423 (clause 9.1.3.2); it conveys the transport-layer address of the Local Gateway used for SIPTO (Selected IP Traffic Offload).

questions.question: Where is the notifCorreId attribute defined across the 5GC event-exposure subscription types, and what does it correlate?
questions.reference_answer: notifCorreId is defined as an attribute of the BsfSubscription type in ts_29_521 (clause 5.6.2.7) and the EventsSubscReqData type in ts_29_565 (clause 6.2.6.2.3); in both it sets the value of the Notification Correlation ID used in the corresponding notification. A related NwdafMLModelProvSubsc type appears in ts_29_520 (clause 5.4.6.2.2).

questions.question: Where is the Query result information element defined across the group/functional-alias query responses, and what does it return in each?
questions.reference_answer: Query result is defined in the group information query response of ts_23_280 (clause 10.2.2.17) and ts_23_434 (clause 10.3.2.5), where it returns the group information retrieved based on the query type (e.g. a list of group members), and in the IWF functional alias information query response of ts_23_283 (clause 10.14.2.2), where it returns the functional alias or MC service ID information retrieved.

questions.question: Which specifications define the uncertaintyEllipse attribute, and what geographic information does it carry in each?
questions.reference_answer: uncertaintyEllipse is defined as an attribute of the PointUncertaintyEllipse type in ts_24_546 (clause C.1.4.4.7) and ts_29_572 (clause 6.1.6.2.8), where it indicates an uncertainty ellipse around a geographic point, and of the PointAltitudeUncertainty type in ts_33_128 (clause 7.3.3.2.18), where it describes an uncertainty ellipse alongside altitude information.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Request Type information element (as capitalized here), and what it represents in each message.
questions.reference_answer: Request Type is defined in the EAR payload of ts_33_180 (clause 9.6.4.2), where it gives the type of the authenticated request, and in the LOCATION REPORT message of ts_36_413 (clause 9.1.12.3), where it is sent as it was provided (IE 9.2.1.34). Related Spending-Limit-Request context and ePDG re-authorization procedures appear in ts_29_219 (clause 4.5.1.1) and ts_29_273 (clause 7.1.2.2.1).

questions.question: Where is the ipTrafficFilter attribute defined across the 5GC data-exposure types, and what does it identify in each?
questions.reference_answer: ipTrafficFilter is defined as an attribute of the ServiceExperienceInfoPerFlow type in ts_29_517 (clause 5.6.2.8), the IpEthFlowDescription/FlowDescription type in ts_29_520 (clause 5.1.6.2.27), and the PerformanceDataInfo type in ts_29_591 (clause 5.1.6.2.12). In each it identifies the IP packet filter for the associated flow.

questions.question: In which clauses does the subscriberId attribute appear, and what identity does it represent in each resource?
questions.reference_answer: subscriberId is defined as a resource URI variable in ts_29_222 (clause 8.3.2.2.2), identifying the ID of the subscriber; as a query parameter in the GET method of ts_29_504 (clause 6.2.3.2.3), representing the Subscription Identifier (SUPI, GPSI, IMPI, IMPU, or Routing Indicator); and as an attribute of the SEALEventSubscription type in ts_29_549 (clause 7.5.1.4.2.2), identifying the subscriber of the event.

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Acknowledgement required information element, and what it indicates in each floor-control flow.
questions.reference_answer: Acknowledgement required is defined in the IOPS floor taken flow of ts_23_180 (clause 10.5.3.2.2), the transmit media granted flow of ts_23_281 (clause 7.7.1.2.3), the IWF floor granted flow of ts_23_283 (clause 10.5.2.3), and the floor granted flow of ts_23_379 (clause 10.9.1.2.3); in each it indicates whether acknowledgement from the participant is required.

questions.question: Which specification defines the NG SETUP REQUEST message and describes the successful NG Setup operation, and which node sends it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.7.1.2 (Successful Operation) defines the NG SETUP REQUEST message and describes the NG Setup procedure. The NG-RAN node initiates the procedure by sending the NG SETUP REQUEST message including the appropriate data to the AMF.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 29.413 lists the NGAP messages, including NG SETUP REQUEST, used between the non-3GPP access network node and the AMF?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.413 clause 5.2 (NGAP messages used for non-3GPP access) lists the NGAP messages used between the Non-3GPP access network node and the AMF, including NG SETUP REQUEST, NG SETUP RESPONSE, and NG SETUP FAILURE, per the tabular and ASN.1 definitions in TS 38.413.

questions.question: The SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message exists in both S1AP and NGAP. Which clauses define it, and which node initiates it in each protocol?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.18.2.1 (S1AP) defines the SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message, initiated by the eNB and sent to the MME. TS 38.413 clause 8.15.1.2 (NGAP) defines the same-named message, initiated by the NG-RAN node and sent to the AMF.

questions.question: According to TS 36.413 clause 8.18.2.1, what does the Time Since Secondary Node Release IE indicate when included in the SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.18.2.1 states that if the Time Since Secondary Node Release IE is included in the SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message, it indicates the time elapsed since EN-DC operation in the eNB was stopped for the UE.

questions.question: The CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message exists in both NGAP and S1AP. Which node initiates it in each, and toward which node?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 38.413 clause 8.3.6.2 (NGAP), the AMF initiates the procedure by sending the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message to the NG-RAN node. In TS 36.413 clause 8.3.9.2 (S1AP), the MME initiates the procedure by sending the same-named message to the eNB.

questions.question: Which unique identifier does the AMF allocate and include in the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message if the UE-associated logical NG-connection is not yet established, and what is the corresponding identifier allocated by the MME in the equivalent S1AP procedure?
questions.reference_answer: In NGAP (TS 38.413 clause 8.3.6.2), if the UE-associated logical NG-connection is not established, the AMF allocates a unique AMF UE NGAP ID for the UE and includes it in the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message. In the equivalent S1AP procedure (TS 36.413 clause 8.3.9.2), the MME allocates a unique MME UE S1AP ID and includes it in its CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message.

questions.question: Which specification and clause define the F1 SETUP REQUEST/RESPONSE exchange, and which node initiates it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.473 clause 8.2.3.2 (Successful Operation) defines the F1 Setup procedure. The gNB-DU initiates the procedure by sending an F1 SETUP REQUEST message including the appropriate data to the gNB-CU, and the gNB-CU responds with an F1 SETUP RESPONSE message.

questions.question: Which specification defines the BROADCAST SESSION TRANSPORT REQUEST/RESPONSE exchange, and which nodes are involved?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.17.5.2 (Successful Operation) defines the Broadcast Session Transport procedure. The NG-RAN node initiates it by sending a BROADCAST SESSION TRANSPORT REQUEST message to the AMF, and the AMF responds with a BROADCAST SESSION TRANSPORT RESPONSE message.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 38.423 defines the XnAP RESET REQUEST/RESPONSE exchange, and what must the receiving node do differently for a full reset versus a partial reset?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.4.4.2 (Successful Operation) defines the XnAP Reset procedure. On a full reset, NG-RAN node2 aborts all ongoing Xn procedures with NG-RAN node1, deletes all context related to it (except application-level configuration exchanged at Xn Setup or NG-RAN node Configuration Update), releases the resources, and then responds with RESET RESPONSE. On a partial reset, it only aborts and releases resources for the indicated UE-associated signalling connections, and responds with RESET RESPONSE listing the UE contexts admitted to be released, without waiting for radio resource release/reconfiguration to complete.

questions.question: Which clauses of TS 25.433 define the NBAP Reset procedure in each direction (CRNC to Node B, and Node B to CRNC), and what must both sides do after the Reset Indicator is set to "Node B"?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.433 clause 8.2.19.2.1 (Reset Initiated by the CRNC) and clause 8.2.19.2.2 (Reset Initiated by the Node B) both define the NBAP Reset procedure. When the Reset Indicator IE is set to "Node B", the Node B removes all Node B Communication Contexts within it and their allocated radio resources, initiates release of the involved user plane transport bearers, and returns RESET RESPONSE to the CRNC (clause 8.2.19.2.1); conversely, initiated the other way, the CRNC removes information related to that Node B and its allocated radio resources, initiates release of the involved transport bearers, and returns RESET RESPONSE to the Node B (clause 8.2.19.2.2).

questions.question: Which clause of TS 25.413 defines the Direct Information Transfer procedure initiated from the RNC, and which three IEs must the DIRECT INFORMATION TRANSFER message include?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.413 clause 8.34.2.1 (Direct Information Transfer initiated from the RNC) defines the procedure, initiated with a DIRECT INFORMATION TRANSFER message sent from the RNC to the CN. The message shall include Inter-system Information Transfer Type, Global RNC-ID, and CN Domain Indicator.

questions.question: The TRACE FAILURE INDICATION message exists in both S1AP and NGAP. Which clauses define it, and which node initiates it toward which node in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.11.2.2 (NGAP) defines the TRACE FAILURE INDICATION message, initiated by the NG-RAN node and sent to the AMF, which takes appropriate action based on the failure reason in the Cause IE. TS 36.413 clause 8.10.2.2 (S1AP) defines the same-named message, initiated by the eNB and sent to the MME, which likewise takes appropriate action based on the Cause IE.

questions.question: The PWS FAILURE INDICATION message exists in both S1AP and SBc-AP. Which node sends it in each, and to which node?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 36.413 clause 8.12.4.2 (S1AP), the eNB initiates the procedure by sending a PWS FAILURE INDICATION message to the MME. In TS 29.168 clause 4.3.4.2.8 (SBc-AP), the Indication is sent by the MME or PWS-IWF to report to the CBC the list of cells no longer available for PWS.

questions.question: According to TS 29.168 clause 4.3.4.2.8, what happens to the Failed-Cell-List IE and Global eNB ID IE if the PWS FAILURE INDICATION is received from a PWS-IWF and the failed cells are NR cells?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.168 clause 4.3.4.2.8 states that if the indication is received from a PWS-IWF and the failed cells are NR cells, then the Failed-Cell-List IE and the Global eNB ID IE shall be populated with a dummy value (all zeros).

questions.question: The RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT REQUEST message exists in both NGAP and X2AP. Which node initiates it toward which node in each protocol?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 38.423 clause 8.2.4.2 (XnAP), the new NG-RAN node initiates the Retrieve UE Context procedure by sending the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT REQUEST message to the old NG-RAN node. In TS 36.423 clause 8.3.13.2 (X2AP), the new eNB initiates the same-named procedure by sending the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT REQUEST message to the old eNB.

questions.question: According to TS 36.423 clause 8.3.13.2, what three identifiers does the old eNB use, alongside the Resume ID, to verify the UE in the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 clause 8.3.13.2 states that the old eNB identifies the UE context and verifies the UE by means of the Resume ID, the ShortMAC-I, optionally the C-RNTI, the failure cell PCI, and the E-UTRAN Cell Identifier of the new cell contained in the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT REQUEST message.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 24.301 defines the GUTI reallocation initiation by the network, and what mandatory IE must the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message include?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.301 clause 5.4.1.2 (GUTI reallocation initiation by the network) states that the MME initiates the GUTI reallocation procedure by sending a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message to the UE and starting timer T3450. The message shall include a GUTI, and may include a TAI list, a DCN-ID, and (in WB-S1 mode, for RACS-supporting UEs) a UE radio capability ID deletion indication or a UE radio capability ID. The message definition also appears in ts_24_301_8.2.16.1 (Message definition; Direction: network to UE).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 24.301 clause 5.4.1.2 (GUTI reallocation initiation by the network) states that the MME initiates the GUTI reallocation procedure by sending a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message to the UE and starting timer T3450. The message shall include a GUTI, and may include a TAI list, a DCN-ID, and (in WB-S1 mode, for RACS-supporting UEs) a UE radio capability ID deletion indication or a UE radio capability ID.

questions.question: The RESET REQUEST/RESET ACKNOWLEDGE exchange over SLmAP is defined for both directions in TS 36.459. Which clauses describe it, and which node's failure triggers each direction?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.459 clause 8.3.2.2.1 (Reset Procedure Initiated from the E-SMLC) describes a RESET REQUEST sent to the LMU following a failure at the E-SMLC that lost transaction reference information; the LMU responds with RESET ACKNOWLEDGE. Clause 8.3.2.2.2 (Reset Procedure Initiated from the LMU) describes the reverse: a RESET REQUEST sent to the E-SMLC following a failure at the LMU, with the E-SMLC responding with RESET ACKNOWLEDGE. The message definition also appears in ts_36_423_9.1.2.7 (RESET RESPONSE; Direction: eNB2 → eNB1, eNB → en-gNB, en-gNB → eNB.), ts_36_459_9.1.8 (RESET ACKNOWLEDGE; Direction: E-SMLC → LMU or LMU → E-SMLC.), ts_38_423_9.1.3.11 (RESET RESPONSE; Direction: NG-RAN node2 → NG-RAN node1.).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 36.459 clause 8.3.2.2.1 (Reset Procedure Initiated from the E-SMLC) describes a RESET REQUEST sent to the LMU following a failure at the E-SMLC that lost transaction reference information; the LMU responds with RESET ACKNOWLEDGE. Clause 8.3.2.2.2 (Reset Procedure Initiated from the LMU) describes the reverse: a RESET REQUEST sent to the E-SMLC following a failure at the LMU, with the E-SMLC responding with RESET ACKNOWLEDGE.

questions.question: According to TS 36.459 clause 8.3.2.2.1, what must the LMU do upon receiving a RESET REQUEST message from the E-SMLC, besides responding with RESET ACKNOWLEDGE?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.459 clause 8.3.2.2.1 states that upon reception of the RESET REQUEST message, the LMU shall abort any other ongoing procedure (except another Reset procedure) on the same SLm interface, delete any measurement information related to the E-SMLC, and release the associated resources, before responding with the RESET ACKNOWLEDGE message. The message definition also appears in ts_36_423_9.1.2.7 (RESET RESPONSE; Direction: eNB2 → eNB1, eNB → en-gNB, en-gNB → eNB.), ts_36_459_9.1.8 (RESET ACKNOWLEDGE; Direction: E-SMLC → LMU or LMU → E-SMLC.), ts_38_423_9.1.3.11 (RESET RESPONSE; Direction: NG-RAN node2 → NG-RAN node1.).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 36.459 clause 8.3.2.2.1 states that upon reception of the RESET REQUEST message, the LMU shall abort any other ongoing procedure (except another Reset procedure) on the same SLm interface, delete any measurement information related to the E-SMLC, and release the associated resources, before responding with the RESET ACKNOWLEDGE message.

questions.question: The DIRECT LINK SECURITY MODE REJECT message exists for both 5G ProSe (TS 24.554) and A2X (TS 24.577) PC5 unicast links, with near-identical cause value lists. Which clauses define it, and which cause value is unique to the 5G ProSe version but absent from the A2X list?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.554 clause 7.2.10.5 (5G ProSe direct link security mode control procedure not accepted by the target UE) and TS 24.577 clause 6.1.2.7.5 (A2X PC5 unicast link security mode control procedure not accepted by the target UE) both define this reject message. Both list cause values #5, #7, #8, #9, #10, and #111, but only the 5G ProSe (TS 24.554) version additionally lists cause #14 "Authentication synchronisation error", tied to relay-based GPI authentication.

questions.question: According to TS 24.554 clause 7.2.10.5, what must the target UE include in the PROSE DIRECT LINK SECURITY MODE REJECT message when it detects an authentication synchronisation error while processing the GPI's authentication vector?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.554 clause 7.2.10.5 states that when the target UE detects a synchronisation error processing the authentication vector contained in the GPI (during direct communication with a UE-to-network or UE-to-UE relay), it shall include PC5 signalling protocol cause #14 "Authentication synchronisation error" and shall include the RAND and AUTS parameters in the PROSE DIRECT LINK SECURITY MODE REJECT message.

questions.question: According to TS 24.577 clause 6.1.2.7.5, what does the initiating UE do upon receiving an A2X DIRECT LINK SECURITY MODE REJECT message with cause #9 "LSB of KNRP-sess ID conflict"?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.577 clause 6.1.2.7.5 states that if the PC5 signalling protocol cause IE is set to #9 "LSB of KNRP-sess ID conflict", the initiating UE shall retransmit the A2X DIRECT LINK SECURITY MODE COMMAND message with a different value for the LSB of KNRP-sess ID and restart timer T5310.

questions.question: According to TS 48.008 clause 3.2.3.14, what does the presence of the DTM Handover Command Indication field element in the New BSS to Old BSS Information IE indicate?
questions.reference_answer: TS 48.008 clause 3.2.3.14 states that the presence of this field element in the New BSS to Old BSS Information IE indicates that an (RLC/MAC) DTM HANDOVER COMMAND message is included within the Layer 3 Information IE carried within the same BSSMAP message. The message definition also appears in ts_36_331_6.2.2p2 (Message definitions (part 2); Direction: UE to E‑UTRAN).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 48.008 clause 3.2.3.14 states that the presence of this field element in the New BSS to Old BSS Information IE indicates that an (RLC/MAC) DTM HANDOVER COMMAND message is included within the Layer 3 Information IE carried within the same BSSMAP message.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.413 defines the KILL REQUEST/KILL RESPONSE exchange, and what must the eNB do if the Kill-all Warning Messages Indicator IE is present in the KILL REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.12.2.2 (Successful Operation) defines the Kill procedure. If the Kill-all Warning Messages Indicator IE is present in the KILL REQUEST message, the eNB shall stop broadcasting and discard all warning messages for the area indicated in the Warning Area List IE (or all cells of the eNB if that IE is absent), then acknowledge with a KILL RESPONSE message copying the Message Identifier and Serial Number IEs, including the Broadcast Cancelled Area List IE with the Number of Broadcasts IE set to 0 if applicable. The message definition also appears in ts_29_168_4.3.4.2.6 (STOP WARNING INDICATION; Direction: MME, PWS-IWF → CBC).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 36.413 clause 8.12.2.2 (Successful Operation) defines the Kill procedure. If the Kill-all Warning Messages Indicator IE is present in the KILL REQUEST message, the eNB shall stop broadcasting and discard all warning messages for the area indicated in the Warning Area List IE (or all cells of the eNB if that IE is absent), then acknowledge with a KILL RESPONSE message copying the Message Identifier and Serial Number IEs, including the Broadcast Cancelled Area List IE with the Number of Broadcasts IE set to 0 if applicable.

questions.question: The RNSAP Kill procedure in TS 25.419 uses KILL COMPLETE for success and KILL FAILURE for failure, similar in role to S1AP's KILL RESPONSE. Which clauses define these two RNSAP messages, and which node sends each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.419 clause 8.3.2 (successful operation) defines KILL COMPLETE, sent by the RNC to the CN when all indicated Service Areas successfully stopped broadcasting the CBS message. Clause 8.3.3 (unsuccessful operation) defines KILL FAILURE, sent by the RNC to the CN if it fails to stop broadcasting in at least one service area, including a Failure List IE with the affected Service Area(s) and cause value.

questions.question: According to TS 25.419 clause 8.3.2, what value does the RNC report in the Number of Broadcast Completed List IE if the version corresponding to the Old Serial Number IE is not recognized for a particular service area?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.419 clause 8.3.2 states that if the version corresponding to the Old Serial Number IE value is not recognized for a particular service area, the number of broadcast completed shall be reported as '0' and the Number of Broadcasts Compl Info IE set to 'unknown'.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 25.413 defines the RAB MODIFY REQUEST message, and which node initiates it toward the CN?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.413 clause 8.30.2 (Successful Operation) defines the RAB MODIFY REQUEST message. The RNC initiates the RAB Modification procedure by generating a RAB MODIFY REQUEST message towards the CN, including a list of RABs To Be Modified IEs.

questions.question: The RADIO LINK SETUP FAILURE message exists in both RNSAP (TS 25.423, DRNC-initiated) and NBAP (TS 25.433, Node B-initiated). Which clauses define the unsuccessful operation in each, and which node sends the failure message in each protocol?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.423 clause 8.3.1.3 (Unsuccessful Operation, RNSAP) defines RADIO LINK SETUP FAILURE as sent by the DRNC when at least one radio link fails to establish. TS 25.433 clause 8.2.17.3 (Unsuccessful Operation, NBAP) defines the same-named message as sent by the Node B for the same condition.

questions.question: According to TS 25.433 clause 8.2.17.3, which Cause category includes 'O&M Intervention' as a value for the NBAP RADIO LINK SETUP FAILURE message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.433 clause 8.2.17.3 lists 'O&M Intervention' under the Miscellaneous Cause category, alongside 'Control processing overload' and 'HW failure'.

questions.question: Comparing the ESM cause values listed for the ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT and ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT messages in TS 24.301, which cause values does the dedicated case list that the default case does not?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.301 clause 6.4.2.4 (Dedicated EPS bearer context activation not accepted by the UE) lists ESM causes #26, #31, #41, #42, #43, #44, #45, and #95-111 for ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT. TS 24.301 clause 6.4.1.4 (Default EPS bearer context activation not accepted by the UE) lists only #26, #31, and #95-111 for ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT. So the dedicated case additionally lists #41 (semantic error in TFT operation), #42 (syntactical error in TFT operation), #43 (invalid EPS bearer identity), #44 (semantic errors in packet filters), and #45 (syntactical errors in packet filters) — all TFT/packet-filter related causes absent from the default bearer case, which has no TFT to validate.

questions.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 6.4.1.4, what does the MME do upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.301 clause 6.4.1.4 states that upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message, the MME shall enter the state BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVE and stop timer T3485, if it is running. The message definition also appears in ts_24_301_8.3.5.1 (Message definition; Direction: UE to network).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 24.301 clause 6.4.1.4 states that upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message, the MME shall enter the state BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVE and stop timer T3485, if it is running.

questions.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 6.4.2.4, when must the UE reject an ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST with ESM cause #41 'semantic error in the TFT operation'?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.301 clause 6.4.2.4 states that the UE shall reject the activation request with ESM cause #41 'semantic error in the TFT operation' when the TFT operation is an operation other than 'Create a new TFT'.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 25.413 defines the IU RELEASE COMMAND/IU RELEASE COMPLETE exchange, and does the RNC have to wait for radio resource release before sending IU RELEASE COMPLETE?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.413 clause 8.5.2 (Successful Operation) defines the Iu Release procedure. The CN initiates it by sending IU RELEASE COMMAND to the UTRAN, and the RNC sends IU RELEASE COMPLETE once it has returned assigned Iu user plane resources to idle — it does NOT need to wait for the release of UTRAN radio resources or transport network layer signalling to complete before returning the IU RELEASE COMPLETE message.

questions.question: According to TS 43.130 clause 7.2.6.2 (Iur-g handover with radio resource reservation), which node sends the IU RELEASE COMMAND message to the SRNS, and what event triggers it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 43.130 clause 7.2.6.2 states that the CN sends the IU RELEASE COMMAND message to the SRNS after receiving the HANDOVER COMPLETE message (forwarded by the TBSS following the MS/UE's access to the target GSM cell).

questions.question: According to TS 24.008 clause 5.3.4.3.2, what must the MODIFY COMPLETE message include if the originating MODIFY message contained a reverse call setup direction IE?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.008 clause 5.3.4.3.2 states that if the MODIFY message had contained a reverse call setup direction IE, the same IE shall be included in the MODIFY COMPLETE message. The message definition also appears in ts_24_008_9.3.14 (Modify complete; Direction: both).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 24.008 clause 5.3.4.3.2 states that if the MODIFY message had contained a reverse call setup direction IE, the same IE shall be included in the MODIFY COMPLETE message.

questions.question: The UE Context Modification Required procedure's unsuccessful operation is defined nearly identically in F1AP and W1AP. Which clauses define it, and which node responds with UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REFUSE in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.473 clause 8.3.5.2A (F1AP) states that if none of the requested modifications of the UE context can be successfully performed, the gNB-CU shall respond with the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REFUSE message with an appropriate cause value. TS 37.473 clause 8.3.5.3 (W1AP) defines the equivalent for the same procedure, but the responding node is the ng-eNB-CU instead of the gNB-CU.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 38.413 defines the successful PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP REQUEST/RESPONSE exchange?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.2.1.2 (Successful Operation) defines the PDU Session Resource Setup procedure, including the PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP REQUEST and PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP RESPONSE messages.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.413 defines the E-RAB SETUP REQUEST message, and which node initiates the E-RAB Setup procedure toward the eNB?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.2.1.2 (Successful Operation) defines the E-RAB SETUP REQUEST message. The MME initiates the E-RAB Setup procedure by sending an E-RAB SETUP REQUEST message to the eNB, which must contain an E-RAB to be Setup Item IE for each E-RAB to be set up.

questions.question: According to TS 36.413 clause 8.2.1.2, what must the eNB do for an E-RAB in the E-RAB SETUP REQUEST message if the Integrity Protection Indication IE is set to "required" but user plane integrity protection is not supported?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.2.1.2 states that if the Integrity Protection Indication IE is set to "required" and the eNB or UE does not support user plane integrity protection, the eNB shall reject the establishment of the concerned E-RAB with an appropriate cause value.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.413 defines the S1 SETUP REQUEST/RESPONSE exchange, and which node initiates it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.7.3.2 (Successful Operation) defines the S1 Setup procedure. The eNB initiates the procedure by sending an S1 SETUP REQUEST message including the appropriate data to the MME, and the MME responds with an S1 SETUP RESPONSE message.

questions.question: The IMSI DETACH INDICATION message is defined in TS 24.008 both from the mobile station's side and the network's side. Which clauses describe each, and what does the network do upon receiving it (besides releasing MM connections)?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.008 clause 4.3.4.1 (IMSI detach initiation by the mobile station) describes the mobile station sending the IMSI DETACH INDICATION message and starting timer T3220. Clause 4.3.4.2 (IMSI detach procedure in the network) describes the network's handling: it may set an inactive indication for the IMSI, sends no response to the mobile station, releases locally any ongoing MM connections, and starts the normal RR connection release procedure. The message definition also appears in ts_24_008_9.2.12 (IMSI detach indication; Direction: mobile station to network).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 24.008 clause 4.3.4.1 (IMSI detach initiation by the mobile station) describes the mobile station sending the IMSI DETACH INDICATION message and starting timer T3220. Clause 4.3.4.2 (IMSI detach procedure in the network) describes the network's handling: it may set an inactive indication for the IMSI, sends no response to the mobile station, releases locally any ongoing MM connections, and starts the normal RR connection release procedure.

questions.question: According to TS 24.008 clause 4.3.4.1, in a shared GERAN network, how is the chosen PLMN identity indicated to the network within the IMSI DETACH INDICATION message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.008 clause 4.3.4.1 states that for a shared GERAN in A/Gb mode, if the MS is a GERAN network sharing supporting MS, the chosen PLMN identity shall be indicated to the GERAN in the IMSI DETACH INDICATION message using the Skip Indicator IE.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 24.301 defines the network-initiated ESM information request procedure, and under what two conditions must the ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message be sent?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.301 clause 6.6.1.2.2 (ESM information request initiated by the network) states the MME sends the ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message to the UE, starting timer T3489. This message shall be sent only after the security context has been set up, and only if the ESM information transfer flag was set in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message.

questions.question: The PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message is defined for both the MME (TS 24.301) and the TWAG (TS 24.244). Which clauses define it, and what ESM/cause value does the TS 24.301 version list that the TS 24.244 version does not?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.301 clause 6.5.2.4 (UE requested PDN disconnection procedure not accepted by the network, MME side) lists ESM cause values #35, #43, #49, and #95-111. TS 24.244 clause 5.4.2 (Procedure description, TWAG side) lists only #35 and #95-111. So the TS 24.301 (MME) version additionally lists cause #43 "invalid EPS bearer identity" and #49 "last PDN disconnection not allowed", both absent from the TWAG version.

questions.question: According to TS 24.244 clause 5.4.2, what does the UE do upon receipt of the PDN DISCONNECT ACCEPT message from the TWAG?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.244 clause 5.4.2 states that upon receipt of the PDN DISCONNECT ACCEPT message, the UE shall stop timer T3592, deactivate all resources associated with the PDN connection, and enter the states PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE and PDN CONNECTIVITY NOT ESTABLISHED.

questions.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 6.5.2.4, when is ESM cause #49 "last PDN disconnection not allowed" not applicable in a PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.301 clause 6.5.2.4 states that if EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is supported by both the UE and the MME, then ESM cause #49 "last PDN disconnection not allowed" is not applicable.

questions.question: According to TS 24.008, when the MS rejects a network-requested PDP context activation with a REQUEST PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION REJECT message, what identifier must the reject message reuse from the original request, and what does the network do upon receiving it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.008 clause 6.1.3.1.4 (Unsuccessful PDP context activation requested by the network) states the REQUEST PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION REJECT message must contain the same TI (Transaction Identifier) as the REQUEST PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION, plus a cause code. Upon receiving it, the network shall stop timer T3385 and enter state PDP-INACTIVE.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.423 defines the SGNB RELEASE REQUIRED/CONFIRM exchange, and which node initiates it toward which node?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 clause 8.7.10.2 (Successful Operation) defines the SgNB initiated SgNB Release procedure. The en-gNB initiates the procedure by sending the SGNB RELEASE REQUIRED message to the MeNB, and the MeNB replies with the SGNB RELEASE CONFIRM message.

questions.question: The RESOURCE STATUS REQUEST message supports a "partial stop" Registration Request value in X2AP (TS 36.423) but not in XnAP (TS 38.423). Which clauses define the Resource Status Reporting Initiation procedure in each, and which node initiates it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.4.10.2 (XnAP, Successful Operation) defines the Resource Status Reporting Initiation procedure with Registration Request values "start", "stop", and "add", initiated by NG-RAN node1 toward NG-RAN node2. TS 36.423 clause 8.3.6.2 (X2AP, Successful Operation) defines the same-named procedure initiated by eNB1 toward eNB2, with an additional "partial stop" value (if supported) that stops measurement for only the cells indicated in the Cell To Report IE list — a value not present in the XnAP version.

questions.question: According to TS 38.423 clause 8.4.10.2, which IE does NG-RAN node2 include in the RESOURCE STATUS UPDATE message if the first bit of the Report Characteristics IE ("PRB Periodic") is set to 1?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.4.10.2 states that if the first bit, "PRB Periodic", of the Report Characteristics IE is set to 1, NG-RAN node2 shall include the Radio Resource Status IE in the RESOURCE STATUS UPDATE message for each cell.

questions.question: The HANDOVER REPORT message exists in both XnAP (TS 38.423) and X2AP (TS 36.423). Which clauses define its successful operation, and which node initiates it toward which node in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.4.8.2 (XnAP) defines the Handover Report procedure, initiated by NG-RAN node1 sending the HANDOVER REPORT message to NG-RAN node2 to indicate a detected mobility-related problem. TS 36.423 clause 8.3.10.2 (X2AP) defines the same-named procedure, initiated by an eNB1 sending HANDOVER REPORT to eNB2 for the same purpose.

questions.question: According to TS 36.423 clause 8.3.10.2, which IE must the HANDOVER REPORT message include if the Handover Report Type IE is set to "HO to wrong cell"?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 clause 8.3.10.2 states that if the Handover Report Type IE is set to "HO to wrong cell", the Re-establishment cell ECGI IE shall be included in the HANDOVER REPORT message.

questions.question: The XnAP HANDOVER REPORT message supports "Inter-system ping-pong" as a Handover Report Type, but not the "InterRAT ping-pong" value that X2AP supports. According to TS 38.423 clause 8.4.8.2, what does NG-RAN node2 deduce when the Handover Report Type IE is set to "Inter-system ping-pong"?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.4.8.2 states that if the Handover Report Type IE is set to "Inter-system ping-pong", NG-RAN node2 shall deduce that a completed handover from a cell of NG-RAN node2 to a cell in another system might have resulted in an inter-system ping-pong, and the UE was successfully handed over to a cell of NG-RAN node1, indicated by the Target cell CGI IE.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 38.423 defines the Mobility Settings Change procedure, and which message does NG-RAN node2 send in reply to an accepted MOBILITY CHANGE REQUEST?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.4.9.2 (Successful Operation) defines the Mobility Settings Change procedure. NG-RAN node1 initiates it by sending the MOBILITY CHANGE REQUEST message to NG-RAN node2, and if NG-RAN node2 is able to successfully complete the request, it replies with a MOBILITY CHANGE ACKNOWLEDGE message.

questions.question: The PRS Configuration Exchange procedure and its PRS CONFIGURATION RESPONSE message are defined in both NRPPa (TS 38.455, LMF-to-NG-RAN) and F1AP (TS 38.473, gNB-CU-to-gNB-DU). Which clauses define the successful operation in each, and which node initiates the request in each protocol?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.455 clause 8.2.11.2 (NRPPa) defines the PRS Configuration Exchange procedure with the LMF initiating it by sending a PRS CONFIGURATION REQUEST message to the NG-RAN. TS 38.473 clause 8.13.17.2 (F1AP) defines the same-named procedure with the gNB-CU initiating it by sending a PRS CONFIGURATION REQUEST message to the gNB-DU. In both, if DL-PRS transmission is successfully configured or updated for at least one TRP, the receiving node responds with the PRS CONFIGURATION RESPONSE message.

questions.question: According to TS 38.473 clause 8.13.17.2, what does the gNB-DU do with the information in the PRS Transmission Off Information IE if the PRS Configuration Request Type IE is set to "off"?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.473 clause 8.13.17.2 states that if the PRS Configuration Request Type IE is set to "off", the gNB-DU should, if supported, use the information in the PRS Transmission Off Information IE to turn off the DL-PRS transmission for the indicated TRP(s), PRS Resource Set(s), or PRS Resource(s).

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.413 defines the E-RAB MODIFICATION INDICATION message, and which node initiates the E-RAB Modification Indication procedure toward the MME?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.2.4.2 (Successful Operation) defines the E-RAB Modification Indication procedure. The eNB initiates it by sending an E-RAB MODIFICATION INDICATION message to the MME.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.423 defines the SeNB Addition Preparation procedure, and which timer does the MeNB start when sending the SENB ADDITION REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 clause 8.6.1.2 (Successful Operation) defines the SeNB Addition Preparation procedure. The MeNB initiates it by sending the SENB ADDITION REQUEST message to the SeNB, starting timer TDcprep when it sends the message.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.413 defines the E-RAB RELEASE INDICATION message, and what must it contain at minimum?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.2.3.2.2 (E-RAB Release Indication - eNB initiated) defines the E-RAB RELEASE INDICATION message, sent by the eNB towards the MME. It must contain at least one E-RAB released at the eNB, in the E-RAB Released List IE.

questions.question: According to TS 36.413 clause 8.2.3.2.2, what procedure should the eNB use instead of E-RAB Release Indication if it wants to remove all remaining E-RABs due to user inactivity?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.2.3.2.2 states that if the eNB wants to remove all remaining E-RABs, e.g. for user inactivity, the UE Context Release Request procedure shall be used instead of the E-RAB Release Indication procedure.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 36.413 defines the NAS NON DELIVERY INDICATION procedure, and under what two circumstances does the eNB send it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.6.2.4 defines the NAS NON DELIVERY INDICATION procedure. The eNB sends the message when it decides not to start delivery of a NAS message received over a UE-associated logical S1-connection, or when it is unable to ensure the message has been received by the UE, including the non-delivered NAS message and an appropriate cause value (e.g. "S1 intra system Handover Triggered").

questions.question: Which clause of TS 25.423 defines the RNSAP Enhanced Relocation procedure, and which node initiates it by sending the ENHANCED RELOCATION REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.423 clause 8.3.28.2 (Successful Operation) defines the Enhanced Relocation procedure. The SRNC initiates the procedure by sending an ENHANCED RELOCATION REQUEST message, starting timer TRELOCprep.

questions.question: According to TS 25.423 clause 8.3.28.2, what must the DRNC do if the ENHANCED RELOCATION REQUEST message includes the SRNC-ID?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.423 clause 8.3.28.2 states that if the ENHANCED RELOCATION REQUEST message includes SRNC-ID, the DRNC shall create a UE Context for this UE and allocate a D-RNTI for the UE Context.

questions.question: According to TS 24.501 clause 6.3.2.4, which 5GSM cause values typically appear in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message the UE sends when rejecting a network-requested PDU session modification?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.501 clause 6.3.2.4 (Network-requested PDU session modification procedure not accepted by the UE) states the 5GSM cause IE of the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message typically indicates one of: #26 insufficient resources; #44 semantic error in packet filter(s); #45 syntactical error in packet filter(s); #83 semantic error in the QoS operation; or #84 syntactical error in the QoS operation.

questions.question: According to TS 24.501 clause 6.3.2.4, what does the SMF do upon receipt of a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message while in state PDU SESSION MODIFICATION PENDING?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.501 clause 6.3.2.4 states that upon receipt of a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message with a 5GSM cause value in state PDU SESSION MODIFICATION PENDING, the SMF shall stop timer T3591, enter the state PDU SESSION ACTIVE, and abort the PDU session modification procedure.

questions.question: According to TS 25.331 clause 8.5.64.3, what must the UE do with the logged measurement results in the LOGGED_MEAS_REPORT_VARIABLE after including them in the UE INFORMATION RESPONSE message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.331 clause 8.5.64.3 (Reception of the UE INFORMATION REQUEST message by the UE) states that the UE shall clear the logged measurement results included in the list of IEs "Logged Measurement Info-FDD" or "Logged Measurement Info-TDD" from the LOGGED_MEAS_REPORT_VARIABLE after including them in the UE INFORMATION RESPONSE.

questions.question: The COMMON MEASUREMENT REPORT message and its Common Measurement Reporting procedure are defined near-identically in RNSAP (TS 25.423, RNC2-initiated) and NBAP (TS 25.433, Node B-initiated). Which clauses define the successful operation in each, and which port does the NBAP version use?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.423 clause 8.5.3.2 (RNSAP) defines the Common Measurement Reporting procedure as initiated by RNC2 sending COMMON MEASUREMENT REPORT. TS 25.433 clause 8.2.9.2 (NBAP) defines the same-named procedure as initiated by the Node B, and specifies that the COMMON MEASUREMENT REPORT message uses the Node B Control Port.

questions.question: According to TS 25.423 clause 8.5.3.2, what must the Common Measurement Value Information IE indicate if the achieved measurement accuracy does not fulfil the given accuracy requirement?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.423 clause 8.5.3.2 states that if the achieved measurement accuracy does not fulfil the given accuracy requirement (per TS 25.133 and TS 25.123) or the measurement is temporarily unavailable (with Measurement Recovery Behavior supported), the Common Measurement Value Information IE shall indicate Measurement not Available.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 24.501 defines the PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation, and what does the SMF set the PTI IE and EAP message IE of the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message to?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.501 clause 6.3.1.2.1 (PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation) states that to initiate the procedure, the SMF creates a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, sets the PTI IE to "No procedure transaction identity assigned", and sets the EAP message IE to the EAP-request message provided by the DN or generated locally, then sends the message and starts timer T3590. The message definition also appears in ts_24_501_8.3.4.1 (Message definition; Direction: network to UE), ts_24_501_8.3.5.1 (Message definition; Direction: UE to network).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 24.501 clause 6.3.1.2.1 (PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation) states that to initiate the procedure, the SMF creates a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, sets the PTI IE to "No procedure transaction identity assigned", and sets the EAP message IE to the EAP-request message provided by the DN or generated locally, then sends the message and starts timer T3590.

questions.question: According to TS 24.501 clause 6.3.1.2.1, what does the UE do with the EAP message received in a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.501 clause 6.3.1.2.1 states that upon receipt of a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message and PDU session ID, the UE passes the EAP message received in the EAP message IE to the upper layers; apart from this action and stopping relevant timers (T3396, T3584, T3485 if running), the DN-initiated authentication and authorization procedure is transparent to the UE's 5GSM layer. The message definition also appears in ts_24_501_8.3.4.1 (Message definition; Direction: network to UE), ts_24_501_8.3.5.1 (Message definition; Direction: UE to network).
questions.reference_answer_legacy: TS 24.501 clause 6.3.1.2.1 states that upon receipt of a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message and PDU session ID, the UE passes the EAP message received in the EAP message IE to the upper layers; apart from this action and stopping relevant timers (T3396, T3584, T3485 if running), the DN-initiated authentication and authorization procedure is transparent to the UE's 5GSM layer.

questions.question: The MEASUREMENT REQUEST/RESPONSE exchange exists in both NRPPa (TS 38.455, LMF-to-NG-RAN) and SLmAP (TS 36.459, E-SMLC-to-LMU). Which clauses define the successful operation in each, and which node initiates it in each protocol?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.455 clause 8.5.1.2 (NRPPa) defines the Measurement procedure, with the LMF initiating it by sending a MEASUREMENT REQUEST message to the NG-RAN node. TS 36.459 clause 8.2.1.2 (SLmAP) defines the same-named procedure, with the E-SMLC initiating it by sending a MEASUREMENT REQUEST message to the LMU.

questions.question: According to TS 36.459 clause 8.2.1.2, under what condition does the E-SMLC include the deltaSS IE in the MEASUREMENT REQUEST message, and what does its presence indicate to the LMU?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.459 clause 8.2.1.2 states the E-SMLC shall include the deltaSS IE in the MEASUREMENT REQUEST message if SRS sequence hopping is enabled for that particular measurement; if the deltaSS IE is included, the LMU shall consider that SRS sequence hopping is enabled for the measurement being requested.

questions.question: According to TS 38.455 clause 8.5.1.2, what does the NG-RAN node do differently in its MEASUREMENT RESPONSE if the Report Characteristics IE in the MEASUREMENT REQUEST is set to "OnDemand" versus "Periodic"?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.455 clause 8.5.1.2 states that if Report Characteristics is "OnDemand", the NG-RAN node returns the measurement results directly in the MEASUREMENT RESPONSE message, and the LMF considers reporting terminated. If it is "Periodic", the NG-RAN node initiates the corresponding measurements and replies with MEASUREMENT RESPONSE without any measurement results, then periodically sends MEASUREMENT REPORT messages at the requested periodicity.

questions.question: The UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message is defined in both S1AP (TS 36.413) and RANAP (TS 25.413). Which clauses define its successful operation, and which node sends it to which node in each protocol?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.3.5.2 (S1AP) defines the UE Radio Capability Match procedure with the MME sending UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST to the eNB. TS 25.413 clause 8.47.2 (RANAP) defines the same-named procedure with the SGSN sending UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST to the RNC.

questions.question: According to TS 36.413 clause 8.3.5.2, what does the eNB use the UE Radio Capability IE for, if it is contained in the UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.3.5.2 states that if the UE Radio Capability IE is contained in the UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message, the eNB shall use it to determine the value of the Voice Support Match Indicator IE to be included in the UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH RESPONSE message.

questions.question: According to TS 25.413 clause 8.47.2, which node initiates the UE Radio Capability Match procedure, and is the RNC's response mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.413 clause 8.47.2 states the SGSN initiates the procedure by sending a UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message to the RNC. The RNC responds with a UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH RESPONSE message only if supported — the response is conditional on support, not unconditionally mandatory.

questions.question: According to TS 36.413 clause 8.3.5.2, what does the MME do if the UE-associated logical S1-connection is not yet established when initiating the UE Radio Capability Match procedure?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.3.5.2 states that if the UE-associated logical S1-connection is not established, the MME shall allocate a unique MME UE S1AP ID for the UE and include the MME UE S1AP ID IE in the UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message; upon receiving this IE, the eNB establishes the UE-associated logical S1-connection.

questions.question: According to TS 23.401 clause 5.11.2, which two S1 interface messages can the MME use to trigger the E-UTRAN to request UE Radio Capability from the UE and upload it via UE CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION, when no INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST is sent under CIoT EPS Optimisations?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.401 clause 5.11.2 (UE Radio Capability Handling) states that under CIoT EPS Optimisations, if the MME does not send an S1 interface INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST, it should obtain UE Radio Capability information by sending either the DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT message (indicating a UE Radio Capability request) or the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message (without UE Radio Capability information included) to the E-UTRAN, which triggers the E-UTRAN to request the capability from the UE and upload it via the S1 interface UE CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION message.

questions.question: What is the Resource Type, Default Priority Level and Packet Delay Budget of 5QI 82 in the standardized 5QI table?
questions.reference_answer: 5QI 82 has Resource Type Delay-critical GBR, Default Priority Level 19, and Packet Delay Budget 10 ms (per NOTE 4), used for Discrete Automation.

questions.question: According to the standardized 5QI table in TS 23.501, what is the Default Maximum Data Burst Volume for 5QI 89, and what example service uses it?
questions.reference_answer: 5QI 89 has a Default Maximum Data Burst Volume of 17000 bytes, used for visual content for cloud/edge/split rendering.

questions.question: In the standardized 5QI table of TS 23.501, which 5QI values carry NOTE 12 (assignable only upon request from the network side, never by the UE or an application)?
questions.reference_answer: NOTE 12 in TS 23.501 clause 5.7.4 applies to 5QI values 65, 66, 67, 69 and 70. Each of these can only be assigned upon request from the network side; the UE and any application running on it are not allowed to request these 5QI values.

questions.question: What Packet Error Rate does 5QI 3 specify in the standardized 5QI table of TS 23.501, and what example services use it?
questions.reference_answer: 5QI 3 specifies a Packet Error Rate of 10-3, used for Real Time Gaming, V2X messages, electricity distribution (medium voltage), and process automation monitoring.

questions.question: In TS 29.502's Cause enumeration, what does the value REL_DUE_TO_S_NSSAI_CONGESTION indicate?
questions.reference_answer: REL_DUE_TO_S_NSSAI_CONGESTION indicates that the SMF has detected congestion for the requested S-NSSAI and performs overload control for that S-NSSAI, which does not allow the PDU session to be established.

questions.question: Which value in TS 29.502's Cause enumeration indicates that a PDU session must be transferred from an old I-SMF to a new I-SMF?
questions.reference_answer: The value ISMF_CONTEXT_TRANSFER indicates that the PDU session shall be transferred from the old I-SMF to the new I-SMF.

questions.question: What does the value DCSF represent in the NFType enumeration of TS 29.510?
questions.reference_answer: DCSF represents the Network Function DCSF in the NFType enumeration of TS 29.510.

questions.question: What does the value MB_SMF represent in the NFType enumeration of TS 29.510?
questions.reference_answer: MB_SMF represents the Network Function MB-SMF in the NFType enumeration of TS 29.510.

questions.question: In TS 29.517's AfEvent enumeration, what does the value GNSS_ASSISTANCE_DATA indicate?
questions.reference_answer: GNSS_ASSISTANCE_DATA indicates that the subscribed/notified event is GNSS Assistance Data Collection.

questions.question: According to TS 29.514's AfEvent enumeration, what does the value SAT_CATEGORY_CHG indicate?
questions.reference_answer: SAT_CATEGORY_CHG indicates that the SMF has detected a change between different satellite backhaul categories, or between satellite and non-satellite backhaul.

questions.question: In TS 29.520's NwdafEvent enumeration, what does the value LOC_ACCURACY indicate is being subscribed to?
questions.reference_answer: LOC_ACCURACY indicates that the event subscribed is the Location Accuracy information.

questions.question: What does the FailureCode value AN_GW_FAILED indicate in TS 29.512, and what should the PCF refrain from doing while this condition holds?
questions.reference_answer: AN_GW_FAILED indicates that the AN-Gateway has failed, and the PCF should refrain from sending policy decisions to the SMF until it is informed that the S-GW has been recovered. This value shall not be used if the SM Policy association modification procedure is initiated for session rule removal only.

questions.question: Which specifications define a PositioningMethod enumeration value for uplink Time Difference of Arrival based on NR signals, and what name does each use for it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.572 clause 6.1.6.3.6 names it UL_TDOA, and TS 33.128 clause 7.3.3.2.52 names it uLTDOA. Both describe Uplink Time Difference of Arrival (UL-TDOA) based on NR signals.

questions.question: Which specifications define the MULTI-RTT value of the PositioningMethod enumeration, and how do they describe it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.545 clause B.2.5.3 and TS 29.572 clause 6.1.6.3.6 both define MULTI-RTT in their PositioningMethod enumeration, describing it as Multi-Round Trip Time Positioning (Multi-RTT based on NR signals).

questions.question: Which specifications define the RELATIVE_2D_LOCATION_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSE / Relative 2D location shape in their SupportedGADShapes enumeration, and what does the value describe?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.572 clause 6.1.6.3.4 defines RELATIVE_2D_LOCATION_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSE, describing a relative 2D location with uncertainty ellipse — a point in 2D local coordinates with origin corresponding to another known point, distances r1 and r2, and an angle of orientation A.

questions.question: Which two specifications both define a LOCAL_3D_POINT_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSOID value in their SupportedGADShapes enumeration, and what does it represent?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.546 clause C.1.4.5.1 and TS 29.572 clause 6.1.6.3.4 both define LOCAL_3D_POINT_UNCERTAINTY_ELLIPSOID, representing a Local 3D point with uncertainty ellipsoid.

questions.question: What does the SmfEvent value SATB_CH indicate in TS 29.508's Enumeration: SmfEvent?
questions.reference_answer: SATB_CH indicates that the SMF has detected a change between different satellite category, or non-satellite backhaul.

questions.question: According to TS 29.508's SmfEvent enumeration, what does the value TRAFFIC_CORRELATION indicate?
questions.reference_answer: TRAFFIC_CORRELATION indicates that the SMF provides 5GC-determined traffic correlation information for a set of UEs identified by a Traffic Correlation ID.

questions.question: In TS 29.518's AmfEventType enumeration, what does an NF receive by subscribing to the LOSS_OF_CONNECTIVITY event, and under what three conditions is it detected?
questions.reference_answer: LOSS_OF_CONNECTIVITY lets an NF receive the event report of a UE or group of UEs when the AMF detects the target UE is no longer reachable for signalling or user plane communication. This is identified when the Mobile Reachable timer expires in the AMF, when the UE detaches, or when the AMF deregisters from the UDM for an active UE. If the UE is already unreachable when the event is subscribed, the AMF reports it directly.

questions.question: According to TS 29.518's AmfEventType enumeration, what does the SUBSCRIPTION_ID_CHANGE event type inform the NF service consumer of, and does it require explicit subscription?
questions.reference_answer: SUBSCRIPTION_ID_CHANGE is used by the AMF to inform the NF service consumer that the subscription Id for the event subscription has changed (e.g. at target AMF creation during mobility registration or handover involving an AMF change). This event needs no explicit subscription from an NF service consumer.

questions.question: In TS 29.122's MonitoringType enumeration, what does the value AREA_OF_INTEREST let the SCS/AS be notified of?
questions.reference_answer: AREA_OF_INTEREST lets the SCS/AS request to be notified when the UE (i.e. UAV) moves in or out of the geographic area.

questions.question: According to TS 29.122's MonitoringType enumeration, what does the SESSION_INACTIVITY_TIME value let the AF be notified of?
questions.reference_answer: SESSION_INACTIVITY_TIME lets the AF request to be notified of the session inactivity time of the measured UE PDU Session.

questions.question: In TS 29.122's UserPlaneEvent enumeration, what does the value BAT_OFFSET_INFO indicate?
questions.reference_answer: BAT_OFFSET_INFO indicates the network-provided BAT (Burst Arrival Time) offset and the optionally adjusted periodicity.

questions.question: According to TS 29.122's UserPlaneEvent enumeration, what does the value L4S_NOT_AVAILABLE indicate?
questions.reference_answer: L4S_NOT_AVAILABLE indicates that the ECN marking for L4S of one or more SDFs is not available.

questions.question: What does the value RANGINGSL_PRIVACY represent in TS 29.503's DataSetName enumeration?
questions.reference_answer: RANGINGSL_PRIVACY represents Ranging and Sidelink Positioning Privacy Subscription Data in TS 29.503's DataSetName enumeration.

questions.question: What does the value UEC_AMF represent in TS 29.503's DataSetName enumeration?
questions.reference_answer: UEC_AMF represents UE Context in AMF Data in TS 29.503's DataSetName enumeration.

questions.question: According to TS 29.562's DataSetName enumeration, what does the value PRIORITY_DATA represent?
questions.reference_answer: PRIORITY_DATA represents Service Priority Levels in TS 29.562's DataSetName enumeration.

questions.question: What does the value NIDD_AUTH represent in TS 29.505's ProvisionedDataSetName enumeration?
questions.reference_answer: NIDD_AUTH represents NIDD Authorization Data in TS 29.505's ProvisionedDataSetName enumeration.

questions.question: What does the value PP_PROF represent in TS 29.505's ProvisionedDataSetName enumeration?
questions.reference_answer: PP_PROF represents Parameter Provisioning Profile Data in TS 29.505's ProvisionedDataSetName enumeration.

questions.question: In TS 29.510's UPInterfaceType enumeration, what does the value N9ROAMING represent?
questions.reference_answer: N9ROAMING represents the User Plane Interface N9 for the roaming interface in TS 29.510's UPInterfaceType enumeration.

questions.question: In TS 29.510's UPInterfaceType enumeration, what does the value N3UNTRUSTEDN3GPP represent?
questions.reference_answer: N3UNTRUSTEDN3GPP represents the User Plane Interface N3 Untrusted Non-3GPP access in TS 29.510's UPInterfaceType enumeration.

questions.question: TS 32.291 defines the NodeFunctionality enumeration in two different clauses. Which two clauses, and what does the I_SMF value mean in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.291 clause 6.1.6.3.4 and clause 6.2.5.3.4 both define a NodeFunctionality enumeration. In both, the I_SMF value identifies that the node is an I-SMF, applicable only for a PDU session served by SMF + I-SMF.

questions.question: According to TS 32.291's NodeFunctionality enumeration (clause 6.1.6.3.4), what does the value 5G_DDNMF identify?
questions.reference_answer: 5G_DDNMF identifies that the NF is a 5G DDNMF in TS 32.291's NodeFunctionality enumeration.

questions.question: In TS 29.571's RatType enumeration, what does the value NR_EREDCAP represent?
questions.reference_answer: NR_EREDCAP represents the NR eRedCap access type in TS 29.571's RatType enumeration.

questions.question: In TS 29.571's RatType enumeration, what does the value WB_E_UTRAN_OTHERSAT represent?
questions.reference_answer: WB_E_UTRAN_OTHERSAT represents the WB-E-UTRAN (OTHERSAT) satellite access type in TS 29.571's RatType enumeration.

questions.question: According to TS 29.520's AnalyticsSubset enumeration, what event does the TIME_TO_COLLISION value apply to, and what does it indicate?
questions.reference_answer: TIME_TO_COLLISION is only applicable to the RELATIVE_PROXIMITY event prediction, and it indicates the time until a collision with another UE happens.

questions.question: According to TS 29.520's AnalyticsSubset enumeration, what event does the value NUM_OF_EXCEED_RES_USAGE_LOAD_LEVEL_THR apply to, and what does it indicate?
questions.reference_answer: NUM_OF_EXCEED_RES_USAGE_LOAD_LEVEL_THR is only applicable to the NSI_LOAD_LEVEL event, and it indicates the number of times the resource usage threshold of the network slice instance is reached or exceeded, if a threshold value is provided by the consumer.

questions.question: In TS 29.512's PolicyControlRequestTrigger enumeration, what does the value VPLMN_QOS_CH indicate?
questions.reference_answer: VPLMN_QOS_CH indicates that the NF service consumer has detected a change of the QoS supported in the VPLMN, or a change between the case where QoS constraints are applicable and the case where they are not applicable (e.g. the UE moves back from home-routed to non-roaming, or vice versa).

questions.question: In TS 29.512's PolicyControlRequestTrigger enumeration, what does the value GROUP_ID_LIST_CHG indicate?
questions.reference_answer: GROUP_ID_LIST_CHG indicates that the UE Internal Group Identifier(s) has changed: the NF service consumer reports that the UDM-provided list of group Ids has changed.

questions.question: What does the SupplementaryServiceType value ECT stand for in TS 32.291, and what does it indicate?
questions.reference_answer: ECT indicates explicit communication transfer in TS 32.291's SupplementaryServiceType enumeration.

questions.question: What does the SupplementaryServiceType value CCNR indicate in TS 32.291's enumeration?
questions.reference_answer: CCNR indicates completion of communications on no reply in TS 32.291's SupplementaryServiceType enumeration.

questions.question: In TS 32.291's TriggerType enumeration (clause 6.1.6.3.6), what does the value MBS_CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED_WITH_UPF indicate?
questions.reference_answer: MBS_CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED_WITH_UPF indicates that a new UPF has established a connection with the MB-UPF in the MBS session.

questions.question: TS 32.291 defines a TriggerType enumeration in two clauses. What does the QOS_CHANGE value mean in clause 6.1.6.3.6, and what does the corresponding value mean in the request vs response message per clause 6.2.5.3.5's description of CHANGE_OF_3GPP_PS_DATA_OFF_STATUS?
questions.reference_answer: In clause 6.1.6.3.6, QOS_CHANGE in a request message indicates that a QoS change has happened (any element of QoSData may cause it); in a response message, it indicates that a change of authorized QoS shall cause the service consumer to ask for re-authorization of the associated quota. In clause 6.2.5.3.5, CHANGE_OF_3GPP_PS_DATA_OFF_STATUS in a request message indicates that a change of 3GPP PS Data Off status has happened.

questions.question: In TS 29.122's Accuracy enumeration, what does the value TWAN_ID mean?
questions.reference_answer: TWAN_ID means the SCS/AS requests to be notified using TWAN identifier level location accuracy.

questions.question: In TS 24.545's Accuracy enumeration, what does the value MBSFN_AREA indicate?
questions.reference_answer: MBSFN_AREA indicates the current MBSFN area.

questions.question: According to TS 29.122's DeliveryStatus enumeration, what does the value SUCCESS_UNACKNOWLEDGED mean?
questions.reference_answer: SUCCESS_UNACKNOWLEDGED means reliable delivery was not acknowledged by the UE.

questions.question: According to TS 29.538's DeliveryStatus enumeration, what does the value DELY_STORED indicate?
questions.reference_answer: DELY_STORED indicates that the message is stored for deferred delivery.

questions.question: Which command code does TS 29.230 assign to the Update-Location-Request/Answer (ULR/ULA) command, and in which specification is it further specified?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.230 clause 5.1 assigns command code 316 to Update-Location-Request/Answer (ULR/ULA), further specified in TS 29.272.

questions.question: Which command code does TS 29.230 assign to the Provide-Location-Request/Answer (PLR/PLA) command, and in which specification is it further specified?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.230 clause 5.1 assigns command code 8388620 to Provide-Location-Request/Answer (PLR/PLA), further specified in TS 29.172.

questions.question: In TS 29.520's EventId enumeration (clause 5.2.6.3.3), what does the value QOS_SUSTAINABILITY represent?
questions.reference_answer: QOS_SUSTAINABILITY represents the analytics of QoS sustainability in a certain area.

questions.question: What does the ServiceName value 'nmfaf-3dadatamanagement' represent in TS 29.510's ServiceName enumeration?
questions.reference_answer: 'nmfaf-3dadatamanagement' represents the Nmfaf_3daDataManagement service offered by the MFAF, in TS 29.510's ServiceName enumeration.

questions.question: What does the ServiceName value 'nhss-gba-sdm' represent in TS 29.510's ServiceName enumeration?
questions.reference_answer: 'nhss-gba-sdm' represents the Nhss_gbaSubscriberDataManagement Service offered by the HSS, in TS 29.510's ServiceName enumeration.

questions.question: According to TS 29.060's GTP information element type table, which IE type value is assigned to the RIM Routing Address IE, and what length type does it use?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.060's General clause (7.7.0) assigns IETYPE 158 to the RIM Routing Address IE (format TLV, reference 7.7.57), with a Variable length type (Number of Fixed Octets not applicable).

questions.question: According to TS 29.060's GTP information element type table, what format and fixed length does the Charging ID IE use, and what IE type value is it assigned?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.060's General clause (7.7.0) assigns IETYPE 127 to the Charging ID IE, format TV (reference 7.7.26), Length Type Fixed, with 4 fixed octets.

questions.question: According to TS 29.276's Information Element Assignments table, what is IE type value 1 assigned to, and what is its reference clause?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.276's Information Element Assignments clause (7.5.1) assigns IE type value 1 to the Session ID information element, a variable-length IE referenced in clause 7.5.2.

questions.question: Which specification defines TRACE as a value of the HttpMethod enumeration, and what does it mean?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.573 clause 6.1.5.3.4 defines TRACE as a value of the HttpMethod enumeration, meaning the HTTP TRACE Method.

questions.question: Which specification defines CONNECT as a value of the HttpMethod enumeration, and what does it mean?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.573 clause 6.1.5.3.4 defines CONNECT as a value of the HttpMethod enumeration, meaning the HTTP CONNECT Method.

questions.question: Which specification's HttpMethod enumeration includes the HEAD value at clause 5.2.3.4, and what does it mean?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.571 clause 5.2.3.4 defines HEAD as a value of the HttpMethod enumeration, meaning the HTTP HEAD method.

questions.question: In TS 24.545's Accuracy enumeration, what does the value MBMS_SA indicate?
questions.reference_answer: MBMS_SA indicates the current MBMS serving area.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Register service operation, and what mandatory inputs does the consumer supply?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.9.5 defines Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Register, by which a consumer registers use and monitoring capability for an ML Model at an NWDAF containing MTLF. Required inputs are the Consumer NF ID and the Unique ML Model identifier; the required output is an ML Model monitoring registration ID.

questions.question: According to TS 29.831 clause 6.11.1, when does the NRF use the Nudr_GroupIDmap_Query service operation, and what does it retrieve?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.831 clause 6.11.1 states that if the NRF has no stored configuration mapping identity sets/ranges to NF Group ID locally, the NRF can retrieve the NF Group ID corresponding to a specific subscriber identifier from the UDR using the Nudr_GroupIDmap_Query service operation.

questions.question: Which clauses of TS 23.502 and TS 23.540 define the Nudm_ReportSMDeliveryStatus_Request service operation, and what inputs does it require?
