questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.3.9.2 and TS 23.540 clause 6.2.2.2 both define Nudm_ReportSMDeliveryStatus_Request, which reports the SM-Delivery Status to the UDM. Required inputs are GPSI and SM-Delivery status; the required output is the Report SM-Delivery status result.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 33.501 defines the Nnssaaf_NSSAA_Authenticate service operation, and what does the NF consumer require the NSSAAF to do?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.501 clause 14.4.1.2 defines Nnssaaf_NSSAA_Authenticate: the NF consumer requires the NSSAAF to relay Network Slice specific authentication messages towards the AAA-S handling the Network Slice specific authentication for the requested S-NSSAI.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.548 defines the Neasdf_DNSContext_Create service operation, and what four inputs are required?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.548 clause 7.1.2.2 defines Neasdf_DNSContext_Create, used to create a DNS context in the EASDF. The required inputs are UE IP address, DNN, S-NSSAI, and Notification Endpoint.

questions.question: In HR-SBO scenarios, why might the V-SMF set the UE IP address to an unspecified/zero value when invoking Neasdf_DNSContext_Create, according to TS 23.548 clause 7.1.2.2?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.548 clause 7.1.2.2 explains that in the HR-SBO scenario, the V-SMF can invoke Neasdf_DNSContext_Create to obtain the IP address of the V-EASDF while the UE UP address has not yet been determined; if the V-SMF is not aware of the UE IP address at that point, it can set the UE IP address to an unspecified value such as zero.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Namf_MT_EnableUEReachability service operation, and what does the AMF do differently depending on whether the UE is in CM-CONNECTED or CM-IDLE state?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.4.2 defines Namf_MT_EnableUEReachability, used by a consumer NF to request enabling UE reachability. The consumer does not need to know the UE state: if the UE is in CM-CONNECTED state, the AMF accepts the request and responds immediately; if the UE is in CM-IDLE state, the AMF may page the UE and respond only after the UE enters CM-CONNECTED state.

questions.question: According to TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.4.2, what does the AMF provide in its response to Namf_MT_EnableUEReachability if the related UE is not served by that AMF but the serving AMF is known?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.4.2 states that if the related UE is not served by the AMF and the AMF knows which AMF is serving the UE, the AMF provides redirection information, which the NF consumer can use to resend the UE-related message to the AMF that actually serves the UE.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnrf_Bootstrapping_Get service operation, and what does it retrieve?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.7.5.2 defines Nnrf_Bootstrapping_Get, used to get the NRF service instances, their addresses, and associated data (required output: NRF service instances and their endpoint addresses; optional output: NF Set ID, NRF instance ID, OAuth2 requirement for authorization, NRF status). It requires no inputs.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Subscribe service operation, and what does it let a consumer subscribe to?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.17.2.2 defines Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Subscribe, used to subscribe to notification of changes in the status of policy counters available at the CHF, and to retrieve the status of the policy counters for which the subscription is accepted by the CHF.

questions.question: According to TS 23.502 clause 5.2.17.2.2, what SUPI-related input is required for the Initial Spending Limit request variant of Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Subscribe, versus the Intermediate Spending Limit report variant?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.17.2.2 requires SUPI as input for the Initial Spending Limit request, while the Intermediate Spending Limit report variant instead requires the SubscriptionCorrelationId.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 29.176 gives the general description of the Nmf_MRM_Update service operation, and what does it say can be added, modified, or deleted within an Update request?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.176 clause 5.2.2.3.1 (General) states that Nmf_MRM_Update is used by an NF service consumer to update one or multiple existing media resources within a specific media context on the MF, and that Terminations and/or Medias can be added, modified, or deleted within an Update request.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.247 defines the Nnef_MBSTMGI_Allocate service operation, and what input can make the Number of TMGIs input zero?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.4.2.2 defines Nnef_MBSTMGI_Allocate, used by the NF Service Consumer to request allocation of TMGI(s) or refresh the expiry time of already allocated TMGI(s). The required Number of TMGIs input may be zero if only a refresh of expiry time is requested.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.273 defines the Ngmlc_Location_LocationUpdate service operation, and what event triggers it according to the required inputs?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.273 clause 8.4.2.3 defines Ngmlc_Location_LocationUpdate, used by a consumer NF to provide UE location information to the GMLC. It requires as input the event causing the location estimate, specifically the 5GC-MO-LR (5GC Mobile Originated Location Request) event, along with UE identifier, location estimate, age of location estimate, accuracy indication, and LCS QoS class.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.632 defines the Nhss_SDM_Subscribe service operation, and what subscription data type does the current release support?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.632 clause 6.1.4.3 defines Nhss_SDM_Subscribe, by which the NF consumer subscribes for updates to subscriber data indicated by the 'subscription data type' input; the HSS checks that the requesting consumer is authorized. In this release, only the PGW-C+SMF FQDN for S5/S8/S2b interface information is supported as subscription data type.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_ConfigCreate operation, and what output does it produce on successful operation?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.27.2.2 defines Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_ConfigCreate: it authorizes the request, creates a time synchronization configuration, and activates the time synchronization service with that configuration. On successful operation, the required output includes the operation execution result indication and the PTP instance reference.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Ndccf_ContextManagement_Register service operation, and what two elements does the required 'Analytics/Data Specification' input identify?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 8.3.2 defines Ndccf_ContextManagement_Register, used by a consumer NF to register with the DCCF the data or analytics it is collecting. The Analytics/Data Specification input is the Service-Operation-specific set of parameters (Analytics ID(s)/Event ID(s), Target of Analytics/Event Reporting, Analytics/Event Filter, etc.) that identify the collected data.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nadrf_MLModelManagement_Delete service operation, and what happens when a Storage Transaction Identifier is given as input?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 10.3.3 defines Nadrf_MLModelManagement_Delete, which instructs the ADRF to delete stored ML Model file(s) or address(es). When a Storage Transaction Identifier is given, the ADRF shall delete all ML models stored in that corresponding storage transaction.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.247 defines the Npcf_MBSPolicyControl_Create service operation, and what is the only required input?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.2.2.2 defines Npcf_MBSPolicyControl_Create, by which the NF Service Consumer requests creation of an MBS Policy Association and provides parameters about the MBS Session to the PCF. The only required input is the MBS Session ID.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_MLModelInfo_Request service operation, and what is the only required input?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.6.2 defines Nnwdaf_MLModelInfo_Request, used by a consumer to request NWDAF ML Model Information. The only required input is the set of Analytics ID(s).

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe service operation, and what does it let NF consumers do?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.5 defines Nnef_ECSAddress_Subscribe, provided by the NEF for NF consumers to explicitly subscribe to notification of changes of ECS Address Configuration Information.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnsacf_NSAC_LocalNumberUpdate service operation, and which entity uses it to update which two possible quantities?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.21.2.6 defines Nnsacf_NSAC_LocalNumberUpdate: the Primary NSACF uses this service operation to update the local maximum number of registered UEs and/or number of PDU sessions of the network slice at NSACFs.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nudm_UECM_PCscfRestoration service operation, and what does the UDM notify to which NFs?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.3.2.6 defines Nudm_UECM_PCscfRestoration: the UDM notifies the AMF and/or SMF(s) that indicated during registration in the UDM their wish to be notified of the need for P-CSCF Restoration.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_RoamingAnalytics_Request service operation, and what four inputs are required?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.7.5 defines Nnwdaf_RoamingAnalytics_Request, by which a consumer requests analytics related to roaming UE(s). The required inputs are the set of Analytics ID(s), the PLMN ID of the consumer NWDAF, the Target of Analytics Reporting, and the Analytics Reporting Parameters.

questions.question: In TS 23.288 clause 7.7.5, how does the Target of Analytics Reporting sent by the V-RE-NWDAF to the H-RE-NWDAF differ from that sent in the reverse direction?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.7.5 states that the Target of Analytics Reporting sent by the V-RE-NWDAF to the H-RE-NWDAF only contains the inbound roaming UE(s), while the Target of Analytics Reporting sent by the H-RE-NWDAF to the V-RE-NWDAF only contains the outbound roaming UE(s).

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nudm_ParameterProvision_Get service operation, and what kind of information does the consumer get?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.3.6.5 defines Nudm_ParameterProvision_Get, by which the consumer gets UE-related information, such as Expected UE Behaviour or Network Configuration parameters, using GPSI, AF Identifier, and the requested information type as inputs.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Npcf_PDTQPolicyControl_Notify service operation, and what does it send to the NF consumer?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.5.9.4 defines Npcf_PDTQPolicyControl_Notify, which sends the PDTQ policy warning notification to the NF consumer, using a PDTQ reference ID and a list of candidate PDTQ policies as required input.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.273 defines the Nlmf_Broadcast_CipheringKeyData service operation, and what four elements does it require for each ciphering key?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.273 clause 8.3.3.2 defines Nlmf_Broadcast_CipheringKeyData, which provides ciphering key data to the consumer NF. For each ciphering key it requires the ciphering key value, ciphering key identifier, validity period, and the set of applicable types of broadcast assistance data.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_TrafficInfluenceData_Subscribe operation, and what does the NF consumer subscribe to?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.35.2 defines Nnef_TrafficInfluenceData_Subscribe, by which the NF consumer subscribes for notifications of AF traffic influence request information.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.247 defines the Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Create service operation, and what is its only required input?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.2.3.2 defines Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Create, which authorizes the request and optionally determines and installs MBS Policy Control Data per the NF Consumer's information. The only required input is the MBS Session ID.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 32.291 describes the Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Create Service Operation, and what does the CHF include in the Location header field of a successful "201 Created" response?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.291 clause 5.3.2.2 describes Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Create, which lets an NF (CTF) request an initial report of service usage. On a successful "201 Created" response, the CHF includes a Location header field containing the URI of the created resource, which the NF (CTF) shall use in subsequent requests for the same PDU session.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Namf_Location_ProvideLocationInfo service operation, and what extra output is included for non-3GPP access?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.5.4 defines Namf_Location_ProvideLocationInfo, which provides Network Provided Location Information (NPLI) of a target UE to the consumer NF. For non-3GPP access, the optional output includes a UE local IP address (used to reach the N3IWF/TNGF) and optionally a UDP source port number if NAT is detected.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnrf_NFManagement_NFDeregister service operation, and what two inputs does it require?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.7.2.4 defines Nnrf_NFManagement_NFDeregister, used to inform the NRF of the unavailability of an NF consumer. It requires NF Instance ID and Reason indication as inputs.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nudr_DM_Delete service operation, and what two inputs does it require?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.12.2.4 defines Nudr_DM_Delete, used when an NF service consumer intends to delete user data stored in the UDR (e.g. an application data record). It requires Data Set Identifier and Data Key(s) as inputs.

questions.question: According to TS 23.502 clause 5.2.16.3.4, what inputs are required for the Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Subscribe service operation when it is invoked to subscribe to a notification for Network Slice Replacement, specifically for the S-NSSAI of the serving PLMN?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.16.3.4 states that for the S-NSSAI of the serving PLMN, subscribing to Network Slice Replacement notifications requires: the set of S-NSSAIs served by the NF Service Consumer that may be replaced, the NF type of the NF Service Consumer (e.g. AMF), the Requester ID, and the event to be subscribed.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Deregister service operation, and when might a consumer use it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.9.6 defines Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Deregister, by which the consumer deregisters a previous MLModelMonitor registration from an NWDAF containing MTLF, for example when it is no longer using or monitoring the accuracy of the analytics generated using the ML Model.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_ASTI_Get operation, and which other NF does the NEF invoke to service the query?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.28.5 defines Nnef_ASTI_Get: the consumer queries the status of access stratum time distribution, and the NEF authorizes the request and invokes the corresponding service operation with the TSCTSF.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_MemberUESelectionAssistance_Subscribe service operation, and what is required if no Subscription Correlation ID is provided?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.32.2 defines Nnef_MemberUESelectionAssistance_Subscribe, by which the NF consumer subscribes (or updates a subscription) to receive Member UE selection assistance information. If no Subscription Correlation ID is provided, the AF Identifier, Notification Target Address (+ Notification Correlation ID), and a list of target member UEs (as GPSIs or UE IP addresses) are conditionally required.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Namf_Communication_RegistrationStatusUpdate service operation, and what does the AMF do to the UE context when it receives this request?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.3 defines Namf_Communication_RegistrationStatusUpdate, used by a consumer NF to inform the AMF that a prior UE context transfer resulted in the UE successfully registering with it. When the AMF receives this request, it marks the UE context information as inactive since the UE context has been successfully transferred to the peer NF and the UE has successfully registered there.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 24.549 lists the three service operations of the Ndcaf_DataReporting API defined in TS 26.532, and which one lets a client create a session?
questions.reference_answer: TS 24.549 clause 8.2.1 (Ndcaf_DataReporting API) states that TS 26.532 specifies the Ndcaf_DataReporting API, which includes Ndcaf_DataReporting_CreateSession, Ndcaf_DataReporting_RetrieveSession, and Ndcaf_DataReporting_Report service operations. Ndcaf_DataReporting_CreateSession is the one that creates a session.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the service operation letting an NF service consumer get a UE's private IP address and IP domain assigned by 5GC, and what does the provided (public) IP address and port uniquely identify?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.26.3.2 (Nupf_GetPrivateUEIPaddrAndIdentifiers_Get / Nupf_GetUEPrivateIPaddrAndIdentifiers_Get service operation) lets an NF service consumer get the UE private IP address and IP domain assigned by the 5GC. The required input IP address and port (e.g. a public IP address) uniquely identifies the UE IP address behind a NAT.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.540 defines the Nmnpf_NPStatus_Get service operation, and what does it retrieve given a GPSI?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.540 clause 6.7.2.2 defines Nmnpf_NPStatus_Get, used to retrieve the PLMN ID of the Subscription Network of a GPSI. GPSI is the required input, and PLMN Id is the required output.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 26.502 defines the Nmbsf_MBSUserDataIngestSession_Create service operation, and what does it create?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.502 clause 7.2.3.1 defines Nmbsf_MBSUserDataIngestSession_Create, used to create an MBS User Data Ingest Session, including a set of subordinate MBS Distribution Session(s). The required output includes a Result indication and the MBS User Data Ingest Session Identifier assigned by the MBSF.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Ntsctsf_QoSandTSCAssistance_Delete operation, and what does the consumer request?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.27.3.4 defines Ntsctsf_QoSandTSCAssistance_Delete: the consumer requests the network to delete the AF session with requested QoS (or the AF session including Alternative Service Requirements) to revoke the Service Requirement(s) and/or additional Alternative Service Requirement(s) for a UE or group of UEs.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Ndccf_ContextManagement_Deregister service operation, and what does the consumer NF use it for?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 8.3.4 defines Ndccf_ContextManagement_Deregister, used by the consumer NF to delete a registration of data or analytics with the DCCF, using a Transaction Reference ID as the required input.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_NIDDConfiguration_Delete service operation, and what required input does it use?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.13.5 defines Nnef_NIDDConfiguration_Delete, used by the NF consumer to request deletion of the NIDD Configuration between the NF consumer and the NEF supporting NIDD via NEF. The required input is TLTRI, and the required output is Cause.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_RoamingData_Unsubscribe service operation, and what optional output can it return?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.8.3 defines Nnwdaf_RoamingData_Unsubscribe, used to unsubscribe from input data related to roaming UE(s), with a required Subscription Correlation ID input. Its optional output is the pending data that have not been sent to the consumer yet.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_CapsSubscribe operation, and what does the AF subscribe to?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.27.2.6 defines Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_CapsSubscribe: the AF subscribes to receive notification about time synchronization capabilities for a list of UE(s), a group of UEs, or any UE using a DNN/S-NSSAI combination.

questions.question: According to TS 23.502 clause 5.2.27.2.6, what does the 'PTP instance types' Event Filter of Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_CapsSubscribe describe?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.27.2.6 describes the 'PTP instance types' Event Filter as the supported PTP instance types, as described in clause 5.27.1.4 of TS 23.501.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.247 defines the Namf_MBSCommunication_N2MessageTransfer service operation, and what does it let the NF Consumer request?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.3.3.2 defines Namf_MBSCommunication_N2MessageTransfer, used by the NF Consumer to request that the AMF transfer the MBS-related N2 message to the NG-RAN nodes serving the multicast MBS session, using MBS Session ID and N2 SM information as required inputs.

questions.question: According to TS 29.255 clause 4.2.2.3.2, what does the USS include in the ReauthRevokeNotify request body when the 'notifyType' attribute is set to REAUTHORIZE?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.255 clause 4.2.2.3.2 states that if the 'notifyType' attribute is set to REAUTHORIZE, the 'authMsg' attribute containing the authorization data shall be included (this attribute is deprecated in favour of 'authContainer', which carries the authorization data instead).

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_TrafficInfluence_AppRelocationInfo operation, and what does the cause code in its required inputs indicate?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.7.6 defines Nnef_TrafficInfluence_AppRelocationInfo, which forwards the acknowledgement to the notification of a UP path management event report to the SMF. The required cause code indicates whether the acknowledgement is a positive or a negative response.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_Location_LocationUpdateNotify service operation, and what does it provide to the consumer NF?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.21.2 defines Nnef_Location_LocationUpdateNotify, which provides UE location information to the consumer NF, requiring the identity of the AF, UE identifier (GPSI), the 5GC-MO-LR event causing the location estimate, location estimate, age of location estimate, accuracy indication, and LCS QoS class.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.247 defines the Npcf_MBSPolicyControl_Update service operation, and what is the only required input?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.2.2.5 defines Npcf_MBSPolicyControl_Update, by which the NF Service Consumer requests an update of the MBS Policy Association. The only required input is the MBS Policy Association ID.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_EASDeployment_Notify service operation, and what does it provide to the NF Consumer?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.26.8 defines Nnef_EASDeployment_Notify, which provides subscribed event information, e.g. updated EAS Deployment Information of an Application Identifier, to the NF Consumer, requiring Event ID, Notification Correlation ID, and EAS Deployment Information as inputs.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.273 defines the Nlmf_Location_UPConfig service operation, and what three actions can the consumer NF request for the LCS-UP connection?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.273 clause 8.3.2.7 defines Nlmf_Location_UPConfig, by which the consumer NF requests to set up, modify, or terminate a secure LCS-UP connection for a target UE.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 32.291 describes the Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Update Service Operation, and what identifies the Offline Only Charging Data to be updated?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.291 clause 5.3.2.3 describes Nchf_OfflineOnlyCharging_Update, which lets an NF (CTF) update charging data. The {OfflineChargingDataRef} in the request URI identifies the Offline Only Charging Data to be updated, and the used service unit is included in the request body.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.247 defines the Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Update service operation, and what service does it communicate with to determine and install the policy?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.2.3.3 defines Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Update, which provides updated application-level information to the PCF, communicating with the Npcf_MBSPolicyControl service to determine and install the policy according to the information provided by the NF Consumer, updating an application context in the PCF.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Unsubscribe service operation, and what two kinds of information does the NF consumer unsubscribe from?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.9.3 defines Nnwdaf_MLModelMonitor_Unsubscribe, by which the NF consumer unsubscribes from the monitored ML Model accuracy information (Analytics accuracy for an ML Model) and the Analytics Feedback Information for the analytics generated by the NWDAF, using the Subscription Correlation ID as required input.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_ASTI_Update operation, and which other NF does the NEF invoke to authorize the update request?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.28.3 defines Nnef_ASTI_Update: the consumer requests an update to the 5G access stratum time distribution configuration, and the NEF authorizes the request and invokes the corresponding service operation with the TSCTSF.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_RoamingAnalytics_Unsubscribe service operation, and what is the only required input?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.7.3 defines Nnwdaf_RoamingAnalytics_Unsubscribe, used to unsubscribe from NWDAF analytics related to roaming UE(s). The only required input is the Subscription Correlation ID.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.247 defines the Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Delete service operation, and what does it let the NF Consumer do?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 9.2.3.4 defines Npcf_MBSPolicyAuthorization_Delete, which provides means for the NF Consumer to delete the context of application-level session information, using the identification of the application session context as the required input.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_MLModelProvision_Unsubscribe service operation, and what is the only required input?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.5.3 defines Nnwdaf_MLModelProvision_Unsubscribe, used to unsubscribe from NWDAF ML Model provision. The only required input is the Subscription Correlation ID.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_PDTQPolicyNegotiation_Create service operation, and what four inputs are required to create a PDTQ policy?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.30.2 defines Nnef_PDTQPolicyNegotiation_Create, by which the consumer requests to create a PDTQ policy. The required inputs are ASP Identifier, Number of UEs, list of Desired time windows, and QoS reference or individual QoS parameters (per TS 23.503 clause 6.1.3.22).

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.288 defines the Nnwdaf_RoamingData_Notify service operation, and what does the Termination Request optional input indicate?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 7.8.4 defines Nnwdaf_RoamingData_Notify, by which the NWDAF notifies the consumer about input data related to roaming UE(s) that the consumer has subscribed to. The optional Termination Request input indicates that the NWDAF requests to terminate the data subscription, meaning it will not provide further notifications related to that subscription.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Namf_MT_UEReachabilityInfoNotify service operation, and what does it provide to NF consumers?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.4.5 defines Namf_MT_UEReachabilityInfoNotify, which provides UE reachability information and user location information from the AMF to NF consumers, using a Notification Correlation ID as the only required input.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nudm_ParameterProvision_Delete service operation, and what four kinds of previously created data can it delete?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.3.6.4 defines Nudm_ParameterProvision_Delete, by which the consumer deletes one or more previously created Network Configuration parameters, a 5G VN group, ECS Address Configuration Information, or Multicast MBS related information.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nbsf_Management_Unsubscribe service operation, and which four NF types can invoke it to undo a subscription?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.13.2.7 defines Nbsf_Management_Unsubscribe, which lets NEF, AF, TSCTSF, or PCF for the UE undo a previous subscription, using the Subscription Correlation ID as the required input.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify operation, and what triggers the NEF to invoke it toward the NF consumer?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.25.8 defines Nnef_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify: when the NEF receives a notification of a change corresponding to a Subscription from the TSCTSF, it forwards the notification by invoking Nnef_TimeSynchronization_CapsNotify to the NF consumer(s) (known consumer: AF) that subscribed for the event.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_ServiceParameter_Notify operation, and what three required inputs identify the notification's target and content?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.11.6 defines Nnef_ServiceParameter_Notify, used by the NEF to notify a Service Parameter Authorisation Update to the AF (e.g. to revoke an authorization) or to forward a notification for a subscribed event. The required inputs are Transaction Reference ID, Target UE (GPSI), and Result.

questions.question: Which clause of TS 23.502 defines the Nnef_TrafficInfluence_Notify operation, and what does the AF Transaction Id in its required inputs identify?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.7.5 defines Nnef_TrafficInfluence_Notify, which forwards the notification of a UP path management event report to the AF. The required AF Transaction Id identifies the AF request for traffic influence that the event report relates to.

questions.question: In the PCF initiated SM Policy Association Modification procedure, what triggers the PCF to issue an Npcf_SMPolicyControl_UpdateNotify request to the SMF, and how does the SMF respond?
questions.reference_answer: The PCF issues an Npcf_SMPolicyControl_UpdateNotify request to the SMF if it has determined that the SMF needs updated policy information, or if it has received a Port Management Information Container for the PDU Session and related port number from the AF or TSCTSF. The SMF acknowledges the PCF's request with an Npcf_SMPolicyControl_UpdateNotify response; if the request came from a new PCF instance in the PCF Set, the SMF stores the SM policy association towards that new PCF instance.

questions.question: In the Network Slice-Specific Authentication and Authorization procedure, how does the AMF route the UE's EAP Identity Response toward the AAA Server, and what does the NSSAAF use to decide the destination?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF sends the EAP Identity Response to the NSSAAF in a Nnssaaf_NSSAA_Authenticate Request, carrying the EAP Identity Response, GPSI and S-NSSAI. The NSSAAF forwards the message to the AAA-P if one is present (e.g. because the AAA-S belongs to a third party and the operator deploys a proxy), otherwise it forwards directly to the AAA-S; the NSSAAF decides the appropriate AAA-S based on local configuration of the AAA-S address per S-NSSAI.

questions.question: In the CHF Spending Limit Report signalling flow, what two alternative reasons can trigger the CHF to notify the PCF, and how does the PCF respond?
questions.reference_answer: The CHF notifies the PCF either because it detects that the status of a subscribed policy counter has changed, or because it detects that a policy counter status will change at a future point and wants to instruct the PCF to apply one or more pending statuses at a given time. The CHF sends Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Notify (with SUPI, Notification Target Address, and the policy counter status/pending statuses); the PCF acknowledges with an Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Notify response and takes the information into account for policy decisions.

questions.question: The S1AP UE CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION and the NGAP UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION serve the same purpose under different names. How do they differ in which node sends the message and which node receives it?
questions.reference_answer: In S1AP (TS 36.413 clause 8.9.2), the eNB controlling a UE-associated logical S1-connection sends the UE CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION message to the MME. In NGAP (TS 38.413 clause 8.14.1.2), the NG-RAN node controlling a UE-associated logical NG connection sends the UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION message to the AMF instead. Both carry UE (radio) capability information that replaces previously stored information at the receiving core-network node.

questions.question: How does UTRAN's decision-making when sending an RRC CONNECTION REJECT compare to the UE's handling upon receiving it, according to TS 25.331?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.331 clause 8.1.3.4 (Reception of an RRC CONNECTION REQUEST message by the UTRAN) states that UTRAN submits an RRC CONNECTION REJECT message on the downlink CCCH when it cannot accept the request, optionally directing the UE to another UTRA carrier or another system, after which UTRAN may delete all UE context information. TS 25.331 clause 8.1.3.9 (Reception of an RRC CONNECTION REJECT message by the UE) states that the UE first compares the "Initial UE identity" IE against its stored value; if identical, it stops timer T300/T318, clears the transaction entry, and — if a wait time and frequency info are given — attempts to select a suitable cell on the designated carrier and resubmit a new RRC CONNECTION REQUEST.

questions.question: The SMS BROADCAST COMMAND message is used in both the GSM and UMTS radio access networks per TS 23.041. Which node sends it in each RAN, and how does the receiving node's handling of the CBS page differ between the two?
questions.reference_answer: In the GSM Radio Access Network (TS 23.041 clause 9.1.1), the BSC sends the SMS BROADCAST COMMAND to the BTS, which then splits the 88-octet fixed length CBS page into four 22-octet blocks, adds sequence numbers, and transmits them on the air. In the UMTS Radio Access Network (TS 23.041 clause 9.1.2), the RNC sends one SMS BROADCAST COMMAND to the UE directly; the CBS message is completely transparent to the Node B, i.e. the Node B does no fragmentation or manipulation of the data.

questions.question: The RADIO LINK PREEMPTION REQUIRED INDICATION message is defined in both RNSAP and NBAP. Which node sends it to which in each protocol?
questions.reference_answer: In RNSAP (TS 25.423 clause 8.3.18.2), the DRNC sends the RADIO LINK PREEMPTION REQUIRED INDICATION message to the SRNC when it detects that one or more Radio Links should be pre-empted. In NBAP (TS 25.433 clause 8.3.16.2), the Node B sends the same-named message to the CRNC, using the Communication Control Port assigned to the concerned Node B Communication Context, under the same trigger condition.

questions.question: Which specifications define the IE Criticality field inside the Criticality Diagnostics information element, and what does it report?
questions.reference_answer: The IE Criticality field is defined as a mandatory sub-field of the Criticality Diagnostics information element in TS 25.413 (RANAP, 9.2.1.35), TS 25.419 (SABP, 9.2.17), TS 25.423 (RNSAP, 9.2.1.13), TS 25.433 (NBAP, 9.2.1.17), TS 25.468 (RUA, 9.2.8), TS 25.469 (HNBAP, 9.2.16), TS 29.168 (SGs/MME interworking, 4.3.4.3.3), TS 36.423 (X2AP, 9.2.7), TS 36.443 (M2AP, 9.2.1.7), and TS 36.444 (M3AP, 9.2.1.7). In every case it is an ENUMERATED(reject, ignore, notify) value reporting the criticality of the triggering IE that was not comprehended or was missing; the value 'ignore' shall not be used for this field.

questions.question: Where is the IE ID sub-field of the Criticality Diagnostics information element specified, and what does it identify?
questions.reference_answer: The IE ID sub-field is specified as a mandatory INTEGER(0..65535) inside the Criticality Diagnostics information element in TS 25.413 (RANAP, 9.2.1.35), TS 25.423 (RNSAP, 9.2.1.13), TS 25.433 (NBAP, 9.2.1.17), TS 25.468 (RUA, 9.2.8), TS 25.469 (HNBAP, 9.2.16), TS 29.168 (4.3.4.3.3), TS 36.423 (X2AP, 9.2.7), TS 36.443 (M2AP, 9.2.1.7), and TS 36.444 (M3AP, 9.2.1.7). It identifies the specific IE that was not understood or was missing in the received message.

questions.question: I need every specification that defines the TMGI information element in a group-communication information flow, and what role it plays in each.
questions.reference_answer: The TMGI information element is defined in TS 23.280 within three MC service information flows: Media distribution request (10.7.2.6, mandatory, identifies the MBMS bearer being requested), Media distribution response (10.7.2.7, mandatory, confirms the bearer), and Media distribution release (10.7.2.10, mandatory, identifies the bearer being released). It is also defined in TS 23.434 clause 14.3.2.11 within the MBMS bearers response (optional, may be omitted if the NRM server itself sent the request), and in TS 23.479 clause 5.10.3.1 (MC MBMS bearer availability notification, mandatory) and clause 5.10.3.2 (MC MBMS bearer quality evaluation, mandatory), both used to identify which MBMS bearer the event or quality report concerns.

questions.question: Across which NF service APIs is the ES3XX supported-feature flag defined, and what capability does it advertise in each?
questions.reference_answer: The ES3XX supported-feature flag is defined in TS 29.507 clause 5.8 for the Npcf_AMPolicyControl API, TS 29.509 for three separate Nausf APIs (clause 6.1.9 UEAuthentication, 6.2.9 SoRProtection, 6.3.9 UPUProtection), TS 29.511 clause 6.1.6 for the N5g-eir_EquipmentIdentityCheck API, and TS 29.521 clause 5.8 for the Nbsf_Management API. In every case it advertises Extended Support for HTTP 3xx (307/308) redirection, i.e. that the NF service consumer can handle redirection for any service operation of that API according to the Stateless NF procedures in TS 29.500.

questions.question: Which charging specifications carry a Result Code field in their Charging Data Response message, and what does it convey?
questions.reference_answer: The Result Code field appears in the Charging Data Response message content table of TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.3 (CHF to NSACF, network slice admission control), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.3 (CHF to NSSAAF/AMF, network slice-specific authentication and authorization), and TS 32.254 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (NEF converged charging). In all three it is an optional-conditional (OC) field whose full semantics are described in TS 32.290, conveying the outcome/result code of the charging data operation.

questions.question: Where is the Procedure Criticality sub-field of Criticality Diagnostics specified, and what does it report?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure Criticality sub-field is specified in the Criticality Diagnostics information element in TS 25.413 (RANAP, 9.2.1.35), TS 25.419 (SABP, 9.2.17), TS 25.423 (RNSAP, 9.2.1.13), TS 25.433 (NBAP, 9.2.1.17), TS 25.468 (RUA, 9.2.8), TS 25.469 (HNBAP, 9.2.16), TS 29.168 (4.3.4.3.3), TS 36.423 (X2AP, 9.2.7), TS 36.443 (M2AP, 9.2.1.7), and TS 36.444 (M3AP, 9.2.1.7). It is an optional ENUMERATED(reject, ignore, notify) value used only when Criticality Diagnostics is part of an Error Indication procedure, reporting the criticality of the Triggering Message (procedure) itself.

questions.question: Which converged-charging specifications include an NF Consumer Identification field in their Charging Data Request message, and what does it hold in each?
questions.reference_answer: The NF Consumer Identification field appears as a mandatory element of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging, sent by the CEF), TS 28.202 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice management charging, holding the identifier of the CEF or MnS producer), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control, holding the identifier of the NSACF), and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization, holding the identifier of the NSACF/NSSAAF/AMF). Its detailed semantics are described in TS 32.290.

questions.question: Where is the Service Specification Information field defined across the network-slice charging Charging Data Request messages?
questions.reference_answer: The Service Specification Information field is listed as an optional-conditional element of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging), TS 28.202 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice management charging), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control charging), and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging). All four cross-reference TS 32.290 for its full description rather than redefining it locally.

questions.question: A CHF is populating a Charging Data Request and needs to record which network function generated it. Which specifications define an NF Address field for this purpose, and what does it hold?
questions.reference_answer: The NF Address field is defined as an optional-conditional element of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control charging, holding the IP address of the NSACF), and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization, holding the IP address of the NSSAAF or AMF); all three cite TS 32.290 for the field's full definition. TS 28.826 clause 6.4.6, describing a common-IE reduction solution, instead marks NF Address 'not applicable' for that particular service charging profile.

questions.question: Which specifications define an NF Name field in a charging Data Request/CDR structure, and what does it identify?
questions.reference_answer: The NF Name field is defined as an optional-conditional element in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (Charging Data Request, performance and analytics charging), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (Charging Data Request, network slice admission control), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (Charging Data Request, network slice-specific authentication and authorization), and again in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.3.2 (Network Slice Admission Control charging CHF CDR data), where it holds the name of the NSACF that produced the record.

questions.question: I need every specification that carries an NF PLMN ID field in its charging data structures, and what it represents.
questions.reference_answer: The NF PLMN ID field appears in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 and TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (all Charging Data Request messages, optional-conditional, described in TS 32.290), and again in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.3.2 and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.3.2 (Network Slice Admission Control / Network slice-specific authentication and authorization CHF CDR data), where it holds the PLMN identifier (MCC+MNC) of the reporting NF (NSACF, NSSAAF, or AMF).

questions.question: Point me to the clauses that define the Triggering Message sub-field inside Criticality Diagnostics, and its meaning.
questions.reference_answer: The Triggering Message sub-field is defined inside the Criticality Diagnostics information element in TS 25.413 (RANAP, 9.2.1.35), TS 25.419 (SABP, 9.2.17), TS 25.423 (RNSAP, 9.2.1.13), TS 25.433 (NBAP, 9.2.1.17), TS 25.468 (RUA, 9.2.8), TS 25.469 (HNBAP, 9.2.16), TS 29.168 (4.3.4.3.3), TS 36.423 (X2AP, 9.2.7), TS 36.443 (M2AP, 9.2.1.7), and TS 36.444 (M3AP, 9.2.1.7). It is an optional ENUMERATED(initiating message, successful outcome, unsuccessful outcome[, outcome]) value used only when Criticality Diagnostics is part of an Error Indication procedure, indicating which message of the procedure triggered the error.

questions.question: Where is the Procedure Code sub-field defined inside the Criticality Diagnostics information element, and what does it identify?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure Code sub-field is defined inside the Criticality Diagnostics information element in TS 25.413 (RANAP, 9.2.1.35), TS 25.419 (SABP, 9.2.17), TS 25.423 (RNSAP, 9.2.1.13), TS 25.433 (NBAP, 9.2.1.17), TS 25.468 (RUA, 9.2.8), TS 25.469 (HNBAP, 9.2.16), TS 29.168 (4.3.4.3.3), TS 36.423 (X2AP, 9.2.7), TS 36.443 (M2AP, 9.2.1.7), TS 36.444 (M3AP, 9.2.1.7), and TS 36.455 (LPPa, 9.2.2). It is an optional INTEGER(0..255) that identifies the procedure to which the error belongs, used only when Criticality Diagnostics is part of the Error Indication procedure rather than a response message of the procedure that caused the error.

questions.question: Which converged-charging specifications carry an Invocation Result field in their Charging Data Response message?
questions.reference_answer: An Invocation Result field is listed as an optional-conditional element of the Charging Data Response message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.3 (performance and analytics charging), TS 28.202 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice management charging), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice admission control charging), and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging). All four cross-reference TS 32.290 for its full semantics rather than defining it locally.

questions.question: I'm auditing charging record structures. Which specifications define an NF Functionality field, and what is it used to record in each?
questions.reference_answer: NF Functionality is a mandatory field defined in the Charging Data Request message of TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control), and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization) -- all pointing to TS 32.290 for its definition -- and also in the CHF CDR record data of TS 32.256 clause 6.1.3.3 (N2 connection charging, records the AMF's node function) and TS 32.257 clause 6.2.1.3.2 (EAS deployment charging, records the CEF's node function).

questions.question: Where is the NF Consumer Information field defined in CHF CDR record structures, and what does it capture?
questions.reference_answer: NF Consumer Information is defined as a mandatory CDR field in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.3.2 (Network Slice Admission Control charging, capturing the NSACF that used the charging service), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.3.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging, capturing the NSSAAF/AMF), TS 32.256 clause 6.1.3.3 (N2 connection charging, capturing the AMF) and clause 6.1.3.4 (Location reporting charging, also the AMF), and TS 32.257 clause 6.2.1.3.2 (EAS deployment charging, capturing the CEF). In each case it holds the identity of the NF that consumed the charging service and triggered the record.

questions.question: Point me to the specifications whose CHF CDR record data includes a Recording Network Function ID field, and what it names.
questions.reference_answer: The Recording Network Function ID field is defined in the CHF CDR record data of TS 28.203 clause 6.1.3.2 (Network Slice Admission Control charging), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.3.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), TS 32.255 clause 6.1.3.3 (Roaming QBC charging) and TS 32.256 clause 6.1.3.3 (N2 connection charging) and clause 6.1.3.4 (Location reporting charging), and TS 32.257 clause 6.2.1.3.2 (EAS deployment charging). In every case it holds the name of the recording entity, i.e. the CHF's own identifier.

questions.question: Across which Diameter-based specifications is a Termination Cause information element defined, and what does it convey in each?
questions.reference_answer: Termination Cause is defined as a mandatory IE in TS 29.219 clause 4.5.3.1 (Sy reference point, Final Spending Limit Report Request, set to "DIAMETER_LOGOUT" when the PCRF unsubscribes from policy counter updates), in TS 29.273 clause 5.1.2.4.1 (STa Session Termination Request, non-3GPP access network informing the 3GPP AAA server of session release) and clause 7.1.2.3.1 (SWm Session Termination Request, ePDG informing the 3GPP AAA Server/Proxy of IKE_SA termination), and in TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging Debit/Reserve Units Request, an optional-conditional field described via TS 32.299 stating the reason a charging session ended). In the Diameter session-management cases it maps to the Termination-Cause AVP; in the charging case it is the analogous charging-domain field.

questions.question: Which online-charging specifications carry a Termination Cause field in their Debit/Reserve Units Request message?
questions.reference_answer: An optional-conditional Termination Cause field is defined in the Debit/Reserve Units Request message of TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging, from PCEF/TDF), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging, from SCEF), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging, from CTF in MRFC/AS or IMS-GWF). All three describe it via TS 32.299.

questions.question: I need every converged-charging specification defining a Failed parameter field in the Charging Data Response message, and what triggers it.
questions.reference_answer: A Failed parameter field is defined as optional-conditional in the Charging Data Response message of TS 32.254 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (NEF converged charging), TS 32.256 clause 6.1.1.3 (5G connection and mobility converged charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.1.1a.2.2 (IMS offline-only charging). In all three it is populated together with Failure Handling when the invocation fails, pointing to the specific parameter that caused the rejection; full semantics are described in TS 32.290.

questions.question: Where is the Destination Domain field defined in Debit/Reserve Units Request messages, and what is it used for?
questions.reference_answer: Destination Domain is a mandatory field of the Debit/Reserve Units Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging), all described in TS 32.299. It identifies the Diameter realm the request is being routed to.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Operation Token field in a Debit/Reserve Units Request message?
questions.reference_answer: The Operation Token field is defined as mandatory in the Debit/Reserve Units Request message of TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging), each pointing to TS 32.299 for the full field semantics.

questions.question: A rating engine is parsing the Destination Host field of an online-charging request. Which specifications define this field, and is it always mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: Destination Host is defined in the Debit/Reserve Units Request message of TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging, category OM -- optional but mandated for offline), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging, category OC), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging, category OC). It is not uniformly mandatory: TS 32.251 marks it OM while the other two mark it OC, but all three describe its full semantics via TS 32.299.

questions.question: Where is the User Name field defined across the online-charging Debit/Reserve Units Request messages, and what does it hold in each?
questions.reference_answer: User Name is defined in the Debit/Reserve Units Request message of TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging, holding the content of the Protocol Configuration Options field of the Create IP-CAN bearer Request), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging, described via TS 32.299), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging, holding the Private User Identity defined in TS 23.003). It is optional-conditional/optional-mandatory in all three.

questions.question: Which specifications define a Priority Level information element as part of an Allocation and Retention Priority structure, and what value range does it use?
questions.reference_answer: Priority Level is defined as a mandatory INTEGER(0..15) within the Allocation and Retention Priority IE in TS 36.463 clause 9.2.20 (M2AP, E-UTRAN ARP for E-RABs), TS 37.473 clause 9.3.1.37 (XnAP, NG-RAN ARP for QoS flows), and TS 37.483 clause 9.3.1.29 (F1AP, NG-RAN ARP for QoS flows). Values are ordered with 1 as highest priority; in the E-RAB variant, 15 explicitly means "no priority", while in the QoS-flow variants values are simply ordered 1 (highest) to 15 (lowest) as further defined in TS 23.501.

questions.question: Point me to the specifications that define an Origination State field, and what it is used for.
questions.reference_answer: Origination State is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging), all cross-referencing TS 32.299 for its full description.

questions.question: Where is the Origination Timestamp field defined in online-charging request messages?
questions.reference_answer: Origination Timestamp is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging), each described via TS 32.299.

questions.question: Which access-network protocol specifications define a PLMN Identity information element, and how is it encoded?
questions.reference_answer: PLMN Identity is defined in TS 36.463 clause 9.2.3 (M2AP), TS 37.473 clause 9.3.1.14 (XnAP), and TS 37.483 clause 9.3.1.7 (F1AP) as a standalone mandatory information element, and in TS 36.455 clause 9.2.26 (LPPa) as a mandatory sub-field of the NR CGI IE. In all cases it is encoded as an OCTET STRING of 3 octets: 3 digits of the MCC followed by either a filler digit plus 2 digits of the MNC (2-digit MNC) or 3 digits of the MNC (3-digit MNC), two BCD digits per octet.

questions.question: Where is the Route Information field defined across the offline-charging Charging Data Request messages, and what is it used for?
questions.reference_answer: Route Information is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.1A.2.1 (PS offline charging / SMS over MME), TS 32.253 clause 6.1.1.2 (Control Plane data transfer offline charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.1.1.2 (Exposure Function API offline charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.1.1.1 (IMS offline charging). In the first three it is described via TS 32.299; in TS 32.260 it directly holds the parameter of the Diameter routing proxy.

questions.question: I need every specification defining a Proxy Information field in a Charging Data Request message, and what it carries.
questions.reference_answer: Proxy Information is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.1A.2.1 (PS offline charging), TS 32.253 clause 6.1.1.2 (Control Plane data transfer offline charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.1.1.2 (Exposure Function API offline charging, described via TS 32.299), and TS 32.260 clause 6.1.1.1 (IMS offline charging, holding the parameter of the proxy directly).

questions.question: Where is the Multiple Operation field defined in online-charging Debit/Reserve Units Request messages, and what does it indicate?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple Operation is a mandatory field of the Debit/Reserve Units Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging). In TS 32.254 it explicitly indicates the occurrence of multiple operations; the other two point to TS 32.299 for the same semantics.

questions.question: Point me to the specifications that define a Multiple Unit Operation field, and what it holds.
questions.reference_answer: Multiple Unit Operation is an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (exposure function API online charging, explicitly holding the parameter for quota management), and TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging), the latter two both grouping quota-related information for the requested rating units.

questions.question: A CDR audit needs to trace terminal identity across service-specific online-charging messages. Which specifications carry a Subscriber Equipment Number field, and what does it contain?
questions.reference_answer: Subscriber Equipment Number is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Request message in TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.1 (IMS online charging), TS 32.271 clause 6.2.1.1 (LCS online charging, from GMLC), TS 32.273 clause 6.2.1.2.1 (MBMS online charging, from BM-SC), TS 32.276 clause 6.2.2 (voice call service online charging), and TS 32.277 clause 6.2.1.2 (ProSe online charging). All five describe it via TS 32.299, where it identifies the subscriber's terminal (IMEI/IMEISV). By contrast, TS 32.270 (MMS) and TS 32.272 (PoC) explicitly mark this field as not used for their respective services.

questions.question: Which network-slice and edge-charging CHF specifications define a Charging Identifier field, and what is it used for?
questions.reference_answer: Charging Identifier is defined as an optional-mandatory field in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.3.2 (Network Slice Admission Control charging CHF CDR data, used for correlation between different records) and clause 6.1.1.2 (its Charging Data Request message, described via TS 32.290), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.3.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging CHF CDR data, described via TS 32.298), and TS 32.257 clause 6.1.1.1.2 (edge enabling infrastructure resource usage charging Charging Data Request, described via TS 32.290). In every occurrence it is a correlation identifier linking related charging records together.

questions.question: Where is the Retransmission Indicator field defined across the converged-charging Charging Data Request messages?
questions.reference_answer: Retransmission Indicator is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control charging), TS 32.255 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G data connectivity converged charging, from the SMF), and TS 28.826 clauses 6.4.6 and 6.4.10 (common-IE reduction solutions for service charging specifications). All four cross-reference TS 32.290 for its full description; its role is to flag a request as a re-sent duplicate of a previous one.

questions.question: I need every access-network protocol specification that defines a Transport Layer Address information element, and how it's structured in each.
questions.reference_answer: Transport Layer Address is defined in TS 25.413 clause 9.2.2.6 and TS 36.413 clause 9.2.2.3 as a mandatory sub-field of the Tunnel Information IE (HNB's/HeNB's address, type 9.2.2.1), in TS 36.423 clause 9.2.89 also inside Tunnel Information but typed as BIT STRING(1..160) for the eNB's address, in TS 36.444 clause 9.2.2.1 as a standalone IP-Address IE typed OCTET STRING(4..16), and in TS 37.473 clause 9.3.2.3 (XnAP) and TS 37.483 clause 9.3.2.4 (F1AP) as a standalone IE typed BIT STRING(1..160). In every case the Radio Network Layer treats it as opaque and passes it to the transport layer for interpretation.

questions.question: Which system architecture study/stage-2 specifications describe a DNN parameter as part of a group or mapping data record, and what is it used for in each?
questions.reference_answer: DNN is described as a parameter of the 5G VN group data record in TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.3b (identifying the DNN for the 5G VN group), as an optional parameter of the EAS Deployment Information record in TS 23.548 clause 6.2.3.4.1 (identifying the DNN the edge deployment applies to) and of the EAS address and DNAI Mapping Information record in clause 6.8.1 (identifying the DNN the mapping applies to), and as an optional parameter of the Ad hoc group data record in TS 23.700-48 clause 6.19.3.1 (identifying the DNN the ad hoc group applies to, later used by the SMF to associate the PDU Session with the group).

questions.question: Where is the Operation Result field defined across the online-charging Debit/Reserve Units Response messages, and what does it report?
questions.reference_answer: Operation Result is defined as a mandatory field of the Debit/Reserve Units Response message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (PS online charging, PCEF/TDF), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (exposure function API online charging, SCEF), TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.2 (IMS online charging), TS 32.270 clause 6.2.1.2 (MMS online charging, where it explicitly identifies the result of the operation), and TS 32.272 clause 6.2.1.2 (PoC online charging). All are always populated by the OCS regardless of the request type being answered.

questions.question: Which online-charging Debit/Reserve Units Response messages carry an Operation Failover field, and where does it not apply?
questions.reference_answer: Operation Failover is an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Response message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (PS online charging), TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.2 (IMS online charging), and TS 32.272 clause 6.2.1.2 (PoC online charging), all described via TS 32.299. TS 32.270 clause 6.2.1.2 (MMS online charging) explicitly marks the field as not used for MMS in 3GPP.

questions.question: I need every specification defining a Redirection Host field in an online-charging response, and where it is explicitly unused.
questions.reference_answer: Redirection Host is an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Response message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (exposure function API online charging), TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.2 (IMS online charging), and TS 32.273 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (MBMS online charging, BM-SC), all via TS 32.299. TS 32.270 clause 6.2.1.2 (MMS online charging) explicitly marks it not used for MMS in 3GPP.

questions.question: Where is the Redirection Host Usage field defined across the online-charging Debit/Reserve Units Response messages?
questions.reference_answer: Redirection Host Usage is an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Response message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (exposure function API online charging), TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.2 (IMS online charging), TS 32.272 clause 6.2.1.2 (PoC online charging), and TS 32.273 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (MBMS online charging), all cross-referencing TS 32.299.

questions.question: Point me to the specifications that define an Operation Failure Action field, and what it controls.
questions.reference_answer: Operation Failure Action is an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Response message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (PS online charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (exposure function API online charging), TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.2 (IMS online charging, where it explicitly defines the OCS behaviour on failure for SCUR and ECUR), TS 32.270 clause 6.2.1.2 (MMS online charging, similarly for ECUR), and TS 32.272 clause 6.2.1.2 (PoC online charging).

questions.question: Which converged-charging specifications include a Final Unit Indication field in their Charging Data Response message, and where is it explicitly not applicable?
questions.reference_answer: Final Unit Indication is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 32.260 clause 6.4.1.2.2 (IMS converged charging) and TS 32.277 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (ProSe converged charging), both via TS 32.290. TS 32.270 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (MMS converged charging) and TS 32.274 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (SMS converged charging) both explicitly mark this field as not applicable to their services.

questions.question: Where is the Granted Unit field defined in Charging Data Response messages, and what does it represent?
questions.reference_answer: Granted Unit is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (NEF converged charging), TS 32.270 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (MMS converged charging), TS 32.274 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (SMS converged charging, present when the number of granted SMS is more than one), and TS 32.277 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (ProSe converged charging). It represents the volume/units of the service that the CHF has granted for the requested rating group.

questions.question: Which service-charging specifications reference IMS Information as a structured component of their Service Information, and what role does it play in each?
questions.reference_answer: IMS Information is defined as the structured field holding IMS-specific charging parameters directly in TS 32.260 clause 6.3.1.1 (IMS charging Service Information assignment, mandatory, all IMS network elements), and reused by reference in TS 32.272 clause 6.3.1.1 (PoC charging Service Information, optional-conditional) and TS 32.273 clause 6.3.1.1 (MBMS charging Service Information, optional-conditional, part of the MBMS Bearer Service specific parameters), both of which point back to TS 32.260 for its definition.

questions.question: Where is the Operation Interval field defined across the offline-charging Charging Data Request messages, and what does it specify?
questions.reference_answer: Operation Interval is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 32.251 clause 6.1A.2.1 (PS offline charging), TS 32.253 clause 6.1.1.2 (Control Plane data transfer offline charging), and TS 32.254 clause 6.1.1.2 (Exposure Function API offline charging), all described via TS 32.299, and in TS 32.260 clause 6.1.1.1 (IMS offline charging), where it explicitly holds the requested time interval between successive Charging Data Request operations.

questions.question: Which converged-charging specifications define a Time Quota Threshold field, and where is it explicitly not applicable?
questions.reference_answer: Time Quota Threshold is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 32.277 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (ProSe converged charging, via TS 32.290). TS 32.270 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (MMS converged charging) and TS 32.274 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (SMS converged charging) both explicitly mark this field as not applicable to their services, since MMS/SMS charging is unit-based rather than time-based.

questions.question: Where is the Quota Holding Time field defined, and in which services does it not apply?
questions.reference_answer: Quota Holding Time is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 32.277 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (ProSe converged charging, via TS 32.290). Both TS 32.270 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (MMS converged charging) and TS 32.274 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (SMS converged charging) explicitly mark it not applicable.

questions.question: I need every specification that defines a Redirection Cache Time field, and where it does not apply.
questions.reference_answer: Redirection Cache Time is an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Response message in TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.2 (IMS online charging), TS 32.272 clause 6.2.1.2 (PoC online charging), TS 32.273 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (MBMS online charging), and TS 32.280 clause 6.3.1.2.2 (Advice of Charge / ACF DCCA response), all via TS 32.299. TS 32.270 clause 6.2.1.2 (MMS online charging) explicitly marks it not used for MMS.

questions.question: Where is the Tariff Time Change field defined, and in which services is it not applicable?
questions.reference_answer: Tariff Time Change is defined as an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 32.277 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (ProSe converged charging, via TS 32.290). TS 32.270 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (MMS converged charging) and TS 32.274 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (SMS converged charging) both explicitly mark it not applicable.

questions.question: Which system architecture study/stage-2 specifications describe an S-NSSAI parameter as part of a subscription, deployment, or group data record, and what role does it play?
questions.reference_answer: S-NSSAI is described as a parameter of the 5G VN group data record in TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.3b (the slice for the 5G VN group) and of the Network Slice Usage Control parameters record in clause 4.15.6.3g (the slice to which inactivity-based control applies), as an optional parameter of the EAS Deployment Information record in TS 23.548 clause 6.2.3.4.1 (the slice the edge deployment applies to), and as an optional parameter of the Ad hoc group data record in TS 23.700-48 clause 6.19.3.1 (the slice for the ad hoc group, later used by the SMF together with the DNN to associate the PDU Session with the group).

questions.question: Across which specifications is an IMEI information element defined, and how does its encoding differ?
questions.reference_answer: IMEI is defined in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.1.4 (RRC) as a mandatory 15-element sequence of individual BCD digits, in TS 29.171 clause 7.4.11 (LCS-AP) as a mandatory OCTET STRING(8) TBCD-encoded 16-digit field that may include the software version number, in TS 23.018 clause 8.1.28 (Provide IMEI ack) as the IMEISV of the mobile equipment, and in TS 29.336 clause 8.4.22 as the IMEI-Change AVP -- an Unsigned32 bitmask flagging whether the IMEI or only its software version has changed, rather than carrying the IMEI value itself.

questions.question: Where is the Registration Request information element defined inside a resource status request message across access-network protocols, and what does it indicate?
questions.reference_answer: Registration Request is defined as a mandatory ENUMERATED IE inside the resource/WT status request message in TS 36.463 clause 9.1.7 (M2AP, WT STATUS REQUEST, values start/stop), TS 37.483 clause 9.2.1.19 (E1AP, RESOURCE STATUS REQUEST, values start/stop), TS 38.423 clause 9.1.3.18 (XnAP, RESOURCE STATUS REQUEST, values start/stop/add), and TS 38.473 clause 9.2.1.20 (F1AP, RESOURCE STATUS REQUEST, values start/stop/add). It indicates the type of measurement-reporting request being made -- to start, stop, or add a resource status subscription.

questions.question: Where is the Downlink Volume field defined across converged-charging messages, and in which services is it explicitly not applicable?
questions.reference_answer: Downlink Volume is defined as an optional-conditional field in TS 32.257 clause 6.1.1.1.2 (edge enabling infrastructure resource usage converged charging, Charging Data Request from the CEF), TS 32.277 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (ProSe converged charging Response), and TS 32.279 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G MBS session converged charging Request from the MB-SMF), all via TS 32.290. TS 32.270 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (MMS converged charging) and TS 32.274 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (SMS converged charging) both explicitly mark it not applicable, since those services are unit-based rather than volume-based.

questions.question: I need every specification defining a Tenant Identifier field in a Charging Data Request message, and what it represents.
questions.reference_answer: Tenant Identifier is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 32.255 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G data connectivity converged charging, may be used in a business context), TS 32.257 clause 6.1.1.1.2 (edge enabling infrastructure resource usage converged charging), and TS 32.279 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G MBS session converged charging, can hold the AF application identifier), all described via TS 32.290.

questions.question: Which converged-charging Charging Data Request messages carry a Notify URI field, and what is it used for?
questions.reference_answer: Notify URI is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 32.255 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G data connectivity converged charging, from the SMF), TS 32.279 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G MBS session converged charging, from the MB-SMF), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control charging, from the NSACF), and TS 28.826 clause 6.4.10 (common-IE-reduction solution example), all cross-referencing TS 32.290 for the URI the CHF uses to notify the requesting NF.

questions.question: Where is the Trigger Timestamp field defined across converged-charging Charging Data Request/CDR structures, and what does it record?
questions.reference_answer: Trigger Timestamp is an optional-conditional field defined in TS 32.279 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G MBS session converged charging Charging Data Request), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control Charging Data Request), and TS 32.255 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G data connectivity converged charging Charging Data Request, holding the timestamp of the 5G-data-connectivity-specific trigger described in clause 5.2.1). All are described via TS 32.290.

questions.question: Which access-network protocol specifications define a Degrees Of Latitude information element as part of geographical coordinates, and how is its value derived?
questions.reference_answer: Degrees Of Latitude is defined as a mandatory INTEGER(0..2^23-1) sub-field of the Geographical Coordinates / Ellipsoid Point IE in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.8.4a (RRC, Ellipsoid Point), TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.30F (RNSAP), TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.7 (PCAP), and TS 25.469 clause 9.2.5 (HNBAP). In every case the value N is derived from the latitude X in degrees (0-90) by the formula N <= 2^23 * X/90 < N+1.

questions.question: Where is the Degrees Of Longitude information element defined, and what value range does it use?
questions.reference_answer: Degrees Of Longitude is defined as a mandatory INTEGER(-2^23..2^23-1) sub-field of the Geographical Coordinates / Ellipsoid Point IE in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.8.4a (RRC, Ellipsoid Point), TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.30F (RNSAP), TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.7 (PCAP), and TS 25.469 clause 9.2.5 (HNBAP). In every case the value N is derived from the longitude X in degrees (-180 to +180) by the formula N <= 2^24 * X/360 < N+1.

questions.question: I need every specification defining a One-time Event field in a Charging Data Request message, and what it flags.
questions.reference_answer: One-time Event is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control charging), and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), all cross-referencing TS 32.290 for its semantics -- it flags that the request reports a one-time (event-based) charging occurrence rather than a session.

questions.question: Where is the One-time Event Type field defined across converged-charging Charging Data Request messages?
questions.reference_answer: One-time Event Type is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control charging), and TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), all described via TS 32.290, qualifying the type of one-time event being reported.

questions.question: Which converged-charging specifications define a Used Unit Container field, and what does it hold?
questions.reference_answer: Used Unit Container is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging), TS 32.257 clause 6.1.1.1.2 (edge enabling infrastructure resource usage charging), and TS 32.279 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G MBS session converged charging), all cross-referencing TS 32.290; it holds the actually-consumed rating units being reported back to the CHF.

questions.question: Where is the Multiple Unit Usage field defined across converged-charging Charging Data Request messages, and is it always mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple Unit Usage is defined in the Charging Data Request message of TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging, optional-conditional but with quota management not applicable), TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control, mandatory), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization, mandatory), and TS 32.255 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G data connectivity converged charging, optional-conditional, not applicable to QBC). Its category varies by service; all reference TS 32.290 for its full definition.

questions.question: Where is the Requested Unit field defined across converged-charging Charging Data Request messages, and what does it carry?
