questions.reference_answer: Requested Unit is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), TS 32.256 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G connection and mobility converged charging), and TS 32.279 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G MBS session converged charging), all cross-referencing TS 32.290; it carries the volume/units of the service being requested for reservation before consumption.

questions.question: I need every specification defining a Supported Features field in a Charging Data Request message.
questions.reference_answer: Supported Features is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice admission control charging), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), and TS 32.255 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G data connectivity converged charging, where it explicitly indicates the features supported by the NF consumer). All cross-reference TS 32.290 for the full negotiation mechanism.

questions.question: Where is the Session Failover field defined across converged-charging Charging Data Response messages, and in which specification does it not apply?
questions.reference_answer: Session Failover is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice admission control charging), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), and TS 32.260 clause 6.1.1a.2.2 (IMS offline-only charging), all via TS 32.290. TS 32.256 clause 6.1.1.3 (5G connection and mobility converged charging) explicitly marks this field as not applicable.

questions.question: I need every specification defining a Multiple Unit Information field in a Charging Data Response message.
questions.reference_answer: Multiple Unit Information is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice admission control charging), TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), and TS 32.256 clause 6.1.1.3 (5G connection and mobility converged charging, explicitly applicable for ECUR). All three describe it via TS 32.290.

questions.question: Where is the Validity Time field defined across converged-charging Charging Data Response messages, and what does it govern?
questions.reference_answer: Validity Time is an optional-conditional field of the Charging Data Response message in TS 28.204 clause 6.1.1.3 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization charging), TS 32.254 clause 6.2a.1.2.2 (NEF converged charging), and TS 32.256 clause 6.1.1.3 (5G connection and mobility converged charging). All three describe it via TS 32.290, where it bounds how long the granted units remain valid before the consumer must re-request.

questions.question: Which online-charging Debit/Reserve Units Response messages define an Operation Event Failure Action field, and what does it control?
questions.reference_answer: Operation Event Failure Action is an optional-conditional field of the Debit/Reserve Units Response message in TS 32.251 clause 6.2.1.2.2 (PS online charging), TS 32.260 clause 6.2.1.2 (IMS online charging, where it defines the OCS behaviour on failure for IEC), and TS 32.270 clause 6.2.1.2 (MMS online charging, likewise for IEC), all via TS 32.299.

questions.question: Which access-network protocol specifications define an Altitude information element as part of a receiver's geographical position, and how is it derived?
questions.reference_answer: Altitude is defined as a mandatory INTEGER sub-field of a geographical-position IE in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.8.4b (RRC, Ellipsoid Point with Altitude, range 0..2^15-1) and, within the GANSS Receiver Geographical Position IE, in TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.109 (RNSAP) and TS 25.433 clause 9.2.1.95 (NBAP), both range 0..2^15-1. In every case the relation between the encoded value N and the altitude a in metres is N <= a < N+1, with N = 2^15-1 extended to cover all greater altitudes.

questions.question: I need every specification defining a List of Multiple Unit Usage field in a CHF CDR record, and what it holds.
questions.reference_answer: List of Multiple Unit Usage is defined as a CHF CDR field in TS 28.203 clause 6.1.3.2 (Network Slice Admission Control charging, optional-conditional), TS 32.257 clauses 6.2.1.3.2 (EAS deployment charging) and 6.3.1.3.2 (edge enabling services charging, both optional-mandatory), TS 32.270 clause 6.1.7.2 (MMS charging, optional-mandatory), and TS 32.274 clause 6.2a.3.2 (SMS charging, present when the number of units is more than one SMS). All are described via TS 32.298, and it holds the set of rated usage containers reported in that CDR.

questions.question: Where is PS Information referenced as a structured component of Service Information across service-charging specifications, and what does it hold?
questions.reference_answer: PS Information is referenced as an optional-conditional structured field of Service Information in TS 32.260 clause 6.3.1.1 (IMS charging), TS 32.272 clause 6.3.1.1 (PoC charging), and TS 32.273 clause 6.3.1.1 (MBMS charging). In every case its complete structure is defined in TS 32.251, holding the PS-domain-specific charging parameters.

questions.question: Which converged-charging specifications define a Local Sequence Number field, and what is it used for?
questions.reference_answer: Local Sequence Number is an optional-mandatory field of the Charging Data Request message in TS 28.201 clause 6.1.1.2 (performance and analytics charging), TS 32.255 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G data connectivity converged charging), TS 32.257 clause 6.1.1.1.2 (edge enabling infrastructure resource usage charging), and TS 32.279 clause 6.1.1.2 (5G MBS session converged charging), all cross-referencing TS 32.290. It is a per-NF-consumer sequential counter used to detect lost or reordered charging messages.

questions.question: Across which access-network protocol specifications is a Bit Rate information element defined, and does the value range differ?
questions.reference_answer: Bit Rate is defined in TS 36.413 clause 9.2.1.19 (S1AP), TS 36.423 clause 9.2.11 (X2AP), TS 36.443 clause 9.2.1.25 (M2AP), and TS 36.444 clause 9.2.1.6 (M3AP) as INTEGER(0..10,000,000,000) bit/s -- indicating the maximum or guaranteed bit rate for a GBR bearer or an aggregated maximum bit rate -- and in TS 37.473 clause 9.3.1.22 (XnAP) with an extended range, INTEGER(0..4,000,000,000,000), reflecting NG-RAN's higher-capacity GBR QoS flows.

questions.question: I need every access-network protocol specification defining an Averaging Window information element, and its unit.
questions.reference_answer: Averaging Window is defined as a standalone mandatory IE (INTEGER 0..4095, unit ms) in TS 38.423 clause 9.2.3.14 (XnAP), and appears as an optional overridable sub-field within a Non Dynamic 5QI/PQI Descriptor in TS 37.473 clause 9.3.1.38 (XnAP, referencing the standalone IE, GBR QoS flows only), TS 37.483 clause 9.3.1.49 (F1AP, standalone IE, default 2000ms), TS 38.413 clause 9.3.1.28 (NGAP), and TS 38.473 clause 9.3.1.126 (F1AP, for sidelink PQI). In every case the full semantics are specified in TS 23.501.

questions.question: Which access-network protocol specifications define a Pre-emption Capability information element, and what does it control?
questions.reference_answer: Pre-emption Capability is defined as a mandatory ENUMERATED(shall not trigger pre-emption, may trigger pre-emption) sub-field of the Allocation and Retention Priority IE in TS 36.463 clause 9.2.20 (M2AP, for E-RABs), TS 37.473 clause 9.3.1.20 (XnAP, for E-RABs) and clause 9.3.1.37 (XnAP, NG-RAN ARP for QoS flows), TS 37.483 clause 9.3.1.18 (F1AP, E-UTRAN ARP), and TS 38.473 clause 9.3.1.20 (F1AP, E-RABs). It indicates whether the resource request may pre-empt other bearers/flows to obtain resources.

questions.question: I need every access-network protocol specification defining a UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate information element, and who provides it.
questions.reference_answer: UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate is defined in TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.137 (RNSAP) and TS 25.433 clause 9.2.1.123 (NBAP), both applicable to all non-GBR bearers per UE and provided by the CN to the RNC, with optional Downlink/Uplink sub-fields (INTEGER 1..1,000,000,000, at least one required); and in TS 38.423 clause 9.2.3.17 (XnAP), applicable to all non-GBR QoS flows per UE and provided by the AMF to the NG-RAN, with mandatory Downlink/Uplink sub-fields typed as the Bit Rate IE.

questions.question: Which access-network protocol specifications define a Trace Collection Entity IP Address information element inside a CELL TRAFFIC TRACE message, and what does it carry?
questions.reference_answer: Trace Collection Entity IP Address is a mandatory sub-field of the CELL TRAFFIC TRACE message, defined in TS 36.413 clause 9.1.18 (S1AP, eNB to MME), TS 36.423 clause 9.1.2.49 (X2AP, en-gNB to MeNB), TS 37.483 clause 9.2.3.3 (E1AP, gNB-CU-UP to gNB-CU-CP), TS 38.413 clause 9.2.10.4 (NGAP, NG-RAN to AMF), TS 38.423 clause 9.1.2.28 (XnAP, S-NG-RAN to M-NG-RAN), and TS 38.473 clause 9.2.7.3 (F1AP, gNB-DU to gNB-CU). In every case it is typed as the Transport Layer Address IE and carries the address of the trace collection entity for file-based trace reporting, as defined in TS 32.422; it is ignored if a Trace Collection Entity URI IE is also present.

questions.question: I'm implementing MDT trace streaming and need to find where Trace Collection Entity URI is defined across access-network protocols, and its purpose.
questions.reference_answer: Trace Collection Entity URI is defined as an optional sub-field of the CELL TRAFFIC TRACE message in TS 37.483 clause 9.2.3.3 (E1AP), TS 38.423 clause 9.1.2.28 (XnAP), and TS 38.473 clause 9.2.7.3 (F1AP), each typed as the URI IE and defined in TS 32.422. It carries the streaming-based reporting destination and takes precedence over the Trace Collection Entity IP Address IE when both are present.

questions.question: Where is a Response Time information element defined for UE positioning across access-network protocol specifications, and what does it indicate?
questions.reference_answer: Response Time is defined in TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.111 as a mandatory sub-field of the UE positioning reporting quantity IE (an integer power-of-two value, though the field is noted as to be ignored), and standalone in TS 25.413 clause 9.2.1.46b (RANAP) and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.52 (PCAP, used for SAS-centric mode) as an ENUMERATED(Low Delay, Delay Tolerant) value referring to TS 22.071, indicating the urgency of the requested location response.

questions.question: I need every access-network protocol specification defining a Message Identifier information element for warning-message delivery, and who sets it.
questions.reference_answer: Message Identifier is defined as a mandatory BIT STRING(16) IE in TS 25.419 clause 9.2.19 (SABP, set by the CN and transferred to the UE by the RNC, treated as an opaque identifier defined in TS 25.324), TS 37.473 clause 9.3.1.67 (XnAP, identifying a warning message, set by the 5GC and transferred by the NG-RAN node), and TS 38.473 clause 9.3.1.81 (F1AP, likewise set by the 5GC and transferred by the gNB).

questions.question: Where is the PDU Session Pair ID information element defined as part of Redundant PDU Session Information, and what does it identify?
questions.reference_answer: PDU Session Pair ID is defined as an optional INTEGER(0..255) sub-field of the Redundant PDU Session Information IE in TS 37.483 clause 9.3.1.80 (F1AP, ignored in the response message), TS 38.413 clause 9.3.1.136 (NGAP, may be present only in the request message), and TS 38.423 clause 9.2.3.112 (XnAP, ignored in the response message). In all three it identifies the pair of redundant PDU sessions as defined in TS 23.501.

questions.question: A cell that had no warning-message data becomes available again for public warning broadcast. Which specifications define the message that reports this restart to the controlling node, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The PWS RESTART INDICATION message is defined in TS 29.168 (SBc-AP), where it is sent by the MME or the PWS-IWF to the CBC to report the list of cells that have become available for PWS broadcast with no warning message data; in TS 37.473 (W1AP), where the ng-eNB-DU sends it to the ng-eNB-CU; and in TS 38.473 (F1AP), where the gNB-DU sends it to the gNB-CU.

questions.question: During an RRC Resume or Reestablishment, the node holding the old UE context is asked to hand it over to the node the UE has now reached. Which specifications define the request message that starts this exchange, and which node sends it in each?
questions.reference_answer: The RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT REQUEST message is defined in TS 36.423 (X2AP), where it is sent by the new eNB to the old eNB to request transfer of the UE context, and in TS 38.423 (Xn AP), where it is sent by the new NG-RAN node to the old NG-RAN node for the same purpose.

questions.question: In the Allocation/Retention Priority information element carried between eNBs, what does a Priority Level value of 15 mean, and how are the values from 1 to 14 ordered?
questions.reference_answer: A Priority Level value of 15 means "no priority". Values between 1 and 14 are ordered in decreasing order of priority, i.e. 1 is the highest priority and 14 is the lowest; a value of 0 shall be treated as a logical error if received.

questions.question: In the one-IWF authentication info retrieval mapping, which dialogue does the IWF open towards the HSS, and what does it do with partial results before answering the MME?
questions.reference_answer: The IWF opens a MAP v3 dialogue towards the HSS by sending SendAuthenticationInfo. If the HSS sends partial results (possibly after initiating MAP version fallback), the IWF performs the version fallback and/or stores the partial results before using the information received from the HSS to construct the AIA sent to the MME/SGSN.

questions.question: With two IWFs in the authentication info retrieval path, which IWF talks to the HSS and which one stores partial results when segmentation is required?
questions.reference_answer: IWF2 talks to the HSS (it constructs and sends the AIR and receives the AIA from the HSS). If segmentation is required, IWF2 sends partial results to IWF1, and IWF1 stores the partial results.

questions.question: When the MSC pages a UE that is already in an IMS VoIP session, over which interface does it reach the MME, and what stops the MME from forwarding that page to the UE?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC reaches the MME over the SGs interface by sending a Paging Request. If the MME had returned the "SMS-only" indication to the UE during Attach or Combined TA/LA Update procedures, the MME shall not send the Paging to the UE, and instead sends a CS Paging Reject towards the MSC to stop the CS Paging procedure.

questions.question: How does a UE attached to E-UTRAN pre-register with the 1xRTT CS domain, and what must it do first if it is in idle state?
questions.reference_answer: The UE attaches to E-UTRAN including an indication of enhanced CS fallback to 1xRTT, and based on a radio layer trigger decides to register with the 1xRTT CS domain, generating a 1xRTT CS registration request that is transferred via E-UTRAN and the MME to the selected 1xCS IWS node. If the UE is in idle state, it must first perform the Service Request procedure to create a signalling connection with the MME.

questions.question: When an EAS cancels an application traffic influence, which check does the EES perform and which two service operations can it use towards the core network?
questions.reference_answer: The EES performs an authorization check to verify whether the EAS has the authorization to request application traffic influence cancellation. Upon successful authorization, the EES can use either the Nnef_TrafficInfluence_Delete service operation towards the NEF or the Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Delete service operation towards the PCF.

questions.question: How does the source EES pass ACR parameters to the target EES and target EAS, and what must the target EES verify before processing?
questions.reference_answer: The source EES (S-EES) sends an ACR parameter information request to the target EES (T-EES); if authorized and the T-EAS has subscribed to ACR notifications, the T-EES notifies the T-EAS via an ACR management notification with the ACR parameters (e.g. prediction expiration time). The T-EES must verify that the requestor is authorized for this operation before processing the request.

questions.question: When a Ranging or SL Positioning service is exposed over PC5, what does the client UE discover first, and what information is carried in the RSPP metadata during Model B discovery?
questions.reference_answer: The client UE first discovers the target UE and/or one or more SL Reference UE(s)/Located UE(s) via the discovery procedure. In Model B discovery, the Solicitation message includes the target UE's (and for Ranging, UE1's and UE2's) user info, with the roles of the target UE and the SL Reference UE/Located UE indicated in the RSPP metadata.

questions.question: In the PDN GW initiated bearer deactivation over S2b, which node forwards messages between the PDN GW and the home PCRF in a local breakout case?
questions.reference_answer: In the Local Breakout case, the vPCRF forwards messages between the PDN GW and the hPCRF. In the non-roaming and home routed roaming cases, the vPCRF is not involved at all.

questions.question: During optimized idle-mode mobility from E-UTRAN to HRPD, which node tells the HSGW that the UE has moved, and what does the HSGW fetch next?
questions.reference_answer: The HRPD access network indicates to the HSGW that the UE has moved to HRPD. The HS-GW then fetches the PDN GW identity for all the active PDN connections from the 3GPP AAA Server.

questions.question: In mobile terminated small data transmission while the UE is in RRC Inactive, which node asks for MT-SDT information and when is that request made?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB-CU-CP requests the gNB-CU-UP to provide MT-SDT information, during the setup or modification of the bearer context.

questions.question: For soft handover between two directly Iurh-connected HNBs, where does RNA signalling terminate when the connection goes via the HNB-GW, and what happens to RNSAP signalling?
questions.reference_answer: When Iurh-connectivity is via the HNB-GW, RNA signalling terminates at the HNB-GW, whereas RNSAP signalling is still performed on a HNB-to-HNB basis.

questions.question: What event does a HNB GW report when a registered target UE moves between a macro cell and a HNB, and what triggers the report?
questions.reference_answer: A HNB GW reports the "Target UE HNB Handover" event when a registered target UE moves from a cell on the serving PLMN to a HNB, from a HNB to a cell on the serving PLMN, or from a HNB to another HNB. It is triggered when the HNB GW receives an inbound UE relocation trigger (e.g. RANAP Relocation Request from the Core Network), receives a HNBAP UE RELOCATION COMPLETE message from the Destination HNB, or (acting as an Iurh proxy) sends a RADIO LINK RESTORE INDICATION message from the Drift HNB to the Serving HNB.

questions.question: During MBMS session start, what does the MCE check across MBSFN areas before the MME can be told the session failed?
questions.reference_answer: The MCE checks whether the E-UTRAN is able to accommodate the requested configuration for any involved MBSFN area (when using MBSFN transmission) or in any involved cell (when using SC-PTM); if it cannot, or if the MBMS Cell List IE includes no cell controlled by an eNB with which the MCE has a connection, the MME is informed via the MBMS SESSION START FAILURE message with a suitable cause value.

questions.question: In mission-critical broadcast delivery, which procedures put FEC encoding and the MC service server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In "FEC encoding by the BM-SC" (TS 23.280 clause 10.7.3.11.2), the MC service server asks the BM-SC to apply FEC using the Setup FEC request, putting FEC encoding and the MC service server in the same step. Likewise, "FEC encoding by the MC service server" (TS 23.280 clause 10.7.3.11.3) and "FEC encoding by the MBSTF" (TS 23.289 clause 7.3.3.13.2, where the MC service server sends the Setup FEC request to the MBSF/MBSTF) both put FEC encoding and the MC service server in the same step.

questions.question: When an IMS session is upgraded to carry an application data channel, which procedures put the DCSF and the media function in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedures "Bootstrap Data Channel Setup Signalling" (TS 23.228 clause AC.7.1), "Person to Person (P2P) Application Data Channel Setup" (clause AC.7.2.1), "Person-to-Application and Application-to-Person (P2A2P) Procedure" (clause AC.7.2.3), and "Network Centric Procedure" (clause AC.9.3.2, together with the Split Rendering Negotiation procedure in TS 26.264 clause A.1.3) all put the DCSF instructing the IMS AS to set up or reserve resources at the MF (media function) in the same step, e.g. via the Nimsas_MediaControl_MediaInstruction operation.

questions.question: For 5G ProSe direct discovery, which procedures put the 5G DDNMF and the HPLMN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedures "Overall procedure for 5G ProSe Direct Discovery (Model A)" and "(Model B)" (TS 23.304 clauses 6.3.1.2 and 6.3.1.3), and the security procedures "Open 5G ProSe Direct Discovery", "Restricted 5G ProSe Direct Discovery Model A", and "Restricted 5G ProSe Direct Discovery Model B" (TS 33.503 clauses 6.1.3.1, 6.1.3.2.2.1, 6.1.3.2.2.2) all put the 5G DDNMF and the HPLMN in the same step, since the UE sends its discovery/authorization request to the 5G DDNMF located in its HPLMN.

questions.question: In IMS media plane security set-up, which procedures put RTP and SDP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedures "IMS UE originating procedures for e2ae", "IMS UE originating procedures for e2e using KMS", "UE terminating procedures for e2ae", and "IMS UE terminating procedures for e2e using KMS" (TS 33.328 clauses 7.2.1, 7.2.3, 7.3.1, 7.3.3) all put RTP and SDP in the same step, since the IMS UE sends an SDP offer/answer carrying cryptographic information for the RTP media stream(s).

questions.question: Which procedures put EAP and NAS signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedures "Registration procedure for untrusted non-3GPP access" and "Network Slice-Specific Authentication and Authorization" (TS 23.502 clauses 4.12.2.2 and 4.2.9.2), together with the RADIUS-based and Diameter-based "Authentication and Authorization procedures" (TS 29.561 clauses 16.2.1 and 17.2.1), all put EAP and NAS signalling in the same step, e.g. the UE sending an EAP Identity Response encapsulated in a NAS message (NAS MM Transport or NAS Network Slice-Specific Authentication Complete).

questions.question: For vulnerable road user zone management in V2X, which procedures put the VAE server and the VRU zone in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedure "VAL server - triggered VRU zone configuration" (TS 23.286 clause 9.21.3) puts the VAE server and the VRU zone in the same step, where the VAE server processes the zone requirement and monitors/configures the VRU zone. The "VRU Zone Management Subscription Creation/Update/Deletion" and "VRU Zone Management Enter/Leave Notification" procedures (TS 29.486 clauses 5.12.2.2.2, 5.12.2.2.3, 5.12.2.2.4, 5.12.2.3.2) also put the VAE Server and VRU Zone Management subscriptions/events in the same step.

questions.question: In roaming interconnect between two networks, which procedures put JSON handling and the SEPP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The "N32-f Context Termination Procedure" and "N32-f Error Reporting Procedure" (TS 29.573 clauses 5.2.4 and 5.2.5) put JSON handling (the "ProblemDetails" JSON body on failure) and the SEPP in the same step. The "Foreign FQDN to Telescopic FQDN Mapping" and "Telescopic FQDN to Foreign FQDN Mapping" procedures (clauses 5.4.2, 5.4.3) also return a JSON object of type "TelescopicMapping" from the SEPP, and the SEPP-to-SEPP message protection procedure (TS 33.501 clause 13.2.4.8) has the SEPP generate and process JSON objects (e.g. clearTextEncapsulatedMessage, dataToIntegrityProtectAndCipher) in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AF, the EAS and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedures "EAS Re-discovery Procedure at Edge Relocation", "Enabling EAS IP Replacement Procedure by AF", "Disabling EAS IP Replacement Procedure", "Packet Buffering for Low Packet Loss", and "Network triggered EAS change in HR-SBO context" (TS 23.548 clauses 6.2.3.3, 6.3.3.1.1, 6.3.3.1.3, 6.3.5, 6.7.3.2) all put the AF, the EAS, and the SMF in the same step, since the AF triggers EAS relocation/IP replacement and interacts with the SMF regarding the EAS.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GLR and the VLR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Authentication Information Retrieval procedure (ARRI), the Insert Subscriber Data Procedure, the Delete Subscriber Data Procedure, the Supplementary services procedures, and the HLR Failure procedure (all in TS 23.119) put the GLR and the VLR in the same step.

questions.question: When a subscriber certificate is enrolled through a PKI portal, which procedures put the bootstrapping transaction identifier and TLS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The signalling flows demonstrating a successful authentication procedure (TS 24.109 Annex B.3 and Annex D.3), Simple subscriber certificate enrolment (Annex E.3.1), Subscriber certificate enrolment with WIM authentication codes (Annex E.3.2), and the signalling flows demonstrating a successful CA certificate delivery (Annex E.5) put the bootstrapping transaction identifier and TLS in the same step.

questions.question: For MC service group regrouping using a preconfigured group, which procedures put the group management server and the MCPTT server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Regroup formation using pre-configured group initiated in the MCPTT system and Regroup rejection using pre-configured group for regroup initiated in the MCPTT system (TS 23.283), and Regroup formation using preconfigured group in single MCPTT system, Regroup formation using preconfigured group in multiple MCPTT systems, and Adding newly affiliated user to preconfigured group regroup (TS 23.379) put the group management server and the MCPTT server in the same step.

questions.question: In CS-domain fallback for a voice call, which procedures put the GBR bearer, the gateway and the MME in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Mobile Originating Call in Active Mode, Mobile Terminating Call, and Mobile Originated or Mobile terminated call rejected by the MME, and Procedures for leaving E-UTRAN (all TS 23.272 Annex B), plus the S1 release procedure (TS 23.401 clause 5.3.5), put the GBR bearer, the gateway and the MME in the same step.

questions.question: For mission-critical group calls under isolated operation, which procedures put MBMS, the MC service server and the MCPTT client in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: IOPS group call setup, IOPS emergency group call, and IOPS floor control during silence (TS 23.180), plus Header compression by the MC service server and MBMS bearer coordination independent on broadcasted media (TS 23.280) put MBMS, the MC service server and the MCPTT client in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put GPS positioning and the SFN timing reference in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The RNC based Network Assisted GPS positioning Procedure and the SAS initiated Network Assisted GPS positioning Procedure (TS 25.305), and the Common Measurement Initiation procedure, Successful Operation, over Iur (TS 25.423) and over Iub (TS 25.433), put GPS positioning and the SFN timing reference in the same step.

questions.question: When a packet-switched radio access bearer is assigned, which procedures put the PS domain and the RAB in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UE Linking/De-linking (TS 25.346), the RAB Assignment procedure, Successful Operation (TS 25.413), and PTC Activation when GANC receives RAB Assignment Request and PTC Activation when GANC receives Relocation Request (TS 43.318) put the PS domain and the RAB in the same step.

questions.question: For a mobile-originated location request raised by the UE, which procedures put the MO-LR service and NAS signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Transmission using PUR for Control Plane CIoT EPS/5GS Optimisations (TS 36.300), and the MO-LR Service Support procedures in TS 36.305 (clauses 7.3.2 and 7.5.2) and TS 38.305 (clause 7.3.3) put the MO-LR service and NAS signalling in the same step.

questions.question: Our GMSC needs to reach a subscriber who is moving between MSCs mid-call. Which procedures involve the HLR, the MSC and the VLR together in one step?
questions.reference_answer: Process Update_Location_Area_VLR (TS 23.012), Mobile Terminating Roaming Retry Call after successful Retrieval of Routeing Information, Mobile Terminating Roaming Retry Call during Retrieval of Routeing Information, and Mobile Terminating Roaming Forwarding Call after successful Retrieval of Routeing Information (TS 23.018), the outbound-roamer call flow to a not enhanced network (TS 23.292 Annex H.5.3.1.4), and the SN Deregistration procedure (TS 29.563) involve the HLR, the MSC and the VLR together in one step.

questions.question: For 5G media streaming provisioning, which procedures put DASH and the MPD in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Baseline provisioning procedure and the Baseline provisioning procedure with authorisation of 5GMSd Application Provider (TS 26.501), and the Procedure clauses A.2.2, A.3.2, and A.4.2 (TS 26.512) put DASH and the MPD in the same step.

questions.question: For charging of handover between EPS and 5GS, which procedures put the charging data record and the EPC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: EPS to 5GS handover using the N26 interface and EPS to 5GS handover for roaming in Home routed scenario (TS 32.255), and the message flows for ProSe EPC-level Discovery Proximity Request and Proximity Request Cancellation (TS 32.277) put the charging data record and the EPC in the same step.

questions.question: In WLAN access to the evolved packet core over S2a, which procedures put the PDN connection and WLCP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Multi-connection mode procedures (TS 23.161 clauses 6.3.2.2.2 and 6.3.3.2.2), the PDN GW initiated Resource Allocation Deactivation in WLAN on GTP S2a procedure, and the UE/TWAN requested PDN disconnection procedure supporting GTP S2a (TS 23.402) put the PDN connection and WLCP in the same step.

questions.question: For NG-eCall handling of the minimum set of data, which procedures put the MSD and the PSAP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MSD Transfer/Acknowledgement during Session Establishment with a PSAP supporting NG-eCall, MSD Transfer/Acknowledgement during Session Establishment with a PSAP not supporting NG-eCall (inband means), and Transfer of an updated MSD (TS 23.167), plus the Performance Requirements clause (TS 26.267 Annex A.2) put the MSD and the PSAP in the same step.

questions.question: When a radio access bearer is modified over the S1 interface, which procedures put the MME and the E-RAB in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The E-UTRAN initiated E-RAB modification procedure (TS 23.401), the Addition of a hybrid HeNB as the SeNB procedure (TS 36.300), and the E-RAB Setup procedure, Successful Operation (TS 36.413) put the MME and the E-RAB in the same step.

questions.question: For anchoring a terminating session at the service centralisation and continuity AS, which procedures put the PS media flow, the SCC AS and the session transfer number in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Terminating sessions that use only PS media flow(s) (TS 23.237), and the Call termination procedures in the SCC AS, SCC AS procedures for PS to CS access transfer, and SCC AS procedures for PS to CS access transfer with MSC server assisted mid-call feature (TS 24.237) put the PS media flow, the SCC AS and the session transfer number in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EAS, the EASDF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure for EAS Discovery with Dynamic PSA Distribution, the EAS Discovery Procedure with EASDF, Coordination among SMFs for Common EAS/DNAI determination, BaselineDNSPattern Management in the EASDF, and N2 Handover with V-SMF insertion/change/removal in HR-SBO case (all TS 23.548) put the EAS, the EASDF and the SMF in the same step.

questions.question: For collaborative sessions where media is replicated to a second device, which procedures put the SDP answer and the SCC AS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Call termination prior to CS to PS SRVCC (TS 24.237), Media flows transfer initiated when no collaborative session has been established, Media flows transfer initiated by a controllee UE of an ongoing collaborative session, and the signalling flows for session replication/media replication performed by the SCC AS in pull mode (TS 24.337) put the SDP answer and the SCC AS in the same step.

questions.question: For redundant transmission arranged by the SEALDD server, which procedures put SEALDD and the URSP rules in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The E2E redundant transmission path establishment procedure and the Client initiated E2E redundant transmission path establishment procedure (TS 23.433), and the AF influence URSP procedure for reliable transmission (TS 23.434) put SEALDD and the URSP rules in the same step.

questions.question: For exposure of SMS-based services to an application function, which procedures put the NEF and SMS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedure of the "Application Triggering" Service and the procedure of MSISDN-less MO SMS Service (TS 23.502), and Configuration of Monitoring Events in MME (TS 23.632) put the NEF and SMS in the same step.

questions.question: When the PDU session anchor is relocated for SSC mode 2 or 3, which procedures put the AMF and the data network in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Change of SSC mode 2 PDU Session Anchor with different PDU Sessions and Change of SSC mode 3 PDU Session Anchor with multiple PDU Sessions (TS 23.502), and the Authentication, Authorization and Accounting procedures in 5GC (TS 29.561) put the AMF and the data network in the same step.

questions.question: For interworking of circuit-switched calls at the network border, which procedures put the CS domain and the IBCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Call Establishment (TS 29.162), and Call Establishment, Call Release, and the Bandwidth policing procedures (TS 29.235) put the CS domain and the IBCF in the same step.

questions.question: For voice call continuity with concurrent packet-switched handover to HRPD, which procedures put HRPD, the MME and the PS domain in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Location Continuity for Handover between 3GPP and 3GPP2 Access Types (TS 23.271), and Mobile Originating Call without concurrent PS handover (or with concurrent non-optimised PS handover or optimised idle-mode PS handover), Mobile Originating Call with concurrent optimised PS handover, and Mobile Terminating Call without PS handover (or with concurrent non-optimised PS handover or optimised idle-mode PS handover) (all TS 23.272 Annex B.2.3a) put HRPD, the MME and the PS domain in the same step.

questions.question: For IMS centralized services, which procedures bring the HSS, the MSC and the VLR into the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Registration concepts for a subscriber roaming into CS domain (TS 23.221), the PN-deregistration procedure in the CS domain and the PN access control procedure when the caller is not in the PN access control list (TS 23.259), the PN access control procedure in CS domain (TS 24.259), and the SN Deregistration procedure (TS 29.563) bring the HSS, the MSC and the VLR into the same step.

questions.question: When an AF session is torn down by the policy function, which procedures put the PCRF and the session termination request in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: AF Session Termination (TS 29.201), PCEF-initiated IP-CAN Session Modification with the AF located in the VPLMN, Final Spending Limit Report Request, and St Session Termination (all TS 29.213) put the PCRF and the session termination request in the same step.

questions.question: For location services requested by an application server through the SEAL layer, which procedures put the radio access technology and the VAL server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Inter-system switching from 5G MBS session to LTE eMBMS bearer, Inter-system switching from 5G MBS session to LTE unicast bearer, Inter-system switching from LTE eMBMS to 5G MBS session, Fetching location reporting configuration, and the Client-triggered or VAL server-triggered location reporting procedure (all TS 23.434) put the radio access technology and the VAL server in the same step.

questions.question: For public warning delivery on the radio interface, which procedures put CBS and ETWS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Warning Message Delivery Procedure in GSM (TS 23.041) and the Write-Replace Procedure, Successful Operation (TS 25.419) put CBS and ETWS in the same step.

questions.question: When RAN congestion is reported to the policy function, which procedures put the APN and the RCAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The APN information retrieval procedure (TS 23.060) and the IMSI and APN information retrieval procedure (TS 23.401) put the APN and the RCAF in the same step.

questions.question: For NAT traversal during IMS session establishment, which procedures put ICE and STUN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Session establishment procedures (TS 23.228 Annex G.6.2) and the call flow for Network-supported RTC sessions (CS#2) (TS 26.506) put ICE and STUN in the same step.

questions.question: For positioning when a mobile base station relay is involved, which procedures put the AMF and the MBSR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The 5GC-MT-LR procedure involving Mobile Base Station Relay (TS 23.273) and the Network-initiated Deregistration procedure (TS 23.502) put the AMF and the MBSR in the same step.

questions.question: When the AMF checks equipment identity, which procedures put the PEI and the SUPI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Location continuity for Handover of an Emergency session from NG-RAN (TS 23.273) and the Procedure using the CheckEquipmentIdentity Operation (TS 29.511) put the PEI and the SUPI in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NWDAF, OAM and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NWDAF Registration in UDM procedure (TS 23.288) and the NWDAF containing AnLF Registration in UDM procedure (TS 29.552) put the NWDAF, OAM and the UDM in the same step.

questions.question: An application provider wants to reach edge servers through our exposure layer. Which procedures place the AF, the EAS and the NEF in one step?
questions.reference_answer: Processing AF requests to influence traffic routing and/or Service Function Chaining for Sessions not identified by an UE address (TS 23.502), and EAS Deployment Information Provision from AF via NEF, Network triggered EAS change in HR-SBO context, and AF request for DNAI Procedures (TS 23.548) place the AF, the EAS and the NEF in one step.

questions.question: We need to apply policy to edge application traffic. In which procedures do the EAS, the NEF and the PCF appear in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Processing AF requests to influence traffic routing and/or Service Function Chaining for Sessions not identified by an UE address (TS 23.502), Coordination among SMFs for Common EAS/DNAI determination (TS 23.548), and the Procedure of application traffic influence trigger from EAS and Procedure of application traffic influence cancellation trigger from EAS (TS 23.558) have the EAS, the NEF and the PCF appear in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF, the CSCF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The P-CSCF Address List Update Procedure, the DHCP based P-CSCF Selection Triggering Procedure, the PDU Session Release with Reactivation Procedure, and the Trigger P-CSCF Restoration Procedure via AMF (all TS 23.380) put the AMF, the CSCF and the UDM in the same step.

questions.question: When IMS voice runs over 5GS, which procedures involve the AMF, the CSCF and the SMF together in a single step?
questions.reference_answer: The P-CSCF Address List Update Procedure, the DHCP based P-CSCF Selection Triggering Procedure, the PDU Session Release with Reactivation Procedure, and the P-CSCF Monitoring and Failure Detection Procedure (all TS 23.380) involve the AMF, the CSCF and the SMF together in a single step.

questions.question: Where do the CSCF, the SMF and the UDM meet inside one procedure step when IMS registration data is involved?
questions.reference_answer: The P-CSCF Address List Update Procedure, the DHCP based P-CSCF Selection Triggering Procedure, the PDU Session Release with Reactivation Procedure, and the Trigger P-CSCF Restoration Procedure via SMF (all TS 23.380) bring the CSCF, the SMF and the UDM together in one procedure step.

questions.question: For ProSe direct communication charging, which message-flow procedures put the CTF and the CHF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Message flows for ProSe Unicast Direct Communication (PEC and SCUR variants), the Message flows for ProSe Broadcast Direct Communication (PEC and SCUR variants), and the Message flows for ProSe UE-to-Network Direct Communication (PEC) (all TS 32.277) put the CTF and the CHF in the same step.

questions.question: In NR standalone FR1 conformance testing, which DAPS handover test procedures involve the SS and the DAPS configuration in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: NR SA FR1 Inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover, NR SA FR1 Inter-band inter-frequency asynchronous DAPS handover, NR SA FR1 synchronous DAPS handover, NR SA FR1 asynchronous DAPS handover, and NR SA FR1 Intra-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover (all TS 38.533) involve the SS and the DAPS configuration in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MSC and the HLR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Mobile Number Portability query procedures in TS 23.066 Annex A.1 — No NP Query required (Number is not subject for portability), TQoD with number not ported, TQoD with number ported, OQoD with number not ported, and OQoD with number ported — put the MSC and the HLR in the same step.

questions.question: In mission-critical group communication over MBMS bearers, which procedures involve the MC service entity and the PDN connection in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The IOPS discovery request procedure and the IP connectivity subscription procedure in IOPS mode (TS 23.180), and the Group communication connect over MBMS bearer and Group communication disconnect from MBMS bearer procedures (TS 23.282) involve the MC service entity and the PDN connection in the same step.

questions.question: An AF is provisioning service parameters and policy has to follow. Which procedures put the AF, the AMF and the PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Service specific parameter provisioning by AF to HPLMN, AM Policy Association Modification initiated by the AMF without AMF relocation, and AM Policy Association Modification with old PCF during AMF relocation (all TS 23.502) put the AF, the AMF and the PCF in the same step.

questions.question: In MCPTT and MCVideo private call security, which procedures use the PCK together with the MCPTT entity in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The IWF media endpoint (TS 29.380), and Security procedures (on-network), Security procedures (off-network), and Security procedures for private communication initiated in the protected MC system (all TS 33.180) use the PCK together with the MCPTT entity in the same step.

questions.question: For IP-PBX business trunking in IMS, which procedures place the CSCF and the PBX in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Originating procedures using the S-CSCF, Originating procedures using the Transit Function, Terminating procedures using the S-CSCF, and Terminating procedures using the Transit Function (all TS 23.228 Annex S.2.2) place the CSCF and the PBX in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the FD and the SDP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The procedures for one-to-one MCData file distribution, group standalone MCData file distribution, off-network one-to-one standalone file distribution, and off-network group standalone file distribution (TS 23.282 clauses 7.5.2.5.2, 7.5.2.7.2, 7.5.3.3.2, and 7.5.3.4.2) put the FD and the SDP in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the FD and the SDS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The One-to-one conversation management procedure, the Group conversation management procedure, and their off-network counterparts (TS 23.282 clauses 7.8.2.2.1, 7.8.2.3.1, 7.8.3.1.1, and 7.8.3.2.1) put the FD and the SDS in the same step.

questions.question: In the V2X application enabler layer, which procedures place the VAE server and the GEO area identity in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure for V2X service continuity management, the Procedure for tracking the client geographical area at the VAE server, the Procedure for delivering messages to target geographical areas from the VAE server, and the Procedure for subscription to message delivery (all TS 23.286) place the VAE server and the GEO area identity in the same step.

questions.question: For MC service resource management over 5GS, which procedures place the MC service server, the NEF and the PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the 'Resource request at session establishment from the MC service server' procedure (ts_23_289 7.2.3.2), step 6 has the MC service server sending a request for communication resources to 5GS, exchanged directly with the PCF via N5/Rx or indirectly with the NEF via N33. In the 'Request of resources for transmission control and media plane' procedure (7.2.5.2), step 8 likewise has the MC service server sending a resource request for the media plane to 5GS, exchanged directly with the PCF via N5/Rx or indirectly with the NEF via N33.

questions.question: In EPS mobility management, which Tracking Area Update procedures involve the EPS bearer context and the PDN connection in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In clause 5.3.3.1 (TAU with Serving GW change) step 2, and 5.3.3.2 (E-UTRAN TAU without S-GW change) step 2, the UE's TAU Request includes the EPS bearer status, and the same step notes that a UE without any activated PDN connection omits the EPS bearer status, and that a UE with a PDN connection of type "non-IP"/"Ethernet" shall send the EPS bearer status. In clause 5.3.3.1p2 step 21 and D.3.6 (Gn/Gp SGSN to MME TAU) step 7, if the RAT type has changed the MME decides per APN whether to maintain, reactivate or deactivate the PDN connection, and disconnecting a PDN connection triggers deactivation of the corresponding EPS bearer context(s), in the same step.

questions.question: For application data analytics enablement, which procedures put the ADAES and the VAL layer in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the ADAES UE-to-UE application performance analytics procedure (ts_23_436 8.4.2), step 4 has the ADAES sending a UE-to-UE analytics request to the ADAEC, which also states that a session starts between VAL UE #1 and VAL UE #2 (VAL layer entities). In the location accuracy analytics procedure (8.5.2), step 1 has the VAL server (VAL layer) sending a subscription request directly to the ADAE server.

questions.question: In network slice lifecycle management, which activation and deactivation procedures place the DN of the managed object and the IOC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Step 1 of each of the four procedures places the DN and the IOC together: Network slice instance activation (ts_28_531 7.18) and deactivation (7.19) step 1 receives a modifyMOIAttributes operation with the DN of the NetworkSlice instance, referencing the NetworkSlice IOC's administrativeState attribute; Network slice subnet instance activation (7.20) and deactivation (7.21) step 1 receives a modifyMOIAttributes operation with the DN of the NetworkSliceSubnet instance, referencing the NetworkSliceSubnet IOC's administrativeState attribute.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AF, the PCF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'Information flow for downlink data delivery status with UPF buffering' (ts_23_502 4.15.3.2.8), step 1 has the AF interacting with the PCF (directly via N5/Rx) or indirectly via the NEF, and the note in that step describes the PCF updating/removing the PCC rule which triggers the SMF to update the PDR in the UPF, placing AF, PCF and UPF together. In 'Change of SSC mode 3 PDU Session Anchor with IPv6 Multi-homed PDU Session' (4.3.5.3), step 2 has the SMF configuring the new UPF via N4 while, if the PCF has subscribed to the IP allocation/release event, the PCF invokes Nbsf_Management_Update — plus the early-notification interaction with the AF; the runtime coordination sub-step also involves the AF. In the QoS monitoring procedure (ts_29_513 5.5.9), step 1 has the AF subscribing to QoS monitoring notifications from the PCF via the NEF, for measurements performed by the UPF and/or the PCF.

questions.question: For AF session control through the policy converter, which procedures place the AAR command and the PC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In each of the four PC procedures (AF session establishment A.2, AF session modification A.3, gate related procedures A.5, subscription to notification of signalling path status A.6), step 2 has the PC converting the AF's request into a Diameter AAR command and sending it to the PCRF.

questions.question: Which procedures place the DCI and the MAC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In all four test procedures (9.8.1.1.4.2, 9.8.1.2.4.2, 9.8.2.1.4.2, 9.8.2.2.4.2), step 1 places DCI and MAC together: the SS transmits PDSCH via R-PDCCH DCI format 2C for C_RNTI to transmit the DL RMC, and the SS sends downlink MAC padding bits on the DL RMC.

questions.question: In sidelink positioning, which location information transfer procedures involve the ARP and NLOS indication in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In all four Location Information transfer procedures (SL-RTT clause 8.15.2.2.3, SL-AoA clause 8.15.3.2.3, SL-TDOA clause 8.15.4.2.3, SL-TOA clause 8.15.5.2.3), step 1's requested measurement information (Table 8.15.x.2.3-1) lists both an ARP Information Request and a LOS-NLOS Indicator Request together as part of the SLPP Request Location Information message.

questions.question: For GERAN location services, which positioning procedures put the SMLC and the LE interface entity in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the 'Common Positioning Procedure for Iu mode' (ts_43_059 9.2b), step 1 has the BSC sending the BSSAP-LE Perform Location Request message to the SMLC, and step 3 has the SMLC sending the BSSAP-LE Perform Location Response message to the BSC — both are LE-interface (BSSAP-LE) exchanges with the SMLC. In 'Intra-BSS Cell Change' (9.2c.1), step 4 has the BSS sending a BSSAP-LE Perform Location Information message to the SMLC. In 'CS U-TDOA Messages and Procedures on the Lb Interface' (9.5.1.2), step 1 has the SMLC sending a BSSMAP-LE Connection Oriented Information message (embedding a BSSLAP U-TDOA Request) to the BSC, and step 2 has the BSC responding to the SMLC with the embedded U-TDOA Response. In 'PS U-TDOA Messages and Procedures on the Lb Interface' (9.5.2.3), step 1 has the SMLC sending a BSSMAP-LE Connection Oriented Information message to the BSS, and step 2 has the BSS responding to the SMLC with the embedded U-TDOA Response.

questions.question: In local call local switch operation, which example sequences put the BSS and the CN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In each of the three LCLS example sequences (ts_23_284 14.6.2.5.2, 14.6.2.6.2, 14.6.2.6.3), the step where the oMSC server sends the LCLS-Connect-Control message to the oBSS to control user plane data from the CN places the BSS (oBSS) and the CN together (e.g. step 3 of 14.6.2.5.2, step 2 of 14.6.2.6.2, step 3 of 14.6.2.6.3). In the Intra-MSC Inter-BSS Handover example (8.4.1.1.7), step 5a has the far end MSC-2 server requesting BSS-2 to start sending data UL via the LCLS_Connect_Control message with 'BicastatHandover', and step 8b has the MSC-2 Server signalling to BSS-2 that DL data from the CN is now real user data.

questions.question: For ProSe restricted discovery, which Match Report procedures place the RPAUID and the IMSI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the Match Report procedures for restricted discovery (ts_23_303 5.3.4.1A non-roaming, 5.3.4.2A roaming, 5.3.4A.1 Model B non-roaming, 5.3.4A.2 Model B roaming), step 1 in each case has the UE sending a Match Report message containing the RPAUID and the UE Identity (set to e.g. IMSI) to the ProSe Function in the HPLMN.

questions.question: In the user data convergence architecture, which Ud procedures place an application FE and the IMSI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In each of the four Ud procedures — Querying data (ts_23_335 5.3), Creating data (5.4), Deleting data (5.5), and Updating data (5.6) within the UDR — step 1 has the application FE issuing the request message (Query/Create/Delete/Update data request) over the Ud reference point to the UDR, with the message containing the user identity, e.g. IMSI (along with MSISDN, IMS public/private user identity).

questions.question: Which procedures put the CSCF and USSD in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In each of the four USSD example flows (ts_24_390 A.1, A.2, A.3, A.4), the step describing the 'USSD operation' places the CSCF and USSD together via the preceding forwarding steps that route the SIP message carrying the USSD data through the P-CSCF and S-CSCF to/from the USSI AS or UE (e.g. steps 2-3 forward the INVITE containing the USSD request through P-CSCF/S-CSCF, and step 10 is the USSD operation itself performed after CSCF-relayed signalling establishes the dialog).

questions.question: For MAP-to-Diameter interworking, which IWF procedures place the DSR command and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the 'One IWF Scenario' for Trace Deactivation (ts_29_305 7.11.1), step 2 has the IWF constructing a DSR message and sending it to the MME, SGSN, or combined MME/SGSN. In the 'Two IWFs Scenario' for Trace Deactivation (7.11.2), step 3 has IWF1 constructing a DSR message and sending it to the MME, SGSN, or combined MME/SGSN. In the 'One IWF Scenario' for Delete Subscriber Data (7.6.1), step 2 has the IWF sending DSR to the MME or SGSN or combined MME/SGSN. In the 'Two IWFs Scenario' for Delete Subscriber Data (7.6.2), step 3 has IWF1 constructing a DSR message and sending it to the MME, SGSN, or combined MME/SGSN.

questions.question: For IMS charging at the PSTN border, which procedures put the MGCF and the CDR generation in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In each of the four IMS-PSTN charging procedures (ts_32_260), the step where the MGCF generates a CDR places the MGCF and CDR generation together: 'Session establishment - PSTN initiated' (5.2.2.1.6) steps 5-6 (MGCF sends Charging Data Request[Start], CDF opens a MGCF CDR); 'Session establishment - IMS initiated' (5.2.2.1.7) steps 5-6 (MGCF sends Charging Data Request[Start], CDF opens a MGCF CDR); 'Session release - PSTN initiated' (5.2.2.1.8) steps 4-5 (MGCF sends Charging Data Request[Stop], CDF closes the MGCF CDR); 'Session release - IMS initiated' (5.2.2.1.9) steps 4-5 (MGCF sends Charging Data Request[Stop], CDF closes the MGCF CDR).

questions.question: Which procedures place the CP and the MDT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In clause 8.13.1 (Signalling based MDT activation) step 2, the gNB-CU-CP sends TRACE START to the gNB-CU-UP including MDT configuration parameters. In clause 8.13.2.2 (Management based MDT Activation in gNB-CU-CP) steps 1-4, the gNB-CU-CP receives the Trace Session activation request and sends TRACE START/CELL TRAFFIC TRACE messages carrying MDT configuration/Trace ID. In clause 8.13.2.3 and 8.13.2.4 (Management based MDT Activation in gNB-DU / gNB-CU-UP), the gNB-CU-CP sends the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST / BEARER CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST including the Management based MDT PLMN List, and later sends CELL TRAFFIC TRACE to the AMF including the Trace ID for MDT.

questions.question: For multi-path relaying in NG-RAN, which path-addition procedures place the gNB-CU and the MP Relay UE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In all four path-addition procedures (Inter-DU direct 8.22.1, Inter-DU indirect 8.22.2, Intra-DU direct 8.22.3, Intra-DU indirect 8.22.4), step 1 places the gNB-CU and the MP Relay UE together: the Uu measurement configuration and measurement report signalling are performed between the MP Remote UE and the gNB-CU, with the MP Remote UE reporting a list of candidate MP Relay UE L2 ID(s) and cell ID(s) to the gNB-CU.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CN, the RNC and MBMS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'RNC Registration' (ts_25_346 5.1.7), the RNC informs the CN by sending an MBMS Registration Request message so it can receive MBMS Session Start Request messages, placing CN, RNC and MBMS together in that step. In the 'MBMS Session Start' successful operation (ts_25_413 8.36.2), the step where the CN initiates the procedure by sending a MBMS SESSION START message to the RNC places CN, RNC and MBMS in the same step.

questions.question: For CS/IMS combinational services, which procedures place the CSI capability and the IM component in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'CSI interworking function establishing a combinational CS call and an IMS session to a terminating UE' (ts_24_279 B.8.2), step 4 ('Termination logic processing by the CSI AS') has the CSI application server invoking its CSI termination logic and, based on the requested media components, deciding to split the session so that the voice component is terminated via the CS domain while the session containing the MSRP stream (the IM component) is terminated via an IP-CAN, placing the CSI capability/logic and the IM (MSRP) component together in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures place the MN and the SRB in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'SN Addition or modification' (ts_33_501 6.10.2.1) step 5, the MN sends the RRC Connection Reconfiguration Request to the UE instructing it to configure the new DRBs and/or SRB for the SN, including the SN Counter parameter. In 'RRC Transfer procedure' (ts_37_340 10.10.1/10.10.2), the split-SRB DL flow step 1 has the MN initiating the RRC Transfer procedure when it decides to use the split SRBs, encapsulating the RRC message in a PDCP(-C) PDU.

questions.question: Which procedures place the HO and the SCG in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In all three change procedures (MeNB/MN to eNB Change ts_36_300 10.1.2.8.5, EN-DC ts_37_340 10.8.1, MR-DC with 5GC ts_37_340 10.8.2), step 4 places HO and SCG together: the source MeNB/MN triggers the UE to apply the new configuration/perform HO, and upon receiving the new configuration the UE releases the entire SCG configuration.

questions.question: Which procedures place the ASC and the RACH in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the 'Physical random access procedure' (ts_25_214 6.1) and its Enhanced Uplink variant (6.1A), the higher layers (MAC) provide the ASC of the PRACH transmission, and step 1 has Layer 1 deriving the available uplink access slots for the set of available RACH sub-channels within the given ASC. In the 'Random access procedure' (ts_25_224 5.6.3), step 3 has the UE, based on the type of random access, randomly selecting one UpPCH sub-channel and one signature from those available for the given ASC (i.e. the RACH/UpPCH access resource selection is scoped to the given ASC).

questions.question: Which detach and bearer deactivation procedures place the PCRF, the SGSN and the PDN connection in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'Detach, PDP Context and EPS-Bearer Deactivation Procedures' (ts_23_139 9.3.3) step 2, for the UE detach or PDN connection deactivation case, the P-GW initiates IP-CAN session termination with the PCRF (referencing SGSN-driven detach/deactivation steps in TS 23.060, and PDN connection release), placing PCRF, SGSN(-driven procedure) and PDN connection together. In 'General Procedure for GTP-based S5/S8 for UTRAN/GERAN' (ts_23_402 8.2.1.3) step 10, the PDN GW may execute a PCEF-Initiated IP CAN Session Modification Procedure with the PCRF while the SGSN is handling the handover/PDP context establishment for the PDN connection being transferred.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF, the PGW and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'UUAA during default PDN connection at Attach' (ts_23_256 5.2.3.3) step 0, the UE sends an Attach Request to the SMF+PGW-C which, based on the Service Level Device Identity, determines to invoke the UAS NF/NEF service operation for UUAA Authentication/Authorization. In 'UE requested PDN connectivity for C2 authorization' (5.2.5.3.1) step 2, the SMF+PGW-C sends a Nnef_Authentication_AuthenticateAuthorize request to the UAS NF/NEF. In the 'AuthenticateAuthorize' service operation (ts_29_256 5.2.2.2.1) step 1, the NF Service Consumer (e.g. AMF, SMF, SMF+PGW-C) sends a POST request to the UAV Authentications resource of the NEF (UAS-NF).

questions.question: Which procedures place the CSCF and the PDP context in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'Context activation and registration' (ts_23_221 8.1) step 4, the UE performs application level registration by providing the IP address obtained during PDP context activation (step 2) to the P-CSCF, and the registration is then forwarded to the S-CSCF. In 'GPRS/EPS procedure for P-CSCF discovery' (ts_23_228 E.1.1.1) step 1, the UE requests establishment of a PDP context and indicates it requests P-CSCF IP address(es) (which the P-CSCF then uses to serve the S-CSCF-bound registration).

questions.question: For IMS registration and terminating calls, which procedures place the CS domain, the CSCF and the HSS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'Mobile Terminating call procedures to unregistered Public User Identity' (ts_23_228 5.12.1) step 9, the S-CSCF performs further actions for the call attempt, and in the case where it decides to redirect the session towards the CS domain, the Mobile Termination Procedure MT#3 applies -- placing CS domain, CSCF (S-CSCF) and HSS-derived context in that step. In 'Procedure for registration utilizing IMS Authorization' (ts_23_292 G.2) steps 5-7, the I-CSCF selects the HSS and, for HPLMN SeDoC subscribers, the I-CSCF indicates to the HSS that the REGISTER (from the MSC Server, i.e. the CS domain) is coming from an MSC, and the HSS selects the appropriate S-CSCF able to handle CS authentication.

questions.question: In location services and ProSe discovery over WLAN, which procedures place the SUPL entity and the SLP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'WLAN UE Originated Procedure in I-WLAN' (ts_23_271 9.2.5) step 2, the WLAN UE initiates positioning by establishing a user plane connection with the GMLC/SLP using the OMA SUPL mechanism to transport location assistance data and location information. In 'Overall call flow for EPC-level ProSe Discovery' (ts_23_303 5.5.2) step 3, to request location updates for UE A, ProSe Function A contacts SUPL Location Platform (SLP) A, and to request location updates for UE B, ProSe Function A contacts ProSe Function B which requests location updates for UE B from SLP B.

questions.question: In the 5G core, which procedures place the UDM, the SUPI and the S-NSSAI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'Authorization of service specific parameter provisioning' (ts_23_502 4.15.6.7a) step 2, the NEF sends a Nudm_ServiceSpecificAuthorisation_Create Request to the UDM including the GPSI/External Group Id and S-NSSAI/DNN; step 3 has the UDM mapping this to SUPI/Internal Group Id. In 'Registration with AMF re-allocation' (4.2.2.2.3) step 3b, the initial AMF sends Nudm_SDM_Get (SUPI, Slice Selection Subscription data) to the UDM to retrieve the Subscribed S-NSSAIs. In 'NIDD Authorization Update' (4.25.6) step 1, the UDM sends a Nudm_NIDDAuthorisation_UpdateNotify Request containing SUPI, GPSI and S-NSSAI to the NEF.

questions.question: Which procedures place the WLAN and the RAT selection in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'Procedures' for WLAN performance analytics (ts_23_288 6.11.4), steps 2-3 have the NWDAF subscribing to information related to the PDU Session for WLAN (i.e. Access Type is Non-3GPP and RAT Type is TRUSTED_WLAN) from the SMF — placing the WLAN access indication and the RAT Type selection value together in the same step.

questions.question: For group communication over a configured MBS session with multiple QoS flows, which procedures place the ARP and the MBS session in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the MC service group media transmission procedure (ts_23_289 7.3.3.5.2) step 1, the MC service server creates an MBS session and can provide default service requirements including a specific allocation and retention priority (ARP); step 4 has the MC service server requesting an MBS session update to provide better ARP for a higher-priority group communication. The equivalent VAL service group procedure (ts_23_434 14.3.4A.6.2) step 4 likewise has the VAL server initiating an MBS session update to the NRM to provide better ARP (e.g. for a VAL emergency group communication) within the configured MBS session.

questions.question: In multicast bearer service activation, which procedures place IGMP and MLD signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the 5G-RG join Multicast Packets transmission procedure (ts_23_316 7.7.1.1.3) step 1, the 5G-RG sends an IGMP or MLD Join message via the IP PDU Session user plane, and step 2 has the UPF identifying and handling IGMP and MLD Join packets. In 'Service activation' (ts_29_061 17.5.1) step 1, the GGSN receives an IGMP (IPv4) or MLD (IPv6) Join message from a UE over the default PDP context, signalling interest in a multicast MBMS bearer service.

questions.question: For gateway restoration and IP address release, which procedures place the GW and the MN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In 'Non-3GPP access initiated IPv4 address Delete Procedure' (ts_23_402 6.14), step 1 has the MAG (in the Trusted Non-3GPP IP Access) sending a Proxy Binding Update (MN NAI, APN, lifetime=0) message to the PDN GW (GW), and step 2 has the PDN GW modifying its Binding Cache entry to delete the IPv4 address for that MN and responding with a Proxy Binding Ack to the MAG.

questions.question: Which procedures place the SGSN and GPRS handling in the same step following a node failure or an ISR-activated detach?
questions.reference_answer: In 'SGSN Failure' restoration (ts_23_119 7.6.4), step 2 has the SGSN receiving the Attach Request message and, identifying no MM context for the MS, initiating the update location procedure (GPRS handling after node failure). In the 'UE-initiated Detach procedure for GERAN/UTRAN with ISR activated' (ts_23_401 5.3.8.2.2), step 4 has the SGSN sending a Detach Notification message to the associated MME because ISR is activated, and step 2 has the SGSN deactivating the active EPS Bearers by sending a Delete Session Request to the Serving GW.

questions.question: Which procedures place the EIR and the IMEI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In the 'ME identity check procedure' (ts_23_401 5.3.10.5) step 2, the MME sends ME Identity Check (ME Identity, IMSI) -- i.e. the IMEI -- to the EIR, and the EIR responds with ME Identity Check Ack (Result). In the 'IMEI Check Procedure with one IWF' (ts_29_305 7.9.1) step 2, the IWF sends Check IMEI to the EIR, and step 3 has the IWF receiving Check IMEI Ack from the EIR.

questions.question: An SCS/AS wants continuous reporting of congestion status for a geographical area, and the RCAF is the node that detects a Threshold crossing and sends the Aggregated Congestion Report. Which procedures put the SCS/AS, the SCEF and the RCAF together in the same Network Status Information reporting flow?
questions.reference_answer: In the 'Request procedure for one-time or continuous reporting of network status' (ts_23_682 5.8.2), step 3 has the SCEF sending an Aggregated Congestion Request to the identified RCAF(s), and step 4 has the RCAF sending an Aggregated Congestion Report to the SCEF, which the SCEF (step 5-6) combines and reports to the SCS/AS via a Network Status Report. In the 'Report procedure for continuous reporting of network status' (5.8.3), step 1 has the RCAF detecting a Threshold crossing and sending the Aggregated Congestion Report to the SCEF, step 3 has the SCEF deriving a new NSI, and step 4 has the SCEF sending the Network Status Report to the SCS/AS -- placing SCS/AS, SCEF and RCAF together in this reporting flow.

questions.question: Which procedures show the PIN Server and an NF service consumer exchanging HTTP requests over the PASRegistration data structure, covering creation, update and deletion of a PAS Registration?
questions.reference_answer: PAS Registration Creation (clause 5.2.2.2.2), Updating an existing Registration (clause 5.2.2.3.2), and Deregistering the Registration (clause 5.2.2.4.2) all show the service consumer sending an HTTP request (POST, PUT/PATCH, or DELETE respectively) to the PIN Server targeting the PASRegistration/Individual PAS Registration resource, with the PIN Server responding via the PASRegistration or PASRegistrationPatch data structure.

questions.question: At an initial successful IMS Registration the P-CSCF creates an Individual Application Session Context towards the PCF. Which procedures place the P-CSCF, the PCF and the Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Create service operation in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Subscription to Notification of Signalling Path Status at IMS Registration (clause B.5), Provisioning of SIP signalling flow information at IMS Registration (clause B.6), and Subscription to Notification of Change of Access Type at IMS Registration (clause B.7) each place the P-CSCF, PCF, and Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Create in the same step, where the P-CSCF invokes Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Create toward the PCF via an HTTP POST to the Application Sessions resource.

questions.question: Which procedures put the gNB-CU-CP, the gNB-DU and the CG-SDT resource configuration in the same small data transmission flow in RRC_INACTIVE?
questions.reference_answer: CG based SDT (clause 8.18.2) and RA-SDT or non-SDT with CG-SDT configuration (clause 8.18.3) place the gNB-CU-CP, gNB-DU, and CG-SDT resource configuration in the same step: in 8.18.2 the gNB-CU-CP requests CG-SDT related resource configuration from the gNB-DU via UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST/RESPONSE, and in 8.18.3 the gNB-CU-CP retrieves the stored CG-SDT resource configurations from the gNB-DU during UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST/RESPONSE.

questions.question: Which procedures describe an IAB-node whose IAB-MT declares backhaul RLF migrating to a new parent node, covering both the intra-CU and the inter-CU IAB-donor-CU cases in SA mode?
questions.reference_answer: Intra-CU Backhaul RLF recovery for IAB-nodes in SA mode (clause 8.2.5) covers the intra-CU case, where the IAB-MT declares BH RLF and migrates to a new parent node under the same IAB-donor-CU. IAB Inter-CU Backhaul RLF recovery for single connected IAB-node (clause 8.17.4) covers the inter-CU case, migrating to a new parent node under a different IAB-donor-CU. Mobile IAB-node RLF recovery (clause 8.23.4) extends the inter-CU procedure of 8.17.4 to mobile IAB-nodes.

questions.question: Which procedures place the VAL server and the NSCE server in the same step for network slice related capability exposure, covering monitoring job creation, report subscription and slice related communication service creation?
questions.reference_answer: Slice related Communication Service Creation (clause 9.12.2.1.1) puts the VAL server and NSCE server together for slice creation. Network slice related performance and analytics monitoring job creation request (clause 9.7.2.1) covers monitoring job creation, and Network slice related performance and analytics report subscription and report (clause 9.7.2.2) covers report subscription. In each, the VAL server sends the corresponding request to the NSCE server, which responds/reports back.

questions.question: Which procedures show the SCC AS anchoring a Collaborative Session where UE-1 is the Controller UE and control is transferred to or claimed by UE-2?
questions.reference_answer: Controller UE transfers Collaborative Session Control to a Controllee UE without Media Transfer (clause 6a.4a.1), where UE-1 as Controller UE requests the SCC AS to transfer control to UE-2, and Transfer of Collaborative Session Control initiated by the target UE (clause 6a.4a.5), where UE-2 requests the SCC AS to take over control from UE-1, both show the SCC AS anchoring the Collaborative Session and transferring/claiming control between UE-1 (Controller UE) and UE-2.

questions.question: Which procedures place the ProSe Function and the OCS in the same message flow in IEC or ECUR charging mode, for Discovery announce, match report and Model B restricted discovery?
questions.reference_answer: Message flows for ProSe Direct Discovery Announce Request (clause 5.3.2.2.2) cover Discovery announce in IEC and ECUR modes, Message flows for ProSe Direct Discovery Match Report Request (clause 5.3.2.2.4) cover match report in IEC and ECUR modes, and Message flow for Discovery Request - Model B procedures (clause 5.3.2.2.5) covers Model B restricted discovery in IEC and ECUR modes. In each, the ProSe Function sends Debit Units Request or Reserve Units Request/Debit Units Request[Terminate] to the OCS, which responds with the corresponding Debit Units Response or Reserve Units Response.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the BPCF, the PCRF and the S9a session in the same Fixed Broadband Access flow when DSMIPv6 over S2c is used, for both trusted and untrusted access and for handover to 3GPP access?
questions.reference_answer: Initial Attach with DSMIPv6 on S2c to trusted Fixed Broadband Access (clause 8.2.1) and Initial Attach with DSMIPv6 on S2c to untrusted Fixed Broadband Access (clause 8.3.1) cover trusted and untrusted access respectively, establishing an S9a session between the BPCF and PCRF. Handover from Trusted Fixed Broadband Access with DSMIPv6 over S2c to 3GPP Access (clause 8.2.6) and Handover from Untrusted Fixed Broadband Access with DSMIPv6 over S2c to 3GPP Access (clause 8.3.6) cover the handover to 3GPP access, where the PCRF (or V-PCRF) executes a Gateway Control and QoS Rules Provision or Termination procedure with the BPCF.

questions.question: Which procedures describe the PGW-C modifying an existing Sx session towards the PGW-U for dedicated bearer deactivation or bearer modification over GTP-based S2a and S2b?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures with bearer deactivation by PGW (clause 6.3.3.6) covers dedicated bearer deactivation for PDN GW Initiated Bearer Deactivation over GTP-based S2a and S2b, where the PGW-C sends an Sx Session Modification Request to the PGW-U to deactivate the dedicated bearer. Procedures with bearer modification (clause 6.3.3.7) covers bearer modification for the S2b/S2a Bearer Modification and HSS Initiated Subscribed QoS Modification procedures, where the PGW-C sends an Sx Session Modification Request to the PGW-U to modify the existing bearer.

questions.question: Which procedures put the P-CSCF, the IBCF and the TrGW in the same step for a roaming UE originating an IMS session, covering both VPLMN routing and home routing?
questions.reference_answer: Flow for originating session with VPLMN routing (Annex M.3.1.3) and Flow for originating session with Home routing (Annex M.3.1.4) put the P-CSCF, IBCF, and TrGW in the same step for a roaming UE originating an IMS session: the P-CSCF forwards the INVITE to the visited IBCF, which allocates a TrGW for the media and applies OMR procedures, before the S-CSCF decides to route back to the VPLMN (VPLMN routing) or route directly from the home network (home routing).

questions.question: Which procedures put the MME/SGSN, the SCEF and a T6a/T6b connection in the same step, covering connection establishment for a non-IP PDN and both release variants?
questions.reference_answer: T6a/T6b Connection Establishment Procedure (clause 5.13.1.2) covers connection establishment for a non-IP PDN, where the MME/SGSN sends a Create SCEF Connection Request to the SCEF. MME/SGSN Initiated T6a/T6b Connection Release procedure (clause 5.13.5.2) and SCEF Initiated T6a/T6b Connection Release procedure (clause 5.13.5.3) cover the two release variants, in which the MME/SGSN or the SCEF respectively sends a Delete SCEF Connection Request, acknowledged by a Delete SCEF Connection Response from the other side.

questions.question: Which procedures place the Source RAN, the HNB-GW and the RANAP RELOCATION REQUIRED message in the same connected mode inbound mobility step towards CSG, hybrid or open access HNBs?
questions.reference_answer: Connected Mode Inbound Mobility for CSG UEs to CSG HNBs or to Hybrid Cells (clause 5.9.2a) covers CSG HNBs and hybrid cells, Connected Mode Inbound Mobility for non-CSG UEs to CSG HNBs or to Hybrid Cells (clause 5.9.3a) also covers CSG/hybrid targets for non-CSG UEs, and Connected Mode Inbound Mobility to open access HNBs (clause 5.9.4a) covers open access HNBs. In each, the Source RAN sends the RANAP RELOCATION REQUIRED message to the Core Network, and the HNB-GW subsequently receives the corresponding RANAP RELOCATION REQUEST to route the relocation to the target HNB.

questions.question: Which procedures show the GANC commanding the MS to release resources with a GA-RRC RELEASE message after the CN has sent an Iu Release Command?
