questions.reference_answer: GA-RRC Connection Release (clause 5.2.5.7.2 of TS 43.902, and clause 9.7.2 of TS 43.318) shows the GANC commanding the MS to release resources with a GA-RRC RELEASE message after the CN has sent a RANAP Iu Release Command to the GANC; the MS confirms with GA-RRC RELEASE COMPLETE and the GANC confirms to the CN with Iu Release Complete.

questions.question: Which procedures describe interactions between the SGW-C and the SGW-U during procedures that need an eNB F-TEIDu update or a Serving GW relocation?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.3.1.2.2 'Type 1' describes SGW-C/SGW-U interactions for procedures needing a Serving GW relocation (Tracking Area Update with SGW change, Routing Area Update with SGW change, X2-based handover with Serving GW relocation, MME triggered Serving GW relocation), where the new SGW-C selects a new SGW-U/creates an Sx session and the old SGW-C releases the old Sx session. Clause 6.3.1.3 'Procedures with eNB F-TEIDu update' describes SGW-C/SGW-U interactions for procedures needing an eNB F-TEIDu update (UE triggered Service Request, Connection Resume, E-UTRAN initiated E-RAB modification, X2-based handover without SGW relocation, S1-based handover without SGW change), where the SGW-C modifies the Sx session at the SGW-U to update the eNB F-TEIDu(s).

questions.question: Which SRVCC call flows describe a source access node splitting the voice bearer from the non-voice bearers and relocating them separately towards the MSC Server and the SGSN in the same flow?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.2.2.2 (SRVCC from E-UTRAN to UTRAN with PS HO or GERAN with DTM HO support) and clause 6.2.2.3 (vSRVCC from E-UTRAN to UTRAN with PS HO support) describe the source MME splitting the voice bearer (QCI 1) from the other PS bearers and relocating them separately towards the MSC Server and SGSN. Clause 6.3.2.1 (SRVCC from UTRAN (HSPA) to GERAN without DTM support) and clause 6.3.2.2 (SRVCC from UTRAN (HSPA) to UTRAN or GERAN with DTM HO support) describe the source SGSN splitting the voice bearer from the non-voice bearers and relocating them towards the MSC server (and, for 6.3.2.2, also towards the target SGSN).

questions.question: In which procedures does an SRVCC HO indication or SRVCC Handover Indication travel from the source radio access node to the MME or SGSN together with a Source to Target Transparent Container?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.2.2.2 (SRVCC from E-UTRAN to UTRAN with PS HO or GERAN with DTM HO support) and clause 6.2.2.3 (vSRVCC from E-UTRAN to UTRAN with PS HO support) have the source E-UTRAN send a Handover Required message with SRVCC HO indication and a Source to Target Transparent Container to the source MME. Clause 6.3.2.1 (SRVCC from UTRAN (HSPA) to GERAN without DTM support) and clause 6.3.2.2 (SRVCC from UTRAN (HSPA) to UTRAN or GERAN with DTM HO support) have the source UTRAN(HSPA) send a Relocation Required message with SRVCC Handover Indication and a Source to Target Transparent Container to the source SGSN. Clause 6.4.3.1 (SRVCC to E-UTRAN/UTRAN (HSPA) from GERAN without DTM/PS HO support) has the source RNC/BSC send a HO required indicating CS to PS to the MSC Server, which is part of the same flow relaying towards MME/SGSN.

questions.question: Which clauses describe cancellation of a handover, where the source access node aborts and the MME/SGSN must return to the state it had before the handover was triggered?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 8.1.3 'Handover Cancellation' (SRVCC from E-UTRAN/UTRAN) and clause 8.2.3 'CS to PS Handover Cancellation' both state that if the source E-UTRAN/UTRAN/RAN decides to terminate the handover procedure before completion, the MME/SGSN (or MSC Server) shall return to its state before the handover was triggered. Clause 4.11.1.2.3 'Handover Cancel' (TS 23.502) covers the same for NG-RAN/E-UTRAN source RAN nodes cancelling towards AMF/MME up to when the handover command is sent to the UE, and clause 5.2.2.11.4 'Handover Cancel' (TS 32.255) describes the corresponding charging aspects for the same Handover Cancel procedure.

questions.question: In which procedures does the GCS AS ask the BM-SC to deallocate TMGIs immediately, irrespective of their expiration times?
questions.reference_answer: The TMGI Deallocation Procedure, described in clause 5.1.2.2.3 of TS 23.468 (stage-2, GCS AS sends a Deallocate TMGI Request to the BM-SC) and its Diameter realization in clause A.1.2 of TS 29.468 (GCS AS sends a Diameter GAR command), is used by the GCS AS to immediately release a set of TMGIs, irrespective of their expiration times.

questions.question: Which MB2 procedures are specified with Diameter commands exchanged between the GCS AS and the BM-SC rather than as abstract stage-2 messages?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.2 'Procedures' (MBMS bearer allocation over MB2-C/MB2-U), clause A.1.2 'TMGI Deallocation Procedure' (GCS AS sends a Diameter GAR command, BM-SC responds with a Diameter GAA command), and clause A.2.4 'MBMS Bearer Status Indication Procedure' (BM-SC sends a Diameter GNR command, GCS AS responds with a Diameter GNA command) are MB2 procedures in TS 29.468 specified with Diameter commands between the GCS AS and BM-SC rather than as abstract stage-2 messages.

questions.question: Which procedures have the BM-SC and the GGSN in the same step when a subscriber's registration to an MBMS multicast bearer service is being torn down?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 17.5.5 'De-registration procedure (GGSN initiated)' (the GGSN sends a STR to the BM-SC and the BM-SC removes the GGSN from the list of downstream nodes, confirming with a STA) and clause 17.5.7 'Service deactivation' (the GGSN sends a STR to the BM-SC when a UE requests to leave the multicast service, and the BM-SC confirms with a STA, after which the GGSN deletes the MBMS UE Context) both place the BM-SC and the GGSN in the same step when a subscriber's registration to an MBMS multicast bearer service is torn down.

questions.question: When a P-CSCF fails and PDN GW must notify affected UEs over S5 PMIP, which node detects the failure and which node relays the notification onward via PMIP?
questions.reference_answer: The GGSN/PDN GW detects the P-CSCF failure (via Gi/sGi) and informs all UEs associated with the failed P-CSCF address by sending a PMIP UPN message (with a P-CSCF failure Indicator in the PCO) to the SGW; the SGW then relays the notification onward via PMIP, sending an Update Bearer Request to the MME and responding to the PDN GW with a PMIP UPA message.

questions.question: Which procedures show the MSC Server and the RNC involved in the same handover flow for CS services, including inter-MSC handover and local switching cases?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 8.2.3 'CS to PS Handover Cancellation' (TS 23.216) involves the MSC Server together with the MME/source RAN in a CS-related cancellation flow. In TS 23.284, clause 8.2.2.1.5 (Basic Sequence for Intra-MSC UMTS to GSM Handover that establishes Local Switching) and clause 8.2.3.1.4 (Example of Inter-MSC UMTS to GSM Handover that establishes Local Switching) place the MSC-1 Server and the RNC together via an Iu Relocation Required message; clause 8.3.1.6.1 (Connection Model for Intra-MSC GSM to UMTS Handover) and clause 8.3.2.4.2 (Basic Sequence for Inter-MSC handover that breaks Local Switching) show the MSC Server and RNC (Target RNC) together for the reverse GSM to UMTS handover, including inter-MSC cases. Clause 9.14.4 of TS 43.318 (CS Handover from GAN Iu mode to UTRAN) also shows the MSC and RNC/UTRAN involved in the CS handover flow, via the Serving GANC signalling Relocation Required to the MSC.

questions.question: Which procedures place the MSC Server, the MME and a gateway node together in one step of a mobile terminating call or SRVCC flow?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.2.2.1 'SRVCC from E-UTRAN to GERAN without DTM support' places the MME and MSC Server together (MME sends SRVCC PS to CS Request to the MSC Server) after splitting the voice bearer, targeting the CS domain gateway side. Clause 7.2 'Mobile Terminating call in idle mode' and clause 7.4 'Mobile Terminating call in Active Mode - No PS HO support' (TS 23.272) place the MSC Server/G-MSC and the MME together via the SGs interface (MME receives Paging Request from the MSC) for a mobile terminating call, involving gateway nodes such as the G-MSC.

questions.question: Which procedures let a supporting UE read the shared RAN broadcast system information and offer the available core network operator PLMN-ids to PLMN selection in a MOCN configuration?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.1.5.1 'UTRAN based MOCN configuration' and clause 7.1.5.2 'GERAN based MOCN configuration' both describe a supporting UE reading the broadcast system information in the shared RAN, decoding it to obtain the available core network operator PLMN-ids from the Multiple PLMN ID List, and supplying them as candidates to the PLMN selection procedure.

questions.question: Which positioning procedures have the LMF and the serving gNB exchanging NRPPa Positioning Information messages about UL-SRS resources in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.14.2 'Area-specific SRS (Pre-)configuration Allocation Procedure' and clause 7.14.3 'Area-specific SRS Configuration Update Procedure' have the LMF and serving gNB exchange NRPPa Positioning Information Request/Response (and Update) messages for area-specific SRS configuration. Clause 8.10.4 'Sequence of Procedure for Multi-RTT positioning', clause 8.13.3.4 'Sequence of Procedure for UL-TDOA positioning', and clause 8.14.3.4 'Sequence of Procedure for UL-AoA positioning' each have the LMF send an NRPPa POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST to the serving gNB to request UL-SRS configuration, with the gNB responding via NRPPa POSITIONING INFORMATION RESPONSE.

questions.question: Which procedures deal with area-specific SRS configuration for a UE in RRC_INACTIVE, where the UE sends an RRC Resume Request with cause srs-PosConfigOrActivationReq and the LMF is informed?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.14.2 'Area-specific SRS (Pre-)configuration Allocation Procedure', clause 7.14.3 'Area-specific SRS Configuration Update Procedure', and clause 7.14.4 'Area-specific SRS Configuration Activation Procedure' all deal with area-specific SRS configuration for a UE in RRC_INACTIVE: the UE sends an RRC Resume Request with resume cause "srs-PosConfigOrActivationReq", and the last serving gNB sends an NRPPa Positioning Information Update message to inform the LMF.

questions.question: Which uplink-based positioning methods describe a sequence where the LMF first obtains TRP information, then requests UL-SRS configuration from the serving gNB, and finally collects measurements from the gNBs?
questions.reference_answer: Multi-RTT positioning (clause 8.10.4), UL-TDOA positioning (clause 8.13.3.4), and UL-AoA positioning (clause 8.14.3.4) each describe a sequence where the LMF first obtains TRP information (step 0), then sends an NRPPa POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST to the serving gNB to request/configure UL-SRS, and finally collects UL-SRS measurements from the gNBs via NRPPa MEASUREMENT REQUEST/Response messages.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the LMF together with PRS or TRP configuration, such as on-demand PRS transmission or a pre-configured PRS processing window?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.6.2 'On-Demand PRS transmission procedures' involves the LMF configuring/receiving requests for On-Demand PRS transmission (via LPP Provide/Request Assistance Data), using TRP Information Exchange information on possible On-Demand PRS configurations. Clause 7.8.2 'Pre-configured PRS processing window procedures' involves the LMF providing PRS information of neighbour TRPs to the serving gNB and requesting/activating a pre-configured PRS processing window via NRPPa MEASUREMENT PRECONFIGURATION/ACTIVATION messages. Clause 8.10.4 'Sequence of Procedure for Multi-RTT positioning' involves the LMF obtaining TRP information (step 0) as part of the Multi-RTT positioning sequence.

questions.question: Which procedures show the E-SMLC exchanging LPP messages with the UE via the MME, including the NB-IoT idle-state measurement case?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.4.2 'LPP PDU Transfer' describes the E-SMLC exchanging LPP PDUs with the UE via the MME (LCS-AP PDU to MME, NAS Transport Message, S1AP Downlink NAS Transport to eNodeB). Clause 7.1.3 'UE positioning measurements in idle state for NB-IoT' covers the NB-IoT idle-state measurement case, with the E-SMLC sending LPP Request Capabilities/Provide Assistance Data/Request Location Information messages to the UE via the MME while the UE is in idle state. Clause 7.3.1 'NI-LR and MT-LR Service Support' and clause 7.3.2 'MO-LR Service Support' also show the E-SMLC exchanging LPP messages with the UE via the MME as part of NI-LR/MT-LR and MO-LR location services.

questions.question: Which procedures put the E-SMLC and the eNB together for uplink SRS positioning information, such as requesting uplink information or updating uplink positioning information?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 8.5.3.1 'Uplink Information Request and Delivery Procedure' has the E-SMLC send an Information Request to the eNodeB to configure SRS for the target UE and retrieve the allocated resources, and clause 8.5.3.2 'Uplink Positioning Information Update Procedure' has the eNB send an Uplink Positioning Information Update message to the E-SMLC when the UE's SRS transmission configuration changes (e.g. due to handover).

questions.question: Which MO-LR service support procedures exist where the UE originates the location request and LPP signalling is used towards the location server?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.3.2 (TS 36.305) 'MO-LR Service Support' and clause 7.3.3 (TS 38.305) 'MO-LR Service Support' both describe the UE-originated MO-LR location request, carrying an LPP PDU to the MME/AMF and on to the E-SMLC/LMF for capability transfer, assistance data and/or location information exchange using LPP signalling. Clause 7.1.2.3 (TS 36.305) 'Location information transfer' describes the underlying LPP Location Information Transfer/Delivery procedure used for this UE-to-server signalling (noting the Delivery procedure can only be piggybacked in the MO-LR request), and clause 7.6.2 (TS 38.305) 'On-Demand PRS transmission procedures' notes that the LPP Request Assistance Data message for On-Demand PRS may also be sent in an MO-LR location service request message.

questions.question: Which UTRAN positioning procedures are initiated by the SAS and use PCAP signalling towards the SRNC in the same flow?
questions.reference_answer: The SAS-initiated procedures using PCAP signalling towards the SRNC are: clause 10.7 'SAS initiated Network Assisted GPS positioning Procedure' (A-GPS), clause 14.3.1 'SAS initiated Barometric Pressure positioning procedure', clause 15.2 'SAS initiated WLAN positioning procedure', clause 16.2 'SAS initiated Bluetooth positioning procedure', clause 17.3.1 'SAS initiated TBS positioning procedure', and clause 9.6.2 'SAS based selection of OTDOA' — each has the SRNC send a PCAP Position Initiation Request to the SAS, and the SAS respond with a PCAP Position Activation Request to the SRNC.

questions.question: Which UTRAN positioning procedures involve the SAS and the SRNC together for OTDOA, either selecting OTDOA or using it as a fallback?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 9.6.2 'SAS based selection of OTDOA' has the SAS send a PCAP Position Activation Request to the SRNC requesting the OTDOA positioning method directly. Clause 14.3.1 'SAS initiated Barometric Pressure positioning procedure' involves OTDOA as a fallback/companion method: the SAS's PCAP Position Activation Request allows for the use of Barometric Pressure positioning "along with GPS or OTDOA".

questions.question: Which SAS-initiated positioning procedures cover sensor-based or short-range methods, namely barometric pressure, WLAN, Bluetooth and TBS?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 14.3.1 'SAS initiated Barometric Pressure positioning procedure', clause 15.2 'SAS initiated WLAN positioning procedure', clause 16.2 'SAS initiated Bluetooth positioning procedure', and clause 17.3.1 'SAS initiated TBS positioning procedure' cover these SAS-initiated sensor-based/short-range positioning methods, each via a PCAP Position Activation Request sent from the SAS to the SRNC.

questions.question: Which procedures describe event reporting to an LCS Client or AF while the UE is in RRC INACTIVE state, involving LPP signalling?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.16.1 'Reporting of Location Events to an LCS Client or AF via user plane' describes event reporting when a user plane connection is established directly from the UE to the LCS Client or AF, with the LMF including an LPP positioning message (or the request for user plane reporting) as part of the flow. Clause 6.7.3 'Event Reporting in RRC INACTIVE state for DL Positioning, RAT Independent Positioning or No Positioning' and clause 6.7.5 'Event Reporting in RRC INACTIVE state for UL+DL Positioning' both describe event reporting to the LCS Client/AF while the UE is in RRC INACTIVE state, where the LMF includes an LPP positioning message in the LCS Periodic-Triggered Invoke Request sent to the UE.

questions.question: Which 5GC location service procedures place the AMF, the LMF and the NG-RAN in the same step of a location request?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.1.1 '5GC-MT-LR procedure for the regulatory location service' places the AMF (via Namf_Location_ProvidePositioningInfo) together with the LMF (and NG-RAN) in the location request step. Clause 6.11.2 'Network Assisted Positioning Procedure' has the LMF invoke Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer towards the AMF to transfer a Network Positioning message to the NG-RAN node, based on NRPPa signalling between LMF and NG-RAN. Clause 6.11.3 'Obtaining Non-UE Associated Network Assistance Data' has the LMF invoke Namf_Communication_NonUeN2MessageTransfer towards the AMF, which forwards the Network Positioning message to a target NG-RAN node.

questions.question: Which procedures cover sidelink positioning where SLPP is used, either the SL-MO-LR involving the LMF or the SLPP PDU transfer itself?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.20.1 'Procedures of SL-MO-LR involving LMF' (TS 23.273) describes SL-MO-LR, where the target UE obtains Ranging/Sidelink Positioning location results using other UEs with the assistance of an LMF via SLPP messages carried in supplementary service messages. Clause 7.3A.4 'SL-MO-LR Service Support' (TS 38.305) describes the corresponding UE-side sequence, where UE1 sends an SL-MO-LR Request to the LMF via the serving AMF. Clause 6.4.3 'SLPP PDU Transfer' (TS 38.305) describes the SLPP PDU transfer itself between the LMF and UE via the AMF and NG-RAN (Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer, DL NAS Transport, NGAP Downlink NAS Transport, RRC DL Information Transfer).

questions.question: Which IMS registration related procedures have the P-CSCF sending a Diameter AAR command to the PCRF to establish a new Rx session for a subscription or a provisioning?
questions.reference_answer: Clause B.1 'Subscription to Notification of Signalling Path Status at IMS Registration', clause B.1a 'Subscription to Notification of Change of IP-CAN Type at IMS Registration', clause B.1b 'Provisioning of SIP signalling flow information at IMS Registration', clause B.1c 'Subscription to Notification of Change of PLMN Identifier at IMS Registration', and clause B.5 'P-CSCF Restoration' all have the P-CSCF send a Diameter AAR command to the PCRF to establish a new Rx session, for the respective subscription (signalling path status, IP-CAN type change, PLMN identifier change) or provisioning (SIP signalling flow information, or P-CSCF Restoration).

questions.question: Which Rx procedures involve the P-CSCF and the PCRF together to subscribe to notifications of a change, for example a change of IP-CAN type or a change of PLMN identifier?
questions.reference_answer: Clause B.1 'Subscription to Notification of Signalling Path Status at IMS Registration', clause B.1a 'Subscription to Notification of Change of IP-CAN Type at IMS Registration', and clause B.1c 'Subscription to Notification of Change of PLMN Identifier at IMS Registration' each have the P-CSCF send a Diameter AAR command to the PCRF, subscribing to notification of a change — respectively IMS signalling path status, IP-CAN type change, and PLMN identifier change.

questions.question: Which procedures show the PCRF issuing a Diameter RAR towards a gateway or TDF and receiving the corresponding RAA in the same flow?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 4.2.3.1 'AF located in the HPLMN' (PCRF-initiated IP-CAN Session Termination, PCRF sends RAR to the PCEF/V-PCRF), clause 4.4.4.2 'PCRF-Initiated Gateway Control Session Termination' (PCRF sends RAR to the BBERF), clause 4.5.1.3 'PCEF IP-CAN session modification – S2c-based IP flow mobility' (H-PCRF sends RAR as part of a Gateway Control and QoS Rules Provision procedure), clause 4.6.2 'TDF Session termination' (PCRF sends RAR to the TDF), clause 4.6.3.2 'Application Detection and Control Rules Provision' (PCRF sends RAR to the TDF with ADC-Rule-Install/Remove), and clause B.5 'P-CSCF Restoration' (PCRF sends RAR towards the corresponding IP-CAN session) all show the PCRF issuing a Diameter RAR towards a gateway (PCEF/BBERF) or the TDF and receiving the corresponding RAA.

questions.question: Which procedures have the BBERF sending a Diameter CCR to the PCRF to establish or modify a Gateway Control session?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 4.5.1.1 'New Gateway Control Session Establishment' has the target BBERF send a CCR with CC-Request-Type set to INITIAL_REQUEST to the H-PCRF (or V-PCRF if roaming) to establish a Gateway Control session. Clause 4.5.2.1 'New Gateway Control Session Establishment' has the target BBERF send a CCR with CC-Request-Type set to INITIAL_REQUEST to the V-PCRF. Clause 4.5.2.2 'PCEF-Initiated IP-CAN session modification-Handover' shows a related CCR (from the PCEF, UPDATE_REQUEST) that leads the V-PCRF to link and modify the Gateway Control Session.

questions.question: Which signalling flows describe a PCEF-initiated IP-CAN session modification where the PCEF sends a CCR with CC-Request-Type set to UPDATE_REQUEST to the PCRF, covering both the handover case and the S2c IP flow mobility case?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 4.5.2.2 'PCEF-Initiated IP-CAN session modification-Handover' and clause 4.5.2.3 'PCEF-Initiated IP-CAN session modification - S2c-based IP flow mobility' both have the PCEF send a CCR with CC-Request-Type AVP set to UPDATE_REQUEST to the V-PCRF (handover case: AN_GW_CHANGE/IP-CAN_CHANGE event trigger; S2c IP flow mobility case: ROUTING_RULE_CHANGE event trigger with Routing-Rule-Install/Removal AVPs). Clause 4.5.1.4 and clause 4.5.2.4 (both titled 'Gateway Control Session Establishment and PCEF IP-CAN session modification – S2c-based IP flow mobility') likewise have the PCEF send a CCR with CC-Request-Type set to UPDATE_REQUEST (to the H-PCRF and V-PCRF respectively) for the S2c IP flow mobility case, combined with a Gateway Control Session establishment for a second BBERF.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BBERF, the PCRF and the bearer control mode together in the same Gateway Control session flow?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 4.5.1.1 'New Gateway Control Session Establishment' has the target BBERF send a CCR (INITIAL_REQUEST) to the H-PCRF/V-PCRF to set up the session. Clause 4.5.1.2 'PCEF IP-CAN session modification – Handover' has the H-PCRF derive QoS rules for the BBERF based on the Bearer Control Mode (BCM) of the Gateway Control session and send a Diameter RAR including the selected BCM. Clause 4.5.1.3 'PCEF IP-CAN session modification – S2c-based IP flow mobility' has the H-PCRF derive QoS rules for the BBERF(s) based on the BCM mode of the Gateway Control session and send a Diameter RAR with the QoS rules.

questions.question: Which S9a procedures describe the HNB GW establishing, modifying and terminating an S15 session with the PCRF using Diameter CCR commands?
questions.reference_answer: Clause E.5.1 'S9a CS Session Establishment', clause E.5.2 'PCRF initiated S9a CS Session Modification', and clause E.5.3 'S9a CS Session Termination' describe the HNB GW establishing (CCR with CC-Request-Type INITIAL_REQUEST), modifying (CCR with UPDATE_REQUEST), and terminating (CCR with TERMINATION_REQUEST) an S15 session with the PCRF, which the PCRF in turn maps to a corresponding S9a session with the BPCF.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the TDF and the PCRF together with ADC rules, either establishing a TDF session or provisioning application detection and control rules?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 4.3.1.1 'Interactions between BBERF, PCEF, TDF, OCS, TSSF and PCRF (PCC/QoS/ADC Rule Provisioning in PUSH mode)' has the H-PCRF select the applicable ADC rules for solicited application reporting with a TDF. Clause 4.6.1 'TDF Session Establishment in case of solicited reporting' has the PCRF establish a TDF session and provision the applicable ADC Rules via a Diameter TS-Request. Clause 4.6.3.1 'Application Detection, Reporting and Control Rules Request' has the TDF report application start/stop events (matching activated ADC rules) to the PCRF via a Diameter CCR.

questions.question: Which procedures describe the P-CSCF restoration flow where the AAR carries Rx-Request-Type set to PCSCF_RESTORATION?
questions.reference_answer: Clause B.5 'P-CSCF Restoration' describes the P-CSCF sending an AAR command to the PCRF with the Rx-Request-Type AVP set to PCSCF_RESTORATION to initiate the P-CSCF Restoration procedure. Clause B.1b 'Provisioning of SIP signalling flow information at IMS Registration' is a related IMS-registration AAR-based procedure but does not itself use the PCSCF_RESTORATION Rx-Request-Type — it provisions SIP signalling flow information via a Diameter AAR/AAA exchange.

questions.question: For NBIFOM, when a UE already attached over 3GPP access wants to add an untrusted WLAN leg to the same PDN connection, what indication must the UE have received first?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must already have received from the network an indication that NBIFOM is supported for that PDN connection.

questions.question: Which Cx procedures describe the detailed behaviour of the HSS when it receives a Server-Assignment-Request from the S-CSCF?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.1.1.1 'Detailed behaviour' (TS 29.228) specifies the HSS's step-by-step processing of a Server-Assignment-Request from the S-CSCF (checking Private/Public User Identity existence and association, barring, User-Authorization-Type, etc.), and clause 6.1.2.1 'Detailed behaviour' describes how the S-CSCF uses this SAR/SAA procedure to inform the HSS of registration/deregistration and to provide a P-CSCF Restoration Indication. Clause 4.2.3 'S-CSCF Restoration during Registration Process' and clause 5.4.2.1 'General' (both TS 23.380) describe related HSS behaviour when the SAR carries S-CSCF or P-CSCF restoration information — e.g. the HSS returning S-CSCF restoration information in the SAA, and the HSS-based P-CSCF restoration call flow triggered by a Cx SAR with a P-CSCF Restoration indication.

questions.question: Which SWx or S6b call flows include an IMEI check performed in the VPLMN as part of the AAA exchange?
questions.reference_answer: Clause A.2.3 'Call flow with IMEI check in VPLMN' (TWAN Authentication and Authorization for SCM/EPC-routed access) and clause A.3.2 'Call flow with IMEI check in VPLMN' (for MCM, EPC-routed access and/or Non-seamless WLAN offload) both have the 3GPP AAA Server request the VPLMN to perform the IMEI check (via IMEI-Check-Request-In-VPLMN in the DEA-Flags AVP and Terminal-Information AVP), which the 3GPP AAA Proxy performs and reports back via IMEI-Check-In-VPLMN-Result. Clause E.3 'Call flow with IMEI check in VPLMN' (Untrusted WLAN Authentication and Authorization) has the ePDG request the UE's Mobile Equipment Identity and the 3GPP AAA Proxy perform the IMEI check in the VPLMN before forwarding the DER. Clause A.2.2 'Unsuccessful call flow' does not itself perform an IMEI check — it describes a rejection due to S2a overload.

questions.question: Which procedures show the PMIPv6 LMA acting on a received Proxy Binding Update, checking the home prefix and selecting or re-assigning GRE keys for the PDN connection?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 5.1.3 'LMA procedures' (Initial Binding Registration) has the LMA, on receiving a PBU, select the PDN based on the APN, check if the received IPv6 Home prefix and/or IPv4 Home address are topologically correct, and generate a new uplink GRE key for the PDN connection. Clause 5.3.3 'LMA procedures' (Binding Lifetime Extension after handoff) has the LMA, on receiving a PBU, re-assign the same uplink GRE key used by the previous MAG and again check whether the received IPv6 Home prefix and/or IPv4 Home address are topologically correct.

questions.question: Which Fixed Broadband Access interworking procedures involve the BPCF and the PCRF together over S9a, for PCC provisioning, resource deactivation or IPSec tunnel modification?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.7 'Network-Initiated Dynamic PCC for NS-WLAN offloaded traffic' has the PCRF/V-PCRF initiate an IP-CAN session modification with the BPCF over S9a to provision PCC Rules. Clause 7.8 'PDN GW initiated Resource Allocation Deactivation' has the PCRF/V-PCRF execute a Gateway Control and QoS Rules Provision or a PCRF-Initiated Gateway Control Session Termination with the BPCF over S9a. Clause 7.9 'Handover from 3GPP Access to Fixed Broadband Access with GTP or PMIPv6 on S2b' includes PCC signalling over S9a to provision policies for offloaded traffic when the BPCF receives the IMSI and UE local IP address. Clause 7.11 'IPSec tunnel modified' has the PCRF/V-PCRF initiate the Gateway Control and QoS Rules Provision Procedure with the BPCF over S9a following an IPSec tunnel update. Clause P.7.5.1 'BBERF-Initiated Gateway Control Session Establishment' (TS 23.203) has the PCRF/V-PCRF trigger Gateway Control Session establishment with the BPCF over S9a.

questions.question: Which N32 handshake procedures are carried out between an initiating SEPP and a responding SEPP over the end to end TLS connection to agree on or exchange security parameters?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 5.2.2 'Security Capability Negotiation Procedure' has the initiating SEPP and responding SEPP agree on the security mechanism (PRINS and/or TLS) over the end-to-end TLS connection. Clause 5.2.3.2 'Parameter Exchange Procedure for Cipher Suite Negotiation', clause 5.2.3.3 'Parameter Exchange Procedure for Protection Policy Exchange', and clause 5.2.3.4 'Parameter Exchange Procedure for Security Information list Exchange' exchange, respectively, cipher suites, protection policy information, and RI public keys/certificates. Clause 5.2.4 'N32-f Context Termination Procedure' has the initiating SEPP terminate the established N32-f context with the responding SEPP.

questions.question: Which SEPP procedures deal with mapping between a foreign FQDN and a telescopic FQDN in either direction?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 5.4.2 'Foreign FQDN to Telescopic FQDN Mapping Procedure' maps a foreign FQDN to a flattened telescopic FQDN (via an HTTP GET with query parameter "foreign-fqdn" to the local SEPP). Clause 5.4.3 'Telescopic FQDN to Foreign FQDN Mapping Procedure' maps in the reverse direction (via an HTTP GET with query parameter "telescopic-label" to another SEPP, returning the "foreignFqdn" attribute). Clause 5.2.2 'Security Capability Negotiation Procedure' establishes the underlying end-to-end TLS connection and security capabilities between SEPPs but does not itself perform FQDN mapping.

questions.question: Which SEPP parameter exchange procedures concern RI public keys or certificates and the protection policy needed to verify modifications at the receiving SEPP?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 5.2.3.3 'Parameter Exchange Procedure for Protection Policy Exchange' exchanges the protection policy information (API-to-IE mapping, list of IE types to be protected, and a modification policy per leaf/non-leaf IE). Clause 5.2.3.4 'Parameter Exchange Procedure for Security Information list Exchange' exchanges the Security Information lists containing RI public keys or certificates needed to verify RI modifications at the receiving SEPP. Clause 5.2.4 'N32-f Context Termination Procedure' establishes/stores the N32-f context identifier used after these exchanges but does not itself concern RI keys/certificates or protection policy.

questions.question: Which GBA-based procedures put the NAF and the BSF together with a USS retrieved from the HSS in the same key request flow?
questions.reference_answer: Clause D.2 (TS 33.110) 'Signalling flow demonstrating a successful key request procedure' and clause C.2 (TS 33.259) 'Signalling flow demonstrating a successful key request procedure' describe the Terminal/Remote Device sending a key request to the NAF Key Center/Centre. Clause 5.3.3 (TS 33.220) 'Procedures using bootstrapped Security Association' describes the UE-NAF interaction where a key selection indication may be present in the application-specific USS. Clause 5.1.3 (TS 33.223) 'BSF processing of NAF GPI request' has the BSF request an AV and the subscriber's GUSS from the HSS, using USS for policy management and key selection indication. Clause B.2.2.2 (TS 33.328) 'Procedures' has the KMS retrieve the B-TID, NAF-Key and related USS information (containing a list of IMPUs) from the BSF as part of the ticket resolve flow.

questions.question: During a multi-connection handover from 3GPP access to Trusted WLAN over GTP S2a, which nodes hold the tunnel between them while the UE is still served by 3GPP access?
questions.reference_answer: The Serving GW and the PDN GW hold the PMIPv6 or GTP tunnel(s) on the S5/S8 interface between them while the UE is still served by 3GPP access.

questions.question: Which IMS media security procedures involve the KMS and MIKEY messages together, either for end-to-end protection or for group communications?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 5.2.8.2.3 (TS 33.180) 'KRR creation procedure by a MCX server or signalling proxy' creates a Key Recommendation Request from a MIKEY message carrying initiating/receiving KMS URIs. Clause 7.2.2 (TS 33.180) 'Security procedures (on-network)' transfers a PCK and PCK-ID to the terminating UE using key material provisioned by a KMS. Clause L.4.4 (TS 33.180) 'Security procedures for group communications (group homed in the protected MC system)' distributes a GMK via a MIKEY payload between GMSs (possibly through a SeGy) using KMS-provisioned key material. Clause 7.2.3 (TS 33.328) 'IMS UE originating procedures for e2e using KMS', clause B.1.2 (TS 33.328) 'Procedures' (originating), and clause B.2.2.2 (TS 33.328) 'Procedures' (terminating) all use MIKEY-TICKET messages exchanged with the KMS for end-to-end IMS media protection.

questions.question: Which procedures protect MSRP media using MIKEY key management in an IMS end-to-end security flow?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.2.3 'IMS UE originating procedures for e2e using KMS' sets up the originating call flow for one RTP or one MSRP session using KMS-based (MIKEY-TICKET) security. Clause B.1.2 'Procedures' details the originating steps, where the initiator prepares a REQUEST_INIT_PSK message sent to the KMS over HTTP. Clause B.2.2.2 'Procedures' details the corresponding terminating steps, where the responder prepares a RESOLVE_INIT_PSK message sent to the KMS to resolve the ticket.

questions.question: Which MC security procedures distribute a GMK from the group management server via the KMS in the same flow, both for the protected and the unprotected group homing case?
questions.reference_answer: Clause L.4.4 'Security procedures for group communications (group homed in the protected MC system)' has the GMS send a MIKEY payload containing a GMK to the GMS in an interconnected (unprotected) system, via the SeGy using key material provisioned by the KMS. Clause L.4.5 'Security procedures for group communications (group homed in the unprotected MC system)' covers the reverse case, where the group is owned by a GMS in the unprotected system and the SeGy generates a GMK/GMK-ID and encrypts it to the GMS in the protected system using KMS-provisioned key material.

questions.question: Which restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery security procedures involve the 5G DDNMF together with an RPAUID or a discovery MIC in the same step, covering Model A and Model B?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.1.3.2.2.1 'Restricted 5G ProSe Direct Discovery Model A' has the Announcing UE send a Discovery Request containing the RPAUID to the 5G DDNMF to obtain the ProSe Code and security material. Clause 6.1.3.2.2.2 'Restricted 5G ProSe Direct Discovery Model B' has the Discoveree UE send a Discovery Request containing the RPAUID to the 5G DDNMF. Clause 6.1.3.3.3.1 'Security procedure for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE Relay Discovery with Model A' has the announcing 5G ProSe End UE protect the direct discovery set including a MIC IE. Clause 6.1.3.3.3.2 'Security procedure for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE Relay Discovery with Model B' has the discoverer 5G ProSe End UE construct a direct discovery set with protected End UE discovery infos, each including a MIC IE.

questions.question: Which CAPIF security procedures are performed between the API invoker and the CAPIF core function over a TLS session, covering both joining and leaving the framework?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.1 'Security procedures for API invoker onboarding' has the API invoker and CAPIF core function establish a secure TLS session and exchange an Onboard API Invoker Request/Response to join the framework. Clause 6.8 'Security procedure for API invoker offboarding' has them use the already-established TLS session to exchange an Offboard API invoker Request/Response, after which the CAPIF core function tears down the TLS session.

questions.question: Which procedures describe a UE or subscriber obtaining a certificate from a PKI portal, including the enrolment request and the delivery of the CA certificate?
questions.reference_answer: Clause E.3.1 (TS 24.109) 'Simple subscriber certificate enrolment' has the UE send an initial enrolment request (a PKCS#10 certification request) to the PKI portal, optionally inside a server-authenticated TLS tunnel. Clause 4.6.1 (TS 33.221) 'Certificate issuing' has the UE request a certificate using PKCS#10 with HTTP Digest authentication (based on B-TID and Ks_NAF). Clause 4.6.2 (TS 33.221) 'CA Certificate delivery' has the UE request and receive the CA certificate from the PKI portal, identifying the CA issuer name in the request URL, again using HTTP Digest authentication.

questions.question: Which procedures require checking certificate revocation using a CRL or OCSP when establishing a secure connection between network entities?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 7.5 (TS 33.310) 'Establishing secure connections between NDS/IP end entities using IKE on the Za interface' has SEGa perform a revocation check with CRL or OCSP to verify the status of SEGb's certificate (and again for the SEG CA cross-certificate). Clause 7.2.4 (TS 33.320) 'SeGW/IKEv2 Processing Requirements for H(e)NB Certificates' has the SeGW check the certificate revocation status if configured by local policy when validating H(e)NB certificates.

questions.question: When the HSS pushes an Insert Subscriber Data message to the MME, what must the MME do with the stored subscription data, and how does it acknowledge the HSS?
questions.reference_answer: The MME updates the stored Subscription Data and acknowledges the HSS by returning an Insert Subscriber Data Ack (IMSI) message, with the update result contained in the Ack message.

questions.question: Which 5G ProSe sidelink security flows derive or distribute SLPGK and SLPTK keys with the SLPKMF for broadcast and groupcast communication?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.4.4.2 'Security flows for broadcast/groupcast communication' has the sending UE send a Key Request to the SLPKMF, which replies with a Key Response containing the SLPGK and SLPGK ID (with validity time and chosen algorithms). Clause 6.4.4.3.1 'Message processing in the sending UE' has the sending UE form an RSPP message header containing the Group member ID, SLPGK ID, and SLPTK ID (with a counter) to protect broadcast/groupcast messages using these keys.

questions.question: Which PIN procedures involve the PINE and the PIN server together for registration lifecycle actions, whether the request goes directly or through an intermediate element?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 8.4.2.2.1 'PINE registration directly to PIN server' has the PINE send a PINE Registration Request directly to the PIN server. Clause 8.4.2.2.2 'PINE registration indirectly to PIN server' has the PEMC substitute for the PINE/PEGC and forward the registration request to the PIN server. Clause 8.4.2.2.5 'PINE de-registration directly to PIN server' has the PINE send a de-registration request directly to the PIN server. Clause 8.4.2.2.7 'PINE update registration to PIN server' has the PINE send an update registration request to the PIN server, either directly or via the PEGC.

questions.question: Which PIN management procedures place the PEMC and the PEGC in the same step, for example when creating a PIN or when a PIN element leaves it?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 8.4.2.2.2 'PINE registration indirectly to PIN server' has the PEMC represent the PINE/PEGC to register into the PIN server, involving the PEMC and PEGC together. Clause 8.5.2.2 (PIN creation procedure) has the PEMC send a PIN creation request to the PIN server that can include PINE-2, the PEGC of the PIN, as one of the listed PIN elements. Clause 8.5.8.2.2 'Procedure of PIN elements decides to leave the PIN' and clause 8.5.8.2.3 'Procedure of PEMC removes the PIN elements from a PIN' both have the PEMC send PIN status notify requests to the PEGC (and PIN server) when a PIN element leaves or is removed.

questions.question: Which procedures describe removing a PIN element from a PIN, either because the element itself decides to leave or because the PEMC removes it?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 8.5.8.2.2 'Procedure of PIN elements decides to leave the PIN' describes the PINE itself deciding to leave, sending a leave request to the PEMC, which authorizes and removes it. Clause 8.5.8.2.3 'Procedure of PEMC removes the PIN elements from a PIN' describes the PEMC itself deciding to remove the PINE. Clause 8.4.2.2.5 'PINE de-registration directly to PIN server' is a related but distinct procedure — de-registration from the PIN server rather than removal from a PIN.

questions.question: Which procedures perform UUAA in EPS, where the UAV supplies a Service Level Device Identity during a PDN connection establishment?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 5.2.3.3 'USS UAV Authorization/Authentication (UUAA) during default PDN connection at Attach' has the UE/UAV supply the Service Level Device Identity (CAA-Level UAV ID) in the PCO during the Attach procedure's default PDN connection establishment. Clause 5.2.3.4 'USS UAV Authorization/Authentication (UUAA) using UE requested PDN connectivity procedure' has the UAV supply the same Service Level Device Identity in the PCO of a UE-requested PDN connectivity request, for the case where UUAA-SM is not performed at Attach.

questions.question: Which procedures have the AF and the NEF together requesting or subscribing to NWDAF analytics on behalf of an application?
questions.reference_answer: AF and NEF jointly request/subscribe to NWDAF analytics in: Analytics subscribe/unsubscribe by AFs via NEF (6.1.1.2, using Nnef_AnalyticsExposure_Subscribe/Unsubscribe and Nnwdaf_AnalyticsSubscription_Subscribe/Unsubscribe), Analytics request by AFs via NEF (6.1.2.2, using Nnef_AnalyticsExposure_Fetch and Nnwdaf_AnalyticsInfo_Request), the relative proximity analytics procedure (6.19.4, where NWDAF may subscribe to AF services via NEF using Nnef_EventExposure_Subscribe for an untrusted DCAF), and the user data congestion analytics procedures for a geographic area (6.8.4.1) and for a specific UE (6.8.4.2), where the NWDAF collects input from AF via Naf_EventExposure_Subscribe or Nnef_EventExposure_Subscribe if via NEF.

questions.question: Which NWDAF data collection procedures involve the AF as a data source, either through the NEF or directly from the UE application?
questions.reference_answer: Data Collection from AF via NEF (6.2.2.3, using Nnef_EventExposure_Subscribe/Unsubscribe and Naf_EventExposure_Subscribe/Unsubscribe), the Data Collection Procedure from UE (6.2.8.2.3, where NWDAF subscribes to a trusted AF directly via Naf_EventExposure_Subscribe or to an untrusted AF via NEF using steps 2-3 of the AF-via-NEF procedure), the Procedure for rating untrusted AF data sources (6.2.13.2), and NF load analytics (6.5.4), where for Collective Behaviour attributes the NWDAF subscribes to AF services via Nnef_EventExposure_Subscribe or Naf_EventExposure_Subscribe.

questions.question: After a PDN GW change for emergency services, which node informs the HSS of the new PDN GW identity, and under what condition does it do so?
questions.reference_answer: The 3GPP AAA Server informs the HSS of the new PDN GW identity, using an Update PDN GW Identity Request message. For emergency services this occurs only when the 3GPP AAA Server has successfully received the PDN GW currently in use for emergency services from the PDN GW to which the UE is attached.

questions.question: Which NSCE procedures involve the AF together with an S-NSSAI and a DNN in the same network slice adaptation or slice information delivery step?
questions.reference_answer: The NSCE server-based procedures putting AF, S-NSSAI and DNN together in the same slice adaptation/delivery step are: VAL server-triggered network slice adaptation (9.11.2.1), VAL UE-triggered network slice adaptation (9.11.2.2) - both where the NSCE server acting as AF provides the updated S-NSSAI and DNN per VAL UE to the PCF via NEF; Network Slice Information delivery to NSCE client (9.17.2.2), where the delivered Network Slice Information contains the VAL service ID, S-NSSAI and DNN; and Network Slice Allocation in NSaaS model (9.18.2.1), which also delivers Network Slice Allocation Information containing the VAL service ID, S-NSSAI and DNN.

questions.question: Which NSCE procedures describe slice lifecycle management or predictive slice modification driven by a VAL server policy?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures on slice lifecycle management (9.4.2.1), where the NSCE server triggers network slice LCM operations (modifyNsi/AllocateNsi/DeallocateNsi) based on network slice status and QoE metrics; Network slice optimization based on VAL server policy (9.5.2.2), where the NSCE server triggers slice modification per a VAL-server-provided policy ID; and Procedures on predictive slice modification in edge based NSCE deployments (9.9.2.1), where slice modification or creation is triggered based on predicted VAL UE mobility to a target service area.

questions.question: Which network slice adaptation procedures deliver a URSP related update to the UE after the NSCE server has interacted with the AF?
questions.reference_answer: VAL UE-triggered and network-based network slice adaptation for VAL application (9.11.2.2), Network Slice Information delivery to NSCE client (9.17.2.2), and Network Slice Allocation in NSaaS model (9.18.2.1). In each, the NSCE server acting as AF sends the updated S-NSSAI/DNN guidance to the PCF via NEF as AF-driven guidance for URSP determination, and the 5GC uses this information to update the URSP delivered to the affected UE(s).

questions.question: Which SEAL NRM procedures let a VAL server request, update or delete a background data transfer policy configuration on the NRM server?
questions.reference_answer: Request and Select Background Data Transfer Policy (14.3.13.2, using BDT_Configuration_request) for requesting a BDT policy configuration; BDT configuration update (14.3.13.5, using BDT_Configuration_Update_request) for updating it; and BDT configuration delete (14.3.13.6, using BDT_Configuration_delete_request) for deleting it.

questions.question: Which HR-SBO procedures involve the V-SMF or the V-EASDF in the VPLMN together with home routed policy from the HPLMN?
questions.reference_answer: PDU Session establishment for supporting HR-SBO in VPLMN (6.7.2.2), where the V-SMF selects UL CL/BP, L-PSA UPF and a V-EASDF and the H-SMF retrieves the VPLMN Specific Offloading Policy from H-PCF in the HPLMN; EAS discovery procedure with V-EASDF/Local DNS Server using IP replacement mechanism for supporting HR-SBO (6.7.2.5); and Inter V-SMF mobility registration update procedure in HR-SBO case (6.7.2.7), where the target V-SMF may invoke Neasdf_DNSContext_Create and the H-SMF authorizes HR-SBO and provides the VPLMN Specific Offloading Information.

questions.question: Which MR-DC procedures involve the MN and the SN together with TNL address information exchanged during Secondary Node addition or modification?
questions.reference_answer: Secondary Node Addition (EN-DC, 10.2.1, and MR-DC with 5GC, 10.2.2) both exchange X2-U/Xn-U TNL address information between the MN and SN during SN addition. The ng-eNB/gNB to MN change procedure (10.9.2) has the target MN provide Xn-U DL TNL address information to the target SN in the Xn-U Address Indication message. The SeNB Addition procedure in TS 36.300 (10.1.2.8.1) similarly exchanges S1/X2 DL TNL address information between the MeNB and SeNB.

questions.question: Which dual connectivity procedures put the MCG and the SCG together in the same flow, covering both the EN-DC variant and the MR-DC with 5GC variant?
questions.reference_answer: Conditional Handover with Secondary Node (EN-DC, 10.19.1, and MR-DC with 5GC, 10.19.2) - the source MN includes MCG configuration and, if configured, SCG configuration in the Handover Preparation procedure. Secondary Node Addition (EN-DC, 10.2.1, and MR-DC with 5GC, 10.2.2) - the MN requests SCG configuration for the SN to configure. The Master/MN to eNB or ng-eNB/gNB Change procedures (EN-DC 10.8.1, MR-DC with 5GC 10.8.2) also include both MCG and SCG configuration in the Handover Preparation procedure.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the gNB-CU-CP and the gNB-CU-UP together during a handover or a bearer context change over F1 or E1?
questions.reference_answer: Inter-gNB handover involving gNB-CU-UP change (8.9.4) involves the gNB-CU-CP and gNB-CU-UP together via the Bearer Context Modification/Setup procedures during handover. LTM with gNB-CU-UP change (8.2.1.6) has the gNB-CU-CP perform Bearer Context Setup and Modification with the target and source gNB-CU-UP during an LTM cell switch. Bearer context setup over F1-U (8.9.2) has the gNB-CU-CP send BEARER CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION REQUEST messages to the gNB-CU-UP as part of a bearer context change.

questions.question: Which HNB procedures rely on the U-RNTI assigned from the S-RNTI prefix to route a Cell Update or URA Update during CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH mobility?
questions.reference_answer: HNB to RNC CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH mobility (5.11.4), RNC to HNB CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH mobility (5.11.5), and CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH Iurh based mobility (Intra-GW, HNB to HNB, 5.7.5) all rely on the U-RNTI (assigned from the S-RNTI prefix given to the HNB by the HNB-GW during HNB Registration, 5.2.2) to route the RRC Cell Update or URA Update message via RNSAP Uplink Signalling Transfer Indication to the correct HNB-GW/source HNB or RNC.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the HNB, the HNB-GW and the RNC together when a UE reselects between an HNB and a macro RNC?
questions.reference_answer: HNB to RNC CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH mobility (5.11.4) and RNC to HNB CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH mobility (5.11.5) both involve the HNB, the HNB-GW and the RNC together: the RNC/HNB detects the reselection via the U-RNTI, forwards the RRC Cell/URA Update via RNSAP Uplink Signalling Transfer Indication to the HNB-GW, which selects the source HNB/RNC to complete the SRNS Relocation. The HNB Registration procedure (5.2.2) also involves HNB and HNB-GW, with the HNB-GW assigning the RNC-ID and S-RNTI prefix used later by the RNC during such reselection.

questions.question: Which HNB procedures use RNSAP over Iurh for SRNS relocation or mobility inside the same HNB-GW?
questions.reference_answer: RNC to HNB CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH mobility (5.11.5) and CELL_FACH, CELL_PCH and URA_PCH Iurh based mobility (Intra-GW, HNB to HNB, 5.7.5) both use RNSAP over Iurh, invoked via the RNSAP Uplink Signalling Transfer Indication and SRNS Relocation/Enhanced SRNS Relocation (or RNSAP Common Transport Channel Resources Initialisation) procedures, to perform SRNS relocation or mobility within the same HNB-GW.

questions.question: Which GAN authentication procedures run EAP between the MS and the AAA server through the GANC-SEGW using IKEv2, including the fast re-authentication variants?
questions.reference_answer: EAP-SIM Procedure for authentication (A.1.1), EAP-AKA Procedure for authentication (A.1.2), EAP-SIM Fast Re-authentication (A.1.3.1), and EAP-AKA Fast Re-authentication (A.1.3.2). In all four, the MS initializes IKEv2 (IKE_SA_INIT/IKE_AUTH) and EAP messages are relayed between the MS and the AAA Server through the GANC-SEGW.

questions.question: Which GAN procedures involve the GANC together with ciphering or security mode control of the MS?
questions.reference_answer: Ciphering Configuration (8.8), where the GANC relays the BSSMAP Cipher Mode Command from the CN as a GA-CSR CIPHERING MODE COMMAND to the MS and verifies the MS's MAC before confirming to the CN, and Security Mode Control (9.8), where the GANC relays the RANAP Security Mode Command as a GA-RRC SECURITY MODE COMMAND, selecting the integrity/ciphering algorithms based on CN-permitted algorithms and MS security capabilities.

questions.question: Which registration signalling flows involve the S-CSCF and the SCC AS together, for multiple registration for service continuity or for SRVCC enhancements?
questions.reference_answer: Signalling flows for multiple registration for service continuity (A.3.2) and Signalling flows for registration with SRVCC enhancements (A.3.3), both in TS 24.237: the SIP REGISTER request is forwarded I-CSCF to S-CSCF, and the S-CSCF sends the SIP 200 (OK) response back, while the SCC AS receives registration state information to implement SCC-specific requirements (A.3.2) or via ATCF-inserted registration (A.3.3).

questions.question: Which signalling flows describe session transfer of a call that is still in the alerting phase using SRVCC procedures involving the ATCF?
questions.reference_answer: Session transfer for originating call in alerting phase using SRVCC procedure with ATCF: PS to CS (A.17.7) and Session transfer for terminating call in alerting phase using SRVCC procedure with ATCF: PS to CS (A.17.8). In both, while the call is in alerting phase, the MSC server sends a SIP INVITE request routed via the STN-SR to the ATCF, and the ATCF establishes a new dialog with the SCC AS using the stored ATU-STI for PS to CS SRVCC to indicate the transfer has taken place.

questions.question: Which XCAP signalling flows show a client manipulating a resource list or a presence authorisation document encoded as XML over UTF-8?
questions.reference_answer: Signalling flows demonstrating how XCAP clients manipulate resource lists (A.8.2), where the client uses XCAP PUT/DELETE/GET on an application/resource-lists+xml document; and Signalling flows demonstrating how XCAP clients manipulate presence authorization policy (A.8.3), where the client uses XCAP PUT/DELETE on an application/auth-policy+xml document. Both documents are encoded as UTF-8 XML.

questions.question: Which mission critical client procedures encrypt sent media with SRTP using an MKI derived from the CSK or the group key, covering both the voice and the video service?
questions.reference_answer: The MCPTT client (TS 24.380 clause 13.3.3) and the MCVideo client (TS 24.581 clause 13.3.3): both, in an on-network group call, shall encrypt sent media according to IETF RFC 3711 and TS 33.180 using SRTP-MK, SRTP-MS and SRTP-MKI generated using the GMK and GMK-ID when protection of media is negotiated, and shall encrypt/decrypt unicast floor/transmission/reception control messages and media control messages using SRTP-MK/MS/MKI generated using the CSK and CSK-ID.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GW, the PDN and the PGW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures with modification of bearer (TS 23.214, 6.3.1.7): the PGW-C/PGW-U (PDN GW) modify the Sx session together with the SGW-C/SGW-U during dedicated bearer activation, PDN GW-initiated bearer modification/deactivation, HSS-initiated QoS modification, and MME-initiated bearer deactivation procedures. PDN GW Identity Notification from AAA Server context (12.1.4) also names PGW together with PDN connection registration to the HSS via SGSN/MME.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AAA and the WLAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Addition of Untrusted WLAN access (TS 23.161, 6.2.4.1) — IKEv2 authentication via WLAN between the UE, ePDG and 3GPP AAA Server/HSS; Handover in multi-connection mode from 3GPP access to WLAN on GTP S2a (TS 23.402, 16.10.2.1) — the UE performs access authentication/authorization with the AAA server in the trusted WLAN; Re-authorization/unsolicited re-authentication (TS 29.273, 9.1.2.5.2) — the 3GPP AAA server re-authorizes sessions active for the user over WLAN; and Unauthenticated emergency calls over trusted WLAN (TS 33.402, 13.4) — the UE and the 3GPP AAA Server exchange identity/connection parameters over trusted WLAN via EAP-3GPP-LimitedService.

questions.question: Which procedures put the HSS, the MME and the PDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Insert Subscriber Data procedure (TS 23.401, 5.3.9.2), where the HSS sends Insert Subscriber Data to the MME which may include PDN subscription contexts; PDN GW Identity Notification from AAA Server (TS 23.402, 12.1.4), where the HSS, upon updating the PDN GW identity, sends Insert Subscriber Data to the SGSN or MME registered for the UE; and PDN GW Identity Notification from MME/SGSN (TS 23.402, 12.1.5), where the MME notifies the HSS of the PDN GW identity/APN for the UE's PDN connection.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SGSN and the SRNC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Enhanced Serving RNS Relocation Procedure (TS 23.060, 6.9.2.2.5), used for relocation when source SRNC and target RNC are connected to the same SGSN — the Target RNC sends the Enhanced Relocation Complete Request to the SGSN, which switches the user plane to the target SRNC. MME to 3G SGSN combined hard handover and SRNS relocation procedure (TS 23.401, D.3.3) and 3G SGSN to MME combined hard handover and SRNS relocation procedure (D.3.4) also put the SGSN and the source/target SRNC (RNC) together during relocation resource allocation.

questions.question: For UE policy provisioning when the UE is attached over EPS, which procedures put the EPS, the PCF and the URSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UE Policy Association establishment (4.11.0a.2a.5), which delivers URSP rules in EPS via the PCF for the PDU Session establishing a UE Policy Association with the PCF for the UE; UE Policy Association Termination initiated by PCF for PDU session (4.11.0a.2a.8), triggered on UE detach from EPS or RAT change; URSP provisioning with EPS applicability indication (TS 23.700-85, 6.17.2.1); UE triggered (6.18.2.1) and PCF triggered (6.18.2.2) UE Policy provisioning procedures in EPS; UE Policy delivery procedure initiated by the UE in EPS (6.20.2.1); UE Policy provisioning procedure with explicit URSP Support Indication in EPS (6.33.2.1); and SM Policy and UE Policy Association Update after 5GS to EPS mobility using N26 interface (6.33.2.5) — all deliver/update URSP rules to a UE attached over EPS via the PCF and SMF+PGW-C.

questions.question: In Personal IoT Network management, which procedures involve the PCF, the PEGC and the PIN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PEMC Triggered Service Request to Update PIN_List Procedure (6.10.2.1 and 6.25.2.2), Mobile termination procedure for PINE (6.12.2.2), Support credential provisioning for PINE (6.12.2.3), Procedures for QoS handling of PINE communication with 5GC via PEGC (6.19.2.2), Registration with PIN_Capability and PIN_List Procedure (6.25.2.1), Add/Update/Remove PEGCs for a PIN (6.8.2.2.5), and Activate/Deactivate a PIN (6.8.2.4) — all involve the PCF exchanging PIN-related requests/policies with the PEGC (directly or via PINMF/AMF) for a PIN in TS 23.700-88.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF, the PCF, the PEMC and the PIN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PEMC Triggered Service Request to Update PIN_List Procedure (6.10.2.1 and 6.25.2.2) and Network Triggered Service Request to Update PIN Policies Procedure (6.10.2.2 and 6.25.2.3), where the AMF relays PIN_List/PIN Policy updates between the PCF/PINCTRL and the PEMC; PIN Establishment with pre-provisioned PIN Policies (6.23.2.1), where the AMF handles PEMC registration/authorization and the PCF delivers PIN policies via UE Configuration Update; and Registration with PIN_Capability and PIN_List Procedure (6.25.2.1), where AMF, PCF and PEMC jointly process PIN_Capability/PIN_List during registration.

questions.question: When URSP rules have to survive a move into EPS, which procedures put the EPS, the SMF and the URSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UE Policy Association Termination initiated by PCF for PDU session (4.11.0a.2a.8), triggered when SMF+P-GW-C notifies a RAT change from EPS to 5GS or the last EPS PDN connection supporting URSP is released; UE triggered (6.18.2.1) and PCF triggered (6.18.2.2) UE Policy provisioning procedures in EPS, where the SMF+PGW-C forwards the UE Policy Container/URSP rules between UE and PCF; UE Policy delivery procedure initiated by the UE in EPS (6.20.2.1); and UE Policy provisioning procedure with explicit URSP Support Indication in EPS (6.33.2.1) — all put the SMF (as SMF+PGW-C) and URSP delivery together for a UE in EPS.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the PCF, the PEGC and the PEMC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PEMC Triggered Service Request to Update PIN_List Procedure (6.10.2.1 and 6.25.2.2), Support credential provisioning for PINE (6.12.2.3), Registration with PIN_Capability and PIN_List Procedure (6.25.2.1), Registration of PEGC (6.8.2.2.2), Add/Update/Remove PEGCs for a PIN (6.8.2.2.5), and Activate/Deactivate a PIN (6.8.2.4) — all in TS 23.700-88, where the PEMC interacts with the PCF (directly, via AMF, or via PINMF/NEF) to provision, register, or activate a PEGC and its PIN-related configuration.

questions.question: For PDU Set handling of extended reality traffic, which procedures put the SMF and XR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PDU Set integrated packet handling (6.12.3.1), PDU Session establishment procedure considering application QoS policy (6.19.3.2), PDU session modification (6.26.3.1), PDU Set based QoS handling (6.52.3.1 and 6.55.3.1 MASQUE-based), and PDU session establish procedures for multi-modality communication (6.66.3.2) — all in TS 23.700-60, where the SMF generates QoS profiles and N4 rules (PDU Set identification/marking rules) for XR/media PDU Sets and sends them to the UPF and RAN.

questions.question: Where a third party application drives Personal IoT Network membership, which procedures involve the AF and the PIN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PIN Establishment with pre-provisioned PIN Policies (6.23.2.1), where an AF provides PIN policies (identifier, privacy, traffic routing) via parameter provisioning services; PINE authentication and registration (6.6.2.2), where the P-NF may notify the PIN AF of PINE addition to the PIN; Query PIN information (6.8.2.1.6), Add/Update/Remove PINEs for a PIN (6.8.2.2.4), and Create/Remove association between PEGC and PINE (6.8.2.3.1), where the PINMF may act as a 3rd party AF for the PIN; and PIN creation from 3rd party (6.9.2.1.2), where an AF requests UDM via NEF to create a new PIN network.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EPS, the PCF, the SMF and the URSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UE Policy Association Termination initiated by PCF for PDU session (4.11.0a.2a.8), triggered by UE Detach from the EPS, release of the last URSP-supporting EPS PDN connection, or SMF+P-GW-C notifying a RAT change from EPS to 5GS; and the UE Policy provisioning procedures in EPS (UE triggered 6.18.2.1, PCF triggered 6.18.2.2, UE-initiated delivery 6.20.2.1, explicit URSP Support Indication 6.33.2.1) where the SMF+PGW-C exchanges the UE Policy Container/URSP rules with the PCF for a UE in EPS.

questions.question: For UAV authentication and authorization, which procedures put the AMF, the SMF and the UAS entity in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UAV Re-authentication procedure in 5GS (5.2.4.1): the UAS NF notifies the target NF (AMF or SMF) via Nnef_Authentication_Notification, and if the UE is CM_Idle the target NF triggers a Network Triggered Service Request before the AMF (UUAA-MM) or SMF (UUAA-SM) performs re-authentication. UUAA Revocation by USS/UTM (5.2.7): similarly the UAS NF notifies the target AMF or SMF of revocation, the AMF or SMF triggers Network Triggered Service Request if the UE is CM_Idle, and then the AMF releases UAS-related PDU sessions/de-registers or the SMF releases the PDU session. The general UUAA overview (TS 33.256 5.2.1.1) also describes AMF-triggered UUAA at registration and SMF-triggered UUAA during PDU Session establishment for the UAS entity (UAV).

questions.question: When an application server manages PIN elements on behalf of a subscriber, which procedures put the AF, the PEMC and the PIN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PIN Establishment with pre-provisioned PIN Policies (6.23.2.1): an AF uses parameter provisioning services to provide PIN policies to the PCF, and the UE (PEMC) informs the AMF of PIN establishment. PIN creation from 3rd party (6.9.2.1.2): the AF requests UDM via NEF to create a new PIN network including PEMC and PINE info, and UDM provisions the PIN info to the PEMC via AMF and gNB.

questions.question: For a mobile base station relay serving UEs on the move, which procedures involve the AMF, the MBSR, NG and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Mobile Base Station Relay broadcast service time (6.11.3.1): the UDM sends Subscription Data with MBSR service time information to the AMF, which relays it to the MBSR (UE) over NAS, and the MBSR sets up an F1 link with NG-RAN (NG). Conditional handover according to service time of Mobile Base Station Relay (6.11.3.2): the AMF queries the UDM for MBSR service time in the subscription data and sends it to the MBSR and to NG-RAN (CU) over N2. Signalling flow for roaming of mobile base station relay (6.6.3.2): the VPLMN AMF checks with the UDM whether the MBSR is authorized to operate as such and sends an MBSR authorized indication to NG-RAN.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the AMF, ATSSS, MA and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Network Modification to MA PDU Session after a UE moving from EPC (TS 23.502 4.22.6.3): the AMF forwards the UE's ATSSS Capabilities/indications to the SMF via UpdateSMContext, and if the SMF decides to change the PDU Session to an MA PDU Session it includes ATSSS rule(s) and returns an 'MA PDU session Accepted' indication so the AMF marks the PDU Session as MA PDU Session. The AF-driven PLR/traffic-duplication procedures (TS 23.700-53 6.4.3.1, 6.4.3.2, 6.5.3.2) also have the SMF derive updated ATSSS rules and send them to the AMF via Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer for delivery to the UE.

questions.question: For UPF selection driven by slice and data network identifiers, which procedures put the DNN, the NRF, the NSSAI and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UPF Event Exposure service Registration (6.1.2.1): the UPF registers its NF profile with the NRF including S-NSSAI(s) and DNN(s). UPF Event Exposure service Discovery (6.1.2.4) and Procedure of UPF selection by the NF with information of S-NSSAI, DNN and/or DNAI (6.1.2.5.3): a consumer NF invokes Nnrf_NFDiscovery_Request to the NRF specifying S-NSSAI, DNN (and DNAI) to discover matching UPF instances. Procedure of UPF selection by the NF targeting specific PDU sessions/UEs with Group Identifier (6.1.2.5.4) also falls back to this S-NSSAI/DNN/DNAI-based UPF selection via NRF. Procedure for NWDAF collecting data from UPF (6.12.3.2): NWDAF invokes Nnrf_NFDiscovery_Request to NRF including S-NSSAI, DNN, DNAI to find appropriate UPF(s).

questions.question: For delivering network slice information to a vertical application server, which procedures put the NSCE, the NSMF, the NSP and the NSSAI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Network Slice Information delivery request (TS 23.435 9.17.2.1) and its TS 23.700-99 counterpart (6.18.1.2): the NSCE server, acting as NSP, retrieves the Network Slice ServiceProfile (including S-NSSAI) from the NSMF and delivers Network Slice Information to the VAL server on request. Network Slice Information subscription (6.18.1.3), Notify (6.18.1.4), and delivery while registration (6.18.1.5) likewise have the NSCE server (as NSP) retrieve the ServiceProfile with S-NSSAI from the NSMF and subscribe/notify/deliver that Network Slice Information to the VAL server.

questions.question: For bi-directional QoS flow mapping driven by IP ToS marking, which procedures involve PCC, SDAP, TCP and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The four candidate IP-PFS solutions in TS 26.804 clause 5.3.6 (3a in 5.3.6.4, 3b in 5.3.6.5, 4a in 5.3.6.6, 4b in 5.3.6.7, and 4c in 5.3.6.7~2) for bi-directional QoS flow mapping using IP ToS marking: in each, the PCF authorizes the AF request and creates a PCC rule that is forwarded to the SMF, which forwards the corresponding QoS rule to the UE and UPF; the UPF then detects a PDR match using the ToS value, encapsulates the downlink IP packet into an N3 packet marked with the QFI, and the UE's SDAP entity (Layer 2) marks/detects the QFI for the TCP traffic being steered.

questions.question: When multicast sessions use the user plane in 5GC, which procedures involve the AMF, the MBS session and the UPF together in one step?
questions.reference_answer: MBS session activation procedure (TS 23.247 7.2.5.2): the AMF invokes Namf_MT_EnableGroupReachability toward SMF(s), pages/reactivates UEs, and the MB-SMF instructs the MB-UPF (via N4mb Session Modification) to forward MBS packets while the AMF relays N2 activation requests to NG-RAN. Broadcast MBS session restoration by MB-SMF upon NG-RAN restart (TS 23.527 8.3.2.3) and upon NG-RAN failure without restart (8.3.3): the AMF detects the NG-RAN event and notifies the MB-SMF via Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextStatusNotify/ContextUpdate, and the MB-SMF modifies the PFCP sessions at the MB-UPF (removing/reprovisioning the NG-RAN DL F-TEID) for the affected MBS session.

questions.question: Which procedures put PCC, the SMF and XR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PDU Set integrated packet handling (TS 23.700-60 6.12.3.1): the PCF sends PCC rules (with PDU Set level handling requirements for XR service) to the SMF, which generates N4 rules for the UPF. PDU Session establishment procedure considering application QoS policy (6.19.3.2), PDU session modification (6.26.3.1), PDU Set based QoS handling (6.52.3.1), and PDU session establish procedures for multi-modality communication (6.66.3.2): in each, PCC rules for XR/media traffic are provided by the PCF to the SMF, which configures the UPF via N4 rules for PDU Set / multi-modality QoS handling.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the SMF, the UPF and XR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PDU Set integrated packet handling (6.12.3.1), PDU Session establishment procedure considering application QoS policy (6.19.3.2), PDU session modification (6.26.3.1), PDU Set based QoS handling (6.52.3.1), and the MASQUE-based PDU Set based QoS handling (6.55.3.1) in TS 23.700-60. In each, the SMF sends N4 rules to the UPF to identify/mark PDU Sets (or configure a MASQUE proxy) for XR traffic, supporting PDU Set-level QoS handling for the XR service.

questions.question: When the visited network influences URSP rule creation for a roaming subscriber, which procedures put the PCF, the UDR and the VPLMN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: VPLMN AF guidance for URSP rule creation at an HPLMN (TS 23.700-85 6.2.2.1): the PCF (for the UE) retrieves Application Data subscription information from the UDR and creates updated URSP rules with per-PLMN (VPLMN) validity conditions. Application Guidance of URSP determination in VPLMN (6.28.2.2), UE Policy Association Establishment/Modification with VPLMN assistant information (6.3.2, 6.3.3), and Procedure for URSP determination based on service parameter obtained from VPLMN (6.5.2.1): in each, the V-PCF (in the VPLMN) obtains VPLMN-specific service parameters or assistant information from the (V-)UDR and forwards them to the H-PCF (or generates VPLMN URSP itself) for URSP rule creation.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EPS, the PCF and SM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UE Policy Container delivery via EPS (TS 23.502 4.11.0a.2a.10) and UE Policy Association establishment (4.11.0a.2a.5): the PCF for the UE and PCF for the PDU Session (SM policy) exchange the UE Policy Container, which the SMF+PGW-C (combining SM function with EPS PGW) delivers to/from the UE. UE Policy delivery procedure initiated by the UE in EPS (TS 23.700-85 6.20.2.1), UE Policy provisioning with explicit URSP Support Indication in EPS (6.33.2.1), and SM Policy and UE Policy Association Update after 5GS to EPS mobility (6.33.2.5): in each, the SM-PCF exchanges the UE Policy Container with the UE-PCF and with the SMF+PGW-C to deliver URSP/UE policy over EPS.

questions.question: In UTRAN mobility signalling carried over the Iur interface, which procedures involve the RNC, RNSAP and the SRNC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Hard Handover via Iur (DCH State) (TS 25.931 7.11.1.1): the SRNC sends a Radio Link Setup Request to the target RNC and exchanges RNSAP Radio Link Failure/Restore/Deletion messages with the source/target RNC. Cell Update via Iur with USCH/DSCH without SRNS relocation (7.11.2.4) and Inter-RNS URA Update via Iur without SRNS relocation (7.12.2): the target RNC forwards the Cell/URA Update to the SRNC via RNSAP Uplink Signalling Transfer, and the SRNC initializes/releases the UE context in the target RNC via RNSAP Common Transport Channel Resource messages. MBMS Service Activation (7.19.1) uses RNSAP MBMS Attach Command / Information Exchange between the SRNC and DRNC. Soft Handover (7.20.2): the SRNC requests radio resources from another RNC (DRNC) via RNSAP Radio Link Setup Request/Response and Radio Link Restore Indication.

questions.question: For packet-switched service continuity between GAN and the cellular radio networks, which procedures put GA, the PDP context and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PDP Context Activation/De-Activation for EGAN capable handsets (TS 43.902 5.1.1.3.2): the MS GA-SM layer activates/deactivates a PDP context via the Proxy-Gn, and on the GERAN/UTRAN side the unchanged SGSN processes the corresponding Activate/Deactivate PDP Context Request/Response. PS Handover procedures between GAN and GERAN/UTRAN (5.1.1.3.3) and CS+PS Handover between GAN and GERAN/UTRAN (5.1.1.3.4): the MS GA-SM initiates/updates a PDP Context Activation while the SGSN (unchanged) processes the Create/Update/Activate PDP Context messages during the RAT switch. PDP Context Activation (TS 43.902 5.2.5.18) and Network Requested PDP Context Activation (5.2.5.19): the MS sends GA-RRC-encapsulated Activate PDP Context Request/Accept messages that the GANC relays to/from the SGSN.

questions.question: When localized service information reaches the UE through broadcast system information, which procedures involve NG and the SIB in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedure for Human Readable Localized Service information in On-Demand SIB (TS 23.700-08 6.34.3.1): NG-RAN broadcasts SIB1 indicating scheduling of an on-demand SIBxx, and broadcasts SIBxx upon UE request. Procedure for retrieval of Localized service information from URL (6.34.3.2): NG-RAN broadcasts a code in SIB (SIB10 or a new SIBxx) that the UE uses to build a URL. Procedure for Hosting network search assistance information in SIB (6.44.3.1): NG-RAN broadcasts hosting network search assistance information in SIB. Mobile Base Station Relay broadcast service time (TS 23.700-05 6.11.3.1) also has the MBSR (DU), commanded by NG-RAN, include service time information in the SIB it broadcasts. 5G access stratum time distribution status reporting (TS 23.502 4.15.9.5.2) has the NG-RAN node indicate timing synchronization status via SIB (SIB9) information.

questions.question: For aggregate maximum bit rate handling of a 5G LAN group, which procedures put the AMBR and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedure for support of the attribute of Group-MBR for a VN group (TS 23.700-74) when a UE initiates a 5G LAN PDU session establishment request (6.21.3.1): the SMF sends group information update requests to the GSMF including Session-AMBR and MFBR, and the PCF can reject or adjust the session if the sum of AMBR for the VN group reaches Group-MBR. The corresponding release (6.21.3.2) and modification (6.21.3.3) procedures likewise have the SMF send a group information update request with AMBR-related information to the GSMF, which updates the sum of Session-AMBR/MFBR for the VN group.

questions.question: For sidelink assisted positioning of a target UE, which procedures involve the KI and the LMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Location service for UE served by a mobile IAB-node (TS 23.700-05 6.18.3.1): the LMF is invoked by the AMF for UE positioning and separately initiates location reporting for the IAB-node/IAB-UE (related to KI#2/KI#3). MT-LR (TS 23.700-86 6.20.3.1) and MO-LR (6.20.3.2) procedures for Network assisted Sidelink positioning explicitly reference 'the procedure defined by the solutions for KI#3' for Located UE discovery, with the (UE1) LMF triggering positioning and determining UE1's location. LMF triggered Ranging/sidelink positioning (6.28.3.1) references KI#4 for the ranging/positioning steps. questions.question: For a session-based messaging session set up without preconditions, why does each UE need to reserve a separate IP-CAN bearer before the first MSRP message is sent?
