questions.reference_answer: Because both the originating and terminating UE use an IP-CAN with a separate bearer for SIP signalling, so each UE needs to reserve a new IP-CAN bearer for the message session media component before sending the first MSRP message.

questions.question: For an IMS emergency call detected by the UE over non-3GPP access to 5GC, what must the P-CSCF do with a registration request that is not for emergency purposes if it came from an emergency PDU session?
questions.reference_answer: For registration requests received from an emergency PDU session, the P-CSCF shall reject any IMS registration which is not for the emergency purpose.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PDN and the RAU in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Routing Area Update with MME interaction and without S-GW change; Routing Area Update with MME interaction and with S-GW change; Successful TAU/RAU procedure with T6a/T6b; and the GTP-C message prioritization procedure based on procedure categories (TAU/RAU with a change of MME/SGSN, which could result in loss of the PDN connection) put the PDN and the RAU in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the LADN and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: 5G-RG PDU Session establishment via W-5GAN (where the AMF assigns a LADN presence indication that induces the SMF to reject the PDU Session establishment) and CN-initiated selective deactivation of UP connection of an existing PDU Session (where the SMF is notified the UE moved out of the LADN service area) put the LADN and the SMF in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MT and the SM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Successful Mobile Terminated short message transfer via IP-SM-GW and Unsuccessful Mobile Terminated short message transfer via IP-SM-GW put the MT and the SM in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AAA, the PGW and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: ePDG triggered PDN connection restoration; Secondary authentication and authorization by DN-AAA at PDN Connection Establishment; and Authentication and Authorization procedures in EPC Interworking (both the RADIUS-based and Diameter-based variants) put the AAA, the PGW and the SMF in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BM, the MBMS and the UDP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Header compression by the BM-SC; Session start procedure (both the GGSN-based and MBMS GW-based variants in TS 29.061); and the MB2-C bearer allocation Procedures in TS 29.468 put the BM, the MBMS and the UDP in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ACK, the CSCF and the UDP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UE initiating an emergency session in IMS; Establishing a session for session-based messaging without preconditions; Establishing a session for session-based messaging with Intermediate Nodes; and Establishing a CSI session when CS call has been setup put the ACK, the CSCF and the UDP in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AP and the WLAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: High Level Procedures for IMS emergency calls; IW-MT-LR Procedure without HLR/HSS or AAA Query; and Procedure for WLAN Connection Status Reporting put the AP and the WLAN in the same step.

questions.question: For SRVCC using ATCF enhancements, which node allocates the STN-SR at initial IMS registration, and which node must receive it before SRVCC is triggered?
questions.reference_answer: The ATCF allocates the STN-SR when the user performs initial registration in the IMS. The STN-SR must be provided (via IMS and third-party registration to the SCC AS, and onward to the UDM/HSS which updates the MME/SGSN, or the AMF in 5GS) so that it reaches the MME before the SRVCC procedure is triggered.

questions.question: During a Tracking Area Update with Serving GW change, what must the timer set by the old MME or S4 SGSN guarantee about buffered data at the old Serving GW?
questions.reference_answer: The timer set by the old MME or S4 SGSN must ensure that the buffered data in the old Serving GW can be forwarded before the old Serving GW resource is released.

questions.question: Before a CM-IDLE UE can send an uplink SMS over NAS, what procedure must the UE and network perform first to reach the AMF?
questions.reference_answer: The UE and network must first perform the UE Triggered Service Request procedure to establish a NAS signalling connection to the AMF.

questions.question: Which procedures put the HSS and the SCC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Registration using ATCF enhancements; Termination to non ICS UE not registered in IMS; and the Enhanced service request procedure (Description) put the HSS and the SCC in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EPS, the MME and the PGW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Tracking Area Update procedure with Serving GW change and data forwarding; 5GS to EPS Mobility; and EPS to 5GS Handover Preparation put the EPS, the MME and the PGW in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF, the CP and the NAS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN; MO SMS over NAS in CM-IDLE (baseline); and Authentication for 5G-RG put the AMF, the CP and the NAS in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the DAPS and the DRB in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: S1-based DAPS handover, normal; Execution phase for DAPS handover; and NR SA FR1 Intra-band inter-frequency asynchronous DAPS handover put the DAPS and the DRB in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ARP, the EPS and the PCC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures with dedicated bearer activation by PGW; the Procedure in TS 23.280 clause 10.11.5.2 (resource request including priority sharing information); and HSS Initiated Subscribed QoS Modification put the ARP, the EPS and the PCC in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the DRX and the PSM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedure for Deployment Option 3; Network parameter coordination procedure; and Notification (Availability Notification after DDN Failure) put the DRX and the PSM in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CAMEL and the CSI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures and information flows for PN UE redirection in the CS domain; Call flows for setting up the voice session for CSI origination and IMS termination with CSI interworking; and PN UE redirection in the CS domain (TS 24.259) put the CAMEL and the CSI in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EPC and the MBMS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure in TS 23.280 clause 10.7.3.10.2 (MBMS bearer event notification); the Procedure in TS 23.379 clause 10.10.6.2 (application paging over an MBMS bearer); and the Procedure in TS 23.434 clause 14.3.4.8.2 (MBMS bearer event notification) put the EPC and the MBMS in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MBMS and the MCH in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure in TS 23.280 clause 10.7.3.8.2 (MBMS suspension notification from MC service client); the Procedure in TS 23.434 clause 14.3.4.7.2 (MBMS suspension notification); and Switching from Unicast Delivery to MBMS Delivery put the MBMS and the MCH in the same step.

questions.question: When a Dedicated Core Network reselection reroutes an Attach Request to another CN node, which node initiates the Reroute NAS Message Request and what does it include in it?
questions.reference_answer: The first new MME/SGSN initiates the Reroute NAS Message Request, sent to the RAN Node. It includes the original RAN message, reroute parameters (MMEGI for E-UTRAN or Null-NRI/SGSN Group ID for UTRAN/GERAN), Additional GUTI/P-TMSI, UE Usage Type, and optionally the IMSI.

questions.question: A VAL Server wants to negotiate a background data transfer policy with the 3GPP network. Which request does it send to the NRM Server, and what information does it include?
questions.reference_answer: The VAL Server sends a BDT_Configuration_request to the NRM Server. It includes the expected data volume, expected number of UEs, and expected time window for the background data transfer, and may also include group ID, geographic information for the UEs, a request expiration time, and guidance for policy selection.

questions.question: During RAN-initiated QoS Flow mobility to a Secondary RAN Node, are the SMF and UPF ever re-allocated, and what connectivity is assumed to exist for this procedure to work?
questions.reference_answer: No, the SMF and UPF are never re-allocated during this procedure. It assumes IP connectivity exists between the UPF and the Master RAN node, as well as between the UPF and the Secondary RAN node.

questions.question: For delivering SMS to a non-ported number via direct routeing, which node does the SMSC forward the message to first, and which entity does that node query about the MSISDN?
questions.reference_answer: The SMSC forwards the SM to the SMS-GMSC. The SMS-GMSC then queries the network's MNP-SRF (via a MAP SRI_for_SM message) about the MSISDN.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ASP and the BDT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Request and Select Background Data Transfer Policy; Procedure for BDT warning notification; and Negotiation for future background data transfer procedure put the ASP and the BDT in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AF and the ASP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Negotiation for future background data transfer (TS 23.203); Procedures for negotiation of planned data transfer with QoS requirements; and Negotiation for future background data transfer procedure (TS 29.513) put the AF and the ASP in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GUTI, the MME and the NAS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: NAS Message Redirection Procedure; E-UTRAN Initial Attach; and TAU Procedure put the GUTI, the MME and the NAS in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NG and the QFI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: RAN Initiated QoS Flow Mobility; EPS to 5GS Handover Preparation; and PDU Session Establishment put the NG and the QFI in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MAP and the SM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Delivery of SMS to a Non-ported Number - Direct Routeing - MNP-SRF acts as SCCP Relay; the IP-SM-GW-to-HSS unavailability signalling flow (TS 24.341 clause B.4); and the Notification procedure in TS 29.305 clause A.4.4.8 (mapping MAP ReadyForSM) put the MAP and the SM in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF and the LADN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: 5G-RG PDU Session establishment via W-5GAN; CN-initiated selective deactivation of UP connection of an existing PDU Session; and N2 Handover Execution put the AMF and the LADN in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AKA, the EAP and the IK in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Authentication and key agreement for trusted access; Authentication procedure for EAP-AKA'; and the EAP-AKA Procedure for authentication in TS 43.318 put the AKA, the EAP and the IK in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the RAB and the TNL in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Mobility procedure (TS 25.467 Annex A.3, Inter-HNB Inter-HNB-GW SRNS Relocation); SeNB Addition; and EN-DC (Secondary Node Addition) put the RAB and the TNL in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the DCH and the RNSAP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: RNSAP Protocol (TS 25.420); RNSAP Procedure Modules (TS 25.423); and RNSAP protocol (TS 43.051) put the DCH and the RNSAP in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CN and the IMSI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: CSPS Coordination; UE Registration: case of non CSG UEs or non CSG HNBs; and Mobile Terminated Call Flow (TS 43.318) put the CN and the IMSI in the same step.

questions.question: For home-routed roaming PDU sessions, which procedures have the AMF, the SMF and a VPLMN entity acting in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Home-routed Roaming; UE or network requested PDU Session Modification (home-routed roaming); The selected N3IWF is in the registered PLMN; and Inter V-SMF mobility registration update procedure in HR-SBO case have the AMF, the SMF and a VPLMN entity acting in the same step.

questions.question: When interworking a PDN connection with 5GS, which procedures involve the AMF, the PDN entity and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: 5GS to EPS handover using N26 interface; EPS to 5GS Mobility Registration Procedure (Idle and Connected State) using N26 interface; EPS to 5GS Mobility; and Handover from EPS to 5GC-N3IWF involve the AMF, the PDN entity and the SMF in the same step.

questions.question: For negotiating background data transfer policies, which procedures place the BDT policy, the NEF and the UDR in a single step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures for future background data transfer; Procedure for BDT warning notification; Negotiation for future background data transfer procedure; and Background data transfer policy applying procedure place the BDT policy, the NEF and the UDR in a single step.

questions.question: In edge computing deployments, which procedures put the EAS, the EDN and the EES together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Subscribe-notify model; Procedure (TS 23.558 clause 8.19.2); Request-response model; and Retrieve T-EES procedure put the EAS, the EDN and the EES together in the same step.

questions.question: For policy and charging enforcement, which procedures involve the BBERF, the PCC rules and the PCEF in one step?
questions.reference_answer: Update of the subscription information in the PCRF; Gateway Control and QoS Rules Provision; PCEF IP-CAN session modification - Handover; and PCEF-Initiated IP-CAN session modification-Handover involve the BBERF, the PCC rules and the PCEF in one step.

questions.question: When user plane resources are set up or released in 5GC, which procedures have the AMF, the access network and the UPF acting in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Network Triggered Service Request; AN Release; UE or network requested PDU Session Modification (non-roaming and roaming with local breakout); and UE or network requested PDU Session Release for Non-Roaming and Roaming with Local Breakout have the AMF, the access network and the UPF acting in the same step.

questions.question: For PDN connectivity with dynamic policy in EPC, which procedures put the MME, the PCRF and the PDN gateway in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Sx Session Modification Procedure; Sx Session Termination Procedure; UE requested PDN connectivity; and PDN GW initiated bearer deactivation put the MME, the PCRF and the PDN gateway in the same step.

questions.question: For federated learning among analytics functions, which procedures put the FL entity, the NRF and the NWDAF in a single step?
questions.reference_answer: Registration and Discovery procedure for Federated Learning; Procedures for Maintaining Federated Learning Processes; Preparation Procedure for Federated Learning; and Procedure for Maintenance of Federated Learning Process put the FL entity, the NRF and the NWDAF in a single step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PCEF, the PCRF and the PDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: IP-CAN Session Establishment; PDN GW initiated IPv4 address Delete Procedure (both the TS 23.402 clause 5.11 and clause 6.13 variants); and IPv4 Home Address Release Procedure for S2c put the PCEF, the PCRF and the PDN in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EPS, the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: EPS to 5GS handover using N26 interface; EPS to 5GS Idle mode mobility using N26 interface with data forwarding; Handover from 5GC-N3IWF to EPS; and EPS to 5GS Handover Execution put the EPS, the SMF and the UPF in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AF, the NEF and the PDTQ in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures for negotiation of planned data transfer with QoS requirements; Procedure for PDTQ warning notification; Modification of PDTQ warning notification request indication procedure; and PDTQ warning notification procedure put the AF, the NEF and the PDTQ in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF, the HPLMN and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Home-routed Roaming; UE or network requested PDU Session Modification (home-routed roaming); UE or network requested PDU Session Release for Home-routed Roaming; and Inter V-SMF mobility registration update procedure in HR-SBO case put the AMF, the HPLMN and the SMF in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CSCF, the GRUU and the HSS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Registration information flow - User not registered; Re-Registration information flow - User currently registered; and PN-registration procedure in the IM CN subsystem put the CSCF, the GRUU and the HSS in the same step.

questions.question: For subscriber identification in packet-switched core, which procedures involve the MSISDN and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Update CSG Location Procedure (both the TS 23.060 and TS 23.401 variants); Procedure for Enhanced Coverage Restriction Control via SCEF; Procedure for Network Parameter Configuration via SCEF; and the Configuration Procedure in TS 23.682 clause 5.6.1.1 involve the MSISDN and the SGSN in the same step.

questions.question: When a public service identity is resolved in IMS, which procedures put the CSCF and the PSI together in one step?
questions.reference_answer: Session based messaging procedure using multiple UEs; Originations with CS media using the Gm reference point; Terminations with CS media using the Gm reference point; Terminations with CS media using the I1 reference point; and HSS initiated Deregistration put the CSCF and the PSI together in one step.

questions.question: For untrusted non-3GPP access into 5GC, which procedures place the AMF and the TNGF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Common Positioning Procedures when a UE is served by only one PLMN; Registration procedure for trusted non-3GPP access; UE Policy Association Modification initiated by the AMF without AMF relocation; Registration procedures for non-3GPP access path switching; and Authentication for trusted non-3GPP access place the AMF and the TNGF in the same step.

questions.question: For GTP tunnel handling in 5GC, which procedures put the SMF and GTP together in one step?
questions.reference_answer: MBS Session Update for Broadcast; Multicast MBS session restoration Procedure for NG-RAN failure with or without restart; Broadcast MBS session restoration Procedure for N3mb path failure; Connection Resume in CM-IDLE with Suspend procedure; and Xn Handover put the SMF and GTP together in one step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BPCF, the PCRF and the UDP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: IPSec tunnel modified; IP-CAN Session Establishment (TS 23.203 Annex P); BBERF-Initiated Gateway Control Session Establishment; PCEF-initiated IP-CAN Session Modification; and S9a CS Session Establishment put the BPCF, the PCRF and the UDP in the same step.

questions.question: When the radio access technology matters to core-network handling, which procedures place the AMF, the NG interface and the RAT indication in one step?
questions.reference_answer: Warning Message Cancel Procedure; Emergency Services Fallback; Secondary RAT Usage Data Reporting Procedure; and Using N2InfoNotify during Inter NG-RAN node N2 based handover procedure place the AMF, the NG interface and the RAT indication in one step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BBF and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: UE/ePDG-initiated Detach Procedure and UE-Requested PDN Disconnection; Network initiated bearer activation, modification and deactivation; UE requested bearer resource modification; Secondary PDP Context Activation and PDP Context Modification Procedure; and IP-CAN Session Termination put the BBF and the PCRF in the same step.

questions.question: At an IMS network border, which procedures involve the CSCF, the IBCF and SDP negotiation in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Flow for originating session (TS 23.228 Annex M.1.1.2) and the Message flow procedures in TS 29.079 (clauses A.3.2, A.4.2, A.5.2, A.6.2) involve the CSCF, the IBCF and SDP negotiation in the same step.

questions.question: For SRVCC with access transfer control, which procedures place the ATCF, the MSC and SRVCC handling in one step?
questions.reference_answer: UE IMS Registration change update; Codec re-negotiation after session transfer (SRVCC); Procedure for codec inquiry prior to session transfer; Registration related procedures in the ATCF; and the signalling flows for UE attaching to CS domain when MSC server is enhanced for ICS and for CS to PS SRVCC (TS 24.237 Annex A.3.6) place the ATCF, the MSC and SRVCC handling in one step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CSCF and SRVCC handling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: IMS Emergency origination flow for PS to CS SRVCC; the Alternative procedure based on redirection (both TS 23.237 clause 6c.2.3.2 and 6c.2.4.2); and the signalling flows for registration with SRVCC enhancements in TS 24.237 (Annex A.3.3 and A.3.4) put the CSCF and SRVCC handling in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BM and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MBMS Multicast Service Activation; MBMS Registration Procedure; Registration procedure (TS 29.061 clause 17.5.4); Trace Session Activation procedure; and Trace Session Deactivation procedure put the BM and the SGSN in the same step.

questions.question: For UAV detect-and-avoid (DAA) support, which procedures put the DAA function, the UAS application specific server and the UAV in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Management of DAA support configuration; DAA support involving UAVs with U2X support; DAA support involving UAVs without U2X support; and the Procedures in TS 23.256 clause 5.7.2 put the DAA function, the UAS application specific server and the UAV in the same step.

questions.question: When a UAE server mediates UAV application traffic on behalf of SEAL services, which procedures put the SEAL layer, the UAE server and the UAV in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Communications between UAVs within a geographical area using unicast Uu; Procedure for group creation for one pair of UAV and UAV-C; Procedure for group-based approach for C2 QoS provisioning; UAE-layer assisted dynamic C2 mode switching; and UAE server triggered change of USS put the SEAL layer, the UAE server and the UAV in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the LCS-AP protocol, the MME and the SMLC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Network Assisted and Network Based Positioning Procedure; Obtaining Non-UE Associated Network Assistance Data; Broadcasting Network Assistance Data; LPP PDU Transfer; and Broadcast Procedures put the LCS-AP protocol, the MME and the SMLC in the same step.

questions.question: When the UAE server registers a UAE client and later has to manage the UAS traffic on its behalf, which procedures put the UAE server, the UAS and the USS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure in TS 23.255 clause 7.1a.2.1.2; C2 communication modes configuration; and UAE-layer assisted dynamic C2 mode switching put the UAE server, the UAS and the USS in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the location management server, the SEAL layer and the UAE server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Communications between UAVs within a geographical area using unicast Uu; UAE-layer assisted dynamic C2 mode switching; and UAE server triggered change of USS put the location management server, the SEAL layer and the UAE server in the same step.

questions.question: For SIPTO, where the MME decides that a GW relocation is desirable and deactivates the PDN connection, which procedures put the Serving GW, the PDN connection and the SIPTO function in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: S4-SGSN triggered Serving GW relocation; UE or MME requested PDN disconnection; MME triggered Serving GW relocation; UE triggered Service Request; and Connection Resume procedure put the Serving GW, the PDN connection and the SIPTO function in the same step.

questions.question: In IAB inter-CU topological redundancy, where a second backhaul path is set up under a different donor-CU, which procedures put the BAP layer, the IAB node and the IAB-MT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Re-establishment procedure; IAB Inter-CU topological redundancy procedure; IAB inter-CU topology adaptation procedure with descendant IAB-node; Intra-CU topology adaptation procedure in SA; and Migration of mobile IAB-MT via Xn handover put the BAP layer, the IAB node and the IAB-MT in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put mobility management, the USS and UUAA in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: General (TS 23.256 clause 5.2.2.1); UUAA-MM Procedure; and USS initiated UAV Re-authorization procedure in 5GS put mobility management, the USS and UUAA in the same step.

questions.question: When an MC service server sets up a pre-created MBS session for group communication in transport-only mode, which procedures put the MBSF, the MC service server and the MB-SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedure for pre-created MBS session and MBS session announcement; Procedure for updating MBS resources without dynamic PCC rule; Procedure for updating MBS resources with dynamic PCC rule; Multicast MBS session activation procedure; and Multicast MBS session de-activation procedure put the MBSF, the MC service server and the MB-SMF in the same step.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MBMS bearer, the NRM server and the TMGI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MBMS bearer announcement over an MBMS bearer used for application control messages procedure (clause 14.3.4.4.2): step 4, where the NRM server sends an MBMS bearer announcement whose content contains the identity of the MBMS bearer (i.e. the TMGI).

questions.question: Which procedures put the W-AGF, the AMF and the fixed network RG in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures: FN-RG Registration via W-5GAN (clause 7.2.1.3), FN-RG Service Request procedure via W-5GAN Access (clause 7.2.2.2), and FN-RG related PDU Session Establishment via W-5GAN (clause 7.3.4) — each has a step where the W-AGF sends a message on behalf of the FN-RG to the AMF.

questions.question: When a residential gateway moves between CM-IDLE and CM-CONNECTED over wireline access, which procedures put the AMF, the connection management state and the RG in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures: 5G-RG Deregistration via W-5GAN (clause 7.2.1.2), 5G-RG Service Request procedure via W-5GAN Access (clause 7.2.2.1), and FN-RG Service Request procedure via W-5GAN Access (clause 7.2.2.2) — each contains a step describing the AMF's action based on whether the RG's CM state was CM-IDLE or CM-CONNECTED.

questions.question: When a PIN element reaches the PIN server through a PIN element with gateway capability, which procedures put the MAC address, the PEGC and the PIN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Service continuity in changing access to 5GS (clause 8.9.2.2), step 3: the PEGC 2 receives the related parameters, including PIN ID and MAC address/IP address, from PINE 2 or PEMC.

questions.question: Which procedures put NIDD, the SCEF and the SCS/AS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures: NIDD Configuration (clause 5.13.2), Mobile Terminated NIDD procedure (clause 5.13.3), Mobile Originated NIDD procedure (clause 5.13.4), and NIDD Authorisation Update (clause 5.13.8) — each contains a step where an NIDD-related message is exchanged directly between the SCS/AS and the SCEF.

questions.question: When a VAL server engages or disengages a slice-related communication service through the network slice capability enablement server, which procedures put the EGMF, the NSCE server and the VAL server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures on network slice fault management capability exposure (clause 9.15.2.1): at step 8, when the NSCE server detects the application/service error is caused by the 5GS, the VAL server sends the fault diagnosis report to the OAM system, using the fault management services exposed by EGMF as defined in TS 28.533.

questions.question: Which procedures put the network slice capability enablement server, the SLA and the VAL server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures: Predictive Inter-PLMN slice service continuity (clause 9.13.2) and Network slice diagnostics procedure (clause 9.14.2.1) — both list as a pre-condition that the enterprise hosting the VAL server has an SLA for slice services with the NSCE service provider.

questions.question: Which procedures put the 3GPP AAA server, the PDN GW and the VPLMN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures: UE-initiated PDN disconnection Procedure (clause 6.5.2), HSS/AAA-initiated Detach Procedure (clause 6.5.3), PDN GW-initiated PDN Disconnection Procedure in Trusted Non-3GPP Access (clause 6.5.4), and PDN GW-initiated PDN Disconnection Procedure in Untrusted Non-3GPP Access (clause 7.5.4) — each has a step stating that the PDN GW informs the 3GPP AAA Server of the PDN disconnection, and that if the PDN GW is in the VPLMN, signalling may be routed via a 3GPP AAA Proxy in the VPLMN.

questions.question: For an MCData one-to-one file distribution where the content is fetched from the media storage function, which procedures put file distribution, the MC service and the download URL in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures: Procedure for single MCData system (clause 7.5.2.4.2) and Procedure with interconnection between MCData systems (clause 7.5.2.4.3) — in each, step 2 has the MCData client sending an MCData FD (file distribution) request containing the content payload as a file URL to the MCData server.

questions.question: For TWAN authentication and authorization with single-connection mode and EPC-routed access, which procedures put the 3GPP AAA server, EAP and the TWAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures: TWAN Authentication and Authorization Procedure for SCM and EPC-routed access — successful call flow (Annex A.2.1), unsuccessful call flow (Annex A.2.2), and the call flow with IMEI check in VPLMN (Annex A.2.3) — each contains steps where the TWAN forwards the EAP payload to/from the 3GPP AAA Server.

questions.question: When a roaming UE registers and the AMF in the VPLMN has to report charging to both the home and visited CHF, which procedures put the AMF, the CDR and the VPLMN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Registration - PEC to HPLMN and AMF to H-CHF and V-CHF (clause 5.2.2.5.2): the AMF in the VPLMN sends Charging Data Request [Event] to the H-CHF (step 21ch-a, which creates the CDR at step 21ch-b) and then to the V-CHF (step 21ch-d, which creates the CDR at step 21ch-e) for the UE's successful registration.

questions.question: When the NAS security mode command establishes a NAS security context and the AMF later has to re-derive the key, which procedures put the AMF, the KAMF key and NAS signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: NAS security mode command procedure (clause 6.7.2), step 1b: the AMF sends the NAS Security Mode Command message, which contains the ngKSI identifying the KAMF and may include the K_AMF_change_flag to indicate a new KAMF is calculated. This is also reflected in the AMF/NAS synchronization rules (clause 6.9.5.1, rule 3): when the AMF has sent a NAS Security Mode Command to a UE to take a new KAMF into use, it must wait for NAS SMC completion before initiating a handover.

questions.question: When the LMF or the UE triggers a user-plane connection so positioning can run over LCS-UPP, which procedures put the AMF, the LCS function and the user plane in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures: LMF initiated User Plane Connection (clause 6.18.1) and UE initiated User Plane Connection (clause 6.18.2) — in each, a step near the end has the LMF indicating/responding to the AMF that the user plane connection between the UE and LMF has been established (step 7 in 6.18.1, step 9 in 6.18.2).

questions.question: For ProSe direct discovery where a UE announces or monitors over PC5 while roaming rules apply, which procedures put the HPLMN, the IMSI and the WLAN-based PC5 in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Announce request (roaming/inter-PLMN transmission) - open discovery (clause 5.3.3.3), step 1: the UE, if authorised to announce in the PLMN operating the signalled carrier frequency or intending to announce using WLAN-based PC5, establishes a secure connection with the ProSe Function in the HPLMN and sends a Discovery Request that includes the UE Identity (e.g. IMSI).

questions.question: When an IMS session changes its codec or media flow and needs new resources with policy control in use, which procedures put the CSCF, the PCF and the SDP offer in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Codec or media characteristics flow change requiring new resources and/or authorization (clause 5.11.3.3): a note after step 9 states that if the session modification request indicates no need for resource reservation or resources are already available, the P-CSCF can send updated session information to the PCRF/PCF whenever an SDP offer is contained in the session establishment request.

questions.question: For restricted ProSe discovery where the application server binds a PDUID to an RPAUID with a validity timer, which procedures put the HPLMN, the PDUID and the time-to-live in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures: Monitor Request (non-roaming) for restricted discovery (clause 5.3.3.4A) and Monitor Request (roaming) for restricted discovery (clause 5.3.3.5A). In step 10 of each, for each Target PDUID with a valid ProSe Restricted Code, the ProSe Function in the HPLMN allocates a Discovery Filter with the corresponding TTL (time-to-live).

questions.question: When a UE establishes PDN connectivity over a WLAN using a home agent and DSMIPv6, which procedures put the PDN GW, the home agent and the PDN connection in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PDN connection establishment over WLAN (clause 5.2.3), step 5: if the HA function is located in the PDN GW and dynamic PCC is deployed, the PDN GW performs an IP-CAN session establishment procedure with the PCRF as part of establishing the PDN connection.

questions.question: For network-requested secondary PDP context activation over the S4 interface, which procedures put GTP, the Serving GW and the PDN GW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Network Requested Secondary PDP Context Activation Procedure using S4 (clause 9.2.2.3A), step 1: the PDN GW sends a Create Bearer Request message (a GTP message) to the Serving GW to activate the secondary PDP context/bearer.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EPS bearer, the SGSN and the TEID in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures: Serving RNS Relocation Procedure, Combined Hard Handover and SRNS Relocation Procedure, and Combined Cell/URA Update and SRNS Relocation Procedure Using S4 (clause 6.9.2.2.1a); Network Requested Secondary PDP Context Activation Procedure using S4 (clause 9.2.2.3A); and S4-SGSN triggered Serving GW relocation (clause 9.2.2.4). Each has steps where the SGSN establishes or acknowledges EPS Bearer context(s) using TEIDs (e.g. sending/receiving Create Session Request/Response or Create Bearer Request/Response messages that include TEIDs).

questions.question: For local call local switch in the CS core where the BSS holds a global call reference, which procedures put the BSS, the GCR and LCLS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures: Basic Sequence for accepting an incoming call while original call is held (clause 13.5.2.2.2), where step 14 has BSS-A updating the GCR and the LCLS-Configuration on receipt of the ASSIGNMENT REQUEST message; Retrieval of held call after ongoing call has completed (clause 13.6.5.2), where step 4 has the MSC-A server sending the ASSIGNMENT REQUEST message to BSS-A including the LCLS-Configuration IE and the GCR IE; and Basic Intra-MSC UMTS to GSM Handover establishing Local Switching (clause 8.2.2.1.5), where step 4 has the Target BSS performing call leg correlation with the GCR and reporting that LCLS is not yet established.

questions.question: When a GCS AS asks the BM-SC to allocate or renew TMGIs over the MB2-C interface, which procedures put the BM-SC, the Diameter GAR command and the GCS AS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TMGI Allocation Procedure (Annex A.1.1): in step 1, when the GCS AS needs to request the BM-SC to allocate or renew one or more TMGIs, the GCS AS sends a Diameter GAR command including the defined parameters.

questions.question: When an MCPTT user calls an LMR user through an interworking function, which procedures put the LMR system, the MC service and MCPTT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MCPTT user initiating a first-to-answer call to communicate with an LMR user via an IWF (clause 10.15.3.1): step 6 has the MCPTT client establishing the media plane for communication to the IWF, noting that the MCPTT system initiating the call is responsible for granting the floor — this is the procedure where an MCPTT user calls an LMR user through the interworking function.

questions.question: When the GANC and the MS negotiate IP address and UDP ports for GA-PSR transport channels, which procedures put the GANC, generic access and the transport channel in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MS initiated Activation of GA-PSR Transport Channel (clause 8.16.1): steps 1-2 describe the GANC and MS dynamically negotiating the IP address and UDP port numbers to be used for the GA-PSR Transport Channel — the MS sends its UDP port to the GANC, and the GANC replies with the IP address and UDP port to be used for uplink data transfer.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CSG, the Serving GW and the TEID in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MME triggered Serving GW relocation (clause 5.10.4), step 2: the MME sends a Create Session Request, including bearer contexts with PDN GW addresses and TEIDs, to the new Serving GW, and includes the User CSG Information IE in this message if the User CSG Information has changed.

questions.question: When the PCRF terminates or modifies a TDF session for a roaming UE, which procedures put the Diameter AVP, the CCR command and the TDF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TDF Session termination (clause 4.6.2), step 4: the TDF sends a CCR command to the PCRF indicating TDF session termination, requesting termination of the Sd session by setting the CC-Request-Type Diameter AVP to TERMINATION_REQUEST.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PCRF, the RCAF and the RUCI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Several procedures: Report RAN user plane congestion information to PCRF (clause 7.10.1), PCRF provided reporting restrictions (clause 7.10.2), Non-aggregated RUCI report procedure (TS 29.213 clause 4.8.2.1), Aggregated RUCI report procedure (clause 4.8.2.2), and UE mobility between RCAFs (clause 4.8.4). In each, the RCAF sends a message (RUCI report / Diameter NR-Request / AR-Request / NRR command) to the PCRF conveying the RUCI (RAN User plane Congestion Information).

questions.question: When an MC service server sets up an MBS session and the policy control has to be arranged for it, which procedures put the MBS session, the MBSF and the PCC rule in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MBS session deletion procedure (clause 7.3.3.3.2), step 5: the MC service server initiates the MBS session deletion procedure with the 5GC (either directly or through NEF/MBSF), and this deletion procedure can be performed either with or without a dynamic PCC rule.

questions.question: When the NRM server checks TSC stream availability and configures DS-TT traffic classes for time-sensitive communication, which procedures put the DS-TT, the NRM server and the time-sensitive translator in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TSC stream availability discovery procedure (clause 14.3.7.2), step 2: the NRM server validates the connectivity between the DS-TTs (device-side TSN translators) connected in the same 5GS TSC bridge and identifies the traffic classes supported by the DS-TTs.

questions.question: When ISR is activated, which procedures put the MME and the SGSN in the same step for a detach?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: UE-initiated Detach procedure for E-UTRAN (clause 5.3.8.2.1), where with ISR activated the MME sends a Detach Indication to the associated SGSN; MME-initiated Detach procedure (clause 5.3.8.3), where the MME sends a Detach Notification to the SGSN; and SGSN-initiated Detach procedure with ISR activated (clause 5.3.8.3A), where the SGSN sends a Detach Notification to the MME.

questions.question: For exposing UE reachability, location or service-authorization information to an application, which procedures put the AF, the AMF and the NEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are the solution procedures for localized-service authorization when the UE's home network is unaware of the hosting network (clause 6.42.3), for determining a UE's unavailability period in 5GS (clause 6.4.3), and for 5GS assistance to federated learning operation (clause 6.44.2) — in each, the AMF and the NEF exchange event or authorization information that is ultimately provided to or received from the AF.

questions.question: For distributing 5G VN group subscription data updates, which procedures involve the AMF, the SMF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are the solution procedures for enhanced group attribute management (clause 6.1.3) and for multi-SMF support in 5G VN group communication (clause 6.19.3), both in TS 23.700-74, where the UDM provides group subscription data to the AMF or the SMF via Nudm_SDM_Notification/Nudm_SDM_Get; and the UE/group subscription-data update solution in TS 23.700-80 (clause 6.36.2), where the UDM notifies the subscribed AMF or SMF via a UDM Notify message.

questions.question: For exposing UE location or event information to an external party, which procedures put the AMF, the NEF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are the Unified Location Service Exposure procedure with routing via a UDM (clause 6.5.2 of TS 23.273), where the UDM invokes Namf_EventExposure_Subscribe towards the AMF and includes a URI for the NEF, and the solution procedure for enhanced 5G VN group status event reporting (clause 6.11.3 of TS 23.700-74), where the AMF reports a subscribed event to the NEF either directly or via the UDM.

questions.question: For delivering a UE's location estimate after a mobile-terminated location request, which procedures put the AF, the GMLC and the LCS client in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are the MT-LR procedure (clause 6.13.1 of TS 23.273), where the 5GC GMLC decides whether to forward the location information to the LCS client or the AF, and the solution procedure for locating a UE out of coverage (clause 6.21.3 of TS 23.700-86), where the GMLC provides the LCS location estimate to the AF or LCS client.

questions.question: For discovering and requesting analytics from a management data analytics function, which procedures involve the MDA, the MDAF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are the Procedure for analytics collection from MDAF (clause 6.2.14.2 of TS 23.288), where the NWDAF selects the most suitable MDAF and sends an MDARequest to the MDA Management Function, and the solution procedure reusing the MDA functional framework (clause 6.74.2 of TS 23.700-81), where the recipient NWDAF discovers the corresponding MDAF or MDA MnS producer.

questions.question: For updating MBS session resources at the 5GC, which procedures put the MBS, the NEF and the NRM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are the Procedure for updating MBS resources without dynamic PCC rule (clause 14.3.4A.3.2) and the Procedure for updating MBS resources with dynamic PCC rule (clause 14.3.4A.3.3), both in TS 23.434, where the NRM server sends an MBS session update request towards the 5GC either directly or indirectly via the NEF.

questions.question: For network-slice-related SMF selection and reselection during registration, which procedures put the AMF, the NSSAI and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures, all in TS 23.700-41, are: clause 6.4.3, where the AMF selects an SMF based on a compatible S-NSSAI when the requested one is overloaded; clause 6.5.3, where the PDU Session switches to the alternative S-NSSAI at the target AMF via SMF-involved PDU Session modification; clause 6.8.3, where the AMF performs S-NSSAI-related subscription-data actions for the PDU Session tied to the SMF; and clause 6.37.3, where the serving AMF checks the S-NSSAI inactivity timer against sessions anchored at the SMF.

questions.question: For managing S-NSSAI-related subscription data and inactivity, which procedures involve the AMF, the NSSAI and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures, all in TS 23.700-41, are: clause 6.8.3, where the UDM notifies the AMF of Access and Mobility Subscription data changes via Nudm_SDM_Notification for an affected S-NSSAI; clause 6.18.2, where the AMF sends allowed/rejected NSSAI assistance information to the UDM via Nudm_UECM_Update; clause 6.36.3, where the AMF retrieves the Subscribed S-NSSAIs from the UDM during UE subscription data retrieval; and clause 6.37.3, where the serving AMF obtains the S-NSSAI inactivity timer from the UDM.

questions.question: For handling an MBS multicast session across NG-RAN mobility and paging, which procedures put the AMF, the MBS session and NG-RAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.247, are: clause 7.2.3.3, the N2 based handover from an MBS supporting NG-RAN node, where the source NG-RAN sends a Handover Required message to the AMF carrying MBS Session information; and clause 7.2.6, the Multicast session update procedure, where the NG-RAN acknowledges an N2 MBS session request to the AMF.

questions.question: For MBS session activation, release and mobility handling, which procedures involve the AMF, the MBS session and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the Multicast session update procedure (clause 7.2.6 of TS 23.247), where the SMF updates its AMF subscription for the MBS Service Area of Interest; the N2 based Handover and IDLE Mobility solution procedure (clause 6.17.3.6 of TS 23.700-47), where the SMF includes UE join information to the target AMF and the AMF maintains the MBS session's joined UE list; and the Solution procedure of clause 6.18.3 of TS 23.700-47, where the SMF invokes Namf_MT_EnableGroupReachability towards the AMF based on the MBS session activation/release event.

questions.question: For configuring or managing Detect-and-Avoid support for a UAV, which procedures put the DAA function, the UAE and the UAS application server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the DAA support configuration procedure of TS 23.255 (clause 7.7.2.1.2), where the UAE server sends a DAA support configuration request to the UAE client based on a UAS application specific server request; the DAA support management procedure of TS 23.700-55 (clause 7.6.2.3.1), where the UAS application specific server sends a DAA support management request/response to the UAE server; and the DAA support configuration procedure of TS 23.700-55 (clause 7.6.2.3.2), where the UAE server configures the UAE client with DAA parameters from the UAS application specific server.

questions.question: For registering, deregistering or redirecting a Personal Network Element, which procedures put the S-CSCF, the PNE and the PNM AS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.259, are: the PN-registration procedure for a PNE other than a PN UE (clause 5.1.4), where the S-CSCF sends a Notify flow to the PNM AS with the PNE identifier and capabilities; the PN-deregistration procedure for a PNE other than a PN UE (clause 5.2.4), where the PNM AS sends the register status of the PNE back to the S-CSCF; and the procedures for PNE redirection in the IM CN subsystem (clause 6.1.3), where the PNM AS redirects an initial request naming a PNE to the S-CSCF.

questions.question: For PN registration, deregistration or UE redirection within a Personal Network, which procedures put the S-CSCF, PN and the PNM AS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.259, are: the PN-deregistration procedure in the IM CN subsystem (clause 5.2.2), where the PNM AS verifies the PN-registration against identities received from the S-CSCF; the procedures for PN UE redirection in the IM CN subsystem (clause 6.1.2), where the PNM AS redirects an initial request from the S-CSCF to the default UE of the PN; and the procedures for PN UE redirection from the IM CN subsystem to the CS domain (clause 6.3.2), where the PNM AS sends the redirected request to the S-CSCF.

questions.question: For interworking location requests between an MC system and an LMR system, which procedures put the LMR system, the LMS and the MC system in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.283, are the LMS-to-IWF procedures for on-demand location request (clause 10.11.4.2.1.1), location information subscription (clause 10.11.4.2.3.1), and location information cancel subscription (clause 10.11.4.2.4.1) — in each, the LMS in the MC system determines that the request has a target user in the LMR system.

questions.question: For releasing EPS bearer resources during a rejected handover with Serving GW relocation, which procedures put the EPS bearer context, the Serving GW and the MME in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.401, are the reject cases of S1-based handover (clause 5.5.1.2.3), UTRAN Iu mode to E-UTRAN inter-RAT handover (clause 5.5.2.2.4), and GERAN A/Gb mode to E-UTRAN inter-RAT handover (clause 5.5.2.4.4) — in each, the Target MME deletes the EPS bearer resources by sending a Delete Session Request to the Target Serving GW.

questions.question: For suspending or resuming a UE connection in CM-IDLE with Suspend, which procedures put the AMF, CM-IDLE and NG-RAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the Connection Suspend procedure (clause 4.8.1.2 of TS 23.502), where the NG-RAN sends an N2 Suspend Request and the AMF enters CM-IDLE with Suspend; the Connection Resume in CM-IDLE with Suspend and MO EDT procedure (clause 4.8.2.4 of TS 23.502), where the AMF may keep the UE in CM-IDLE with Suspend when responding to NG-eNB; and the solution procedure of clause 6.3.2 of TS 23.700-68, where the AMF sends Inactive Assistance Information to the NG-RAN for a UE in CM-IDLE.

questions.question: For modifying or transferring an SM context across a resume or handover, which procedures put SM context information, the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the Connection Resume in CM-IDLE with Suspend procedure (clause 4.8.2.3 of TS 23.502), where the SMF sends an N4 Session Modification Request to the UPF while N2 SM information is exchanged with the AMF; the SMF Context Transfer procedure (clause 4.26.5.3 of TS 23.502), where the Old SMF returns the SM Context to the New SMF; and the Procedure for subscribing information (clause 6.5.3.1 of TS 23.700-60), where N2 SM information is forwarded to the SMF, which subsequently updates the N4 session with the UPF.

questions.question: For modifying user-plane tunnel and QoS information at a Target NG-RAN, which procedures put NG-RAN, the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the Xn based inter-NG-RAN handover without UPF re-allocation (clause 4.9.1.2.2 of TS 23.502), where the SMF sends an N4 Session Modification Request to the UPF for sessions modified by the Target NG-RAN; the Handover from 5GS to EPC/ePDG procedure (clause 4.11.4.2 of TS 23.502), whose initial status has PDU Sessions established between the UE and the SMF/UPF via NG-RAN; and the solution procedure of clause 6.16.3 of TS 23.700-25, where the SMF sets a dynamic CN PDB based on the UPF and NG-RAN of the PDU Session.

questions.question: For creating or updating PCC rules based on an AF request, which procedures put the AF, PCC rules and the PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures are clause 6.23.2 of TS 23.700-17, clause 6.74.3 of TS 23.700-60, and clause 6.18.2 of TS 23.700-88 — in each, the PCF creates or updates PCC rules based on the AF's request, in the first and third case additionally accounting for the Default non-3GPP delay budget from the UDR.

questions.question: For satellite-backhaul monitoring and non-3GPP access switching involving user-plane resources, which procedures put the AMF, the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures are: clause 6.9.2 of TS 23.700-27, where the SMF informs the AMF about satellite backhaul monitoring capability on the UPF side; clause 6.8.3 of TS 23.700-53, where the AMF notifies the SMF of non-3GPP access switching and the SMF establishes user-plane resources involving the UPF; and clause 6.1.3.2 of TS 23.700-68, the Network triggered Connection Resume procedure, where the SMF/UPF checks with the AMF on data-delivery possibility.

questions.question: For propagating parameter or policy updates between subscription storage and policy control, which procedures put the NEF, the PCF and the UDR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures are: clause 6.21.2 of TS 23.700-33, where a ProSe Application parameter update flows from the NEF into the UDR and the PCF receives the resulting notification; clause 6.57.3 of TS 23.700-60, where the NEF retrieves marking-mechanism configuration from the UDR and forwards it to the PCF; and the Procedure for UDR collects UE unavailable period (clause 6.5.3.3 of TS 23.700-61), where the NEF sends the UE unavailable period to the UDR for later provisioning to the PCF.

questions.question: For migrating MC users or their configuration between primary and partner MC systems, which procedures put the ACMC, the ACMS and the MC system in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures, all in TS 23.700-38, are: clause 7.7.1.3, where the primary ACMC requests the primary ACMS to authorize a list of MC users to migrate to the partner MC System; clause 7.9.1.3, where the primary ACMC sends the primary ACMS an update to the MC service UE initial configuration; and clause 7.10.1.3, where the primary ACMC sends the primary ACMS an MC service user profile update request for a migrating user.

questions.question: For establishing an Access and Mobility policy association during registration, which procedures put the AM policy, the AMF and the PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the Registration solution procedure of clause 6.2.3.2 of TS 23.700-41, where the AMF may request the PCF to obtain AM policy; and the solution procedures of clauses 6.2.2 and 6.6.2 of TS 23.700-89, where the AMF establishes an AM Policy association with the PCF as part of registration.

questions.question: For assigning or restricting a Registration Area based on supported network slices, which procedures put the AMF, NSSAI and the RA in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures, all in TS 23.700-41, are: clause 6.23.3, where the AMF may assign the UE an RA that does not support all of the requested S-NSSAIs; clause 6.26.3, where the AMF provides a Registration Accept with a Secondary Allowed NSSAI and its associated Secondary RA; and clause 6.29.3.2.1, where the AMF forms an RA spanning two TAIs to satisfy support for a second S-NSSAI.

questions.question: For exposing UPF-detected data-rate or interruption events, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures, both in TS 23.700-60, are: clause 6.5.3.2, the Procedure for notify of information via user plane, where the UPF sends a Nupf_EventExposure_Notify to the AF directly (when trusted) or to the NEF for onward delivery to the AF; and clause 6.30.3.1, the Procedure for network exposure of network latency or jitter to AF, where the UPF sends its QoS monitoring notification to a Notification Target Address that is either the AF or the NEF.

questions.question: For requesting an AF session with RT latency requirements, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and the RT latency requirement in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures, all in TS 23.700-60, are clauses 6.27.3, 6.28.3 and 6.71.3, in each of which the AF provides an RT latency requirement to the NEF via the Nnef_AFsessionWithQoS_Create request.

questions.question: For obtaining a Ranging/sidelink positioning result, which procedures put the AMF, the LMF and SL positioning in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant solution procedures, all in TS 23.700-86, are: clause 6.22.3, where the LMF sends the Ranging/SL positioning Response to the AMF; clause 6.31.3.1, the deferred MT-LR procedure, where the LMF determines the target UE's location from the SL positioning result and sends it to the AMF; and clause 6.33.3, the common Ranging/sidelink positioning exposure procedure, where the AMF involves the LMF once no SL Positioning Server UE is available.

questions.question: For sending standalone SDS data in IOPS mode, which procedures put IOPS, the MC system and SDS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.180, are the IOPS one-to-one standalone SDS procedure over signalling control plane (clause 10.6.1.3.2) and the IOPS group standalone SDS procedure over signalling control plane (clause 10.6.1.4.2), where an MCData user sends an IOPS standalone SDS data request within the MC system's IOPS mode of operation.

questions.question: For distributing group data or notifying MC users about IOPS coverage, which procedures put IOPS, MBMS and the MC system in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.180, are: the IOPS group standalone SDS procedure (clause 10.6.1.4.2), whose preconditions include an MBMS bearer established and announced by the IOPS MC connectivity function; and the MC IOPS notification procedure (clause 10.7.3), where the notification to nearby MC service users can itself be sent on an MBMS bearer configured within the IOPS MC system's coverage.

questions.question: For deactivating a PDN connection with a split control- and user-plane architecture, which procedures put the CP function, the PDN connection and the UP function in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.214, are clause 6.3.4.1.1 (procedures with SGSN terminating the S4 interface) and clause 6.3.4.1.2 (procedures with SGSN terminating the Gn/Gp interface) — each clause defines the interactions between the CP and UP function during the procedures related to PDN connection deactivation.

questions.question: For establishing or modifying an Sx session during SGSN-served PDN procedures, which procedures put the PGW, the SGSN and the SGW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.214, are clause 6.3.4.2.1 (procedures with SGSN terminating the S4 interface, covering location management, handover and service request procedures) and clause 6.3.4.3 (procedures with PDN connection establishment) — both describe how the SGW-C/SGW-U and PGW-C/PGW-U establish or modify their Sx sessions during S4-SGSN-served PDN procedures.

questions.question: For SRVCC of an IMS emergency session via an Enhanced STN-SR, which procedures put the MSC Server, session transfer and the STN-SR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both alternative forking-based flows in TS 23.237, are clause 6c.2.3.1 (active session case) and clause 6c.2.4.1 (early dialogue phase case), where the MSC Server initiates the session transfer with the E-STN-SR, including the equipment identifier.

questions.question: For obtaining or reusing a CAA-Level UAV identity after UUAA, which procedures put CAA, the UAV and UUAA in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the USS initiated UAV Re-authorization procedure in EPS (clause 5.2.4.4 of TS 23.256), where the UE receives a Service Level Device Identity (e.g. CAA-Level UAV ID) together with a UUAA Authorization Payload; and the solution procedure of clause 6.4.3 of TS 23.700-58, where the UAV performs the UUAA procedure and may obtain a new CAA-Level UAV ID as a result.

questions.question: For collecting service-flow or dispersion analytics data from the user plane, which procedures involve the AF, the NWDAF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the Dispersion Analytic Procedure (clause 6.10.4 of TS 23.288), where the NWDAF subscribes to application service data from the AF and collects data-volume information from the UPF; and the solution procedure of clause 6.8.2 of TS 23.700-81, where a change of user-plane traffic information reported by the UPF or the AF is notified to the NWDAF.

questions.question: For updating or revoking a ProSe discovery entry across PLMNs, which procedures put the HPLMN, the TTL and the VPLMN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.303, are the network-initiated discovery update procedure (clause 5.3.6A.1.2) and the UE-initiated discovery update procedures (clause 5.3.6A.1.3) — in each, the HPLMN ProSe Function informs the ProSe Function in the VPLMN (or other PLMN) of an Announce/Monitor Update, with the TTL of the Discovery Filter set to zero when the entry is revoked.

questions.question: For a 5G-RG or AUN3 device to register to 5GC over wireline access, which procedures put the AMF, NAS and the RG in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the 5G-RG Registration via W-5GAN procedure (clause 7.2.1.1 of TS 23.316), where NAS messages, including the NAS Security Mode Complete, are exchanged between the 5G-RG and the AMF; and the solution procedure of clause 6.25.2 of TS 23.700-17, where the 5G-RG sends a NAS Registration Request to the AMF on behalf of an AUN3 device.

questions.question: For reporting Secondary RAT usage data during connection suspend or handover, which procedures put the Serving GW, the MME and the RAT usage data in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.401, are: the Connection Suspend procedure (clause 5.3.4A), where the MME sends a Release Access Bearers Request carrying Secondary RAT usage data to the Serving GW; and the X2-based handover without Serving GW relocation (clause 5.5.1.1.2), where the MME buffers Secondary RAT usage data received from the source eNodeB before forwarding it to the Serving GW.

questions.question: For acknowledging session deletion with APN Rate Control status during detach, which procedures put the APN, the PDN GW and rate-control status in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.401, are the UE-initiated Detach procedure for E-UTRAN (clause 5.3.8.2.1) and the MME-initiated Detach procedure (clause 5.3.8.3) — in each, the PDN GW acknowledges the Delete Session Request with a Delete Session Response that optionally carries the APN Rate Control Status.

questions.question: For relaying APN Rate Control status between core-network nodes during detach, which procedures put the APN, the MME and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.401, are the UE-initiated Detach procedure for E-UTRAN (clause 5.3.8.2.1) and the MME-initiated Detach procedure (clause 5.3.8.3) — in each, the SGSN sends a Detach Acknowledge message to the MME carrying the APN Rate Control Status, which the MME stores in the MM context.

questions.question: For relaying a Detach Accept or routing a NAS request between MME and SGSN, which procedures put the MME, a NAS message and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.401, are: the HSS-initiated Detach procedure (clause 5.3.8.4), where the eNodeB forwards the UE's Detach Accept as a NAS message to the MME/SGSN; and the Attach, TAU and RAU procedure for Dedicated Core Network (clause 5.19.2), where the RAN node selects a serving MME/SGSN for the NAS Request message based on the DCN-ID.

questions.question: For coordinating dedicated bearer activation with the Serving GW and PDN GW, which procedures put the Serving GW, the MME and the PDN GW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the combined Dedicated bearer activation with default bearer activation at Attach/UE-requested PDN connectivity (Annex F of TS 23.401), where the PDN GW initiates dedicated bearer activation and the MME combines the resulting Create Bearer Request with the Attach/PDN Connectivity Accept; and the Handover Phase (clause 9.3.2 of TS 23.402), where the MME releases EPS bearer resources at the Serving GW while instructing it not to trigger deletion towards the PDN GW.

questions.question: For updating subscription or authorization data at the PDN GW via the 3GPP AAA Server, which procedures put the AAA server, the Serving/PDN GW and the PDN connection in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.402, are: the HSS-initiated User Profile Update Procedure (clause 12.2.1), where the 3GPP AAA Server updates the PDN GW with new authorisation, service-authorisation and subscribed QoS data; and the DSMIPv6-to-PMIPv6 non-roaming handover (Annex C.4), where EAP authentication involving the 3GPP AAA Server conveys the selected PDN GW's address.

questions.question: For reporting or switching based on MBMS bearer quality for a VAL application, which procedures put MBMS, the NRM client/server and the VAL UE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.434, are: clause 14.3.4.5.2, MBMS bearer quality detection, where the NRM client determines and reports MBMS bearer quality that the VAL UE helps estimate; and clause 14.3.4.9.2, switching between MBMS delivery and unicast delivery, where the NRM client notifies the NRM server of the MBMS bearer condition detected by the VAL UE.

questions.question: For coordinating network slice resource optimization or adaptation for a VAL application, which procedures put the NSCE server, OAM and the VAL server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.435, are: the procedure on multiple slices coordinated resource optimization (clause 9.10.2.1), where the VAL server's request to the NSCE server leads the NSCE server to retrieve network slice status from 5GC or OAM; and the VAL server-triggered network slice adaptation procedure (clause 9.11.2.3), where the NSCE server likewise interacts with the 5GC and OAM following the VAL server's subscribe request.

questions.question: For subscribing to network slice adaptation with an optional DNN, which procedures put the DNN, the NSCE server and the VAL application in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.435, are: the VAL server-triggered network slice adaptation procedure (clause 9.11.2.3), where the VAL server sends the NSCE server a subscribe request optionally naming the DNN for the VAL application; and the VAL UE-triggered network slice adaptation procedure (clause 9.11.2.4), where the NSCE client sends the NSCE server a trigger subscribe request that may likewise include the DNN.

questions.question: For marking guidance exchanged between an application function and the network, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and RTP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both procedures are the 'Setting up an AF session with required QoS' variants in TS 23.700-60 clauses 6.54.3 and 6.57.3, where the AF sends the NEF guidance about RTP header/payload priority information or the acceptable RTP-based marking mechanisms.

questions.question: When an AF session needs to be set up with per-flow QoS coordination across a group, which procedures involve the AF, GPSI and the NEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The two procedures are 'Enhanced interaction between AF and 5GS for QoS policy coordination among multiple QoS flows' (TS 23.700-60 clause 6.65.3.1), where the AF sends the NEF an AF-session-with-QoS request whose UE identifier may be a GPSI, and the exposure procedure in TS 23.700-62 clause 6.18.3, where the AF's Nnef_EventExposure_Subscribe request to the NEF carries the GPSI.

questions.question: For a network-assisted UE location request that also needs to reach a location client, which procedures put the AMF, the GMLC and the LMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The two procedures are the Network Assisted Positioning Procedure in TS 23.700-71 clause 6.4.3.1, where the AMF invokes Nlmf_Location_DetermineLocation on the LMF with a GMLC notification address, and TS 23.700-86 clause 6.8.3, where the GMLC sends the location request to the LMF via the AMF.

questions.question: When location measurement data is collected as input for network data analytics, which procedures put the GMLC, the LMF and NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant clauses are the 'Location Accuracy Sustainability' analytics data-collection procedure in TS 23.700-71 clause 6.12.2, where a location request from a location client is received via the GMLC and the LMF reports measurements to the NWDAF, and the 'QoS Sustainability' analytics procedure in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.50.2, where the GMLC/LMF provides UE location information to the NWDAF.

questions.question: For registering and positioning a Pedestrian/Personal Reference UE via its serving access, which procedures put the AMF, the LMF and a PRU in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both are PRU procedures in TS 23.700-71 clause 6.28.3: the Registration Procedure (6.28.3.1), where the PRU sends its Registration Request to the LMF via the serving AMF, and the Positioning Procedure for a PRU (6.28.3.3), where the LMF accesses the PRU through the serving AMF.

questions.question: For PIN client interactions that reference a resource by address, which procedures put a PIN, a PINE and a URL in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The two clauses are the Procedures of PIN Service Switch (TS 23.700-78 clause 7.9.2.2.2), where the PIN server sends a Switch Application Session request naming destination PINE PE IDs including a URL, and the Procedures of PIN Application Server Discovery (clause 7.12.2.2.2), where the PIN server responds to a PINE's Application Client with an AS URL.

questions.question: For enhanced QoS-flow coordination combined with request exposure, which procedures put the AF, NWDAF and the PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both procedures are in TS 23.700-80: clause 6.19.2, where the NWDAF sends the PCF an Npcf_EventExposure request with the Application ID from an AF-initiated request, and clause 6.26.2, where the PCF checks an AF request and may interact with the NWDAF for network performance analytics.

questions.question: For federated-learning member selection assisted by network exposure, which procedures put the AF, FL and the NEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The two clauses are in TS 23.700-80: clause 6.19.2, where the NEF sends the AF a UE identity list via Nnef_AnalyticsExposure_Notify so the AF can determine FL members, and clause 6.40.2.2, where the AFLSF's FL configuration recommendation is notified to the AF via the NEF.

questions.question: For exposing UE authorization status or subscription data toward an application function, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-80: 6.33.2.1, 'Procedure for 5GC Exposure of Network Authorization Status of UE for Application AI/ML operation', where the UDM sends an Nudm_EventExposure_Notify to the NEF (or directly to the AF), and 6.43.2.1, 'Procedure for AF directly collection information for FL member selection', where the AF retrieves consent data from the UDM via the NEF.

questions.question: For deriving AI/ML traffic-related analytics and sharing a trained model, which procedures put AI, ML and NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The two clauses are TS 23.700-80 clause 6.34.2, where the NWDAF derives analytics for Application AI/ML traffic transmission, and TS 23.700-81 clause 6.14.1.2, 'Registration and discovery of NWDAF (containing MTLF) with ML model Format Information', where an NWDAF (MTLF) notifies an NWDAF (AnLF) of its AI-framework ML model information.

questions.question: For monitoring the accuracy of analytics derived from a trained model, which procedures put the ADRF, ML and NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-81: 6.5.2.1, 'Procedures for AnLF based error monitoring', where the NWDAF containing AnLF requests the ADRF to store ML-model-related events and data, and 6.5.2.2, 'Procedures for MTLF based error monitoring', where the NWDAF containing AnLF provides ADRF information while subscribing to a trained ML model.

questions.question: For registering and discovering a model-training function's ML model in the NRF, which procedures put ML, the MTLF and the NRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both are TS 23.700-81 clauses: 6.15.2, 'Procedure for sharing of ML model', where the MTLF registers its NF profile including ML-model support information in the NRF, and 6.23.2, 'Support of model training using federated learning', where the AnLF discovers the (central) MTLF from the NRF.

questions.question: For roaming NWDAF data collection between home and visited networks, which procedures put the DCCF, HPLMN and VPLMN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-81: 6.39.2.1, 'Procedure for NWDAF in HPLMN to collect data from VPLMN', where the HPLMN DCCF subscribes to data collection from the VPLMN DCCF, and 6.39.2.2, 'Procedure for NWDAF consumer in HPLMN to obtain analytics from VPLMN NWDAF', where the VPLMN DCCF sends analytics or data toward the HPLMN.

questions.question: For roaming analytics collection where a home-network data-collection function forwards results to the analytics function, which procedures put the DCCF, HPLMN and NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-81: 6.39.2.1, 'Procedure for NWDAF in HPLMN to collect data from VPLMN', where the HPLMN DCCF sends the collected data to the HPLMN NWDAF, and 6.39.2.2, 'Procedure for NWDAF consumer in HPLMN to obtain analytics from VPLMN NWDAF', where the HPLMN DCCF sends the analytics result to the HPLMN NWDAF consumer.

questions.question: For deriving roaming analytics on visited-network data at the home NWDAF, which procedures put the HPLMN, NWDAF and VPLMN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-81: 6.39.2.1, 'Procedure for NWDAF in HPLMN to collect data from VPLMN', where the HPLMN NWDAF derives requested analytics from data collected in the VPLMN, and 6.39.2.2, 'Procedure for NWDAF consumer in HPLMN to obtain analytics from VPLMN NWDAF', where the VPLMN NWDAF collects data and derives analytics for the roaming UE(s) on behalf of the HPLMN.

questions.question: For PDU session establishment steered by a URSP rule, which procedures put the DNN, NSSAI and URSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-85: 6.9.2, where the UE requests PDU session establishment with a specific S-NSSAI and DNN chosen via a URSP rule, and 6.15.2, where the UE selects the S-NSSAI and DNN for the PDU Session Establishment Request based on applicable URSP rules.

questions.question: For carrying URSP rule information inside session-management signalling, which procedures put NAS, SM and URSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-85: 6.12.2, where the URSP rule ID that triggered the PDU Session Establishment/Modification procedure is carried in the UE's SM NAS request message, and 6.13.2, where the UE includes the URSP Rule Precedence and application identity in the SM NAS request message.

questions.question: For validating a UE's compliance with URSP rules during session policy control, which procedures put the PCF, SMF and URSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-85: 6.12.2, where the SMF sends the PCF an Npcf_SMPolicyControl_Create/Update request carrying the UE's URSP rule ID, and 6.15.2, where the PCF's URSP validity check result is returned to the SMF in the Npcf_SMPolicyControl_Create response.

questions.question: For obtaining a location-service capability and delivering a location estimate, which procedures put the GMLC, LCS and the LMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-86: 6.8.3, where the LMF obtains LCS capability and location information and the internal Application ID it uses was provided by the GMLC, and 6.21.3, where the LMF provides the LCS location estimation of the UE to the GMLC.

questions.question: For a mobile-terminated location request that supports sidelink positioning of several UEs, which procedures put the LMF, LR and MT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses are in TS 23.700-86: 6.19.3.3, 'MT-LR Procedure for Sidelink Positioning/Ranging with LMF Assistance', where the LMF sends an MT-LR request to the principal target UE, and 6.19.3.4, 'Periodic or Triggered MT-LR Procedure for Sidelink Positioning/Ranging with LMF Assistance', where the LMF instigates the periodic/triggered MT-LR sidelink positioning.
