questions.question: For application-layer signalling exchanged through a PIN gateway, which procedures put the AF, PEGC and a PINE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both clauses in TS 23.700-88 clauses 6.11.2 and 6.18.2 describe application-layer signalling exchanged between an application on a PINE connected to the PEGC and an application function (AF).

questions.question: For monitoring event reporting and configuration between the serving node and the core, which procedures put the HSS, the MME, the SCEF and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: Reporting Procedure (clause 5.6.3.1), Configuration Procedure (clause 5.6.6.1), and Reporting Procedure for roaming scenarios (clause 5.6.8.1) — all in TS 23.682, covering monitoring events configured at or detected by the MME/SGSN or the HSS and reported to the SCEF.

questions.question: For creating and provisioning group membership data in the 5G core, which procedures involve the AF, the NEF, the UDM and the UDR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: creation of a group and using it for selecting the local part of DN (TS 23.700-48, clause 6.14.3), AF creating and provisioning Group ID profiles to 5GC (TS 23.700-74, clause 6.13.3), and the procedure for support of SMF service area (TS 23.700-74, clause 6.18.3) — in all of them the AF sends group/area information to the NEF, which authorizes it and stores or updates it via the UDM/UDR.

questions.question: For exposing QoS-related delay information to an application, which procedures put the AF, the NEF, the PCF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.700-60, are: the round-trip delay exposure procedure (clause 6.42.3), the high-level procedure for delay status information subscription and notification (clause 6.47.3), and the procedure for reserving resources for an AF session with required QoS for multi-modal (XRM) applications (clause 6.62.3). In each, the AF requests QoS monitoring or resource reservation via the NEF, which invokes the PCF, and the PCF in turn coordinates with the SMF.

questions.question: For obtaining a UE's location for analytics purposes, which procedures involve the AMF, the GMLC, the LMF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the Location Measurement Accuracy data collection procedure (TS 23.700-71, clause 6.12.2), where the NWDAF requests location measurement accuracy data from the GMLC or the LMF; and the QoS Sustainability analytics procedure (TS 23.700-81, clause 6.50.2), where the NWDAF obtains a UE list from the AMF and then initiates an LCS Service Request to the GMLC/LMF for the location of those UEs.

questions.question: For subscribing to and exposing analytics results, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the UE mobility analytics procedure provided to an Analytics Service Consumer (TS 23.288, clause 6.7.2.4), the Movement Behaviour analytics procedure (TS 23.288, clause 6.21.4), and four procedures in TS 23.700-80 related to AI/ML/Federated Learning assistance: the 5G-assisted FL member selection procedure (clause 6.19.2), the 5GC information preparation and exposure procedure with AIML-T integrated at DCAF/AF or NEF (clause 6.30.2), the AF-NWDAF interaction procedure for generating AI/ML assistance information (clause 6.32.2), and the 5G-assisted FL member selection procedure with restriction criteria (clause 6.44.2). In each, the AF requests or subscribes to analytics via the NEF, which forwards the request to the NWDAF.

questions.question: For collecting UPF-related data and event exposure for analytics purposes, which procedures involve the NWDAF, the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the UE communication analytics procedure (TS 23.288, clause 6.7.3.4), the information flow for subscription to UPF event exposure service for certain UEs via SMF (TS 23.502, clause 4.15.4.5.2), the QoS Flow Performance data collection procedure from UPF for Observed Service Experience Analytics (TS 23.700-62, clause 6.8.3), the UPF Information Exposure to NWDAF procedure (TS 23.700-62, clause 6.10.3), and the QoS Sustainability analytics procedure (TS 23.700-81, clause 6.50.2). In each, the NWDAF requests or subscribes to UPF-related data via the SMF.

questions.question: For N4 session and PDU session related signalling, which procedures put the AMF, the PCF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the N4 Session Modification procedure (TS 23.502, clause 4.4.1.3) and N4 Session Release procedure (TS 23.502, clause 4.4.1.4), where the SMF interacts with the AMF or the PCF that triggered the procedure; the procedure for enabling QoS monitoring for dynamic satellite backhaul delay control (TS 23.700-27, clause 6.9.2); the procedure of AF influence on area-based AI/ML operations related policies (TS 23.700-80, clause 6.9.2.1), where the PCF and SMF coordinate location monitoring via the AMF; and the URSP Compliance Verification procedure in PDU Session Establishment (TS 23.700-85, clause 6.7.2.2), where the AMF forwards the request to the SMF together with PCF binding information.

questions.question: For applying AF-requested policy and QoS changes to a PDU session, which procedures involve the AF, the PCF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the overview of QoS Flow establishment (TS 23.700-25, clause 6.16.3), where the PCF composes PCC rules from an AF/NEF/TSCTSF request and invokes the SMF; the PDU-set related packet handling procedure (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.23.3); the AF-requesting-jitter-calculation procedure (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.31.3); the coordinated delivery of multiple QoS flows procedure (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.65.3.2); and the procedure of AF influence on area-based AI/ML operations related policies (TS 23.700-80, clause 6.9.2.1). In each, the PCF updates the SMF with policy information derived from an AF request.

questions.question: For QoS monitoring and backhaul delay control involving the user plane, which procedures put the PCF, the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: PDU session establishment when the gNB has multiple satellite backhaul UP connections (TS 23.700-27, clause 6.2.2), and the procedure for enabling QoS monitoring for dynamic satellite backhaul delay control (TS 23.700-27, clause 6.9.2), where the UPF reports QoS monitoring results and the SMF notifies the PCF; Setting up an AF session with required QoS (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.13.3.1) and the variant meeting an RT latency requirement (clause 6.27.3); and the procedure of UPF information in BSF (TS 23.700-62, clause 6.15.3.1.2).

questions.question: For configuring and reporting monitoring events at the serving node, which procedures put the MME, the SCEF and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.682, are: the Configuration Procedure (clause 5.6.2.1), where the SCEF sends a Monitoring Request to the MME(s)/SGSN(s); the Reporting Procedure (clause 5.6.3.1), where the MME/SGSN sends a Monitoring Indication to the SCEF; the Configuration Procedure via IWK-SCEF (clause 5.6.6.1); and the Reporting Procedure for roaming scenarios (clause 5.6.8.1).

questions.question: For monitoring the accuracy of a trained ML model, which procedures put the ADRF, the MTLF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-81, are: the procedure for trained ML model(s) storage in ADRF (clause 6.42.2.1), where the NWDAF containing AnLF requests the NWDAF containing MTLF to store a model, which the MTLF then sends to the ADRF; and the procedure of ML model storage in ADRF and ML model provision from ADRF (clause 6.43.2), where the NWDAF containing MTLF stores its trained ML model at the ADRF.

questions.question: For discovering an Edge Application Server via DNS, which procedures put the DNS, the EAS, the EASDF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: EAS (UPF on-board) discovery procedure with EASDF (TS 23.700-27, clause 6.5.2), EAS rediscovery procedure in roaming scenario (TS 23.700-48, clause 6.3.2.2), the EASDF-related procedure to discover the same EAS (TS 23.700-48, clause 6.18.2.1), and EAS discovery in VPLMN with dynamic setup of a LBO PDU Session (TS 23.700-48, clause 6.27.2). In each, the SMF interacts with the EASDF to resolve or manage the DNS query that leads to the EAS.

questions.question: For distributing QoS policy from the network to the user plane, which procedures involve the PCC, the PCF, the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: enabling QoS monitoring for dynamic satellite backhaul delay control (TS 23.700-27, clause 6.9.2), setting up an AF session with required QoS meeting an RT latency requirement (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.27.3), PDU Set integrated packet handling (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.56.3), and the 5G-assisted FL member selection procedure (TS 23.700-80, clause 6.19.2). In each, the PCF issues PCC rules that the SMF installs and pushes down to the UPF.

questions.question: For handling PDN GW-initiated or HSS/AAA-initiated session termination over S2c, which procedures put the AAA, the GW, the HSS and the PDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the HSS/AAA-initiated Detach Procedure for Fixed Broadband Access (TS 23.139, clause 7.4), the UE-Initiated PDN disconnection Procedure (TS 23.402, clause 7.5.2), and the HSS/AAA-initiated Detach Procedure over S2c (TS 23.402, clause 7.5.3). In each, the PDN GW and the 3GPP AAA Server/HSS exchange detach or disconnection notifications for the UE's PDN connection.

questions.question: For requesting and subscribing to an LMR user's location on behalf of the MC system, which procedures involve the LMC, the LMR, the LMS and the MC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.283, are: the on-demand request of location information procedure from LMS to IWF (clause 10.11.4.2.1.1), the location information subscription procedure from LMS to IWF (clause 10.11.4.2.3.1), and the location information cancel subscription procedure from LMS to IWF (clause 10.11.4.2.4.1). In each, the MC service server or LMC sends the request to the LMS, which forwards it to the IWF for the LMR user.

questions.question: For selecting an SMF using service-area conditions, which procedures put the AMF, the DNN, the NSSAI and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: PDU Session Establishment for Localized Service (TS 23.700-08, clause 6.45.3), the procedure for support of service area group attribute (TS 23.700-74, clause 6.1.3), and UE's URSP enforcement validation by the network (TS 23.700-85, clause 6.15.2). In each, the AMF forwards the DNN and S-NSSAI to the SMF as part of SMF selection or session context creation.

questions.question: For authorizing an RT latency requirement from the AF, which procedures put the AF, the NEF, the PCF and the RT (latency requirement) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.700-60, are: setting up an AF session with required QoS meeting an RT latency requirement (clause 6.27.3), the general setting up an AF session with required QoS procedure (clause 6.28.3), and the same procedure for XRM services (clause 6.71.3). In each, the NEF authorizes the AF's RT latency requirement and forwards it to the PCF.

questions.question: For updating PCC rules following a PDN GW notification, which procedures involve the GW, the PCC, the PCRF and the PDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.161, are: UE Requested IP Flow Mapping via Untrusted WLAN access (clause 6.4.3) and IP flow mobility triggered by an Access Stratum move-to-WLAN indication (clause 6.7.2). In each, the PDN GW notifies the PCRF, which updates the PCC rules and returns them to the PDN GW.

questions.question: For coordinating multicast MBS session updates between the AMF and the SMF, which procedures put the AMF, the MBS, the SM and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.247, are: N2 based handover from an MBS supporting NG-RAN node (clause 7.2.3.3), where the target AMF and SMF exchange multicast MBS session information via Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext; and the Multicast session update procedure (clause 7.2.6), where the MB-SMF notifies the AMF, and the AMF in turn notifies the SMFs serving the affected UEs.

questions.question: For redirecting an initial request to a Personal Network Element, which procedures involve the CSCF, the PN, the PNE and the PNM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.259, are: the PN-deregistration procedure for a PNE other than a PN UE (clause 5.2.4) and the procedure for PNE redirection in the IM CN subsystem (clause 6.1.3). In each, the S-CSCF forwards requests to the PNM AS, which manages the PN configuration to route them to the correct PNE.

questions.question: For selecting an LMF and forwarding a location request via the AMF, which procedures involve the AMF, the LMF, the LR (location request) and the MT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the generalized positioning procedure for a UE with MBSR access covering MT-LR/MO-LR/NI-LR (TS 23.700-05, clause 6.15.3), the Deferred 5GC-MT-LR Procedure via user plane (TS 23.700-71, clause 6.3.3.2a), and the LMF Change Procedure with user plane positioning (TS 23.700-71, clause 6.3.3.5). In each, the AMF selects an LMF and forwards the MT-LR location request to it.

questions.question: For deactivating a subscriber's EPS bearer context at the Serving GW, which procedures put the EPS, the GW, the PDN and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.401, are: the SGSN-Initiated Detach procedure with ISR activated (clause 5.3.8.3A) and the HSS-Initiated Detach procedure (clause 5.3.8.4). In each, the SGSN sends a Delete Session Request per PDN connection to the Serving GW to deactivate the EPS bearer context.

questions.question: For an X2-based handover reported to the MME, which procedures involve the CSG, the EPS, the GW and the MME in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.401, are: X2-based handover without Serving GW relocation (clause 5.5.1.1.2) and X2-based handover with Serving GW relocation (clause 5.5.1.1.3). In each, the target eNodeB sends a Path Switch Request to the MME, and the MME may relocate the Serving GW; a CSG cell case affects whether the target cell is checked against the UE's CSG subscription.

questions.question: For establishing a QoS monitoring subscription via the NEF, which procedures put the DN, the NEF, the NRM and the VAL in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.434, are: the unicast QoS monitoring subscription procedure (clause 14.3.3.4.1.2) and the retrieval of unicast QoS monitoring data procedure (clause 14.3.3.4.4.2). In each, the VAL server requests the NRM server to interact with the NEF, using DN Performance Analytics exposure, on behalf of the VAL server.

questions.question: For switching a VAL UE from broadcast to unicast reception based on reception quality, which procedures involve the BLER, the MBS, the NRM and the VAL in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.434 clause 14.3.4A (service continuity from broadcast to unicast, sub-clauses 8.2.2 and 9.2.2), describe how the NRM client of a VAL UE detects bad broadcast reception quality of the MBS session, using the BLER of the received media, and triggers the switch to unicast delivery.

questions.question: For revoking or generating an SM policy from an AF request via the NEF, which procedures put the AF, the NEF, the PCF and the SM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: revoking a Multi-member AF session with required QoS (TS 23.502, clause 4.15.6.13.4), where the NEF sends an Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Delete request and the PCF proceeds with SM Policy Association Modification; and PDU Set transmission coordination between RAN and UPF (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.53.3), where the NEF forwards the AF request to the PCF to generate the SM policy.

questions.question: For a PINE registering to the PIN server via a discovered FQDN, which procedures involve the FQDN, the PEGC, the PIN and the PINE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.542, are: PINE registration to the PIN server via the PEGC before join (clause 8.4.2.2.3) and PINE registration to the PIN server during PIN join via the PEGC (clause 8.4.2.2.4). In each, the PINE, having discovered the PIN server's FQDN, routes its registration or join request through the PEGC.

questions.question: For an EASDF reporting a DNS query FQDN to the SMF, which procedures put the DNS, the EASDF, the FQDN and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-48, are: the EASDF-related procedure to discover the same EAS (clause 6.18.2.1), where the EASDF provides the FQDN from the DNS query to the SMF; and EAS discovery in a shared-EAS scenario (clause 6.40.3), where EASDF1 forwards the DNS query message to the SMF when it matches a peer PLMN's FQDN information.

questions.question: For sending a DNS response directing a UE to an EAS at a target DNAI, which procedures involve the DNAI, the DNS, the EAS and the EASDF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-48, describe Server Discovery with dedicated (re)location information (clauses 6.35.2 and 6.36.2): in each, the EASDF sends the DNS response to the UE pointing to the EAS within the target DNAI, or to the target EAS directly.

questions.question: For mapping an RT latency requirement into a PCC rule's PDB, which procedures put the PCC, the PCF, the PDB and the RT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-60, are: setting up an AF session with required QoS meeting an RT latency requirement (clause 6.27.3), where the PCF splits the RT latency requirement into UL/DL PDB parts and determines PCC rules; and the general setting up an AF session with required QoS procedure (clause 6.28.3), where the PCF maps the RT latency requirement to a PDB-bearing PCC rule.

questions.question: For collecting a UE's location using its SUPI or GPSI via the UDM, which procedures involve the GPSI, the NWDAF, the SUPI and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-71, are: the One-time Collection Procedure (clause 6.13.3.1) and the Continuous Collection Procedure (clause 6.13.3.2). In each, the NWDAF invokes Nudm_UECM_Get toward the home UDM using the target UE's GPSI or SUPI to obtain the serving AMF address.

questions.question: For registering or updating a Pedestrian/Reference UE's status with the LMF using its SUPI, which procedures put the AMF, the LMF, the PRU and the SUPI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-71, are: the Registration Procedure for a PRU (clause 6.28.3.1), where the LMF verifies the PRU's SUPI via the AMF; and the Registration Modification Procedure for a PRU (clause 6.28.3.2), where the LMF sends a Registration Modification to the serving AMF including the PRU's SUPI.

questions.question: For preparing federated learning member candidates at the AF, which procedures involve the AF, the AI, the FL and the ML in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-80, are: federated learning analytics as assistance to an AI/ML application server (clause 6.6.2) and the Federated Learning Assistance Function assisting FL member selection (clause 6.23.2). In each, the AF prepares candidate FL member information for the AI/ML federated learning operation.

questions.question: For an AF influencing AI/ML-related policies or requesting assistance information via the NEF, which procedures put the AF, the AI, the ML and the NEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-80, are: the procedure of AF influence on area-based AI/ML operations related policies (clause 6.9.2.1), where the AF sends AI/ML configuration information via the NEF's enhanced parameter provisioning API; and the 5GC information preparation and exposure procedure with AIML-T integrated at DCAF/AF or NEF (clause 6.30.2).

questions.question: For selecting UEs for federated learning based on location reported via the NEF, which procedures involve the AF, the AMF, the FL and the NEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-80, are: 5GS assistance for FL member selection based on a UE's visited AOI (clause 6.18.2), where the NEF invokes Namf_EventExposure_Subscribe toward the AMF on the AF's behalf; and the procedure for AF direct collection of information for FL member selection (clause 6.43.2.1), where the AF requests UE location reporting from the AMF, via the NEF if untrusted.

questions.question: For discovering a central MTLF via the NRF to coordinate federated learning, which procedures put the FL, the ML, the MTLF and the NRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, both in TS 23.700-81, are: support of model training using federated learning (clause 6.23.2), where the AnLF discovers the central MTLF supporting FL aggregation from the NRF; and the Horizontal Federated Learning training procedure (clause 6.53.2.4), where the coordinating MTLF selects other MTLFs with FL client role based on the NRF response.

questions.question: For terminating a PDN connection over S2c with the BPCF involved, which procedures involve the BPCF, the PCRF and the PDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.139, are the UE-initiated, HSS-initiated, and PDN GW-initiated detach/disconnection procedures with DSMIPv6 on S2c in both trusted (clauses 8.2.2, 8.2.3, 8.2.4) and untrusted (clauses 8.3.2, 8.3.3, 8.3.4) Fixed Broadband Access. In each, the PCRF executes a Gateway Control and QoS Rules Provision procedure or, for the last PDN connection, a PCRF-Initiated Gateway Control Session Termination Procedure with the BPCF.

questions.question: For fetching and updating IMS repository data at the UDR via a front-end, which procedures put the FE, the HSS and the UDR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.335 Annex A, are: the IMS service data change flow with Ud Update from HSS-FE (clause A.2.3), the Application Server Subscription flow (clause A.3.2), the Application Server Notification flow without Ud-Notify (clause A.4.3) and with Ud-Notify (clause A.4.4), and their subscription-expired variants (clauses A.4.5 and A.4.6). In each, the HSS-FE queries or updates user data at the UDR on behalf of an Application Server.

questions.question: For an AF requesting AI/ML-related network assistance, which procedures put the AF, the AI and the ML in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.700-80, are: session inactivity time and traffic volume monitoring for AI/ML-based services (clause 6.1.2.2), traffic routing enhancements for Application AI/ML traffic (clause 6.11.2), 5GC information preparation and exposure to assist AI/ML operations at the UE side (clause 6.30.2), AF-NWDAF interaction to generate AI/ML assistance information (clause 6.32.2), Application AI/ML traffic transmission status exposure to the AF (clause 6.34.2), and external parameter provisioning via the AI/ML AF (clause 6.36.2). In each, the AF requests or receives AI/ML-related assistance from the 5GC.

questions.question: For a UAE server subscribing UAVs to dynamic location information within or across UAS operators, which procedures involve the UAE, the UAS and the UAV in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the subscription procedure within a UAS operator (TS 23.255, clause 7.8.2.3.1, and its TS 23.700-55 counterpart clause 7.7.2.3.4.1), C2 direct mode feasibility reporting (TS 23.700-55, clause 7.5.2.2), the subscription procedure across UAS operators (TS 23.700-55, clause 7.7.2.3.4.2), and the notification procedure (TS 23.700-55, clause 7.7.2.3.5). In each, a UAE server subscribes UAE clients (UAVs) belonging to a UAS operator to dynamic location information.

questions.question: For an AMF forwarding a positioning request to the LMF for location services, which procedures put the AMF, the LCS and the LMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the UE Assisted and UE Based Positioning Procedure (TS 23.273, clause 6.11.1); the One-time and Continuous Collection procedures where the AMF invokes Nlmf_Location_DetermineLocation toward the LMF (TS 23.700-71, clauses 6.13.3.1 and 6.13.3.2); Support for 5GS Localization via Reference UE, where the LCS client's request reaches the LMF via the AMF (TS 23.700-71, clause 6.17.3); and network assisted sidelink positioning for partial coverage, where the GMLC forwards an LCS service request to the AMF, which relays it to the LMF (TS 23.700-86, clause 6.21.3).

questions.question: For an MC service client obtaining an MBMS bearer's TMGI from the service description, which procedures involve the MBMS, the MC and the TMGI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the use of pre-established MBMS bearers (TS 23.280, clause 10.7.3.1.2), the use of an MBMS bearer for application level control signalling (TS 23.280, clause 10.7.3.4.2), MBMS bearer announcement over an existing MBMS bearer (TS 23.280, clause 10.7.3.5.2), MBMS user service usage in MCData (TS 23.282, clause 7.3.5.3.1.2), and the MC MBMS bearer registration procedure (TS 23.479, clause 5.8.2). In each, the MC service client or MC application obtains or registers the TMGI identifying the MBMS bearer.

questions.question: For an MSC Server managing LCLS status during a BSS-related handover, which procedures put the BSS, the LCLS and the MSC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.284, are: the Inter-MSC GSM to GSM handover that breaks Local Switching (clause 8.4.2.1.4), and the BSS Internal Handover sequences that establish (clause 8.4.5.5.2), break (clause 8.4.5.6.2), or leave unmodified the LCLS status of a locally switched call (clause 8.4.5.7.2) or a non-locally switched call (clause 8.4.5.8.2). In each, the MSC-1 Server determines the LCLS connection control status and signals it to the BSS.

questions.question: For a VAL server discovering the SEALDD server via CAPIF before subscribing to data delivery, which procedures involve the CAPIF, the SEALDD and the VAL in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the SEALDD enabled regular data transmission connection establishment procedure (TS 23.433, clause 9.2.2.2), the SEALDD enabled bandwidth control transmission procedure (TS 23.433, clause 9.8.2), E2E redundant transmission path establishment (TS 23.700-34, clause 6.2.2.2), SEALDD enabled data transmission quality monitoring (TS 23.700-34, clause 6.12.2.2), and SEALDD enabled rate control for different VAL users (TS 23.700-34, clause 6.18.2.2). In each, the VAL server discovers and selects the SEALDD server via CAPIF functions before sending its service request.

questions.question: For an SM Policy Association exchanging QoS or PDU set information between the PCF and SMF, which procedures involve the PCF, the SM and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: subscribing to normal data transmission interruption events and data rate (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.5.3.1), setting up an AF session with required QoS with dropping data authorization (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.13.3.1), PDU Set transmission coordination between RAN and UPF (TS 23.700-60, clause 6.53.3), URSP Compliance Verification in PDU Session Establishment (TS 23.700-85, clause 6.7.2.2), and 5GS-to-EPC handover with distinct SM and UE PCFs (TS 23.700-85, clause 6.16.2.3.3). In each, the SMF and the PCF exchange SM Policy Association messages.

questions.question: For an MCPTT server routing a group-broadcast call through the IWF to LMR users, which procedures involve the IWF, the LMR and the MCPTT in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.283, are: the group-broadcast group call procedure with an interworking group defined in the MCPTT system (clause 10.3.4.2) and in the LMR system (clause 10.3.4.3), and their call release counterparts (clauses 10.3.4.4 and 10.3.4.5). In each, the MCPTT server or IWF routes the group-broadcast call setup or release request to reach the group's LMR users.

questions.question: For the IWF requesting or subscribing to an MC service user's location on behalf of the LMR system, which procedures put the IWF, the LMR and the MC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures, all in TS 23.283, are: the on-demand request of location information procedure, both from LMS to IWF (clause 10.11.4.2.1.1) and from IWF to LMS (clause 10.11.4.2.1.2); the location information subscription procedure from IWF to LMS (clause 10.11.4.2.3.2); and the location information cancel subscription procedure from IWF to LMS (clause 10.11.4.2.4.2). In each, the IWF in the LMR system requests or subscribes to an MC service user's location from the LMS in the MC system.

questions.question: For an AMF forwarding a PDU session update or context transfer to the SMF, which procedures involve the AMF, the SM and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: Connection Resume in CM-IDLE with Suspend (TS 23.502, clause 4.8.2.3), Handover of a PDU Session from 3GPP to untrusted non-3GPP access (TS 23.502, clause 4.9.2.2), the SMF Context Transfer procedure for LBO or no roaming (TS 23.502, clause 4.26.5.3), and the procedure for switching data traffic between non-3GPP access paths (TS 23.700-53, clause 6.9.3). In each, the AMF and SMF exchange SM context or PDU session update messages.

questions.question: For a PEMC coordinating PIN membership and PEGC selection, which procedures put the PEGC, the PEMC and the PIN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: the PIN delete procedure involving the PIN server (TS 23.542, clause 8.5.3.2.1), where deleting the PIN disables the PEGC's access control; PIN discovery with assistance of the PIN server via PEGC (TS 23.542, clause 8.5.7.2.2); the PINAPP Role Change procedure, where the PEMC selects a new PEGC (TS 23.700-78, clause 7.10.2.2); and PEGC selection information during initial registration (TS 23.700-88, clause 6.4B.2), where the PEMC requests PEGC selection information from the 5GC.

questions.question: For a PINE discovering or joining a PIN via the PEMC, which procedures involve the PEMC, the PIN and the PINE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: PIN discovery based on the PEMC (TS 23.542, clause 8.5.7.2.1), the Creation of PIN procedure (TS 23.700-78, clause 7.3.2.2), the internal PIN service switch procedure (TS 23.700-78, clause 7.11.2.2), and PINE Authorization (TS 23.700-88, clause 6.21.2). In each, a PINE sends a discovery, creation, or join request to the PEMC, which performs authorization on behalf of the PIN.

questions.question: For an SMF invoking EASDF DNS context creation over satellite backhaul, which procedures put the DNS, the EASDF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The relevant procedures are: EAS (UPF on-board) discovery procedure with EASDF over satellite backhaul (TS 23.700-27, clause 6.5.2), EAS discovery procedure accessing V-EHE in a roaming scenario (TS 23.700-48, clause 6.3.2.1), and Server Discovery with dedicated (re)location information (TS 23.700-48, clauses 6.35.2 and 6.36.2). In each, the SMF invokes a DNS context request toward the EASDF to manage the UE's DNS query handling.

questions.question: For background data transfer and QoS negotiation with an application server, which procedures put the SCEF, the PCRF and the SCS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure for resource management of background data transfer (TS 23.682 clause 5.9) and the Setting up an AS session with required QoS procedure (TS 23.682 clause 5.11) both have the SCEF, the PCRF, and the SCS/AS interacting within the same step.

questions.question: For home network authorization via Steering of Roaming, which procedures involve the AMF, the AUSF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Home network authorization via Steering of Roaming (SOR) procedure (TS 23.700-08 clause 6.25.3.2) and the Registration procedure (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.2.3.2) both put the AMF, the AUSF, and the UDM in the same step.

questions.question: For localized service registration and AaaML service profile handling, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and the UDR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Localized service procedures (TS 23.700-08 clause 6.43.3) and the AaaML Service Profile support procedures (TS 23.700-80 clause 6.28.3.1) both involve the AF, the NEF, and the UDR within the same step.

questions.question: For time-sensitive communication and (g)PTP time synchronization signalling, which procedures involve the AF, the PCF and the TSCTSF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedures for burst timing adaptation capability signalling (TS 23.700-25 clause 6.13.3) and the Procedure for (g)PTP time synchronization service with AF request (TS 23.700-25 clause 6.18.3.4) both put the AF, the PCF, and the TSCTSF in the same step.

questions.question: For burst arrival time adjustments in time-sensitive networking, which procedures put the PCF and the TSCTSF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedures for burst arrival time (TS 23.700-25 clause 6.6.3) and Procedures related to QoS flow adjustment (TS 23.700-46 clause 6.3.3) both involve the PCF and the TSCTSF within the same step.

questions.question: For mobile-terminated location request handling, which procedures put the AMF and the GMLC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Several location-related procedures put the AMF and the GMLC in the same step, including the Procedures of SL-MT-LR for periodic, triggered Location Events (TS 23.273 clause 6.20.4), procedures in TS 23.700-71 clause 6.26.3, and multiple procedures in TS 23.700-86 (clauses 6.12.3, 6.20.3.4, 6.23.2, 6.32.2).

questions.question: For UPF data collection and analytics generation, which procedures put the NWDAF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple procedures put the NWDAF and the UPF in the same step: TS 23.288 clause 6.7.3.4, and several procedures in TS 23.700-62 (clauses 6.4.3, 6.10.3, 6.11.3) and TS 23.700-81 (clause 6.8.2).

questions.question: For UE mobility and coverage analytics exchange, which procedures put the AMF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple procedures put the AMF and the NWDAF in the same step: TS 23.288 clause 6.21.4, the 5GS UE Leaving Coverage Procedure (TS 23.700-28 clause 6.11.2.1), and procedures in TS 23.700-71 (clauses 6.13.3.1, 6.18.3), TS 23.700-80 (clause 6.31.2), and TS 23.700-81 (clause 6.50.2).

questions.question: For EPS bearer and session management signalling with the Serving GW, which procedures put the GW and the MME in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple EPS procedures put the Serving GW and the MME in the same step: the Connection Suspend procedure (TS 23.401 clause 5.3.4A), the HSS-initiated Detach procedure (TS 23.401 clause 5.3.8.4), X2-based handover procedures (TS 23.401 clauses 5.5.1.1.2 and 5.5.1.1.3), the Handover Phase in TS 23.402 clause 9.3.2, and a procedure in TS 23.700-28 clause 6.12.2.

questions.question: For inter-RAT handover rejection and monitoring event reporting, which procedures put the MME and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple procedures put the MME and the SGSN in the same step: the SGSN-initiated Detach procedure with ISR activated (TS 23.401 clause 5.3.8.3A), inter-RAT handover reject procedures (TS 23.401 clauses 5.5.2.1.4, 5.5.2.2.4, 5.5.2.3.4, 5.5.2.4.4), and the Reporting Procedure (TS 23.682 clause 5.6.8.1).

questions.question: For SMF subscription and context retrieval from UDM, which procedures put the SMF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple procedures put the SMF and the UDM in the same step: the information flow for subscription to UPF event exposure via SMF (TS 23.502 clause 4.15.4.5.2), the SMF Context Transfer procedure (TS 23.502 clause 4.26.5.3), and procedures in TS 23.700-48 (clause 6.44.2), TS 23.700-62 (clause 6.1.2.5.2), and TS 23.700-74 (clauses 6.7.3, 6.11.3).

questions.question: For UE mobility analytics requested by an application function, which procedures put the AF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Procedures in TS 23.700-80 clause 6.19.2 and clause 6.45.2 both put the AF and the NWDAF in the same step, where the AF's request or policy input directly drives the NWDAF's analytics action.

questions.question: For QoS sustainability analytics exposure toward an application server, which procedures put the NEF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple procedures put the NEF and the NWDAF in the same step: the Procedure for notification on QoS Sustainability Analytics to the V2X Application Server (TS 23.287 clause 6.4.1), and procedures in TS 23.700-80 (clauses 6.19.2, 6.24.2, 6.25.2.1, 6.44.2).

questions.question: For non-3GPP access UE registration and profile management, which procedures put the AAA and the HSS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple procedures put the 3GPP AAA Server and the HSS in the same step: UE Registration Notification, AAA-initiated UE De-registration Notification, HSS-initiated UE De-registration Notification, HSS-initiated User Profile Update Procedure, and AAA-initiated Provide User Profile Procedure (all in TS 23.402 clause 12.1.1, 12.1.2, 12.1.3, 12.2.1, 12.2.2 respectively).

questions.question: For traffic characteristic configuration exchange in time-sensitive networking, which procedures put the PCF and the TSCTSF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Multiple procedures put the PCF and the TSCTSF in the same step, all in TS 23.700-25 (clause 6.6.3), TS 23.700-46 (clauses 6.3.3, 6.4.3), and TS 23.700-74 (clause 6.2.3.1).

questions.question: For a mission-critical UE reporting or querying its MBMS service area, which procedures put the MC application, the MC MBMS user agent and the MBMS SAI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Get MBMS SAI procedure (TS 23.479 clause 5.2.2) and the MBMS SAI update notification procedure (TS 23.479 clause 5.3.2) both put the MC application, the MC MBMS user agent, and the MBMS SAI in the same step.

questions.question: For updating access and mobility management parameters or slice continuity across NG-RAN nodes, which procedures involve the AMF, NG-RAN and the NSSAI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The UE Configuration Update procedure for access and mobility management related parameters (TS 23.502 clause 4.2.4.2) and the SSC mode 3 slice continuity procedure (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.3.3) both involve the AMF, NG-RAN, and the NSSAI within the same step.

questions.question: For enforcing the maximum number of PDU sessions or registered UEs per network slice, which procedures put the NSACF, NSAC and the NSSAI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Hierarchical NSACF-based number of PDU Sessions per network slice availability check and update procedure (TS 23.502 clause 4.2.11.4a) and the NSAC check of the maximum number of UEs procedure (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.13.3.1) both put the NSACF, NSAC, and the NSSAI in the same step.

questions.question: For resuming a suspended connection or handing over between NG-RAN nodes, which procedures involve the AMF, NG-RAN and SM information in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Connection Resume in CM-IDLE with Suspend procedure (TS 23.502 clause 4.8.2.3) and the Xn based inter NG-RAN handover without User Plane function re-allocation procedure (TS 23.502 clause 4.9.1.2.2) both involve the AMF, NG-RAN, and SM information within the same step.

questions.question: For moving a PDU session between 3GPP and untrusted non-3GPP access, which procedures put the SMF, SM information and the QFI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Handover of a PDU Session procedure from untrusted non-3GPP to 3GPP access (TS 23.502 clause 4.9.2.1) and the Handover of a PDU Session procedure from 3GPP to untrusted non-3GPP access (TS 23.502 clause 4.9.2.2) both put the SMF, SM information, and the QFI in the same step.

questions.question: For delivering UE parameter updates or steering-of-roaming data over the control plane, which procedures put the AMF, the UDM and NAS signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The UE Parameters Update via UDM Control Plane procedure (TS 23.502 clause 4.20.2) and the steering of roaming information delivery procedure (TS 23.700-08 clause 6.18.3) both put the AMF, the UDM, and NAS signalling in the same step.

questions.question: For a PEMC discovering or querying a PIN server, which procedures involve the PEMC, the PIN and the FQDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Query PIN profile procedure (TS 23.542 clause 8.5.5.2) and the PIN server discovery from PEMC procedure (TS 23.700-78 clause 7.8.2.2.3) both involve the PEMC, the PIN, and the FQDN within the same step.

questions.question: For an edge enabler client registering or updating its registration, which procedures put the EES, the EEC and the AC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The EEC registration procedure (TS 23.558 clause 8.4.2.2.2) and the EEC registration update procedure (TS 23.558 clause 8.4.2.2.3) both put the EES, the EEC, and the AC in the same step.

questions.question: For assisting hosting network search or authorizing multi-path transmission via a UE-to-network relay, which procedures involve the AMF, NG-RAN and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Hosting network search assistance information in SIB procedure (TS 23.700-08 clause 6.44.3.2) and the Multi-path transmission via Layer-2 UE-to-Network Relay procedure (TS 23.700-33 clause 6.26.2) both involve the AMF, NG-RAN, and the UDM in the same step.

questions.question: For an AF influencing service function chaining for a target UE, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and the SFC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Procedure to associate SFC with an individual UE (TS 23.700-18 clause 6.3.2.2) and the SFC policy configuration procedure for target UEs (TS 23.700-18 clause 6.6.2) both put the AF, the NEF, and the SFC in the same step.

questions.question: For applying PCC-derived QoS monitoring or coordinated QoS flow treatment, which procedures involve the AMF, the SMF and PCC rule information in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The QoS monitoring for dynamic satellite backhaul delay control procedure (TS 23.700-27 clause 6.9.2) and the coordination group ID and group level treatment policy distribution procedure (TS 23.700-60 clause 6.65.3.2) both involve the AMF, the SMF, and PCC rule information within the same step.

questions.question: For a UE switching to an alternative S-NSSAI according to its URSP rules, which procedures involve the AMF, the NSSAI and the URSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PDU session handover to a target CN with an alternative S-NSSAI support procedure (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.5.3) and the S-NSSAI replacement signalling procedure (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.42.3) both involve the AMF, the NSSAI, and the URSP within the same step.

questions.question: For registering a UE with conditional network slices or providing rejected S-NSSAI information, which procedures put the AMF, the NSSAI and the TA in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The UE registration for conditional network slices procedure (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.23.3) and the UE registration and registration update procedure with additional slice information in TA granularity (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.25.3) both put the AMF, the NSSAI, and the TA in the same step.

questions.question: For registering a UE with secondary allowed slices or replacing an unavailable S-NSSAI, which procedures involve the AMF, the NSSAI and the NSSF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Registration procedure with Secondary Allowed NSSAI (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.26.3) and the S-NSSAI replacement signalling procedure (TS 23.700-41 clause 6.42.3) both involve the AMF, the NSSAI, and the NSSF within the same step.

questions.question: For starting or updating a broadcast MBS session on a shared NG-RAN, which procedures put the MOCN, NG-RAN and the TMGI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Broadcast Session Start procedure (TS 23.700-47 clause 6.9.3.2) and the Broadcast Session update and release procedure (TS 23.700-47 clause 6.9.3.3) both put the MOCN, NG-RAN, and the TMGI in the same step.

questions.question: For a second UE establishing a session and resolving DNS via an edge-configured DNS handler, which procedures involve the DNS, the EASDF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The dedicated (re)location information server discovery procedure (TS 23.700-48 clause 6.35.2) and its EAS Deployment Information variant (TS 23.700-48 clause 6.36.2) both involve the DNS, the EASDF, and the UPF within the same step, where UE2's session establishment with the C-UPF triggers an EASDF configured with DNS handling rules.

questions.question: For a UE switching its data traffic between non-3GPP access paths, which procedures put the AMF, the MA PDU Session and the TNGF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The non-3GPP access switching procedure (TS 23.700-53 clause 6.8.3) and the data traffic switching between two non-3GPP access paths procedure (TS 23.700-53 clause 6.9.3) both put the AMF, the MA PDU Session, and the TNGF in the same step.

questions.question: For redirecting a UE from 5G to 4G based on radio frequency selection priority, which procedures involve the PCF, the AM and the RFSP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both procedures in TS 23.700-89 clause 6.2.2 and clause 6.6.2 involve the PCF, the AM (Access and Mobility) Policy Modification procedure, and the RFSP in the same step: the PCF initiates the AM Policy Modification procedure to provide the UE's new Authorized RFSP index.

questions.question: For an application server updating or being notified of repository data via the Sh interface, which procedures put the HSS and the FE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five Sh/Ud information flow examples in TS 23.335 annex A put the HSS and the FE (front-end) in the same step, as the HSS-FE: the IMS service data change flow (A.2.3), the Application Server Subscription flow (A.3.2), the IMS user capability change with Ud notification flow (A.4.2), the Application Server Notification flow without Ud-Notify (A.4.3), and the Application Server Notification flow with Ud-Notify (A.4.4).

questions.question: For confirming or changing the local-switching status of a call, which procedures put the BSS and the LCLS status in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Six call-flow procedures in TS 23.284 put the BSS and the LCLS-BSS status in the same step: the MSC server initiated example call flow (7.3.4.2), the intermediate node/GMSC server initiated example call flow (7.3.4.3), the inter-MSC handover that breaks local switching (8.4.2.1.4), and three BSS internal handover sequences (8.4.5.5.2 establishing, 8.4.5.6.2 breaking, and 8.4.5.7.2 not modifying local switching).

questions.question: For establishing, updating or path-switching a group communication over broadcast/multicast delivery, which procedures involve the MBS session and MC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Six procedures in TS 23.289 involve the MBS session and an MC service (client/server) in the same step: the dynamic MBS session announcement (7.3.3.1.3), the MBS session creation for application-level control signalling (7.3.3.6.2), MC group communication delivered over a broadcast MBS session (7.3.3.8.2.2), path switch from an MBS session to a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay (7.3.3.8.4.2), and MCVideo/MCData call/group connect-disconnect over an MBS session (7.3.3.11.2, 7.3.3.12.4.2).

questions.question: For adjusting or applying PCC rules to satellite backhaul, multi-modal or PDU Set QoS flows, which procedures put the PCF and the PCC rule in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Six procedures put the PCF and a PCC rule in the same step: QoS monitoring for dynamic satellite backhaul delay control (TS 23.700-27 clause 6.9.2), and five TS 23.700-60 procedures — PCC rule adjustment for coordinated flows (6.1.3), AF session with QoS revoke for multi-modal QoS flow (6.4.3.2), Importance-Level-based PCC rule generation (6.10.3), conditional-QoS PCC rule generation (6.35.3), and PDU-Set-indication PCC rule determination (6.51.3).

questions.question: For deactivating, updating or authorizing a multicast/broadcast MBS session, which procedures put the SMF and the MBS session in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures put the SMF and the MBS session in the same step: the MBS session deactivation procedure (TS 23.247 clause 7.2.5.3), the multicast session update procedure (TS 23.247 clause 7.2.6), and three TS 23.700-47 procedures — MB-SMF notifying SMF of MBS session status (6.18.3), SMF authorizing UE join to a multicast MBS session (6.27.3), and MB-SMF deciding to establish an MBS session towards the radio based on join requests (6.30.3).

questions.question: For an unmanned aerial system application enabler aggregating or subscribing to dynamic UAV information, which procedures involve the UAE and the UAV in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures involve the UAE server and the UAV in the same step: the cross-operator subscription procedure (TS 23.255 clause 7.8.2.3.2) and its notification counterpart (7.8.2.3.3), the C2 direct mode feasibility request procedure (TS 23.700-55 clause 7.5.2.2), and its own cross-operator subscription (7.7.2.3.4.2) and notification (7.7.2.3.5) procedures.

questions.question: For an interworking function handling group calls or location information requests with a land mobile radio system, which procedures put the IWF and the LMR system in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures in TS 23.283 put the IWF and the LMR system in the same step: the group-broadcast group call release procedure (10.3.4.3), the on-demand location information request (10.11.4.2.1.1), the location information subscription procedure (10.11.4.2.3.1), and the location information subscription cancellation from LMS to IWF (10.11.4.2.4.1) and IWF to LMS (10.11.4.2.4.2).

questions.question: For an ICS-enhanced UE registering or changing from speech to video, which procedures involve the MSC and ICS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures in TS 23.292 involve the MSC Server enhanced for ICS in the same step: registration using the I2 reference point (7.2.1.2), registration after deregistration (7.2.1.4) and before deregistration (7.2.1.5) using I2, and speech-to-video service change completion using the Gm (7.9.2.2) and I1 (7.9.2.3) reference points.

questions.question: For a mobile base station relay handing over between NG-RAN nodes or registering with the core network, which procedures put the MBSR and NG-RAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures in TS 23.700-05 put the MBSR and NG-RAN in the same step: the N2 handover procedures (6.4.3.3.2 and 6.5.3.2.1), the Xn handover procedure (6.5.3.2.2), the MBSR mobility registration procedure with AMF change (6.5.3.3), and the MBSR handover with UEs during an AMF change (6.5.3.4).

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF and the UDR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Several procedures have a step where the NEF directly stores, updates, or removes data in the UDR (or receives the UDR's response). In TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.9.3 (Processing AF requests to influence access and mobility management policies), the NEF stores/updates/removes the AM-influence policy data in the UDR and later receives the UDR's result. In TS 23.700-48 clause 6.51.2.1 (Provisioning), the NEF invokes Nudr_DM_Create/Update/Delete toward the UDR, which stores/updates/removes the data and responds. In TS 23.700-74 clause 6.22.3.1 (Traffic Characteristics provisioning and Performance Characteristics Monitoring), the NEF invokes Nudr_DM Create/Update/Remove to store Internal Group ID related information in the UDR. In TS 29.513 clause 5.5.2.1 (AF-initiated PFD management procedure), the NEF invokes the Nudr_DataRepository Create/Update/Delete operation on the UDR and the UDR sends the HTTP response back to the NEF.

questions.question: For a PIN endpoint (PINE) association being activated or deactivated through the PIN element with gateway capability, which procedures put the PEGC, the PEMC and the PINE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures have a step where the PEGC, the PEMC and the PINE act together. In TS 23.700-78 clause 7.16.2.2.2 (Change application layer communication to communication via 5GS with PIN server support), the PEMC client configures the PINE with new PEGC information and coordinates PEGC selection with the PINE(s). In TS 23.700-88 clause 6.8.2.3.2 (Activate association), when the PEGC receives or detects an Association Activate Request from the PINE it forwards this toward the PEMC (directly or via PINMF), and the PEMC responds back through the PEGC to the PINE. Clause 6.8.2.3.3 (Deactivate association) mirrors this for association deactivation: the PEGC signals the PEMC about the PINE's lost connection and forwards the PEMC's response back. In TS 33.882 clause 6.3.2 (Solution details for PINE authentication), the PINE connects to the PEGC, the PEGC indicates the connection to the PEMC, and the PEMC authorizes the PINE's connection to the PEGC.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the AAA and EAP messaging in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures show the 3GPP AAA Server directly handling EAP messages within one step. In TS 29.273 Annex E.2 (Successful call flow for trusted WLAN / S2b access), the ePDG forwards the EAP payload to the 3GPP AAA Server, and the AAA Server sends back an EAP Request/AKA-Challenge and later an EAP Success message. In TS 33.320 Annex A.2 (Combined Device and HP Authentication Call-flow Example), the SeGW sends an Authentication Request with an EAP AVP to the 3GPP AAA Server, and the AAA Server responds with an Authentication Answer containing an EAP Success and key material.

questions.question: In handover with early status transfer, which procedures put DAPS, PDCP and the SN status information together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four handover-related clauses have a single step tying DAPS, PDCP and SN together: for E-RABs/DRBs configured with DAPS, the source eNB/gNB sends the EARLY STATUS TRANSFER message, whose DL COUNT value conveys the PDCP SN and HFN of the first PDCP SDU forwarded to the target node; the source node keeps assigning PDCP SNs to downlink packets until it sends the SN STATUS TRANSFER message to the target. This appears in TS 36.300 clause 10.1.2.1.1 (C-plane handling, LTE X2 handover), TS 38.300 clause 9.2.3.2.1 (NR Xn handover), and TS 38.523-1 clauses 8.1.4.3.1 and 8.1.4.3.2 (Conditional handover conformance test procedures), which reproduce the same EARLY STATUS TRANSFER / SN STATUS TRANSFER step for DAPS-configured DRBs.

questions.question: For gateway control session establishment and termination over the WLAN S9a interface, which procedures put the BPCF and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures have a step in which the PCRF and the BPCF exchange messages directly over S9a. In TS 23.139 clause 7.6 (Network-Initiated Dynamic PCC for EPC-routed Traffic), the PCRF (or V-PCRF) initiates the Gateway Control and QoS Rules Provision Procedure with the BPCF over S9a. In TS 23.203 Annex P.7.5.4 (PCRF-Initiated Gateway Control Session Termination), the (h)PCRF or V-PCRF sends the termination procedure toward BPCF over S9a and the BPCF acknowledges. In TS 29.213 Annex E.4.2.1 (IP-CAN Session Establishment for EPC-routed traffic), the PCRF sends a TER/RAR command to the BPCF to trigger or update an S9a session, and the BPCF acknowledges with a TEA/RAA command. In Annex E.5.2a (BPCF-initiated S9a CS Session Modification), the BPCF initiates an S9a session modification by sending a CCR to the PCRF, which acknowledges with a CCA.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF and the NG-RAN in the same step when managing MBS sessions?
questions.reference_answer: Four MBS-related procedures have a step where the AMF and the NG-RAN interact directly. In TS 23.247 clause 7.2.2.3 (Multicast session leave requested by the network or MBS session release), the AMF sends an N2 Request to the NG-RAN and the NG-RAN sends the N2 Response back to the AMF. In clause 7.3.1 (MBS Session Start for Broadcast), the AMF transfers the MBS Session Resource Setup Request to all NG-RAN nodes supporting MBS in the service area, and each NG-RAN reports back with an MBS Session Resource Setup Response. In clause 7.3.6 (Broadcast MBS Session Release Require), the NG-RAN sends a Broadcast Session Release Require message to the AMF, and the AMF may initiate broadcast session release toward the NG-RAN. In TS 23.700-47 clause 6.7.3.5 (Broadcast MBS Session Transport Request), the NG-RAN sends an N2 message (e.g. BROADCAST SESSION TRANSPORT REQUEST) to the AMF, and the AMF forwards the corresponding N2 response back to the NG-RAN.

questions.question: I need every place where the GW (Serving GW) and the SGSN are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures have a step where the Serving GW (S-GW) and the SGSN act on each other directly. In TS 23.060 clause 8.1.3a (Ready to Standby state transition in S4 architecture), the SGSN sends a Release Access Bearers Request to the S-GW, and the S-GW returns a Release Access Bearers Response to the SGSN. In TS 23.401 clause 5.3.4.3 (Network Triggered Service Request), the Serving GW sends a Downlink Data Notification message to the MME and SGSN nodes serving the UE, and the SGSN/MME acknowledge with a Downlink Data Notification Ack. In clause 5.5.2.2.3 (Execution phase, UTRAN Iu mode to E-UTRAN handover), the source SGSN sends a Delete Indirect Data Forwarding Tunnel Request to the S-GW to release temporary forwarding resources. In clause 5.5.2.4.3 (Execution phase, GERAN A/Gb mode to E-UTRAN handover), the source SGSN sends a Delete Session Request to the Source Serving GW, which acknowledges with a Delete Session Response.

questions.question: For federated learning data lifecycle management, which procedures put the ADRF, the DCCF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures have a step where the ADRF, the DCCF and the NWDAF appear together. In TS 23.288 clause 6.2.6.3.6 (Data collection profile registration), the ADRF or NWDAF registers/updates/deregisters a data collection profile at the DCCF by invoking Ndccf_ContextManagement_Register/Update/Deregister, and the DCCF responds. In clause 6.2B.2 (Historical Data and Analytics storage), the DCCF or NWDAF may retrieve data/analytics from the ADRF, indicate whether they will retrieve it, or request its deletion, and the ADRF stores/deletes data accordingly. In clause 6.2B.4 (Data removal from an ADRF), the ADRF indicates a deletion result, noting the NWDAF, DCCF or ADRF can alert the consumer before deletion. In TS 29.552 clause 5.5.2 (Data collection profile registration, stage-3), the ADRF or NWDAF sends the corresponding HTTP request to register/update/deregister the profile at the DCCF, which responds accordingly.

questions.question: In mission-critical push-to-talk group calls, which procedures put MBMS and the MCPTT server/client in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures have a step tying MBMS delivery to MCPTT server/client actions. In TS 23.379 clause 10.10.4.2.2 (Call disconnect over MBMS), the MCPTT server determines to disconnect the call over the MBMS bearer and sends an UnmapGroupFromBearer message to the MCPTT clients over the MBMS bearer(s). In clause 10.6.2.5.2.4 (Server-initiated broadcast group call release procedure), the MCPTT server may send the group call release request to the MCPTT clients via MBMS, in which case no response is expected from the clients. In TS 24.380 Annex A.6.4 (Releasing floor and ending a conversation), the participating MCPTT function sends the Unmap Group to Bearer message over the MBMS subchannel, and the MBMS interfaces in the MCPTT clients remove the association between the TMGI, the MBMS subchannel and the MCPTT group identity.

questions.question: For UE positioning via LPP, which procedures put the AMF, the LMF and LPP signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four positioning procedures have a step tying the AMF, the LMF and LPP signalling together. In TS 23.700-71 clause 6.3.3.2 (5GC-MT-LR Procedure via user plane), the AMF invokes Nlmf_Location_DetermineLocation toward the LMF to request the UE's location, carrying user-plane location capability and LPP-related indications. In TS 38.305 clause 6.4.2 (Control-Plane LPP PDU Transfer), the AMF carries an LPP PDU in a DL NAS Transport message to the UE via NG-RAN, and separately the LMF invokes Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer toward the AMF to request transfer of an LPP PDU to the UE. In clause 7.1.3 (UE positioning measurements in RRC_IDLE for NB-IoT), the LMF learns the UE's access type from the Location Service Request received from the AMF and then exchanges LPP Request Capabilities/Provide Capabilities messages with the UE. In clause 7.3.2 (NI-LR and MT-LR Service Support), the AMF sends a location request to the LMF including the UE's LPP positioning capabilities, and the LMF returns a location response, possibly with LPP UE capabilities, to the AMF.

questions.question: For federated learning client selection via network function discovery, which procedures put the NRF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures have a step where an NWDAF (in a Federated Learning server/client/consumer role) interacts directly with the NRF. In TS 23.700-81 clause 6.21.2.3 (FL operation between NWDAFs containing MTLF), the "FL Consumer" NWDAF discovers and selects the "FL Server" NWDAF via the NRF before subscribing to its ML model training/provision service. In clause 6.51.2.3.1 (New Client NWDAF(s) Inform Server NWDAF Directly), the Server NWDAF registers the Federated Learning procedure (FL Correlation ID, Analytics ID) into the NRF, and a Client NWDAF queries the NRF to discover an ongoing FL procedure and obtain the Server NWDAF's identity. In TS 33.738 clause 6.17.2 (Solution details), the Server NWDAF discovers Client NWDAFs from the NRF based on FL selection criteria and requests access tokens for them from the NRF, which verifies the Server NWDAF's authorization and grants the tokens.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CHF and the PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.502 clause 4.16 put the CHF and the PCF together in the same step: Final Spending Limit Report Retrieval (4.16.8.4), where the PCF sends Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Unsubscribe to the CHF and the CHF removes the subscription and responds; Spending Limit Report (4.16.8.5), where the CHF sends Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Notify to the PCF and the PCF acknowledges; and CHF report the removal of the subscriber (4.16.8.6), where the CHF sends Nchf_SpendingLimitControl_Notify to the H-PCF (a PCF) to report subscriber removal and the H-PCF acknowledges. In all three, the CHF and PCF directly exchange the Nchf_SpendingLimitControl service operation.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GW and the HNB in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three HNB-related procedures in TS 25.467 put the HNB-GW (GW) and the HNB together in the same step: UE Registration for CSG UEs and CSG or Hybrid HNBs (5.1.3), where the HNB transmits a UE REGISTER REQUEST to the HNB-GW and the HNB-GW responds with UE REGISTER ACCEPT; UE Registration for Open Access HNBs (5.1.5), same request/accept exchange; and the Iuh Disconnect procedure (5.5.2), where the HNB sends a Disconnect message to the HNB-GW and the HNB-GW forwards messages back to the HNB. In each, the HNB and HNB-GW directly exchange registration or disconnect signalling.

questions.question: For a P-CSCF handling media/session parameters based on operator policy, which procedures put the CSCF and the PCRF/PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures in TS 23.228 put a CSCF (P-CSCF/S-CSCF) and the PCRF/PCF together in the same step: Codec and media characteristics flow negotiation during initial session establishment (5.11.3.1), where the P-CSCF examines bandwidth authorization limitation information coming from the PCRF/PCF; the Non-IMS Origination (NI-O) procedure (5.6.4), where the P-CSCF may instruct the PCRF/PCF to authorize resources; Establishment of sessions without preconditions (5.7a.2), same instruct-to-authorize pattern for P-CSCF#1/#2; and Subscription to changes of PLMN ID at IMS Initial Registration (W.4.1), where the P-CSCF subscribes to the PCRF/PCF and the PCRF/PCF forwards the PLMN ID back to the P-CSCF. Across these, the CSCF and PCRF/PCF interact for QoS authorization and PLMN-change notification.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BBERF and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures in TS 23.203 clause 7.7 put the GW acting as BBERF and the PCRF together in the same step: Gateway Control Session Establishment during BBERF Relocation (7.7.1.2), where the target GW (BBERF) sends the PCRF a Gateway Control Session Establishment message and the PCRF acknowledges with QoS Rules; GW-Initiated Gateway Control Session Termination (7.7.2.1), where the GW (BBERF) initiates termination towards the H-PCRF and the H-PCRF replies with an acknowledgement; PCRF-Initiated Gateway Control Session Termination (7.7.2.2), where the PCRF sends the termination request to the GW (BBERF) and the GW (BBERF) replies with an acknowledgement; and Event reporting for PCEF in visited network with locally terminated Gxx interaction (7.7.3.2), where the GW (BBERF) sends a Gateway Control and QoS Rules Request to the V-PCRF. In every case the GW/BBERF and PCRF exchange Gateway Control Session messages directly.

questions.question: I need every place where the API publishing function (APF) and the CAPIF core function are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: All four CAPIF service-API lifecycle procedures in TS 23.222 clause 8 put the API publishing function and the CAPIF core function together in the same step, always as a request/response pair: Service API publish (8.3.3) - API publishing function sends the publish request, CAPIF core function checks authorization, stores the API in its registry, and returns a publish response; Service API unpublish (8.4.3) - same pattern for removal; Service API get (8.5.3) - same pattern for retrieval; and Service API update (8.6.3) - same pattern for updating a published API's information. In each, the CAPIF core function also triggers notifications to subscribed API invokers.

questions.question: Which procedures put the Serving GW, the MME and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures in TS 23.401 put the Serving GW, the MME and the SGSN together in the same step: Network Triggered Service Request (5.3.4.3), where the Serving GW sends a Downlink Data Notification to the MME and SGSN nodes, and either node can notify the Serving GW back (e.g. Stop Paging, Failure Indication); the E-UTRAN to GERAN/UTRAN Iu mode Inter RAT handover / PS Handover execution (5.5.2.3.3), where the Target SGSN and Serving GW exchange Modify Bearer Request/Response and the Target SGSN informs the Source MME via Forward Relocation Complete Notification; PS Handover Cancel (5.5.2.5.2), where the target MME/SGSN sends a Delete Indirect Data Forwarding Tunnel Request to the Serving GW during handover cancellation; and Inter-RAT handover from UTRAN/GERAN to E-UTRAN (D.3.5), where the old MME (from the new SGSN's perspective) triggers updates to the GWs and HSS as part of the SGSN Context exchange. All three network elements participate in coordinated signalling in each of these clauses.

questions.question: For RTC (real-time communication) sessions using network assistance, which procedures put the AF and the RTC MSH in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four call-flow procedures in TS 26.506 put the (Network Support/RTC) AF and the RTC Media Session Handler (RTC MSH) together in the same step: Call flow for over-the-top RTC sessions (5.3), where the RTC MSH requests network assistance from the Network Support AF and later the AF sends QoS-change notifications back to the RTC MSH; Call flow for MNO-facilitated RTC sessions (5.5), where the NS-AF sends QoS notifications/bit-rate recommendations to the RTC MSH, which forwards them to the application; Client-driven management of RTC edge processing (6.1), where the RTC MSH retrieves Service Access Information from the RTC AF and exchanges reporting/policy information with it; and AF-driven management of RTC edge processing (6.2), same retrieval and reporting exchange between RTC MSH and RTC AF. In each, the AF and RTC MSH exchange session, QoS or edge-resource information directly.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CSCF and the MSC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four ICS (IMS Centralized Services) procedures in TS 23.292 put the S-CSCF and the MSC Server together in the same step: Termination using I2 reference point (7.4.2.1.2), where the S-CSCF forwards the INVITE to the MSC Server and the MSC Server sends a Setup message to UE B; Network initiated Session Release (7.7.2.4), where the S-CSCF initiates session release towards the MSC Server, which then releases the CS session; Addition/Removal of video media flow through SCUDIF via I2 (7.9.1.2), where the MSC Server sends a re-INVITE to the S-CSCF to add/remove video media; and Addition/Removal of video media flow through redial via I1 (7.9.2.5), where the MSC Server sends the INVITE to the S-CSCF as part of the redial flow. In each, the S-CSCF and MSC Server directly exchange SIP/session-control signalling.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ACM server and the ACM client in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 23.700-38, the ACM server and ACM client exchange requests/responses in the same step across several MC interconnection procedures: 'Authorized user providing interconnection group ID(s) to authorized user of a partner MC system' (clause 7.11.1.3.1), where the ACM client sends a group information provision request to its ACM server and servers forward it across systems; 'ACMX authorisation for an authorised user' (clause 7.5.1.2), where the ACMC requires authorisation from the primary ACMS before starting an ACMX session; 'Group membership update by authorized user from a partner MC system' (clause 7.6.1.2.1), where the ACM client sends a group membership update request to its ACM server which forwards it to the partner ACMS; and 'Remove user configuration request from a partner MC system' (clause 7.8.1.3), where the ACM client sends a remove user configuration request to its ACM server, which is relayed to the partner ACM client. In all four, the ACM server acts as the routing/authorization intermediary between the ACM client and the partner MC system.

questions.question: For LCLS (Local Call Local Switch) call handling in GSM/UMTS, which procedures put the BSS and the LCLS status/control signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 23.284, the BSS actively sends and receives LCLS status/control messages in the same step across the LCLS disconnection procedures: 'MSC server Initiated' (clause 7.2.4.2), where the BSS reports LCLS disconnection via LCLS-Connect-Control Acknowledge and LCLS-Notification messages carrying the LCLS-BSS-Status IE; 'BSS Initiated, LCLS Break requested from Core Network' (clause 7.2.4.4), where the BSS itself determines local switching should be disconnected and sends the LCLS-Notification with LCLS-Break-Request; 'Intermediate Node/GMSC Server Initiated' (clause 7.2.4.5), where the oBSS/tBSS confirm and report LCLS disconnection via LCLS-Connect-Control Acknowledge/LCLS-Notification; and the worked 'Example' in clause 8.4.1.2.8, where BSS-2 notifies the MSC server of LCLS status changes via LCLS_Notification and returns LCLS_Connect_Control_ACK. In each case the BSS is the entity that sets and reports the LCLS-BSS-Status.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NWDAF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NWDAF and the SMF directly exchange requests/responses in at least three procedures: the Session Management Congestion Control Experience analytics procedure in TS 23.288 clause 6.12.4, where the consumer SMF requests/subscribes to analytics from the NWDAF via Nnwdaf_AnalyticsInfo/Nnwdaf_AnalyticsSubscription and the SMF(s) also provide collected data back to the NWDAF; the UPF event exposure via SMF procedure in TS 23.700-62 clause 6.9.3.1, where the NWDAF sends Nsmf_EventExposure_Subscribe to the SMF asking it to perform data collection from the UPF, and the SMF responds to the subscription; and the QoS Sustainability Analytics procedure in TS 23.700-80 clause 6.8.3.1, where the SMF subscribes to related analytics from the NWDAF for a PDU Session based on PCF instructions.

questions.question: I need every place where the PCF and the UDR are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: The PCF and UDR co-act directly in at least five procedures: AMF-initiated UE Policy Association Termination completion in TS 23.502 clause 4.16.13.2, where the UDR sends a Nudr_DM_Notify_Request to the PCF and the PCF confirms reception; the localized service provisioning procedure in TS 23.700-08 clause 6.24.3.2, where the PCF queries the UDR for localized service data and receives it; the RG location information procedure in TS 23.700-17 clause 6.2.2.3, where the UDR notifies the PCF about changes in stored data after NEF writes it; the non-3GPP device information procedure in TS 23.700-17 clause 6.21.2, where the PCF subscribes to non-3GPP device information from the UDR and the UDR notifies the PCF of updates; and the Background Data Transfer policy/warning notification procedure in TS 29.513 clause 5.5.5, where the (H-)PCF queries, updates, and deletes background transfer policies stored in the UDR via Nudr_DataRepository operations and the UDR replies with HTTP responses.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF and the (R)AN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 23.700-28, the AMF and the (R)AN directly exchange N2 signalling in the same step in two related discontinuous-coverage procedures: the UE-triggered/AMF-triggered AN release procedure in clause 6.1.2.1, where the AMF sends an N2 UE Context Release Command to the (R)AN and the (R)AN confirms with an N2 UE Context Release Complete message; and the leaving-coverage handling procedure in clause 6.8.2.1, where, after the UE indicates it is about to leave coverage, the AMF again sends an N2 UE Context Release Command to the (R)AN to release the (R)AN connection.

questions.question: For location services involving UE positioning, which procedures put the LCS Client and the LMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The LCS Client and the LMF interact directly in at least two procedures: the ML-assisted location accuracy prediction procedure in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.59.2, where the LCS Client requests the UE location with a required accuracy from the LMF, and the LMF (after querying the NWDAF for predicted accuracy) returns the location estimate to the LCS Client; and the periodic/triggered sidelink positioning procedure in TS 38.305 clause 7.3A.3, where the LMF returns the event report and sidelink location results to the LCS Client or AF after receiving them from UE1.

questions.question: Where does the AF get involved in the same step as the SMF during PDU session anchor management?
questions.reference_answer: The AF and the SMF interact directly in the same step across several PDU Session Anchor (PSA) related procedures in TS 23.502: additional PDU Session Anchor addition for a multi-homed PDU session (clause 4.3.5.4), where the SMF sends early/late notifications to the AF and waits for a notification response before configuring the new PSA; additional PDU Session Anchor change/release with new PSA and UL CL relocation (clause 4.3.5.6), where the SMF again sends late notifications to the AF and stops on a negative AF response; and additional PDU Session Anchor relocation for IPv6 multi-homing/UL CL (clause 4.3.5.7), where the SMF sends notifications about a change of DNAI to the source and target AF. Additionally, in the XR/media (XRM) QoS procedure of TS 23.700-60 clause 6.17.3, the XRM AF/NEF sends a Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Create/Update request via the PCF, and the SMF later responds to the AF/NEF as part of the QoS Rules signalling chain.

questions.question: For Federated Learning coordination among NWDAF instances, which procedures put the FL Server NWDAF and the FL Client NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The FL Server NWDAF and FL Client NWDAF(s) directly send and receive requests in the same step in at least three procedures: the Federated Learning based Model Training procedure in TS 23.288 clause 6.2C.2.2, where the FL Server NWDAF sends Nnwdaf_MLModelTraining_Subscribe/Nnwdaf_MLModelTrainingInfo_Request to selected FL Client NWDAF(s) and the client(s) report interim local model information back; the Federated Learning group formation/selection procedure in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.51.2.1, where the Server NWDAF sends a preparation request and test tasks to Client NWDAF(s), which respond indicating whether to join; and the security-enhanced FL group formation procedure in TS 33.738 clause 6.17.2, where the Server NWDAF requests tokens and sends an FL request to Client NWDAF(s), which check authorization via the token and respond.

questions.question: For an application server updating or being notified of subscriber data via the Sh/Rx interfaces, which procedures put the P-CSCF and the PCF in the same step?
