questions.reference_answer: The P-CSCF and the PCF interact directly in the same step across several IMS-related procedures: PLMN ID notification during IMS registration in TS 23.228 Annex Y.9.4, where the P-CSCF subscribes to the PCF for PLMN ID changes and the PCF forwards the PLMN ID; P-CSCF restoration after failure in TS 23.380 clause 5.8.5.2, where the PCF sends a P-CSCF restoration indication that reaches the SMF, and the newly selected alternative P-CSCF sends an Rx AAR/Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Create to the associated PCF which replies; gate control at call setup in TS 29.513 Annex B.3.2, where the P-CSCF requests the PCF to open media gates via Diameter AAR/HTTP PATCH and the PCF replies with AAA/200 OK; gate control at call hold in Annex B.3.3, where the P-CSCF requests the PCF to close gates similarly; and PLMN Identifier Change subscription at registration in Annex B.8, where the P-CSCF creates an Individual Application Session Context / Rx session with the PCF to subscribe to PLMN change notifications, and the PCF confirms the subscription.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CSCF and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The P-CSCF and the (H-)PCRF interact directly in several procedures: in the IMS Flow for originating session (TS 23.228 clause M.2.1.2) the P-CSCF provides session information to the H-PCRF/hPCRF; in the network recovery information flows of TS 23.380 (clauses 5.1.2 Update PDP context/Bearer and 5.2.2 Inform UE at P-CSCF failure) the P-CSCF sends an Rx Push to the PCRF to report the selected P-CSCF address; and in TS 29.213 Annex B (clauses B.3.2 Enabling of IP Flows and B.3.3 Disabling of IP Flows) the P-CSCF sends Diameter AAR requests to the PCRF to open or close media gates.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the GANC and the MSC at the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The GANC and the MSC exchange messages directly in the GAN Mobile Terminated CS Call procedure (TS 43.318 clause 9.11 and the equivalent TS 43.902 clause 5.2.5.11), where the MSC pages, sets up and confirms the call via the GANC, and in the CS Handover from GAN to UTRAN procedure (TS 43.902 clause 5.2.5.13.4), where the Serving GANC signals handover need to the MSC via Relocation Required/Command messages.

questions.question: For location event reporting to the LMF, which procedures put the AMF, the LMF and NAS signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF processes a NAS message and forwards it to the LMF in the Event Reporting with no change of LMF procedure (TS 23.273 clause 6.7.1) and the Event Reporting in RRC INACTIVE state for UL Positioning procedure (clause 6.7.4), both via Namf_Communication_N1MessageNotify; and in the 5GC-MT-LR Procedure via user plane (TS 23.700-71 clause 6.3.3.2) the AMF relays user-plane positioning information between the LMF and the UE inside a DL/UL NAS Transport message.

questions.question: Which procedures put the HSS and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The HSS and the UDM interact directly in TS 23.632: in the T-ADS procedure (clause 5.4.1) the HSS uses Nudm_MT_ProvideDomainSelection to retrieve domain-selection information from the UDM, which responds with the 5G domain selection info; and in the P-CSCF Restoration procedure (clause 5.4.2) the HSS triggers P-CSCF restoration via Nudm_UECM_P-CscfRestorationTrigger and the UDM acknowledges the request back to the HSS.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BSS and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Source BSS and the (Source) SGSN exchange handover-preparation messages directly in the execution phase of PS handover to E-UTRAN (TS 23.401 clause 5.5.2.4.3, and the equivalent Gn/Gp Annex D.3.8.3), and in the Intra-SGSN PS Handover preparation phase (TS 43.129 clause 5.8.5.1), where the source RNC/BSS sends a Relocation Required message to the SGSN and the SGSN sends the PS Handover Request to the target GANC on the BSS's behalf.

questions.question: I need every place where the AGF and the RG are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: The W-AGF and the 5G-RG interact directly in TS 23.316's 5G-RG Deregistration via W-5GAN when also serving AUN3 devices (clause 7.2.8.3), where the W-AGF releases the signalling connection with the 5G-RG, and in the 5G-RG or Network Requested PDU Session Modification via W-5GAN procedure (clause 7.3.2), where the W-AGF forwards the PDU Session Modification Command to and from the 5G-RG; also in TS 33.887's WLAN key derivation procedure (clause 6.9.2.1), where the W-AGF and RG jointly derive the KRG from the WAGF key.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PCRF and the SCEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PCRF and the SCEF interact directly in TS 23.682's Request of monitoring event reporting (clause 5.6.4.1), where the SCEF triggers a PCRF-initiated IP-CAN session modification; in the group-of-UEs variant (clause 5.6.4.1a), where each PCRF serving a group member sends a Monitoring Response/Indication to the SCEF; and in TS 29.213's background data transfer negotiation over Nt (clause 4.10), where the SCEF and H-PCRF exchange Diameter BTR/BTA commands to negotiate a transfer policy.

questions.question: Which procedures involve both the PEGC and the PINE at the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PEGC and the PINE interact directly across several PIN (Personal IoT Network) procedures: PIN communication via 5GS and credential provisioning to PINE via 5GS (TS 23.700-78 clauses 7.15.2.2 and 7.15.2.3), where the PINE connects to and sends connection requests to the PEGC; Management of relay path (TS 23.700-88 clause 6.12.2.1) and the QoS-differentiated PDU session procedures (clause 6.13.2), where the PEGC establishes PDU sessions and relays traffic on behalf of the PINE; and Activate association (clause 6.8.2.3.2), where the PINE sends an Association Activate Request to the PEGC and the PEGC responds.

questions.question: In network data analytics collection, which procedures put the NRF, the NWDAF and OAM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NRF, NWDAF and OAM co-appear as data sources/consumers in the Network Performance analytics procedure (TS 23.288 clause 6.6.4), where a change reported by OAM or a change in NF load reported by NRF is notified to the NWDAF, and in TS 33.738's NF anomalous-behaviour detection procedures (clauses 6.6.2.2 and 6.6.2.3), where the NWDAF derives analytics using inputs collected jointly from OAM and NRF (plus the NFs themselves).

questions.question: Which procedures put the MME and the SMLC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MME and the E-SMLC exchange messages directly in TS 23.271's UE Assisted and UE Based Positioning and Assistance Delivery procedure (clause 9.3a.1), where the E-SMLC sends Downlink Positioning Information to the MME and receives Uplink Positioning Information back; in the Delivery of Ciphering Keys for Broadcast Assistance Data procedure (clause 9.3a.5), where the E-SMLC sends ciphering-key data to the MME; and in TS 36.305's NI-LR/MT-LR service support procedure (clause 7.5.1), where the MME sends a location request to the E-SMLC and receives a location response.

questions.question: For edge application context relocation, which procedures put the EAS, the ECS and the EES in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The EAS, the ECS and the EES co-appear in the EES registration procedure (TS 23.558 clause 8.4.4.2.2), where the ECS stores EES registration information and associates the EES with other EESs sharing the same EAS bundle information, and in the dynamic EAS instantiation procedure (TS 23.700-98 clause 7.33.2.2), where the EES registers with the ECS and its profile lists the EAS(s) it is allowed to instantiate.

questions.question: In mission-critical service session establishment, which procedures put the MC service server and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MC service server sends resource requests directly to the PCRF over Rx in TS 23.280's session establishment procedures (clauses 10.11.2a.2 and 10.11.6.2), where the MC service server requests and later releases media-plane resources with the PCRF, and in TS 23.783's proposed EPS-related update to the same procedure (clause 6.3.1.2.10), which carries the identical MC service server-to-PCRF resource request and release steps.

questions.question: For unmanned aircraft USS change, which procedures put the UAE, the UAS and the USS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The UAE (client or server), the UAS application specific server and the USS interact together in the UAE client assisted change of USS procedure (TS 23.255 clause 7.6.2.4), where the UAE client initiates a change of USS on behalf of the USS and notifies the UAS application specific server; the UAE layer assisted change of USS procedure (TS 23.700-55 clause 7.3.2.4), where the UAE server receives a USS change request from the UAS application specific server; and the USS mapping/tracking procedure (clause 7.4.2.2), where the UAE server notifies the UAS application specific server of a completed USS change.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PEGC and the PEMC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PEGC and the PEMC interact directly in TS 23.700-78's PEGC relocation procedure (clause 7.16.2.2.1), where the outgoing PEGC requests the PEMC to discover a new gateway and the PEMC in turn responds to and configures the new PEGC, and in TS 23.700-88's Registration of PEMC and PINMF procedure (clause 6.8.2.1.1), where a PEMC located behind a PEGC sends its Registration Request to the PINMF via the PEGC and the PEGC forwards the corresponding transfer messages.

questions.question: During NR/LTE handover execution, which procedures put the RACH configuration and the C-RNTI (RNTI) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five handover test-sequence procedures include a step that reconfigures the RACH procedure on a dedicated or C-RNTI basis: the LTE intra-cell handover sequence in TS 36.523-3 clause 7.16.2 ("Sequence of intra-cell handover"), and four NR handover sequences in TS 38.523-3 - clause 7.3.5.3.1 (intra-NR inter-cell handover), 7.3.5.3.2 (intra-NR intra-cell handover), 7.3.5.3.4 (intra-NR inter-cell CA handover) and 7.3.5.5.3 (NR-DC intra-PCell handover / intra-cell PSCell change). In each, the target cell step reads "Configure RACH procedure either dedicated or C-RNTI based", tying RACH re-configuration directly to whether a new C-RNTI is assigned.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SCC AS and the SDP (offer/answer) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures show the SCC AS directly handling an SDP offer or answer within a step: the Collaborative Session establishment at originating IMS session setup (TS 23.237 clause 6a.2.3), where the SCC AS sends responses carrying the SDP answer of Media-A/Media-B to UE-1/UE-2; the terminating-side counterpart (TS 23.237 clause 6a.2.4), where the SCC AS again forwards SDP answers for Media-A and Media-B; and the SCC AS procedures for PS to CS access transfer of an additional call (TS 24.237 clause 12.3.4.4), where the SCC AS populates SIP responses with the SDP answer/offer exchanged during SRVCC access transfer.

questions.question: For ICS (IMS Centralized Services) call handling, which procedures put the CS domain and the SCC AS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures put the CS domain and the SCC AS in the same step: the Session Release procedure for Gm and I1 (TS 23.292 clause 7.7.1.2), where the SCC AS initiates release of the CS Bearer Control Signalling Path and the MSC Server releases the CS Session with the ICS UE; the CS UE origination signalling flow via an MSC Server enhanced for ICS (TS 24.292 clause A.4.4), where the CS UE's SETUP/CONNECT messages are relayed through the MSC Server to the SCC AS over SIP; and the termination signalling flow to a CS UE (TS 24.292 clause A.5.1), where the MSC Server forwards CS UE signalling (SETUP, ALERTING, CONNECT) while the SCC AS handles the corresponding SIP INVITE/response exchange.

questions.question: In 5G edge computing, which procedures put the EAS and the EEC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures put the EAS and the EEC in the same step: the common-EAS discovery procedure for EECs connected to the same EES (TS 23.700-98 clause 7.31.2.3), where EEC-1/EEC-3 use EDN configuration information to establish a connection to the common EAS discovered via EES; the EAS instantiation-on-demand procedure (TS 23.700-98 clause 7.33.2.2), where the EEC sends an EAS selection request identifying the selected (not-yet-instantiated) EAS and later the AC accesses that EAS; and the 5GMS client-driven Edge Processing procedure (TS 26.501 clause 8.1), where the EEC discovers, requests and selects a "5GMS AS" EAS instance and registers with the serving EES.

questions.question: For mission-critical location reporting, which procedures put the LMC and the LMS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures put the location management client (LMC) and location management server (LMS) directly in the same step: the on-demand report location history procedure (TS 23.280 clause 10.9.3.9.2.1), where the LMS requests stored location information and the LMC responds with location history reports; the status location history reporting procedure (TS 23.280 clause 10.9.3.9.3.1), where the LMC reports status to the LMS unsolicited; the on-demand status location history reporting procedure (TS 23.280 clause 10.9.3.9.3.2), where the LMS requests status and the LMC reports it; the cancel location history reporting procedure (TS 23.280 clause 10.9.3.9.4.2), where the LMS requests cancellation and the LMC confirms it; and the location-QoS-based location source/positioning method selection procedure with FLF (TS 23.700-96 clause 7.7.1.1), where the LMS (enhanced with FLF) queries and fuses location information for the target LMC.

questions.question: I need every place where the MBS session, the NRM and the VAL server are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures in TS 23.434 clause 14.3 put the MBS session, the NRM (server/client) and the VAL server in the same step: the pre-created MBS session and announcement procedure (14.3.4A.2.2), where the VAL server requests multicast/broadcast resources from the NRM server which then creates and announces the MBS session to NRM clients; the dynamic MBS session procedure (14.3.4A.2.3), which follows the same VAL-server-to-NRM-server resource-request and announcement pattern for a dynamically created session; the multicast MBS session activation procedure (14.3.4A.5.2), where the VAL server invokes activation via the NRM server which triggers 5GC to activate the session; the multicast MBS session de-activation procedure (14.3.4A.5.3), the mirrored deactivation flow; and the application-level control signalling procedure (14.3.4A.7.2), where the VAL server creates an MBS session via the NRM for control messages, and the NRM client/server pass the session ID to enable monitoring.

questions.question: For CS Fallback call handling, which procedures put the CS domain, CSFB, the MME and the MSC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.272 put the CS domain, CSFB, the MME and the MSC together in a single step: the Mobile Originating call in Active Mode with PS HO supported (clause 6.2), where the MME sends an MO CSFB indication via SGs to the MSC to mark the CM Service Request as due to CSFB via a CS MO call; the Mobile Terminating call in Active Mode with PS HO supported (clause 7.3), where, upon receiving an Extended Service Request reject for mobile terminating CS fallback, the MME sends a Paging Reject to the MSC to stop CS paging and end the CSFB procedure; and the MT-LR procedure while the UE is in an IMS VoIP session (clause 8.3.2.2), which has the identical MME-sends-Paging-Reject-to-MSC step when the UE rejects mobile terminating CS Fallback.

questions.question: Which procedures put the gNB-CU-CP and the gNB-CU-UP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three F1/E1-related procedures in TS 38.401 put the gNB-CU-CP and gNB-CU-UP directly in the same step: inter-gNB-CU mobility between MBS-supporting nodes (clause 8.15.2.1), a long sequence of MC BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST/RESPONSE exchanges between the source/target gNB-CU-CP and gNB-CU-UP to hand over multicast bearer contexts; the gNB-CU-CP initiated bearer context release (clause 8.9.3.1), where the gNB-CU-CP sends a BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST and the gNB-CU-UP responds with the PDCP UL/DL status; and the RRC Connected to RRC Inactive transition (clause 8.9.6.1), where the gNB-CU-CP and gNB-CU-UP exchange BEARER CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION messages to move the UE into RRC-inactive state.

questions.question: In 5G core service-based operations, which procedures put the NRF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.700-62 put the NRF and the UPF directly in the same step: the UPF Event Exposure service update procedure (clause 6.1.2.2), where the UPF sends an Nnrf_NFManagement_NFUpdate request and the NRF updates the UPF's NF profile and acknowledges; the UPF Event Exposure service deregistration procedure (clause 6.1.2.3), where the UPF informs the NRF of its unavailability via Nnrf_NFManagement_NFDeregister and the NRF marks the UPF unavailable; and the general UPF event exposure procedures (clause 6.5.3), where UPF(s) register their event exposure service onto the NRF and an event consumer discovers the UPF's exposure service via Nnrf_NFDiscovery_Request.

questions.question: For QoS flow handling in NR, which procedures put the QFI and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 38.300 Annex A put the QFI and the UPF in the same step: the new QoS flow with Reflective QoS (RQoS) procedure (A.2), where the gNB receives a downlink packet carrying a new QFI from the UPF and maps it onto a DRB; the new QoS flow with explicit RRC signalling procedure (A.3), which has the identical "gNB receives a downlink packet with a new QFI from UPF" step before reconfiguring the DRB mapping via RRC; and the UE-initiated uplink QoS flow procedure (A.6), where the gNB forwards uplink packets to the UPF including the corresponding QFI.

questions.question: In RAT-frequency selection priority handling across 5GS/EPS, which procedures put the PCF and the RFSP index in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.700-89 put the PCF and the RFSP index in the same step: the general RFSP-in-use provisioning procedure (clause 6.4.2), where the PCF determines a change of authorized RFSP index (e.g. to redirect the UE from 5G to 4G priority) and provisions it via AM Policy Modification, propagating through AMF/UDM/HSS/MME to the RAN; the procedure for triggering a UE to move from 5G to 4G (clause 6.9.2.1), where the PCF updates the RFSP index for the UE and provides the new value to the AMF; and the mirrored procedure for triggering a UE from 4G to 5G (clause 6.9.2.2), where the PCF again decides and updates the RFSP index, propagated to the MME/eNB.

questions.question: For IoT device monitoring via SCEF, which procedures put the SCEF and the SCS/AS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures in TS 23.682 put the SCEF and the SCS/AS directly in the same step: changing the chargeable party during a session (clause 5.12.2), where the SCS/AS sends a Change chargeable party request to the SCEF and the SCEF responds with the result; the RACS information provisioning procedure via SCEF (clause 5.19.2), where the SCS/AS sends a Radio Capability Entry Request to the SCEF, which relays it to the UCMF and returns the response; the request of monitoring event reporting procedure (clause 5.6.4.1), where the SCS/AS sends a Monitoring Request to the SCEF and receives a Monitoring Response; the group-monitoring variant of that procedure (clause 5.6.4.1a), where the SCEF aggregates PCRF responses and exchanges Monitoring Indication/Response messages with the SCS/AS; and the reporting of monitoring events from the PCRF (clause 5.6.5), where the SCEF forwards a Monitoring Indication to the SCS/AS and receives an acknowledgement.

questions.question: In GERAN PS handover signalling, which procedures put the BSS, the SGSN and the TLLI parameter in the same step (i.e. the BSS and the SGSN exchange a message that carries the TLLI)?
questions.reference_answer: Three PS handover procedures in TS 43.129 have a step where the BSS and the SGSN exchange a TLLI-bearing message directly: (1) clause 5.4.2 'Inter-SGSN HO Reject', where the old SGSN sends a PS Handover Required Negative Acknowledge (Old TLLI, Cause, ...) message to the source BSS; (2) clause 5.7.2.1.1 'Initial Access Failure in the Target Cell during PS handover', where the source BSS sends a PS Handover Cancel (TLLI, Cause = MS Back on old Channel, ...) PDU to the old SGSN; (3) clause 5.8.1.1 'Intra SGSN PS Handover, Preparation phase', where the source BSS sends a PS Handover Required (Old TLLI, Cause, ...) message to the SGSN. In each case the TLLI (or Old TLLI) is the mobile identity carried directly between the BSS and the SGSN in the handover signalling.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GGSN and the SGSN in the same step for MBMS bearer service handling?
questions.reference_answer: Three MBMS procedures in TS 23.246 have a step where the GGSN and the SGSN directly exchange a message: (1) clause 8.6.1 'BM-SC initiated MBMS De-Registration Procedure', where the GGSN sends an MBMS De-Registration Request to all SGSNs in its list of downstream nodes and each SGSN returns an MBMS De-registration Response to the GGSN; (2) clause 8.7 'MBMS Multicast Service Deactivation', where the GGSN sends an MBMS UE Context Deactivation Request to the SGSN and the SGSN acknowledges with an MBMS UE Context Deactivation Response, and separately the SGSN sends an MBMS De-Registration Request to the GGSN when it has no more interested users; (3) clause 8.8.3 'BM-SC initiated Session Update for GERAN and UTRAN for MBMS Broadcast service', where the GGSN sends an MBMS Session Start/Stop/Update Request directly to the relevant SGSNs based on the updated list of downstream nodes.

questions.question: In mission-critical interworking with a Land Mobile Radio system, which procedures put the IWF and the LMR user in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.283 have a step where the IWF and the LMR user directly interact: (1) clause 10.13.3.2 'Group call with talker ID update initiated by an LMR user on an interworking group defined in the LMR system', where the IWF receives knowledge of the LMR user's talker ID and updates the MCPTT server accordingly; (2) clause 10.5.10 'Floor control in private call controlled by the MCPTT system', where the floor is granted to the LMR user via the IWF, and voice media flows from the LMR user via the IWF to the MCPTT server; (3) clause 10.5.9 'Floor control in private call controlled by the LMR system', where media flows from the LMR user to the IWF, and the IWF indicates that the floor has been taken by or is idle for the LMR user. In all three, the IWF is the node that directly carries the LMR user's floor/media state into the MCPTT system.

questions.question: For SRVCC access transfer signalling flows, which procedures put the ATCF and the MSC server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three SRVCC signalling-flow procedures in TS 24.237 Annex A have steps where the ATCF and the MSC server exchange SIP messages directly: (1) clause A.18.4 'Session transfer for originating call is in alerting phase using PS to CS SRVCC procedure with ATCF: PS to CS', with multiple direct SIP exchanges between the MSC server and the ATCF (e.g. SIP INVITE from MSC server to ATCF, SIP 200 OK / PRACK / ACK / INFO exchanged in both directions); (2) clause A.18.6 'Signalling flows for PS to CS Access Transfer... with ATCF and session traverses IBCF', where the MSC server sends a SIP INVITE to the ATCF and the ATCF returns a SIP 200 OK to the MSC server; (3) clause A.20.3 'Signalling flows for CS to PS Access Transfer without CS media anchored in ATGW', where the MSC server sends SIP INFO/INVITE requests to the ATCF and the ATCF acknowledges with SIP 200 OK responses back to the MSC server, coordinating the CS-to-PS access transfer.

questions.question: In FLUS/NBMP live-uplink-streaming call flows, which procedures put the EA (Enabling Application) and the UA (UE Application) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three call-flow mappings in TS 26.939 clause 8.4 have a step where the UA and the EA directly interact: (1) clause 8.4.2.4.1, where the UE Application (UA) makes a request through F8 to the Enabling Application (EA) to start a live session, and the EA later responds to the UA with Control Sink and Media Sink information; (2) clause 8.4.3.4.1, with the same UA-to-EA live-session request and the EA responding to the UA with FLUS Control Sink and Media Sink information after MPE capability discovery; (3) clause 8.4.4.3 'Interfaces', again showing the UA making the F8 request to the EA to start a live session and the EA responding to the UA with the FLUS Sink information. In all three, F8 is the interface over which the UA and EA exchange these session-start/response messages.

questions.question: For Edge Configuration Server (ECS) registration and discovery, which procedures put the ECS and the ECS registration/discovery function (ECS-ER) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.558 clause 8.17.2 have a step where the ECS and the ECS-ER directly exchange a request/response: (1) clause 8.17.2.2.2 'ECS registration', where the ECS sends an ECS registration request to the ECS-ER and the ECS-ER returns an ECS registration response; (2) clause 8.17.2.2.3 'ECS registration update', where the ECS sends an ECS registration update request to the ECS-ER and the ECS-ER returns an ECS registration update response; (3) clause 8.17.2.3.2 'Request-response model' (ECS discovery), where the ECS sends an ECS discovery request to the ECS-ER, which authorizes and processes it and returns an ECS discovery response listing partner ECS(s).

questions.question: Which procedures put the ME and the USIM in the same step, i.e. where the ME and the USIM directly exchange information for false-base-station protection?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 33.809 clause 6.9.2 have a step where the ME and the USIM directly interact: (1) clause 6.9.2.2.1 'Protection Key Agreement (PKA) and Protection Key Transfer (PKT) procedure', where the ME sends the NONCE to the USIM to initiate key derivation and the USIM returns an indication to the ME once CKp has been generated; (2) clause 6.9.2.3.1 'Security procedure for broadcast messages', where the ME sends the EKRBS and <bsGKI,bsGNI> (and HASHMS or the concatenated DL_ARFCN+message) to the USIM, and the USIM decrypts EKRBS, computes XMAC-I and returns it to the ME for comparison against MAC-I; (3) clause 6.9.2.3.2 'Security procedure for unicast messages', where the ME again sends EKRBS, <bsGKI,bsGNI>, sensitive information and NONCE to the USIM, and the USIM derives Ke and returns it to the ME so the ME can generate the keystream and encrypt the sensitive information.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AF and the PC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three PCC signalling-flow procedures in TS 29.201 annex A.7 put the AF and the PC (Protocol Converter) in the same step, since the PC always terminates the HTTP side towards the AF and converts it to/from Diameter towards the PCRF: (1) Traffic plane event reporting (A.7.1) - the PC converts the PCRF's Diameter RAR into an HTTP PUT, and the AF answers with HTTP 200 OK that the PC converts back to a Diameter RAA; (2) Service data flow deactivation when all service data flows are affected (A.7.2) - the PC forwards the PCRF's Diameter ASR as an HTTP PUT to the AF, and the AF's HTTP 200 OK is converted by the PC into a Diameter ASA; (3) IP-CAN Session Termination (A.7.3) - the same ASR/HTTP-PUT and AF 200-OK/ASA exchange occurs via the PC when the IP-CAN session is terminated.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ECS and the EES in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures directly involve the EES sending a request to the ECS (or the ECS acting on it) in the same step: (1) EES registration (TS 23.558 clause 8.4.4.2.2) - the EES sends an EES registration request to the ECS, which verifies credentials and responds; (2) EES registration update (8.4.4.2.3) - the EES sends an update request, the ECS updates the stored registration; (3) EES de-registration (8.4.4.2.4) - the EES sends a de-registration request, the ECS removes the registration; (4) the client-driven 5GMS Edge Processing management procedure (TS 26.501 clause 8.1), whose 'EES Registration with ECS' step has the EES register directly with the ECS that is in authority over the target EDN; (5) the EES registering to ECS using the Eecs_EESRegistration_Request operation (TS 29.558 clause 6.2.2.2.2), where the ECS verifies the EES identity/authorization and creates the registration resource.

questions.question: In dynamic UE location based group management for UAV proximity services, which procedures place the UAE server and the LMS in the same step handling the UAV's location?
questions.reference_answer: Two near-identical 'Management of dynamic UE location based group' procedures put the UAE server, the LMS, and the UAV together in one step: TS 23.255 clause 7.8.2.2 and TS 23.700-55 clause 7.7.2.3.3. In both, UAE server 1 uses its associated LMS 1 to obtain the dynamic UE list and location information in the proximity area of the host UAV, by providing the application-defined proximity range and the UE location of the host UAV; UAE server 1 also queries other UAE servers 2..N, each of which similarly obtains UE information for the same UAV from its own corresponding LMS.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MN and the SN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two dual-connectivity procedures put the Master Node (MN) and the Secondary Node (SN) in the same step directly exchanging messages: (1) the security procedure for UE access to a target PSCell or SN (TS 33.501 clause 6.10.2.4.4) - the MN sends an SN Addition/Modification Request over Xn-C to each candidate target SN with the derived KSN keys, and the SN responds with an SN Addition/Modification Acknowledge indicating available resources and chosen algorithms; later the MN forwards the SN Reconfiguration Complete to the target SN; (2) the EN-DC handover procedure (TS 37.340 clause 10.9.1) - the target MN sends an SgNB Addition Request to the target SN, which replies with an SgNB Addition Request Acknowledge, and the target MN subsequently informs the target SN when the RRC reconfiguration succeeds.

questions.question: Which procedures put the LMF and the NRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two positioning procedures put the LMF and the NRF in the same step for discovering other LMFs: (1) Positioning of a target UE (TS 23.273 clause 6.17.4) - the serving LMF may invoke an Nnrf_NFDiscovery Request to an NRF, including a PRU indication and area, and the NRF selects other PRU-serving LMFs and returns their profiles to the serving LMF in an Nnrf_NFDiscovery Response; (2) PRU Utilization (TS 23.700-71 clause 6.16.3.2) - if the LMF needs PRU information it invokes an Nnrf_NFDiscovery Request to the NRF (including NF type=LMF, cell ID/list, PRU indication), and the NRF returns a response with LMF ID and PRU information.

questions.question: I need every place where the AC and the EEC are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Seven edge-enabler procedures put the Application Client (AC) and the Edge Enabler Client (EEC) directly in the same step, each following an AC-sends-request / EEC-validates-and-responds pattern: (1) ACR trigger request (TS 23.558 clause 8.14.2.4) - the AC sends an ACR trigger request, the EEC validates credentials and responds; (2) EEC services subscription (8.14.2.5.2) - the AC sends a subscription request, the EEC creates the subscription and responds; (3) EEC services subscription update (8.14.2.5.4) - same pattern for updates; (4) AC registration (8.14.2.2.2) - the AC sends an AC registration request, the EEC registers it and responds; (5) ACR request (TS 23.700-98 clause 7.34.2.2.4) - equivalent ACR request/response between AC and EEC; (6) AC subscription request (7.34.2.2.5) - equivalent subscription request/response; (7) AC registration request (7.34.2.2.2) - equivalent registration request/response. In all seven, the EEC checks the AC's security credentials before acting.

questions.question: For a UDR notifying an application front end of a data change, which procedures put the FE and the UDR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two UDC procedures put the Front End (FE) and the UDR directly in the same step: (1) the Notification procedure (TS 23.335 clause 5.8.1) - once notification conditions are met, the UDR selects an available FE, fetches the data the FE needs, sends it a notification request, and the FE returns a success/failure response, with the UDR repeating the process with a different FE on failure; (2) the LDAP transaction flow for UDC (TS 29.335 annex B.2) - the FE issues a Start Transaction Request to the UDR, the UDR checks whether the transaction is allowed and returns a transaction identity, the FE then issues operations and an End Transaction Request, and the UDR commits or rolls back the updates and returns the result to the FE.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AAA server and the HSS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the AAA server and the HSS act together. In TS 29.273 Annex E.2 (Successful call flow, untrusted non-3GPP access via ePDG), the 3GPP AAA Server retrieves authentication vectors for the UE directly from the HSS, and later downloads the user's subscription information from the HSS after successful authentication. In TS 43.902 clause 5.1.1.3.7 (EGAN Registration and subscriber management in PS Domain, HSS purge procedure), the HSS initiates termination of a registration by sending a Registration-Termination-Request to the AAA server, which deletes the subscriber information and answers with a Registration-Termination-Answer.

questions.question: For BM-SC initiated MBMS de-registration and UE context modification, which procedures put the BM-SC and the GGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures place the BM-SC and the GGSN in the same step. In TS 23.246 clause 8.6.1 (BM-SC initiated MBMS De-Registration Procedure), the BM-SC sends a De-Registration Request to all GGSNs on the corresponding MBMS Bearer Context's list of downstream nodes, and each GGSN returns a De-Registration Response and releases the affected MBMS UE contexts. In TS 29.061 clause 17.5.10 (MBMS UE Context Modification Procedure), the GGSN sends updated MBMS UE Context parameters (RAI, CGI/SAI) to the BM-SC in an AAR message, and the BM-SC updates its context fields and responds with an AAA message.

questions.question: For PFD retrieval and management, which procedures put the NEF (PFDF) and the UDR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the NEF, acting as PFDF, and the UDR act together. In TS 23.502 clause 4.18.3.1 (PFD Retrieval by the SMF), the NEF(PFDF) invokes Nudr_DM_Query towards the UDR to retrieve PFDs for an Application Identifier when they are not already cached, and the UDR replies with a Nudr_DM_Query response containing the PFD(s). In TS 23.700-81 clause 6.9.4 (Procedures, PFD analytics), the NEF(PFDF) fetches the currently stored PFD information from the UDR, and later invokes Nudr_DM_Create/Update/Delete on the UDR to create, update or delete PFD information for an application ID.

questions.question: Which procedures put the LM server (LMS) and the VAL server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures place the LM server and the VAL server in the same step. In TS 23.434 clause 9.3.11.2 (Monitoring Location Deviation procedure), the VAL server sends a Monitor Location Subscription Request to the LM server, and the LM server later notifies the VAL server (Notify Presence, Notify Absence, or Notify Mismatch Location) once it evaluates the VAL UE's location against the requested area of interest. In TS 23.700-96 clause 7.5.1.2 (fused location procedure), the LMS receives a location request from the VAL server (as fused location service consumer) and, once the fused location estimate is calculated, the LMS sends the fused location report to the VAL server.

questions.question: I need every place where the SEALDD server and the VAL server are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the SEALDD server and the VAL server act together. In TS 23.433 clause 9.9.2.1 (SEALDD enabled data transmission quality guarantee by switching SEALDD server), the VAL server sends a Sdd_RegularTransmission request to the SEALDD server, which performs an authorization check and, if successful, sends a response back to the VAL server. In TS 23.700-34 clause 6.15.2.2 (SEALDD traffic forwarding procedure), the SEALDD server establishes a connection with the VAL server, maps application traffic from the VAL server into SEALDD traffic sent through the UPF, and sends recovered application traffic back to the VAL server.

questions.question: For QoS monitoring exposure and multi-member AF sessions, which procedures put the NEF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures place the NEF and the UPF in the same step. In TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.13.2 (Procedures for Creating a Multi-member AF session with required QoS), when direct event notification is requested, the QoS Monitoring events are reported by the UPF(s) directly to the NEF using the Nupf_EventExposure service. In TS 23.700-46 clause 6.2.3 (DetNet capability reporting procedure), the UPF collects DetNet-related network information and may report the identification and link of adjacent DetNet nodes directly to the NEF via the network exposure service, upon indication of direct notification from the NEF.

questions.question: For PIN element registration and management, which procedures put the PEMC and the PIN server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the PEMC and the PIN server act together. In TS 23.542 clause 8.5.8.2.1 (PIN client requests to join into a PIN), after a new PIN client joins, the PEMC sends a PIN status notify message to the PIN server containing the details of the new PIN client (including PIN client ID and GPSI). In TS 23.700-78 clause 7.13.2.2 (Procedures of PEMC registration), the PEMC sends a Registration Request (including GPSI) to the PIN server, and the PIN server checks the PEMC's subscription and role with the 5GS before responding to the PEMC with an allocated PEMC ID or a failure cause.

questions.question: In network slice communication service management, which procedures put the EGMF and the NSCE server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the NSCE server invokes network-slice management services exposed by the EGMF. In TS 23.435 clause 9.12.2.1.2 (Slice related Communication Service Reconfiguration), after receiving a reconfiguration request from the VAL server, the NSCE server initiates the Slice Service update procedure by using the network slice modification management service exposed by the EGMF (as defined in TS 28.531 by SA5). In TS 23.700-99 clause 6.19.1.2 (Slice requirements alignment capability), when the NSCE server decides the slice requirements need updating, it performs the network slice modification operation by using the modifyMOIAttributes operation of the management service exposed by the EGMF.

questions.question: For UAV command-and-control mode management and status subscription, which procedures put the UAE server and the UAS application specific server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Six procedures have a step where the UAE server and the UAS Application Specific Server act together. In TS 23.255 clause 7.4.2.1 (Management of C2 mode selection/switching capability), the UAS application specific server sends a C2 operation mode management request to the UAE server, and the UAE server responds and then notifies the UAS application specific server once the C2 mode configuration completes. In TS 23.255 clause 7.5.2.2 (Subscription for real-time UAV status information), the UAS application specific server sends a subscription request to the UAE server, which stores it and sends a subscription response back. In TS 23.255 clause 7.5.2.4 (Unsubscription for real-time UAV status information), the UAS application specific server sends an unsubscribe request to the UAE server, which cancels the subscription and responds. In TS 23.255 clause 7.8.2.1 (Subscription for host UAV dynamic information), the UAS Application Specific Server sends a subscribe request to the UAE server, which stores the subscription and responds. In TS 23.255 clause 7.8.2.5 (Unsubscription for host UAV dynamic information), the UAS Application Specific Server sends an unsubscribe request to the UAE server, which removes the subscription and responds. In TS 23.700-55 clause 7.6.2.2 (Registration of DAA capability), the UAE server performs authentication and authorization of a registration request by interacting with the UAS application specific server.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF and the NRM server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.434 clause 14.3 place the NRM server and the NEF in the same step, both around QoS monitoring subscription lifecycle management: the QoS monitoring unsubscribe procedure (clause 14.3.3.4.3.2), where after the VAL server requests unsubscription, the NRM server interacts with the NEF to terminate the related QoS monitoring subscription; and the QoS monitoring subscription update procedure (clause 14.3.3.4.5.2), where the NRM server interacts with the NEF to update the relevant QoS monitoring subscription parameters and reporting frequency after the VAL server's update request.

questions.question: In 5G NR split architecture, which procedures put the gNB-CU, the gNB-DU and the gNB-CU-UP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two TS 38.401 procedures involve the gNB-CU, gNB-DU and gNB-CU-UP together in a single step. In the RRC Inactive to other states transition (clause 8.6.2), the gNB-CU shall trigger UE Context Setup between gNB-CU and gNB-DU, and the security indication of each PDU session is communicated to the gNB-CU-UP as part of that same context handling. In the trace activation/deactivation over F1 and E1 procedure (clause 8.9.7), the gNB-CU-CP initiates the Trace Start / Deactivate Trace procedure by sending the TRACE START / DEACTIVATE TRACE message to the gNB-DU, the gNB-CU-UP, or both, which then stop or start the requested trace session.

questions.question: Where do the WLAN and the WT (WLAN Termination) act together in the same step of a procedure?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 36.300 LTE-WLAN Aggregation (LWA), the WT and WLAN resources appear together in the same step in both the WT Addition procedure (clause 22A.1.7.1) and the WT Release procedure (clause 22A.1.7.3). In WT Addition, the eNB sends the WT Addition Request message asking the WT to allocate WLAN resources for specific E-RABs, and the WT responds whether it can admit the full or partial WLAN resource request. In WT Release, the WT sends the WT Release Required message to the eNB, and the WT then initiates the release of all allocated WLAN resources.

questions.question: For an edge application client managing its automatic client relocation, which procedures place the EEC, the AC and the EDGE-5 interface in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 23.700-98, two Automatic Client Relocation (ACR) modification procedures put the EEC, the AC, and the EDGE-5 interface together in the same step: the EEC-based ACR modification procedure (clause 7.6.2.1.1) and the EES-based modification procedure (clause 7.6.2.1.2). In both, once the ACR modification result is available, the EEC may optionally provide a notification to the AC over the EDGE-5 interface to inform it of the ACR modification result.

questions.question: Which procedures put the gNB-CU-CP and the gNB-CU-UP (CU and UP) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.401 clause 8.9.6 describes two related transitions where the gNB-CU-CP and the gNB-CU-UP repeatedly interact in the same step: the RRC Connected to RRC Inactive transition (8.9.6.1), where the gNB-CU-CP sends the BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST and BEARER CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST messages to the gNB-CU-UP and receives its BEARER CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE / MODIFICATION RESPONSE; and the RRC Inactive to other states transition (8.9.6.2), where the gNB-CU-CP sends a BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST with an RRC Resume indication to the gNB-CU-UP, which responds with the BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE.

questions.question: In UAV detect-and-avoid support, which procedures place the UAE (server/client) and the UAS application specific server in the same step, exchanging DAA support information?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-98/700-55 clause 7.6.2.4 has two DAA (Detect-And-Avoid) support procedures where the UAE and the UAS application specific server exchange DAA information in the same step: the client-initiated DAA support procedure (7.6.2.4.1), where the UAE server sends the DAA support information to the UAS application specific server after recording the DAA event and client location; and the server-initiated DAA support procedure (7.6.2.4.2), where the UAS application specific server sends DAA support information (e.g. other UAVs in proximity) to the UAE server, which the UAE server verifies and forwards to the UAE client.

questions.question: For a 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay discovery, which procedures put the NSSAI and the RSC (Relay Service Code) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay discovery procedures in TS 23.304 clause 6.3.2.3 tie the RSC to the NSSAI in the same step: Model A discovery (6.3.2.3.2), where a Layer-3 UE-to-Network Relay shall only include an RSC in its Discovery Announcement message when the S-NSSAI associated with that RSC belongs to its Allowed NSSAI; and Model B discovery (6.3.2.3.3), where the Relay shall only respond to a matching RSC in the Discovery Solicitation when the S-NSSAI associated with that RSC belongs to its Allowed NSSAI.

questions.question: I need every place where the PIN server, the PEMC and the PEGC are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-78 has two Personal IoT Network (PIN) procedures where the PIN server, PEMC and PEGC act together in the same step: the PIN modification triggered by a PEGC event (clause 7.3.2.3.2), where the PIN server or PEMC subscribes to and is notified of PEGC mobility/status events, decides to modify the PIN, and after modification the PIN server delivers access control information to the new PEGC; and the PIN Profile retrieval procedure (clause 7.3.2.4), where the PEMC sends a PIN Profile Query request to the PIN server, which determines whether that PEMC is an authorized manager (having received its PEMC role from the PIN server) and responds with the profile, including PEGC information.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MSA and the MSISDN in the same step for a mobile-originated call?
questions.reference_answer: Both mobile number portability call-routing procedures in TS 23.066 Annex C put the MSA and the MSISDN in the same first step, 'MSA originates a call to MSISDN': direct routeing when the originating network equals the subscription network (clause C.3.2), where the MNP_SRF/MATF identifies the MSISDN as ported and re-routes to the correct HLR; and direct routeing when the originating network differs from the subscription network (clause C.3.3), where the MNP_SRF/MATF checks whether the MSISDN is known to be ported and returns routeing information accordingly.

questions.question: For an MCPTT user initiating a private call to an LMR party, which procedures place the LMR party, the MCPTT client/server and the SDP offer in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.283 clause 10.4 has two MCPTT-to-LMR private call setup procedures where the MCPTT client, the called LMR party and the SDP offer appear in the same initiating step: automatic commencement mode (10.4.2.1) and manual commencement mode (10.4.3.1). In both, the MCPTT client sends an MCPTT private call request toward the MCPTT server containing the MCPTT IDs for the calling MCPTT party and the called LMR party plus an SDP offer with one or more media types, which the MCPTT server then forwards toward the IWF for the LMR interworking.

questions.question: For a mobile-originated call to a possibly-ported number, which procedures put the GMSCA, the RN and the MSISDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two number-portability call-routing procedures in TS 23.066 Annex C put GMSCA, RN and MSISDN together in the same step: (1) 'Mobile Originated Call to a Ported or not known to be Ported Number - Originating Network != Subscription Network - Direct Routeing' (clause C.3.3), and (2) 'Call to a Ported Number - Indirect Routeing' (clause C.3.4). In both, GMSCA uses the (RN +) MSISDN to route the call onward to GMSCB in the subscription network, and whether the RN is carried in the IAM depends on the interconnect agreement.

questions.question: Which procedures put the HLRB, the MATF and the MSISDN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two number-portability call procedures in TS 23.066 Annex C put HLRB, MNP_SRF/MATF and MSISDN together in one step: 'Call to a Non-Ported Number or Number Ported into the Network' (clause C.3.1) and 'Call to a Ported Number - Indirect Routeing with Reference to Subscription Network' (clause C.3.5). In both, when the MNP_SRF/MATF receives the message it analyses the MSISDN in the CdPA and, if the number is (or is not) ported, replaces the CdPA with an HLRB address so the message is routed to HLRB.

questions.question: For uncrewed aerial system operation with multiple USSs, which procedures put the UAE, the UAS and the USS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two Multi-USS procedures in TS 23.700-55 put the UAE (server/client), the UAS application specific server and the USS together in one step: 'UAE layer assisted change of USS' (clause 7.3.2.4), where the UAE server receives a USS change request from the UAS application specific server naming the new serving USS, and the general Multi-USS management/change procedure (clause 7.4.2.2), where the UAE server exchanges USS-change triggers and notifications with the UAS application specific server about a USS.

questions.question: For an application requesting network-based media processing, which procedures put the EA and the MPE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two NBMP/FLUS deployment call flows in TS 26.939 put the Application (EA) and the Media Processing Entity (MPE) in the same step: the 'Mapping call flow to the standard APIs' flow (clause 8.4.3.4.1), where the EA requests MPE's capabilities and the MPE provides them back to the EA (supported by NBMP), and the 'Call flow' of clause 8.4.6.2, where the NBMP Client instantiates the workflow in the assigned MPE and the EA is involved in that same NBMP/FLUS session setup.

questions.question: For rendering AR media in an IMS communication session, which procedures put the AR device and the RTP channel in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two AR-media-rendering procedures in TS 23.700-87 put the AR device and the RTP channel together in one step: the general 'Network rendering process' (clause 6.9.2), where IMS sends the rendered AR media to the calling/called user's AR device over the normal audio/video RTP channel, and the detailed 'Terminal Rendering Process' (clause 6.9.2.1), where UE-A (the AR device) sends its rendered AR audio/video media to the peer through the RTP channel.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CS domain and GERAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two CS Fallback procedures in TS 23.272 put the CS domain and GERAN together in the same step: 'Mobile Originating call in Active Mode - No PS HO support' (clause 6.3), where the eNodeB can trigger RRC connection release with redirection to GERAN or UTRAN for the CS Fallback call, and 'Mobile Originated or Mobile terminated call rejected by the MME' (clause 6.6), where a Service Reject with a reason code results in the UE selecting GERAN or UTRAN CS Domain.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ADRF and the MTLF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two NWDAF analytics/ML procedures in TS 23.700-81 put the ADRF and the MTLF together in one step: 'MTLF-initiated accuracy monitoring' (clause 6.34.2.2), where the ADRF executes the subscribe-to-analytics operations requested by the MTLF and stores the notifications, and the general procedure of clause 6.67.2, where the MTLF retrieves from the ADRF the data belonging to the specified DataSetTag to train its ML model.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AVP, the CC, the CP function and the OCS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two PFCP/Sy pooled-quota example call flows in TS 29.244 Annex C put AVP, CC, the CP function and the OCS together in one step: 'Example Call Flow 1' (clause C.2.1.2.2) and 'Example Call Flow 2' (clause C.2.1.2.3). In both, upon the CP function's quota request for the rating groups, the OCS grants quota together with a G-S-U-Pool-Reference AVP whose CC-Unit-Type AVP and Unit-Value AVP define the credit-pool multiplier.

questions.question: For MCPTT interworking with an LMR system, which procedures put the FM radio system, the IWF, the LMR user and the MCPTT server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two talker-ID-update group-call procedures in TS 23.283 put the FM radio system, the IWF, the LMR user and the MCPTT server together in one step: the interworking-group-defined-in-MCPTT-system case (clause 10.13.3.1) and the interworking-group-defined-in-LMR-system case (clause 10.13.3.2). In both, the MCPTT server calls the affiliated users while a step notes the LMR user is on a legacy conventional FM radio system, so E2EE is not specified and transcoding is needed at the IWF.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the PLR and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two PMFP packet-loss-rate measurement procedures in TS 24.193 put the PLR measurement and the UPF together across their steps: the UE-initiated PLR measurement (clause 5.4.6.1), where the UE sends PMFP PLR count/report request messages to the UPF and the UPF counts and reports UL packets, and the network-initiated PLR measurement (clause 5.4.7.1), where the UPF sends the PMFP PLR count/report request messages to the UE for DL packets.

questions.question: For ProSe direct discovery, which procedures put the HPLMN and WLAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two ProSe direct discovery procedures in TS 23.303 put the ProSe Function in HPLMN and WLAN together in the same step: the restricted-discovery 'Announce Request (non-roaming)' procedure (clause 5.3.3.2A), where the UE announces using radio resources authorised by E-UTRAN or WLAN and, for 'on demand' announcing, waits on the ProSe Function in HPLMN, and the open-discovery 'Monitor request (roaming)' procedure (clause 5.3.3.5), where a UE intending to use WLAN-based PC5 for monitoring establishes a secure connection with the ProSe Function in HPLMN.

questions.question: For VRU protection-zone management, which procedures put the VAE server and the VASS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two VRU-related procedures in TS 23.700-64 put the VAE server and the VASS together in one step: 'Procedure on VAL server-triggered VRU zone creation' (clause 6.2.1.1), where the VAE server sends the VRU zone creation subscription response to the VASS and later alerts the VASS about UE1's expected entry into the zone, and the protection-zone procedure of clause 6.4.1.2, where the VAE server requests the VASS to authorize creation of a protection zone and the VASS responds with the authorization and zone configuration.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ADRF and ML models in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.288 clause 6.2B put the ADRF and ML Model handling in the same step: (1) "ML Model Storage in ADRF" (6.2B.5), where the NWDAF containing MTLF requests the ADRF to store or update an ML Model via Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest, and the ADRF stores/downloads and acknowledges; (2) "ML Model removal from ADRF" (6.2B.6), where the NWDAF containing MTLF requests the ADRF to delete a previously stored ML Model via Nadrf_MLModelManagement_Delete, and the ADRF deletes it and returns the result.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PRUK, RSC and SUCI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 33.740 combine PRUK, RSC and SUCI in the same step: (1) "Procedure for PC5 security establishment between the 5G ProSe Source UE and 5G ProSe UE-to-UE Relay" (6.3.2.1), where the Source UE sends a Direct Communication Request containing PRUK ID or SUCI plus the Relay Service Code (RSC), and the Relay sends a Key Request containing PRUK ID or SUCI, RSC and a freshness parameter to the 5GC; (2) the equivalent chained relay procedure (6.31.2.1, second relay hop), where the second relay likewise sends a Key Request with PRUK ID or SUCI and RSC to the 5GC.

questions.question: Which procedures put the IAB and the MBSR in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two solution procedures in TS 23.700-05 clause 6 involve the IAB-UE/IAB-DU and the MBSR (mobile IAB-node) acting together in the same step: (1) the MBSR mobility/handover procedure (6.13.3), where the IAB-UE of the MBSR registers with a serving AMF, establishes F1 with the m-CU, and is handed over between IAB donors while continuing to serve its own UEs; (2) the MBSR TAC/registration procedure (6.16.3), where the MBSR (as IAB-DU) sends an F1 SETUP REQUEST including a mobile IAB indication and the IAB-donor gNB configures and later updates its TAC.

questions.question: Which procedures put the HSS and a ULA message in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two interworking-function procedures in TS 29.305 have the HSS sending/receiving a ULA (Update Location Answer) in the same step: (1) the "Two IWFs Scenario" (7.2.2), where IWF2 constructs and sends a ULR to the HSS and the HSS's ULA is received back by IWF2; (2) the "Update Location" procedure (A.4.4.2), where the IWF forwards a ULR to the HSS after receiving one from the MME/SGSN, and the HSS answers with a ULA (and an insertSubscriberData / updateLocationAck exchange).

questions.question: Which procedures put MAC computation and SLPP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two security-flow procedures in TS 33.893 tie MAC computation to SLPP (Sidelink Positioning Protocol) messages in the same step: (1) "Message processing in the sending UE" (6.15.2.2.1), where the sending UE calculates the MAC over the SLPP message header and payload and applies confidentiality protection to that SLPP-formatted message; (2) "SLPP signalling protection and verification" (6.25.2.3), where a receiving UE verifies the message by checking the MAC using the groupcast integrity key to ensure the GKID and the SLPP signalling were not tampered with.

questions.question: For PS to CS and CS to PS access transfer, which procedures put CS and PS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two SRVCC access-transfer signalling flows in TS 24.237 Annex A combine CS and PS handling in the same step: (1) "PS to CS Access Transfer" (A.18.3), where the source E-UTRAN triggers a PS to CS SRVCC handover to CS access and the MSC server initiates session transfer; (2) "CS to PS Access Transfer" (A.20.3), where the MSC server receives a CS to PS request indicating that a CS to PS SRVCC access transfer is initiated and the ATCF reconfigures the media path accordingly.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SLPKMF/DAPS security state and the RLC/PDCP entities in the same step for a DAPS handover?
questions.reference_answer: Two DAPS handover test-procedure variants in TS 38.523-1 clause 8.1.4.3 contain the same UE-side step where DAPS, the RLC entity and the PDCP entity are all acted on together: on receiving an RRCReconfiguration that includes daps-SourceRelease, the UE releases the RLC entity for the source SpCell for each DAPS bearer and reconfigures the PDCP entity to release DAPS, per TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.3. This step is identical in (1) "DAPS handover with key change / Success / Intra-frequency" (8.1.4.3.1) and (2) "DAPS handover / HO Failure and source link available / HO Success and RLF in source / Intra-frequency" (8.1.4.3.2).

questions.question: Which procedures put the PDUID and the RPAUID in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two restricted ProSe discovery "Announce Request" procedures in TS 23.303 clause 5.3.3 have the same preparatory step (step 0) linking PDUID and RPAUID: the application client in the UE retrieves the PDUID and provides it to the ProSe Application Server, which allocates an RPAUID for that PDUID, stores the PDUID-RPAUID binding, and returns the RPAUID to the UE. This appears identically in (1) the non-roaming Announce Request (5.3.3.2A) and (2) the roaming/inter-PLMN Announce Request (5.3.3.3A).

questions.question: Which procedures put the H(e)NB and the OCSP responder in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two H(e)NB security procedures in TS 33.320 have the H(e)NB and OCSP interacting in the same step: (1) the SeGW certificate revocation check requirement (7.2.3), where the H(e)NB sends an OCSP request to the OCSP responder and checks the SeGW certificate status from the OCSP response; (2) the "Combined Device and HP Authentication" call-flow example (A.2), where the H(e)NB retrieves SeGW certificate status information from the OCSP responder as part of the IKE_AUTH exchange.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GMSCA, the MSRN and VMSCB in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two number-portability call-routing procedures in TS 23.066 contain the identical step "GMSCA uses the MSRN to route the call to VMSCB": (1) "International SOR for a Non-ported Number" (B.4.5), where HLRB returns an SRI ack with an MSRN to GMSCA which then routes to VMSCB; (2) "Call to a Ported Number - Direct Routeing" (C.3.2), where HLRA returns the MSRN to GMSCA, which again routes the call to VMSCB.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GMLC and the LRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two location-continuity handover procedures in TS 23.271 clause 9.4.5.4 have the LRF and a GMLC acting together in the same step: (1) "Location Continuity for E-UTRAN Handover to WLAN" (9.4.5.4.3), where during the emergency call an LRF is assigned and a source location server (e.g. a GMLC) is chosen; (2) "Location Continuity for WLAN Handover to E-UTRAN, UTRAN or GERAN" (9.4.5.4.4), where after handover the LRF may instigate an MT-LR request via the target GMLC if needed.

questions.question: Which procedures put GERAN and SRVCC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two SRVCC test procedures in TS 36.523-1 combine SRVCC and GERAN in the same step: (1) "SRVCC Emergency Call Handover to GERAN" (11.2.12), where, based on UE measurement reports, the source E-UTRAN decides to trigger an SRVCC handover to GERAN; (2) the SRVCC handover-cancellation notification procedure (13.4.3.41), where the UE (having failed to retune to UTRAN or GERAN after the handover command) sends a SIP re-INVITE/UPDATE to recover the session following an "SRVCC handover cancelled" notification.

questions.question: For a live streaming workflow bridging FLUS and NBMP, which procedures put the EA and the NBMP Client/Workflow Manager in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two call-flow mappings in TS 26.939 clause 8.4 contain the step "EA requests NBMP Client to start an NBMP Workflow": (1) the basic "Mapping call flow to the standard APIs" (8.4.2.4.1), where the EA (Edge/External Application) directly requests the NBMP Client to start a workflow; (2) the "Interfaces" call flow (8.4.4.3), where the EA additionally supplies the FLUS Media Sink Address discovered from a FLUS Sink before requesting the NBMP Client to start the workflow.

questions.question: For a live streaming workflow bridging FLUS and NBMP, which procedures put the EA, FLUS and NBMP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two call-flow mappings in TS 26.939 clause 8.4 have a single step where the EA, FLUS and NBMP are all acted on together: (1) "Mapping call flow to the standard APIs" (8.4.3.4.1), where the EA requests the NBMP Client to start an NBMP Workflow using the FLUS Media Sink Address obtained from a FLUS Sink; (2) the "Interfaces" call flow (8.4.4.3), where the EA picks a FLUS Sink that can run the workflow in its MPE and locates its NBMP Workflow Manager and Media Sink address from the Sink capabilities.

questions.question: In AR immersive calling, which procedures put AR and STAR UEs in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two AR conferencing call-flows in TS 26.998 clause 6.5.3 have STAR UEs jointly initiating and running the AR call in the same step: (1) the "Symmetrical case" (6.5.3.1), where either STAR UE (Alice or Bob) may initiate the AR immersive call and both communicate with a signalling server to establish it; (2) the "Asymmetrical case" (6.5.3.2), where STAR UE Alice initiates the AR immersive call and communicates with a signalling server, while non-STAR UE Bob participates with reduced (2D) capability.

questions.question: For DRBs with UP integrity protection, which procedures put the DRB and UP integrity handling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two security procedures in TS 33.401 have a step that both configures/activates UP integrity protection and applies it per DRB: (1) the "UP integrity protection activation mechanism" (7.3.4), where the eNB indicates in the RRC Connection Reconfiguration message which DRBs have UP integrity protection activated, and both the eNB and the UE generate KUPint and start UP integrity protection for those DRBs; (2) the dual-connectivity "Activation of encryption/decryption" procedure (E.2.3), where the SeNB shall activate UP integrity protection per DRB according to the received UP integrity protection policy and indicate that to the UE.

questions.question: For PS to CS access transfer with media anchoring, which procedures put the ATCF and the ATGW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two SRVCC signalling flows in TS 24.237 Annex A have the ATCF configuring the ATGW in the same step: (1) "PS to CS Access Transfer with ATCF and media anchored" (A.18.3), where, on receiving the access transfer message, the ATCF correlates the session using the C-MSISDN and updates the ATGW by sending it a Configure ATGW message (acknowledged by the ATGW); (2) "Session origination with PS to CS SRVCC enhancements" (A.4.2), where the ATCF reserves resources in and configures the ATGW as part of establishing the original session.

questions.question: Which procedures put SL positioning and the SLPKMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two sidelink (SL) positioning security solutions in TS 33.893 have the UE contacting the SLPKMF for SL positioning key material in the same step: (1) the group-based "Security flows" solution (6.15.2.1), where the UE establishes a secure connection with the Sidelink Positioning Key Management Function (SLPKMF) and sends it a Key Request including the Ranging/SL positioning application identifier; (2) the broadcast "Solution details" (6.28.2), where UE1 sends a broadcast authorization request to the SL Positioning Key Management Function (SLPKMF) including its UE ID and Zone ID for the SL Ranging/positioning action.

questions.question: In mission-critical call diversion with LCLS, which procedures put the GCR, the IAM message and LCLS negotiation in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two call-forwarding signalling examples in TS 23.284 clause 13.4 contain the identical step where the sMSC server, supporting LCLS, modifies the LCLS-Negotiation Request IE and LCLS-Configuration-Preference IE before sending an IAM message containing the GCR (with the encapsulated oBSS ID): (1) the "Call Forwarding Busy" example (13.4.3.2.7); (2) the "Call Forwarding on No Reply" basic sequence (13.4.4.7.2).

questions.question: Which procedures put the PGW and the SGW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.214 (control and user plane separation for EPC) have a step where the PGW and the SGW act together: (1) clause 6.3.1.1 'Procedures with PDN connection establishment', where the SGW-C includes the F-TEIDu of the default bearer received from the PGW when sending the Sx Session Modification Request to the SGW-U, and where the PGW-C's Sx Session Modification Request (on handover indication) instructs the PGW-U to start routing downlink packets to the SGW/SGW-U; (2) clause 6.3.3.8 'Procedures with handover from non-3GPP access', where the PGW-C's Sx Session Modification Request prompts the PGW-U to tunnel packets from the non-3GPP IP access and immediately start routing packets to the SGW-U for the established EPS bearers.

questions.question: Which procedures put the HPLMN and the IMSI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two ProSe Match Report procedures in TS 23.303 have a step where the HPLMN and the IMSI are involved together: (1) clause 5.3.4.1 'Match report (non-roaming) - open discovery', where the UE (re)establishes a secure connection with the ProSe Function in the HPLMN and sends a Match Report message with the UE Identity set to e.g. IMSI; (2) clause 5.3.4.2 'Match report (roaming/inter-PLMN transmission) - open discovery', where the UE likewise (re)establishes a secure connection with the ProSe Function in the HPLMN and sends a Match Report message including UE Identity set to e.g. IMSI, VPLMN ID and Monitored PLMN ID.

questions.question: In NBMP-enabled FLUS session establishment, which procedures put the MPE and the NBMP Workflow Manager in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two deployment call-flow clauses in TS 26.939 have a step where the NBMP Workflow Manager and the MPE act together: (1) clause 8.4.4.3 (WM-MPE-Sink scenario, 'Interfaces'), where the NBMP Workflow Manager instantiates the workflow in the assigned MPE; (2) clause 8.4.6.2 (NBMPSource-FLUSSource scenario, 'Call flow'), where the NBMP Workflow Manager likewise instantiates the workflow, again targeting the assigned MPE within the FLUS Sink.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SRC and the SRS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two split-rendering call flows in TS 26.565 have steps where the Split Rendering Client (SRC) and the Split Rendering Server (SRS) act directly with each other: (1) clause 5.2.1.2 'Client-driven procedures and call flows', where the SRC and SRS negotiate the configuration of the split rendering session, and the SRS sends the rendered media to the SRC; (2) clause C.2.2 'Procedures and Call Flows', where the SRC and the SRS acquire the scene description of the scene to be rendered together during the split rendering session.

questions.question: For SMS delivery to a mobile number ported under Mobile Number Portability, which procedures put the GMSC and the SM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two Annex B call flows in TS 23.066 (MNP-SRF signalling) have a step where the SMS-GMSC acts directly on the SM: (1) clause B.4.2 'Delivery of SMS to a Non-ported Number - Direct Routeing', where the SMS-GMSC generates a routeing enquiry (MAP SRI_for_SM) for SM delivery, routed to the network's MNP-SRF; (2) clause B.4.3 'Delivery of SMS to a Ported Number - Indirect Routeing', where the SMS-GMSC likewise generates the routeing enquiry for SM delivery, routed to the number range holder network's MNP-SRF.

questions.question: I need every place where the SCEF and the SCS/AS exchange messages in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Six T8-interface procedures in TS 23.682 have a step where the SCEF and the SCS/AS send a message directly to each other: (1) clause 5.12.1 'Set the chargeable party at session set-up' - SCEF sends a Set chargeable party response to the SCS/AS; (2) clause 5.12.2 'Change the chargeable party during the session' - SCEF sends a Change chargeable party response to the SCS/AS; (3) clause 5.17.1 'Device triggering procedure via T8' - SCEF sends a Trigger Submit Confirmation and later a Trigger Delivery Report to the SCS/AS; (4) clause 5.17.2 'Device triggering recall/replace procedures via T8' - SCEF indicates recall/replace success or failure in a Trigger Modify Response to the SCS/AS; (5) clause 5.6.5 'Reporting of Monitoring Events from the PCRF' - SCEF sends a Monitoring Indication to the SCS/AS, which replies with a Monitoring Indication Response; (6) clause 5.6.9 'Network-initiated Explicit Monitoring Event Deletion Procedure' - SCEF sends a Cancel Monitoring Event Request to the SCS/AS, which replies with a Cancel Monitoring Event Response.

questions.question: In NR-NR and E-UTRA-NR dual connectivity mobility, which procedures put the MN and the SN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five dual-connectivity mobility procedures in TS 37.340 clause 10 have steps where the MN and the SN act directly with each other: (1) clause 10.17.1 'MR-DC with 5GC' (RRC_INACTIVE resume with UE Context Retrieve) - the target MN sends an SN Addition Request to the SN, which replies with an SN Addition Request Acknowledge, and the source MN later sends an SN Release Request to the SN; (2) clause 10.3.1 'EN-DC' (SN-initiated SN Modification) - the SN sends the SgNB Modification Required to the MN, which forwards the SN RRC reconfiguration to the UE and back; (3) clause 10.3.2 'MR-DC with 5GC' (SN-initiated SN Modification with LTM) - the SN sends the SN Modification Required to the MN, and the MN provides data forwarding address information to the SN; (4) clause 10.4.1 'EN-DC' (SN-initiated SN Release) - the SN sends the SgNB Release Required, and the MN provides data forwarding addresses to the SN in the SgNB Release Confirm; (5) clause 10.9.1 'EN-DC' (inter-eNB handover to SgNB addition) - the target MN sends an SgNB Addition Request to the target SN, which replies with an SgNB Addition Request Acknowledge and provides forwarding addresses.

questions.question: For MCPTT users setting up or releasing an IOPS private call over IP connectivity functionality, which procedures put the IOPS MC connectivity function and the MCPTT client in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures in TS 23.180 clause 10.5.2 put the IOPS MC connectivity function and an MCPTT client in the same step, each time as sender/distributor of session packets to or from the client: 10.5.2.3 IOPS private call setup in automatic commencement mode (the IOPS MC connectivity function distributes the IOPS call setup request/response session packets to MCPTT client 1 and MCPTT client 2); 10.5.2.4 IOPS private call setup in manual commencement mode (same distribution pattern plus the IOPS MCPTT ringing message); 10.5.2.5 IOPS private call release (the IOPS MC connectivity function distributes the IOPS call release request/response); and 10.5.2.6 IOPS emergency private call (the IOPS MC connectivity function distributes the IOPS call setup request/response for an emergency call, including priority handling).

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF, the SMF and the MBS session in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.247 clause 7 put the AMF, the SMF and the MBS session in the same step. In 7.2.2.3 (Multicast session leave requested by the network or MBS session release), the SMF invokes Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer to the AMF to inform the NG-RAN to remove a UE from the MBS Session, and the AMF forwards the N2 message and later the N2 message received from NG-RAN back to the SMF via Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext. In 7.3.1 (MBS Session Start for Broadcast), the AMF transfers the Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextCreate Response/Notify to the MB-SMF, which stores the MBS Session Context, coordinating with NG-RAN over the MBS session resources.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CN and the GANC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures put the CN and the GANC in the same step, all exchanging Handover Request / Handover Request Acknowledge / Handover Detect / Handover Complete / Clear Command signalling: TS 43.318 8.14.1.1 (GERAN to GAN CS Handover), 8.14.1.2 (UTRAN to GAN CS Handover), 8.14.2 (CS Handover from GAN A/Gb mode to GERAN), 8.14.3 (CS Handover from GAN A/Gb mode to UTRAN), and TS 43.902 5.2.5.13.1 (CS Handover from GERAN to GAN). In each, the CN requests the target GANC to allocate handover resources, the GANC acknowledges and later confirms handover completion/detection, and the CN tears down or switches the connection based on the GANC's indications.

questions.question: I need every place where the NWDAF and the UPF are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures put the NWDAF and the UPF in the same step. TS 23.288 6.16.4 (PFD Determination analytics procedure): the NWDAF collects User Data Usage Measures from the UPF via SMF, and the UPF may also report data directly to the NWDAF. TS 23.700-62 6.7.3.1 (Subscription to UPF for Data Collection for "Any UE"): the UPF registers its profile in NRF, the NWDAF sends Nupf_EventExposure Subscribe to the relevant UPF(s), and the UPF sends Nupf_EventExposure Notify back to the NWDAF. TS 23.700-62 6.9.3.1 (UPF data collection for single UE): the NWDAF determines the event ID for UPF event exposure, the UPF registers to SMF with supported event exposure, and the UPF sends notifications toward the NWDAF (directly or via SMF).

questions.question: Which procedures put the SMF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures put the SMF and the UDM in the same step. TS 23.502 4.15.3.2.5 (Downlink data delivery status with SMF buffering): the UDM sends Nsmf_EventExposure_Subscribe Request to each SMF serving the UE, and the SMF replies with the subscribe response and later sends event notifications back toward the UDM/NEF chain. TS 29.503 5.3.2.2.4 (SMF registration): the SMF sends a PUT request to create/update its SMF registration resource, and the UDM responds with 201 Created or 200 OK, invoking Deregistration Notification toward an old SMF if it changes. TS 29.503 5.3.2.4.4 (SMF deregistration): the SMF sends a DELETE request for its individual SMF registration, and the UDM responds with 204 No Content, optionally terminating the associated SDM Subscription.
