questions.question: For NWDAF instances retrieving trained ML Models or accuracy-related data, which procedures put the ADRF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures put the ADRF and the NWDAF in the same step. TS 23.288 6.2B.7 (ML Model retrieval from ADRF): the NWDAF service consumer (NWDAF containing MTLF/AnLF) invokes Nadrf_MLModelManagement_RetrievalRequest toward the ADRF, and after verifying the consumer, the ADRF responds with the ML Model identifier(s)/file address(es). TS 23.700-81 6.34.2.2 (MTLF-initiated accuracy monitoring): the NWDAF containing MTLF requests the ADRF to subscribe for collection of analytics/data related to the deployed ML model, and the NWDAF containing MTLF later receives that analytics and data from the ADRF to compute model accuracy.

questions.question: For a presence watcher subscribing to a presentity's status via the IMS core, which procedures put the S-CSCF and the Presence Server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures put the S-CSCF and the Presence Server (PS) in the same step. TS 24.141 A.3.4.1 (Successful subscription): S-CSCF#2 forwards the SUBSCRIBE request to the PS, and the PS performs authorization and sends a 200 (OK) response and subsequent NOTIFY request back to the S-CSCF. TS 24.141 A.3.5 (Network based watcher subscribing on behalf of IMS watcher to IMS presentities): the S-CSCF forwards the SUBSCRIBE request to the PS, and the PS authorizes the watcher and returns the 200 (OK) response and NOTIFY request to the S-CSCF for onward forwarding to the network watcher.

questions.question: Which procedures put the W-AGF and the AMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures put the W-AGF and the AMF in the same step. TS 23.316 7.2.8.2 (AUN3 device De-registration via W-5GAN): the AMF sends an N2 UE Context Release Command to the W-AGF, and the W-AGF removes the context and confirms with an N2 UE Context Release Complete back to the AMF. TS 23.316 7.3.2 (5G-RG or Network Requested PDU Session Modification via W-5GAN): the AMF sends an N2 PDU Session Resource Modify Request to the W-AGF, and the W-AGF acknowledges with an N2 PDU Session Resource Modify Response, also forwarding NAS messages between the 5G-RG and AMF. TS 33.887 6.9.2.1 (AUN3 device authentication procedure): the AMF derives the WAGF key and sends it to the W-AGF via NAS Security Mode Command, after which the W-AGF/RG derive further keys.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF and the NRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures put the AMF and the NRF in the same step, all involving the AMF using the NRF for discovery/registration lookups. (1) TS 23.700-05 clause 6.14.3 ("Procedures" for IAB-node positioning): the UE-AMF sends a Cell ID lookup request to the NRF, and the NRF returns the IAB-UE ID and the identifier of the AMF serving the IAB-UE corresponding to that Cell ID. (2) TS 29.518 clause 5.2.2.3.5.2 ("Using N1MessageNotify in the Registration with AMF Re-allocation Procedure"): the initial AMF discovers the target AMF (NF Service Consumer) from the NRF and fetches the N1 Notification URI from the registered default notification subscription. (3) TS 29.518 clause 5.2.2.3.6.4 ("Using N2InfoNotify during AMF planned removal procedure with UDSF deployed procedure"): the initial AMF discovers the target AMF from the NRF and fetches the N2 Notification URI, similarly via the default notification subscription.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MME and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three execution-phase procedures in TS 23.401 clause 5.5.2 (inter-RAT handover) put the MME and the SGSN in the same step, all around the Forward Relocation Complete exchange. (1) Clause 5.5.2.2.3 (UTRAN Iu mode to E-UTRAN handover, execution phase): once the UE has arrived at the target side, the target MME informs the source SGSN by sending the Forward Relocation Complete Notification message, and the source SGSN acknowledges; later the source SGSN releases resources towards the source RNC and, if a Serving GW change was indicated, deletes EPS bearer resources. (2) Clause 5.5.2.4.3 (GERAN A/Gb mode to E-UTRAN handover, execution phase): the same Forward Relocation Complete Notification/acknowledge exchange occurs between the target MME and source SGSN, after which the source SGSN stops data forwarding and cleans up resources towards the source BSS. (3) Annex D.3.8.3 (execution phase for a Gn/Gp SGSN interworking case): the target MME informs the old SGSN via a Forward Relocation Complete message, the old SGSN acknowledges and stops data forwarding.

questions.question: Which procedures put the IWF and the MME in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three MAP-D interworking procedures in TS 29.305 Annex A.4.4 put the IWF and the MME in the same step, all involving the IWF relaying HSS-originated MAP messages to the MME. (1) Clause A.4.4.5.2 ("Insert Subscriber Data over MAP D"): if the received MAP InsertSubscriberData contains SMS-related data, the IWF maps it into an IDR sent towards the MME, and later receives the corresponding IDA from the MME. (2) Clause A.4.4.6.2 ("Delete Subscriber Data over MAP D"): the IWF maps SMS-related DeleteSubscriberData into a DSR towards the MME and receives a DSA from the MME; if the SMS subscription is withdrawn, the IWF also sends an IDR to the MME to remove the MME's SMS registration. (3) Clause A.4.4.7 ("Reset"): the IWF exchanges Reset (RSR/RSA) messages with the MME, receiving an RSA from the MME and sending an RSR unchanged to the MME.

questions.question: For interconnection border control between visited, home and interconnection SIP networks, which procedures put the CSCF and the IBCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three IMS interconnect registration/subscription procedures in TS 29.949 clause 5.2 put a CSCF entity (P-CSCF, S-CSCF or I-CSCF) and an IBCF in the same step. (1) Clause 5.2.2 ("Registration via IC SIP proxies"): the P-CSCF-vA1 selects an IBCF acting as the exit point towards the home network and sends the REGISTER request to that IBCF. (2) Clause 5.2.3.2 (registration-state subscription flow): the P-CSCF-vA1 sends a SUBSCRIBE request to the IBCF-vA1, which forwards it via the interconnection network towards the home IBCF and on to the S-CSCF-hA1, and later the S-CSCF-hA1 sends a NOTIFY towards the IBCF chain back to the P-CSCF. (3) Clause 5.2.3.3 (equivalent subscription flow, alternate routing case): the same SUBSCRIBE/NOTIFY exchange occurs between the P-CSCF-vA1, the IBCFs (IBCF-vA1 and IBCF-hA1) and the I-CSCF-hA1/S-CSCF-hA1.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MBS and the NRM server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three MBS session procedures in TS 23.434 clause 14.3.4A put the MBS session and the NRM server in the same step, all showing the NRM server as the entity that creates or activates the MBS session on behalf of a VAL service group. (1) Clause 14.3.4A.2.2 ("Procedure for pre-created MBS session and MBS session announcement"): the NRM server initiates an MBS session creation procedure towards the 5GC (via TMGI allocation and MBS session creation requests) and then announces the created MBS session to NRM clients. (2) Clause 14.3.4A.2.3 ("Procedure for dynamic MBS sessions"): the NRM server decides to create an MBS session dynamically (invoking the same creation procedure as 14.3.4A.2.2) and provides the MBS session announcement to the NRM client. (3) Clause 14.3.4A.5.2 ("Multicast MBS session activation procedure"): upon a VAL server request, the NRM server sends an MBS session activation request towards the 5GC (directly to the MB-SMF or via NEF/MBSF), indicating the TMGI to be activated.

questions.question: For IP-CAN session termination or modification with application-layer service information, which procedures put the AF and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three IP-CAN session procedures in TS 23.203 clause 7 put the AF and the PCRF in the same step, all around the PCRF notifying the AF of transmission-resource events and the AF acknowledging. (1) Clause 7.3.1 ("UE initiated IP-CAN Session termination"): the PCRF notifies the AF that there are no transmission resources for the service if requested by the AF, and the AF acknowledges the notification of the loss of transmission resources. (2) Clause 7.3.2 ("GW (PCEF) initiated IP-CAN Session termination"): the same PCRF-to-AF notification and AF acknowledgment of the loss of transmission resources occurs. (3) Clause 7.4.1 ("IP-CAN Session Modification; GW (PCEF) initiated"): the AF provides or revokes service information to the PCRF due to AF session signalling, and the PCRF stores the service information and responds with an acknowledgement to the AF; the PCRF may also report bearer-level events to the AF, which the AF acknowledges.

questions.question: I need every place where the MBS session and the MCPTT server are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Two MCPTT group-call procedures put the MBS session and the MCPTT server in the same step, both showing the MCPTT server sending or de-associating group-call media over an MBS session. (1) TS 23.289 clause 7.3.3.10.2 ("Call connect and disconnect over MBS session procedures"): the MCPTT server grants MCPTT client 1 the floor and sends the MC media over the associated MBS session to MCPTT clients 2 to n, sends a floor-taken message over that MBS session, and, once transmission is over, sends an UnMapGroupFromSessionStream to de-associate the group call from the MBS session. (2) TS 23.783 clause 6.29.2.1 ("Call connect over MBS session procedure"): the MCPTT server similarly grants the floor, sends the floor-taken message and the MC media over the associated MBS session to MCPTT clients 2 to n, and sends a MapGroupToSessionStream with the stream information needed to receive the MC media within that MBS session.

questions.question: In GAN mobile-originated CS call setup, which procedures put the GANC, the MSC, RANAP signalling and the CS domain indicator in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures put the GANC and the MSC together acting over RANAP signalling with the CS domain indicator in the same step: the Mobile Originated CS Call procedure in TS 43.318 clause 9.10 (GAN Iu mode), and the equivalent Mobile Originated CS Call procedure described in TS 43.902 clause 5.2.5.10 (the GAN feasibility study). In both, the GANC establishes an SCCP connection to the MSC and forwards the NAS CM Service Request to the MSC using the RANAP Initial UE Message, with the Domain Indicator set to 'CS domain'; later the MSC requests the GANC to assign call resources via the RANAP RAB Assignment Request, again carrying the CS domain context.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PDP context and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures show the SGSN directly acting on PDP context(s) in the same step: the Routing Area Update procedure in TS 23.401 Annex D.3.5, where the new SGSN sends an Update PDP Context Request (with QoS Negotiated, serving network identity, CGI/SAI, etc.) to the GGSN(s) concerned to update PDP context fields; and the Agreed handover principles in TS 43.129 Annex A.1, where information pertaining to all PDP contexts and PFCs relating to the MS is sent from the old SGSN to the target SGSN during PS handover signalling.

questions.question: For a PCEF reporting an event that requires new or revised policy rules, which procedures put the PCC rules, the PCEF and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures show the PCRF directly provisioning PCC rules to the PCEF in the same step: the Event reporting for PCEF in visited network and locally terminated Gxx interaction procedure in TS 23.203 clause 7.7.3.2, where a PCEF-initiated IP-CAN Session Modification may forward the deployed Event Trigger report to the H-PCRF or request new or revised PCC Rules and Event Triggers; and the Network-initiated Dynamic PCC on S2a procedure in TS 23.402 clause 6.6.1, where the PCRF initiates the PCC Rules Provision Procedure and provides updated PCC rules to the PCEF for enforcement.

questions.question: For an AF provisioning expected-UE-behaviour parameters, which procedures put the AF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures put the AF and the UDM together acting in the same step: the NEF service operations information flow for external parameter provisioning in TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.2, where the UDM authorises the AF-provisioned parameters, resolves the GPSI to SUPI, and requests to create/update/delete the data (with subsequent Nudm_ParameterProvision response to the AF/NEF); and the Network Triggered capability indication procedure in TS 23.700-41 clause 6.6.3.1.2, where during UE registration the UDM may interact directly with the SoR AF to provide SoR information to the UE.

questions.question: For an AF requesting time-synchronization services from the 5G core, which procedures put the AF, the NEF and the TSCTSF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures place the AF, the NEF and the TSCTSF together in the same step: the Exposure of UE availability for Time Synchronization service procedure in TS 23.502 clause 4.15.9.2, where the NEF discovers and invokes the TSCTSF on behalf of the AF's Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_CapsSubscribe/Unsubscribe request, noting that an AF within the operator's trust domain may also invoke the TSCTSF directly; and the Procedures for 5G access stratum time distribution in TS 23.700-25 clause 6.14.3.2, where the AF provides access-stratum time-distribution parameters to the NEF via Nnef_ASTI_Create, which the NEF forwards to the TSCTSF (again with the direct-invocation option for a trusted AF).

questions.question: Which procedures put the CCA, the NRF and the SCP in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures put the SCP, the NRF and the CCA together acting in the same step: the Authorization for indirect communication with delegated discovery procedure in TS 33.501 clause 13.4.1.3.2, where the SCP sends an Nnrf_AccessToken_Get access token request to the NRF that may include the NF Service Consumer's CCA received earlier; and the Request of access token on behalf of the consumer procedure in TS 33.875 clause 6.3.2.1, where the SCP sends an access token request to the NRF including the CCA received from the consumer.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BSC and the RNC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two MBMS bearer-service procedures in TS 23.246 clause 8 put the BSC and the RNC in the same step: (1) clause 8.3.1, 'MBMS Session Start Procedure for GERAN and UTRAN for GPRS', where the SGSN sends an MBMS Session Start Request message to each BSC and/or RNC connected to it, and the BSC/RNC establishes the radio resources and, if it accepts IP Multicast distribution, joins the multicast group and returns an MBMS Session Start Response; (2) clause 8.6.1, 'BM-SC initiated MBMS De-Registration Procedure', where the SGSN sends an MBMS De-Registration Request message to all BSCs/RNCs connected to it, and the BSC/RNC releases the affected radio resources, the MBMS UE Contexts and the MBMS Service Context, and returns an MBMS De-Registration Response. In both procedures the BSC and the RNC are addressed together as the set of downstream radio-access nodes that receive the same MBMS session-control message from the SGSN and act on it identically.

questions.question: For an edge application server discovering and notifying an edge enabler client, which procedures place the ECS, the EEC and the ENS in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two notification-delivery procedures in TS 23.700-98 clause 7.20.2 put the ECS, the EEC and the ENS together in the same step: (1) clause 7.20.2.2, 'Notification delivery over a direct Notification Channel Procedure', where the EEC sends a request to the ENS for a direct notification channel, the ENS assigns and returns a CallBack/Channel URL, the EEC also subscribes for service provisioning to the ECS using that CallBack URL, and when an event of interest occurs at the ECS it pushes the notification to the CallBack URL terminated at the ENS, which the ENS then forwards on to the EEC; (2) clause 7.20.2.3, 'Notification delivery using a Push Server Procedure (indirect Notification Channel)', the same three-way flow but routed through an indirect push server: the EEC requests an indirect channel from the ENS, subscribes to the ECS, the ECS pushes events to the ENS's CallBack URL, and the ENS relays them onward via the push server to the EEC. In both procedures the EEC is the subscriber/requester, the ECS is an event source that pushes notifications to a callback address, and the ENS is the notification-channel broker that receives from the ECS and forwards to the EEC.

questions.question: In RAN timing synchronisation status reporting, which procedures put the CU and the DU in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two RAN TSS (Timing Synchronisation Status) reporting procedures in TS 38.401 clause 8.24 put the gNB-CU and the gNB-DU in the same step: (1) clause 8.24.1, 'RAN TSS reporting towards the CN', where the gNB-CU requests RAN TSS reporting from at least one gNB-DU by sending a TIMING SYNCHRONISATION STATUS REQUEST message, the gNB-DU replies with a TIMING SYNCHRONISATION STATUS RESPONSE and later, on detecting a primary source event, sends an updated TIMING SYNCHRONISATION STATUS REPORT to the gNB-CU; (2) clause 8.24.2, 'RAN TSS reporting towards the UE', where the same gNB-DU-to-gNB-CU reporting exchange (steps reused from 8.24.1) is followed by the gNB-CU forwarding the latest clock quality information to the UE via a DLInformationTransfer message. In both procedures the gNB-DU is the source that detects timing-synchronisation status/primary-source events and reports them, and the gNB-CU is the node that requests and receives those reports from the gNB-DU before passing information onward.

questions.question: For sessions transferred by the SCC AS, which procedures put the SCC AS and the STI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two session-continuity procedures in TS 23.237 put the SCC AS and the Session Transfer Identifier (STI) together in the same step: clause 6.2.1.3 'Originating sessions that use only PS media flow(s)', where the SCC AS anchors the session and an STI is assigned for it; and clause 6.3.2.1.2a 'PS-CS Access Transfer: CS to PS - Dual Radio with Session State Information', where the SCC AS provides Session State Information including a dynamic STI needed for a held session, and the UE later uses that STI to initiate the Access Transfer request towards the SCC AS.

questions.question: In IAB topology adaptation, which procedures put the CU and the DU in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two IAB (Integrated Access and Backhaul) topology procedures in TS 38.401 put the IAB-donor-CU and an IAB-DU together in the same step: clause 8.2.3.2 'Intra-CU topology adaptation procedure in NSA using MCG SRB', where the IAB-donor-CU sends UE CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION REQUEST messages to the source or target parent node IAB-DU and receives the corresponding RESPONSE messages back; and clause 8.2.4 'Intra-CU topological redundancy procedure', where the IAB-donor-CU configures BH RLC channels and sends UE CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION REQUEST messages to the first- and second-path parent IAB-DUs, which respond with UE CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION RESPONSE and forward RRC messages on the CU's behalf.

questions.question: For edge application discovery via the ECS, which procedures put the ECS and the ECS-ER in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two ECS discovery-subscription procedures in TS 23.558 put the ECS and the ECS Enabler Registry (ECS-ER) together in the same step: clause 8.17.2.3.3.2 'Subscribe', where the ECS sends an ECS discovery subscription request to the ECS-ER, and the ECS-ER authorizes it, stores the subscription and sends back a subscription response; and clause 8.17.2.3.3.4 'Subscription update', where the ECS sends an update request to the ECS-ER, which authorizes and updates the stored subscription and returns an update response.

questions.question: For NF event-exposure subscription flows involving the AF, which procedures put the NEF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Seven procedures across five specs put the NEF and the UDM together in the same step, always as a request/response or notify pair: TS 23.502 clause 4.15.3.2.5 (NEF sends Nudm_EventExposure_Subscribe to UDM for downlink data delivery status, UDM replies); TS 23.700-28 clause 6.19.2 (NEF invokes Nudm_ParameterProvision to give UE-behaviour parameters to UDM, UDM stores and replies); TS 23.700-47 clause 6.26.3 (NEF stores in UDM the users to be kept connected); TS 23.700-74 clause 6.14.3 (NEF subscribes to UDM via Nudm Event Exposure, UDM sends event reports back to NEF); TS 23.700-74 clause 6.8.3 and clause 6.9.3.1 (NEF invokes Nudm_ParameterProvision for 5G VN group / LADN area data, UDM stores it and replies to NEF); and TS 23.700-88 clause 6.8.2.1.1, where the combined UDM/NEF entity registers and queries PINMF information in the UDR on behalf of PEMC registration.

questions.question: I need every place where the LMF and NG-RAN are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Five positioning procedures across three specs put the LMF and NG-RAN in the same step: TS 23.273 clause 6.7.4 'Event Reporting in RRC INACTIVE state for UL Positioning', where NG-RAN gNB nodes transfer UL location measurements to the LMF; TS 23.700-05 clause 6.8.3 'Positioning procedure for UE accessing via mobile base station relay', where the LMF sends and receives NRPPa messages to/from NG-RAN; TS 38.305 clause 7.3.2 'NI-LR and MT-LR Service Support' and clause 7.3.4 'Deferred MT-LR Event Reporting Support', where the LMF instigates NRPPa procedures with the NG-RAN node to obtain UE location information; and TS 38.305 clause 7.5.2 'Broadcast Procedures', where the LMF sends NRPPa Assistance Information Control messages to the NG-RAN node, and the NG-RAN node sends back Assistance Information Feedback.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the HSS and the IWF at the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Eight MAP-to-Diameter interworking procedures in TS 29.305 (the 'One IWF Scenario' and MAP D-interface call flows) put the HSS and the IWF together in the same step: clause 7.10.1 (Trace activation: IWF receives ActivateTraceMode from HSS and acknowledges it); clause 7.4.1 (Purge MS: IWF opens a MAP dialogue and sends PurgeMS to HSS, receives PurgeMS Ack); clause 7.5.1 (Insert Subscriber Data/Provide Subscriber Info: IWF receives the MAP message from HSS and acknowledges it, HSS closes the dialogue); clause 7.8.1 (Notify Request: HSS may continue with InsertSubscriberData, IWF sends UpdateGprsLocation/ReadyForSM to HSS, HSS closes the dialogue); clause A.3.4.3 (Report SM Delivery Status: IWF receives SRA from HSS and sends RDR to HSS); clause A.4.4.3.2 (Cancel Location over MAP D: IWF receives CancelLocation from HSS and acknowledges it); clause A.4.4.5.2 (Insert Subscriber Data over MAP D: IWF receives the MAP message from HSS and sends the Ack, HSS closes the dialogue); and clause A.4.4.6.2 (Delete Subscriber Data over MAP D: IWF receives the MAP message from HSS, sends PurgeMS to HSS and receives the Ack). In every case the IWF acts as the protocol-interworking function translating MAP requests from/to the HSS.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures place the NEF and the SMF in the same step, each with a direct NEF-SMF message exchange: (1) NEF Anchored Mobile Originated Data Transport (TS 23.502 clause 4.25.4) - the NEF sends the Nnef_SMContext_Delivery Response back to the SMF after receiving unstructured data from it; (2) NEF Anchored Mobile Terminated Data Transport (TS 23.502 clause 4.25.5) - the SMF indicates to the NEF that the requested Nsmf_NIDD_Delivery has failed; (3) the DetNet capability reporting procedure (TS 23.700-46 clause 6.2.3) - the SMF integrates reporting messages that the NEF collects, and the NEF forwards the requested capability reporting requirements to the SMF.

questions.question: For the AF and the NEF exchanging event subscription and NIDD delivery messages, which procedures put them in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures place the AF and the NEF in the same step, exchanging requests and responses directly: (1) Downlink data delivery status with SMF buffering (TS 23.502 clause 4.15.3.2.5) - the AF sends an Nnef_EventExposure_Subscribe Request to the NEF; (2) NEF Anchored Mobile Originated Data Transport (TS 23.502 clause 4.25.4) - the AF responds to the NEF with a Nnef_NIDD_DeliveryNotify Response; (3) AF triggered MBS Session management procedures without PCC (TS 23.700-47 clause 6.10.3.3) - the NEF responds to the AF and the NEF notifies the AF after interacting with the SMF.

questions.question: I need every place where the MSC server and the MGW are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures put the MSC (server) and the MGW in the same step: (1) Basic Sequence for LCLS call retrieval (TS 23.284 clause 13.6.2.3.2) - the MSC-A server requests the MGW-A to re-establish communication to the held party and, separately, requests the MGW-A to stop the announcement towards the held party; (2) Addition/Removal of video media flow through SCUDIF using the I2 reference point (TS 23.292 clause 7.9.1.2) - the MSC Server initiates interaction with the MGW, instructing it to modify the bearer characteristics for the added video media.

questions.question: Which procedures place the AMF and the NEF in the same step of the flow?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures put the AMF and the NEF in the same step, each with a direct AMF-NEF event exchange: (1) AMF service operations information flow (TS 23.502 clause 4.15.3.2.1) - the NEF sends an Namf_EventExposure_Subscribe request to the AMF; (2) NEF Anchored Mobile Terminated Data Transport (TS 23.502 clause 4.25.5) - the AMF indicates to the NEF that the UE has become reachable; (3) local service subscription exposure (TS 23.700-08 clause 6.15.3) - the NEF subscribes to the Local Service Subscription event notification from the AMF, which later sends the event notification to the NEF; (4) group-based event exposure (TS 23.700-74 clause 6.14.3) - for events about the number of UEs in an area, the NEF subscribes directly to the AMF, and the AMF sends event reports to the NEF.

questions.question: For a network-initiated Detach or Monitoring Event Deletion, which procedures put the HSS and the MME in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures confirmed to put the HSS and the MME together in one step: (1) the HSS-initiated Detach procedure for E-UTRAN in TS 23.139 clause 9.1.2, where the HSS sends a Cancel Location Request message directly to the MME to trigger detach; (2) the Network-initiated Explicit Monitoring Event Deletion procedure in TS 23.682 clause 5.6.9, where the HSS also deletes the previously configured Monitoring Event in the MME/SGSN, e.g. upon deletion of an External Group ID.

questions.question: For a CS UE attached to an MSC Server enhanced for ICS, which procedures put the CS, ICS and MSC actors in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Six procedures confirmed: (1) TS 23.292 7.3.2.1.2 'Origination using I2 reference point' - UE A sends a CS call setup message to the MSC Server enhanced for ICS; (2) TS 23.292 7.7.1.2 'Session Release for Gm and I1' - the MSC Server releases the CS Session with the ICS UE; (3) TS 23.292 7.9.2.4 'Addition/Removal of video media flow through redial using Gm Reference Point' - the ICS UE A sends a CS call setup/disconnect message to the MSC server; (4) TS 23.292 7.9.2.5, the equivalent flow using the I1 Reference Point, same CS/ICS UE/MSC server exchange; (5) TS 24.292 A.4.3 'Signalling flows for CS UE origination when using an MSC Server enhanced for ICS - multiple codecs used' - the CS UE sends a SETUP message to the MSC Server enhanced for ICS; (6) TS 24.292 A.4.4, the equivalent one-codec-used signalling flow with the same CS UE / MSC Server enhanced for ICS exchange.

questions.question: In mission-critical group communication using MBMS bearers, which procedures put the MC service actors and the TMGI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures confirmed: (1) TS 23.280 10.7.3.9.2.2 'MBMS bearer coordination within one group call' - the discover bearer response sent by the MC service server (MBMS bearer control role) includes the TMGI of the MBMS bearer shared between the MC service servers; (2) TS 23.282 7.3.5.3.2 'Use of dynamic MBMS user service establishment' - in response to the MCData server's MBMS session creation, the MCData server obtains the TMGI of the MBMS bearer used for the MBMS session.

questions.question: For a CS Fallback mobile originating call, which procedures put the CS, GERAN and MME actors in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures confirmed: (1) TS 23.272 6.3 'Mobile Originating call in Active Mode - No PS HO support' - the MME sends an S1-AP UE Context Modification Request with a CS Fallback Indicator and LAI to the eNodeB, moving the UE to GERAN/UTRAN for the CS domain; (2) TS 36.523-1 13.1.4 'Call setup from E-UTRAN RRC_IDLE / CS fallback to UTRAN with handover / MT call' - the MME sends the same S1-AP UE Context Modification Request (CS Fallback Indicator, LAI) instructing the eNodeB to move the UE to UTRAN/GERAN.

questions.question: For an inter-RAT PS handover to GERAN, which procedures put the BSS, the PS domain and the SGSN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures confirmed: (1) TS 23.401 5.5.2.3.3 'Execution phase' - during the PS handover execution, the Target BSS informs the Target SGSN by sending PS Handover Complete, and the two exchange further PS-handover-related signalling (XID negotiation, Modify Bearer Request) to complete the RAT change; (2) TS 43.129 A.1 'Agreed handover principles' - describes the general PS Handover forwarding-of-data principles between the old/target SGSN and the source/target BSS.

questions.question: Which procedures put the UP data path and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.700-60, both titled 'Procedures': (1) clause 6.20.3, where after a PDU Session is established, the UPF receives UP data from the application server, which may include PDU Set assistance metadata; (2) clause 6.60.3, where the same UPF-receives-UP-data-from-the-application-server step occurs as the basis for the UPF determining data burst termination (End of Data Burst Indication).

questions.question: For a GAN mobile call, which procedures put the CS domain and GA-RRC signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 43.318: (1) clause 9.10 'Mobile Originated CS Call' - the MS sends the CM Service Request message to the GANC within a GA-RRC INITIAL DIRECT TRANSFER message that includes the CN Domain identity set to CS; (2) clause 9.11 'Mobile Terminated CS Call' - the GANC pages the MS with a GA-RRC PAGING REQUEST including the CN Domain identity (CS or PS), and the MS replies with a GA-RRC INITIAL DIRECT TRANSFER carrying the same CS/PS domain identity.

questions.question: Which procedures put the BSS, the PS domain and the SGSN in the same step during PS handover preparation?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 43.129: (1) clause 5.8.1.1 'Intra SGSN PS Handover, Preparation phase' - the source BSS sends a PS Handover Required message to the SGSN, which in turn sends a PS Handover Request to the target GANC/BSS to prepare the PS handover; (2) clause A.1 'Agreed handover principles' - states the general principle that for PS Handover, data forwarding is performed from the old SGSN to either the target BSS (intra-SGSN) or the new SGSN (inter-SGSN).

questions.question: Which procedures put the OCS, the PCRF and a Diameter SLA command (with its AVP) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 29.213: (1) clause 4.7.1 'Initial Spending Limit Report Request' - the OCS sends a Diameter SLA command to the PCRF, carrying a Policy-Counter-Status-Report AVP for each requested policy counter identifier plus a Result-Code AVP; (2) clause 4.7.2 'Intermediate Spending Limit Report Request' - the OCS again sends the Diameter SLA command to the PCRF with Policy-Counter-Status-Report AVP(s) after the PCRF requests an updated list of policy counters.

questions.question: Which procedures put the ASR command, the PC and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 29.201: (1) clause A.7.2 'Service data flow deactivation when all service data flows are affected' - the PCRF sends the ASR command to the PC after detecting all service data flows in the AF session have terminated; (2) clause A.7.3 'IP-CAN Session Termination' - the PCRF sends the ASR command to the PC after detecting the IP-CAN session is terminated and the AF session must end.

questions.question: For bundled EAS application context relocation, which procedures put the EAS, ECS, EES and EHE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two ACR (Application Context Relocation) flows for bundled EAS in TS 23.700-98 clause 7.26.2.5 put EAS, ECS, EES and EHE together in one step: the S-EES-executed ACR scenario (7.26.2.5.1) and the S-EAS-decided ACR scenario (7.26.2.5.2). In both, S-EES#1 sends a Retrieve T-EES request to the ECS carrying the bundled EAS information; the ECS determines the T-EES and target EHE for the bundled EAS so that all T-EES and T-EAS end up within the same EHE, then returns that information to S-EES#1.

questions.question: Which procedures put the EAS and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both EAS re-selection procedures in TS 23.700-48 clause 6.15.3 place the EAS and the UPF in the same step: the ECS-option/preconfigured flow (6.15.3.3), where the application client and the EAS transmit data via the user plane via UPF1, and the ECS-option/dynamic SCMF-invoke flow (6.15.3.4), where the application client and EAS transmit data via the user plane via the (local) UPF after re-selection.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CN and GERAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both GAN/GERAN CS handover procedures in TS 43.318 clause 8.14 put the CN and GERAN together in a step: GERAN-to-GAN CS handover (8.14.1.1), where the CN forwards the Handover Command message to the GERAN to complete handover preparation, and CS handover from GAN A/Gb mode to GERAN (8.14.2), where the CN selects a target GERAN cell and requests it, via Handover Request, to allocate the necessary resources.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NRF and a UUID in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both NRF registration procedures in TS 29.510 clause 5.2.2.2 put the NRF and a UUID in the same step: NF (other than NRF) registration to NRF (5.2.2.2.2), where the NF Service Consumer's PUT request identifies the NF Instance by a UUID version 4 nfInstanceId, and if that UUID is sent with upper-case hex digits the NRF must still handle it as lower-case; and Shared Data registration to NRF (5.2.2.2.4), where the same UUID-formatting rule applies to the sharedDataId used in the PUT request the NRF processes.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AC, the ACR scenario negotiation and the EEC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Both ACR-related procedures in TS 23.700-98 involve the AC, ACR scenario negotiation and the EEC in one step: the ACR scenario selection procedure (7.19.2.2), where the EEC sends an ACR scenario selection request to the EES that reports which ACR scenarios are supported by the AC and the EEC; and the ACR request procedure (7.34.2.2.4), where the AC sends an ACR request (detection or initiation) to the EEC, and the EEC checks the AC's credentials and processes the request. (EES only co-occurs with all of AC/ACR/EEC in the first flow, not the second, so this group is reported with AC/ACR/EEC only.)

questions.question: For a PDN connection routed over both 3GPP and WLAN access, which procedures put the PDN GW and WLAN in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five IP flow mobility procedures in TS 23.161 put the PDN (connection/GW) and WLAN together in a step: multi-connection mode routing rule update (6.4.2.2), where the PDN connection is active simultaneously over 3GPP access and WLAN access; 3GPP access becomes unusable in untrusted WLAN access (6.6.1.2), where the PDN GW moves IP flows from 3GPP to WLAN; trusted WLAN access becomes unusable (6.6.1.3), where the PDN GW moves IP flows from WLAN back to 3GPP; multi-connection mode WLAN-usable-again handling (6.6.2.2.2), where the PDN GW may release 3GPP resources once flows move to WLAN; and multi-connection mode move-to-WLAN handling (6.7.1.2), where the PDN GW releases 3GPP access resources once IP flows are moved to WLAN.

questions.question: I need every place where MCPTT and an SDP offer are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: Eight MCPTT call-setup procedures in TS 23.379 clause 10 put MCPTT (client) and an SDP offer in the same step, all as the initial call/request step: first-to-answer call setup (10.15.3); ad hoc group call setup (10.19.3.1.1); ad hoc group call setup with server-determined participant list (10.19.3.1.3); private call setup in automatic commencement mode (10.7.2.2.1 and its variant 10.7.2.2.2.2); private call setup across multiple MCPTT systems (10.7.2.3.1); and private call setup with a generic call setup request, both automatic (10.7.3.3) and manual (10.7.3.4) commencement mode. In each, MCPTT client 1's call/request message to the MCPTT server (or peer client) includes an SDP offer with one or more media types.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF and the NEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF and the NEF appear together in a step across six procedures: the AMF service operations information flow (TS 23.502, 4.15.3.2.1), where the AMF sends event reports to a subscribing NEF via Namf_EventExposure_Notify; NEF Anchored Mobile Terminated Data Transport (TS 23.502, 4.25.5), where the AMF indicates UE reachability to the NEF; local-service event subscription in TS 23.700-08 clause 6.15.3, where the NEF subscribes to the AMF for Local Service Subscription events; group event exposure in TS 23.700-74 clause 6.14.3, where the AMF sends event reports to the NEF; and the AmfRegistration information retrieval procedures in TS 29.503 clauses 5.3.2.5.2 and 5.3.2.5.3, where the NEF (as NF service consumer) queries the AMF's 3GPP and non-3GPP registration resources.

questions.question: For network slice admission and access control, which procedures place the AMF and the NSSAI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF and NSSAI handling appear in the same step across six procedures: the N26-based EPS to 5GS mobility registration procedure (TS 23.502, 4.11.1.3.4), where the AMF derives the S-NSSAI for the serving PLMN before network slice selection; the General Registration procedure (TS 23.502, 4.2.2.2.2), where the AMF processes the Requested NSSAI/Mapping Of Requested NSSAI from the UE; localized-service slice selection in TS 23.700-08 clause 6.35.3, where the AMF provides the Configured and Mapped Configured NSSAI; non-3GPP registration via N3IWF in TS 23.700-17 clause 6.15.3, where the AMF selects based on the Requested NSSAI; temporary slice registration in TS 23.700-41 clause 6.10.2, where the AMF registers the UE's subscribed NSSAI with the UDM and manages a validity timer per S-NSSAI; and slice usage control notifications in TS 23.700-41 clause 6.35.3, where the AMF reports PDU session status per S-NSSAI to the NSACF and updates the UE's Allowed NSSAI.

questions.question: I need every place where the NRF and OAM are involved in the same step of a procedure.
questions.reference_answer: The NRF and OAM occur together in a step across six procedures: NF service registration (TS 23.502, 4.17.1), where an NF instance registers with the NRF using an NF profile that was configured by the OAM system; NF service update (TS 23.502, 4.17.2), where the updated NF profile sent to the NRF again originates from OAM configuration; NF (NF service) failure handling (TS 23.527, 6.2.2), where NF B or OAM updates the NF profile in the NRF to SUSPENDED; NF registration to the NRF (TS 29.510, 5.2.2.2.2), where registration failures can relate to Shared Data IDs configured locally by OAM; and NF-instance/NF-set registration in TS 29.831 clauses 6.2.1.3 and 6.2.1.6, where the NF instance reports errors to OAM or OAM directly provisions the NF Set profile at the NRF.

questions.question: Which procedures show the NWDAF and the SMF acting in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NWDAF and SMF act together in a step across five procedures: session-management congestion-control-experience analytics (TS 23.288, 6.12.4), where the SMF requests or subscribes to NWDAF analytics and also supplies collected data to the NWDAF; UPF data collection for a single UE (TS 23.700-62, 6.9.3.1), where the NWDAF subscribes to the SMF for UPF event exposure and the SMF relays the subscription to the UPF; AF subscription for 5GC information/analytics (TS 23.700-80, 6.8.3.1), where the SMF subscribes to NWDAF analytics for the PDU session after the PCF instructs it to; service-experience analytics collection in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.49.2, where the NWDAF collects service data from SMF/UPF; and the SmfRegistration information retrieval procedure (TS 29.503, 5.3.2.5.7), where the NWDAF, as NF service consumer, queries the SMF registration resource.

questions.question: We are looking at how tracking area updates interact with mobility signalling — which procedures put the MME and a TAU (tracking area update) exchange in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MME and a TAU exchange appear together in a step across six procedures: delivery of ciphering keys for broadcast assistance data (TS 23.271, 9.3a.5), where the MME returns Attach/TAU Accept carrying ciphering keys to the eNodeB; S102 tunnel redirection (TS 23.272, B.2.1.2), where the TAU procedure runs as part of inter-eNodeB handover with MME relocation; the S101 tunnel redirection procedure (TS 23.402, 9.7), which similarly runs the TAU procedure after MME relocation; power-saving enhancement for EPS (TS 23.700-28, 6.1.2.2), where the UE sends a TAU request to the MME to update power-saving parameters and the MME returns the TAU Accept; EPS NAS security context handling after TAU (TS 33.401, 9.2.2.1), where the MME processes the KSIASME/GUTI carried in the TAU Request to decide on activating a non-current native security context; and public-key distribution for PWS (TS 33.969, A.1.1), where the MME distributes the latest public key and NSUC to the UE in response to an Attach or TAU request.

questions.question: For non-3GPP access via N3IWF, which procedures put the AMF and the access network (AN) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF and the access network appear together in a step across five procedures: PDU session release via untrusted non-3GPP access (TS 23.502, 4.12.7), where the N3IWF (as the AN) releases AN resources on an N2 SM request from the AMF; non-3GPP registration via N3IWF in TS 23.700-17 clause 6.15.3, where the N3IWF selects an AMF from the AN parameters and forwards the Registration Request; power-saving enhancement for 5GS (TS 23.700-28, 6.1.2.1), where the AMF sends an N2 UE Context Release Command to the (R)AN and the (R)AN confirms release; the leaving-coverage notification procedure (TS 23.700-28, 6.8.2.1), where the AMF sends an N2 UE Context Release Command to the (R)AN; and trusted/untrusted non-3GPP interworking in TS 23.700-53 clause 6.7.3, where the N3IWF selects the same AMF chosen via trusted access and forwards the Registration Request within an N2 message.

questions.question: Which procedures place the PCC rule framework and the PCF and SMF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PCC rule delivery from the PCF to the SMF occurs in the same step across six procedures: the AF-influence procedure of TS 23.700-17 clause 6.7.2, where the PCF sends PCC rules to the SMF; the procedure of TS 23.700-18 clause 6.2.2, where the PCF sends PCC rule(s) to the SMF; the Periodicity Jitter Provision procedure (TS 23.700-60, 6.32.3.1) and the Periodicity Jitter Report procedure (TS 23.700-60, 6.32.3.2), both where the PCF generates PCC rules with periodicity/jitter parameters via Npcf_SMPolicyControl_UpdateNotify to the SMF; the single-UE procedure of TS 23.700-60 clause 6.36.3.1, where the PCF sends or revokes a group of PCC rules and the SMF binds them to QoS flows or reports rule failures back; and the AF-session-for-QoS procedure of TS 23.700-80 clause 6.38.2.1, where the PCF sends PCC rule(s) with timing-map information to the SMF.

questions.question: For NWDAF analytics that depend on operations-and-maintenance data, which procedures put the NWDAF and OAM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NWDAF and OAM appear together in a step across six procedures: prepared-analytics-subscription transfer (TS 23.288, 6.1B.2.3), where the source and target NWDAFs collect data from NFs or OAM; the QoS-sustainability procedure for a coarse-granularity area (TS 23.288, 6.9.4.1), where the NWDAF collects data from the OAM; the estimated-QoS information-exposure procedure (TS 23.700-60, 6.45.3), where the NWDAF subscribes to OAM services; service-experience analytics in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.18.3, where the NWDAF again collects data from the OAM; and security log collection via NF EventExposure APIs (TS 33.738, 6.6.2.2) and via OAM (TS 33.738, 6.6.2.3), where the OAM (or an operator's AF) requests NF anomalous-behaviour analytics from the NWDAF, and the NWDAF derives analytics or retrieves security logs using OAM- and NRF-supplied inputs.

questions.question: Which procedures place the GAN and the GANC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The GAN and the GANC act together in a step across three procedures: the preparation phase of intra-SGSN PS handover (TS 43.129, 5.8.5.1), where the MS performs GAN registration and the target GANC decides whether to activate a GA-PSR transport channel; implicit PTC deactivation due to MS de-registration in TS 43.318 clause 9.16.8, where the GAN de-registration procedure is initiated by the MS or the GANC; and the equivalent implicit PTC deactivation procedure in TS 43.902 clause 5.2.5.17.8, with the same GAN de-registration initiated by the MS or the GANC.

questions.question: For multicast/broadcast MBS sessions, which procedures put the MBS session and the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MBS session and the SMF act together in a step across three procedures: multicast session leave requested by the network or MBS session release (TS 23.247, 7.2.2.3), where the SMF removes UEs from the MBS session and informs the AMF/NG-RAN via N1N2MessageTransfer; selecting an alternative AMF for a Broadcast MBS session at AMF failure (TS 23.527, 8.3.2.4), where the MB-SMF sends Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextUpdate and receives the ContextStatusNotify confirming the new controlling AMF; and broadcast session establishment (TS 23.700-47, 6.13.3.2), where the MB-SMF continues the MBS Session Creation procedure defined in TS 23.247.

questions.question: Which procedures involve the MBS session and its TMGI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MBS session handling and TMGI usage appear in the same step across three procedures: GCS AS configuration of both broadcast and multicast services (TS 23.700-47, 6.16.2.1), where the GCS AS activates a Multicast TMGI session and starts a Broadcast TMGI session, and the UE chooses between them; the MC data MBS procedure (TS 23.783, 6.34.1.1.2), where the MCData client obtains the TMGI from the MBS user service description and activates monitoring of the session; and broadcast MBS session setup for MOCN resource efficiency (TS 38.401, 8.15.1.1a), where the gNB-DU configures both TMGI 1 and TMGI 2 and each 5GC triggers its own broadcast MBS session setup with its TMGI.

questions.question: Which procedures show the NWDAF and the UDM cooperating in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NWDAF and the UDM cooperate in the same step across six procedures: NWDAF de-registration from UDM (TS 23.288, 6.1C.3), where the NWDAF triggers de-registration and the UDM responds; data collection from NFs (TS 23.288, 6.2.2.2), where the NWDAF checks and subscribes to user consent at the UDM via Nudm_SDM_Get/Subscribe; network consent and multiple IEAF handling (TS 23.700-80, 6.2.2.3), where the NWDAF or IEAF verifies network consent with the UDM via Nudm_SDM_Subscribe; NWDAF registration (TS 29.503, 5.3.2.2.8), where the UDM responds to the NWDAF's registration request; and update-of-registration (TS 29.552, 5.8.3.2.2) and de-registration (TS 29.552, 5.8.3.2.3) of an NWDAF containing AnLF in the UDM, where the NWDAF sends Nudm_UECM_Update/Deregistration requests and the UDM responds.

questions.question: Which procedures put the 3GPP AAA server and an EAP exchange in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The 3GPP AAA Server and an EAP exchange appear together in a step across four procedures: the successful call flow of TS 29.273 clause E.2, where the AAA Server sends EAP Request/AKA-Challenge and later EAP Success, and the ePDG forwards EAP payloads between the UE and the AAA Server; the combined device and HP authentication call flow (TS 33.320, A.2), where the SeGW forwards EAP-Response/AKA-Challenge between the H(e)NB and the AAA Server, which returns EAP success with key material; and PAP-based (TS 33.402, 6.5.2) and CHAP-based (TS 33.402, 6.5.3) authentication for private network access, where the ePDG relays EAP-GTC/MD5-Challenge exchanges and the external AAA server ultimately returns an Access Accept that results in an EAP-success message to the UE.

questions.question: Which procedures place the LCS Client and the LMF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The LCS Client and the LMF act in the same step across three procedures: event reporting in RRC_INACTIVE for UL positioning (TS 23.273, 6.7.4), where the LMF indicates UL-positioning use and later handles event reporting on behalf of the LCS Client or AF; a positioning-accuracy procedure in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.59.2, where the LCS Client requests a UE location with a required accuracy from the LMF, and the LMF compares the achieved accuracy and re-executes the LCS procedure if needed; and SL-MT-LR service support for periodic/triggered location events (TS 38.305, 7.3A.3), where the LMF returns the event report and sidelink location results to the LCS Client or AF, after the AMF requests periodic/triggered sidelink location from the LMF.

questions.question: We are tracing charging-and-policy control across access types — which procedures put PCC rules and the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PCC rules and the PCRF appear together in a step across six procedures: network recovery on PDP context/bearer update (TS 23.380, 5.1.2) and network recovery informing the UE at P-CSCF failure (TS 23.380, 5.2.2), both where the PCRF provides PCC rules in a CCA; UE-initiated resource request/release on S2a (TS 23.402, 6.7.1), where the PCRF makes a PCC decision and updates PCC rules at the PDN GW via the Policy and Charging Rules Provision Procedure; enabling of IP flows (TS 29.213, B.3.2), where the PCRF updates the flow status of PCC rules to open the gates; IP-CAN session establishment for NSWO traffic (TS 29.213, E.4.2.2), where the H-PCRF provisions PCC rules to the V-PCRF/BPCF, which stores and enforces them; and BPCF-initiated IP-CAN session modification (TS 29.213, E.4.4.2.2), where the BPCF reports a PCC rule failure to the (V-/H-)PCRF via Diameter CCR.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CAPIF core function (CCF) and CAPIF authorization in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: CAPIF and the CCF act together in a step across six procedures: service API publish/unpublish (TS 23.222, 8.24.3), where the CCF applies topology hiding when publishing or removing a service API; CCF-to-CCF interconnection publish and discovery (TS 23.222, 8.25.3.1 to 8.25.3.3), where CCF-A shares and discovers service APIs with CCF-B; NF Set Capability Exposure via CAPIF (TS 23.435, 9.3.2.2), where the NSCE server acts as an AEF and CAPIF authorization is obtained by the CCF; and network-slice-capability-enablement API invocation (TS 23.700-99, 6.3.1.3), where the enablement server likewise acts as AEF with authorization obtained by the CCF.

questions.question: For GAN circuit-switched call control, which procedures put the GA-RRC signalling, the GANC, and the MSC together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: GA-RRC signalling, the GANC and the MSC appear together in a step across four clauses: TS 43.318 clauses 9.10 and 9.11, and the corresponding TS 43.902 clauses 5.2.5.10 and 5.2.5.11, all describing mobile-originated/terminated CS call setup over GAN — the MS exchanges Setup, Call Proceeding, Alerting and Connect messages with the MSC, each relayed through the GANC inside GA-RRC UL/DL DIRECT TRANSFER messages, including the GANC paging the MS via GA-RRC PAGING REQUEST on the MSC's behalf.

questions.question: In positioning reference-unit handling, which procedures put the LMF, the NRF, and PRU(s) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The LMF, the NRF, and PRUs act together in a step across five clauses: PRU-indication removal in TS 23.273 clauses 6.17.2 and 6.17.3, where the serving LMF invokes Nnrf_NFManagement_NFUpdate to have the NRF remove a TAI-associated PRU-existence indication; multi-LMF PRU coordination in TS 23.273 clause 6.17.4, where the serving LMF discovers other PRU-serving LMFs via Nnrf_NFDiscovery and the NRF returns their profiles; and PRU information registration/discovery in TS 23.700-71 clauses 6.16.3.1 and 6.16.3.2, where the LMF stores or retrieves PRU information at the NRF via Nnrf_NFManagement_NFUpdate/Nnrf_NFDiscovery.

questions.question: For CS-domain SMS delivery over SGs, which procedures put the MME, the MSC, and the VLR together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MME, the MSC and the VLR appear together in a step across six clauses: mobile-terminated and mobile-originated SMS transfer via the MME (TS 23.272, 8.2.2 and 8.2.4), where the MSC/VLR pages the MS via the MME and exchanges SMS/delivery-report Uplink/Downlink Unitdata messages; supplementary-service paging (TS 23.272, 8.4.2.1), where the MSC/VLR sends a Paging message to the MME; power-saving-aware SMS delivery (TS 23.272, 8.2.4a.2 and 8.2.4a.3), where the MME may report the UE unreachable or send a Service Request to the MSC/VLR depending on extended-DRX/PSM state; and HSS-initiated deregistration (TS 29.563, 5.4.2.2.2), where the HSS sends Cancel Location toward the MME/SGSN and, if a VLR number is stored, toward the MSC/VLR.

questions.question: For Isolated E-UTRAN Operation for Public Safety, which procedures put IOPS, the MC connectivity function, and MCPTT clients in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: IOPS, the IOPS MC connectivity function and MCPTT clients act together in a step across seven procedures in TS 23.180: IOPS group call (10.5.1.3) and IOPS emergency group call (10.5.1.4), where the connectivity function distributes group-call announcements/responses among IOPS MCPTT clients; IOPS private call setup (10.5.2.3), emergency private call setup (10.5.2.6), and private call release (10.5.2.5), where the connectivity function relays call setup/ringing/release requests and responses between MCPTT client 1 and client 2 by IP address; a further private-call ringing variant (10.5.2.4); and IOPS floor control (10.5.3.3), where the connectivity function distributes floor-request and floor-taken messages to the target IOPS MCPTT group.

questions.question: We are wiring up MBS session creation for a content provider — which procedures put the AF, the MBS session, and its TMGI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AF, an MBS session, and its TMGI appear together in a step across seven procedures: TMGI allocation and MBS session creation (TS 23.247, 7.1.1.2), where the AF requests TMGI allocation via NEF/MBSF and MB-SMF, then creates the session description; broadcast MBS session establishment (TS 23.247, 7.3.1), where the AF performs TMGI allocation before the MB-SMF creates broadcast contexts at the AMF(s); group-message delivery request in TS 23.700-47 clause 6.13.3.2, where the AF includes the TMGI when requesting session establishment via NEF; MOCN multi-PLMN TMGI allocation (TS 23.700-47, 6.8.3.1), where the AF requests TMGIs across several PLMNs for the same broadcast service; and primary-TMGI selection/update for MOCN NG-RAN (TS 23.700-47, 6.9.3.2, 6.9.3.3, 6.29.3), where the NG-RAN selects and updates the primary TMGI and the AF is notified to re-announce it to UEs.

questions.question: For CS-to-IMS interworking at call release/setup, which procedures put the (I/S-)CSCF, the MGCF, and the MSC server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MGCF and the MSC server exchange ISUP-mapped messages in the same step across two call-continuity clauses of TS 23.292: clause 7.9.2.4 and clause 7.9.2.5, both showing the MSC server sending an IAM (call setup) or a REL (release) message to the MGCF, which the MGCF maps onto the IMS/SIP side handled by the CSCF/SCC AS.

questions.question: Bringing up NWDAF-assisted PFD management — which procedures put the NEF, the NWDAF, and PFD/PFDF handling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NEF(PFDF) and the NWDAF cooperate on PFD determination in the same step across four clauses: PFD management with NWDAF assistance (TS 23.502, 4.18.2.1 and 4.18.2.2), where the NEF(PFDF) subscribes to NWDAF PFD-determination analytics and compares NWDAF-observed PFD information against what is stored in UDR to decide on create/update/delete; the equivalent solution procedure in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.9.4, with the same fetch-compare-notify pattern; and PFD-determination analytics procedure (TS 23.288, 6.16.4), where the consumer NF (NEF(PFDF)) subscribes to the NWDAF and the NWDAF notifies suggested PFD information back.

questions.question: I need every place where the AF, a GPSI, and the NEF's NIDD configuration are involved in the same step.
questions.reference_answer: The AF, GPSI, and NIDD configuration act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.502: NIDD configuration establishment (4.25.3), where the AF sends Nnef_NIDDConfiguration_Create identifying the UE by GPSI, the NEF authorises it with the UDM via Nudm_NIDDAuthorisation_Get, and returns a TLTRI to the AF; NEF-anchored MT data delivery (4.25.5), where the NEF looks up the 5GS QoS Flow context by GPSI before accepting an AF's Nnef_NIDD_Delivery request; and NIDD authorization update notification (4.25.6), where the NEF informs the AF of a change in a GPSI-identified user's NIDD authorization status.

questions.question: For sponsored-data/background-transfer negotiation with third-party service providers, which procedures put the PCRF, the SCEF, and the SCS/AS together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PCRF, the SCEF and the SCS/AS act together in a step across six clauses: monitoring status aggregation (TS 23.682, 5.6.4.1a), where the SCEF collates per-PCRF monitoring responses before replying to the SCS/AS; setting/changing the chargeable party at session setup and mid-session (TS 23.682, 5.12.1 and 5.12.2), where the SCEF authorizes the SCS/AS request and triggers a PCRF-initiated IP-CAN session modification carrying the Sponsoring Status; connection/resource status reporting (TS 23.682, 5.11), where the SCEF requests transmission-resource notifications from the PCRF and relays bearer-level status to the SCS/AS; background-data-transfer policy negotiation (TS 23.682, 5.9), where the SCEF negotiates transfer policies with the PCRF on behalf of the SCS/AS and the SCS/AS selects one; and the corresponding Diameter BTR exchange in TS 29.213 clause 4.10, where the SCEF forwards the SCS/AS-selected transfer policy to the H-PCRF.

questions.question: For positioning reference-unit subscription and registration, which procedures put the AMF, PRU handling, and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF and the UDM cooperate over PRU handling in the same step across two clauses of TS 23.700-71: clause 6.15.3.2, where the AMF updates PRU state information at the UDM and separately invokes Nudm_SDM_Get to obtain and check PRU privacy settings; and clause 6.16.3.1, where the AMF invokes Nudm_SDM_Get to verify the UE's subscription data includes PRU subscription, rejecting Registration if it does not.

questions.question: For vulnerable-road-user (VRU) protection zones, which procedures put the VAE server, the VASS, and VRU zone handling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The VAE server and the VASS act together over a VRU zone in the same step across three clauses: VRU-zone creation and mobility alerting (TS 23.700-64, 6.2.1.1), where the VASS subscribes to zone creation and the VAE server alerts it when a UE is expected to enter/leave the VRU zone; dynamic protection-zone creation for a cyclist UE (TS 23.700-64, 6.4.1.2), where the VAE server requests VASS authorization to create the zone and later notifies a vehicular UE once it enters the updated zone; and VRU zone-management subscription/alerting (TS 23.286, 9.21.3), where the VAE server responds to a VASS subscription and alerts it of a UE's expected VRU-zone entry.

questions.question: For traffic-routing via service function chaining, which procedures put the AF, the PCF, and SFC policy in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AF and the PCF act on SFC policy in the same step across four clauses of TS 23.700-18: subscription-and-notify for AF SFC-influence requests (6.3.2.1), where PCFs subscribe to and receive UDR notifications of AF SFC-influence data and update the SMF with SFC-tagging policy; AF-influenced traffic routing for an individual UE (6.4.2), where the PCF authorizes the AF's SFC request (received directly or via the NEF) and the SMF configures the UPF-SFC PDR/FAR accordingly; PDU-session impact update (6.5.2.2), where the PCF pushes new SFC-ID policy information to the SMF; and SFC policy inclusion in TS 23.700-18 clause 6.7.2.1, where the PCF includes the SFC policy identified by an SFC policy identifier per the AF request.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NWDAF and MDAS/MDAF-based fault prediction in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NWDAF and MDAS/MDAF fault prediction interact in the same step across two clauses of TS 23.700-81: clause 6.72.2.1, where the NWDAF subscribes to MDAS/MDAF for fault prediction and determines whether the reported fault affects the accuracy of its generated analytics, notifying the consumer if so; and clause 6.72.2.2, where the NWDAF (acting as MTLF) instead determines whether the fault affects ML-model training accuracy and disregards data collected from the affected NF during the faulty period.

questions.question: For Federated Learning group/role discovery, which procedures put an FL role, the MTLF, the NRF, and the NWDAF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: An FL role, the MTLF, the NRF and the NWDAF act together in a step across four clauses: FL group registration and reselection via the NRF (TS 33.738, 6.17.2), where the Server NWDAF registers/updates its FL group at the NRF and discovers new Client NWDAFs through NRF notifications; FL-Consumer-triggered FL (TS 23.700-81, 6.21.2.3), where an NWDAF containing MTLF discovers and subscribes to an FL Server NWDAF via the NRF; central-NWDAF selection for federated learning (TS 23.700-81, 6.22.2), where an NWDAF with MTLF/AnLF and Model-Aggregation capability decides to act as Central NWDAF, discovering candidates via the NRF; and FL client status/reselection logic (TS 23.288, 6.2C.2.3), where the FL Server NWDAF reselects FL Client NWDAF(s) based on status reported via the NRF.

questions.question: For network-slice capability exposure toward vertical (VAL) applications, which procedures put the NEF, OAM, SEAL, and the VAL server in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NEF, OAM, SEAL, and the VAL server act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.700-99: clause 6.3.1.2, where the network slice capability enablement server maps a VAL application's requirement to a slice API backed by a list of NEF APIs, SEAL APIs, or OAM-provided APIs; and clause 6.3.1.3, where the VAL server sends a slice API invocation request to that enablement server, referencing the same NEF/SEAL/OAM-backed service APIs.

questions.question: For network-slice capability enablement toward a VAL server, which procedures put the EGMF, the NSCE server, and the VAL server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The EGMF, the NSCE server, and the VAL server act together in a step across seven clauses: slice de-allocation (TS 23.435, 9.12.2.1.3), where the NSCE server invokes network-slice de-allocation exposed by the EGMF; fault diagnosis reporting (TS 23.435, 9.15.2.1), where the VAL server sends a fault diagnosis report through the NSCE server reusing fault-management services exposed by the EGMF; slice-requirements alignment subscription (TS 23.435, 9.16.2.1), where the VAL server subscribes the NSCE server to verify slice requirements; MnS discovery (TS 23.435, 9.6.2.1 and 9.6.2.2), where the NSCE server discovers management services for a target slice/VAL application, with exposure via CAPIF or EGMF; and communication-service disengagement (TS 23.700-99, 6.11.1.2) and slice-requirements-alignment authorization/response (TS 23.700-99, 6.19.1.2), where the NSCE server responds to VAL-server requests, retrieving slice performance data exposed by the EGMF.

questions.question: For CS-to-PS SRVCC access transfer, which procedures put the ATCF, the ATGW, and the MSC server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The ATCF, the ATGW, and the MSC server act together in a step across eight clauses spanning TS 34.229-1 (12.27.2, 12.27a.2), TS 24.237 (A.4.3, A.18.6, A.20.2, A.20.3), TS 23.237 (B.2.1), and TS 23.334 (6.2.14.4): the MSC server sends a codec-carrying Re-INVITE / session-transfer request to the ATCF, which selects/negotiates codecs and decides whether transcoding is needed in the ATGW versus the CS-MGW; the ATCF (as IMS-ALG) configures the ATGW (IMS-AGW) to anchor and transcode media between access legs; and, in access-transfer completion flows, the ATCF exchanges SIP INFO/INVITE/BYE with the MSC server while reconfiguring the media path through the ATGW.

questions.question: For MBSFN/SC-PTM MBMS session control, which procedures put the MME, the MCE, and the MBMS session together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MME, the MCE and the MBMS session act together in a step across two clauses of TS 36.300: MBMS Session Start (15.7.1.1), where the MME sends an MBMS Session Start Request to the MCE(s), and the MCE decides SC-PTM vs. MBSFN, checks radio resources, forwards the session start toward eNBs, and confirms reception to the MME; and MBMS Session Stop (15.7.1.2), where the MME sends an MBMS Session Stop Request to the MCE(s), which confirms reception back to the MME.

questions.question: For NBMP-enabled FLUS media processing, which procedures put an external application (EA), an MPE (media processing entity), and NBMP workflow control in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The EA, an MPE, and NBMP workflow control appear together in a step across three clauses of TS 26.939: the WM-MPE-Sink deployment call flow (8.4.3.4.1), where the EA requests the MPE's capabilities, the MPE responds, and the NBMP Client/Workflow Manager instantiates a workflow on the assigned MPE; the equivalent flow in clause 8.4.4.3, where the EA picks a FLUS Sink that can run the workflow on its MPE by discovering the NBMP Workflow Manager and Media Sink address; and the WM-MPE-Sink-AF flow (8.4.6.2), where the Application/FLUS Control Source discovers and connects to a FLUS Sink that runs the NBMP workflow on its MPE.

questions.question: For UE positioning via LPP, which procedures put the AMF, the LMF, and LPP signalling in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF, the LMF, and LPP signalling act together in a step across four clauses of TS 38.305: bidirectional LPP PDU transfer (6.4.2), where the AMF relays LPP PDUs between the LMF and UE via DL NAS Transport / Namf_Communication_N1MessageNotify and Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer; UE-capability request (7.1.3), where the LMF sends an LPP Request Capabilities message to the UE based on access-type information received from the AMF; and periodic/triggered location handling (7.3.2, 7.3.3), where the AMF sends a location request to the LMF (or invokes Nlmf_DetermineLocation_Request), the LMF instigates LPP procedures with the UE to obtain location/capabilities, and returns the location estimate to the AMF.

questions.question: For SRVCC calls with Lawful-Call-Linked-Signalling, which procedures put the GCR, the IAM message, and LCLS handling together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The GCR, the IAM message, and LCLS handling appear together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.284: clauses 13.4.3.2.7 and 13.4.4.7.2, where the sMSC server, if it supports LCLS, modifies the LCLS-Negotiation-Request and LCLS-Configuration-Preference IEs before sending the IAM message carrying the GCR with the encapsulated oBSS ID; and clause 13.5.2.2.2, where MSC-B sends the IAM message with a supported-codecs list, the GCR carrying the encapsulated BSS-B ID, and the same LCLS IEs.

questions.question: For roaming analytics exchange, which procedures put the HPLMN, the NWDAF's roaming-exchange function, and the VPLMN together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The HPLMN, the RE-NWDAF, and the VPLMN act together in a step across four clauses of TS 23.288: outbound-roaming analytics request handling (6.1.5.2 and 6.1.5.3), where the H-RE-NWDAF checks roaming agreements and user consent, discovers the V-RE-NWDAF via the NRF, forwards the roaming analytics request, and each side relays the resulting analytics back to its own PLMN's consumer NF; and roaming input-data exposure (6.2.10 and 6.2.11), where the H-RE-NWDAF and V-RE-NWDAF discover each other via the NRF and each checks whether the counterpart PLMN is authorised to subscribe to the indicated input data before restricting/exposing it.

questions.question: For mission-critical interconnection between MC systems, which procedures put the ACM server, ACMS interconnection, and the MC system in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The ACM server and ACMS-to-ACMS interconnection act together in a step across five clauses of TS 23.700-38: authorised-user-authorisation check (7.5.1.2), where an ACMC must be authorised by its primary ACMS before any cross-system exchange; group-membership update (7.6.1.2.1), where the ACM server of MC system A sends an update request to the ACM server of MC system B and stores the response; remove-user-configuration handling (7.8.1.3), where the primary ACM server stores the remove-user response; group-information provisioning (7.11.1.3.1), where the primary ACM server forwards a provisioning request to the partner ACM server and stores the response; and UE-initial-configuration update (7.9.1.3), where the primary ACMS sends an update to the partner ACMS, which processes it and may involve an ACM client.

questions.question: For UAV location monitoring via SEAL, which procedures put the LMS, the UAE server, and the UAV together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The LMS, the UAE server, and the UAV act together in a step across six clauses spanning TS 23.255 (7.2.2.1, 7.4.2.4, 7.6.2.5, 7.8.2.2) and TS 23.700-55 (7.4.2.2, 7.7.2.3.3): the UAE server obtains other UAVs' location information from the LMS; the UAE server receives periodical/event-based UAV location reports from the SEAL LM server; the UAE server tracks UAV location via LMS on-demand monitoring or subscription and detects area/USS-overlap changes; and UAE server 1 uses its associated LMS to build/update a dynamic UE-location group in the proximity of a host UAV.

questions.question: For S-CSCF restoration and (de)registration handling, which procedures put the CSCF, the HSS, and IMPI/IMPU identities together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The CSCF, the HSS, and IMPI/IMPU identities act together in a step across two clauses: P-CSCF restoration indication handling (TS 23.632, 5.4.2), where the HSS receives a restoration indication from the S-CSCF carrying the user's IMPU and IMPI; and S-CSCF (de)registration via Nhss_ImsUECM (TS 29.562, 5.2.2.4.2), where the HSS checks the stored S-CSCF name against the received one and, given an IMPI, deregisters all associated IMPUs, or given an IMPU, deregisters it and its Implicit Registration Set.

questions.question: For mobile number portability routing, which procedures put MNP handling, the MSISDN, and the SRF (MNP-SRF) together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MNP handling, the MSISDN, and the SRF (MNP-SRF) act together in a step across six clauses of TS 23.066 (B.4.3, B.4.4, B.4.6, B.4.7, B.4.8, B.4.9): each shows an MNP-SRF (at various points, e.g. MNP-SRFA/MNP-SRFB/MNP-SRFB') receiving a message, analysing the MSISDN in the CdPA against NP database information, and either populating the CdPA with an HLRB address (call-related case) or with a routeing number / routeing-number-plus-MSISDN (non-call-related case) before re-routing the message.

questions.question: For IMS media-gating over Rx, which procedures put the CSCF, PCC rules, and the PCF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The (P-)CSCF, PCC rules, and the PCF act together in a step across two clauses of TS 29.513: enabling of IP flows (B.3.2), where the PCF approves enabling and updates the flow status of affected PCC rules before replying to the P-CSCF; and subscription to PLMN-identifier-change notification at IMS registration (B.8), where the PCF subscribes to required QoS-level events for the affected PCC rules on behalf of the P-CSCF's request.

questions.question: For packet-core health-check and PDU-session restoration for IMS, which procedures put the PCF/PCRF, the PGW/SMF, and health-check signalling together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PCF/PCRF, the PGW/SMF, and health-check signalling act together in a step across two clauses of TS 29.866-110: clause 6.5.1.2, where the PGW-C/SMF detects that all PCRF/PCF instances have failed and falls back to a local default IMS bearer; and clause 6.9.1.2, where the SMF/PGW-C detects a UPF/PGW-U failure via PFCP heartbeat and triggers PDU-session restoration, the P-CSCF initiates a packet-core health-check via an Rx AAR to the PCF/PCRF, and the PCF/PCRF relays the health-check outcome back to the P-CSCF via an Rx RAR.

questions.question: For ported-number call routing with routeing-number insertion, which procedures put GMSCA, the IAM message, and the MSISDN/RN together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: GMSCA, the IAM message, and the MSISDN/RN act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.066 (C.3.3, C.3.4, C.3.5): each shows GMSCA using the RN (plus MSISDN) to route the call to GMSCB in the subscription network, with the RN optionally added to the IAM message depending on the interconnect agreement.

questions.question: For legacy 2G/3G MBMS bearer control, which procedures put the BSC, an MBMS bearer service, and the RNC together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The BSC, an MBMS bearer service, and the RNC act together in a step across four clauses of TS 23.246: MBMS Session Start (8.3.1), where the SGSN sends an MBMS Session Start Request to each BSC/RNC, which establishes radio resources and an MBMS Service Context; MBMS Session Update (8.8.3), where the SGSN forwards an MBMS Session Update Request to the BSCs/RNCs; MBMS Session Stop (8.5.1), where the SGSN sends an MBMS Session Stop Request and the BSC/RNC releases the affected radio/Iu resources; and MBMS de-registration (8.6.1), where the SGSN sends an MBMS De-Registration Request and the BSC/RNC releases bearer resources and responds.

questions.question: For VAL applications discovering and subscribing to SEALDD service, which procedures put CAPIF, SEALDD service, and the VAL server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: CAPIF, SEALDD service, and the VAL server act together in a step across eight clauses spanning TS 23.433 (9.2.2.2, 9.3.2.1, 9.7.2.1, 9.8.2, 9.9.2.1) and TS 23.700-34 (6.2.2.2, 6.12.2.2, 6.18.2.2): the VAL server discovers a SEALDD server via CAPIF, then sends a service request such as Sdd_RegularTransmission, Sdd_URLLCTransmission, a transmission-quality-measurement subscription, a bandwidth-limit request, or a SEALDD service subscription request; the SEALDD server performs authorization and responds accordingly.

questions.question: For BPCF-initiated IP-CAN session modification acknowledgement, which procedures put the BPCF, a CCA/CCR Diameter exchange, and the PCRF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The BPCF, a CCA/CCR Diameter exchange, and the PCRF act together in a step across two clauses of TS 29.213 (E.4.4.1.2 and E.4.4.2.2), both showing the V-PCRF sending a Diameter CCR to the H-PCRF to report a PCC/QoS rule failure, the H-PCRF acknowledging with a Diameter CCA back toward the BPCF (directly, or via the V-PCRF in the roaming case), and the V-PCRF forwarding the CCA onward to the BPCF.

questions.question: Which procedures put MBMS coverage, the MCCH, and the session's TMGI in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MBMS coverage, the MCCH, and the session TMGI appear together in a step across two near-identical clauses of TS 23.468 (5.3.3.2 and 5.3.3.3): the UE monitors the SIBs to detect the TMGI advertised on MCCH, which is how it determines it has returned to MBMS coverage for the MBMS bearer service.

questions.question: For IoT traffic-pattern coordination, which procedures put the IoT-PCS server, SEAL-based signalling, and the IoT-App VAL server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The IoT-PCS server and the IoT-App VAL/SEAL server act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.700-97: clause 5.7.2.2, where the IoT-PCS server aggregates traffic-pattern and monitoring subscriptions from multiple IoT-App VAL/SEAL servers, sends traffic-pattern update notifications to them, and executes management/5GC-exposure procedures on their behalf; and clause 5.7.2.4, where the IoT-PCS server requests service-specific traffic-pattern configuration for given UEs from the IoT-App VAL/SEAL server.

questions.question: For PIN element management-client (PEMC) trust verification, which procedures put the NEF, the PEMC, the UDM, and the UDR together in the same step?
