questions.reference_answer: The NEF, the PEMC, the UDM, and the UDR act together in a step across six clauses of TS 23.700-88 (6.8.2.1.1, 6.8.2.1.2, 6.8.2.1.3, 6.8.2.1.5, 6.8.2.1.6, 6.8.2.2.3): the PINMF checks with the UDR, via the UDM or NEF, whether a GPSI-identified UE has subscribed to be a PEMC, whether additional/newly-added PEMCs are Trust Members, whether a PEMC is allowed to manage a PIN, or to query trust members of a PEMC/PIN manager — with the NEF verifying that the requesting PINMF is the one registered with that Trust Member Group.

questions.question: For PC5 unicast-link QoS-flow modification, which procedures put the GFBR/MFBR bit rates, PFI, and PQI together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: GFBR/MFBR, PFI, and PQI act together in a step across two clauses: V2X PC5 unicast-link modification (TS 23.287, 6.3.3.4) and ProSe PC5 unicast-link modification (TS 23.304, 6.4.3.4), both showing UE-1 sending a Link Modification Request to add/modify/remove PC5 QoS Flow(s), each Flow carrying its PFI and PQI (plus MFBR/GFBR where applicable), and UE-2 responding with a Link Modification Accept echoing the same QoS Info.

questions.question: For application-client registration with edge configuration awareness, which procedures put the AC, an ASP service agreement, the ECS, and the EEC together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AC, an ASP service agreement, the ECS, and the EEC act together in a step across two near-identical clauses (TS 23.558, 8.14.2.2.2; TS 23.700-98, 7.34.2.2.2): the AC sends an AC registration request to the EEC carrying its profile, security credentials, and optionally ECS configuration information (set per the ASP-ECSP service agreement); the EEC validates and registers the request, then responds with an AC registration response listing which EEC services the AC is authorized for.

questions.question: For sidelink positioning discovery, which procedures put LCS-style discovery, RSPP metadata, and sidelink (SL) solicitation/response together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: RSPP metadata and sidelink discovery act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.586: clause 6.4.2.1, where the Discoverer UE sends a Ranging/SL Positioning Solicitation message with RSPP metadata and the matching Discoveree UE responds with a Ranging/SL Positioning Response; and clause 6.4.2.2, the group-member variant, where the Discoverer UE sends a Group member discovery Solicitation (with Group ID and RSPP metadata) and a matching Discoveree UE in that group responds with the corresponding Response message.

questions.question: For 5G ProSe relay key derivation, which procedures put the PRUK identity, the Relay Service Code (RSC), and the SUCI together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PRUK identity, the RSC, and the SUCI act together in a step across three clauses of TS 33.740: emergency UE-to-network relay connection (6.27.2), where a USIM-equipped Remote UE sends a Direct Communication Request containing PRUK ID or SUCI, Emergency RSC, and a key-freshness parameter to the Relay, which then runs UP/CP security procedures; UE-to-UE relay key request (6.3.2.1), where the Source UE sends a DCR with PRUK ID/SUCI and the Relay's RSC, and the Relay forwards a Key Request with the same identifiers to the 5GC; and UE-to-UE relay-2 authorization (6.31.2.1), where relay-2 sends a further Key Request with the Source UE's PRUK ID/SUCI and the previously received RSC to the 5GC to derive KNRP and complete security-mode signalling.

questions.question: For GAN registration lifecycle management, which procedures put GA-RC signalling, the GANC, and MS registration/deregistration together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: GA-RC signalling and the GANC act together on MS registration state across eight clauses spanning TS 43.318 (8.4.1.6.1, 8.4.2, 8.4.3, 8.14.2, B.2) and TS 43.902 (5.2.5.4.2, 5.2.5.4.3): GAN registration handling (8.4.1.6.1), where the GANC accepts, redirects, or rejects an MS's GA-RC REGISTER REQUEST; deregistration (8.4.2, 9.14.3, 8.14.2, 5.2.5.4.2), where the GANC sends GA-RC DEREGISTER to the MS, or the MS sends it to the GANC (with the GANC commanding release of resources if it hasn't received it first); registration update (8.4.3, 5.2.5.4.3), where the GANC sends GA-RC REGISTER UPDATE DOWNLINK with updated system information, optionally followed by a redirect or deregister; and UARFCN selection guidance for GA-RC REGISTER ACCEPT (B.2).

questions.question: For dual-connectivity and L2 relay handover status transfer, which procedures put PDCP status, RLC AM, and SN STATUS TRANSFER-style signalling together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: PDCP status preservation over RLC AM and SN STATUS TRANSFER-style signalling act together in a step across four clauses: MR-DC SN modification (TS 37.340, 10.3.1), where an SN Status Transfer occurs between the MN and the SN when the PDCP termination point changes for RLC-AM bearers; and three L2 U2N Remote-UE handover clauses in TS 38.300 (16.12.6.1, 16.12.6.2, 16.12.6.3), each showing the source gNB sending an SN STATUS TRANSFER message to the target gNB carrying the uplink PDCP SN receiver status and downlink PDCP SN transmitter status for RLC-AM DRBs.

questions.question: For GAN security-gateway resolution, which procedures put a DNS query, the SEGW's FQDN, and the security gateway together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: A DNS query, the SEGW's FQDN, and the SEGW act together in a step across two clauses (TS 43.318, 8.4.1.6.1; TS 43.902, 5.2.5.4.1): if the MS was provided the FQDN of the Default or Serving SEGW, the MS performs a DNS query via the generic IP access network interface to resolve it to an IP address, unless it already has a provisioned IP address for the SEGW.

questions.question: For DCAF-mediated analytics exposure to UE applications, which procedures put the DCAF, a DNN, and NSSAI together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The DCAF, a DNN, and NSSAI act together in a step across two clauses: UE-ID retrieval by DCAF (TS 23.700-28, 6.15.2.3), where the DCAF requests a UE ID via Nnef_UEID_Get, the NEF retrieves session-binding information (SUPI/GPSI, S-NSSAI, DNN) from the BSF, and DCAF retrieves the S-NSSAI+DNN of the UE's PDU session; and the analytics-request procedure (TS 23.700-80, 6.2.2.4), where the UE sends an Analytics Request to the DCAF via application-layer signalling optionally including S-NSSAI, and the DCAF likewise retrieves the S-NSSAI+DNN of the UE's configured PDU session.

questions.question: For selecting a common DNAI/EAS across a UE group, which procedures put the DNAI, the EAS, and the SMF's Edge-relocation-Data-Information (EDI) together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The DNAI, the EAS, and the SMF's EDI act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.700-48: clause 6.34.2, where the SMF checks the EDI for an already-selected DNAI/EAS for a Dynamic External Group ID and, if none exists, selects one and updates the EDI (notifying subscribed SMFs); and clauses 6.38.2.1 and 6.38.2.2, which reuse the EAS Discovery procedure with the difference that the SMF determines N6 traffic routing information for the selected DNAI based on the N6 routing information stored in the EDI.

questions.question: For fetching and provisioning packet-flow descriptions, which procedures put the NEF, a PFD, the PFDF, and the UDR together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The NEF(PFDF) and the UDR act together over PFD data in a step across three clauses of TS 23.502/TS 23.700-81: PFD provisioning with NWDAF assistance (TS 23.502, 4.18.2.2), where the NEF(PFDF) fetches PFD information from the UDR, compares it against NWDAF-observed data, and invokes Nudr_DM_Create/Update/Delete accordingly; the retrieval-of-PFDs-for-application-detection procedure (TS 23.502, 4.18.3.1), where the NEF(PFDF) queries the UDR via Nudr_DM_Query if the PFDs aren't already cached; and the equivalent NWDAF-assisted procedure in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.9.4.

questions.question: For SGd Diameter interworking, which procedures put an IDR message, the IWF, the MME, and the SGSN together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: An IDR message, the IWF, the MME, and the SGSN act together in a step across two clauses of TS 29.305 (7.5.1 and 7.10.1): both show the IWF constructing an Insert-Data-Request (IDR) message and sending it to the MME, the SGSN, or a combined MME/SGSN.

questions.question: For application-client-managed application context relocation, which procedures put the AC, ACR handling, EDGE-interface signalling, and the EEC together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AC, ACR handling, and the EEC act together over EDGE interfaces in a step across four clauses: EEC-services subscription (TS 23.558, 8.14.2.5.2) and the equivalent AC subscription request (TS 23.700-98, 7.34.2.2.5), where the AC subscribes the EEC to EAS discovery/dynamic-information and ACR-management operations (ACR notifications, ACR monitoring, or EEC-managed ACR) over EDGE-1; and ACR-modification notification (TS 23.700-98, 7.6.2.1.1 and 7.6.2.1.2), where the EEC detects a change in expected UE behaviour reported by the AC over EDGE-5 and optionally notifies the AC back of the ACR modification result.

questions.question: For emergency IMS registration under RLOS, which procedures put the CSCF and RLOS handling together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The CSCF and RLOS handling act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.228: clause Z.3.1, where the P-CSCF, based on the RLOS indication for a roaming subscriber without a roaming agreement, forwards the Register information to the S-CSCF configured for RLOS, and the S-CSCF either responds 420 (GIBA supported) or 403 with a temporary unauthenticated registration record; and clause Z.3.2.1, the I-CSCF variant, where the P-CSCF forwards Register information to the I-CSCF, which queries the HSS and selects an RLOS-capable S-CSCF, and the S-CSCF likewise creates a temporary registration record on failed authentication.

questions.question: For emergency-call location handling across a handover, which procedures put the GMLC and the LRF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The GMLC and the LRF act together in a step across five clauses: post-handover MT-LR handling in TS 23.271 (9.4.5.4.2, 9.4.5.4.3, 9.4.5.4.4), where the LRF instigates an MT-LR via the target GMLC/E-SLP after handover and the LRF/source and target location servers are reconfigured; and 5GC positioning-information retrieval in TS 23.273 (6.10.2, 6.10.3), where the LRF/GMLC determines the AMF and invokes Namf_Location_ProvidePositioningInfo to obtain the current UE location for an emergency session.

questions.question: For CS-domain call teardown at IMS/PSTN boundaries, which procedures put the MSC and a REL message together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC and a REL message act together in a step across two clauses: call-waiting/setup signalling (TS 23.292, 7.6.3.10.1), where the MSC Server may send a REL response immediately depending on call-waiting settings, and maps a Release Complete to a REL message; and video-call failure handling (TS 23.903, 4.4.1), where MSC B sends a REL message to MSC A in each failure scenario (unsupported video calls, resource unavailability, or callee rejection).

questions.question: For CS-to-PS access transfer with media transcoding, which procedures put the IMS-AGW (ATGW) and the IMS-ALG (ATCF) together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The IMS-AGW (ATGW) and the IMS-ALG (ATCF) act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.334: media-anchoring without transcoding (6.2.14.3), where the ATCF sends an H.248 ADD request to the ATGW to create incoming/outgoing terminations and the ATGW replies with allocated address/port information that the ATCF folds into the SDP; and access-transfer with transcoding (6.2.14.4), where the ATCF signals media sub-fields to the ATGW for a target access leg, the ATGW determines whether transcoding is needed and creates/releases terminations accordingly, and reports back to the ATCF.

questions.question: For local-breakout PDU session handling and URSP generation, which procedures put the AMF and LBO information/authorization together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF and LBO information/authorization act together in a step across five clauses: PDU session modification/release with LBO branching (TS 23.502, 4.12.6 and 4.12.7), where the AMF drives the non-roaming/LBO branch of the underlying PDU Session Modification/Release procedure; dynamic LBO setup for edge connectivity (TS 23.700-48, 6.27.2), where the AMF receives an LBO-authorized indication and target DNAI from the (V-)SMF and later uses it to select a local UPF for the next PDU session; and VPLMN URSP generation with LBO roaming data (TS 23.700-85, 6.28.2.1 and 6.28.2.2), where the AMF retrieves LBO information (DNN/S-NSSAI, SSC mode) and URSP-generation indications from the UDM during registration and forwards them to the V-PCF when creating the UE Policy Association.

questions.question: For SEAL Location Management server operations, which procedures put the LM server and the VAL server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The LM server and the VAL server act together in a step across five clauses: UAV location reporting (TS 23.255, 7.4.2.4), where the UAE Server (as a VAL server) receives location reports from the SEAL LM server; area-of-interest monitoring (TS 23.434, 9.3.11.2), where the VAL server subscribes the LM server to monitor a VAL UE's presence/absence in an area of interest and the LM server notifies Presence/Absence/Mismatch results; VAL-UE registration (9.3.15) and registration update (9.3.18), where the LM Client sends a location-service registration(-update) request identifying the VAL UE and the LM server checks authorization; and location-report triggering (9.3.14.2), where the LM Server receives a reporting trigger from the VAL server and sends back the location information report.

questions.question: For H(e)NB security-gateway certificate validation, which procedures put the H(e)NB and OCSP-based revocation checking together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The H(e)NB and OCSP-based certificate-revocation checking act together in a step across four clauses of TS 33.320: post-tunnel OCSP checking (7.2.3), where the H(e)NB sends an OCSP request to the responder after the IPsec tunnel is established if it had no access earlier; SeGW-side revocation checking (7.2.4); and device-only (A.1) and combined device/HP (A.2) authentication call flows, where the H(e)NB retrieves SeGW certificate status from the OCSP responder (or embeds an OCSP request in the IKE message) and verifies the SeGW certificate using the OCSP response, while the SeGW may likewise check the H(e)NB's certificate via CRL or OCSP.

questions.question: For sidelink positioning group-key provisioning, which procedures put sidelink (SL) signalling and the SLPKMF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Sidelink signalling and the SLPKMF act together in a step across three clauses: unicast group-key request/response (TS 33.533, 6.4.4.2, and the equivalent TS 33.893, 6.15.2.1), where a UE sends a Key Request to the SLPKMF with its Ranging/SL positioning application identifier, and the SLPKMF replies with a Key Response containing the SLPGK, SLPGK ID, validity time and chosen algorithms; and SL broadcast group-key provisioning (TS 33.893, 6.28.2), where UE1 sends a broadcast authorization request to the SLPKMF and UE2/UE3/UE4 each send a Broadcast Key Request to the SLPKMF carrying the temporary group ID and Zone ID.

questions.question: For NBMP-enabled FLUS session establishment, which procedures put the External Application (EA) and the UE Application (UA) together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The EA and the UA act together in a step across four clauses of TS 26.939 (8.4.2.4.1, 8.4.3.4.1, 8.4.4.3, 8.4.6.2): the UA makes an F8 request to the EA to start a live session, and the EA responds with FLUS Control Sink/Media Sink information (and, in the deeper deployment scenarios, the NBMP Client acknowledges workflow instantiation back to the EA once the FLUS Control Source has discovered a Sink and established the FLUS session).

questions.question: For MBS media transport function provisioning and distribution, which procedures put an MBS session/distribution session and the MBSTF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: An MBS session/distribution session and the MBSTF act together in a step across six clauses: MBS session deletion (TS 23.247, 7.1.1.4), where the MBSF requests the MBSTF to release user-plane resources if one was inserted; FEC protection setup (TS 23.289, 7.3.3.13.2), where the MC service server sends an FEC request to the MBSF/MBSTF, which then performs FEC encoding and delivers it over 5G MBS; MC data file distribution over MBS (TS 23.783, 6.34.1.1.2), where the MCData server signals file transmission over the MBS user service and the MBSTF fetches or receives the file for distribution to MCData clients; and MBS Distribution Session provisioning/activation in TS 26.502 (5.2, 5.3, 5.3A), where the MBSF creates and subscribes to status of the MBS Distribution Session in the MBSTF, and the MBSTF establishes content ingest and notifies the MBSF of the outcome.

questions.question: For DAPS handover across radio bearers, which procedures put DAPS handling and a DRB together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: DAPS handling and a DRB act together in a step across six clauses: E-UTRAN eNodeB status transfer for DAPS DRBs (TS 23.401, 5.5.1.2.2a) and the corresponding 5GS handover-success handling (TS 23.502, 4.9.1.3.3a); NR DAPS handover with key change conformance tests (TS 38.523-1, 8.1.4.3.1 and 8.1.4.3.2), where the source gNB requests a DAPS handover for one or more DRBs and the UE suspends/releases source-cell resources per DRB after execution; PDCP COUNT transfer for a DAPS DRB (TS 38.523-3, 7.3.5.3.5), where the source and target cells exchange PDCP COUNT for the DAPS-configured DRB; and the RRC reconfiguration test procedure that reconfigures a DRB as a DAPS radio bearer (TS 38.533, 6.3.1.10).

questions.question: For RAT/Frequency Selection Priority continuity across 4G/5G interworking, which procedures put the MME and the RFSP index together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MME and the RFSP index act together in a step across six clauses of TS 23.700-89: RFSP storage and expiry handling (6.2.2), where the MME stores the Subscribed/Authorized RFSP with a validity condition and provides it to the eNB; RFSP-in-use provisioning with validity time (6.4.2), where the MME stores and re-evaluates the RFSP index in use as the validity time expires; inter-MME handover of RFSP context (6.6.2), where the AMF/source MME forwards the RFSP Index in use and its validity timer to the target MME; UDM+HSS-provided Authorized RFSP (6.7.2), where the MME stores and uses the value received from UDM+HSS; and RFSP index updates via PCF/HSS notification (6.9.2.1, 6.9.2.2), where the MME updates its in-use RFSP index and forwards it to the eNB.

questions.question: For E-UTRAN interworking with cdma2000 HRPD access, which procedures put HRPD signalling and the MME together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: HRPD signalling and the MME act together in a step across seven clauses: emergency-call location handling on handover to HRPD (TS 23.271, 9.4.5.4.2), where the source SGSN/MME reports handover events (excluding HRPD-specific identity in some fields); HRPD pre-registration and handover (TS 23.402, 9.3.1 and 9.3.2), where the MME tunnels HRPD messages to/from the HRPD access network over S101, allocates GRE keys, and configures indirect data forwarding; inter-eNodeB handover with MME relocation for HRPD (TS 23.402, 9.7), where the old/new MME manage the S101 tunnel with the HRPD Access Network; and enhanced 1xCS fallback with concurrent HRPD handover (TS 23.272, B.2.3a.2 to B.2.3a.4), where the MME sets CS-Fallback and priority indications and treats the HRPD PS handover independently of the 1xCS fallback signalling.

questions.question: For common-DNAI edge-application relocation across a group of UEs, which procedures put the EAS and the UPF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The EAS and the UPF act together in a step across eight clauses of TS 23.700-48/TS 23.700-27: satellite UL-CL/local-PSA selection based on EAS information (TS 23.700-27, 6.5.2); common-DNAI selection and UPF reselection when the SCMF signals a new common DNAI (TS 23.700-48, 6.15.3.3, 6.15.3.4, 6.15.3.5), with the application client and EAS exchanging traffic through the (new) UPF; roaming EASDF/DNS-routing setup (6.3.2.1), where V-SMF configures V-UPF to route DNS queries to V-EASDF and other traffic to the H-PSA; roaming charging/offload via V-UPF (6.5.2.1), where the V-SMF inserts/relocates UL-CL/BP V-UPF for traffic to the V-EAS and configures usage-reporting rules; and group-based EAS relocation (6.35.2, 6.36.2), where the SMF inserts a BP/local UPF so the application client can reach the (re)located EAS.

questions.question: For discovering edge configuration servers when OAM-provided information is unavailable, which procedures put the ECS and OAM configuration together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The ECS and OAM configuration act together in a step across three clauses: partner-ECS query authorization (TS 23.558, 8.17.2.4.2.2), where the partner ECS authorizes the request and gathers EDN provisioning information; and ECS discovery (TS 23.700-98, 7.50.2.2 and 7.50.2.3), where the Primary ECS retrieves configuration information of partner ECS(s) using preconfigured information, information configured via OAM, or a discovery mechanism via the ECS-ER.

questions.question: For SGd Diameter interworking with subscriber-data withdrawal, which procedures put the HSS and an IDR message together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The HSS and an IDR message act together in a step across three clauses of TS 29.305: clauses 7.5.2 and 7.10.2, where IWF2 receives an Insert-Subscriber-Data-Request (IDR) message from the HSS; and clause A.4.4.6.2, where the IWF acknowledges a DeleteSubscriberData from the HSS and, if the SMS subscription is withdrawn, sends its own IDR to the MME to remove the MME's SMS registration.

questions.question: For QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping in the AS layer, which procedures put the DRB and the QFI together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The DRB and the QFI act together in a step across six clauses of TS 38.300, annex A: initial DRB/QFI-mapping-rule establishment for a new PDU session (A.1); reflective-QoS updates when the gNB sends a DL packet with new QFI/RDI (A.2); explicit mapping-rule update via RRCReconfiguration (A.3); new-QoS-flow mapping with a NAS message (A.4); QFI-to-DRB mapping-rule release without releasing the DRB itself, since it still carries other flows (A.5); and default-DRB fallback when a QFI has no existing mapping rule (A.6).

questions.question: For USIM-based authentication and key derivation, which procedures put the ME and the USIM together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The ME and the USIM act together in a step across eight clauses: operator-defined access category persistence (TS 31.121, 5.4.11.2 and 5.4.12.2), where the ME checks the SUPI from the USIM against the stored SUPI before reusing category definitions; ProSe out-of-coverage direct communication (TS 32.277, 5.2.2.3.3), where the UE uses pre-configured resources in the USIM or ME; GBA-Push key derivation (TS 33.223, 5.1.4), where the ME issues an Authenticate command to the USIM and processes the returned Ks; 5G-AKA' authentication (TS 33.501, 6.1.3.1), where the ME forwards RAND/AUTN to the USIM and the USIM returns RES/CK/IK; and false-base-station protection key handling (TS 33.809, 6.9.2.2.1, 6.9.2.3.1, 6.9.2.3.2), where the ME sends NONCE/EKRBS material to the USIM and the USIM returns CKp or XMAC-I/Ke for verification.

questions.question: For UE-mobility-driven data-collection handover, which procedures put the AMF and the DCCF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF and the DCCF act together in a step across four clauses: source/target DCCF subscription-context transfer on UE mobility (TS 23.288, 6.2.6.3.8), where the source DCCF subscribes to AMF UE-mobility events and determines whether to transfer the subscription context to a target DCCF; the equivalent multi-UE transfer procedure (TS 23.700-81, 6.66.2); area-of-interest notification (TS 23.700-81, 6.12.2), where the AMF notifies DCCF-1 that the UE has entered a new area of interest; and MTLF re-training data collection (TS 23.700-81, 6.6.2), where the NWDAF containing MTLF may collect data from NFs including the AMF/DCCF/ADRF to re-train an ML model.

questions.question: For SRVCC handover to GERAN with session continuity, which procedures put GERAN and SRVCC handling together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: GERAN and SRVCC handling act together in a step across three clauses of TS 36.523-1: SRVCC handover triggering (11.2.12), where the source E-UTRAN decides to trigger an SRVCC handover to GERAN and, after completion, PS services are resumed and a Subscriber Location Report may be sent for emergency continuity; SRVCC-capable UE behaviour for eCall/session release (11.3.8), where the SRVCC UE indicates SRVCC capability and supports in-band MSD transfer after handover to GERAN/UTRAN; and IMS session re-establishment on failed/cancelled SRVCC (13.4.3.41), where the UE sends a SIP re-INVITE/UPDATE toward IMS after failing to retune to GERAN/UTRAN.

questions.question: For IMS roaming call routing and CS-domain registration, which procedures put the CSCF and the HPLMN together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The CSCF and the HPLMN act together in a step across six clauses: optimal-media-routing loopback vs. home routing decisions (TS 23.228, M.3.1.3 and M.3.1.4), where the S-CSCF decides whether to route back to the VPLMN or anchor media in the HPLMN; PLMN-change re-registration with encryption update (TS 23.228, W.4.2 and W.4.3), where the P-CSCF may update SIP signalling encryption per HPLMN/VPLMN roaming agreements during UE re-registration; and MSC-Server-enhanced IMS registration for HPLMN subscribers and inbound roamers (TS 23.292, G.2 and H.5.2.3.1), where the I-CSCF/S-CSCF select the HSS (or the ICS-IWF acting as HSS) based on HPLMN/VPLMN identity comparison.

questions.question: For SRVCC access-transfer signalling via the SCC AS, which procedures put the SCC AS and an STI-addressed INVITE together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The SCC AS and an STI-addressed INVITE act together in a step across four clauses: held-session access transfer with dynamic STI (TS 23.237, 6.3.2.1.2a), where the UE initiates Access Transfer using the dynamic STI and the SCC AS provides Session State Information; ATCF-management registration continuity (TS 23.380, 6.2.2.2), where SCC-AS2 sends a MESSAGE using its own ATU-STI toward the ATCF; PS-to-CS session transfer via static STI (TS 24.237, 9.3.3), where the SCC AS matches the dialog to be transferred and sends a re-INVITE toward the remote UE; and the full SRVCC ATU-STI signalling trace (TS 29.949, 5.11.3), where the ATCF creates a dialog toward the SCC AS via the ATU-STI, and the SCC AS forwards a re-INVITE and relays responses back through the IBCF/S-CSCF chain.

questions.question: For SRVCC codec negotiation across access legs, which procedures put the CS-MGW and the MSC server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The CS-MGW and the MSC server act together in a step across two clauses: SRVCC codec handling (TS 23.237, B.2.1), where the MSC server sends a Re-INVITE with its supported codec list to the ATCF, and transcoding may occur in the CS-MGW (or ATGW) depending on codec overlap; and access-transfer with media transcoding (TS 23.334, 6.2.14.4), where the ATCF receives an SDP offer from the MSC Server and determines whether transcoding is required at the ATGW.

questions.question: For MCPTT signalling-key distribution and MC service delivery, which procedures put an MC UE and the MCX server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: An MC UE and the MCX server act together in a step across four clauses: eMBMS-bearer-based MC service delivery decision (TS 23.783, 6.32.1.1), where the MC service server analyses location information and may announce an eMBMS bearer; signalling-key download (TS 33.180, 5.8.2), where the MCX Server sends a key-download message (SIP NOTIFY/MESSAGE) to the MC UE and the MC UE confirms extraction with a 200 OK; and CSK/SPK-protected session signalling across a security gateway (TS 33.180, L.4.2 and L.4.3), where signalling between the client and MCX server is protected with the CSK and between the MCX server and the SeGy with the SPK.

questions.question: For inter-UE transfer of media in a Collaborative Session, which procedures put an IUT request and the SCC AS together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: An IUT request and the SCC AS act together in a step across six clauses of TS 23.237, annex 6a: media transfer (6a.2.1), where UE-1 sends an IUT media transfer request and the SCC AS responds, making UE-1 the Controller UE; add-media (6a.2.2), where UE-1 requests adding Media Flow-B on UE-2 via the SCC AS; collaborative-session setup (6a.2.3), where UE-1 requests the SCC AS to set up a session split across UE-1 and UE-2; media release (6a.4.3), where UE-1 asks the SCC AS to remove a media flow; media-and-service-control transfer (6a.6.1), where UE-1 transfers a whole session's control to UE-2 via the SCC AS; and supplementary-service execution (6a.7.7.1), where UE-1 asks the SCC AS to invoke HOLD on a media flow hosted on UE-2.

questions.question: For SGd Diameter interworking with update-location handling, which procedures put the HSS and a ULA together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The HSS and a ULA (Update-Location-Answer) act together in a step across three clauses of TS 29.305: clause 7.2.1, where the IWF uses information received from the HSS to construct a ULA sent to the MME/SGSN; clause 7.2.2, where IWF2 receives a ULA from the HSS; and clause A.4.4.2, where the IWF sends a MAP updateLocation with the MME Number for MT SMS if the ULA indicates the SMS-in-MME feature is cleared and NAM is PS+CS, and the HSS answers with a ULA.

questions.question: For PCRF binding and congestion-report routing via the DRA, which procedures put the DRA and the PCRF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The DRA and the PCRF act together in a step across four clauses: RUCI congestion-report routing (TS 23.203, 7.10.1), where the RCAF's RUCI report is routed by the DRA to the appropriate PCRF based on IMSI/APN, which then makes a policy decision; DRA-redirect PCRF selection (TS 29.213, 7.4.2.1.1), where the DRA creates or reuses a DRA binding to select and redirect to the target PCRF; roaming H-DRA redirect (TS 29.213, 7.4.2.1.2), where the H-DRA binds and redirects the V-PCRF's Rx/S9 request to the appropriate H-PCRF; and DRA-binding deletion (TS 29.213, E.6.4.2.2), where the H-PCRF sends a TER to the V-DRA to delete a binding, which returns the TEA.

questions.question: For CS-to-IMS call setup and codec change at the MGCF/MSC boundary, which procedures put the MGCF and the MSC server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MGCF and the MSC server act together in a step across six clauses: incoming-call announcement (TS 23.292, 7.6.3.10.1), where the MGCF sends an IAM to the MSC Server; codec change to multimedia (TS 23.292, 7.9.1.3), where the MSC Server sends a Modify Codec message to the MGCF; call setup/release (TS 23.292, 7.9.2.4 and 7.9.2.5), where the MSC server sends IAM/REL messages to the MGCF; and ICS call-continuity flows (TS 24.292, A.4.2 and A.5.4), where the MSC Server (not enhanced for ICS) maps a SETUP to an ISUP IAM routed to the MGCF, and the MGCF generates an ISUP ANM back to the MSC Server on receiving a SIP 200 OK.

questions.question: For data-channel-signalling-function registration and discovery, which procedures put the DCSF and the NRF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The DCSF and the NRF act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.700-87: DCSF registration (6.17.2.1), where the DCSF sends Nnrf_NFManagement_NFRegister_Request and the NRF stores/acknowledges its profile; and DCSF discovery (6.17.2.2), where the IMS AS sends Nnrf_NFDiscovery_Request to the NRF, which returns matching DCSF instance(s) for selection.

questions.question: For L2 UE-to-Network relay selection reporting, which procedures put an SD-RSRP measurement together with candidate relay reporting in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: SD-RSRP measurements and candidate-relay reporting act together in a step across two clauses of TS 38.300 (16.12.6.2 and 16.12.6.3): the L2 U2N Remote UE, after measuring/discovering candidate L2 U2N Relay UE(s) and filtering by relay-selection criteria, reports one or more candidates to the source gNB including the Relay UE ID, its serving cell ID, and SD-RSRP as the sidelink measurement quantity.

questions.question: For AR split-rendering session establishment via IMS, which procedures put the AR AS/application and the MF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AR AS/application and the MF act together in a step across five clauses: AR session upgrade (TS 23.228, AC.9.3.1), where UE-A initiates a re-INVITE adding AR media descriptors that may anchor a data channel in the MF; network-assisted AR rendering (TS 23.228, AC.9.3.2), where UE-A sends AR data to the MF and the MF performs AR media rendering per the negotiated result and AR AS instructions; split-rendering resource setup (TS 26.264, A.1.3), where the AR AS requests the DCSF/IMS AS to allocate MF rendering resources and the MF forwards the outcome to UE1; scene-description distribution (A.1.4), where the MF distributes scene-description updates to all UEs; and AR media/metadata exchange (A.1.5), where UE1/UE2 send AR media and metadata to the MF, which renders and combines the AR objects.

questions.question: For gNB context setup and RAN-status signalling via the CU, which procedures put the AMF and the gNB-CU together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF and the gNB-CU act together in a step across seven clauses: NG interface setup and UE context establishment (TS 38.401, 8.1, 8.19.1, 8.24.2), where the AMF sends INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST to the gNB-CU and the gNB-CU replies with INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE / INITIAL UE MESSAGE, including clock-quality reporting control information; RAN TSS reporting (8.24.1), where the AMF requests and receives timing-synchronisation-status reports from the gNB-CU; trace control (8.9.7), where the gNB-CU-CP receives TRACE START/DEACTIVATE TRACE from the AMF; and MBSR service-time distribution and mobility (TS 23.700-05, 6.11.3.2 and 6.13.3), where the AMF sends MBSR service-time information via N2 to the NG-RAN (CU) and the IAB-DU/m-CU pair serves as the MBSR's gNB.

questions.question: For Ranging/SL Positioning authorization and policy provisioning, which procedures put the PCF and sidelink (SL) positioning together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The PCF and Ranging/SL Positioning act together in a step across five clauses: UE-policy provisioning that includes Ranging/SL Positioning parameters alongside V2X policy (TS 23.700-86, 6.2.3.1.2) or 5G ProSe policy (6.2.3.2.2), where the PCF determines and delivers the authorized policy; SUPI/Application-Layer-ID registration with the GMLC (6.25.3.3), where the PCF registers and the GMLC stores the UE SUPI to Ranging/SL Positioning Application Layer ID relationship; client-authorization request (TS 33.893, 6.11.2.2), where UE1's and the Client UE's PKMF/PCF exchange Authorization Requests with the Ranging/SL positioning server; and service/privacy authorization checks (6.11.2.3), where the PKMF/DDNMF/PCF checks with the Ranging/SL Positioning Server whether the Client UE and UE1 are authorized.

questions.question: For priority-service call authorization, which procedures put a PIN and the SIM together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: A PIN and the SIM act together in a step across two clauses of TS 22.950 (6.2.2 and 6.3.2): both describe authorizing a subscriber's priority-service call origination based on subscription, with an optional second-level authentication via PIN, alongside priority-level or access-class information stored in the SIM.

questions.question: For application-server invocation via initial filter criteria, which procedures put the CSCF and the ISC interface together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The CSCF and the ISC interface act together in a step across two clauses: presence registration forwarding (TS 23.141, A.2.3.2), where the S-CSCF sends the registration to the Presence Network Agent via the ISC interface; and initial-filter-criteria-triggered AS invocation (TS 23.218, 5.2.3), where the S-CSCF forwards the request via the ISC interface to the matched Application Server, which may modify and return the request back to the S-CSCF via the ISC interface.

questions.question: For V2X dynamic-UE-location-group information sharing, which procedures put a V2X SP and the VAE server/client together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: A V2X SP and VAE servers/clients act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.286: clause 9.16.5.1, where VAE server 1 sends a subscribe-dynamic-information request to VAE clients belonging to the same V2X SP as the host vehicle; and clause 9.16.5.3, where VAE clients and VAE server 2 (of another V2X SP) notify VAE server 1 of dynamic information, using temporary V2X UE IDs if raw IDs aren't shareable per SP agreement.

questions.question: For MCData group short data service, which procedures put the MCData emergency/imminent-peril state (MCPTT-linked) and SDS group data requests together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: MCData emergency/imminent-peril state and SDS group data requests act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.282 (7.4.2.5.2, 7.4.2.6.2, 7.4.2.7.2): MCData client 1 sends a group (session) standalone/data request to the MCData server carrying the group ID or target recipients and a conversation identifier, and if initiating an emergency or imminent-peril short data service communication, sets the corresponding indicator and enters (or is already in) the retained MCData emergency state, tied to the MCPTT emergency state, until explicitly cancelled.

questions.question: For V2X application-enabler (V1-AE) provisioning to the VAE client, which procedures put the V1-AE reference point and the VAE server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The V1-AE reference point and the VAE server act together in a step across five clauses of TS 23.286: local-service-information delivery (9.10.4.2), where the VAE server provides V2X USD and geographic location info to the VAE client; dynamic-group PC5-parameter storage and announcement (9.12.3.2, 9.12.4.2), where the VAE client stores PC5 parameters from the VAE server and may announce dynamic-group info (ProSe Layer-2 Group ID) to nearby VAE clients over PC5; PC5-parameter provisioning (9.15.3.2), where the VAE server provides PC5 parameters via V1-AE; and V2X USD announcement storage (9.6.3.2), where the VAE client stores V2X USDs received via V1-AE.

questions.question: For IOPS-based short data service delivery, which procedures put the MC (IOPS connectivity function) and SDS content together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The IOPS MC connectivity function and SDS content act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.180: private standalone data (10.6.1.3.2), where MCData client 1 sends an IOPS MCData standalone data request (carrying SDS content and a conversation identifier) to the IOPS MC connectivity function for distribution to MCData client 2's IP address; and group standalone data (10.6.1.4.2), where MCData client 1 sends an IOPS MCData group standalone data request with the same SDS content to the IOPS MC connectivity function for distribution to the IOPS group's IP multicast address.

questions.question: For data-channel-media-function registration and discovery, which procedures put the DCMF and the NRF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The DCMF and the NRF act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.700-87: DCMF registration (6.17.3.1), where the DCMF sends Nnrf_NFManagement_NFRegister_Request with its data-channel-media capabilities and the NRF stores/acknowledges its profile; and DCMF discovery (6.17.3.2), where the IMS AS sends Nnrf_NFDiscovery_Request to the NRF, which returns matching DCMF instance(s) for selection.

questions.question: For MC service session-management and location-notification handling via policy control, which procedures put the MC service server and the PCF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The MC service server and the PCF act together in a step across four clauses of TS 23.289: session management with PCF policy enforcement (7.2.4), initiated by the MC service server via direct SIP-core/PCF interaction; path-selection policy provisioning (7.3.3.8.4.3), where the PCF may provide the (remote) MC service UE's path-selection policies; and location-information handling via PCF notification subscription (7.3.3.9.2 and 7.3.3.9.3), where the MC service server subscribes to PCF-related notifications (via N5 or Rx) for events such as access-network-information changes.

questions.question: For Sh/Ud front-end data access, which procedures put the FE (application-specific front-end) and the UDR together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The FE and the UDR act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.335: transparent-data update flow (A.2.3), where the HSS-FE checks AS permissions, fetches service data via Ud Query, updates it via Ud Update with a sequence-number condition, and the UDR stores the new configuration or responds with the requested data; and subscription-to-notification flow (A.3.2), where the FE sends a Subscription Request to the UDR, and the HSS-FE checks permissions and queries the UDR to fetch data needed to process the subscription/notification.

questions.question: For HD-map dynamic information aggregation for V2X applications, which procedures put HD map data and the VAE server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: HD map data and the VAE server act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.286: HD-map subscription (9.16.3), where the V2X application specific server sends a subscribe HD-map-dynamic-information request to VAE server 1, including the host vehicle's V2X UE ID and proximity range; and HD-map aggregation (9.16.5.3), where VAE server 1 aggregates information from different VAE clients to create the HD map dynamic information.

questions.question: For V2X application-server discovery data distribution, which procedures put the USD (user service description) and the VAE server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The USD and the VAE server act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.286: local-service-information response (9.10.4.2), where the VAE server determines and provides V2X server/USD information with geographic-location data to the VAE client; inter-VAE-server local-service exchange (9.10.5), where VAE server 2 determines local USD information and sends it to VAE server 1, which stores it; and V2X USD announcement (9.6.3.2), where the VAE server sends the V2X USD announcement (TMGI, SAI list, frequency, SDP) to the VAE client, which stores the received USDs.

questions.question: For network-assisted-bitrate reporting from a media session handler, which procedures put the Data Collection AF and ANBR-based network-assistance reporting together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: The Data Collection AF and ANBR-based network-assistance reporting act together in a step across two clauses of TS 26.501: downlink ANBR reporting (4.7.2.1), where the Direct Data Collection Client in the Media Session Handler reports ANBR-based downlink Network Assistance invocations to the Data Collection AF in the 5GMSd AF over reference point R2; and uplink ANBR reporting (4.7.2.2), the equivalent flow for uplink Network Assistance via the 5GMSu AF.

questions.question: For SEAL location-management reporting that supplements positioning with non-3GPP sources, which procedures put GNSS-derived location information and the VAL server together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: GNSS-derived location information and the VAL server act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.434: periodic location reporting (9.3.8), where the location management server, triggered by configuration/subscription, reports the UE's latest location to the VAL server, optionally improved using non-3GPP positioning technologies such as GNSS or Bluetooth; and immediate location reporting (9.3.9), the equivalent flow where the location management server immediately sends a location report for one or more VAL users/UEs, likewise potentially considering GNSS/Bluetooth-derived location information.

questions.question: When the network decides to release an MBS session because the AF asked for it, what does the MB-SMF do, and who ends up removing joined UEs?
questions.reference_answer: The MB-SMF notifies the SMF of the multicast session release via Nmbsmf_MBSSession_ContextStatusNotify carrying the MBS Session ID; the SMF then checks all joined UEs and, for each one, initiates the steps to remove it from the MBS session (and may also release associated QoS flows). The MB-SMF may additionally trigger Multicast Session Deactivation toward the NG-RAN to release radio resources early, before or in parallel with notifying the SMF.

questions.question: If the AMF handling a Broadcast MBS session fails without restarting and no replacement AMF proactively notifies the network, how does the MB-SMF recover?
questions.reference_answer: The MB-SMF detects that the AMF handling the Broadcast MBS session has failed without restart, and since no Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextStatusNotify Request arrived from any AMF in the same AMF set, the MB-SMF reselects an alternative AMF itself by sending a Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextUpdate Request. That request indicates the alternative AMF need not trigger any NGAP message to deliver the stored N2 container (MBS Session Setup/Modification Request Transfer) — it just stores it for use if NG-RAN restoration signalling arrives.

questions.question: Our NWDAF thinks a UE it's tracking is about to move outside its coverage area. What can it do before that happens, and when should it hold off?
questions.reference_answer: The source NWDAF can prepare to transfer the analytics subscription to another (target) NWDAF instance ahead of time, using the Nnwdaf_AnalyticsSubscription_Transfer service operation, based on predicting the UE's mobility (e.g. via AMF UE-mobility event exposure or its own/another NWDAF's mobility analytics). It should hold off if it discovers the analytics consumer might change concurrently with the transfer, and must weigh the signalling/load cost of sending prepared data to a candidate NWDAF that may never end up serving the UE.

questions.question: Network performance in an area has degraded below a monitored threshold. How does the PCF find out, and what does it do about background data transfer policies affected by it?
questions.reference_answer: The (H-)PCF has already subscribed to network performance from the NWDAF and is notified when performance in the area of interest drops below the configured criteria. On notification, the PCF queries the UDR (Nudr_DataRepository_Query on the BdtData resource) for all stored transfer policies, identifies which ones are affected by the degradation, and for each affected policy determines the ASP whose background traffic will be impacted and which originally requested the warning notification.

questions.question: How do NWDAF instances decide which candidates become Client NWDAFs during the Federated Learning preparation phase?
questions.reference_answer: NWDAFs first register into the NRF with their Federated Learning capability; the Server NWDAF discovers potential Client NWDAFs from the NRF based on criteria such as Federated Learning capability and Analytics ID, and then sends an Nnwdaf_MLPreparation_Request to those candidates carrying Interoperability information (what abilities are needed, e.g. shared-model support) and an indication that they should act as Client NWDAF(s); final selection follows a handshake pattern based on availability and capability.

questions.question: Before an FL Server can pull ML models from an FL Client, how does the NRF get involved in authorizing that relationship?
questions.reference_answer: NWDAFs (containing MTLF, acting as FL server or FL client) first register with the NRF, including their Analytics ID(s), Interoperability ID, Vendor ID, address information, FL capability type, and service area. The Server NWDAF then discovers Client NWDAFs from the NRF using FL selection criteria (capability, Interoperability ID, Analytics ID) and requests access tokens for each selected Client from the NRF, including Analytics ID, Vendor ID and FL capability in the request; the NRF verifies eligibility (e.g. the Vendor ID) before issuing tokens.

questions.question: A V2X application server wants ongoing HD-map dynamic information about a specific host vehicle. What does it do first, and what does the VAE server do in response?
questions.reference_answer: The V2X application specific server, already registered with VAE server 1 responsible for the host vehicle, sends a subscribe HD-map-dynamic-information request naming the host vehicle's V2X UE ID and an application-defined proximity range. VAE server 1 stores the subscription, sends a subscription response back to the V2X application server, and begins obtaining and tracking the host vehicle's location from the location management server.

questions.question: A PEMC that's behind a PEGC needs to register with the PINMF. How does its registration request actually get there, and how does the network confirm it's allowed to be a PEMC?
questions.reference_answer: The PEMC sends a Message Transfer Request (containing the Registration Request) to the PEGC, which forwards it as a Transfer Message Request (with the PEMC Transport Address) to the PINMF. The PINMF-A then interacts with the UDR, via the UDM or NEF, to check whether the UE identified by the GPSI has subscribed to be a PEMC — the UDR returns the subscribed PIN-related information, including whether the UE is a PEMC and its Trust Member Group ID if one exists, plus any already-registered PINMF Info for that GPSI.

questions.question: An ECS wants to register with its ECS-ER for the first time. What must it already know, what does it send, and how does it keep the registration alive afterward?
questions.reference_answer: The ECS must already know the address (e.g. URI) of the ECS-ER. It sends an ECS registration request carrying its ECS profile and security credentials, optionally a proposed expiration time, a list of partner ECSPs allowed to receive its information, and (for roaming UEs) DNN/S-NSSAI information. The ECS-ER verifies the credentials, stores the registration, and responds with success/failure and an expiration time; to keep the registration alive the ECS must send a registration update request before that expiration time, otherwise the ECS-ER treats it as implicitly deregistered.

questions.question: What must the SGW-C take into account when it determines the candidate SGW-U list from the user's location, and which identifiers represent that location for E-UTRAN versus UTRAN?
questions.reference_answer: The SGW-C shall take into account the SGW-U location and the user's location, the SGW-U's capabilities versus the capabilities required for the UE session, the mapped UE Usage Type, the SGW-U's dynamic load, the SGW-U's relative static capacity, and the UP Function Selection Information Flags. The user's location is represented by ECGI, eNodeB ID or TAI for E-UTRAN, and by RAI or RNC-ID for UTRAN.

questions.question: When a Combined SGW-C/PGW-C selects user-plane functions for a requested APN, what must it optimise for instead of picking the SGW-U and the PGW-U independently?
questions.reference_answer: A Combined SGW-C/PGW-C function shall select the best couple of SGW-U and PGW-U (e.g. the combined SGW-U/PGW-U function) for the requested APN among all candidate couples of (SGW-U, PGW-U), instead of selecting the SGW-U and the PGW-U independently.

questions.question: In a non-roaming or LBO scenario where DNS canonical node names start with the topon label, what does the PGW-C have to give precedence to when picking a PGW-U, and what must the SGW-C supply for that to work?
questions.reference_answer: In non-roaming or LBO scenarios where the PGW-U canonical node names in DNS use "topon" as the first label, the PGW-C shall give precedence first to collocation of SGW-U and PGW-U, then to topological closeness (the pair with the highest number of matching labels in the canonical node names). This requires the SGW-C to provide the SGW-U Node ID to the PGW-C.

questions.question: A terminating UE already has a bootstrap data channel for an MMTel session and receives a re-INVITE offering an application data channel it accepts. Which responses is it allowed to return, and which specifications must the SDP answer be based on?
questions.reference_answer: The terminating UE shall return a 183 (Session Progress) or 200 (OK) response to the re-INVITE request, with the SDP answer generated based on 3GPP TS 26.114 and IETF RFC 8864.

questions.question: How does a terminating UE recognise from an SDP offer that the far end wants to close an application data channel, and does accepting that affect the audio and video already running in the session?
questions.reference_answer: The terminating UE recognises the close request when the re-INVITE's SDP offer sets the UDP port number of the data channel media description to zero, or removes the "a=dcmap" line associated with the application data channel. Accepting the termination does not impact the ongoing audio, video, or other data channels within the MMTel session.

questions.question: For Call Deflection in the BICC CS core, may the (G)MSC server bypass the media gateway, and how should its behaviour after assignment compare with CFNRy?
questions.reference_answer: If there is no need for the (G)MSC server to manipulate the bearer, it may apply MGW bypass (as specified in clause 4.4.5) prior to the assignment for Call Deflection. After the assignment, however, the MSC behaviour should be the same as CFNRy.

questions.question: If a media gateway only supports SIP-I associated Nb, how must the internal Nb bearer to the VGCS multiparty bridge be established, and how does the MSC server learn which Nb flavours that gateway supports?
questions.reference_answer: If the MGW only supports SIP-I associated Nb, the internal Nb bearer between the peripheral context and the VGCS Multiparty Bridge context must be established in accordance with the standard SIP-I based Nc external bearer setup procedures, with the Establish Bearer and Prepare Bearer procedures replaced by Reserve RTP Connection Point, Reserve and Configure RTP Connection Point, and Configure RTP Connection Point. The MSC-S knows whether the MGW supports SIP-I and/or BICC associated Nb through local configuration data.

questions.question: In a non-CUPS deployment, which payload format value must the CC-POI set for a GTP-U packet, and how is an ICE-type such as sgw carried?
questions.reference_answer: In a non-CUPS deployment, the CC-POI must set the payload format to value 12 for a GTP-U packet (5 for IPv4, 6 for IPv6, 7 for Ethernet frame). An ICE-type such as "sgw" is carried by setting the NFID attribute to the corresponding value from the ICE-type enumeration in TS 33.108 Annex B.10 as a single octet (sgw = value 3).

questions.question: Under CUPS, which node provisions the CC-POI in the SGW-U/PGW-U, over which interface, and what triggers the interception of a given IP packet?
questions.reference_answer: Under CUPS, the CC-POI in the SGW-U/PGW-U is provisioned by the CC-TF in the SGW-C/PGW-C, using a Triggering message (i.e. ActivateTask message) sent over the LI_T3 interface. Interception of a given IP packet is triggered when the packet matches the criteria specified in that Triggering message.

questions.question: For a PSS client that supports 360 VR video over DASH, which video media profile receiver is mandatory, which is only recommended, and which is purely optional?
questions.reference_answer: For a PSS client supporting 360 VR video over DASH: the Basic Video Media Profile Receiver (per TS 26.118 clause 5.2.2.3) is mandatory ("shall"); the Main Video Media Profile Receiver (clause 5.2.3.3) is recommended ("should"); and the Advanced Video Media Profile Receiver (clause 5.2.3.4) is purely optional ("may").

questions.question: If a PSS client supports vector graphics, which profile and scripting language must it support, and what compression format applies to that content?
questions.reference_answer: A PSS client supporting vector graphics shall support SVG Tiny 1.2 and ECMAScript. The compression format for SVG content is GZIP, in accordance with the SVG specification.

questions.question: What does the UE have to count as data available for transmission in the RLC layer for buffer status reporting, and when must the size of a pending STATUS PDU be included in that estimate?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall consider as data available for transmission in the RLC layer: RLC SDUs, or segments thereof, not yet included in an RLC data PDU; and RLC data PDUs, or portions thereof, pending for retransmission (RLC AM). The size of a pending STATUS PDU must be included in that estimate if the STATUS PDU has been triggered and t-StatusProhibit is not running or has expired.

questions.question: When a Timing Advance Command addressed with a PUR-RNTI arrives and a stored NTA exists, what must the MAC entity do with the pur-TimeAlignmentTimer and what must it tell the upper layers?
questions.reference_answer: When a Timing Advance Command MAC control element or PDCCH indicating timing advance adjustment addressed with a PUR-RNTI is received and an NTA has been stored, the MAC entity shall apply the Timing Advance Command/adjustment, start or restart the pur-TimeAlignmentTimer if configured, and indicate to upper layers that the Timing Advance value has been adjusted.

questions.question: During voice call continuity, is a subscriber's CLIP presentation allowed to change part-way through a call, and what must a called user be told when identity restriction applies?
questions.reference_answer: No: the CLIP identity presentation (or appropriate IMS information) is not changed for the duration of the call regardless of whether the call undergoes VCC. When identity restriction (CLIR or IMS identity restriction) applies, the called user shall receive an indication at call setup time that the identity is not available because of restriction, and this indication likewise does not change for the duration of the call.

questions.question: Which file transfer protocol must a CGF always support for CDR files even when other protocols are offered, and in push mode which events must be capable of triggering a transfer?
questions.reference_answer: FTP (RFC 959) is the default protocol for CDR file transport and shall always be supported even when other protocols are offered. In push mode, the events capable of triggering a file transfer are: a configured number of new CDR file(s) becoming available, the CDR file(s) exceeding a configurable total size limit, a configurable regular time interval elapsing, and the CGF filestore utilization exceeding a configurable level.

questions.question: The Averaging Window IE carried over PFCP measures a duration — which bit rates is that duration used to calculate, and where is the default value for a standardized 5QI specified?
questions.reference_answer: The Averaging Window duration is used to calculate the GFBR and MFBR (or the Session-AMBR, or the Authorized DL Session AMBR for Offloading). The default value for a standardized 5QI is specified in the QoS characteristics Table 5.7.4.1 of TS 23.501.

questions.question: How must the Domain Name Pattern field of the DNS Query/Response Filter IE be encoded, and when an FQDN pattern is provisioned which of the two matching forms takes precedence?
questions.reference_answer: The Domain Name Pattern field is encoded as an Octetstring representing a JSON object of the FqdnPatternMatchingRule data type (TS 29.571 clause 5.2.4.23). When an FQDN pattern is provisioned, the stringMatchingRule form shall be preferred over the regex form and used whenever possible, to optimize matching and reduce processing load.

questions.question: How is the Area Session ID value encoded on PFCP, and together with which other identifier does it uniquely identify a location-dependent MBS session?
questions.reference_answer: The Area Session ID value is encoded as an Unsigned16 binary integer. Together with the MBS Session Identifier (i.e. TMGI or Source Specific IP Multicast address), it uniquely identifies a location-dependent MBS session within a specific MBS Service Area.

questions.question: What do the two values of the RQI flag mean, and what must the NG-RAN node do with the indicator when Reflective QoS Activation was never configured for that QoS flow?
questions.reference_answer: RQI set to 0 means deactivate Reflective QoS; RQI set to 1 means activate Reflective QoS. If Reflective QoS Activation (RQA) has not been configured for the involved QoS flow, the RQI shall be ignored by the NG-RAN node.

questions.question: When the ADAEC notifies a VAL performance analytics event, which status code must the ADAES return on success and which data type must the request body carry?
questions.reference_answer: On success, the ADAES must return a "204 No Content" status code, and the notification request body must carry the AppPerfNotif data type.

questions.question: For an edge load data collection notification, which data type is sent, and under what condition must the confidence level attribute be present?
questions.reference_answer: The edge load data collection notification is sent as the EdgeNotif data type. The confidence level (confLevel) attribute must be present if the analyticsType in the subscription request is set to "PREDICTIVE".

questions.question: If a REFER request inviting a user to a conference arrives without a Referred-By header, what must the AS do, and what must the conference focus set the P-Asserted-Identity header to?
questions.reference_answer: If no Referred-By header is available in the REFER request, the AS shall add a Referred-By header that matches the P-Asserted-Identity header in the REFER request. The conference focus shall set the P-Asserted-Identity header of the REFER request to the conference URI of the conference the user shall be invited to.

questions.question: How many UTRA carriers must be used when testing a single-carrier capable base station, and against what declared information are the multi-carrier test configurations constructed?
questions.reference_answer: A single UTRA carrier must be used for testing a single-carrier capable base station. For other BS types, the multi-carrier test configurations (UTCx, per TS 25.141 clause 4.12) are constructed subject to the parameters declared by the manufacturer for the supported RF configurations.

questions.question: Which information element in a PFCP Heartbeat Request is mandatory on every interface, and when may the Source IP Address be included?
questions.reference_answer: The Recovery Time Stamp IE is mandatory (M) on every interface (Sxa, Sxb, Sxc, N4, N4mb) in a PFCP Heartbeat Request. The Source IP Address IE is optional and may be included when a Network Address Translation device is deployed in the network.

questions.question: What must the CP function include in a PFCP Session Establishment Request, and which optional timestamp may it add?
questions.reference_answer: The CP function shall send the PFCP Session Establishment Request message with a new PFCP F-SEID together with Rules to be created, and may include its current Recovery Time Stamp.

questions.question: How must a globally unique Trace Reference be composed, and how many bytes does the Trace ID occupy?
questions.reference_answer: The Trace Reference shall be composed as MCC+MNC+Trace ID, where the MCC and MNC come with the Trace activation request to identify one PLMN containing the management system. The Trace ID is a 3 byte Octet String.

questions.question: In the PDN GW initiated resource allocation deactivation over S2b, what happens to the other bearers when the default bearer of a PDN connection is deactivated, and is the PDN address released during a handover?
questions.reference_answer: If the default bearer belonging to a PDN connection is deactivated, the PDN GW deactivates all bearers belonging to that PDN connection. When performed for a handover, the connections associated with the PDN address are released, but the PDN address itself is kept in the PDN GW (i.e. not released).

questions.question: For optimized idle-mode mobility from E-UTRAN to cdma2000 HRPD, what must the UE already have in the target network, and which node fetches the PDN GW identity once the UE has tuned away?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must already have a dormant HRPD session in the target HRPD network, established either through the pre-registration procedure or a previous HRPD attachment. Once the UE has tuned to HRPD, the HS-GW fetches the PDN GW identity for all the active PDN connections from the 3GPP AAA Server.

questions.question: When timer T4100 expires during direct link setup and the initiating UE has already retransmitted the maximum allowed times, what must it do, and what extra action applies if it is a remote UE talking to a relay?
questions.reference_answer: After reaching the maximum number of allowed retransmissions, the initiating UE shall abort the direct link setup procedure and may notify the upper layer that the target UE is unreachable. If the initiating UE is a remote UE requesting link setup to a ProSe UE-to-network relay UE, it shall additionally initiate the relay reselection procedure.

questions.question: A target UE receives a DIRECT_COMMUNICATION_REQUEST from a Layer 2 ID it already has a link with, carrying identical User Info. When may it delete the existing link context?
questions.reference_answer: The target UE shall only delete the existing link context after the new link setup procedure succeeds, or after the link keepalive procedure fails.

questions.question: If the requesting UE gets no keepalive response after the maximum retransmissions of T4101, which procedure must it start instead, and what must a remote UE additionally initiate?
questions.reference_answer: If no response is received after reaching the maximum number of allowed retransmissions of T4101, the requesting UE shall abort the link keepalive procedure and initiate the direct link release procedure instead. If the requesting UE is a remote UE, it shall additionally initiate the relay reselection procedure.

questions.question: When inactivity timer T4108 expires at a peer UE that is a ProSe UE-to-network relay, which release reason must it use, and what choice do non-relay UEs have instead?
questions.reference_answer: If the peer UE is a ProSe UE-to-network relay UE, it shall initiate the direct link release procedure with release reason #3 "Direct connection is not available any more". Otherwise (non-relay UEs), the peer UE may either (A) initiate its own keepalive procedure to check the link, or (B) initiate the direct link release procedure with the same release reason #3 — the choice is left to UE implementation.

questions.question: If an MSC Server does not support accepting REFER requests on behalf of a UE per operator policy, which response code must it return?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC Server shall return a 403 Forbidden response.

questions.question: When an MSC Server receives an INVITE for a user already in an established SIP dialog and the request carries a Replaces header matching that dialog, what role must the MSC Server take?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC Server must act as a transfer target on behalf of the UE.

questions.question: For an MSC server supporting early-session as a network option, what option tag must it include and in which header field before sending the generated INVITE?
questions.reference_answer: It must include the option tag "early-session" in the Supported header field before sending the generated SIP INVITE request.

questions.question: On receiving a REFER request within a dialog, what role must the MSC Server take on behalf of the UE, and why is acceptance made subject to operator policy?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC Server shall act as a transferee on behalf of the UE. Acceptance is subject to operator policy because CS domain access signalling does not provide a mechanism to present the transfer request to the transferee for authorization, so automatic acceptance and execution of the REFER request can pose a security risk or have unwanted charging consequences.

questions.question: On the fifth expiry of timer T3595, what must the TWAG do with the PDN connection, and is any peer-to-peer WLCP signalling exchanged with the UE?
questions.reference_answer: On the fifth expiry of timer T3595, the TWAG shall abort the procedure and deactivate the PDN connection locally, without any peer-to-peer WLCP signalling between the TWAG and the UE.

questions.question: When the UE's timer T3592 expires for the fifth time during PDN disconnection, what must the UE release and which state must it enter?
questions.reference_answer: On the fifth expiry of timer T3592, the UE shall abort the procedure, release all resources associated with the PDN connection locally (without peer-to-peer signalling with the TWAG), release the PTI allocated for this invocation, and enter the state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE.

questions.question: If a WLCP entity receives a STATUS message with cause #81 Invalid PTI value, what must it abort and what must it stop?
questions.reference_answer: It must abort any ongoing WLCP procedure related to the received PTI value and stop any related timer.

questions.question: When the UE is configured with both a measurement gap and a PPW for positioning, within which of the two must it measure a positioning frequency layer whose PRS resources overlap the gap?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must measure the positioning frequency layer within the MG if its PRS resources overlap with the MG, or within the PPW if its PRS resources overlap with the PPW.

questions.question: For FR1 when the SSB used for RLM has a different subcarrier spacing than the CSI-RS configured for L1-SINR, what determines whether the UE can measure without restrictions?
questions.reference_answer: Whether the UE can perform CSI-RS measurement without restrictions is determined by whether the UE supports simultaneousRxDataSSB-DiffNumerology: if it does, the UE shall be able to perform CSI-RS measurement without restrictions even with different SCS; if it does not, it is required to measure only one of CSI-RS for L1-SINR or SSB (with restrictions).

questions.question: In sidelink resource allocation mode 1 for SL PRS, which grant types are supported and what is the cap on the total number of configured grants across all resource pools?
questions.reference_answer: For SL PRS transmission in sidelink resource allocation mode 1, dynamic grant, configured grant type 1, and configured grant type 2 are supported. The total number of SL configured grants (type 1 and type 2 combined) across all resource pools is not greater than 8.

questions.question: For CLI-RSSI in frequency range 1, where is the reference point, and what constraint applies to the reported value when the UE uses receiver diversity?
questions.reference_answer: For frequency range 1, the reference point for CLI-RSSI is the antenna connector of the UE. If receiver diversity is in use by the UE, the reported CLI-RSSI value shall not be lower than the corresponding CLI-RSSI of any of the individual receiver branches.

questions.question: When the AMF receives an initial request carrying a PDU Session Id that already exists, which cause value must it set in the release request to the SMF, and what must it wait for before proceeding?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF shall set the cause IE to REL_DUE_TO_DUPLICATE_SESSION_ID in the release request to the SMF. Before proceeding with the initial request, the AMF must wait for a subsequent SM context status notification indicating that the SM context has been deleted in the SMF.

questions.question: If a network slice becomes unavailable, which cause values may the AMF use when asking the SMF to release the affected PDU session, and what optional IE skips RAN resource release?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF may use cause value S_NSSAI_CONGESTION or REL_DUE_TO_SLICE_NOT_AVAILABLE. The optional skipN2PduSessionResRelInd IE, set to "true", skips RAN resource release for the PDU session.

questions.question: During I-SMF change with downlink data buffered at the I-UPF, what must the request carry, and what response does the SMF return on success?
questions.reference_answer: The request must carry the n9ForwardingTunnel IE indicating the allocated tunnel endpoint information to receive the buffered downlink data packets. On success, the SMF initiates N4 session modification to the I-UPF to trigger sending of the buffered DL data towards the received tunnel endpoints and returns a "204 No Content" response.

questions.question: For 5GS to EPS idle mode mobility over N26 with data forwarding, what information must the consumer include in the request, and what must the SMF then do with buffered data?
questions.reference_answer: The consumer must include the forwardingFTeid received from the MME in the Context Acknowledge, if any, or the forwarding bearer contexts received from the MME in the Context Acknowledge, if any. Upon receipt of the request, the SMF shall forward the buffered DL data on the forwarding tunnel(s).

questions.question: A base station manufacturer declares Category A spurious emission limits. Which conformance subclause becomes mandatory and which one need not be tested?
questions.reference_answer: If the manufacturer declares Category A limits, conformance with the spurious emissions requirements in subclause 6.6.3.2.1.1 becomes mandatory, and the requirements in subclause 6.6.3.2.1.2 need not be tested.

questions.question: What must a manufacturer declare about GSM 900 coexistence, and how does that declaration change which conformance requirements must be tested?
questions.reference_answer: The manufacturer shall declare whether the BS is intended to operate in geographic areas where GSM 900 is also deployed, and whether it is intended to operate co-located with a GSM 900 BTS. If the first is declared, compliance with subclause 6.6.3.2.2.1 is mandatory (otherwise not tested); if the second is declared, compliance with subclause 6.6.3.2.2.2 is mandatory (otherwise not tested).

questions.question: On the first expiry of timer T3595 at the TWAG, what must it resend and what must it restart?
questions.reference_answer: On the first expiry of timer T3595, the TWAG shall resend the PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST message and shall reset and restart timer T3595.

questions.question: For an MSC Server acting on behalf of a UE to join a conference, which two call legs must it establish and what must it do with them?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC Server must establish a terminating call leg toward the UE and an originating call leg toward the URI identified in the Refer-To header (e.g. the conference URI), and combine these two call legs into a single call.

questions.question: When an INVITE arrives for an idle user, which set of procedures must the MSC Server follow?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC Server shall act according to the mobile terminating call set up procedures specified in clause 5.4.

questions.question: After receiving the first 18x response containing early-session SDP, which message must the MSC server send toward the CS side?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC server shall send the ALERTING message as described in 3GPP TS 24.008.

questions.question: If the need for a direct link disappears before setup completes, what must the initiating UE do?
questions.reference_answer: The initiating UE shall abort the procedure.

questions.question: When a keepalive procedure is aborted because the link is no longer needed, which procedure must the requesting UE start instead?
questions.reference_answer: The requesting UE shall start a direct link release procedure instead.

questions.question: For a WLCP STATUS message carrying cause #97 message type non-existent, what must the receiving entity do?
questions.reference_answer: The receiving entity (UE or TWAG) shall abort any ongoing WLCP procedure related to the PTI and stop any related timer.

questions.question: When measurement gaps and PPW do not overlap in time and every positioning frequency layer can be measured completely, what requirement applies to the measurement period?
questions.reference_answer: The measurement period is defined as Tmeasure_MG_PPW, computed from the maximum measurement time within MG (defined in clause 9.9.2.5, covering all positioning frequency layers measured within MG), the maximum measurement time within PPW (defined in clause 9.9.2.7, covering all positioning frequency layers measured within PPW), and the maximum Teffect among all PFLs defined in those two clauses.

questions.question: If the UE does not support simultaneousRxDataSSB-DiffNumerology, what restriction applies to CSI-RS measurement for L1-SINR?
questions.reference_answer: The UE is required to measure only one of CSI-RS for L1-SINR measurement and SSB, not both; a longer measurement period for CSI-RS based L1-SINR measurement is expected, and no requirements are defined.

questions.question: Which transport protocol must carry ProSe messages between the UE and the Key Management Function, and which HTTP method is used for the procedures?
questions.reference_answer: HTTP 1.1 (as specified in IETF RFC 2616) must carry ProSe messages between the UE and the ProSe Key Management Function, and HTTP POST methods are used for the procedures.

questions.question: In the CMPv2 profile for PKIMessage, how many PKIMessages may a single message contain, and is the protection field optional?
questions.reference_answer: All CMPv2 messages used within this profile shall consist of exactly one PKIMessage (the sequence size shall be 1 in all cases). The protection field of type PKIProtection is optional in the RFC but its support and usage is required by this profile.
