questions.question: For a Certification Request, which private key must the NF sign the PKIMessage with, and what must the extraCerts field contain?
questions.reference_answer: The PKIMessage sent by the NF shall be signed with the private key related to one of the valid operator provided NF certificates. The mandatory extraCerts field shall contain the NF certificate related to the signing private key, plus any intermediate CA certificates if the NF certificate is not signed directly by a root CA.

questions.question: For a Key Update Request, which certificate's private key must sign the PKIMessage, and should the response carry the operator root certificate?
questions.reference_answer: The PKIMessage sent by the NF shall be signed with the private key related to the last received operator provided NF certificate. The response (PKIMessage carrying the key update response) should not contain the operator root certificate in the extraCerts field.

questions.question: When a web server uses CGI or other scripting, what restriction applies to the upload directory?
questions.reference_answer: The associated CGI/script directory shall not be used for uploads — the upload directory must be different from the CGI/Scripting directory.

questions.question: A manufacturer declares the base station will operate co-located with a DCS 1800 BTS. Which conformance requirement becomes mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: Compliance with the conformance requirement specified in subclause 6.6.3.2.3.2 becomes mandatory.

questions.question: What must a manufacturer declare regarding UTRA FDD coexistence, and how does each answer affect testing obligations?
questions.reference_answer: The manufacturer shall declare whether the BS is intended to operate in geographic areas where UTRA FDD is also deployed, and whether it is intended to operate co-located with a UTRA FDD BS. If the first is declared, compliance with subclause 6.6.3.2.4.1 is mandatory (otherwise not tested); if the second is declared, compliance with subclause 6.6.3.2.4.2 is mandatory (otherwise not tested).

questions.question: When the SMF receives a release request due to a duplicated PDU Session Id, which network functions' resources must it release?
questions.reference_answer: The SMF shall start the PDU Session Release procedure to release all the associated resources in UPF, PCF, CHF, and UDM. If the UP connection of the existing PDU session is active, the SMF should also request (R)AN to release associated resources.

questions.question: During network slice replacement, under what circumstance does the AMF release a PDU session instead of retaining it with the alternative S-NSSAI?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF releases the PDU session instead of retaining it with the alternative S-NSSAI if it determines the PDU session cannot be retained with the alternative S-NSSAI for some reason, e.g. the V-SMF/I-SMF cannot support the alternative S-NSSAI.

questions.question: If the SMF cannot proceed with a request to forward buffered downlink data at the I-UPF, what must it return?
questions.reference_answer: If the SMF cannot proceed with the request, it shall return an error response, as specified for step 2b of figure 5.2.2.3.1-1.

questions.question: Which two alternatives may the consumer supply for data forwarding during 5GS to EPS idle mode mobility over N26?
questions.reference_answer: The consumer may supply the forwardingFTeid received from the MME in the Context Acknowledge, if any, or the forwarding bearer contexts received from the MME in the Context Acknowledge, if any.

questions.question: For SL PRS in sidelink resource allocation mode 1, which clause's procedure must the UE follow for a dedicated resource pool, and what substitution applies?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall follow the procedure described in clause 8.6 (excluding the case of PSSCH for retransmission of a transport block). The substitutions applied are: "PSSCH for a transport block" is replaced by "SL PRS", and "PSSCH" is replaced by "SL PRS".

questions.question: For frequency range 2, how must CLI-RSSI be measured with respect to antenna elements?
questions.reference_answer: For frequency range 2, CLI-RSSI shall be measured based on the combined signal from antenna elements corresponding to a given receiver branch.

questions.question: When a UE is configured with a PUCCH-SCell, to which cell groups must it apply the physical uplink control channel procedures?
questions.reference_answer: If the UE is configured with a PUCCH-SCell, it shall apply the physical uplink control channel procedures for both the primary PUCCH group and the secondary PUCCH group.

questions.question: The TrGW supports only a subset of the image sizes that arrive in an SDP body on the Mx interface. What must the IBCF forward to the TrGW, and what must it do if none of the received image sizes is supported at all?
questions.reference_answer: The IBCF shall send only the list of image sizes per payload type that are supported by the TrGW (preconfigured in the IBCF). If none of the received image sizes is supported by the TrGW, the IBCF shall not send the generic image attribute parameter to the TrGW at all.

questions.question: Full ICE functionality is optional for the IBCF and the TrGW. If a vendor nevertheless claims ICE support, what is the minimum ICE variant both entities must implement?
questions.reference_answer: Both the IBCF and the TrGW shall at least support ICE lite as specified in IETF RFC 8445.

questions.question: When Predefined ROI mode is indicated to the TrGW, which RTCP feedback capability parameter and which media-level SDP attribute must the IBCF send?
questions.reference_answer: The IBCF must send the RTCP feedback message capability parameter "3gpp-roi-predefined" (for "Predefined ROI" type) along with the RTP Header Extension capability for predefined ROI information, and the media-level SDP attribute "a=predefined_ROI".

questions.question: For Arbitrary ROI mode, which parameter name expresses the RTCP feedback message capability that the IBCF sends to the TrGW?
questions.reference_answer: The parameter is "3gpp-roi-arbitrary".

questions.question: Once an IP realm identifier has been assigned to an IP bearer termination, may it be changed later, and what applies to the other media streams associated with that termination?
questions.reference_answer: The IP realm identifier shall not be changed after the initial assignment. The same IP realm shall be applied to all media streams associated with that termination.

questions.question: On receiving the very first SDP offer from network A, what must the IMS-ALG request from the TrGW, and what does it replace in the SDP before offering towards network B?
questions.reference_answer: The IMS-ALG must request the TrGW to allocate a termination towards answering network B and provide IP address(es) and port number(s) from its pool for this termination. Before offering towards network B, it replaces the IP address(es) and port number(s) in the SDP with those received from the TrGW for that termination.

questions.question: After the first SDP answer arrives from network B, what three things must the IMS-ALG ask the TrGW to do so that user plane traffic can be routed?
questions.reference_answer: The IMS-ALG must: (1) provide to the TrGW the address(es) and port number(s) received in the c-line(s) and m-line(s) of the SDP answer as destinations for the termination towards network B; (2) request the TrGW to allocate a termination towards offering network A, providing IP address(es)/port number(s) from its pool and the address/port from the first SDP offer as destination (unless already done earlier); and (3) request the TrGW to bind the termination towards network A and the termination towards network B to enable routing of user plane traffic through the TrGW.

questions.question: A mid-dialog SDP offer/answer reassigns the users' IP addresses and port numbers without adding or deleting any. What must the IMS-ALG/TrGW do with the existing bindings, and what if nothing changed at all?
questions.reference_answer: When IP address(es) and port number(s) have been reassigned (but none added or deleted), the existing binding(s) shall be updated to reflect the reassignment. If no change has been made to the IP address(es) and port number(s) at all, no change shall be made to the existing binding(s).

questions.question: Two networks connected via CS-IBCF and CS-TrGW sit in different IP realms. Is IP realm indication mandatory for both entities, and how must the CS-TrGW react if the available IP realms change?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the CS-IBCF and the CS-TrGW shall support IP realm indication. If there is a change in the IP Realms that are available or if they are modified in the CS-TrGW, the CS-TrGW shall inform the CS-IBCF via the IP Realm Availability Procedure, if this procedure is supported by the CS-TrGW.

questions.question: Which subset of XPath must GCL support, and what form must expressions inside predicates take?
questions.reference_answer: GCL shall support the subset of XPath consisting of only the child:: and attribute:: axes, with predicates supported. Expressions inside predicates shall be of the form "node <op> value", where <op> ranges over the usual string and arithmetic operators.

questions.question: For a PFCP Request message, which IP address must appear as destination and which as source, and can the destination address agreed for a PFCP session be changed later?
questions.reference_answer: The IP Destination Address of a Request message shall be an IP address of the peer entity, and the IP Source Address shall be an IP address of the sending entity. Yes, the CP and UP functions may change the destination address subsequently during a PFCP Session Modification procedure.

questions.question: A UP function receives a GTP-U Error Indication message. Which procedure must it start towards the CP function, and which two IEs of the Error Indication must be reported?
questions.reference_answer: The UP function shall initiate a PFCP Session Report procedure towards the CP function, sending an Error Indication Report that includes the remote F-TEID signalled in the GTP-U Peer Address IE and the Tunnel Endpoint Identifier Data I IE of the GTP-U Error Indication.

questions.question: A user subscribes to both transport layer and service level SMS interworking but is only authorised for one of them at the time the message is processed. Which interworking may the IP-SM-GW perform?
questions.reference_answer: Only the authorised interworking shall be performed by the IP-SM-GW.

questions.question: Which content types must be supported for the Nudr_GroupIDmap-related HTTP bodies, and which content type signals the use of JSON Merge Patch in a request body?
questions.reference_answer: JSON, the Problem Details JSON Object, JSON Merge Patch, and JSON Patch content types must be supported. The content type "application/merge-patch+json" signals the use of JSON Merge Patch in a request body.

questions.question: During an AMF relocation, under which two conditions must the old AMF delete the AM policy association, and which HTTP method and resource URI does it use?
questions.reference_answer: The old AMF must delete the AM policy association when the resource URI of the "Individual AM Policy Association" resource is not transferred to the new AMF, or when the new AMF informs the old AMF that this resource is not being reused (i.e. the old PCF is not being reused). It uses an HTTP DELETE request with Resource URI "{apiRoot}/npcf-am-policy-control/v1/policies/{polAssoId}".

questions.question: The Extended Local Emergency Number List returns a sub-services field of length zero for a detected number. Which emergency service URN must the UE use, and how is the URN built when the field is non-empty?
questions.reference_answer: If the sub-services field length is "0", the UE shall use the emergency service URN "urn:service:sos". If non-empty, the UE constructs the URN using "urn:service:sos" followed by a dot and the content of the sub-services field (e.g. "urn:service:sos.gas").

questions.question: A UE attached to the EPC via S2b over untrusted WLAN establishes an additional IPSec ESP tunnel while a SIP dialog is already up. What must the UE send if the related SDP media description has to change, and over which dialog?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must send a new SDP offer within a SIP request, over the existing SIP dialog.

questions.question: For a UE attached over untrusted non-3GPP access using IPSec tunnel mode, what must it subtract from the path MTU to the ePDG before selecting the SIP transport, and why?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must subtract (decrement) the IPSec tunnel overhead from the path MTU between the UE and the ePDG prior to applying the transport selection for SIP requests, in order to reduce the risk of UDP fragmentation.

questions.question: A participating MCPTT function receives a location information report forwarded by another MCPTT server. Which Content-Type and MIME body elements must be present, and what must the participating function do with the Request-URI before forwarding?
questions.reference_answer: The Content-Type header field must be set to "application/vnd.3gpp.mcptt-location-info+xml", and the MIME body must contain a <Report> element including a <ReportID> attribute and a <mcptt-reporting-uri> element included in the <location-info> root element. Before forwarding the report to the requesting MCPTT client, the participating function must update the Request-URI.

questions.question: A location reporting trigger fires while the minimumReportInterval timer is still running at the MCPTT client. What must the client do, and on what condition does it actually send the report when the timer expires?
questions.reference_answer: The MCPTT client waits until the minimumReportInterval timer expires. When it expires, the client sends a location information report only if any of the reporting triggers are still true.

questions.question: When the participating MCPTT function cancels an MBMS bearer announcement, which element must carry an unchanged value and which three elements or bodies must be omitted?
questions.reference_answer: The <TMGI> element must carry the same (unchanged) TMGI value as in the announcement being cancelled. The three items that must be omitted are: the <mbms-service-areas> element; the <GPMS> element (if the MIME body only contains announcements to be cancelled); and the application/sdp MIME body (if the MIME body only contains announcements to be cancelled).

questions.question: How does a UE announce support for the LCS notification mechanism or LPP messages, where is its PRU capability stored, and is a UE served by satellite NG-RAN allowed to act as a PRU?
questions.reference_answer: The UE announces support for the LCS notification mechanism or LPP messages using the 5GMM capability IE. Its PRU capability is stored in the UDM, without any indication in the 5GMM capability IE. A UE accessing the 5G network via satellite NG-RAN shall not operate as a PRU.

questions.question: For downlink positioning information transport, which Payload container type must the AMF set in the DL NAS TRANSPORT message, and what is the Routing identifier it puts in the Additional information IE?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF shall set the Payload container type to "LPP message container" in the DL NAS TRANSPORT message. The Routing identifier it puts in the Additional information IE is the Correlation ID.

questions.question: An FR1-NTN UE has the SSB used for RLM/BFD inside the active BWP but with a different SCS than the CSI-RS for candidate beam detection. What may it do if it does not support simultaneousRxDataSSB-DiffNumerology?
questions.reference_answer: If the UE does not support simultaneousRxDataSSB-DiffNumerology, it is required to measure only one of but not both CSI-RS for CBD measurement and SSB; a longer measurement period for CSI-RS based CBD measurement is expected, and no requirements are defined.

questions.question: When a UE transitions between DRX and no DRX, which evaluation period must it apply to each BFD-RS resource during the transition window, and which one afterwards?
questions.reference_answer: During the transition window (a duration equal to the evaluation period of the second mode), the UE shall use an evaluation period no less than the minimum of the evaluation periods corresponding to the first and second modes, for each BFD-RS resource. Afterwards, it shall use the evaluation period corresponding to the second mode.

questions.question: Is a UE required to use measurement gaps to measure SSB for beam failure detection, and in FR1 what happens when the SSB for BFD and the CSI-RS share an OFDM symbol with the same SCS?
questions.reference_answer: No, the UE is required to be capable of measuring SSB for BFD without measurement gaps. In FR1, if the SSB for BFD and CSI-RS share the same OFDM symbol and have the same SCS, the UE shall be able to measure the SSB for BFD without any restriction.

questions.question: An NG-RAN node sends an MT COMMUNICATION HANDLING REQUEST with the 5GC Action IE set to "HLCom Activate". What must the AMF do, and which IE must it take into account when applying the handling?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF shall activate MT communication handling for the PDU session(s) indicated in the PDU Session Resource List IE, as specified in TS 23.501, and shall take into account the NR Paging Long eDRX Information for RRC INACTIVE IE when applying MT communication handling, as specified in TS 38.304 and TS 23.502.

questions.question: After receiving a UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with the Cause IE set to "User inactivity", under what extra condition should the AMF still initiate the UE Context Release procedure?
questions.reference_answer: The UE Context Release procedure should still be initiated if there is no downlink signaling, as specified in TS 23.502.

questions.question: On receiving an AMF CP RELOCATION INDICATION message, what must the NG-RAN node stop doing, and which procedure may it start for NAS PDUs it received earlier from that AMF?
questions.reference_answer: The NG-RAN node shall terminate the delivery of NAS messages that have been received from the AMF, and may initiate the NAS Non Delivery Indication procedure(s) to report the non-delivery of any NAS PDUs previously received from that AMF.

questions.question: A manufacturer declares that the BS under test is intended to operate co-sited with another TDD or FDD BS having uplink receive functionality on an adjacent frequency. Which ACLR conformance subclause becomes mandatory, and which one need not be tested if the declaration is negative?
questions.reference_answer: Conformance with the ACLR requirement specified in subclause 6.6.2.2.2.3 becomes mandatory. If the declaration is negative (not co-sited), that same requirement (subclause 6.6.2.2.2.3) need not be tested.

questions.question: The UTRAN cannot support any of the ciphering or integrity protection algorithms carried in a SECURITY MODE COMMAND. Which message must go back to the CN and with which cause value, and what cause is used instead when the radio interface procedure itself fails?
questions.reference_answer: The UTRAN shall return a SECURITY MODE REJECT message to the CN with cause value "Requested Ciphering and/or Integrity Protection Algorithms not Supported". If the radio interface Security Mode Control procedure itself fails, the SECURITY MODE REJECT message shall instead carry cause value "Failure in the Radio Interface Procedure".

questions.question: A SECURITY MODE COMMAND arrives from a core network domain that already has a signalling connection with integrity protection started, and the Key Status IE is set to "Old". What must be returned and with which cause value?
questions.reference_answer: A SECURITY MODE REJECT message shall be returned with cause value "Conflict with already existing Integrity protection and/or Ciphering information".

questions.question: In GERAN Iu-mode CS, the BSC cannot provide a RAB matching the GERAN BSC Container IE it received. Which cause value and which additional IE must it report inside the RAB ASSIGNMENT RESPONSE?
questions.reference_answer: The BSC shall report unsuccessful RAB establishment/modification with cause value "GERAN Iu-mode Failure", including the GERAN Classmark IE, in the GERAN Iu mode specific RABs Failed To Setup Or Modify List IE within the RAB ASSIGNMENT RESPONSE message.

questions.question: May a vendor use the Iur private message mechanism to carry basic functionality, and what are the two purposes for which it is allowed?
questions.reference_answer: No, the private message mechanism shall not be used for basic functionality (which shall be standardised). It may be used for special operator/vendor-specific features not considered part of basic functionality, and for vendor research purposes, e.g. to implement and evaluate new algorithms/features before proposing them for standardisation.

questions.question: An RNC uses the IP transport option over slow E1/T1/J1 PPP links. Which two extra capabilities must it support, and how must header compression be negotiated over PPP?
questions.reference_answer: It shall also support IP Header Compression (RFC 2507) and the PPP extensions ML/MC-PPP (RFC 1990, RFC 2686). Negotiation of header compression over PPP shall be performed via RFC 2509.

questions.question: For the Iur IP option, which IP version must a UTRAN node support and which is optional, and which four fields identify the transport bearer?
questions.reference_answer: An IP UTRAN node shall support IPv6; support of IPv4 is optional. The transport bearer is identified by the source UDP port number, destination UDP port number, source IP address, and destination IP address.

questions.question: On receiving an F1-C TRAFFIC TRANSFER message over X2, what must the MeNB do with the contained F1-C traffic, and how does the en-gNB handle it differently?
questions.reference_answer: Upon reception of the F1-C TRAFFIC TRANSFER message, the MeNB shall deliver the contained F1-C traffic to the IAB-node as specified in TS 36.331. The en-gNB, by contrast, shall handle the received F1-C traffic as specified in TS 38.473 and TS 38.472.

questions.question: When the Lower Layer presence status change IE is set to "release lower layers" or "suspend lower layers", which resources and contexts must still be kept, and after which prior value may "re-establish lower layers" be set?
questions.reference_answer: PDCP entities, X2-U bearer resources, S1-U bearer resources and UE context information shall be kept. "re-establish lower layers" shall only be set after "release lower layers" has previously been indicated.

questions.question: What integer range does the NR Cell Capacity Class Value IE take, which end means minimum capacity, and what kind of relation should hold between the value and the actual cell capacity?
questions.reference_answer: The IE takes an integer value of 1 to 100. Value 1 means the minimum cell capacity (and 100 the maximum). There should be a linear relation between the Cell Capacity Class Value and the actual cell capacity.

questions.question: If a UE-associated signalling connection over X2 was set up including the eNB UE X2AP ID Extension, for how long and by which peers must that extension be used?
questions.reference_answer: The eNB UE X2AP ID Extension shall be used by both peers for the life-time of the respective UE-associated signalling connection.

questions.question: Subscriber A activates a CCBS request against destination B. Which two queues must HLR A inspect to detect an identical request already existing, and why both?
questions.reference_answer: HLR A shall check subscriber A's originating queue for any previous requests activated by subscriber A against destination B for the same basic service group, and shall also check subscriber A's target queue for any requests activated by destination B against subscriber A for the same basic service group — because checking for an identical CCBS request must include checks in both directions.

questions.question: Destination B activates Call Forwarding on Busy after subscriber A has already activated a CCBS request against B. What must HLR B do with the queued requests, and which two network provider options exist when a CCBS call later reaches MSC B with MS B NDUB?
questions.reference_answer: HLR B shall continue to process CCBS Requests in the queue. When a CCBS call subsequently arrives at MSC B and MS B is NDUB, a network provider option exists: either the CCBS call is treated as when MS B is busy for the CCBS call without CFB active, or the CCBS call is forwarded without the CCBS call Indicator.

questions.question: How many streams must each termination in a conference context support and for which media, and from how many through-connected terminations must the MRFP treat the context as an ad-hoc conference?
questions.reference_answer: Each termination shall support up to three streams: one for audio, one for messaging, and one for video. The MRFP shall consider the context to represent an ad-hoc conference when three or more terminations have been through-connected.

questions.question: In MIKEY replay protection for MBMS, when must the BM-SC increment the 32-bit timestamp counter for MSK messages including retransmissions, and how many counters exist for MSK versus MTK delivery?
questions.reference_answer: The BM-SC shall increase the 32-bit timestamp counter by one for each MSK message sent to the UE, even when retransmitting a previously sent MSK message. There is one counter per UE for MSK delivery, and one counter common to all UEs for MTK delivery.

questions.question: The BM-SC sets the V-bit in the MIKEY common header of an MSK transport message. Which fields must the UE's verification message consist of, what must the ID Type of IDr be set to, and is the NULL MAC algorithm permitted?
questions.reference_answer: The verification message shall consist of HDR || TS || IDr || V. The ID Type field of IDr shall be set to value 0 (=NAI). The use of the NULL algorithm in the MAC alg field is not allowed.

questions.question: When SRTP is applied to an MBMS RTP stream, is encryption of the SRTCP packets mandatory, and which key material and MKI value must SRTCP share with the corresponding SRTP stream?
questions.reference_answer: Encryption of SRTCP packets is optional (not mandatory), though SRTCP packets shall be integrity protected. SRTCP shall share the master key and master salt with the corresponding SRTP stream, and shall carry the same MKI field value as the corresponding SRTP stream.

questions.question: If a UE decides to use TLS for MBMS key management, is a ciphersuite with NULL encryption allowed, and is support of certificate revocation mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: No, when the UE decides to use TLS, use of a TLS ciphersuite without NULL encryption is mandatory (a NULL-encryption ciphersuite is not allowed). Support of certificate revocation is optional, not mandatory.

questions.question: Which two RTP profiles must an MCPTT client support in SDP offer/answer, may it reject an offer because of the offered profile, and which codec payload type must it always offer?
questions.reference_answer: MCPTT clients shall support both "RTP/AVP" and "RTP/SAVP" profiles in SDP offer/answer, and shall not reject an SDP offer due to the offered RTP profile being either of these. MCPTT clients shall support and offer a payload type with AMR-WB.

questions.question: For EVS error concealment, what must the decoder be informed about before concealment actions start, and which kind of substitute frame is explicitly not allowed?
questions.reference_answer: The decoder shall be informed about erroneous/lost frames so that error concealment actions can be initiated, using a set of predicted parameters in the speech synthesis. Insertion of speech signal independent silence frames is not allowed.

questions.question: A hardware implementation of the AMR-WB encoder is under test using the *.INP sequences. Which output frame is allowed to differ from the *.COD file, and what must hold for all the remaining frames?
questions.reference_answer: The first speech encoder output frame is undefined and need not be identical to the first frame in the *.COD file. All remaining speech encoder output frames shall be identical to the corresponding frames in the *.COD file.

questions.question: How must the system authenticate a Service User requesting an MPS MMTEL voice call from a UE that has no MPS subscription, and what must a visited PLMN be able to verify with the home PLMN?
questions.reference_answer: The system shall support means to authenticate and authorize the Service User request using predetermined MPS credentials (e.g. a calling card number, PIN or security token) assigned specifically for obtaining MPS from a UE without an MPS subscription. A visited PLMN must be able to verify with the home PLMN that the UE is authorized for MPS, and to authorize MPS for the MMTEL voice or voice conference call.

questions.question: An MPS MMTEL video call is never explicitly ended and the UE simply powers down. What must the 3GPP system in the RPLMN do, and what must not happen on the UE's next registration?
questions.reference_answer: The 3GPP system in the RPLMN shall automatically revoke MPS. On the UE's next registration, MPS priority treatment must not automatically apply to subsequent calls.

questions.question: During an MPS MMTEL video call the network can no longer support both audio and video. Which media must be retained, and what must happen once the blocking conditions disappear?
questions.reference_answer: The audio must be retained. Once the conditions that previously blocked the video media are no longer applicable, the system shall support priority re-establishment of the video media.

questions.question: For the RAB.AttRelPS per-cause measurement, which RANAP message received by the RNC triggers the count, and what must the sum of all supported per-cause measurements equal?
questions.reference_answer: The count is triggered on receipt by the RNC of a RANAP RAB ASSIGNMENT REQUEST message for the PS domain. The sum of all supported per-cause measurements shall equal the total number of RAB Release Attempts.

questions.question: In the YANG mapping of NRM classes, how must an attribute with isNotifyable=False be marked, and how must an attribute with isNotifyable=True be treated?
questions.reference_answer: An attribute with isNotifyable=False shall be marked with the "yext3gpp:notNotifiable" YANG extension statement defined in the _3gpp-common-yang-extensions.yang module. An attribute with isNotifyable=True shall not be marked in any way, as it is the default case.

questions.question: A concrete NRM class is mapped to YANG. What must the grouping and the list be named, which attribute serves as the key, and where must all the other attributes be placed?
questions.reference_answer: The grouping shall be named <IocName>Grp and the list shall be named <IocName>. The NamingAttribute shall be used as the key. All other attributes shall be placed inside a non-presence "container" named "attributes".

questions.question: For the NR sidelink test model requiring GNSS support, which four satellite systems must the positioning simulator be able to generate and broadcast?
questions.reference_answer: The positioning simulator shall be capable of generating and broadcasting GPS, Galileo, GLONASS and BDS.

questions.question: When the ME returns an AT Response to the UICC and the response string exceeds the maximum transmittable length, what must the ME do with it?
questions.reference_answer: If the AT Response string is longer than the maximum length capable of being transmitted to the UICC, the ME shall truncate the AT Response string to this length.

questions.question: When the APN-AMBR for uplink and downlink arrives over a non-GTP interface in bits per second and the conversion to kbps yields a fraction, how must the GTP entity treat that fractional value?
questions.reference_answer: The value of APN-AMBR for uplink and downlink shall be rounded upwards.

questions.question: From Release 8 onwards, which specification supersedes all GTPv1 user-plane provisions of TS 29.060, and what does the TEID field in the GTP header have to indicate for a given T-PDU?
questions.reference_answer: From Release 8 onwards, 3GPP TS 29.281 supersedes all GTPv1 user-plane provisions of TS 29.060. The TEID field in the GTP header shall indicate which tunnel a particular T-PDU belongs to.

questions.question: If a GTP-U-CONTROL-RX-SETUP.request arrives carrying a TEID that is already in use, how must the receiving entity interpret that primitive, and what is the IP address parameter needed for beyond identifying the remote endpoint?
questions.reference_answer: It shall be interpreted as a resource modification request. The IP address parameter is needed to identify the path being used, which is necessary in order to send ECHO messages used to detect path failure.

questions.question: For a collaborative session whose participants belong to different subscriptions, which media feature tag in the Contact header field and which Feature-Caps header field parameter must be supported at the non-roaming II-NNI and for loopback traversal?
questions.reference_answer: The "g.3gpp.iut-focus" media feature tag in the Contact header field, and the "+g.3gpp.iut-focus" header field parameter in the Feature-Caps header field, must both be supported at the non-roaming II-NNI and for the loopback traversal scenario.

questions.question: In pull-mode IUT replication over the roaming II-NNI, which method parameter value must the Refer-To header field of the REFER request carry, and which option tag has to populate its Require header field?
questions.reference_answer: The Refer-To header field must carry the method parameter set to "MESSAGE", and the Require header field must be populated with the option tag value "tdialog".

questions.question: For push-mode replication at the roaming II-NNI, what must the Accept-Contact header field of the REFER request carry alongside the g.3gpp.iut-focus media feature tag, and which header fields must the embedded Refer-To content include?
questions.reference_answer: The Accept-Contact header field must carry the "g.3gpp.iut-focus" media feature tag with explicit and require tags. The embedded Refer-To content must include the Accept-Contact header field, the P-Preferred-Service header field, and the "application/sdp" MIME body.

questions.question: Over CAPIF-1/1e, does the Onboard_API_Invoker service operation use the same TLS authentication mode as the remaining CAPIF APIs, and what certificate arrangement is mandated for each?
questions.reference_answer: No. For the Onboard_API_Invoker service operation, the TLS connection shall be established using a server certificate; for the rest of the CAPIF APIs, the TLS connection shall be established with certificate-based mutual authentication.

questions.question: When an API exposing function issues an HTTP GET to fetch an access control policy, what must the CAPIF core function verify first, and what must it do if errors occur while processing that request?
questions.reference_answer: The CAPIF core function must first verify the identity of the API exposing function and check whether it is authorized to obtain the access control policy corresponding to the API identification. If errors occur when processing the request, the CAPIF core function shall respond to the API exposing function with an appropriate error status code.

questions.question: When an API management function registers an API provider domain with CAPIF, who assigns the identities of the individual API provider domain functions, and what must the HTTP POST body contain besides the enrolment details?
questions.reference_answer: The CAPIF core function assigns the identities for the API provider domain functions. The HTTP POST body must contain API provider Enrolment Details, consisting of details of all API provider domain functions and security information for the CAPIF core function to validate the registration request.

questions.question: On S6a, which Error-Diagnostic value must be sent when Experimental-Error is DIAMETER_ERROR_UNKNOWN_EPS_SUBSCRIPTION but GPRS Subscription Data does exist for the user, and which value applies when Operator Determined Barring indicates all packet oriented services barred?
questions.reference_answer: GPRS_DATA_SUBSCRIBED (0) must be sent when Experimental-Error is DIAMETER_ERROR_UNKNOWN_EPS_SUBSCRIPTION and GPRS Subscription Data exists for the user. ODB_ALL_APN (2) applies when Experimental-Error is DIAMETER_ERROR_ROAMING_NOT_ALLOWED and the Operator Determined Barring indicates "All Packet Oriented Services Barred".

questions.question: Which specification defines the values carried in the RAT-Type AVP, and are the separate values for LTE-M and NB-IoT over satellite access required in MME/SGSN-to-HSS signalling?
questions.reference_answer: The values carried in the RAT-Type AVP are defined in 3GPP TS 29.212. Yes, distinct RAT-Type values for LTE-M over satellite access and EUTRAN-NB-IoT over satellite access are defined and shall be used in the signalling between the serving nodes (MME/SGSN) and the HSS.

questions.question: In the grouped MDT-Configuration AVP, which member AVP is mandatory rather than optional, and how many MDT-Allowed-PLMN-Id and MBSFN-Area occurrences may the AVP carry?
questions.reference_answer: Job-Type is the mandatory member AVP; all other listed members, including MDT-Allowed-PLMN-Id and MBSFN-Area, are optional. The MDT-Allowed-PLMN-Id and MBSFN-Area AVPs may each occur zero or more times.

questions.question: When the HSS returns several serving nodes for a device trigger, which of them should the MTC-IWF prefer, and what must it set in the SIR Flags IE when it sends the retrieval request?
questions.reference_answer: The MTC-IWF should give higher preference to the serving node included in the "Serving Node" IE than to those in the list of "Additional Serving Node" IEs. It shall set the S6m/S6n indicator bit in the SIR Flags IE.

questions.question: Because S6m sessions between MTC-IWF and HSS are implicitly terminated, which value of Auth-Session-State must be used, and are the Authorization-Lifetime and Session-Timeout AVPs allowed to appear?
questions.reference_answer: The Auth-Session-State AVP must be set to NO_STATE_MAINTAINED (1). Neither the Authorization-Lifetime AVP nor the Session-Timeout AVP shall be present in requests or responses.

questions.question: If the MTC-IWF does not know the address of the HSS serving a subscriber, which Diameter routing AVPs may it include in the request, and what must the receiving node do with a Vendor-Specific-Application-ID AVP it receives?
questions.reference_answer: Only the Destination-Realm AVP shall be present, and the command shall be routed to the next Diameter node. If a Vendor-Specific-Application-ID AVP is received in any command, it shall be ignored by the receiving node and shall not be used for routing purposes.

questions.question: When the UE builds an RRCSystemInfoRequest purely for positioning system information, which list does it populate instead of requested-SI-List, and which broadcast-status flag must the SI message have for it to be listed?
questions.reference_answer: The UE populates the requestedPosSI-List instead of requested-SI-List. An SI message is listed only if its posSI-BroadcastStatus (in posSchedulingInfoList) or the si-BroadcastStatus of the type2 SIB configured by schedulingInfoList2 is set to notBroadcasting.

questions.question: An NPN-capable UE camping on an NPN-only cell receives SIB9 carrying eventID-TSS. From which SIB1 list entry must it derive the gNB identity and PLMN identity, and does the same source apply to a UE on an ordinary PLMN cell?
questions.reference_answer: It must derive the gNB identity from gNB-ID-Length and cellIdentity of the first NPN-IdentityInfo list entry of NPN-IdentityInfoList in SIB1, and derive the plmn-Identity from the first NPN-Identity list entry of NPN-IdentityList within that same NPN-IdentityInfo entry. No — for a UE on an ordinary PLMN cell, the source is instead the first PLMN-IdentityInfo list entry of PLMN-IdentityInfoList in SIB1, for both the gNB identity and the plmn-Identity.

questions.question: If the UE has already stored some SIB23 segments and the SIB23 value tag then changes, what must it do with those stored segments before storing the new one?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall discard all stored segments before storing the new one.

questions.question: A UE declares radio link failure after a random access problem indication from MCG MAC while that random access run had been started for beam failure recovery. Which rlf-Cause value must it record in VarRLF-Report, and which value would apply had the random access not been for beam failure recovery?
questions.reference_answer: It must record rlf-Cause as beamFailureRecoveryFailure. Had the random access not been for beam failure recovery, it would record rlf-Cause as randomAccessProblem.

questions.question: When a UE needs to send E-UTRA MR-DC dedicated information such as an MCGFailureInformation message, which field of the ULInformationTransferMRDC message must it populate, and which field would carry NR-related dedicated information instead?
questions.reference_answer: It must populate the ul-DCCH-MessageNR field. The ul-DCCH-MessageEUTRA field would instead carry E-UTRA-related dedicated information (e.g. E-UTRA RRC MeasurementReport or MCGFailureInformation).

questions.question: Is a UE with no serving cell at all permitted to run NR sidelink communication, and when the UE does have a suitable serving cell, what relationship must the selected cell on the sidelink frequency have to the registered PLMN?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, a UE with no serving cell at all (RRC_IDLE) is permitted to perform NR sidelink communication. When the UE does have a suitable serving cell, the selected cell on the sidelink frequency must belong to the registered or equivalent PLMN (as specified in TS 24.587 or TS 24.554), unless the UE is out of coverage on that frequency.

questions.question: On receiving an RRCReconfigurationCompleteSidelink that contains sl-DRX-ConfigReject, which timer must the UE stop for that destination and what does it conclude about sidelink DRX for the unicast link?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must stop timer T400 for that destination. It concludes that no sidelink DRX is to be applied for the corresponding sidelink unicast communication.

questions.question: In a UE supporting TDD and GSM in CELL_DCH with idle intervals configured, how are the GSM measurement opportunities split between initial BSIC identification, GSM carrier RSSI measurement and BSIC reconfirmation?
questions.reference_answer: Every second GSM measurement opportunity is allocated for GSM initial BSIC identification. Of the remaining opportunities, 3 out of 4 are allocated for GSM carrier RSSI measurements and 1 out of 4 for GSM BSIC reconfirmation, with scheduling between the latter two left up to the UE.

questions.question: After how many consecutive failed BSIC decoding attempts must the UE abandon BSIC re-confirmation for a GSM BCCH carrier, how is that carrier then treated, and how many identified GSM cells must the UE keep timing information for?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must abandon BSIC re-confirmation after two successive failed decoding attempts (or after failing to re-confirm within Tre-confirm_abort = 5000 ms). That carrier is then treated as a new GSM BCCH carrier with unidentified BSIC and moved to the initial BSIC decoding procedure. The UE must maintain timing information for at least 8 identified GSM cells.

questions.question: When several HS-PDSCHs are sent to one UE in the same cell, what must hold for their transmit powers, and which channels are counted together in the total-power limit signalled by higher layers?
questions.reference_answer: All the HS-PDSCHs intended for that UE shall be transmitted with equal power. The total-power limit counts together HS-PDSCHs, HS-SCCHs, E-AGCHs, E-RGCHs and E-HICHs in the cell.

questions.question: For a UE in soft handover receiving several E-HICH ACK/NACKs in one E-DCH TTI, which of those indications must be soft-combined before being handed to higher layers, and what happens when a radio link set holds only one radio link?
questions.reference_answer: ACK/NACKs from the same radio link set must be soft combined into one ACK/NACK information before being delivered to higher layers. If a radio link set contains only one radio link, detection is done as for a UE not in soft handover (no combining).

questions.question: Which three conditions must all hold for the UE to set the DPCCH2_TRANSMISSION variable to TRUE, and what must the UE do with the stored DPCCH2 info FDD IE when one of them stops being met?
questions.reference_answer: The three conditions are: the UE is in CELL_DCH state, the UE has stored the IE "DPCCH2 info FDD", and the variable HS_DSCH_RECEPTION is set to TRUE. If any condition stops being met, the UE shall clear the stored IE "DPCCH2 info FDD" (as well as set DPCCH2_TRANSMISSION to FALSE and trigger lower layers to stop DPCCH2 transmission).

questions.question: When a Node B cannot start a requested dedicated measurement and the Node B Communication Context ID IE was set to All NBCC, what value must the CRNC Communication Context ID IE take in the failure message, and which Measurement ID must that message carry?
questions.reference_answer: The CRNC Communication Context ID IE shall be set to the value "All CRNCCC". The message must carry the same Measurement ID that was used in the DEDICATED MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST message.

questions.question: On the Xw interface, a node receives a message whose AP IDs name a logical connection it knows but that was established for LWIP while the message concerns LWA. How must the node treat those AP IDs, and which cause value should its Error Indication carry?
questions.reference_answer: The node shall behave as if those AP ID(s) identify a logical connection which is unknown to it. If it subsequently initiates an Error Indication procedure, it shall include an appropriate cause value such as "Wrong WLAN Interworking Mode".

questions.question: A MExE classmark 2 device supports the JavaPhone Power Monitor package. Which two battery events must it generate as a minimum, and are the remaining Power Monitor events mandatory or merely recommended?
questions.reference_answer: It must at least generate BatteryCritical (when the battery is at a critically low level) and BatteryNormal (when the battery is no longer low). All the other Power Monitor events are merely recommended ("should be supported"), not mandatory.

questions.question: Beyond the mandated PersonalJava APIs, is a MExE classmark 2 device obliged to support any further Java APIs, and under what condition may the OpenCard terminal API be used to reach a smartcard other than the (U)SIM?
questions.reference_answer: No, MExE classmark 2 devices shall not be required to support any other Java APIs beyond the mandated PersonalJava APIs (though they may optionally do so). The OpenCard terminal API (opencard.core.terminal) may be used to access a smartcard other than the (U)SIM if the MExE device supports such smartcards and the smartcard is open to 3rd party applications.

questions.question: When a dynamic PCC/ADC rule from the PCRF carries an application identifier but the application detection filter sits in the UP function rather than in the PGW-C/TDF-C, what exactly must the control-plane function pass down to the PGW-U/TDF-U?
questions.reference_answer: The PGW-C/TDF-C must pass down the application identifier together with the parameters for traffic handling in the UP function, as required based on the dynamic PCC/ADC rule.

questions.question: At what point in solicited application reporting mode must the TDF-C choose the TDF-U, and which load and capacity parameters may drive that choice?
questions.reference_answer: The TDF-C shall select the TDF-U at PDN connection establishment (TDF session establishment). The selection may be based on the TDF-U's dynamic load and its relative static capacity, along with the capability of the UP function needed for the particular UE session.

questions.question: Which SEAL location management requirement covers finding the set of UEs near a requested location together with each one's position, and is on-demand as well as trigger-based reporting required?
questions.reference_answer: Requirement [AR-4.3.2-g] covers this: the SEAL shall provide a mechanism to enable vertical applications to obtain a list of UE(s), and the location information of each UE, in the proximity to a designated/requested location. Yes, both on-demand location reporting ([AR-4.3.2-c]) and trigger-based client location reporting ([AR-4.3.2-d]) are required.

questions.question: Which reference points must LM-UU use for subscription and notification signalling, and which pair does it use for transporting and routing the location management signalling itself?
questions.reference_answer: LM-UU shall use the SIP-1 and SIP-2 reference points for subscription/notification related signalling. For transport and routing of the location management signalling itself, LM-UU uses the HTTP-1 and HTTP-2 signalling control plane reference points.

questions.question: When a CC-POI is triggered by a CC-TF, over which interface and in which message does it obtain the CorrelationID, and where must it then place that CorrelationID?
questions.reference_answer: The CC-POI obtains the CorrelationID from the CC-TF over the LI_T3 interface, in the ActivateTask message. It then places that CorrelationID in the xCC sent to the MDF3.

questions.question: In the alternate deployment option for session-based IMS interception, under which roaming and redirection conditions must the IBCF provide the IRI-POI functions?
questions.reference_answer: The IBCF shall provide the IRI-POI functions if: the target is an outbound roaming (with LBO) IMS user; the IMS session to a target is redirected to a user in the IP domain; the IMS session to a target is redirected to an outbound roaming (with LBO) IMS user; or an inbound roaming (with LBO) IMS user is in communication with a target non-local ID on an IMS session employing home-routed media.

questions.question: To bring a non-current full native EPS security context back into use after handover from GERAN or UTRAN, which procedure must the UE and MME run, and what must the MME do before the NAS COUNT wraps around?
questions.reference_answer: The UE and the MME must run a NAS SMC (Security Mode Command) procedure. Before the NAS uplink or downlink COUNT wraps around with the current security context, the MME shall activate fresh NAS keys from an EPS AKA run or activate a native security context with sufficiently low NAS COUNT values.

questions.question: When an eNB turns on user plane integrity protection while adding a DRB, how must it choose the NR integrity algorithm relative to the EPS algorithm it had signalled in the AS Security Mode Command, and what does 128-EIA2 map onto?
questions.reference_answer: The eNB shall select the NR integrity algorithm (NIA) that corresponds to the EPS integrity algorithm (EIA) it selected and indicated to the UE in the AS Security Mode Command procedure. 128-EIA2 maps onto 128-NIA2.

questions.question: For an analogue connection to the POI, what nominal SJLR and RJLR values apply, and what limits constrain the RJLR at the maximum and minimum settings of a user-controlled receiving volume control?
questions.reference_answer: The nominal values are SJLR = 0 ± 3 dB and RJLR = 0 ± 3 dB. When the user-controlled receiving volume control is set to maximum, the RJLR shall not be ≤ -15 dB, and when set to minimum, the RJLR shall not be ≥ 16 dB.

questions.question: When several serviceURI elements appear under consumptionReporting, how must the UE pick one, and for how long must it keep using the chosen consumption report server unless it is redirected?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall randomly select one of the serviceURI elements with uniform distribution as the destination. It shall keep using that selected consumption report server for the entire duration of its "start", "ongoing", and "stop" consumption report submissions, unless the server redirects the UE to another one using an HTTP 3xx status code.

questions.question: Which of the four alternatives for obtaining SACH metadata fragments is the default one an MBMS Client must use, and which element with its child must the USBD describing the SACH contain?
questions.reference_answer: The default alternative is alternative d), where the MBMS Client constructs the bootstrap URL from MNC and MCC. The USBD describing the SACH shall contain the requiredCapabilities element with its feature child element.

questions.question: In a multiParty call, when a party is newly added, is the notification sent to the served mobile subscriber as well as to the remote parties, and what happens when a previously private communication rejoins the multiParty call?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, a notification is sent towards both the served mobile subscriber and all remote parties at invocation of the service; however, when a new party is subsequently added, the notification is sent only to all remote parties, not to the served mobile subscriber. When a previously private communication is added again (rejoins) the multiParty call, a notification shall be sent towards all remote parties.

questions.question: If the served subscriber has one active call and a held MPTY and chooses to join them, which notification goes to all remote parties, which notification goes to the previously held party, and what prevents the join from producing an active MPTY?
questions.reference_answer: A "MPTY invoke" notification is sent towards all remote parties, and a Retrieve notification (per TS 22.083) is sent towards the previously held remote party. The join results in an active MPTY except if the number of remote parties exceeds the number allowed, which prevents it.

questions.question: For Customized Ringing Signal in the CS domain, whose CRS takes priority when neither operator preference is configured, and what conditions must be met before the called party can copy the calling party's CRS as his own?
questions.reference_answer: By default, if no operator preference is set, the CRS set by the called party takes priority. The called party may copy the calling party's CRS as his own only if the calling user has enabled CRS sharing (if applicable) for that CRS instance, and both parties are subscribers to the same HPLMN with the called party within the HPLMN.

questions.question: A CTF receives a Charging Data Response [Initial] whose response code says the initial request failed. Beyond running the error handling for that code, what further request is it permitted to send to the CHF, and does the same option exist after a failed Termination response?
questions.reference_answer: Beyond performing the error handling applicable to the response code, the CTF may send a Charging Data Request [Termination] to the CHF. This same option does not exist after a failed Termination response — in that case the CTF shall only perform the error handling, with no further request permitted.

questions.question: When an NG-RAN node cannot deactivate a trace session because the UE is being handed over to another NG-RAN node, which message must it send to the AMF, and what deactivates the trace session besides an explicit DEACTIVATE TRACE?
questions.reference_answer: The NG-RAN node must send the TRACE FAILURE INDICATION message to the AMF using the NG interface. Besides an explicit DEACTIVATE TRACE message, the trace session is also deactivated when the NG-RAN node releases the UE context, which stops the Trace Recording Session.

questions.question: In the E-UTRAN Allocation and Retention Priority IE, what does Priority Level 15 mean, how are values 1 to 14 ordered, and how must a received value of 0 be treated?
questions.reference_answer: Priority Level 15 means "no priority". Values 1 to 14 are ordered in decreasing order of priority, i.e. 1 is the highest and 14 the lowest. A received value of 0 shall be treated as a logical error.

questions.question: For handheld UE in roaming bands, how must the total radiated power results from the right and left sides of the phantom head be combined, and besides the average, which per-channel TRP figure must also be met?
questions.reference_answer: The TRP results from the right and left sides of the phantom head shall be averaged in linear scale. Besides the average TRP, the lowest (minimum) TRP of each measured channel must also be higher than the minimum TRP requirement.

questions.question: In the ENVELOPE command for the (I-)WLAN Access Status event download, how many events may the Event list data object carry, and what source and destination must the terminal set in the Device identities?
questions.reference_answer: The Event list data object shall contain only one event, set to (I-)WLAN Access Status. The terminal shall set the Device identities source to terminal and destination to UICC.

questions.question: If a UE has ranging and sidelink positioning configuration both pre-configured in the ME and delivered as an RSLPP by the PCF, which one wins, and where does UICC configuration sit in that precedence order?
questions.reference_answer: The configuration provided as a RSLPP by PCF takes precedence over the ME pre-configured information, since PCF-provided RSLPP configuration is first in the precedence order (a) while ME pre-configured information is last (d). UICC-configured information sits third, between the application-server-provided configuration (via SR1) and the ME pre-configured information.

questions.question: Before a target UE may select a discovered UE as its located UE, what must the UE role in the RSPP metadata indicate, and in which message does that metadata arrive for V2X capable UEs?
questions.reference_answer: The UE role in the RSPP metadata must indicate that the UE supports UE role as a located UE. For V2X capable UEs, that metadata arrives in the DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message (for non-V2X capable UEs it arrives in the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message).

questions.question: In the ECSRedirectInfo type, which attribute is mandatory and what does the EEC use it for, and which two optional attributes are needed to set up the PDU session towards the redirected ECS?
questions.reference_answer: The mandatory attribute is ecsEndPt, which the EEC uses as the endpoint information (e.g. URI, FQDN, IP address) of the redirected ECS to which it sends the ECS service provisioning request. The two optional attributes needed to set up the PDU session towards the redirected ECS are dnn and snssai.

questions.question: When the transmission control server interface receives a Queue Position Info message whose Track Info field holds more than one Participant Reference, what exactly must it strip before forwarding, and how does that differ when only one Participant Reference is present?
questions.reference_answer: When the Track Info field contains more than one Participant Reference value, the transmission control server interface shall remove only the last Participant Reference value from the Track Info field before forwarding. When only one Participant Reference value is present, it instead removes the entire Track Info field from the outgoing message.

questions.question: If a Transmission Request arriving from a transmission participant carries no Track Info field, which three values must the transmission control server interface place into the Track Info field it creates, and what does it use when the participant-type element is unavailable?
questions.reference_answer: It must place the negotiated "mc_queueing" fmtp attribute value into the Queueing Capability value, a Participant Type value, and the temporary identifier as the first Transmission Participant Reference value. When the participant-type element is unavailable, it sets the Participant Type value to "unknown".

questions.question: When the AMF receives an UPLINK RAN CONFIGURATION TRANSFER carrying a SON Configuration Transfer IE whose Target RAN Node ID IE includes an NR CGI IE, which other identifier inside that IE must it ignore, and where does an EN-DC SON Configuration Transfer IE get forwarded instead?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF must ignore the Global RAN Node ID IE within the Target RAN Node ID IE (using the NR CGI IE instead to identify the target gNB). An EN-DC SON Configuration Transfer IE is instead transparently transferred towards an MME serving the eNB indicated in the Target eNB-ID IE.

questions.question: A warning message arrives with a Repetition Period IE of 0 and no Concurrent Warning Message Indicator IE. Under what single condition may the NG-RAN node still broadcast the secondary notification?
questions.reference_answer: The NG-RAN node may still broadcast the secondary notification only if the Number of Broadcasts Requested IE is set to "1".

questions.question: For non-UE-associated F1AP procedures, which IE must additionally accompany the Criticality Diagnostics IE when an Abstract Syntax Error or a Logical Error is reported, and how must a Class 1 response carrying a logical error be regarded?
questions.reference_answer: The Transaction ID IE must additionally accompany the Criticality Diagnostics IE in both cases (Abstract Syntax Error and Logical Error). A Class 1 response carrying a logical error must be regarded as the procedure being unsuccessfully terminated or not terminated, triggering local error handling.

questions.question: If the CP function receives a PFCP Session Report Request whose F-SEID it does not recognise, which rejection cause must it return, and when the EPFAR feature is in use what does a PSDBU flag set to 1 tell it about the session in the UP function?
questions.reference_answer: It shall return the rejection cause "Session context not found". When the EPFAR feature is in use, a PSDBU flag set to "1" tells the CP function that the PFCP Session is locally deleted in the UP function.

questions.question: An IMS ALG supporting OMR receives an SDP offer whose media line carries a "visited-realm" attribute. Which two checksums must it derive, and exactly which SDP lines feed the media level checksum?
questions.reference_answer: It must derive a session level checksum and a media level checksum. The media level checksum is calculated by summing the hex values of the individual ASCII characters (excluding white space) of the "m", "b", and "a" media level lines, including OMR-specific attributes but excluding the checksum attribute lines themselves.

questions.question: Local policy at an IMS-ALG forbids sending OMR related attributes towards the outgoing IP realm. What is the IMS-ALG obliged to do with the modified SDP offer before forwarding it?
questions.reference_answer: The IMS-ALG shall delete all OMR related attributes from the modified SDP offer before forwarding it.

questions.question: An IMS-ALG has forwarded an SDP offer without allocating a primary local MR and now gets back an SDP answer carrying a valid connection address. If it had earlier bypassed previous MRs, what must it copy into the media line of that answer?
questions.reference_answer: It must copy into the media line of the SDP answer the visited-realm or secondary-realm instance from the media line of the received SDP offer that was used to populate the connection address and port information in the forwarded offer, replacing the connection-address and port with those from the received SDP answer (and replacing the IP realm name with the local IP realm name if it is a connected IP realm).

questions.question: On what basis alone is an IMS-ALG permitted to decide that an IP realm is a connected IP realm of one of its local IP realms?
questions.reference_answer: The IMS-ALG shall determine if an IP realm is connected to a local IP realm based only on provisioning.

questions.question: A UA supporting OMR is about to send an initial SDP offer. Besides adding a visited-realm instance, what must it allocate for each IP realm/nettype/addrtype combination on the outgoing side, and what attribute does it compute last?
questions.reference_answer: For each IP realm/nettype/addrtype combination on the outgoing side (not already associated with the media line), the UA shall allocate an MR termination using the same codecs as the media line. The attribute it computes last is the checksum values, adding the "omr-s-cksum" and "omr-m-cksum" attributes for the media line.

questions.question: An MSC/IWF receives a call setup requesting "unrestricted digital information" on a 3,1 kHz audio bearer service. What must happen to the call, and what else besides compatibility checking has to be performed?
questions.reference_answer: The call shall fail with an error cause indicating that the network is unable to support the service requested. Besides compatibility checking, subscription checking shall also be performed, and if the subscription check fails the call setup shall be rejected.

questions.question: For a single data call, in which mode must the modem function operate for a mobile originated call versus a mobile terminated call, and what decides the mode when the "Reverse Call Setup Direction" IE is absent from a MODIFY message?
questions.reference_answer: For a mobile originated call the modem function shall operate in the calling mode, and for a mobile terminated call in the answering mode. When the Reverse Call Setup Direction IE is absent from a MODIFY message, the direction is derived from the initial call setup direction, i.e. the mode is the same as for single calls.

questions.question: Before user data may be carried on a PLMN traffic channel, the controlling entities have to run an end-to-end synchronization process. At which message is the "physical connection established" indication given for a mobile terminated call, and for a mobile initiated in-call modification?
questions.reference_answer: For a mobile terminated call (MTC), the indication is given on sending the CONNECT ACKNOWLEDGE message. For a mobile initiated in-call modification, it is given on sending the MODIFY COMPLETE message (sent after reception of the ASSIGNMENT COMPLETE or RAB ASSIGNMENT RESPONSE message).

questions.question: On the transit side towards the fixed network, what is done with circuit 108 to the selected modem at the start of timer T, and how are the remaining interchange circuits treated until timer T expires?
questions.reference_answer: At the start of timer T, circuit 108 to the selected modem is switched from the "OFF" to "ON" condition, initiating establishment of the modem connection. The remaining interchange circuits towards the modem (except CT108) are held in the OFF condition until timer T expires, when they are switched to ON.

questions.question: During an ongoing multimedia call the modems renegotiate to 28.8 kbit/s using the V.34 seamless data rate change mechanism. Which message must the MSC initiate towards the UE, and how is the new rate adapted to the 33.6 kbit/s traffic channel between the UE and the IWF?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC shall initiate a MODIFY message to indicate the new data rate to the UE. HDLC flag stuffing or the stuffing mode defined in ITU-T Recommendation H.223 (Annexes A, B and C) shall be used to adapt the 31.2 or 28.8 kbit/s data rate to the 33.6 kbit/s traffic channel between the UE and the IWF, using the stuffing pattern found during traffic channel setup.

questions.question: An I-MGCF supporting the PSTN XML body received two PSTN XML Bearer Capability elements in an INVITE, but the succeeding trunk does not support TMR "64 kBit/s preferred" and no matching elements arrived in the Access Transport Parameter. What must the I-MGCF build, and in which response does it place it?
questions.reference_answer: The I-MGCF must build a PSTN XML body containing a BearerCapability element copied from the first BearerCapability element received in the PSTN XML in the INVITE, a HighLayerCompatibility element (copied from the first one received, if two were present), and a ProgressIndicator element with "Progress Description" value 5, "Coding Standard" value "00", and default "Location" value "0011 (Transit Network)". It places this PSTN XML body in the 18x Response.

questions.question: Which received ISUP messages force the I-MGCF to send a SIP 181 Call is being forwarded, and what must the call diversion information and the optional backward call indicators show for that obligation to apply?
questions.reference_answer: The I-MGCF sends the SIP 181 Call is being forwarded upon receiving an ACM or a CPG message. For that obligation to apply, the call diversion information must not indicate that presentation is not allowed, and the optional backward call indicators must indicate that in-band information is available.

questions.question: With the in-dialog overlap signalling network option enabled, under what condition on the incoming INVITE must the I-MGCF send a reliable 183 Session Progress, and how soon?
questions.reference_answer: The I-MGCF must send a reliable 183 Session Progress if the incoming SIP INVITE request contains an indication that the 100rel extension is supported or required. It must be sent immediately after reception of the INVITE request.

questions.question: An O-MGCF sent an INVITE without determining the end of address signalling and then receives a 484 Address Incomplete while Ti/w2 is running. Which timer must it start, what stops both timers, and which REL cause value is sent if that timer expires?
questions.reference_answer: The O-MGCF must start timer Ti/w3 (if there are no other pending INVITE transactions for the call). Both Ti/w2 and Ti/w3 are stopped at the receipt of a SAM, a SIP 18x provisional response, or a SIP 200 OK (INVITE). If Ti/w3 expires, the O-MGCF sends a REL message with Cause Value 28.

questions.question: When a BYE arrives at the O-MGCF without any Reason header field carrying a Q.850 Cause Value, which ISUP cause code must the REL message use?
questions.reference_answer: The O-MGCF sends a REL message with Cause Code value 16 (Normal Call Clearing).

questions.question: In the non-roaming case, when a PCEF or BBERF first contacts the PCRF realm through a DRA acting as a redirect agent, which AVP carries the PCRF identity back to it, and which AVPs may convey the UE's IPv4 address?
questions.reference_answer: The DRA includes the PCRF identity in the Redirect-Host AVP in the Diameter reply. The UE's IPv4 address may be conveyed in the Framed-IP-Address AVP (and the UE's IPv6 prefix may be conveyed in the Framed-Ipv6-Prefix AVP).

questions.question: Password procedures were started by an MS that gives no SS version indicator, and the procedure runs into errors. Which three protocol error values is the network forbidden to send back?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall not send the protocol error values "DataMissing", "CallBarred", or "NumberOfPWAttemptsViolation".

questions.question: In supplementary service compatibility, which entity has to declare its capabilities to the other, and what is the network expected to cope with because the reverse declaration is not required?
questions.reference_answer: The MS has to declare its capabilities to the network (providing information about its capabilities so the network can adjust to them), while the network does not provide the MS with capability information in return. Because the reverse declaration is not required, the network is expected to be able to cope cleanly with unexpected information.

questions.question: A new call independent SS transaction arrives at the network and the SS version indicator carries a value the network does not recognise. How must the network proceed, and what must it do with the noted indicator once the transaction ends?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall attempt to handle the communication at its highest possible version when the SS version indicator value is unrecognised. Once the transaction ends, the network shall discard the noted indicator information.

questions.question: For a call related common information element SS operation, in which message must the network look for the SS version indicator, and which phase governs its behaviour if the indicator turns out to be absent?
questions.reference_answer: The network must check the 3GPP TS 24.008 carrier message for the SS version indicator. If the indicator is absent, the network shall operate according to Phase 1.

questions.question: When offering the vnd.3gpp.clearmode RTP payload, what media name must appear in the SDP m= line, and how must the optional network-initiated-service-change parameter be carried?
questions.reference_answer: The media name "audio" (the MIME type) shall appear in the SDP "m=" line. The optional "network-initiated-service-change" parameter, if supplied, shall be encoded within the "fmtp" SDP attribute, with no values supplied for the parameter.

questions.question: At which node does interworking between the radio interface compatibility mechanisms and MAP take place, and what must happen when the MS signals a higher SS version than the MSC/VLR can support at all?
questions.reference_answer: Interworking between the radio interface compatibility mechanisms and MAP occurs at the MSC/VLR. If the MS signals a higher version than the MSC/VLR is capable of supporting at all, the MSC/VLR shall attempt to support service at the highest version it does support, and if that is not possible the communication is rejected.

questions.question: Which kind of protocol change is defined as non-compatible for supplementary services, and what must that change cause with respect to the SS version indicator?
questions.reference_answer: Non-compatible protocol changes are defined as the introduction of mandatory protocol elements or new operations. Such a change shall cause an increment in the protocol version, which must be reflected in the use of the SS version indicator.

questions.question: When supplementary services data held in the HLR may have been corrupted, which operation does the network send and on what kind of transaction, and what must the procedure create?
questions.reference_answer: The network sends the ForwardCheckSSIndication operation on a call independent SS transaction. The procedure shall create a new network initiated transaction.

questions.question: An ATCF supporting CS to PS SRVCC has to hand ATGW information to the SC UE. When it builds the SDP, what must the c-line be set to for IPv4 and for IPv6, and which port number goes on the media line?
questions.reference_answer: The c-line shall be set to the unspecified address (0.0.0.0) for IPv4, or to a domain name within the ".invalid" DNS top-level domain for IPv6. The port number on the media line shall be set to 9.

questions.question: An SC UE that supports the MSC server assisted mid-call feature and PS to CS SRVCC for calls in alerting phase is sending an initial SIP INVITE. Which media feature tags must appear in its Contact header field?
questions.reference_answer: It must include the g.3gpp.mid-call media feature tag (for MSC server assisted mid-call support) and the g.3gpp.srvcc-alerting media feature tag (for PS to CS SRVCC for calls in alerting phase), both as described in annex C.

questions.question: When an SCC AS supporting OMR merges media lines from a source access leg and a target access leg into one SDP offer and any of them carries OMR attributes, what is it required to do before sending the offer to the remote party?
questions.reference_answer: It is required to recalculate the checksums as specified in subclause 5.6.3 of TS 29.079 before sending the offer to the remote party. (If it has not changed the content of an m-line and its associated attributes, it shall only calculate the session level checksum and replace the value in each occurrence of the "a=omr-s-cksum" attribute.)

questions.question: For an MSC server supporting PS to CS SRVCC access transfer, which option tag must go into the Supported header field of an initial INVITE, and which header field mechanism is it explicitly forbidden to use for preconditions?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC server must include the "precondition" option tag in the Supported header field of the initial INVITE. It is explicitly forbidden to indicate the requirement for the precondition mechanism using the Require header field.

questions.question: A UE wants to move an existing PDU session over to an ePDG connected to EPC. Which PDU session types and which SSC modes is it forbidden to attempt to transfer?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall not attempt to transfer PDU sessions with PDU session type "Ethernet" or "Unstructured", and shall not attempt to transfer PDU sessions with the selected SSC mode set to "SSC mode 2" or "SSC mode 3", to an ePDG connected to EPC.

questions.question: For 5GS session management in NB-N1 mode, how many extra seconds must a UE add to the applicable NAS timer value, and at which point in a NAS procedure is that value allowed to be recalculated?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must add 180 seconds to the applicable NAS timer value. That value shall be calculated at the start of a NAS procedure and shall not be re-calculated until the NAS procedure is completed, restarted, or aborted.

questions.question: On the fifth expiry of timer T5012, what must the LMF release and what does it do with the network initiated user plane connection establishment procedure?
questions.reference_answer: The LMF must release the allocated LCS-UP binding ID value and its association with the UE, and release the association of the TLS connection with the UE, if any. It then aborts the network initiated user plane connection establishment procedure.

questions.question: The VLR invokes MAP_FORWARD_NEW_TMSI but at that moment there is no radio connection to the MS. What is the MSC obliged to do with the received MAP service request?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC shall ignore the received MAP_FORWARD_NEW_TMSI request message.

questions.question: A UE receives a USER PLANE CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT COMMAND message while an LCS-UP connection binding procedure is still running. Which timer must it stop, what stored identifier must it delete, and what happens to both procedures?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must stop timer T5110 and delete the stored LCS-UP binding ID. It must abort the ongoing LCS-UP connection binding procedure and the ongoing network initiated user plane connection establishment procedure, then progress the network initiated user plane connection establishment procedure initiated by the newly received message.

questions.question: A UE has stored some segments of SIB17bis and then notices the value tag has changed since an earlier segment was stored. What must it do with the stored segments, and after how long without a complete assembly should it discard them?
