questions.reference_answer: The UE must discard all stored segments of SIB17bis. It should discard stored segments if the complete SIB17bis has not been assembled within a period of 3 hours.

questions.question: A UE cannot comply with part of the configuration carried in an RRCResume message. Which state must it move to and with which release cause?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must move to RRC_IDLE (performing the actions upon going to RRC_IDLE as specified in 5.3.11) with release cause 'RRC Resume failure'.

questions.question: On receiving an RRCReject that carries a waitTime, which timer does the UE start with that value, and when the RRCReject came from upper layers, for which access categories is the UE told that access barring does NOT apply?
questions.reference_answer: The UE starts timer T302 with the value set to waitTime. When the RRCReject came from upper layers, the UE informs upper layers that access barring is applicable for all access categories except categories '0' and '2' — meaning barring does NOT apply to access categories '0' and '2'.

questions.question: Upper layers ask a UE in RRC_IDLE to establish an RRC connection and supply an Access Category and Access Identities. Which procedure must the UE run first, and what must it have ensured before initiating RRC connection establishment at all?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must first perform the unified access control procedure (as specified in clause 5.3.14) using the Access Category and Access Identities provided by upper layers. Before initiating RRC connection establishment at all, it must have ensured it has valid and up to date essential system information (as specified in clause 5.2.2.2).

questions.question: When a UE receives a SecurityModeCommand, which key must it derive before it can ask lower layers to verify the message's integrity protection, and which algorithm identifier selects that key?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must derive the KRRCint key before requesting lower layers to verify the integrity protection of the SecurityModeCommand message. The key is associated with (selected by) the integrityProtAlgorithm identifier indicated in the SecurityModeCommand message.

questions.question: How does a UE compute the SFN and subframe at which each RMTC occasion starts from rmtc-Periodicity and rmtc-SubframeOffset, and what is it forbidden to consider on the rmtc-Frequency?
questions.reference_answer: The SFN and subframe are computed as: SFN mod T = FLOOR(rmtc-SubframeOffset/10), subframe = rmtc-SubframeOffset mod 10, with T = rmtc-Periodicity/10. On the rmtc-Frequency, the UE shall not consider RSSI measurements taken outside the configured RMTC occasion (which lasts for measDurationSymbols).

questions.question: For an event-triggered report, which threshold or offset parameter does the UE take as the sorting quantity for an NR cell under eventA3 versus eventA5, and what does it use for an E-UTRA cell?
questions.reference_answer: For an NR cell under eventA3, the UE takes the quantity used in the aN-Offset as the sorting quantity; under eventA5, it takes the quantity used in the a5-Threshold2. For an E-UTRA cell, it uses the quantity used in the bN-ThresholdEUTRA.

questions.question: When a UE builds a LocationMeasurementIndication to signal the start of RSTD measurements towards E-UTRA, what must measurementIndication be set to, and what value is used when the procedure signals the stop of location related measurements?
questions.reference_answer: measurementIndication is set to eutra-RSTD (according to information received from upper layers) to signal the start of RSTD measurements towards E-UTRA. When the procedure signals the stop of location related measurements, measurementIndication is set to the value release.

questions.question: An IAB-MT in RRC_CONNECTED needs to send F1-C related information over the UL information transfer procedure. Which radio bearer must already be established before it is allowed to initiate the procedure?
questions.reference_answer: SRB2 or split SRB2 must already be established before the IAB-MT is allowed to initiate the UL information transfer procedure to send F1-C related information.

questions.question: An NG-RAN node receives a MULTICAST GROUP PAGING message. Which IE identifies the MBS session to be paged, and what must the node do if the Paging DRX IE is present?
questions.reference_answer: The MBS Session ID IE identifies the MBS session to be paged. If the Paging DRX IE is present, the NG-RAN node shall use it according to TS 38.304.

questions.question: Which two conditions involving the Partially Allowed NSSAI IE in an INITIAL UE MESSAGE force the AMF to consider the procedure failed?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF considers the procedure failed if the Partially Allowed NSSAI IE is received and the total number of S-NSSAIs in the Allowed NSSAI and Partially Allowed NSSAI together exceeds eight, or if any S-NSSAI present in the Partially Allowed NSSAI IE is also present in the Allowed NSSAI IE.

questions.question: On receiving a REROUTE NAS REQUEST, which IE tells the NG-RAN node where to reroute the INITIAL UE MESSAGE, and what must it do with the Allowed NSSAI IE if that IE is present?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF Set ID IE tells the NG-RAN node where to reroute the INITIAL UE MESSAGE. If the Allowed NSSAI IE is present, the NG-RAN node shall propagate it in the rerouted INITIAL UE MESSAGE message.

questions.question: An NG RESET message arrives with a UE-associated Logical NG-connection Item that carries neither the AMF UE NGAP ID IE nor the RAN UE NGAP ID IE. What must the NG-RAN node do with that item, and what may it put in the NG RESET ACKNOWLEDGE?
questions.reference_answer: The NG-RAN node shall ignore that UE-associated Logical NG-connection Item IE. It may return the empty UE-associated Logical NG-connection Item IE in the UE-associated Logical NG-connection List IE in the NG RESET ACKNOWLEDGE message.

questions.question: Which IEs must an ERROR INDICATION message carry as a minimum, and which two identifiers have to be added when the Error Indication was triggered through UE-associated signalling?
questions.reference_answer: The ERROR INDICATION message shall contain at least either the Cause IE or the Criticality Diagnostics IE. When triggered through UE-associated signalling, the AMF UE NGAP ID IE and the RAN UE NGAP ID IE must also be included.

questions.question: After an AMF STATUS INDICATION arrives, what must the NG-RAN node conclude about the indicated GUAMIs, and how does the presence of the Backup AMF Name IE change the reselection it performs?
questions.reference_answer: The NG-RAN node must conclude that the indicated GUAMI(s) will be unavailable and perform AMF reselection. If the Backup AMF Name IE is included, the NG-RAN node shall, if supported, perform AMF reselection considering the AMF as indicated by that Backup AMF Name IE (instead of a normal reselection).

questions.question: A UE receives a TRANSPORT FORMAT COMBINATION CONTROL message on AM or UM RLC whose protocol error sets PROTOCOL_ERROR_REJECT to TRUE. Which failure message must it send, on which logical channel and RLC mode, and where does it read the RRC transaction identifier from?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must send a TRANSPORT FORMAT COMBINATION CONTROL FAILURE message on the uplink DCCH using AM RLC. It reads the RRC transaction identifier from the value of "RRC transaction identifier" in the entry for the TRANSPORT FORMAT COMBINATION CONTROL message in the table "Rejected transactions" in the variable TRANSACTIONS.

questions.question: After a UE discards an invalid PHYSICAL SHARED CHANNEL ALLOCATION message, which message does it submit on the uplink SHCCH, which counter is reset and which timer is started?
questions.reference_answer: It submits the PUSCH CAPACITY REQUEST message on the uplink SHCCH. Counter V310 is reset, and timer T310 is started.

questions.question: A CELL UPDATE CONFIRM message arrives with a protocol error and V302 is still not greater than N302. Which variable must the UE set to TRUE, and which message does it rebuild and send on the uplink CCCH?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must set the variable PROTOCOL_ERROR_INDICATOR to TRUE. It rebuilds and sends the CELL UPDATE message (or the URA UPDATE message for a URA update procedure) on the uplink CCCH.

questions.question: Timer T314 expires while T302 is not running but T315 is. Which radio bearers must the UE release locally, judged by which value of the "Re-establishment timer" IE in ESTABLISHED_RABS?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must release locally all radio bearers associated with radio access bearers for which, in the variable ESTABLISHED_RABS, the "Re-establishment timer" IE is set to "useT314".

questions.question: On expiry of timer T315 with T302 stopped and T314 running, which flag in RB_TIMER_INDICATOR must the UE set, and from which variable must the information about the released radio access bearers be deleted?
questions.reference_answer: The UE must set the "T315 expired" flag in variable RB_TIMER_INDICATOR to TRUE. Information about the released radio access bearers must be deleted from the variable ESTABLISHED_RABS.

questions.question: An ACTIVE SET UPDATE message carries a protocol error that sets PROTOCOL_ERROR_REJECT to TRUE. Which failure cause value must the UE put into the ACTIVE SET UPDATE FAILURE message, and from which table in the variable TRANSACTIONS does it take the RRC transaction identifier?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall set the IE "failure cause" to the cause value "protocol error", and it takes the "RRC transaction identifier" from the entry for the ACTIVE SET UPDATE message in the table "Rejected transactions" in the variable TRANSACTIONS.

questions.question: An ACTIVE SET UPDATE message reaches a UE that is not in CELL_DCH state. Which "Protocol error cause" must be carried in the failure message, and from which table in TRANSACTIONS is the transaction identifier taken in this case?
questions.reference_answer: The IE "Protocol error cause" must be set to "Message not compatible with receiver state", and the RRC transaction identifier is taken from the entry for the ACTIVE SET UPDATE message in the table "Accepted transactions" in the variable TRANSACTIONS.

questions.question: A UE performs an inter-RAT cell reselection to UTRAN and the associated NAS procedures need an RRC connection. What value must ESTABLISHMENT_CAUSE be set to, and how does it rank against the cause requested by upper layers?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall set the variable ESTABLISHMENT_CAUSE to "Inter-RAT cell reselection", and this value has priority over the cause requested by upper layers.

questions.question: When a MEASUREMENT CONTROL message is rejected for a protocol error, which additional IE must a UE that supports it copy into the MEASUREMENT CONTROL FAILURE message besides the RRC transaction identifier?
questions.reference_answer: If the UE supports inclusion of measurement identity, it must also set the IE "Measurement Identity" in the MEASUREMENT CONTROL FAILURE message to the value of "Measurement identity" in the entry for the MEASUREMENT CONTROL message in the table "Rejected transactions" in the variable TRANSACTIONS.

questions.question: On transition from CELL_FACH to CELL_DCH with stored intra-frequency measurements, under what condition on the old cell does the UE resume measurement reporting, and what must happen before reporting on the downlink frequency associated with the secondary uplink frequency can restart?
questions.reference_answer: The UE resumes measurement reporting on that frequency only if the cell from which it transited from CELL_FACH state is included in the active set for CELL_DCH state. Reporting on the downlink frequency associated with the secondary uplink frequency is not resumed and can only restart after a MEASUREMENT CONTROL message is received with the corresponding measurement identity.

questions.question: A COMMON TRANSPORT CHANNEL RESOURCES REQUEST carries only one of the Transport Layer Address IE and the Binding ID IE for a transport channel to be established. What must the DRNC do, and with which message?
questions.reference_answer: The DRNC shall reject the procedure using the COMMON TRANSPORT CHANNEL RESOURCES FAILURE message.

questions.question: On receiving a COMMON TRANSPORT CHANNEL RESOURCES RELEASE REQUEST, when is the DRNC obliged to release only the C-RNTI and its RACH/FACH resources rather than the whole UE Context identified by the D-RNTI?
questions.reference_answer: The DRNC shall release only the C-RNTI and its related RACH and/or FACH (and, for FDD/1.28Mcps TDD, HS-DSCH) resources, instead of the whole UE Context identified by the D-RNTI, when the UE is using dedicated resources (DCH, or for TDD USCH and/or DSCH) in the DRNS.

questions.question: An ERROR INDICATION on Iur must reuse which signalling bearer, and when a DRNC sends it to an SRNC in connectionless mode, under what condition must the S-RNTI IE be included?
questions.reference_answer: The ERROR INDICATION message shall reuse the same mode of the signalling bearer and the same signalling bearer connection (if connection oriented) as the message that triggered the procedure. When sent from a DRNC to an SRNC using connectionless mode, the S-RNTI IE shall be included if the UE Context addressed by the D-RNTI IE received in the triggering message exists.

questions.question: A RESET REQUEST arrives on Iur with the Reset Indicator IE set to "Context". What must RNC2 remove for UE Contexts identified by the S-RNTI IE while acting as DRNC, compared with those identified by the D-RNTI IE while acting as SRNC?
questions.reference_answer: For UE Contexts identified by the S-RNTI IE, RNC2 acting as DRNC shall remove all the indicated UE Contexts and all radio resources allocated for them (and take actions per Annex D.2). For UE Contexts identified by the D-RNTI IE, RNC2 acting as SRNC shall remove only the information related to RNC1 for those UE Contexts and the radio resources allocated for them.

questions.question: On receiving an initial INVITE, what must the MGCF send to the IM-MGW as remote information, and what value must the reserve value indicator take when DTMF support is required together with speech?
questions.reference_answer: The MGCF shall send the appropriate remote codec(s), the remote UDP port, and the remote IP address to the IM-MGW as remote information. If DTMF support together with speech support is required, the reserve value indicator shall be set to "true".

questions.question: In an INFORMATION TRANSFER CONTROL REQUEST on Iur, which IE decides between suspending and resuming information transfer, and which IE names the cells the control applies to?
questions.reference_answer: The Control Type IE (indicating Suspension IE or Resume IE) decides between suspending and resuming information transfer, and the UMTS Cell Information IE within the Controlled Object Scope IE names the cells the control applies to.

questions.question: A UE is moved to RRC_IDLE by an RRCConnectionRelease that carries no redirectedCarrierInfo. On which carrier must it then try to select a suitable cell?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall attempt to select a suitable cell on an EUTRA carrier.

questions.question: An NB-IoT UE receives an RRCConnectionRelease-NB whose redirectedCarrierInfo points to a carrier where no suitable cell can be found. What is it then allowed to camp on?
questions.reference_answer: It is allowed to camp on a suitable cell of any NB-IoT carrier.

questions.question: In the Any Cell Selection state, what must a UE do once a complete scan of all RATs and frequency bands it supports has failed to turn up a suitable cell, and what kind of cell does it search for first?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall attempt to find an acceptable cell of any PLMN to camp on, trying all RATs supported by the UE, and it searches first for a high quality cell.

questions.question: While Camped on Any Cell, which two occasions must trigger the UE's cell reselection evaluation process?
questions.reference_answer: The cell reselection evaluation process must be triggered by UE internal triggers (to meet performance as specified in TS 36.133) and when information on the BCCH or BR-BCCH used for the cell reselection evaluation procedure has been modified.

questions.question: For a UE camping on E-UTRA connected to EPC, what is it required to ignore about Access Class and ACDC category restrictions when choosing a cell to camp on?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall ignore Access Class or ACDC category related cell access restrictions when selecting a cell to camp on, i.e. it shall not reject a cell for camping on because access on that cell is not allowed for any of its Access Classes or ACDC categories; a change of the indicated access restriction shall not trigger cell reselection.

questions.question: When NAS asks the AS to hunt for available CSGs, what must the UE search for on each carrier as a minimum, and which items does it report back to NAS alongside the CSG ID?
questions.reference_answer: On each carrier the UE shall at least search for the strongest cell and read its system information, and it reports back to NAS the available CSG ID(s) together with their "HNB name" (if broadcast) and PLMN(s).

questions.question: An eNB receives an E-RAB MODIFY REQUEST whose E-RAB Level QoS Parameters IE has a QCI indicating a GBR bearer for an E-RAB that was previously non-GBR, but no GBR QoS Information IE is present. How must the eNB treat that modification?
questions.reference_answer: The eNB shall consider the modification of the corresponding E-RAB as failed.

questions.question: Which three defects in an E-RAB MODIFICATION INDICATION message force the MME to trigger the UE Context Release procedure?
questions.reference_answer: The MME triggers the UE Context Release procedure if: (1) the E-RAB MODIFICATION INDICATION message does not contain all the E-RABs previously included in the UE Context; (2) it contains several E-RAB ID IEs set to the same value; (3) the CSG Membership Info IE does not contain the Cell Access Mode IE set to "hybrid".

questions.question: When a UE INFORMATION TRANSFER message from the MME carries the UE Level QoS Parameters IE or the UE Radio Capability IE, what must the eNB do with that information?
questions.reference_answer: If the UE Level QoS Parameters IE or the UE Radio Capability IE is contained in the UE INFORMATION TRANSFER message, the eNB shall store this information in the UE context and use it as specified in TS 23.401.

questions.question: A PRACK arrives at the MGCF carrying no SDP at all. Is the Configure IMS Resources procedure invoked, and under what other SDP condition is it also skipped?
questions.reference_answer: No, if no SDP is received the Configure IMS Resources procedure is not invoked. It is also skipped if the received SDP does not contain relevant changes compared to the previous SDP.

questions.question: Which node generates the UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST on S1, and give some of the cause values it is expected to indicate for the release of the UE-associated logical S1-connection.
questions.reference_answer: The eNB controlling the UE-associated logical S1-connection generates the UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST. Example cause values include "User Inactivity", "Radio Connection With UE Lost", "CSG Subscription Expiry", "CS Fallback triggered", "Redirection towards 1xRTT", "Inter-RAT Redirection", "UE Not Available for PS Service", and "Release due to pre-emption".

questions.question: A UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION INDICATION arrives at the MME without any CSG Membership Info IE, although the UE had earlier been given resources from a hybrid cell. What must the MME conclude?
questions.reference_answer: The MME shall consider that the UE has moved into an open access cell.

questions.question: A target eNB gets a HANDOVER REQUEST carrying a CSG Id IE but no CSG Membership Status IE, and the CSG Id does not match that of the target cell. What must it send back to the MME?
questions.reference_answer: The target eNB shall send the HANDOVER FAILURE message to the MME with an appropriate cause value.

questions.question: In a HANDOVER REQUEST, what must the target eNB do when several E-RAB ID IEs inside the E-RABs To Be Setup List IE carry the same value, and what is triggered when the Subscriber Profile ID for RAT/Frequency priority IE is missing from the transparent container although the source eNB had it?
questions.reference_answer: The target eNB shall not admit the corresponding E-RABs when several E-RAB ID IEs in the E-RABs To Be Setup List IE carry the same value. When the Subscriber Profile ID for RAT/Frequency priority IE is missing from the Source eNB to Target eNB Transparent Container IE despite being available in the source eNB, the target eNB shall trigger a local error handling.

questions.question: At what moment must the target eNB send the HANDOVER NOTIFY message, and under what condition is the PSCell Information IE mandatory in it?
questions.reference_answer: The target eNB shall send the HANDOVER NOTIFY message when the UE has been identified in the target cell and the S1 handover has been successfully completed. The PSCell Information IE shall be included if the UE is configured with EN-DC radio resources and the PSCell information is available.

questions.question: What must the source eNB stop doing before it sends the eNB STATUS TRANSFER message, and which three IEs go into the E-RABs Subject to Status Transfer Item IE for every E-RAB where PDCP-SN and HFN status preservation applies?
questions.reference_answer: The source eNB must stop assigning PDCP-SNs to downlink SDUs before sending the eNB STATUS TRANSFER message. For every E-RAB where PDCP-SN and HFN status preservation applies, it includes the E-RAB ID IE, the UL COUNT value IE, and the DL COUNT value IE in the E-RABs Subject to Status Transfer Item IE.

questions.question: An MS sits in STANDBY state and has uplink data to send, but it is now in a different mode (A/Gb versus Iu) from when it last sent anything. What must it do first, and which single signalling message exempts it from that obligation?
questions.reference_answer: The MS must perform the RA update procedure before sending the data or signalling. The RA update procedure need not be performed if the signalling message is a power-off detach.

questions.question: When an SGSN using S4 receives a Downlink Data Notification from the S-GW for an MS in PMM-IDLE state, where must it page, and which cell types can that cover?
questions.reference_answer: The SGSN shall page in the RA where the MS is located, which may include both A/Gb mode and Iu mode cells.

questions.question: In which message must the MS always send its MS radio access capability to the SGSN irrespective of whether it is attaching in A/Gb or Iu mode, and in which later messages does the SGSN ask for the remaining radio capabilities?
questions.reference_answer: The MS shall always send its MS radio access capability in the GPRS Attach Request message, regardless of whether it is attaching in A/Gb or Iu mode. The SGSN requests the MS's remaining radio capabilities in the Attach Complete or RA Update Complete messages.

questions.question: When an MS has to be paged, which Gb Coverage Class Information must the SGSN hand to the BSS, in which BSSGP message, and what associated identity has to accompany it?
questions.reference_answer: The SGSN shall provide the most recently received Gb Coverage Class Information to the BSS as part of the BSSGP Paging Request message, accompanied by the associated cell identity that was indicated in the BSSGP PDU carrying that Gb Coverage Class Information.

questions.question: The MGCF has requested a continuity check tone on the TDM termination towards the CS network. Which procedure does the IM-MGW use to report the incoming tone, and what must the MGCF wait for before it may send the COT?
questions.reference_answer: The IM-MGW uses the Continuity Check Verify procedure to notify the MGCF of an incoming continuity check tone. The MGCF shall wait until receiving this notification before sending the COT.

questions.question: What event resets and starts the READY timer in the MS and in the SGSN respectively, which state do the MM contexts fall back to when it expires, and which node alone may change its length and in which messages?
questions.reference_answer: The READY timer is reset and begins running in the MS when an LLC PDU is transmitted, and in the SGSN when an LLC PDU is correctly received. When it expires, the MM contexts in the MS and SGSN return to STANDBY state. Only the SGSN may change the length of the READY timer, by transmitting a new value in the Attach Accept or Routeing Area Update Accept messages.

questions.question: An MSC/VLR wants an SGSN to report the next activity from a particular subscriber. Which BSSAP+ message does it send, what flag must the SGSN set, and what must the SGSN do if the detected activity leads to no procedure towards the MSC/VLR?
questions.reference_answer: The MSC/VLR sends a BSSAP+ Alert Request (IMSI) message to the SGSN; the SGSN shall set NGAF. If the detected activity leads to no procedure towards the MSC/VLR, the SGSN shall send an MS Activity Indication (IMSI) message towards the MSC/VLR.

questions.question: Once a P-TMSI Signature has been given to the MS, in which three uplink requests must the MS include it, and what should the SGSN do when the value it receives does not match the stored one?
questions.reference_answer: The MS must include the P-TMSI Signature in the next Routeing Area Update Request, Detach Request, and Attach Request. If the value received does not match the stored one, the SGSN should use the security functions to authenticate the MS.

questions.question: In A/Gb mode, at which message does the MS start ciphering and at which point does the SGSN start it? During a routeing area update where authentication is skipped but ciphering was already in use, what resumes ciphering on each side?
questions.reference_answer: In A/Gb mode, the MS starts ciphering after sending the Authentication and Ciphering Response message, and the SGSN starts ciphering when it receives a valid Authentication and Ciphering Response message. If authentication is omitted during a routeing area update and ciphering was already in use, the SGSN resumes ciphering with the same algorithm when it sends a ciphered Routeing Area Update Accept message, and the MS resumes ciphering when it receives that ciphered Routeing Area Update Accept message.

questions.question: Which category of GPRS-attached MS is excused from performing periodic RA updates, and for an MS that is both IMSI- and GPRS-attached in a network operating in mode I, which periodic updates are performed and what must the MSC/VLR disable?
questions.reference_answer: A/Gb mode MSs in class-B mode of operation engaged in CS communication are excused from periodic RA updates. For an MS that is both IMSI- and GPRS-attached in a network operating in mode I, periodic RA updates shall be performed and periodic LA updates shall not be performed; the MSC/VLR must disable implicit detach for GPRS-attached MSs and instead rely on the SGSN to receive periodic RA updates.

questions.question: A VLR that does not support Long Forwarded-to Numbers is updated for a subscriber who has a Long Forwarded-to Number registered for CFB. What does the HLR send if a default forwarded-to number is stored, and what service state does it send otherwise?
questions.reference_answer: If a default forwarded-to number (up to 15 digits) is stored in the HLR, the HLR sends the VLR an Insert Subscriber Data message containing that default forwarded-to number in the Forwarded-to number parameter. Otherwise, the HLR sends the VLR the service state (Provisioned, Not Registered, Not Active, Not Induced).

questions.question: When a subscriber with CFB in registration state "Registered" attaches to a VLR, which registration parameter and which three subscription options must the HLR pass to that VLR?
questions.reference_answer: The HLR must pass the registration parameter "forwarded-to number", and information about the subscription options "notification to the calling party", "notification to the forwarding party", and "MSISDN of the served subscriber can be presented to the forwarded-to subscriber".

questions.question: For CFNRy, which two registration parameters must the HLR send to the VLR when the registration state is "Registered", on top of the subscription options?
questions.reference_answer: The HLR must send the registration parameters "forwarded-to number" and "no reply condition timer", on top of the subscription options "notification to the calling party", "notification to the forwarding party", and "MSISDN of the served subscriber can be presented to the forwarded-to subscriber".

questions.question: In an Any Time Modification ack, when must the Forwarded-to number IE be present and when must the Long forwarded-to number IE be used instead?
questions.reference_answer: The Forwarded-to number IE shall be present if at least one of the HLR and the gsmSCF does not support Long Forwarded-to Numbers (otherwise absent). The Long forwarded-to number IE shall be present if both the HLR and the gsmSCF support Long Forwarded-to Numbers (otherwise absent).

questions.question: Which parameters may a PCEF hand to the DRA on its first contact with the PCRF realm for unsolicited application reporting by a TDF, and which AVP carries the PDN information?
questions.reference_answer: The parameters from the TDF to the DRA may comprise the UE IP address, in either the Framed-IP-Address AVP or the Framed-Ipv6-Prefix AVP, and PDN information is carried in the Called-Station-ID AVP.

questions.question: For the CS-originating case, which procedure must the MGCF use to obtain a local IP address and UDP port from the IM-MGW before sending the INVITE, and where does it get the candidate local codecs from?
questions.reference_answer: The MGCF shall use the Reserve IMS Connection Point procedure to obtain the local IP address and UDP port from the IM-MGW. The candidate local codec(s) are derived by the MGCF from configuration data.

questions.question: For EPC-routed traffic in the roaming case, what creates the V-PCRF routing information in the V-DRA and what removes it again?
questions.reference_answer: The V-PCRF routing information (DRA binding) in the V-DRA is created when the S9 session establishment trigger is received, and it is removed when the S9 session termination notification is received.

questions.question: For distribution of ProSe group keys, what protection must the shared and session keys get, which UEs alone may receive them, and which party must a Public Safety ProSe-enabled UE be able to authenticate?
questions.reference_answer: The shared keys and session keys shall be protected in integrity and confidentiality during their distribution. Only authorized Public Safety ProSe-enabled UEs shall receive the shared keys. The Public Safety ProSe-enabled UE must be able to authenticate the network entity distributing the shared keys.

questions.question: Which three pieces of security information does the PDCP header of a user-plane packet carry for ProSe group communication, how many bits of each, and what must the transmitting UE set them to when confidentiality protection is not configured?
questions.reference_answer: The PDCP header carries the 5 least significant bits each of the PGK Identity, PTK Identity, and Counter. If confidentiality protection is not configured, the transmitting UE shall set the values of these security information fields (PGK Identity, PTK Identity, and Counter) to zero.

questions.question: What minimum key strength must the signing asymmetric keys for a ProSe proximity request meet, and what minimum key lengths apply if RSA, DSA or ECDSA is chosen?
questions.reference_answer: The signing asymmetric keys shall have at least a key strength equivalent to a 128-bit symmetric key. Minimum key lengths are 3072 bits for RSA, 256 bits for DSA, and 256 bits for ECDSA.

questions.question: For ProSe Direct One-to-one Communication, which protections are mandatory to support and use for direct link signalling, and what is explicitly stated about integrity protection of direct link user plane packets between UEs?
questions.reference_answer: Direct link signalling ciphering and direct link user plane ciphering shall be supported and may be used; direct link signalling integrity protection and replay protection shall be supported and used. Direct link user plane packets between UEs shall not be integrity protected.

questions.question: By when at the latest must a ProSe one-to-one connection be rekeyed, and which keys does a rekeying operation always refresh versus only optionally refresh?
questions.reference_answer: Rekeying must be done before the counter for a particular LCID repeats with the current keys. A rekeying operation shall always refresh KD-sess, PEK, and PIK, and may optionally also refresh KD.

questions.question: Which integrity algorithms must a ProSe enabled Public Safety UE implement for one-to-one direct link signalling, which key is used, and how is the Direction bit chosen relative to the Direct Security Mode Command?
questions.reference_answer: ProSe enabled Public Safety UEs shall implement 128-EIA1 and 128-EIA2 (and may implement 128-EIA3) for one-to-one direct link signalling integrity protection, using the key PIK. The Direction bit is set to 1 for direct link signalling transmitted by the UE that sent the Direct Security Mode Command for that security context, and 0 otherwise.

questions.question: For ciphering of ProSe one-to-one traffic, which algorithms are mandatory to implement, which key is used, and what are Bearer[0]-Bearer[4] and COUNT[0]-COUNT[15] set to?
questions.reference_answer: ProSe enabled Public Safety UEs shall implement EEA0, 128-EEA1, and 128-EEA2 (and may implement 128-EEA3) for ciphering of one-to-one traffic, using the key PEK. Bearer[0] to Bearer[4] are set to LCID, and COUNT[0] to COUNT[15] are set to KD-sess ID.

questions.question: When certificates authenticate a ProSe Proximity Request, which single key usage bit must be set as mandatory critical, and which TS 33.310 certificate profile clauses apply to ALUID-associated certificates and to the CA certificates in the validation chain?
questions.reference_answer: Only digitalSignature shall be set as the mandatory critical key usage. Clause 6.1.3 (SEG certificates) applies to ALUID-associated certificates, and clause 6.1.4 (SEG CA certificates) applies to any CA certificates used in a chain to validate the certificates.

questions.question: Service Dialling Numbers can be dialled by the user for outgoing calls, but who must control the ability to update them?
questions.reference_answer: The access for updating the Service Dialling Numbers shall be under the control of the operator.

questions.question: Which procedure does the MGCF use to have the IM-MGW prepare CS network side bearer establishment, what three things does it ask the IM-MGW for, and which message does the MGCF then send to the preceding node?
questions.reference_answer: The MGCF uses the Prepare Bearer procedure to have the IM-MGW prepare for CS network side bearer establishment. It requests the IM-MGW to provide a bearer address, a binding reference, and (optionally) notification when the bearer is established. The MGCF then sends the APM message to the preceding node.

questions.question: How must the ME present a Message Waiting Indication received by short message, where must the indication status be stored and why, and what memory condition must not stop the ME accepting these messages?
questions.reference_answer: The ME shall present the Message Waiting Indication as an icon on the screen or other MMI indication. The indication status is stored on the SIM/USIM to allow the status to be retained through power off/on and SIM/USIM movement between UEs. The ME shall be able to accept and acknowledge these message waiting status short messages irrespective of the memory available in the SIM/USIM.

questions.question: Within how many seconds of end-to-end connection with the PSAP should the eCall MSD typically be available, and where eCall indicators are unsupported by the serving network, what is the limit on the PSAP modem differentiating an eCall from another TS12 call?
questions.reference_answer: The MSD should typically be available to the PSAP within 4 seconds of end-to-end connection being established. Where eCall indicators are unsupported by the serving network, the PSAP modem's differentiation of an eCall from another TS12 call shall not exceed 2 seconds from when the IVS receives notification that the PSAP has answered the call.

questions.question: For UEs on an indirect network connection, which clock synchronization protocols must the 5G system support for the working clock domain, and how many simultaneous synchronization domains must be supported on such a UE?
questions.reference_answer: The 5G system shall support Precision Time Protocol-based (IEEE 802.1AS or another applicable IEEE Std 1588 profile) or 5G sync domain-based clock synchronization for UEs using indirect network connection. It shall support up to four simultaneous synchronization domains on such a UE.

questions.question: For cooperative carrying, up to what distance between UEs must the 5G system support direct device connection, and what must it support in addition for a group of UEs using such connections?
questions.reference_answer: The 5G system shall support direct device connection between UEs up to 50 m distance for cooperative carrying. In addition, it must support mobility of the group of UEs using such direct device connections.

questions.question: Why can a supplementary service never be sold to a user on its own, and what must it always be offered together with?
questions.reference_answer: A supplementary service modifies or supplements a basic telecommunication service, so it cannot be offered to a user as a stand-alone service. It shall be offered together or in association with a basic telecommunication service.

questions.question: How are user device IP addresses normally allocated in a PLMN, when must a static address be possible instead, who assigns it, and where must the details of an assigned static address be kept?
questions.reference_answer: User device IP addresses should normally be allocated dynamically by the network operator and managed without user intervention. For business critical applications and firewall configuration simplification, a static IP address must be possible; it shall be assigned by the network operator, and details of an assigned static IP address shall be maintained with the subscriber's records in the HLR/HSS.

questions.question: The S4-SGSN does not itself generate charging information. When an IP-CAN session is activated and Charging Characteristics came from the HLR/HSS, what must the S4-SGSN do with them, and which value takes precedence when the PDN connection has its own Charging Characteristics?
questions.reference_answer: If Charging Characteristics were received from the HLR/HSS, the S4-SGSN shall forward them to the S-GW as provided by the HLR/HSS, regardless of the home, visiting, or roaming case. When the PDN connection (e.g. APN) has its own Charging Characteristics present in the subscription information, that PDN-connection-specific value shall be forwarded (taking precedence); only if none is present for the PDN connection does the subscription-level Charging Characteristics get forwarded instead.

questions.question: Which Charging Characteristics does the MME apply for the generation of SMS CDRs, and what does it fall back to when the subscription supplies none?
questions.reference_answer: The MME applies the subscription specific Charging Characteristics for generation of SMS CDRs, and if none is supplied, it shall apply a pre-configured default behaviour instead.

questions.question: In which cases may an S-GW be configured to ignore the Charging Characteristics supplied by the S4-SGSN or MME for its IP-CAN bearers?
questions.reference_answer: The S-GW may be configured to ignore the Charging Characteristics supplied by the S4-SGSN/MME in any combination of: the visiting case (S-GW and P-GW belong to the same PLMN, subscriber belongs to a different PLMN); the roaming case (P-GW belongs to a different PLMN); the home case (subscriber belongs to the same PLMN as the S-GW and P-GW); or unconditionally, i.e. it always ignores the supplied parameters.

questions.question: Which node forwards the Charging Characteristics parameter to the TDF at IP-CAN session establishment, and in which cases may the TDF be configured to ignore them for its TDF session?
questions.reference_answer: The P-GW forwards the Charging Characteristics parameter to the TDF (via the PCRF) at IP-CAN session establishment. The TDF may be configured to ignore the supplied Charging Characteristics in any combination of: the visiting case (subscriber belongs to a different PLMN), the roaming case (home routed traffic), the home case (subscriber belongs to the same PLMN as the TDF), or unconditionally, i.e. it always ignores the supplied parameters.

questions.question: For Fixed Broadband Access interworking with EPC-routed traffic and PMIP-based S5/S8 (case 2b), from which node must the PCRF be able to receive the H(e)NB local IP address and UDP source port?
questions.reference_answer: The PCRF must be able to receive the H(e)NB Local IP address and, if available, UDP source port number from the BBERF (S-GW).

questions.question: For online charging of a TDF session, what must the quota handling be associated with, whose value space is that identifier drawn from, and what exactly is metered as the counted amount of data?
questions.reference_answer: The quota handling for the TDF session shall be based on associating a specific Rating Group/Service Identifier with the TDF session, and the value of this TDF session specific Rating Group/Service Identifier shall be vendor specific. The amount of data counted with this Rating Group/Service Identifier shall be the user plane payload.

questions.question: When an IP-CAN bearer is online charged by FBC with GTP based tunnelling to an external IP network, which packets are the data volumes counted on for the bearer-specific Rating Group/Service Identifier?
questions.reference_answer: In the case of GTP based tunnelling and interworking with external IP networks, the data volumes for the IP-CAN bearer specific Rating Group/Service Identifier shall be counted on the inner IP packets in the GTP-U packet (T-PDU).

questions.question: Which fields are mandatory in the SGSN MBMS bearer context record (S-MB-CDR), and what does the Charging ID field identify?
questions.reference_answer: The mandatory (M) fields in the SGSN MBMS bearer context record (S-MB-CDR) are: Record Type, SGSN Address used, Charging ID, Record Opening Time, Duration, and Cause for Record Closing. The Charging ID field is the bearer context identifier used to identify this MBMS bearer context in different records created by GSNs.

questions.question: Because the IP-Edge [PCEF] does not support individual bearers, to what do the high-level charging requirements 1 and 2 apply instead, and what must the IP-Edge be able to categorise data volumes, elapsed time and events by?
questions.reference_answer: Since the IP-Edge [PCEF] does not support individual bearers, high-level charging requirements 1 and 2 apply to the IP-CAN session instead of an IP-CAN bearer. The IP-Edge [PCEF] shall be capable of identifying (categorising) data volumes, elapsed time, or events by QoS (as defined in TS 23.203).

questions.question: Which chargeable events defined for TDF session and ABC functionality do NOT apply for fixed user traffic and 3GPP UE NSWO traffic when offline charging is activated?
questions.reference_answer: For fixed user traffic and 3GPP UE NSWO traffic, when offline charging is activated the following chargeable events defined for TDF session/ABC functionality do not apply: serving node (e.g. SGSN/S-GW/ePDG) change; change of charging condition (TDF session modification, e.g. SGSN change, S-GW change, user location change, user CSG information change); intersystem change (e.g. GSM to UMTS radio interface change, RAT change); PLMN change; and MS Timezone change.

questions.question: With the FailureHandling enumeration set to CONTINUE, what should an NF consumer do on a transport temporary failure, and what happens to the service and the Charging Information if the charging data request still cannot be delivered?
questions.reference_answer: With FailureHandling set to CONTINUE, the NF consumer should re-send and continue the request to an alternative server in case of transport temporary failures, provided a failover procedure is supported by both the CHF and the NF consumer and an alternative server is available. Otherwise, if the charging data request still cannot be delivered, the service SHOULD still be granted, and the Charging Information may be stored even though the charging data request can't be delivered.

questions.question: In the Nchf_ConvergedCharging API, what data structure must the CHF include with an application error and which attribute of it names the error, and which HTTP status code goes with CHARGING_FAILED?
questions.reference_answer: The CHF shall include in the HTTP status code a "ProblemDetails" data structure, with the "cause" attribute indicating the application error. CHARGING_FAILED is associated with HTTP status code 400 Bad Request.

questions.question: For the VariablePartType enumeration, how do INTEGER and NUMBER differ in the way digits are announced and in their digit limits, and what form must a CURRENCY value take?
questions.reference_answer: For INTEGER, the value's digits shall be announced as a single number, up to 10 digits. For NUMBER, the digits shall be announced as individual digits, up to 24 digits. A CURRENCY value must take the form AAAAAABB, where AAAAAA is the integer part and BB is the decimal part.

questions.question: EFPST tells the ME which ProSe services are available. What is the ME forbidden to do with a service that the ProSe Service Table does not mark as available, and which USIM service number gates the presence of that file?
questions.reference_answer: If a service is not indicated as available in the ProSe Service Table (EFPST), the ME shall not select that service. The presence of EFPST is gated by USIM service n°101: this file shall be present if service n°101 is "available" in the USIM Service Table.

questions.question: What controls whether the In Case of Emergency dialling number file EFICE_DN is available, and what are its READ and UPDATE access conditions?
questions.reference_answer: The availability of EFICE_DN is controlled by user/activation status: the file shall be deactivated if the user does not wish the ICE information in it to be available, and activated if the user wishes it to be available. Its access conditions are READ: ALWAYS and UPDATE: PIN.

questions.question: In the WLAN scenario over GTP-based S2b with Fixed Broadband Access interworking, which two addresses must the PCEF report over the Gx reference point in addition to the UDP source port?
questions.reference_answer: In addition to the UDP source port number (if available), the PCEF must report the UE local IP address and the P-GW IP address over the Gx reference point.

questions.question: Which two USIM services must both be available for EFPSISMSC to be present, what identity does it hold, and what does the ME use it for?
questions.reference_answer: EFPSISMSC shall be present if and only if USIM services n°12 and n°91 are both "available". It holds the Public Service Identity of the SM-SC (either a SIP URI or tel URI), which the ME shall use to submit SMS over IP as defined in TS 24.341.

questions.question: An ITT4RT-Tx client wants to advertise that it will react to PAUSE and RESUME requests for the RTP streams it sends but will never issue them itself. Which attribute and which optional parameter setting expresses that?
questions.reference_answer: The ITT4RT-Tx client uses the a=rtcp-fb ccm pause attribute, and the optional parameter setting a=rtcp-fb ccm pause config=3 can be used to indicate that it will only receive and react to PAUSE and RESUME requests but will not send them.

questions.question: When several 360-degree videos appear in an ITT4RT conference, what must the ITT4RT MRF negotiate with each remote participant, and which two media line attributes identify a 360-degree video in its SDP offer?
questions.reference_answer: When multiple 360-degree videos are present in an ITT4RT conference, the ITT4RT MRF shall negotiate an SDP session with every remote participant. A 360-degree video is identified in the SDP offer by either the a=3gpp_360video or a=3gpp_fisheye media line attributes.

questions.question: An ITT4RT-Tx client includes the "a=no_other_overlays" attribute with its 360-degree video stream. What is the MRF then forbidden to do, and how must it group that stream in the itt4rt_group attribute?
questions.reference_answer: When an ITT4RT-Tx client includes the "a=no_other_overlays" attribute, the MRF shall not group that client's 360-degree media stream with overlay media streams from other ITT4RT clients. Instead, the MRF shall group the 360-degree video media stream together with one or more overlays of that same ITT4RT-Tx client in a separate <rest-group> in the itt4rt_group attribute when describing them to any ITT4RT-Rx client.

questions.question: What must an ITT4RT MRF assume when it receives an offer with no data channel carrying the "mpeg-sd" sub-protocol, and what must it do right after a scene description data channel is successfully established?
questions.reference_answer: If the ITT4RT MRF receives an offer that does not contain a data channel with the "mpeg-sd" sub-protocol, it shall assume the offering ITT4RT client does not support scene description-based overlays. Right after a scene description data channel is successfully established (offer accepted), the ITT4RT MRF shall generate and send the scene description to the offerer.

questions.question: In which stream id range must the "mpeg-sd" data channel sit, how many such channels may appear in the offer/answer SDP, and which one is used if several are detected?
questions.reference_answer: The stream id of the "mpeg-sd" data channel shall be in the range allocated for bootstrap data channels, i.e. below 1000 (excluding values in Table 6.2.10.1-2). A single "mpeg-sd" data channel shall be present in the offer/answer SDP, and if multiple such channels are detected, the one with the lowest stream ID shall be used.

questions.question: A UE is receiving a PSS streaming session and issues a SIP Re-INVITE to move to MBMS reception. What role must the SCF take, and which two messages tear down the leg towards the PSS Server?
questions.reference_answer: The SCF shall act as a B2BUA. It sends a SIP BYE message to the PSS Adapter to terminate the SIP session between them, and the PSS Adapter shall send an RTSP TEARDOWN message to the PSS Server to release the RTSP session.

questions.question: For NG-RAN ANR management, what must the initial status of a newly created NCR be with respect to handover, X2 or Xn connection setup, and removal by the ANR function in the gNB?
questions.reference_answer: For NG-RAN ANR management, the initial status of a newly created NCR by the ANR function to a NG-RAN cell shall be such that HO is allowed, X2 or Xn connection setup is allowed, and the NCR is allowed to be removed by the ANR function in the gNB.

questions.question: In intent driven closed-loop management, which part of the MnS producer's behaviour is explicitly declared out of scope for standardisation?
questions.reference_answer: The mechanisms by which the MnS producer uses closed-loop automation to satisfy the intent are considered the implementation of the MnS producer and shall not be standardized.

questions.question: For WLAN cases 2a and 2b the Gxx reference point corresponds to Gxb*. Which two bearer-related functions are explicitly not supported there, and what must the BBERF(ePDG) still report to the PCRF?
questions.reference_answer: Bearer Binding and uplink bearer binding verification functions are not supported for WLAN cases 2a and 2b (where Gxx corresponds to Gxb*). The BBERF(ePDG) must still report the UE's Local IP address, the UDP source port number if NA(P)T is detected, and the ePDG IP address to the PCRF.

questions.question: In the UEGroup dataType, under which condition must the fiveQI attribute be supported and under which must sNSSAI be supported?
questions.reference_answer: In the UEGroup dataType, the fiveQI attribute shall be supported when the UE group is represented by 5QI, and the sNSSAI attribute shall be supported when the UE group is represented by S-NSSAI.

questions.question: An MS with PEO or EC operation enabled receives a cell re-selection command. What kind of cell reselection does it use instead, and what must any MS indicate if the command points at a GSM cell it is not synchronised to?
questions.reference_answer: An MS with PEO or EC operation enabled uses only autonomous cell reselection instead of following the network's cell re-selection command. If any MS receives a cell re-selection command towards a GSM cell to which it is not synchronised, it shall indicate a packet cell change failure.

questions.question: For a PDCH/H in Exclusive MAC mode while in DTM, to which channels must the MS apply the output power ordered on the SACCH, and what is the exception for bursts sent on the BCCH carrier?
questions.reference_answer: For a PDCH/H in Exclusive MAC mode while in DTM, the MS shall apply the output power ordered by the network on the SACCH to all channels, both the TCH/H and the PDCH/H. The exception is that bursts transmitted on the BCCH carrier shall be transmitted at the BCCH level (rather than the SACCH-ordered power).

questions.question: Where in the multiframe is the channel quality measured for the derivation of a Channel Quality Report, and on which carrier is measurement forbidden and why?
questions.reference_answer: Channel quality is measured as the interference signal level during idle frames of the multiframe, when the serving cell is not transmitting. No measurements shall be taken on the BCCH carrier of the serving cell, because the BTS transmits with constant output power on that carrier.

questions.question: In the GGSN/P-GW location IE, which bits of octet 3 are spare and who must ignore them, and how are the bit patterns 100 to 111 to be treated?
questions.reference_answer: In octet 3 of the GGSN/P-GW location IE, bits 8 to 4 are spare, set to zero by the SGSN and shall be ignored by the BSS. The bit patterns 100 to 111 (bits 3 to 1) are for future use and shall be treated as VPLMN.

questions.question: How is the Delay Value field of the BVC Measurement IE coded, and what special meaning does the hexadecimal value 0xFFFF carry?
questions.reference_answer: The Delay Value field is coded as a 16-bit integer value in units of centi-seconds (one hundredth of a second), giving a range of over 10 minutes in increments of 10 ms. The hexadecimal value 0xFFFF (decimal 65535) shall be interpreted as "infinite delay".

questions.question: What event makes the HNB GW open an S15 session with the PCRF, which CC-Request-Type value is used, and which two AVPs carry the HNB local IP address and the IPSec tunnel UDP source port?
questions.reference_answer: The HNB GW initiates an S15 Session Establishment with the PCRF if the HNB registers to the HNB GW. It sends a CC-Request with CC-Request-Type set to "INITIAL_REQUEST"; the HNB Local IP address is carried in the HeNB-Local-IP-Address AVP and the UDP source port number of the IPSec tunnel is carried in the UDP-Source-Port AVP, if available.

questions.question: When a RAB assignment message asks the HNB GW to allocate new resources, which AVP must carry the QoS derived from the RAB message and which AVP carries the QoS request identifier the HNB GW assigns?
questions.reference_answer: When the RAB assignment requests to allocate new resources, the HNB GW shall include the requested QoS information derived from the RAB message within the QoS-Information AVP, and the QoS request identifier it assigns within the CS-Service-QoS-Request-Identifier AVP.

questions.question: The PCRF gets a QoS rule failure report from the BPCF with PCC-Rule-Status set to "INACTIVE". Which AVP must it place in the RAR command, with which value of CS-Service-Resource-Result-Operation, and what must the HNB GW then initiate?
questions.reference_answer: The PCRF shall include the CS-Service-Resource-Report AVP in the RAR command with the CS-Service-Resource-Result-Operation AVP set to "DELETION" (along with the CS-Service-QoS-Request-Identifier AVP for the corresponding QoS request identifier and the CS-Service-Resource-Failure-Cause AVP). The HNB GW shall then initiate a RAB modification or RAB release procedure to release the corresponding resource allocated in the 3GPP network.

questions.question: An HNB GW must terminate an S15 session towards a PCRF that is known to have restarted since the session was established. What should it refrain from doing?
questions.reference_answer: If the HNB GW needs to send an S15 Session termination request towards a PCRF known to have restarted since the S15 Session establishment, the HNB GW should not send a CC-Request to inform the PCRF.

questions.question: When the BBERF(ePDG) opens a Gateway Control Session for a 3GPP UE attached via BBF access, which value must the IP-CAN-Type AVP carry and which AVP conveys the ePDG address used as the IPSec tunnel endpoint?
questions.reference_answer: The IP-CAN-Type AVP must be set to "Non-3GPP-EPS", and the ePDG IP address used as the IPSec tunnel endpoint is conveyed in the AN-GW-Address AVP.

questions.question: When the PCRF links an incoming TDF session to an S9a* session, which address must match, which AVP may supply the PDN information as a secondary criterion, and which annex governs the APN matching?
questions.reference_answer: The PCRF links a TDF session to an S9a* session if the IPv4 address or IPv6 address of the TDF session matches the UE local IP address of the S9a* session. The PDN information (i.e. NSWO-APN), if available in the Called-Station-Id AVP, may also be used as a secondary criterion, and when the PCRF checks whether APNs within Called-Station-Id AVPs match, it shall apply the APN matching procedures in Annex H of 3GPP TS 29.213.

questions.question: How do the PCRF and the HNB GW advertise support for the S15 application after the transport connection comes up, and which two AVP values go inside the Vendor-Specific-Application-Id AVP?
questions.reference_answer: After establishing the transport connection, the PCRF and the HNB GW shall advertise support for the S15 Application by including the application identifier in the Auth-Application-Id AVP and the value 3GPP (10415) in the Vendor-Id AVP, both contained within the Vendor-Specific-Application-Id AVP of the Capabilities-Exchange-Request and Capabilities-Exchange-Answer commands.

questions.question: For a routed mode RG with NAT in Fixed Broadband Access, how many IP-CAN sessions must be established relative to Subscriber IP sessions on the IP Edge, and what changes when the PPP pass-through feature is enabled?
questions.reference_answer: For a routed mode RG with NAT, one IP-CAN session shall be established for each corresponding Subscriber IP session on the IP Edge (for the IPv4 address and/or IPv6 address or IPv6 prefix assigned to the RG) — i.e. a 1:1 relationship. When the PPP pass-through feature is enabled, an IP-CAN session shall instead be established for each single fixed device starting the PPP session, and in this case the 3GPP UE does not have a Subscriber IP session in the IP Edge.

questions.question: Which node enforces the default QoS provisioned over Gx for a Fixed Broadband Access IP-CAN session, in which AVP is that default QoS carried, and what does the IP Edge/PCEF not enforce when a PCRF is deployed?
questions.reference_answer: The IP Edge/PCEF enforces the default QoS provisioned over Gx, which is carried in the Default-QoS-Information AVP. When a PCRF is deployed, the IP Edge/PCEF does not enforce the default Access Profile QoS provided by the Broadband Fixed Access Network.

questions.question: When the Extended-Max-Requested-BW-NR feature is supported, which AVPs replace the Max-Requested-Bandwidth-DL/UL AVPs and in what unit do the replacements express the bitrate?
questions.reference_answer: For the Extended-Max-Requested-BW-NR feature, Extended-Max-Requested-BW-DL/UL AVPs shall be used instead of Max-Requested-Bandwidth-DL/UL AVPs, expressing the bitrate in kbps (instead of bps).

questions.question: Which two exceptions to the normal PCRF functionality apply for Fixed Broadband Access, regarding IP-CAN bearer control mode negotiation and subscriptions to IP-CAN type / RAT type changes?
questions.reference_answer: For Fixed Broadband Access, no negotiation of IP-CAN bearer control mode applies, and subscriptions to changes of IP-CAN type, RAT type, or Access Network Information do not apply.

questions.question: In a Multipath Applicable Indication IE, what do the MTAI and MQAI flags in octet 5 indicate about the PDR, and how are bits 3 to 8 defined?
questions.reference_answer: Bit 1 (MTAI) set to "1" indicates the PDR is used to detect user plane traffic for which MPTCP is applicable; bit 2 (MQAI) set to "1" indicates the PDR is used to detect user plane traffic for which MPQUIC is applicable. Bits 3 to 8 are spare and reserved for future use.

questions.question: In the L2TP Session Indications IE, what do the REUIA, REDSA and RENSA bits tell the UP function to request from the LNS?
questions.reference_answer: REUIA (bit 1), if set to "1", indicates to the UP function that it shall request the UE IP address from the LNS. REDSA (bit 2), if set to "1", indicates that the UP function shall request the DNS Server Address from the LNS. RENSA (bit 3), if set to "1", indicates that the UP function shall request the NBNS Server Address from the LNS.

questions.question: In the Thresholds IE, which flags in octet 5 control the presence of the RTT value and the Packet Loss Rate value, and how many of those bits must be set to "1"?
questions.reference_answer: Bit 1 (RTT), if set to "1", means the RTT value field shall be present; bit 2 (PLR), if set to "1", means the Packet Loss Rate value field shall be present. At least one of these bits shall be set to "1" (several may be).

questions.question: In the Number of UE IP Addresses IE, which two flags in octet 5 decide whether the IPv4 and IPv6 count fields are present, and how is each count field encoded?
questions.reference_answer: Bit 1 (IPv4) in octet 5, if set to "1", means the Number of UE IPv4 Addresses field shall be present; bit 2 (IPv6), if set to "1", means the Number of UE IPv6 Addresses field shall be present. Each present count field is encoded as an Unsigned32 binary integer value.

questions.question: The UE local IP address behind the ePDG changes mid-session. Which CC-Request-Type value must the BBERF put in the CCR, and which event trigger must accompany it?
questions.reference_answer: The BBERF shall send a CCR command with the CC-Request-Type AVP set to "UPDATE_REQUEST", accompanied by the event trigger set to the value UE_LOCAL_IP_ADDRESS_CHANGE.

questions.question: Which SRVCC message travels over Sv from the target MME/SGSN to the source MSC Server to say the handover with the PS domain has finished, and under what condition must the SRVCC failure Cause IE be included in it?
questions.reference_answer: The SRVCC CS to PS Complete Notification message is sent across Sv from the target MME/SGSN to the source MSC Server. The SRVCC failure Cause IE shall be included if there is a failure detected by the target MME/SGSN during the UTRAN/GERAN to E-UTRAN/UTRAN (HSPA) SRVCC procedure.

questions.question: For an EPS Bearer ID assignment over N16, what value must requestIndication carry, and what must the V-SMF or I-SMF do with the EBIs listed in revokeEbiList including their QFI associations?
questions.reference_answer: The requestIndication shall be set to EBI_ASSIGNMENT_REQ. For the EBIs listed in revokeEbiList, the V-SMF or I-SMF shall release the requested EBI(s), delete the corresponding EPS bearer context stored in the V-SMF or I-SMF, and disassociate those EBI(s) from the QFI(s) with which they were associated.

questions.question: When an I-SMF adds a PSA together with a BP or UL CL, which requestIndication value is used and which pieces of N4 and DNAI information must the POST request carry?
questions.reference_answer: The requestIndication shall be set to NW_REQ_PDU_SES_MOD. The POST request must carry: N4 information for handling local traffic offloaded at the PSA; N4 information for the local offload rules at the UL CL/BP; and the DNAI related to N4 information targeting the local PSA (plus, if applicable, indications that the DNAI and/or local PSA shall not change).

questions.question: Which N1 SM information must a V-SMF place in n1SmInfoFromUe as opposed to unknownN1SmInfo, and what encoding fields must accompany each IE?
questions.reference_answer: The V-SMF shall place NAS SM information it only needs to transfer to the H-SMF — known IEs, and IEs with an unknown value not set to "reserved" that only need forwarding — in n1SmInfoFromUe; it shall place NAS SM information it does not comprehend (unknown IEs, or known IEs with an unknown value not set to "reserved" that the V-SMF is supposed to interpret) in unknownN1SmInfo. Each IE in both cases must be encoded per 3GPP TS 24.501 including the Type field and, for TLV or TLV-E IEs, the Length field.

questions.question: When the H-SMF receives unknownN1SmInfo binary data from the V-SMF, which N1 SM IEs must it process and which must it drop?
questions.reference_answer: When receiving unknownN1SmInfo from the V-SMF, the H-SMF shall process any N1 SM IE in it that does not require interpretation by the V-SMF; other N1 SM IEs — e.g. those the H-SMF comprehends but which require interpretation by the V-SMF — shall be dropped.

questions.question: A Create SM Context request collides with an existing PDU session context at the SMF. Which header decides the outcome, and under what condition alone may the SMF accept the new establishment request?
questions.reference_answer: The Origination Time Stamp header decides the outcome. The SMF shall accept the new PDU session establishment request only if it contains a more recent time stamp than the one stored for the existing PDU session (an incoming request is also considered more recent and accepted if no Origination Time Stamp was provided for at least one of the two sessions); otherwise it is rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden and application error LATE_OVERLAPPING_REQUEST.

questions.question: When UE location is reported to the SMF with the UserLocation data type, which identifiers must be present for NR user location, for E-UTRA, and for untrusted non-3GPP access?
questions.reference_answer: For NR user location, the TAI and NCGI must be present. For E-UTRA user location, the TAI and ECGI must be present. For untrusted non-3GPP access, the TAI, UE local IP address, Port (if NAT is detected), and optionally n3Iwid (if available) must be present.

questions.question: How is the 3gpp-Sbi-Origination-Timestamp header encoded, at what granularity is the time given, and how does its format differ from the ordinary HTTP Date header?
questions.reference_answer: The 3gpp-Sbi-Origination-Timestamp header is encoded per the ABNF in IETF RFC 9110, giving the date and time with millisecond granularity. It uses the same format as the ordinary HTTP Date header but adds milliseconds to the time-of-day (e.g. "Sun, 04 Aug 2019 08:49:37.845 GMT"), whereas the Date header does not include milliseconds.

questions.question: Which content type signals a Problem Details JSON object in an Nsmf_PDUSession HTTP response body, and which content type is used for multipart messages?
questions.reference_answer: The content type "application/problem+json" signals a Problem Details JSON object in the HTTP response body. Multipart messages use the content type "multipart/related".

questions.question: An HTTP multipart message on the Nsmf_PDUSession API must include how many JSON body parts and how many binary body parts, and in which service operations is multipart support mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: An HTTP multipart message on the Nsmf_PDUSession API shall include one JSON body part and one or two binary body parts. Multipart support is mandatory for: Create SM Context Request and Response, Update SM Context Request and Response, Release SM Context Request, Create Request and Response, and Update Request and Response.

questions.question: An SMC-CS entity receives a CP-ERROR message while in an arbitrary state. Which two indications must it pass upwards and downwards, and which state must it then enter? How does this differ for an SMC-GP entity?
questions.reference_answer: On receiving a CP-ERROR message, an SMC-CS entity shall pass an error indication to SM-RL and an MM-connection release request to the MM-sublayer, then enter the Idle State. An SMC-GP entity, in contrast, shall only pass an error indication to SM-RL (no MM-connection release request) before entering the Idle State.

questions.question: What must the <apiName> and <apiVersion> components of the Nsmf_PDUSession API URI be set to?
questions.reference_answer: The <apiName> shall be "nsmf-pdusession" and the <apiVersion> shall be "v1".

questions.question: An I-SMF is removing a PSA together with its BP or UL CL. What must the POST request carry, and what must come back in the POST response regarding the DNAI?
questions.reference_answer: The POST request must carry N4 information for the removal of the local offload rules at the UL CL/BP and PSA, and the DNAI related to N4 information targeting the local PSA. The POST response must return N4 response information and the DNAI related to the N4 information if it relates to a local PSA.

questions.question: For a PSA change for IPv6 multi-homing controlled by an I-SMF, which three kinds of N4 information must be present in the POST request, covering the removed PSA, the inserted PSA and the UL CL/BP?
questions.reference_answer: The POST request must contain: N4 information for the removal of the local offload rules at the removed PSA; N4 information for the handling of local traffic offloaded at the inserted PSA; and N4 information for updating the local offload rules at the UL CL/BP (plus the DNAIs related to N4 information targeting the removed or inserted PSA).

questions.question: An I-MGCF has to decide whether to send a SIP 183 Session Progress carrying an ISUP Cause. Which received messages can trigger it, which header field carries the received Cause Value, and is the behaviour mandatory or a network option?
questions.reference_answer: Receipt of an ACM or CPG message containing an ISUP Cause can trigger it (provided the I-MGCF did not already send a SIP provisional response due to interworking procedures). The received Cause Value is carried in the Reason header field of the SIP 183 Session Progress. This behaviour is a network option, not mandatory (the I-MGCF "may" send it).

questions.question: An O-MGCF selecting to route an incoming call to the IMS domain must first determine the end of address signalling. Which four criteria decide that, and which one involves a timer?
questions.reference_answer: The end of address signalling is determined by whichever of the following occurs earlier: (a) receipt of an end-of-pulsing (ST) signal; (b) receipt of the maximum number of digits used in the national numbering plan; (c) analysis of the called party number showing sufficient digits have been received to route the call; or (d) observing that timer Ti/w1 has expired after receipt of the latest address message, with the minimum number of digits required for routing already received. Criterion (d) involves a timer.

questions.question: For an SDP answer whose media line has an unspecified connection address and a visited-realm instance, which clause governs the IMS-ALG's handling, and which one applies when a secondary-realm instance is present instead?
questions.reference_answer: Clause 6.2.5 governs the IMS-ALG's handling when the SDP answer's media line has an unspecified connection address together with a visited-realm instance. Clause 6.2.6 applies when a secondary-realm instance is present instead.

questions.question: An AS gets a SUBSCRIBE for the load-control event package from a source it does not recognise as authorised. Which SIP response must it generate, and for an authorised source, what constraint applies to the Expires header field in the 200 OK?
questions.reference_answer: The AS shall generate a "403 Forbidden" response to the SUBSCRIBE request when the source is unauthorised or unexpected. For an authorised source, the Expires header field in the 200 OK response must be set to either the same value or a decreased value compared to the Expires header field in the SUBSCRIBE request.

questions.question: On receiving an initial request for a dialog, which header field parameters of the P-Charging-Vector must an AS store, and what must it do with that header field and the P-Charging-Function-Addresses header field in the forwarded message?
questions.reference_answer: On receiving an initial request for a dialog, the AS shall store the values received in the P-Charging-Vector header field parameters (e.g. "orig-ioi" if present, and "icid-value"). It must retain the P-Charging-Vector header field in the message, and likewise store the values received in the P-Charging-Function-Addresses header field and retain that header field in the forwarded message.

questions.question: An AS supporting resource sharing sees a Resource-Share header field in a response destined to its served user. What must it do with that header field before the response leaves the AS?
questions.reference_answer: The AS shall remove the Resource-Share header field from the outgoing response or request before it leaves the AS.

questions.question: An AS receives from a served user an SDP offer that conflicts with an earlier decision to share resources. Which Resource-Share value must go into the response carrying the SDP answer, which header field parameter accompanies it, and what must the AS stop doing?
questions.reference_answer: The response carrying the SDP answer must include a Resource-Share header field set to the value "no-media-sharing", along with the "origin" header field parameter set to "session-initiator" or "session-receiver" as appropriate. The AS must stop applying resource sharing with sessions involving the UE that sent the conflicting request or response.

questions.question: A mobile station receives a short-message control message whose type is not defined for the protocol discriminator. Which CP-ERROR cause value must it return, and which different cause applies when the message type is defined but inconsistent with the protocol state?
questions.reference_answer: The mobile station returns a CP-ERROR message with cause #97 "message type non-existent or not implemented" when the message type is not defined for the protocol discriminator. It returns cause #98 "message type not compatible with the short message protocol state" when the message type is defined but inconsistent with the protocol state.

questions.question: If the resource sharing options must change mid-call, for example because the UE adds media streams, where must the AS put the updated options?
questions.reference_answer: The AS shall include a Resource-Share header field with the updated resource sharing options (as specified in subclause 7.2.13) in the outgoing request or response that causes the reason for the change.

questions.question: When an AS translates a service access number into a routeable number, which value must the "cause" SIP URI parameter carry in the outgoing Request-URI, and what must the hi-targeted-to-uri of the last hi-entry in the History-Info header field be set to?
questions.reference_answer: The outgoing Request-URI's "cause" SIP URI parameter must be set to the value "380". The hi-targeted-to-uri of the last hi-entry in the History-Info header field must be set to the new Request-URI, also with the "cause" SIP URI parameter set to "380".

questions.question: An AS gets a SIP 491 Request Pending to a re-INVITE it sent. What random back-off interval should it choose when it serves the originating side of the call, and what interval when it serves the terminating side?
questions.reference_answer: If the AS is serving the originating side of the call, it acts as the owner of the Call-ID of the dialog ID and should choose a random back-off time between 2.1 and 4 seconds (in units of 10 ms). If the AS is serving the terminating side of the call, it acts as not being the owner of the Call-ID and should choose a random time between 0 and 2 seconds (in units of 10 ms).

questions.question: In what order of preference must an AS acting for an originating user determine the served user from the header fields it supports, and what is the final fallback?
questions.reference_answer: The AS first determines the served user from the P-Served-User header field, if it supports that header and the field is available; otherwise, if it supports the History-Info header field, it determines the served user from that field's content if available; otherwise, as the final fallback, the AS determines the served user by taking the identity contained in the P-Asserted-Identity header field.

questions.question: For an AS acting on behalf of a terminating user, what is the last resort for determining the served user when neither the P-Served-User nor the History-Info header field is available?
questions.reference_answer: The last resort for an AS serving a terminating user, when neither the P-Served-User nor the History-Info header field is available, is to determine the served user from the content of the Request-URI.

questions.question: An AS ends up treating a user as anonymous after trying to verify their identity. What must it check before going ahead, and what must it do if that check fails?
questions.reference_answer: Before proceeding, the AS must check whether the authorization policy defined for the request allows anonymous requests. If anonymous requests are allowed, the AS can proceed with the requested functionality; if that check fails (anonymous requests are not allowed), the AS shall not proceed with the requested functionality.

questions.question: How must an AS interpret a non-international phone number in the Request-URI whose "phone-context" tel URI parameter carries the home network domain name prefixed by the "geo-local." string?
questions.reference_answer: If the "phone-context" tel URI parameter contains access technology information, or the home network domain name prefixed by the "geo-local." string, the AS shall interpret the non-international phone number as a geo-local number.
