questions.question: Which bit in the 5GMM capability IE and which bit in the 5GS network feature support IE let the UE and the network respectively declare support for user plane location solutions, and in which registration procedures is that done?
questions.reference_answer: UEs indicate support for user plane location solution(s) using the LCS-UPP bit, the SUPL bit, or both in the 5GMM capability IE. The network indicates its support using the LCS-UPP bit, the SUPL bit, or both in the 5GS network feature support IE. Both indications are done during the initial registration procedure and the mobility registration update procedure.

questions.question: Which identifier must the LMF allocate to tie a UE to an LCS secured user plane connection, what else does the user plane connection information carry, and which message can the UE send to obtain it?
questions.reference_answer: The LMF shall allocate the LCS-UP binding ID to associate the UE with the LCS secured user plane connection. The user plane connection information also carries an address of the LMF. The UE can send the USER PLANE CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message to the LMF to obtain the user plane connection information.

questions.question: On the fifth expiry of timer T5010, what must the LMF do with the ongoing LCS-UPP procedures and with the LCS secured user plane connection itself?
questions.reference_answer: On the fifth expiry of timer T5010, the LMF shall abort ongoing LCS-UPP procedures on this LCS secured user plane connection and locally release the LCS secured user plane connection between the UE and the LMF.

questions.question: A message with semantically incorrect contents arrives and no procedural reaction is specified. What must the mobile station do when the corresponding SM transfer is NOT yet seen as successfully transferred, and what must it do instead when the offending message is itself a CP-ERROR?
questions.reference_answer: When the corresponding SM transfer is not yet seen as successfully transferred, the mobile station shall ignore the message and return a CP-ERROR message with cause value #95 "semantically incorrect message", if an appropriate connection exists. When the offending message is itself a CP-ERROR message, the mobile station shall ignore the message and enter the Idle State.

questions.question: A UE gets a DL LCS-UP TRANSPORT message whose LCS-UP payload type IE says "LTE Positioning Protocol (LPP) message". Which two items must the LCS-UP entity forward, and to which upper layer application?
questions.reference_answer: The LCS-UP entity of the UE shall forward the contents of the LCS-UP payload IE and the value of the LCS session identity IE to the upper layer location services application for LPP.

questions.question: When a POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION CONTROL message carries the Positioning Assistance Information IE, what must the gNB-DU do with any assistance information it already holds, and what does a Broadcast IE set to "start" permit?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB-DU shall replace any previously received positioning assistance information with the newly received information (and use it to configure positioning assistance information broadcasting). A Broadcast IE set to "start" permits the gNB-DU to start broadcasting the positioning assistance information.

questions.question: With the E-CID Report Characteristics IE set to "OnDemand", in which message must the gNB-DU return the measurement result, which IEs should it carry if available, and what must the gNB-CU then conclude about the measurements?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB-DU shall return the measurement result in the E-CID MEASUREMENT INITIATION RESPONSE message, including, if available, the Geographical Coordinates IE (within the E-CID Measurement Result IE) and the Cell Portion ID IE. The gNB-CU shall then consider that the E-CID measurements for the UE have been terminated by the gNB-DU.

questions.question: Under what condition must the Measured Results List IE appear inside the E-CID Measurement Result IE of an E-CID MEASUREMENT REPORT?
questions.reference_answer: The Measured Results List IE shall be included in the E-CID Measurement Result IE of the E-CID MEASUREMENT REPORT message when measurement quantities other than "Default" have been requested.

questions.question: A POSITIONING INFORMATION UPDATE arrives at the gNB-CU carrying both the SRS Configuration IE and the SFN Initialisation Time IE. How must the gNB-CU treat each of them?
questions.reference_answer: If the SRS Configuration IE is included, the gNB-CU shall consider this information as the updated SRS Configuration for the UE. If the SFN Initialisation Time IE is included, the gNB-CU shall consider this information as the SFN Initialisation Time associated to the SRS Configuration.

questions.question: What must the gNB-CU conclude when a POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION FEEDBACK message includes the Positioning Assistance Information Failure List IE, and what does the Positioning Broadcast Cells IE tell it?
questions.reference_answer: If the Positioning Assistance Information Failure List IE is included, the gNB-CU shall consider that positioning assistance information broadcasting could not be configured for the relevant information. The Positioning Broadcast Cells IE tells the gNB-CU that the feedback provided is applicable to the cells indicated in that IE.

questions.question: On receiving a POSITIONING SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND, which IE tells the gNB-DU which Positioning SI messages to broadcast, and what must it delete when the UE named by the Confirmed UE ID IE is not in RRC connected state?
questions.reference_answer: The PosSITypeList IE tells the gNB-DU which Positioning SI messages to broadcast. If the UE corresponding to the Confirmed UE ID IE is not in the RRC connected state, the gNB-DU shall delete the UE context, if any.

questions.question: In a SRS INFORMATION RESERVATION NOTIFICATION, what must the gNB-DU do when the SRS Reservation Type IE is set to "reserve" versus "release", and which IE names the cells affected?
questions.reference_answer: If the SRS Reservation Type IE is set to "reserve", the gNB-DU shall reserve the indicated (preconfigured) SRS information; if set to "release", it shall release that SRS information. In both cases, the cells affected are named by the Positioning Validity Area Cell List IE.

questions.question: When a POSITIONING MEASUREMENT UPDATE arrives, what must the gNB-DU do with the measurement configuration it already has, and what must it do with previously stored information if the Number of TRP Rx TEGs IE is included?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB-DU shall overwrite the previously received measurement configuration for the corresponding measurements. If the Number of TRP Rx TEGs IE is included, the gNB-DU shall clear any previously stored information and store the newly received information.

questions.question: A POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST includes the Requested SRS Transmission Characteristics IE but the gNB-DU cannot configure any SRS transmission for that UE. Which message must it send back?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB-DU shall respond with a POSITIONING INFORMATION FAILURE message with an appropriate cause value.

questions.question: Which two roles must an Application Server implementing the PNM application implement, and which media feature tag carrying an IMEI must it strip from Contact header fields of non-REGISTER requests before forwarding?
questions.reference_answer: The AS implementing the PNM application shall implement the role of a XCAP server and shall implement the Network Application Function (NAF) as described in 3GPP TS 33.220. It shall remove the g.3gpp.pne-id media feature tag containing IMEI from the Contact header field of requests and responses of SIP methods other than SIP REGISTER prior to forwarding.

questions.question: On F1, if a MULTICAST GROUP PAGING message arrives without the UE Identity List for Paging IE, in which paging occasions must the gNB-DU page the MBS session?
questions.reference_answer: If the UE Identity List for Paging IE is absent, the gNB-DU shall perform multicast group paging of the MBS session in all paging occasions within at least one default paging cycle, as specified in TS 38.304.

questions.question: A PN UE registers several PNEs on behalf of a personal area network. Which feature tag must it include when it acts as PN controller, and what must differ per PNE when the multiple registrations mechanism is used?
questions.reference_answer: As PN controller, the PN UE shall include a g.3gpp.iari_ref feature tag containing the IARI value defined in subclause 10.4 in the Contact header of the REGISTER request. When using the multiple registrations mechanism, the PN UE shall use a different "reg-id" value when registering each PNE.

questions.question: When the PNM application receives an HTTP PUT for PN configuration, which two pieces of GBA material must it use to verify the Authorization header, and against what does it compare the received public user identity to authorise the PN UE?
questions.reference_answer: The PNM application verifies the Authorization header using the bootstrapping transaction identifier B-TID and the key material Ks_NAF obtained from the BSF. It authorises the PN UE by comparing the received public user identity with the preconfigured one identified by the private user identity obtained after verification.

questions.question: An MCPTT server must copy XML elements from an incoming SIP request into an outgoing one without modification. Which clause's procedures does it follow instead of the normal server encryption procedures?
questions.reference_answer: The MCPTT server shall perform the procedures specified in clause 6.6.2.5.

questions.question: At what point relative to sending a SIP request or response must a functional entity perform integrity protection of XML MIME bodies, and does one signature cover all bodies or one per body?
questions.reference_answer: The functional entity shall perform integrity protection just prior to sending the SIP request or SIP response. Each XML MIME body has its own signature (one signature per body, not one covering all bodies).

questions.question: For MCPTT attribute URI encryption, which encryption algorithm and key must be used, how long must the randomly selected IV be, and what URI scheme must the replacement URI use?
questions.reference_answer: Encryption is performed using the AES-128-GCM algorithm HMAC as the encryption algorithm and the XPK as the key, with a randomly selected IV of 96 bits. The replacement URI must use the "sip:" URI scheme.

questions.question: An MCVideo transmission participant receives a Transmission Revoked message whose reason is to queue the transmission. Which message must it send, which timer must it start, and which state must it enter?
questions.reference_answer: It shall send a Queue Position Request message towards the transmission control server, start timer T102 (Transmission Queue Position Request), and enter the 'U: queued transmission' state.

questions.question: Handover with PSCell is commanded from NR SA to EN-DC and the target PSCell is unknown with SMTC configuration present in RRCConnectionReconfiguration. What value does Tprocessing take for a target PSCell in FR2, and what value applies if the target PSCell were known?
questions.reference_answer: When the target PSCell is unknown and SMTC configuration of the target unknown PSCell is present in RRCConnectionReconfiguration, Tprocessing = 50 ms for a target PSCell in FR2. If the target PSCell were known instead, Tprocessing = 45 ms for FR2.

questions.question: For handover with PSCell, up to what value may Tprocessing reach for the PCell handover, and what does TIU_PCell amount to when PCell and PSCell RACH occasions do not collide?
questions.reference_answer: Tprocessing for the PCell handover can be up to 25 ms. When PCell RACH and PSCell RACH occasions do not collide (or the UE can perform them simultaneously), TIU_PCell can be up to the summation of the SSB to PRACH occasion association period and 10 ms.

questions.question: A UE is configured in SA NR operation mode. Beyond the per-RAT carrier counts, what total number of effective carrier frequency layers must it be capable of monitoring, and when are several measurement objects counted as only one SSB frequency layer?
questions.reference_answer: In SA NR operation mode, beyond the per-RAT carrier counts (6 NR SSB inter-frequency carriers, 6 E-UTRA TDD, and 6 E-UTRA FDD inter-RAT carriers), the UE shall be capable of monitoring a total of at least [10] effective carrier frequency layers comprising any combination of NR, E-UTRA FDD, and E-UTRA TDD layers. Multiple measurement objects (MOs) are counted as one SSB frequency layer when ssbfrequency, smtc1, smtc2 and ssbSubcarrierSpacing are the same across those MOs.

questions.question: A PDCP entity configured for unrecoverable error detection receives three consecutive PDCP PDUs with an invalid PDU Type. Is the UE required or merely permitted to report the error, and at how many consecutive invalid PDUs does the obligation become mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: If the PDCP entity receives 2 or 3 consecutive PDCP PDUs with an unexpected or invalid PDU Type or PID value, the UE PDCP entity may (is only permitted to) indicate PDCP Unrecoverable Error to upper layer. The obligation becomes mandatory (shall) at 4 consecutive invalid PDUs.

questions.question: For the IP transport option on Iub and Iur, which IP version must an IP UTRAN Node support and which is optional, and which four parameters identify the transport bearer?
questions.reference_answer: An IP UTRAN Node shall support IPv6; support of IPv4 is optional. The transport bearer is identified by the source UDP port number, destination UDP port number, source IP address, and destination IP address.

questions.question: In the Dialled Services IP Multimedia CAMEL Subscription Information, how many DP Criteria entries may the list hold, and which item decides whether an IP Multimedia session is released or continued when the IM-SSF to gsmSCF dialogue fails?
questions.reference_answer: The DP Criteria list of the D-IM-CSI may hold 1 to 10 entries. The default Call Handling item decides whether the IP Multimedia session is released or continued in case of error in the IM-SSF to gsmSCF dialogue.

questions.question: Both 3G_MSC-A and 3G_MSC-B support the Multicall supplementary service. After an inter-3G_MSC relocation that already carries one or more circuit connections, are they required to allow a further circuit connection to be set up, and do the establishment procedures differ from the basic case?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, if 3G_MSC-A and 3G_MSC-B support the Multicall supplementary service, a new circuit connection shall be able to be set up after an Inter-3G_MSC relocation that already carries one or more circuit connections. The establishment procedures for the additional circuit connection are the same as those described in clause 13.4.1 (the basic case), so they do not differ.

questions.question: For Fixed Access interworking in the home routed scenario, at which point must the H-PCRF establish a Gateway Control Session to the V-PCRF over S9, and at which point must it terminate it?
questions.reference_answer: For case 1, if an IP-CAN Session Establishment indication is received over Gx and it is the first IP-CAN session for this UE, the H-PCRF shall establish a Gateway Control Session to the V-PCRF over S9. It shall terminate that Gateway Control Session over S9 when an IP-CAN Session Termination indication is received over Gx and it is the last IP-CAN session for this UE.

questions.question: For Fixed Broadband Access, what mapping must the PCEF in the IP-Edge be able to perform on the QoS parameters it receives from the PCRF, and which clause's IP-CAN bearer level QoS control requirements stop applying?
questions.reference_answer: The PCEF in the IP-Edge shall be able to perform the appropriate mapping from the QoS parameters it receives from the PCRF to Broadband Forum specific parameters. The requirements for QoS control at IP-CAN bearer level defined in clause 4.3.3.2 no longer apply for Fixed Broadband Access.

questions.question: An audio recording on the MRFP finishes unsuccessfully. What must the MRFP do with the record file, and what must it do instead when the recording succeeded and the MRFC had asked to be notified?
questions.reference_answer: If the audio recording is not successful, the MRFP shall delete the record file. If the recording succeeded and the MRFC had requested notification, the MRFP shall instead save the record file to the specified URI and notify the audio recording completion event and cause to the MRFC.

questions.question: In which format must the MRFP generate an ASR result, and what must it return to the MRFC when that script exceeds the transport capability of the Mp interface?
questions.reference_answer: The MRFP shall generate the ASR result in the EMMA format. If the size of the EMMA script is larger than the transport capability of the Mp interface, the MRFP shall return to the MRFC that the ASR is not successful.

questions.question: For separate delivery of SMS in conjunction with GPRS or UMTS access, which four HLR related REPORT Records must DF2 send to the LEMF, and does their delivery depend on whether other services are being intercepted?
questions.reference_answer: DF2 must send to the LEMF the following HLR Related REPORT Records: Serving System REPORT Record, Cancel location REPORT Record, Register location REPORT Record, and Location information request REPORT Record. These REPORT Records shall be reported independent of any other services that may or may not be intercepted.

questions.question: The MF retrieves Cell Site Supplemental Information over LI_CELL_INFO but the corresponding IRI event is not available in the MF. Into which parameter would the information normally be placed, and what must the MF be able to do instead?
questions.reference_answer: The information would normally be placed into the Location parameter of the IRI event. If that IRI event is not available in the MF, the MF shall instead have the ability to create a CSR to be delivered to the LEMF.

questions.question: For GTP-C messages crossing inter-security-domain boundaries, must IPsec ESP provide encryption, integrity protection, or both? And when SEG functionality sits inside the same physical entity, what is the status of transport mode IPsec on Gn and Gp?
questions.reference_answer: IPsec ESP shall be used with both encryption and integrity protection for all GTP-C messages traversing inter-security domain boundaries. If a network node has implemented SEG functionality within the same physical entity, transport mode IPsec is optional for implementation and use on the Gn and Gp interfaces.

questions.question: Setting up and configuring a gNB from an O&M system: which entity must authenticate and authorise that action, and is support of the TS 33.310 certificate enrolment mechanism mandatory or left to operators?
questions.reference_answer: Setting up and configuring gNBs by O&M systems shall be authenticated and authorized by the gNB. The certificate enrolment mechanism specified in TS 33.310 for base stations should be supported for gNBs, but the decision on whether to use it is left to operators (not mandatory).

questions.question: A gNB deployment stores keys in cleartext but is not itself placed in a physically secure location. What must then hold for storage and processing of those keys, and under what condition may a key leave the secure environment?
questions.reference_answer: If a part of a gNB deployment stores or processes keys in cleartext and is not placed in a physically secure location, keys in cleartext shall still be stored and processed in a secure environment. Keys stored inside a secure environment shall never leave that secure environment except when done in accordance with this or other 3GPP specifications.

questions.question: A UE indicates it is capable only of asynchronous dual connectivity. What relative receive timing difference between MCG and SCG subframe timing must it handle, and which inter-band combinations do those requirements cover?
questions.reference_answer: A UE capable only of asynchronous dual connectivity shall be capable of handling a relative receive timing difference between MCG and SCG subframe timing of up to 500 µs. These requirements are only applicable for FDD-FDD inter-band dual connectivity.

questions.question: A UE capable of synchronous dual connectivity is configured with powerControlMode set to 1. What maximum uplink transmission timing difference between PCell and PSCell must it handle, and what is it permitted to do if that difference is exceeded?
questions.reference_answer: With powerControlMode set to 1, the UE shall be capable of handling a maximum uplink transmission timing difference between PCell and PSCell of at least 35.21 µs (for synchronous dual connectivity). If configured with powerControlMode<1> and that difference exceeds 35.21 µs, the UE may stop transmission on the PSCell.

questions.question: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED state needs measurement gaps to perform UTRAN FDD CPICH Ec/No measurements. Which measurement gap pattern and procedure apply, and whose accuracy and reporting range specification must be reused?
questions.reference_answer: The UTRAN FDD measurement procedure and measurement gap pattern stated in clause 8.1.2.4.1 shall apply. The reporting range and mapping specified for FDD CPICH Ec/No in TS 25.133 shall be reused.

questions.question: Which three special font names must a terminal recognise, what pixel size must it support, and what should it do when a requested size is not among the supported ones?
questions.reference_answer: The terminal shall recognize the three special font names Serif, Sans-Serif, and Monospace, and shall support a pixel size of 12. If a requested size is not among the supported ones, the next smaller supported size should be used; if the requested size is smaller than the smallest supported size, the terminal should use the smallest supported size.

questions.question: An NF service consumer's UDSF subscription to data change expires. To which URI must the UDSF send its POST, what must the request body contain, and which status code does the consumer return on success?
questions.reference_answer: The UDSF shall send a POST request to the expiryCallbackReference URI. The request shall contain the NotificationInfo. On success, the NF Service Consumer returns "204 No content" to the UDSF.

questions.question: An NF service consumer PUTs a subscription to UDSF data-change notifications but the resource named in the URI does not exist. What must the UDSF do, which parameter must always be present in the request, and why may the returned expiry attribute differ from the requested one?
questions.reference_answer: If the resource indicated in the URI doesn't exist, the UDSF shall trigger the creation of the subscription. The parameter clientId shall always be included in the request. The returned expiry attribute may differ from the requested one if, due to operator policy, an expiry time is enforced or if the requested value exceeded a maximum allowed expiry time.

questions.question: A service wants to play an announcement to a user while a communication session is still being established. Which three methods is it restricted to, and which header field is used with the 180 (Ringing) response?
questions.reference_answer: The service is restricted to: using an Alert-Info header field in the 180 (Ringing) response to the INVITE request; using early media (annex G) with the P-Early-Media header field; or using multiple early dialogs (annex D) with the P-Early-Media header field. The 180 (Ringing) response uses the Alert-Info header field.

questions.question: An announcement must be mixed into an existing media stream of an already established session. Which header field would be used in a re-INVITE, and which 3rd party call control procedure must the AS apply?
questions.reference_answer: A Call-Info header field would be used in the re-INVITE request. The AS must apply the 3rd party call control procedure specified in subclause 5.7.5 of 3GPP TS 24.229.

questions.question: A UE configured with one PCell and one PSCell receives a PSCell release in subframe n. By when must it complete the release actions, and during which procedure alone is PCell interruption permitted?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall accomplish the release actions no later than subframe n+TRRC_delay, where TRRC_delay is the RRC procedure delay specified in TS 38.331. PCell interruption is allowed only during the RRC reconfiguration procedure in TS 38.331.

questions.question: A base station is declared capable of NB-IoT operation in NR in-band. Is it still required to repeat the NR-only transmitter and receiver tests, and which NR resource block position is punctured for the in-band test?
questions.reference_answer: No, a base station declared capable of NB-IoT operation in NR in-band is only required to pass the transmitter and receiver tests for NR with NB-IoT operation in NR in-band; it is not required to perform those tests again for NR only. One NR RB is punctured at the eligible in-band position closest to the NR minimum guard band.

questions.question: For CDR transfer over the Bx interface, which encoding rules must every 3GPP system support and which two are optional? Which Data Record Format value signifies aligned basic PER?
questions.reference_answer: For CDR transfer via the Bx interface, Basic Encoding Rules (BER) shall be supported by all 3GPP systems; Packed Encoding Rules (PER) and XML Encoding Rules (XER) are optional. Data Record Format value "3" signifies the use of aligned basic Packed Encoding Rules (PER).

questions.question: An idle timeout associated with a granted quota expires at a Credit-Control client. What must its expiry trigger, and what two things must the client do when a re-authorization is triggered?
questions.reference_answer: Expiry of the idle timeout shall trigger a re-authorization request. When a re-authorization is triggered, the client shall report quota usage, and the reason for the quota being reported shall be notified to the server.

questions.question: For roaming-band TRP conformance of laptop mounted equipment, which two limits must be met (per-channel and aggregate), in which scale must the averaging be done, and which ground plane phantom applies?
questions.reference_answer: The average measured TRP of low, mid and high channel must be higher than the average TRP requirement, and the lowest TRP of each measured channel must be higher than the minimum TRP requirement. Averaging shall be done in linear scale, and the laptop ground plane phantom defined in TR 25.914 subclauses 5.1.3 and 5.1.4 applies.

questions.question: How do the measurement conditions for laptop embedded equipment differ between notebook devices and tablet devices when checking roaming-band TRP?
questions.reference_answer: LEE requirements are measured as defined in TR 25.914: subclause 5.3.1 applies to notebook devices, and subclause 5.3.2 applies to tablet devices.

questions.question: The USIM application toolkit Rejection Cause Code object is populated after a Routing Area Update Reject on UTRAN. Which cause must it carry and how is it coded, and what would it carry instead after an EMM ATTACH REJECT on E-UTRAN?
questions.reference_answer: After a Routing Area Update Reject on UTRAN, the object shall contain the GMM Cause as received in the Routing Area Update Reject message, coded in the same manner as the value part of the GMM Cause information element in TS 24.008. After an EMM ATTACH REJECT on E-UTRAN, it shall instead contain the EMM Cause as received in the EMM ATTACH REJECT message, coded in the same manner as the value part of the EMM Cause information element in TS 24.301.

questions.question: In the Tracking Area Identification object of the USIM application toolkit, how many bytes does the TAC occupy for NG-RAN compared with E-UTRAN, and which specification defines the coding of the value part in each case?
questions.reference_answer: The TAC is coded in 3 bytes for NG-RAN/Satellite NG-RAN, compared with 2 bytes for E-UTRAN/Satellite E-UTRAN. For E-UTRAN, the value part is coded as the Tracking Area Identity information element in TS 24.301; for NG-RAN, it is coded as the Tracking Area Identity information element in TS 24.501.

questions.question: For LSA scenario 2, which entity must let the NM obtain the constraints on cell parameters needed to use LSA spectrum, and which two inputs must the LC take into account when calculating those LSA cell constraints?
questions.reference_answer: The LC shall support a capability allowing the NM to obtain the constraints on cell parameters needed to use LSA spectrum resources. The LC shall take into account LSRAI and the range for cell parameters provided by the NM when calculating the LSA cell constraints.

questions.question: An MS receives the RESET MS POSITIONING STORED INFORMATION signal with MS POSITIONING TECHNOLOGY set to AGPS. Which stored items must it discard, and what must it then do to obtain reference time or reference location?
questions.reference_answer: The MS shall discard any internally stored GPS reference time, reference location, and any other aiding data obtained or derived during the previous test instance. It must then accept or request a new set of reference time or reference location or other required information, as in a TTFF condition.

questions.question: A BSSAP+ receiving entity gets a message whose message type is not defined or not implemented by it. Beyond ignoring the message, what response message must it return and which Gs Cause Value and which IE must that response carry?
questions.reference_answer: It must return a BSSAP+-MOBILE-STATUS message with the Gs Cause Value set to "message unknown" and the Erroneous message IE containing the received message.

questions.question: After the SGSN receives a BSSAP+-LOCATION-UPDATE-ACCEPT message from the VLR, which timer must it stop, which state must the Gs association move to, and what values must it set for the MM context variables 'VLR-Reliable' and 'EMM Combined UE Waiting Flag'?
questions.reference_answer: The SGSN shall stop timer T6-1, move the state of the association to Gs-ASSOCIATED, set the MM context variable 'VLR-Reliable' to 'true', and set the MM context variable 'EMM Combined UE Waiting Flag' to 'false'.

questions.question: In the Downlink Tunnel Payload Control and Info IE, what obligation does the Cipher Request bit E place on the SGSN when it is set to 1, and what when it is set to 0?
questions.reference_answer: When the Cipher Request bit E is set to 1, it indicates that the SGSN shall cipher the payload. When set to 0, it indicates that the SGSN shall not cipher the payload.

questions.question: When the number of IMSI digits carried in the BSSAP+ IMSI information element is even, what must be placed in bits 5 to 8 of the last octet, and what is the maximum number of digits the IMSI may not exceed?
questions.reference_answer: If the number of IMSI digits is even, bits 5 to 8 of the last octet shall be filled with an end mark coded as 1111. The IMSI shall not exceed 15 digits.

questions.question: For the SGSN number information element, which parts are excluded when applying the digit-count limit, and what is that limit?
questions.reference_answer: The IEI, Length indicator and Octet 3 are excluded from the digit-count limit. The value part of the SGSN number information element shall not exceed 15 digits.

questions.question: The IWF floor control server receives a Floor Request from an MCPTT floor participant that has already been granted permission to send overriding media. Which message must the arbitration logic send to the previously granted participant, which timer value must go in the Duration field, and which state must the server remain in?
questions.reference_answer: The arbitration logic shall send a Floor Granted message to the previously granted MCPTT floor participant. The Duration field shall include the value of the T12 (Stop talking dual) timer. The server shall remain in the 'D: Floor Taken' state.

questions.question: When the overriding MCPTT media endpoint starts to disconnect from the call, what must the IWF floor control server request the media distributor to do, and what value of the G-bit must the Floor Idle message it sends carry?
questions.reference_answer: The IWF floor control server shall request the media distributor to stop distributing RTP media packets received from the overriding MCPTT media endpoint to other media endpoints. The Floor Idle message it sends shall have the Floor Indicator field's G-bit set to '1' (Dual floor).

questions.question: An originating IWF floor participant receives a floor control message before the SIP 200 (OK) response arrives. Is it obliged to act on it immediately or to store it, and what must it do with a floor control message received after a SIP INVITE with implicit floor request but before the 200 (OK)?
questions.reference_answer: If the originating IWF floor participant receives a floor control message before the SIP 200 (OK) response, it shall store the message rather than act on it immediately. If a floor control message is received after a SIP INVITE with implicit floor request but before the 200 (OK), it shall act upon that floor control message.

questions.question: The IWF floor participant decides to release permission to send media in a broadcast call that was established as a normal call. Which value of the A-bit must the Floor Indicator carry, and what must it include if the earlier Floor Granted message had the G-bit set to 1?
questions.reference_answer: If the session is a broadcast call established as a normal call, the Floor Indicator must carry the A-bit set to '1' (Normal call). If the earlier Floor Granted message had the G-bit set to '1' (Dual floor), the Floor Release message must include the Floor Indicator with the G-bit set to '1' (Dual floor).

questions.question: An IWF floor participant receives a Floor Queue Position Info message whose first subtype bit is set to 1. What must it send back, and which two field values must that response carry?
questions.reference_answer: It must send back a Floor Ack message, which shall include the Message Type field set to '9' (Floor Queue Position Info) and the Source field set to '0' (the IWF floor participant is the source).

questions.question: For a 5G-RG connected via wireline access, which single category of UE policy should the PCF provide, and does the V-PCF apply in this deployment?
questions.reference_answer: The PCF should only provide URSP policy for a 5G-RG connected via wireline access. The V-PCF (Visited Policy Control Function) shall not apply for a 5G-RG connecting via wireline access and FN-RG.

questions.question: When the H-PCF derives the 5G ProSe Policy after being notified of an Application Data change from the UDR, which service and which NAS message must be used to convey the policy to the UE via the AMF in the non-roaming case?
questions.reference_answer: For the non-roaming case, the (V-)PCF shall use the Namf_Communication Service (defined in 3GPP TS 29.518) to convey the ProSeP to the UE via the AMF by sending "MANAGE UE POLICY COMMAND" message(s) as defined in 3GPP TS 24.554.

questions.question: Before an NF Service Consumer may consume the Nhss_UEAU API when OAuth2 is used, what must it obtain and from which network function acting as authorization server, and how many scopes does that API define?
questions.reference_answer: The NF Service Consumer must obtain a "token" from the authorization server by invoking the Access Token Request service, where the NRF plays the role of authorization server. The Nhss_UEAU API defines a single scope, "nhss-ueau", for the entire API.

questions.question: A UDM invokes the HSS to modify a subscription it created earlier. Which HTTP method must be used and against which resource, and which status code must the HSS return on success?
questions.reference_answer: The HTTP method PATCH must be used, against the URI of the individual subscription resource to be modified. On success, the HSS shall respond with "204 No Content".

questions.question: An originating UE is configured with IMS_DC_configuration whose DC_Setup_Option leaf says the data channel is set up simultaneously with the IMS session. In the early session model, what must the UE include in the SDP offer of the initial SIP INVITE for an MMTel session with an IMS data channel?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall include the data channel media description in the SDP offer of the initial SIP INVITE, as specified in clause 9.3.2.1.2.

questions.question: Explicit Communication Transfer has been triggered and the IMS AS serving the transferor receives a REFER message. Which data channels must it trigger the closing of, and where must it route the session setup INVITE request?
questions.reference_answer: The IMS AS serving the transferor shall trigger the closing of all established data channels on the transferor's network, including the data channel between the transferor's network and the transferor, the data channel between the transferor's network and the transferee, and the data channel between the transferor's network and the transfer target. It must route the session setup INVITE request (including audio, video and data channel media) towards the REFER-TO user.

questions.question: A UE wants to suspend a data channel media stream that was previously active. Which SDP direction attribute must the invoking UE associate with the corresponding m=application line, and which attribute is used to resume a previously suspended data channel media?
questions.reference_answer: To suspend a previously active data channel media stream, the invoking UE must associate the SDP direction attribute "a=inactive" with the corresponding "m=application" line. To resume a previously suspended data channel media, it uses the SDP direction attribute "a=sendrecv" (or omits the direction attribute) for that line.

questions.question: The CFNR no-reply timer at the IMS AS expires after a 180 (Ringing) response was received. Which requests must the IMS AS send to the diverting UE, whom must it notify, and what must it ask the MF to release?
questions.reference_answer: On no-reply timer expiry, the IMS AS shall send a CANCEL or BYE request to the diverting UE, shall notify the DCSF about the session establishment cancellation or session termination, and shall request the MF to release the allocated data channel media resource on the early dialog of the MMTel session.

questions.question: A UE requests discovery information from the ANDSF using a client initiated session with a generic alert. What value must the Type element of the OMA DM generic alert message be set to, and what must the UE do with a descendant of the DiscoveryInformation node that it does not support?
questions.reference_answer: The "Type" element of the OMA DM generic alert message shall be set to "urn:oma:at:ext-3gpp-andsf:1.0:provision-disc-info". The UE shall ignore any node that is a descendant of the DiscoveryInformation node and is not supported by the UE.

questions.question: A single ANDSF/Policy/<X>/ValidityArea/3GPP_Location/<X> node instance carries a PLMN leaf plus a TAC leaf and a UTRAN_CI leaf. Under what condition may the UE consider the 3GPP location validity condition fulfilled, and what must it do with the other existing values?
questions.reference_answer: The UE may consider the 3GPP location validity condition fulfilled only if the present leaf values in the node (PLMN plus TAC/UTRAN_CI etc.) match the UE's location in that radio access technology. The UE shall ignore other existing values, if any.

questions.question: The MBMS interface in an MCVideo client receives an RTP media packet over an MBMS subchannel that has no association between the TMGI and an ongoing group session transmission. What is it obliged to do with that packet?
questions.reference_answer: If there is no association between the TMGI and the MBMS subchannels to an ongoing transmission in a group session, the MBMS interface shall ignore the received transmission control message or received RTP media packet.

questions.question: An SDP offer contains the mc_priority fmtp attribute and the on-network-recvonly element is absent for the MCVideo user. Which three input values must the controlling MCVideo function compare, and which of them must it choose for the SDP answer?
questions.reference_answer: The controlling MCVideo function must compare: (1) the value of transmission priority in the "mc_priority" fmtp attribute in the SDP offer, (2) the value of the <user-priority> element in the MCVideo group document, and (3) the value of the <num-levels-priority-hierarchy> element in the MCVideo service configuration document. It must choose the lowest of these three values for the SDP answer.

questions.question: Why must the offerer assign a unique SSRC value in the mc_transmission_ssrc fmtp attribute, and in which SDP messages is that attribute mandatory when multiplexing is supported?
questions.reference_answer: The offerer assigns a unique SSRC value so that the answerer can use it in media transmission control messages sent to the offerer, letting the offerer associate the received message to the correct session and avoid SSRC collision in case of multiplexing. The "mc_transmission_ssrc" fmtp attribute is mandatory in SDP offers when multiplexing is supported.

questions.question: A UE supporting NR sidelink U2U Relay operation performs U2U Relay Discovery with Model A. Which RSRP thresholds decide whether a potential UE is considered a neighbour, and which layer 3 filter coefficients must be applied before using those measurement results?
questions.reference_answer: A potential UE is considered a neighbour if its SL-RSRP is above sl-RSRP-Thresh-DiscConfig (if configured) or its SD-RSRP is above sd-RSRP-ThreshDiscConfig (if configured). Before using those measurement results, the UE shall apply layer 3 filtering per clause 5.5.3.2 using sl-FilterCoefficientU2U or sd-FilterCoefficientU2U in SL-RelayUE-ConfigU2U, if provided.

questions.question: When sl-ZoneConfig is configured, which formulae must the UE use to determine the Zone_id it is located in, and what does the parameter L correspond to?
questions.reference_answer: The UE uses: x1 = Floor(x / L) Mod 64; y1 = Floor(y / L) Mod 64; Zone_id = y1 * 64 + x1. The parameter L is the value of sl-ZoneLength included in sl-ZoneConfig.

questions.question: A U2N Relay UE transmits a NotificationMessageSidelink because of a Uu radio link failure, and separately because of cell reselection. Which indicationType value must it set in each of those two cases?
questions.reference_answer: For Uu radio link failure, the U2N Relay UE sets indicationType as relayUE-Uu-RLF. For cell reselection, it sets indicationType as relayUE-CellReselection.

questions.question: An L2 U2U Relay UE receives a UEInformationRequestSidelink. What must it decide per QoS flow, which field of the UEInformationResponseSidelink must carry the outcome, and what must it do if it is in RRC_IDLE or out of coverage?
questions.reference_answer: The L2 U2U Relay UE must perform QoS split based on sl-QoS-InfoList to decide the split PDB value for each PC5 hop, per QoS flow. The outcome is carried in the sl-SplitQoS-InfoListPC5 field of the UEInformationResponseSidelink message. If the UE is in RRC_IDLE (or RRC_INACTIVE or out of coverage), it must derive the PC5 Relay RLC channel configuration on the second PC5 hop and (re)configure the SRAP entity to map the end-to-end DRB with the PC5 Relay RLC channel, if needed.

questions.question: For FR1-NTN and FR2-NTN, when the SSB for RLM falls in the same OFDM symbol as a CSI-RS with a different subcarrier spacing and the UE does not support simultaneousRxDataSSB-DiffNumerology, is the UE required to measure both, and what does the specification say about the requirements in that case?
questions.reference_answer: No, the UE is required to measure only one of SSB for RLM and CSI-RS, not both. A longer measurement period for SSB based RLM is expected, and no requirements are defined for that case.

questions.question: One SCell in the SCG that is configured with PUCCH is activated. Within what delay must the interruption start, and for inter-band CA what additional interruption is allowed if the UE is not capable of parallelTxPRACH-SRS-PUCCH-PUSCH?
questions.reference_answer: The starting time of the interruption shall be within the delay defined in clause 8.3.12. For inter-band CA, if the UE is not capable of parallelTxPRACH-SRS-PUCCH-PUSCH, additional interruption is allowed on SRS/PUCCH/PUSCH of active serving cells when colliding with RACH transmission on the PUCCH SCell, occurring on the symbols containing SRS/PUCCH/PUSCH that overlap with the duration of the PRACH preamble transmitted on the PUCCH SCell.

questions.question: An MCData UE needs to send a disposition request for a session SDS transmission, but the media plane is no longer available. Which plane must it use for the disposition notification in that situation, and which plane must be used for standalone SDS and FD?
questions.reference_answer: For session SDS, the MCData UE shall use the signalling plane for disposition notifications when the media plane is no longer available. For standalone SDS and FD, the MCData UE shall use the signalling plane for disposition request and disposition notifications.

questions.question: Who is obliged to configure the preset enhanced status values for MCData, on what granularity is the configuration applicable, and what minimum and maximum number of possible values must the configuration mechanism allow?
questions.reference_answer: The MCData administrator is obliged to configure the preset enhanced status values, and the configuration is applicable on a per-group basis (part of the MCData group configuration data). The configuration mechanism shall allow a minimum of 32 possible values and up to 65536 separate values.

questions.question: In the MCData transmission control arbitration function, may a single request sit in more than one queue at the same time, and who is allowed to configure the queue types and the order of queues?
questions.reference_answer: Each request shall not be present in more than one queue at any given time. The queue types and the order of queues may be configured by the MCData administrator.

questions.question: Which reference points must the MCData service use for the procedure of using pre-established MBMS bearers, and may a single such bearer be used by more than one group?
questions.reference_answer: The MCData service shall use the MCData-6, MCData-SDS-1, MCData-SDS-2, MCData-SDS-3, MCData-FD-1, MCData-FD-3, MCData-DS-1 and MCData-DS-3 reference points. Yes, the MBMS bearer can be used by any group.

questions.question: Once an MCData user has de-affiliated from an MCData group, what is the user no longer able to do, and which clause of TS 23.280 provides the affiliation procedures that the MCData service must support?
questions.reference_answer: Once de-affiliated from an MCData group, the MCData user cannot send and receive MCData related media to and from that MCData group. The MCData service shall support the affiliation and de-affiliation procedures and related information flows as specified in subclause 10.8 of 3GPP TS 23.280.

questions.question: An RNC cannot end broadcasting in the Service Areas indicated by a RESET message. Which failure message must it respond with, which IE must that message contain, and what constraint applies to the sum of Service Areas across the Service Areas List and Failure List IEs?
questions.reference_answer: The RNC shall respond using a RESET FAILURE message. The RESET FAILURE message shall contain the Failure List IE (and may contain the Service Areas List IE). The sum of the Service Area(s) included in the Service Areas List and Failure List IEs shall be the same as indicated in the Service Areas List IE of the initiating RESET message.

questions.question: After the CN receives a FAILURE message from the RNC indicating a Service Area broadcasting problem, which messages must the CN refrain from generating for those Service Areas, and what message tells it that normal broadcasting may resume?
questions.reference_answer: The CN will not generate further WRITE or REPLACE messages for those Service Area(s). Normal broadcasting may resume once the CN is informed by a RESTART message that the Service Area can resume normal Service Area broadcasting operation.

questions.question: For what purposes may the protocol extension mechanism for non-standard use be used over the SABP interface, and what is it explicitly forbidden to be used for?
questions.reference_answer: The protocol extension mechanism for non-standard use may be used for special operator- and/or vendor-specific features not part of the basic functionality, and by vendors for research purposes (e.g. to implement and evaluate new algorithms/features before standardisation). It shall not be used for basic functionality, which shall be standardised.

questions.question: A UE is transmitting on uplink physical channels and UTRAN has indicated that the UE may autonomously increase the spreading factor. Along which branch of the allowed OVSF sub-tree must the UE vary the channelisation code, and how many physical channels per timeslot may a UE use for multicode transmission?
questions.reference_answer: If the UE autonomously changes the SF, it shall always vary the channelisation code along the branch with the higher code numbering of the allowed OVSF sub-tree. For multicode transmission a UE shall use a maximum of two physical channels per timeslot simultaneously.

questions.question: Which midambles must beacon channels use exclusively in their time slot, which midambles must always be left unused when 16 midambles are allowed in the cell, and to what does the reference power of a beacon channel correspond?
questions.reference_answer: Beacon channels shall use midamble m(1) and m(2) exclusively in this time slot. Midambles m(9) and m(10) are always left unused in this time slot when 16 midambles are allowed in that cell. The reference power corresponds to the sum of the power allocated to both midambles m(1) and m(2).

questions.question: Why must the GTP TEID be unpredictable, and which two concrete attacks does that requirement prevent according to the security assurance requirement?
questions.reference_answer: The GTP TEID shall be unpredictable in order to prevent a hacker from injecting GTP-U packets with a spoofed TEID into a user's session (causing e.g. overbilling problems) or from sending malicious GTP-C messages to delete an established session (causing a DoS).

questions.question: During PC5 unicast establishment between A2X-enabled UEs, must the initiating UE reuse one security context across peer UEs or establish a different one per peer, and which three protections must the PC5 unicast signalling and user plane support?
questions.reference_answer: The initiating UE shall establish a different security context for each peer UE during PC5 unicast establishment if security is activated. The PC5 unicast signalling and user plane shall support confidentiality protection, integrity protection and anti-replay protection.

questions.question: Which two mutually alternative TLS authentication mechanisms must a Remote Device support for key establishment, and what credential must the device be equipped with in each case?
questions.reference_answer: The Remote Device shall support TLS with certificate-based mutual authentication (in which case it shall be equipped with a valid Client Certificate), or shall support shared key based mutual authentication using PSK-TLS (in which case it shall be equipped with a valid pre-shared key).

questions.question: A Remote Device has a stored Ks_local_device key for a UICC Hosting Device but the attempt to use it fails because the UICC Hosting Device does not share that key. What must the Remote Device do next?
questions.reference_answer: The Remote Device shall initiate a new request to the UICC Hosting Device to initiate a new key establishment procedure in order to establish a new Ks_local_device key.

questions.question: For lawful interception of the device triggering service, upon which four specific events must the IRI-POI present in the SCEF generate an xIRI?
questions.reference_answer: The IRI-POI present in the SCEF shall generate an xIRI upon: device trigger, device trigger replacement, device trigger cancellation, and device trigger report notification.

questions.question: In case of service selection personalisation, which entity must authenticate the user, which specification must that authentication follow, and under what condition does that entity not need to authenticate the user itself?
questions.reference_answer: The SSF shall authenticate the user, following 3GPP TS 33.222. The SSF does not need to authenticate the user itself when an Authentication Proxy (AP) is in the path and the SSF receives an HTTP request from that trusted source containing an HTTP X-3GPP-Asserted-Identity header with an asserted identity of the user (in that case it only provides authorization).

questions.question: A bitstream claims conformance to the 3GPP VR Main 8K H.265/HEVC Operation Point. What value must general_profile_idc be set to, what value must general_tier_flag be set to, and what is the upper bound on level_idc?
questions.reference_answer: general_profile_idc shall be set to 2 (Main10 profile), general_tier_flag shall be set to 0 (Main tier), and level_idc shall not be greater than 183 (corresponding to Level 6.1).

questions.question: An LCS request towards a user is barred by the operator. What is returned to the LCS Requestor, and for which categories of service must the location request still be processed with the highest priority regardless of the barring status?
questions.reference_answer: If the LCS request fails due to barring, an error cause is returned to the LCS Requestor. For Emergency Services and other services where required by local regulatory requirements, and for PLMN operator Services, the location request shall still be processed with the highest priority level regardless of the barring status.

questions.question: An IRPAgent wants to pack multiple notifications into a single push operation. What must it implement so that the IRPManager is not made to wait an objectionable amount of time, what must happen on expiry of that mechanism, and when is it restarted?
questions.reference_answer: The IRPAgent shall implement an IRPAgent-wide timer configurable by the administrator. On expiration of this timer, the IRPAgent shall invoke push if there is at least one notification to be conveyed to the IRPManager. This timer is re-started after each push invocation.

questions.question: For a UE that supports ca-IdleModeMeasurements, how many non-overlapping and how many overlapping inter-frequency carriers must it at least support for idle mode CA measurements, and who decides whether those measurements are performed when T331 is absent or has expired?
questions.reference_answer: A UE that supports ca-IdleModeMeasurements shall support idle mode CA measurements of at least 1 non-overlapping and 1 overlapping inter-frequency carrier. In the absence or expiration of T331, it is up to UE implementation to decide whether the idle mode CA measurement is performed.

questions.question: A USIM stores a Service Provider Name and the UE is registered on a PLMN that is not the HPLMN and is not one of the PLMN Identifications configured for Service Provider Name display. Which name must be displayed, how many PLMN Identifications must it be possible to associate with the same SP Name, and from which end is the name cut if the UE cannot display it in full?
questions.reference_answer: The PLMN name shall be displayed. It shall be possible to associate at least 10 PLMN Identifications with the same SP Name. If the UE cannot display the full name, it is cut from the tail end.

questions.question: What must the 5G system support for the fully distributed model of time-sensitive networking configuration, and with which IEEE protocols such as MSRP, LRP and RAP must that support be aligned?
questions.reference_answer: The 5G system shall support the fully distributed model for configuration of time-sensitive networking, aligned with Multiple Stream Registration Protocol (MSRP, IEEE 802.1Q clause 35.1), IEEE P802.1CS Link-local Registration Protocol (LRP), and IEEE P802.1Qdd Resource Allocation Protocol (RAP).

questions.question: An MCX client obtains an access token to reach an MCX resource server. Which access token type must MCX Connect support, in which HTTP header must the token be carried, and what does the client know about the token itself?
questions.reference_answer: MCX Connect shall initially support the bearer access token type, carried in the HTTP Authorization Header. The access token is opaque to the MCX client, meaning the client has no knowledge of the access token itself (only metadata such as its expiration time).

questions.question: Which parameter must the authorising server use to decide that an access token is no longer valid, and which parameter must the UE client use for the same purpose in a token response message?
questions.reference_answer: The authorising server shall use the "exp" parameter to determine whether the token is valid. The UE client(s) shall use the "expires_in" parameter for the same purpose in a token response message.

questions.question: For AMR wideband speech, what must the speech decoder be told about erroneous or lost frames, what insertion is explicitly not allowed as concealment, and what technique must be used when several subsequent frames are lost?
questions.reference_answer: The speech decoder shall be informed about erroneous/lost frames so error concealment actions can be initiated using predicted parameters. Insertion of speech signal independent silence frames is not allowed. For several subsequent erroneous/lost frames, a muting technique shall be used to indicate to the listener that transmission has been interrupted.

questions.question: When the AMF requests PDU Session Release towards an alternative V/I-SMF in the same SMF Set because it detected the V/I-SMF has failed, what must the POST request contain in the release IE and the cause IE?
questions.reference_answer: The POST request shall contain the release IE set to true and the cause IE set to REL_DUE_TO_SMF_NOT_SUPPORT_PSETR.

questions.question: On inter-AMF change or mobility, what must the new AMF acting as NF Service Consumer set in servingNfId and supportedFeatures when it informs the SMF it has taken over the role of serving the UE?
questions.reference_answer: The new AMF (NF Service Consumer) shall set servingNfId to the new serving AMF Id, and shall set the supportedFeatures IE to indicate the features it supports, if at least one feature defined in clause 6.1.8 is supported.

questions.question: For a UE Triggered Service Request with I-SMF Insertion, what value must the upCnxState IE be set to in the POST request to indicate that user plane resource for the PDU Session is going to be established by the I-SMF?
questions.reference_answer: The upCnxState IE must be set to ACTIVATING to indicate that User Plane resource for the PDU Session is going to be established by the I-SMF.

questions.question: During PDU Session modification with I-SMF or V-SMF change, which IEs must the new V-SMF or new I-SMF include in the POST request to convey the callback URI representing the PDU session, and what values may requestIndication take?
questions.reference_answer: The new V-SMF or new I-SMF shall include the ismfPduSessionUri or vsmfPduSessionUri IE (containing the callback URI representing the PDU session) in the POST request. requestIndication may be set to NW_REQ_PDU_SES_MOD or UE_REQ_PDU_SES_MOD, for network requested or UE requested PDU session modification respectively.

questions.question: In PFCP load control, how often must the sender include load control information, and what delay guarantee does the specification place on propagating new or updated load control information to target CP functions?
questions.reference_answer: How often the sender includes the load control information is implementation specific. The sender shall ensure that new/updated load control information is propagated to the target CP functions within an acceptable delay, such that the purpose of the information (effective load balancing) is achieved.

questions.question: What are the permitted approaches a PFCP sender may implement for including the OCI IE towards a receiver, and what obligation does the sender carry regarding propagation delay of overload control information?
questions.reference_answer: The sender may include the OCI IE towards a receiver only when the new/changed value has not already been provided to that receiver; may include the OCI IE in a subset of the messages towards the receiver; or may include the OCI IE periodically (during a first period then cease during a second period), or a combination of these. The sender shall ensure that new/updated overload control information is propagated to the target receivers with an acceptable delay so that effective overload control protection is achieved.

questions.question: When a PFCP node performs message throttling, how must PFCP requests related to eMPS priority traffic and emergency be treated relative to other sessions?
questions.reference_answer: PFCP requests related to eMPS priority traffic and emergency have the highest priority: they shall be the last to be throttled when applying traffic reduction, and shall be exempted from throttling due to PFCP overload control up to the point where the requested traffic reduction cannot be achieved without throttling them.

questions.question: When message prioritization is based on the message priority signalled in the PFCP header, how should a sending PFCP entity determine the relative message priority when the message affects multiple bearers, and what should it set in a Response message?
questions.reference_answer: SEID shall be set to 0 in the PFCP Session Establishment Request message on Sxa/Sxb/Sxc/N4 (and in messages where a peer's SEID is not otherwise available, e.g. certain response/report messages). If a node receives a message for which it has no session (SEID in the PFCP header not known), it shall respond with the "Session context not found" cause.

questions.question: In which PFCP messages must the SEID field be set to 0 when a peer's SEID is not available, and what cause must a node return when the SEID in the PFCP header is not known?
questions.reference_answer: SEID shall be set to 0 in the PFCP Session Establishment Request message on Sxa/Sxb/Sxc/N4 when a peer's SEID is not available (also in the response message SEID when the node has no session for the received SEID, and when the UP function sends a PFCP Session Report Request over N4 towards another SMF/PFCP entity). If SEID in the PFCP header is not known, the node shall respond with the "Session context not found" cause.

questions.question: When the PCRF receives service information for a prioritized GC session including a GCSE session indication and service priority level from the GCSE AS, what must it do with the ARP of the derived PCC Rules and of the default bearer?
questions.reference_answer: The PCRF shall derive the PCC Rules for the Group Communication Service and set the ARP (priority level, pre-emption capability, pre-emption vulnerability) of these PCC Rules based on the information received over Rx and operator policies, and shall ensure that the ARP of the default bearer is assigned a prioritized value.

questions.question: At IP-CAN session establishment with NBIFOM, what values must the PCRF set in the NBIFOM-Support AVP depending on whether it determines NBIFOM applies to the IP-CAN session?
questions.reference_answer: If the PCRF determines that NBIFOM does not apply to the IP-CAN session, it shall set the NBIFOM-Support AVP to NBIFOM_NOT_SUPPORTED (0); otherwise it shall set it to NBIFOM_SUPPORTED (1).

questions.question: When the PCEF receives both a handover request and an NBIFOM indication from the UE, which Event-Trigger value must it include in the CCR command sent to the PCRF to notify the addition of an access?
questions.reference_answer: The PCEF shall include the Event-Trigger AVP set to the value ADDITION_OF_ACCESS in the CCR command.

questions.question: Which AVPs may be used when the PCRF provisions the maximum allowed bit rate to the TDF within a TSR, CCA or RAR Diameter message, and in which AVP is that information carried?
questions.reference_answer: Only the Max-Requested-Bandwidth-UL AVP and the Max-Requested-Bandwidth-DL AVP, or the Extended-Max-Requested-BW-UL AVP and the Extended-Max-Requested-BW-DL AVP, shall be used. This information is carried within the QoS-Information AVP.

questions.question: When the PCRF provides OFCS and OCS addresses to the TDF in the Charging-Information AVP, must both primary and secondary addresses be provided, and what must the TDF do if no OCS address is available?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, both primary and secondary addresses for OFCS and/or OCS shall be provided simultaneously. If no OCS address is available at the TDF, the TDF shall use the IMSI (MNC and MCC values) of the user to construct the OCS Home network domain name as specified in 3GPP TS 23.003 clause 25.

questions.question: If the TDF receives the 3GPP-Charging-Characteristics AVP together with Charging-Information, Online and Offline AVPs, which of these takes precedence in determining the values applied?
questions.reference_answer: The Charging-Information AVP, Online AVP or Offline AVP shall supersede (take precedence over) the values determined from the received 3GPP-Charging-Characteristics AVP.

questions.question: When the ProvAFsignalFlow feature is supported and the AF provisions information about AF signalling flows for IMS Restoration, what must the PCF include in the PccRule instances regarding flowInfos and afSigProtocol?
questions.reference_answer: The PCF shall include, within the associated PccRule instance(s), the signalling flows between the UE and the AF within the "flowInfos" attribute, and set the "afSigProtocol" attribute to the value corresponding to the signalling protocol used between the UE and the AF.

questions.question: When the PCF receives a request for P-CSCF restoration from the P-CSCF under the PCSCF-Restoration-Enhancement feature, what must it send to the SMF and what attribute must it set to true?
questions.reference_answer: The PCF shall send a notification (HTTP POST) message to the SMF, including the "pcscfRestIndication" attribute set to true for the corresponding PDU session.

questions.question: With the SessionRuleErrorHandling feature supported, what HTTP status code must the SMF return when validation of ALL received session rules was unsuccessful, versus when only some failed, and which attribute reports the failures?
questions.reference_answer: If validation of ALL received session rules was unsuccessful, the SMF shall reject the request with HTTP "400 Bad Request" and include the "sessRuleReports" attribute (SessionRuleReport data structure(s) within the ErrorReport data structure). If only some failed, the SMF shall reply with HTTP "200 OK" and include the "sessRuleReports" attribute (within the PartialSuccessReport data structure).

questions.question: In the SCPDomainRoutingInfoGet service operation, what does SCP Domain Routing Information with an empty map indicate, and to which document resource must the SCP send the HTTP GET request?
questions.reference_answer: SCP Domain Routing Information with an empty map indicates that no SCP domain is registered in the network (or in the producer NRF for the local request). The SCP shall send the HTTP GET request to the resource URI representing the "scp-domain-routing-info" document resource.

questions.question: In the SCPDomainRoutingInfoNotify operation, what must the NRF set the localInd IE to when the notification concerns a change of local SCP Domain Routing Information?
questions.reference_answer: The NRF must set the "localInd" IE to value "true" if the notification is for a change of local SCP Domain Routing Information.

questions.question: In the RANAP Data Volume Report procedure, which IE list must the DATA VOLUME REPORT REQUEST contain, and what must the UTRAN include for each successfully addressed RAB in the DATA VOLUME REPORT message?
questions.reference_answer: The DATA VOLUME REPORT REQUEST must contain the list of RAB ID IEs (RAB Data Volume Report List IE) identifying the RABs for which unsuccessfully transmitted DL data volume shall be reported. For each successfully addressed RAB, the UTRAN must include in the DATA VOLUME REPORT message the Unsuccessfully Transmitted DL Data Volume IE, giving the amount of unsuccessfully transmitted DL data since the last report for that RAB.

questions.question: When the RNC sends a DIRECT TRANSFER message to the PS domain, which two IEs must it additionally add, and which values must they take if the UTRAN had not yet indicated any LAI and RAC to the UE via the current RRC connection?
questions.reference_answer: The RNC must additionally add the LAI and RAC IEs. If the UTRAN had not yet indicated any LAI + RAC to the UE via the current RRC connection, these shall be set to the LAI + RAC of the cell via which the current RRC connection was established.

questions.question: Upon receipt of the RADIO LINK RECONFIGURATION CANCEL message from the SRNC, what must the DRNS release and which configuration must it continue using?
questions.reference_answer: The DRNS shall release the new configuration previously prepared by the Synchronised RL Reconfiguration Preparation procedure, and continue using the old configuration.

questions.question: If the Transport Bearer Request Indicator IE is set to "Bearer Requested" and the DRNC cannot provide a Transport Bearer, which failure message must it send to the SRNC and what must it include in it?
questions.reference_answer: The DRNC shall respond to the SRNC with the COMMON TRANSPORT CHANNEL RESOURCES FAILURE message, including the reason for the failure in the Cause IE.

questions.question: In UTRAN positioning, what must the CRNC do if an LMU fails to send Radio Interface Timing information, and what must it do if restarting the LMU also fails?
questions.reference_answer: If an LMU fails to send Radio Interface Timing information, the CRNC shall try to restart the LMU; if the restart also fails, the CRNC shall inform the O&M system.

questions.question: When a Media Application Provider invokes the purge Content Hosting cache operation, which HTTP method and MIME content type must be used, and what must the Media AF do immediately on receiving the purge request?
questions.reference_answer: The HTTP POST method shall be used, with the request body encoded using the application/x-www-form-urlencoded MIME content type. On receiving the purge request, the Media AF shall immediately invalidate all media resources in the Media AS cache matching the regular expression by declaring them as stale.

questions.question: When more than one content contribution configuration is provided in the request body of an Update Content Publishing Configuration operation, under what condition is the update successful, and which status code should be returned if the request causes no change?
questions.reference_answer: The update shall be successful if and only if all provided content contribution configurations are acceptable to the Media AF. If the request causes no change to the resource representation, a 204 (No Content) response should be returned.

questions.question: For the 5GMSu Purge Content Publishing cache procedure, how must the request body be encoded, what must the key and the value of the key-value pair be, and what response does the 5GMSu AS return on success?
questions.reference_answer: The request body shall be a single key-value pair encoded per the application/x-www-form-urlencoded MIME content type: the key shall be the string "pattern" and the value shall be a regular expression identifying the media resource URL(s) to purge. On success, the 5GMSu AS shall return an HTTP 200 (OK) response, with the body indicating the total number of cache entries purged.

questions.question: For which domain name and initial path element must the Media Session Handler register itself as URL handler to play the role of 3GPP Service Handler for 5GMS Service URLs?
questions.reference_answer: The Media Session Handler shall register itself as URL handler for the domain name launch.3gppservices.org and the initial path element /ms.

questions.question: If the optional Notification_test_event feature is supported, what must the SCEF do immediately after establishing the notification delivery mechanism when the SCS/AS sets requestTestNotification to true?
questions.reference_answer: The SCEF shall send, immediately after establishing the notification delivery mechanism, a test notification with a body formatted according to the "TestNotification" data type.

questions.question: If the NF service producer rejects a service request with 401 Unauthorized and the SCP had included an access token it had cached or obtained from the NRF, is the SCP allowed to repeat the request with that access token?
questions.reference_answer: No, the SCP shall not repeat the request with the access token that was used; it may repeat the request with a new access token instead, and otherwise (or if the repeated request also fails) shall forward the response to the NF service consumer.

questions.question: For authorization in indirect communication without delegated discovery, what kind of access token must the NF service consumer include when the SCP may select or reselect a producer NF instance?
questions.reference_answer: The NF service consumer shall include an access token that is valid for any producer's NF instance the SCP may select or reselect, i.e. an access token not specific to a particular producer NF instance, but valid for the target NF type and producer's NF set.

questions.question: Which requirements does the 5G system have to support for monitoring timing source failure, and what must it be able to indicate to devices about an alternate time source, taking into account their holdover capability?
questions.reference_answer: The 5G system shall support mechanisms to monitor for timing source failure, detect when reference timing signals are no longer viable, and determine if there is degradation of 5G time synchronization. It shall be able to indicate to devices that an alternate time source is available for use, taking into account the holdover capability of the devices.

questions.question: Via how many gateways at minimum must the 5G system support access to the network and its services for authorised UEs and non-3GPP devices in a PIN or CPN, and what must an eRG be able to deliver under operator control?
questions.reference_answer: The 5G system shall be able to support access via at least one gateway (a PIN Element with Gateway Capability or an eRG). Under operator control, an eRG shall be able to efficiently deliver 5G multicast/broadcast services to authorized UEs and non-3GPP devices in the CPN.

questions.question: If a user receives a CCNR recall while that user's CCNR queue as terminating party is being processed, which takes priority, and how do CCNR requests activated by this user rank against those activated by other users?
questions.reference_answer: The CCNR recall shall take priority over the handling of the CCNR queue. Handling of CCNR requests activated by this user shall have priority over the handling of CCNR requests activated by other users on this user.

questions.question: If user B activates Communication Forwarding Unconditional after user A has already activated CCNR on user B, what happens to the CCNR request and what notification is given?
questions.reference_answer: If user B activates CFU after user A has already activated CCNR on user B, the CCNR request shall be cancelled and a notification "CCNR cancelled" shall be sent to user A. As a network option, the CCNR request may instead be suspended until user B deactivates CFU.

questions.question: Which MCX Service prioritization requirements cover establishing dynamically and in real-time the relative priorities of Private and Group Communications with respect to transport and to presentation?
questions.reference_answer: [R-6.7.4-001] (transport, Private vs Group Communications) and [R-6.7.4-002] (presentation, Private vs Group Communications) cover establishing dynamically and in real-time the relative priorities of Private and Group Communications with respect to transport and to presentation.

questions.question: Which enumeration values of ProSeCapability indicate that Layer-2 and Layer-3 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay are supported by the UE?
questions.reference_answer: PROSE_L2_U2N_RELAY indicates Layer-2 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay is supported, and PROSE_L3_U2N_RELAY indicates Layer-3 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay is supported by the UE.

questions.question: In UTRAN, under which conditions must the HS_DSCH_DRX_CELL_FACH_2CYCLE_STATUS variable be set to TRUE, and from which System Information Block must the IE "HS-DSCH DRX in CELL_FACH with second DRX cycle Information" have been received?
questions.reference_answer: HS_DSCH_DRX_CELL_FACH_2CYCLE_STATUS shall be set to TRUE only when the UE supports HS-DSCH DRX operation with second DRX cycle in CELL_FACH state, is in CELL_FACH state, has a dedicated H-RNTI configured, and has received the IEs "HS-DSCH DRX in CELL_FACH Information" and "Common E-DCH system info" from System Information Block Type 5 or 5bis. The IE "HS-DSCH DRX in CELL_FACH with second DRX cycle Information" must have been received from System Information Block Type 22.

questions.question: When the variable HS_DSCH_DRX_CELL_FACH_STATUS is set to TRUE and the E-DCH resource index received from MAC with the CMAC-STATUS primitive is not equal to -1, what must the UE do with timer T321 and with HS-DSCH reception?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall stop the timer T321, if ongoing, and continuously receive HS-DSCH.

questions.question: For 1.28 Mcps TDD CELL_FACH HS-DSCH DRX operation, which inequality on the SFN determines the frames in which the UE receives on downlink, and which IEs signal DRX_cycle and Rx burst?
questions.reference_answer: The inequality is (SFN * H-RNTI + 65536) mod DRX_cycle < Rx_burst. DRX_cycle is signalled by the IE "DRX cycleFACH" and Rx burst is signalled by the IE "Rx burstFACH".

questions.question: When a GPRS MS returns to state GMM-DEREGISTERED from another GMM state, which substate applies if no cell has been found, and which substate applies if no SIM/USIM is present or the inserted SIM/USIM is considered invalid?
