questions.reference_answer: If no cell has been found, the substate is NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, until a cell is found. If no SIM/USIM is present, or the inserted SIM/USIM is considered invalid by the MS, the substate shall be NO-IMSI.

questions.question: With the Final-Unit-Indication AVP carrying Final-Unit-Action TERMINATE, what must the Network Element do when the user has consumed the final granted units, and which CC-Request-Type value must the CCR message use to report the Used-Service-Unit AVP?
questions.reference_answer: When the user has consumed the final granted units, the Network Element shall terminate the service. It shall send a CCR message with CC-Request-Type AVP set to UPDATE_REQUEST and report the Used-Service-Unit AVP for the service that has terminated.

questions.question: Which AVP does the server include in the CCA to indicate that quota consumption shall stop after an idle period, is that idle period included in the reported usage, and when does quota consumption resume?
questions.reference_answer: The server includes the Quota-Consumption-Time AVP in the CCA. Yes, the idle period equal to the Quota Consumption Time is included in the reported usage. Quota consumption resumes on receipt of a further packet belonging to the service data flow.

questions.question: On sending a 401 Unauthorized response to an unprotected REGISTER request with SIP digest as the security mechanism, which header field parameters must the S-CSCF transport in each WWW-Authenticate header field, and what value must qop take if it is not provided in the authentication vector?
questions.reference_answer: The WWW-Authenticate header field must transport a protection domain in the "realm" parameter, a "nonce" parameter generated by the S-CSCF, an "algorithm" parameter, and a "qop" parameter. If the qop value is not provided in the authentication vector, it shall contain the value "auth".

questions.question: With SIP digest as the security mechanism, if the REGISTER request carrying the authentication challenge response does not match the expected request and the integrity-protected header field parameter is set to tls-yes, which two alternatives may the S-CSCF choose, and may it update the registration state?
questions.reference_answer: The S-CSCF may either send a 403 (Forbidden) response to the UE (considering the authentication attempt failed, without updating the registration state), or rechallenge the user by issuing a 401 (Unauthorized) response with a fresh challenge. It shall not update the registration state of the subscriber in the 403 case.

questions.question: With IMS AKA as the security mechanism, if the S-CSCF receives a REGISTER request with integrity-protected set to yes whose public and private user identities do not match any registered user, which response must it send when it does not support S-CSCF restoration procedures?
questions.reference_answer: The S-CSCF shall respond with a 500 (Server Internal Error) response to the UE.

questions.question: When the UE disables its N1 mode capability for non-3GPP access, what must the UE NAS layer refrain from doing, and what restriction applies to a UE operating in single-registration mode regarding transferring PDN connections?
questions.reference_answer: The UE NAS layer shall not initiate any 5GS NAS procedures towards the network over non-3GPP access. A UE operating in single-registration mode shall not transfer any PDN connection to a non-3GPP access network connected to the 5GCN.

questions.question: Which conditions permit closure of the ePDG-CDR under the "End of IP-CAN bearer within the ePDG" trigger, and which OAM&P partial record reasons are covered?
questions.reference_answer: Under "End of IP-CAN bearer within the ePDG", closure is permitted for termination of the IP-CAN bearer, any abnormal release, and inter serving node change. OAM&P Partial Record Reasons cover data volume limit, time (duration) limit, maximum number of charging condition changes (QoS/tariff time change), and management intervention.

questions.question: For management based MDT with several PLMNs supported in the RAN, which UEs may the eNB select, and what condition on pLMNTarget and selectedPLMN-Identity must hold?
questions.reference_answer: The eNB shall only select UEs whose selected UE satisfies the MDT UE selection criteria (capability condition), where pLMNTarget = selectedPLMN-Identity that the UE includes in the RRCConnectionSetupComplete message.

questions.question: In the abnormal case where a DETACH REQUEST carries an EMM cause value not otherwise treated and the Detach type IE indicates re-attach not required, what must the UE delete, what update status must it set, and which timer must it start?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall delete any GUTI, TAI list, last visited registered TAI, list of equivalent PLMNs, and KSI, shall set the update status to EU2 NOT UPDATED, and shall start timer T3402.

questions.question: For a tracking area updating request for access to RLOS that is not accepted by the network, what must the UE do when the reject action involves attempting to select GERAN or UTRAN radio access technology or disabling the E-UTRAN capability?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall skip the action for as long as access to RLOS is still needed.

questions.question: When SMS services are not accepted in a tracking area update, which timer must the UE stop, what value caps the tracking area updating attempt counter, and which timer must it start when the counter is less than 5?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall stop timer T3430. The tracking area updating attempt counter is capped at 5. If the counter is less than 5, the UE shall start timer T3411.

questions.question: How does the controlling MCVideo function determine that a request with the alert-ind element set to false is an authorised MCVideo emergency alert cancellation request, and which element of the ruleset in the MCVideo user profile does it check?
questions.reference_answer: If the <allow-cancel-emergency-alert> element of the <ruleset> element of the MCVideo user profile document identified by the MCVideo ID of the calling user is set to "true", the controlling MCVideo function considers the request an authorised MCVideo emergency alert cancellation request; the function checks the <allow-cancel-emergency-alert> element.

questions.question: If the gNB-CU-UP receives a BEARER CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST containing an E-UTRAN QoS IE for a GBR QoS DRB but the GBR QoS Information IE is not present, how must it report that DRB and in which list of the response?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB-CU-UP shall report the establishment of the corresponding DRB as failed, with an appropriate cause value, in the DRB Failed List IE of the BEARER CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message.

questions.question: When the gNB-CU-UP cannot perform any of the requested bearer context modifications or cannot handle SCG with the indicated activated or deactivated status, with which message must it respond?
questions.reference_answer: It shall respond with a BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION FAILURE message and an appropriate cause value.

questions.question: For MR-DC with 5GC, what must the SN assume for SCG (re)selection when roaming and access restriction information is not available at the SN, and over which protocol must the MN convey the latest information?
questions.reference_answer: The SN shall assume there is no restriction for SCG (re)selection. The MN must convey the latest roaming and access restriction information to the SN via XnAP messages.

questions.question: Under which condition may the E-UTRAN/Satellite E-UTRAN Inter-frequency Network Measurement Results TLV object be used, and how must the frequency value be coded?
questions.reference_answer: This TLV object shall be used only if the service "extended EARFCN" is available in the USIM Service Table. The frequency value shall be coded as the ARFCN-ValueEUTRA-v9e0 as defined in TS 36.331.

questions.question: For the general result "Terminal currently unable to process" on a UICC More Data request, which additional information values are defined in the first byte, and how must the UICC interpret all other values?
questions.reference_answer: The defined additional information values are: '00' No specific cause can be given, '01' No more data available, '02' Pending data deleted by the ME, '03' Incorrect data index provided by the UICC. All other values shall be interpreted by the UICC as '00'.

questions.question: For charging correlation on a session transferred due to STN-SR, which header field parameter must the SCC AS include in the P-Charging-Vector header field of SIP 1xx and 2xx responses, and what must it contain?
questions.reference_answer: The SCC AS shall include the "related-icid" header field parameter, containing the ICID value of the source access leg, in the P-Charging-Vector header field.

questions.question: On reception of a BROADCAST SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message, what must the NG-RAN node stop and release, and what must the AMF transfer transparently to the MB-SMF on receiving the response?
questions.reference_answer: The NG-RAN node shall stop broadcasting and release all MBS session resources associated with the broadcast session. On receiving the BROADCAST SESSION RELEASE RESPONSE message, the AMF shall transfer transparently the Broadcast Session Release Response Transfer IE, if available, to the MB-SMF.

questions.question: In the NGAP Uplink RAN Status Transfer procedure, which three IEs must the source NG-RAN node include within the DRBs Subject to Status Transfer List IE for each DRB where PDCP-SN and HFN status preservation applies?
questions.reference_answer: The source NG-RAN node shall include the DRB ID IE, the UL COUNT Value IE, and the DL COUNT Value IE within the DRBs Subject to Status Transfer List IE.

questions.question: On receiving the DOWNLINK RAN STATUS TRANSFER message, which target NG-RAN node must ignore the information it carries, and what constraint applies to delivering uplink packets whose PDCP-SN is lower than the UL Count Value IE?
questions.reference_answer: The target NG-RAN node using Full Configuration for this handover shall ignore the information received in the DOWNLINK RAN STATUS TRANSFER message. For each DRB in the DRBs Subject to Status Transfer List IE, the target NG-RAN node shall not deliver any uplink packet with a PDCP-SN lower than the value of the UL Count Value IE.

questions.question: In the F1AP Broadcast Context Setup procedure, what must the gNB-DU take into account when the MBS Service Area IE is included, and in which list must successfully established MRBs be reported?
questions.reference_answer: If the MBS Service Area IE is included, the gNB-DU shall take this information into account for shared F1-U tunnel assignment. Successfully established MRBs shall be reported in the Broadcast MRB Setup List IE.

questions.question: In the Multicast Distribution Setup procedure, what must the MULTICAST DISTRIBUTION SETUP REQUEST contain, and what must the MBS Multicast F1-U Context Descriptor IE indicate about how shared F1-U tunnels are established?
questions.reference_answer: The MULTICAST DISTRIBUTION SETUP REQUEST shall contain F1-U TNL information for the MRBs accepted for the MBS Session by the gNB-DU. The MBS Multicast F1-U Context Descriptor IE must indicate whether the shared F1-U tunnel(s) for the MRB(s) are established on a per NR CGI basis, per MBS Area Session ID basis, or for a ptp MRB leg.

questions.question: When a MULTICAST CONTEXT NOTIFICATION INDICATION contains the MBS Multicast Configuration Notification IE within the Multicast DU to CU RRC Information IE, what must the gNB-CU replace, and with which message must it respond if it can execute the requested functions?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB-CU shall replace, for the respective cell, the Multicast Configuration Information previously received with the information received in the MBS Multicast Configuration Notification IE. If it can execute the requested functions, it shall respond with the MULTICAST CONTEXT NOTIFICATION CONFIRM message.

questions.question: How must the UE set the ul-DCCH-MessageEUTRA when there is a need to transfer dedicated LTE information related to V2X sidelink communications in the ULInformationTransferIRAT message?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall set the ul-DCCH-MessageEUTRA to include the V2X sidelink communication information to be transferred (e.g. the E-UTRA RRC MeasurementReport message, the E-UTRA RRC SidelinkUEInformation message, or the E-UTRA RRC UEAssistanceInformation message).

questions.question: In (NG)EN-DC, what failureType must the UE set when SCGFailureInformationNR transmission is triggered by T310 expiry, and how must failureType and failureType-v1610 be set for T312 expiry?
questions.reference_answer: For T310 expiry, the UE shall set failureType as t310-Expiry. For T312 expiry, the UE shall set failureType as any value and set failureType-v1610 as t312-Expiry.

questions.question: When setting the SCGFailureInformationEUTRA message, how must the UE order the best measured cells in measResultFreqListMRDC, and which measurement quantity takes precedence for ordering?
questions.reference_answer: The best cell is listed first, using RSRP to order if RSRP measurement results are available for cells on that frequency, otherwise RSRQ, otherwise SINR. RSRP takes precedence for ordering.

questions.question: If the S-NODE RELEASE REQUEST message refers to a context that does not exist, what must the S-NG-RAN node do, and how must the M-NG-RAN node regard the UE resources when it omitted the S-NG-RAN node UE XnAP ID IE?
questions.reference_answer: The S-NG-RAN node shall ignore the message. When the M-NG-RAN node omitted the S-NG-RAN node UE XnAP ID IE, it shall regard the resources for the UE at the S-NG-RAN node as being fully released.

questions.question: If the XN SETUP FAILURE message includes the Time To Wait IE, what must the initiating NG-RAN node do before reinitiating the Xn Setup procedure towards the same node?
questions.reference_answer: The initiating NG-RAN node1 shall wait at least for the indicated time before reinitiating the Xn Setup procedure towards the same NG-RAN node2.

questions.question: When NG-RAN node2 cannot accept an NG-RAN node Configuration Update, which failure message must it send, and with which configuration data must both nodes continue to operate the Xn interface?
questions.reference_answer: It shall respond with the NG-RAN NODE CONFIGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message with an appropriate cause value. Both nodes shall continue to operate the Xn interface with their existing configuration data.

questions.question: For mobile IAB cells, which part of the NR Cell Identity may be reconfigured by the F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU on an NCI collision, and to what must the value change of cellLocalId be indicated?
questions.reference_answer: The F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU may reconfigure the cellLocalId part of the NCI. The value change of cellLocalId(s) shall be indicated to the OAM system of the mobile IAB-DU.

questions.question: For two redundant PDU Sessions in NG-RAN, what must the RAN ensure regarding the resources of the data radio bearers, and what happens if the RAN cannot satisfy the disjoint user plane requirement?
questions.reference_answer: The RAN shall ensure that the resources of the data radio bearers for the two redundant PDU sessions are isolated. If the RAN cannot satisfy the disjoint user plane requirement, the redundant PDU sessions may be kept or not kept according to the RAN local configuration.

questions.question: For Inter-system Automatic Neighbour Cell Relation, what does the Inter Frequency Search list of each cell contain, and what does the UE report about detected cells in the target system?
questions.reference_answer: The Inter Frequency Search list of each cell contains all frequencies that shall be searched. The UE reports the PCI and carrier frequency of the detected cells in the target system.

questions.question: For a PDU Session associated with the emergency DNN, what traffic must the UPF block, and may the UE request a second emergency PDU Session over another Access Type?
questions.reference_answer: The UPF shall block any traffic that is not from or to addresses of network functions (e.g. P-CSCF) providing Emergency Services. No, if there is already an emergency PDU Session over a given Access Type, the UE shall not request another emergency PDU Session over any Access Type, except for handing over the existing one to the other Access Type.

questions.question: For secondary DN authentication and authorization in the EPS interworking case, which combined network function must serve DNNs requiring secondary authentication by a DN-AAA server, and is UE support of EAP-based secondary authentication over EPC mandatory?
questions.reference_answer: An SMF+PGW-C shall be used to serve DNN(s) requiring secondary authentication/authorization by a DN-AAA server. No, it is optional for the UE to support EAP-based secondary authentication and authorization by DN-AAA over EPC.

questions.question: For interworking without N26 interface, what must the AMF subscribe to on behalf of the SCEF+NEF during mobility from 5GS to EPS so that the SCEF+NEF can configure the monitoring request to the new MME?
questions.reference_answer: The AMF shall subscribe on behalf of the SCEF+NEF for UDM+HSS notification of MME ID.

questions.question: When the SGW receives a GTP-U PDU for which no Bearer context exists, what must it discard and return to the originating node, and why should previously used TEID values not be immediately reused after an SGW restart?
questions.reference_answer: The SGW shall discard the GTP-U PDU and return a GTP error indication to the originating node (the PGW, the eNodeB, the S4-SGSN, or the RNC if Direct Tunnel is established). Previously used TEID values should not be immediately reused after an SGW restart in order to avoid inconsistent TEID allocation throughout the network.

questions.question: When an SGW-U detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SGW-C has restarted, which contexts must it delete, and what exception applies to sending an Error indication message when restoration of PDN connections is supported?
questions.reference_answer: The SGW-U shall delete all its Sx session contexts affected by the restart. If restoration of PDN connections after an SGW failure is supported, the SGW-U shall not send an Error indication message for a configurable period after the restart in the SGW-C.

questions.question: If F-TEID allocation is performed in the SGW-U, what must the SGW-U ensure about previously used F-TEID values after a restart, and for what two reasons?
questions.reference_answer: The SGW-U shall ensure that previously used F-TEID values are not immediately reused after an SGW-U restart, in order to avoid inconsistent TEID allocation throughout the network and to enable the restoration of Sx sessions affected by the failure.

questions.question: When an IP-CAN bearer is modified such that the requested QoS falls outside the previously authorized limits, what must the PCEF verify, and what must it do if it lacks sufficient information to authorize the modification?
questions.reference_answer: The PCEF shall verify the authorization of the IP-CAN bearer modification. If it does not have sufficient information to authorize the request, the PCEF shall send an authorization request to the PCRF.

questions.question: In the SLF on UE invite flow, what must the I-CSCF do first if the user identity in the INVITE request is an E.164 number in SIP URI with the user=phone parameter, before sending the DX_SLF_QUERY?
questions.reference_answer: The I-CSCF shall first translate the E.164 number into the Tel: URI format (per IETF RFC 3966) before sending the DX_SLF_QUERY to the SLF.

questions.question: To reduce network load from periodic RAU signalling, on what basis does the SGSN allocate the periodic RAU timer value to the UE during Attach and RAU procedures?
questions.reference_answer: The SGSN allocates the periodic RAU timer value based on VPLMN operator policy, low access priority indication from the MS, the periodic RAU/TAU timer value requested by the MS, and subscription information received from the HSS.

questions.question: At each PDP Context Request, what determines whether SCEF based delivery or Gi/SGi based delivery is used for Non-IP data, and what connection is established towards the selected SCEF?
questions.reference_answer: An indication associated with the used APN determines if SCEF based delivery or Gi/SGi based delivery is used. A T6b connection (also known as an "SCEF Connection") is established towards the selected SCEF.

questions.question: For which access is the LIPA function available, and what must the PDN GW/GGSN reject regarding secondary PDP context on the LIPA PDN connection?
questions.reference_answer: LIPA is available for UTRAN access only. The PDN GW/GGSN shall reject any MS initiated Secondary PDP Context Activation Procedure or any PDP Context Modification Procedure that is for the LIPA PDN Connection.

questions.question: In GW initiated IP-CAN Session termination for GTP, when must the GGSN set the Teardown Indicator in the Delete PDP Context Request, and what does that indicate?
questions.reference_answer: The GGSN shall set the Teardown Indicator in the Delete PDP Context Request message when this is not the deletion of the last PDP Context for the IP Address, to indicate that all PDP contexts sharing that same IP address shall also be deactivated.

questions.question: For 3GPP GTP-based access, if a QCI assigned to a PCC or QoS rule is not supported by all RATs of the IP-CAN, which event trigger must the PCRF subscribe to and what must it do at inter-RAT mobility?
questions.reference_answer: The PCRF shall subscribe to the 'RAT change' event trigger. At inter-RAT mobility, the PCRF shall modify those PCC/QoS rules in the PCEF/BBERF to align their QCI values with those supported by the current RAT.

questions.question: What must a UE configured for eCall Only Mode do regarding its EMM state and network signalling, and under what circumstances may it instigate Mobility Management and Connection Management procedures?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall remain in EMM-DEREGISTERED state, camp on a network cell when available, but refrain from any Mobility Management or other signalling with the network. It may instigate Mobility Management and Connection Management procedures in order to establish, maintain and release an eCall Over IMS session or a session to a non-emergency MSISDN/URI configured in the UICC for test and/or terminal reconfiguration services.

questions.question: When an emergency attached UE's periodic TAU update timer expires, what must the UE do instead of initiating a periodic TAU procedure, and what timer does the MME run for such UEs?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall not initiate a periodic TAU procedure but shall enter EMM-DEREGISTERED state. The MME runs a mobile reachable timer with a similar value to the UE's periodic TAU timer for such UEs.

questions.question: In the roaming OAuth 2.0 model for service access authorization, which NRF acts as the authorization server that authenticates the NF Service Consumer, and which NRF generates the access token?
questions.reference_answer: The visited Network Repository Function (vNRF) shall be the OAuth 2.0 Authorization server for vPLMN and authenticates the NF Service Consumer. The home Network Repository Function (hNRF) shall be OAuth 2.0 Authorization server for hPLMN and generates the access token.

questions.question: When a management service consumer resides outside the 3GPP operator's trust domain, which protocol must be used for mutual authentication with the management service producer, and what two credential options are permitted?
questions.reference_answer: TLS shall be used for mutual authentication. The two permitted credential options are: client and server certificates with the profiles given in TS 33.310 clause 6.1.3a, or pre-shared keys following RFC 5489 (TLS 1.2) / RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3).

questions.question: How must the CC-POI interpret the IP address and UDP port number received as target identifiers in the LI_T3 ActivateTask when the TriggerScope value is Unidirectional?
questions.reference_answer: When TriggerScope is "Unidirectional", the IP address and UDP port number received as target identifiers in the LI_T3 ActivateTask shall match the destination IP address and UDP port number of the media packets.

questions.question: How must the UE derive KeNB* at handover when the NCC value received in the HO Command equals the NCC associated with the currently active KeNB, and which target cell parameters are used?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall derive the KeNB* from the currently active KeNB and the target PCI and its frequency EARFCN-DL, using the function defined in Annex A.5.

questions.question: Once NAS integrity has been activated, may the UE or MME accept NAS messages without integrity protection, and for which integrity protection algorithm is replay protection not activated?
questions.reference_answer: No, once NAS integrity has been activated, NAS messages without integrity protection shall not be accepted by the UE or MME. Replay protection is not activated when the selected integrity protection algorithm is EIA0.

questions.question: Which protocol must be supported to provide certificate lifecycle management for SEGs, and must all SEGs and SEG CAs support initial enrolment and key update via that protocol before the certificate expires?
questions.reference_answer: Certificate Management Protocol v2 (CMPv2) shall be the supported protocol to provide certificate lifecycle management for SEGs. Yes, all SEGs and SEG CAs shall support initial enrolment and key update via CMPv2 before the certificate expires.

questions.question: In NDS/AF CRL management, why is the use of delta CRLs not allowed, and must the CRL issuer issue a CRL even when there are no revoked certificates?
questions.reference_answer: The use of delta CRLs is not allowed because of possible interoperability problems and because in the NDS/AF environment the full CRL is not expected to grow too large. Yes, the CRL issuer shall issue a CRL also in cases where there are no revoked certificates.

questions.question: In the UTRAN E-RAB Release Indication procedure initiated by the eNB, what must the E-RAB RELEASE INDICATION message contain at minimum, and what must the MME normally initiate upon reception?
questions.reference_answer: The E-RAB RELEASE INDICATION message shall contain at least one E-RAB released at the eNB, in the E-RAB Released List IE. Upon reception, the MME shall normally initiate the appropriate release procedure on the core network side for the identified E-RABs.

questions.question: When the eNB receives an INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST containing an E-RAB Level QoS Parameters IE whose QCI indicates a GBR bearer but with no GBR QoS Information IE, how must the eNB treat the establishment of that E-RAB?
questions.reference_answer: The eNB shall consider the establishment of the corresponding E-RAB as failed.

questions.question: If the UE is unable to comply with part of the configuration in an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message, which configuration must it continue using, and which procedure must it initiate when security has already been activated?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall continue using the configuration used prior to the reception of the RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. If security has already been activated, the UE shall initiate the connection re-establishment procedure.

questions.question: What set of PC5 signalling protocol cause values can a target UE include in a PROSE DIRECT LINK MODIFICATION REJECT message, and under what condition must it use cause #6?
questions.reference_answer: The PROSE DIRECT LINK MODIFICATION REJECT message contains a PC5 signalling protocol cause IE set to one of: #5 lack of resources for 5G ProSe direct link, #6 required service not allowed, #12 security policy not aligned, #16 lack of local capabilities, #20 Failure from 5G ProSe end UE, #23 MAC address not unique, #24 relay UE is not selected for link setup with integrated discovery, or #111 protocol error, unspecified. The target UE shall use cause #6 "required service not allowed" if it is not allowed to accept the request, e.g. because the ProSe application to be added is not allowed per operator policy or configuration parameters for ProSe communication over PC5.

questions.question: What must the SRNC include in a UE MEASUREMENT INITIATION RESPONSE message if the DRNC allowed parameter modification and the SRNC changed the requested measurement parameters?
questions.reference_answer: The UE MEASUREMENT INITIATION RESPONSE message shall include the same Measurement ID used in the corresponding UE MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST message. If the DRNC allowed parameter modification and the SRNC modified either the Measurement Filter Coefficient IE or the UE Measurement Report Characteristics IE, the SRNC shall include the modified value(s) in the UE MEASUREMENT INITIATION RESPONSE message.

questions.question: What five pieces of information must a BSS supply when sending a LOAD INDICATION message, and what should a receiving BSS do if the message arrives without the Resource situation information element?
questions.reference_answer: The BSS shall send the LOAD INDICATION message to the MSC with the Cell Identifier of the affected cell, a Time indication (validity period of the information), a Cell identifier list of the affected neighbour cells, the Resource situation information (total and currently available channels per type), and a Cause indicating the reason for sending the message. If the target BSS receives a LOAD INDICATION message without the Resource situation information element, that means the indicated cell cannot perform incoming handover requests, and the receiving BSS may stop the whole handover traffic to that cell.

questions.question: Under which three conditions must the network send back an A ROUTING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message from the MS, and what must it contain if Receive N-PDU Numbers were included in the accept message?
questions.reference_answer: A ROUTING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message shall be returned to the network if the ROUTING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message contains any of: a P-TMSI and/or a TMSI; Receive N-PDU Numbers; or a request for the provision of Inter RAT handover information. If Receive N-PDU Numbers were included, the Receive N-PDU Numbers that are valid in the MS shall be included in the ROUTING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message, and if Inter RAT handover information was requested, the message shall include the Inter RAT handover information IE as applicable.

questions.question: What information must the Source HNB provide to the Target HNB within the RANAP ENHANCED RELOCATION INFORMATION REQUEST message to support seamless Iu-UP operation, and what must the Target HNB refrain from doing after receiving it?
questions.reference_answer: The Source HNB shall provide the Target HNB, within the RANAP ENHANCED RELOCATION INFORMATION REQUEST message, with the CS Iu-UP control information needed to allocate IuUP instances for RABs operated in support mode, plus the latest CS Iu-UP user-data frame numbers for uplink and downlink for all CS RABs operated in support mode whose numbering is time-based, together with the UL/DL packet time difference. After receiving this message, the Target HNB shall use this information to establish Iu-UP instances but shall not initiate any Iu-UP procedure and shall ignore incoming Iu-UP control frames.

questions.question: Under what condition should the MS reply with cause #48 in a SECONDARY PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION REJECT message, and what must the network do upon receiving that message?
questions.reference_answer: The MS should reply with the REQUEST SECONDARY PDP CONTEXT ACTIVATION REJECT message using cause #48 "request rejected, Bearer Control Mode violation" if the previously negotiated Bearer Control Mode is 'MS-only'. Upon receiving this reject message, the network shall stop timer T3385 and enter state PDP-INACTIVE.

questions.question: If the SRS Resource Trigger IE is included in a POSITIONING ACTIVATION REQUEST for aperiodic UL SRS, what must the gNB-DU do with it, and how does the gNB-DU treat the Activation Time IE when present?
questions.reference_answer: For aperiodic UL SRS, if the SRS Resource Trigger IE is included in the POSITIONING ACTIVATION REQUEST message, the gNB-DU shall take the value of this IE into account when triggering aperiodic SRS transmission by the UE. If the Activation Time IE is included, the gNB-DU shall take the indicated value as the requested time for activation of the UE's SRS transmission.

questions.question: When must the MS indicate its selected downlink Coverage Class using the field carried in an EC PACKET CHANNEL REQUEST message, and what does the network do with that indicated value?
questions.reference_answer: The MS shall indicate the selected downlink Coverage Class using the Selected DL Coverage Class field in the EC Packet Channel Request message in advance of the next occurrence of its paging group (or the corresponding EC-PICH block, if EC Paging Indication Channel monitoring is supported), and at least whenever the selected downlink CC is higher than the last one communicated, is CC1 after CC4 was last communicated, or the MS has completed an uplink data transfer in a cell not supporting EC-GSM-IoT since it last communicated a downlink CC. The network shall then apply the indicated downlink Coverage Class on EC-PCH messages sent to that MS.

questions.question: Under what circumstance does the delivery of the MDFCellSiteReport record use an IRI REPORT rather than the location field of an ordinary IRI message, and what field must MDF2 set in the PDU header in that case?
questions.reference_answer: The MDF2 shall use an IRI message containing the MDFCellSiteReport record to convey cell site information and cell radio related information when that information is retrieved asynchronously with respect to the sending of the IRI message that caused the retrieval, and this IRI REPORT is allocated the same CIN, if any, as the IRI message that triggered the retrieval. In generating this IRI message, MDF2 shall set the Payload Direction field in the PDU header to "not applicable" (Direction Value 5).

questions.question: Under what two algorithm-mismatch conditions must the S-NG-RAN node reject the modification procedure with an S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUEST REJECT message?
questions.reference_answer: The S-NG-RAN node shall reject the procedure using the S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUEST REJECT message if the UE's supported encryption algorithms (from the NR Encryption Algorithms IE, plus the mandated NEA0 support) do not match any algorithm in the S-NG-RAN node's configured list of allowed encryption algorithms, and likewise if the UE's supported integrity protection algorithms (from the NR Integrity Protection Algorithms IE) do not match any algorithm in the configured list of allowed integrity protection algorithms.

questions.question: In the pre-configured measurement gap procedure, at what step does the serving gNB send a MEASUREMENT PRECONFIGURATION CONFIRM message to the LMF, and what must have happened at the UE just before that?
questions.reference_answer: The gNB sends the NRPPa MEASUREMENT PRECONFIGURATION CONFIRM message to the LMF to indicate the success of the pre-configuration only after the UE has sent an RRC Reconfiguration Complete message to the gNB, confirming its reception of the pre-configured measurement gap configuration(s) that the gNB had earlier provided based on the LMF's assistance information and the UE's capability.

questions.question: A customer registers a new supplementary-service password but enters the old password incorrectly for the fourth consecutive time. What must the network do?
questions.reference_answer: If the subscriber enters an incorrect password more than three consecutive times, all control procedures related to the use of the password are made impossible until the service provider instructs the network to again accept password-related requests from that subscriber. (A single incorrect entry is simply rejected and the subscriber notified, with the old password left unchanged.)

questions.question: An incoming PSTN call arrives on the Single Numbering Scheme with no Bearer Capability information element attached, and the network needs to apply supplementary services to it. Which basic service must the network fall back to, and how is it chosen?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall handle the call, for supplementary-service purposes, based on a "default basic service". If the subscriber has a subscription to telephony, the network shall use telephony as the default basic service; if not, the HLR shall choose a basic service from the set of services provisioned to the subscriber as the default. When such a call is subsequently call-forwarded, no modifications or additions may be made to the original BC-IE information, whether or not it was present.

questions.question: A PLMN offers CLIP but has chosen not to support CLIR. What must the operator ensure about a subscriber's line identity being shown to the called party?
questions.reference_answer: A PLMN that supports CLIP shall also support CLIR. If a PLMN does not support CLIR, it shall ensure that the calling subscriber's line identity is not displayed to the called party unless the called party has CLIR override capability (the equivalent rule applies to CoLP/CoLR for the connected line identity).

questions.question: An operator wants to identify a stolen handset reported by a customer. What must be true of the IMEI's composition to let the operator trace the equipment back to its origin of production, and what protects against manual transcription errors when it is read out at a customer care desk?
questions.reference_answer: The IMEI shall directly or indirectly contain all the information necessary for the network operator to trace the equipment, through its administrative system, back to its origin of production, and each individual mobile equipment must be separately identifiable by its IMEI. The IMEI is complemented by a check digit specifically to avoid manual transmission errors (e.g. when customers register stolen MEs at a customer care desk); the check digit is not itself part of the digits transmitted at IMEI check occasions and is not applied to the Software Version Number.

questions.question: The EIR reports back that a UE's IMEI is on the prohibited list during an access attempt. What must the network do with that access attempt or ongoing call, what must it never do, and what indication is given to the user?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall terminate the access attempt or ongoing call, and shall give the user an indication of "illegal ME". This is treated as equivalent to an authentication failure, so any call, IMS session establishment, or location updating is forbidden for that MS and it cannot answer paging; it is only allowed to perform emergency calls. Emergency calls must never be terminated as a result of the IMEI check procedure.

questions.question: A handset was previously network-personalised to network code N1 with subscriber profile SP1 (giving N1-SP1). Someone tries to add personalisation for network code N2 with profile SP2. Is that allowed, and why?
questions.reference_answer: No. Before any changes are made to existing personalisation data, it must be checked that the category to be personalised is not currently activated and that the new codes to be stored are a subset of the existing codes. Since N2-SP2 is not a subset of the existing N1-SP1 codes, it cannot be added; only additional codes that are subsets of what is already stored (e.g. more SP codes under N1) are permitted, and if the category is active it must first be de-personalised using the appropriate Control Key.

questions.question: A new SIM is inserted into an ME that has network-subset personalisation enabled, and the SIM's network subset code group does not match what is stored in the ME. What must the ME do, and what must the ME be able to store to support this feature?
questions.reference_answer: If no match is found between the SIM's network subset code group and the value(s) stored in the ME, the ME shall go into emergency-calls-only mode. To support the feature, the ME shall have storage for the network subset personalisation indicator, the network subset code group(s), and the Network Subset Control Key (NSCK) needed to de-personalise it.

questions.question: During the SIM/USIM personalisation process for an ME that is to be personalised to more than one SIM/USIM, what must happen if any of the pre-personalisation checks in clause 13 fail, and what single value governs both single and multiple SIM/USIM personalisation?
questions.reference_answer: If any of the pre-personalisation checks fail, the personalisation process shall be terminated. A single value of the Personalisation Control Key (PCK) shall be used for both single and multiple SIM/USIM personalisation, and it is stored in the ME once all checks pass, after which the SIM/USIM personalisation indicator is set to "on".

questions.question: A phone corporate-personalised via GID1/GID2 is given a SIM whose GID2 code does not match the corporate code group stored in the ME. What does the ME do, and what must it be able to store to support corporate personalisation?
questions.reference_answer: If the GID2-based corporate code group read from the SIM does not match the code group(s) stored in the ME, the ME shall go into emergency-calls-only mode. To support corporate personalisation, the ME must have storage for the corporate personalisation indicator, a list of corporate code group(s), and the Corporate Control Key (CCK) needed to de-personalise it.

questions.question: A subscriber's Accumulated Call Meter (ACM) reaches its ACMmax limit while a chargeable call is already in progress. What happens to that call, and can the subscriber then place a new outgoing call?
questions.reference_answer: Once ACMmax is valid and the ACM becomes equal to or exceeds it, all calls in progress that are chargeable to the user shall be terminated by the ME once the chargeable interval determined by the CAI has elapsed, and the user must be given an appropriate indication of why the call was terminated. After that, no outgoing calls can be placed except emergency calls; an incoming call that subsequently receives a non-zero CAI shall likewise be terminated by the ME with an indication to the user.

questions.question: The SIM/USIM only lets the Accumulated Call Meter (ACM) be incremented. Under what condition can it be reset, and what security reason motivates this restriction?
questions.reference_answer: Resetting of the ACM shall only be possible after presentation of PIN2. For security reasons, the SIM/USIM only allows the ACM value to be incremented, never decremented, which prevents a user from covertly reducing the recorded accumulated charge.

questions.question: During SCUDIF mode modification (e.g. Audio to Video) the network sends a Facility message carrying new CAI parameter values. What must the MS do with CDUR and the CCM once it receives those new values?
questions.reference_answer: On receipt of new CAI values triggered by a SCUDIF-based service change, the MS shall reset CDUR and continue incrementing the CCM using the new CAI parameters; the MS shall add initial units to the CCM and measure further units on a time basis using those new values.

questions.question: A user wants to set a single common password for all applicable supplementary services rather than one specific service. Which MMI procedure must the UE support for this, and must the UE also support the alternative form that starts with a double asterisk?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall support the registration procedure "* 03 ** OLD_PASSWORD * NEW_PASSWORD * NEW_PASSWORD #" (with the ZZ service code omitted for a common password), and it shall also support the alternative procedure "** 03 ** OLD_PASSWORD * NEW_PASSWORD * NEW_PASSWORD #".

questions.question: A SIM returns a "technical problem with no diagnostic given" status code in response to an ENVELOPE (SMS-PP DOWNLOAD) command. Must the UE indicate this to the user, and why does this case differ from the other mandatory status indications?
questions.reference_answer: No indication shall be given to the user in this case, because the code is not related to a user action (it is returned in response to a network-triggered ENVELOPE command such as SMS-PP DOWNLOAD or CELL BROADCAST DOWNLOAD), unlike other mandatory status indications (e.g. memory problem, access conditions not fulfilled, CHV verification failure) which must always be shown to the user since they relate directly to something the user did.

questions.question: An HPLMN wants a VPLMN to stop fraud-information-gathering monitoring on a subscriber whose activity is already ongoing and being monitored. What must the VPLMN do once it receives that request, and can the subscriber themselves detect that they were being monitored?
questions.reference_answer: The VPLMN shall immediately cease sending information on that activity to the HPLMN once it receives the request to stop monitoring. Subscribers upon whom fraud information gathering has been set shall not be able to determine this by interrogating the network, nor by observing changes to normal call set-up times, speech quality, or general transmission characteristics.

questions.question: A VPLMN has already reached its maximum number of subscribers it can monitor for Fraud Information Gathering. What must it do with further monitoring requests from HPLMNs, and until when does that restriction last?
questions.reference_answer: The VPLMN shall reject requests for monitoring of subscribers from HPLMNs until the number of monitored subscribers decreases below its upper limit; the same applies per-HPLMN if the VPLMN also enforces a per-HPLMN monitoring limit.

questions.question: Fraud Information Gathering is running for a long call. Besides the information sent at the start and end of the call, what else must the VPLMN send to the HPLMN, and who alone controls activating and deactivating this monitoring?
questions.reference_answer: For long calls, the VPLMN shall also send partial call information to the HPLMN a certain time (e.g. 15 minutes) after the call has begun, in addition to the call information sent at the start and end of all calls and on invocation of supplementary services. Fraud information gathering is controlled by the HPLMN and can only be activated and deactivated by the HPLMN.

questions.question: A network wants to apply access control that differentiates between the CS and PS domains during a state of emergency. Is this differentiation required to be possible, and is it intended that access control of this kind be used under normal operating conditions?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it should be possible to differentiate access control between the CS and PS domains (details specified in TS 23.122 and TS 25.304, though not all RATs need support this). It is not intended that access control be used under normal operating conditions; it exists to let the operator prevent overload of the access channel under critical conditions such as states of emergency or a co-located PLMN failure.

questions.question: A UE is rejected during registration due to a "temporary" PLMN restriction, with the reject cause indicating it should search for a suitable cell in the same PLMN. What must the UE do with the tracking area or location area identity, and what counts as a suitable cell afterward?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall store the tracking area identity or location area identity in the list of "5GS forbidden TAs" or "forbidden LAs for roaming" respectively, and shall then search for a suitable cell in the same PLMN. A suitable cell belongs to a different TA or LA that is not in that forbidden list; note that when a TA supports multiple systems, a cell may be suitable for one system while not being suitable for another.

questions.question: A network is running both ACDC and the third-party-server traffic control feature at the same time, and ACDC allows a given piece of UE traffic. Which of the two features takes precedence for that traffic, and must the third-party-server control feature apply to connections that already exist as well as new ones?
questions.reference_answer: The third-party-server traffic control feature shall take precedence over ACDC to control traffic from applications in the UE, but only when that traffic is already allowed by ACDC. The feature shall be applicable both to new connections being set up and to existing connections from the UE towards the application on the third-party server or the third-party server itself.

questions.question: The HPLMN triggers Immediate Service Termination for a subscriber, but that subscriber has no activities at all in the VPLMN that received the command. What must the VPLMN do?
questions.reference_answer: The VPLMN shall inform the HPLMN that the specified subscriber has no activities in the VPLMN. (Where the subscriber does have activity, the VPLMN must instead confirm receipt of the IST command, terminate all of that subscriber's activities including forwarded/deflected/transferred calls, tag the resulting call records as IST-terminated, and then confirm completion to the HPLMN.)

questions.question: Can Immediate Service Termination be applied to a subscriber who is not marked as subscribed to any CAMEL-based service, and who alone can trigger IST for a subscriber?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, IST shall also be possible for subscribers not marked as subscribed to any CAMEL-based service. IST is controlled by the HPLMN and can be triggered by the HPLMN only, and the subscriber to be terminated is specified by the IMSI.

questions.question: A user has indicated a preference for downlink-biased channel coding asymmetry, and the network sets up an asymmetric channel coding connection accordingly. What must the network always assign on the unbiased (uplink) link, and to which GERAN channel codings does channel coding asymmetry apply?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall always assign a TCH/F14.4 channel on the unbiased link. Channel coding asymmetry shall only be applicable to NT services using the GERAN channel codings TCH/F14.4, TCH/F28.8 and TCH/F43.2.

questions.question: A mobile requests an AIUR that exceeds what its ME can support symmetrically, and the network can allocate an asymmetric air interface connection. What must the network assign in the downlink, and what caps that assignment?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall assign the maximum AIUR supported by the ME in the downlink at GERAN, upper-bounded by the maximum number of TCH/F indicated by the mobile user and by the number of TCH/F supported by the network, while maintaining a minimum of one TCH/F.

questions.question: Asymmetric air interface connections in HSCSD are restricted to which direction of asymmetry, and to which class of general bearer service do they apply?
questions.reference_answer: Asymmetric air interface connections are only applicable to downlink-biased asymmetry, i.e. where the ME receives at a higher rate than it transmits, and they shall only be applicable to NT (non-transparent) GBS (general bearer services).

questions.question: For accurate charging of an HSCSD multislot call whose TCH/F allocation changes during the call, what record must be kept, and who is normally liable for the TCH/F usage on a mobile-originated multislot call?
questions.reference_answer: A record of start and stop timestamps versus the number of TCH/F must be provided for each change in TCH/F allocation. For mobile-originated multislot calls, the A-party (calling subscriber) is liable for the use of all the TCH/F in her PLMN.

questions.question: USAT applications on the UICC run in a highly secure environment. What must not be compromised by the introduction of USAT services, and what treats an external execution environment such as MExE as untrusted?
questions.reference_answer: The integrity of the USIM and existing security mechanisms shall not be compromised by the introduction of USAT services, and the security of the PLMN, the USIM, and the USAT applications shall not be able to be compromised by an external execution environment. Applications running within an external execution environment (such as MExE) are considered non-trusted until a secure authentication and identification procedure has been successfully performed.

questions.question: For which set of activities related to USAT applications must it be possible to charge a subscriber?
questions.reference_answer: It shall be possible to charge for subscription (registration to use USAT services), application transfer/download, application upgrading, application use, content provided within a USAT application, roaming use of USAT applications, and use of a transport/bearer service (e.g. SMS).

questions.question: A subscriber's service profile is barred from Packet Oriented Services within her HPLMN only for APNs outside the HPLMN, while she is roaming in a VPLMN. Can the network allow her to access some specific APNs while barring the rest, and is roaming-based barring of home-network access points required to be possible?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: the network shall be able to allow a subscriber to access some specific APNs while barring the subscriber from the other Packet Oriented Services, and it shall be possible to bar a subscriber from requesting Packet Oriented Services from access points within the HPLMN while the subscriber is roaming in a VPLMN.

questions.question: Besides preventing future calls, what must the HLR, MSC and VLR be able to do about calls that were already established before an Operator Determined Barring category was applied?
questions.reference_answer: In addition to ensuring barring integrity for future calls, the HLR, and consequently the MSC and VLR, shall provide means to terminate the calls of a user that were established prior to the application of the ODB service and are still ongoing.

questions.question: A subscriber with an active call-forwarding programme has an Operator Determined Barring category activated that contravenes it. What happens to the forwarding programme, and what happens if the subscriber then tries to activate a new forwarding programme that also contravenes an ODB category?
questions.reference_answer: Activation of the ODB category shall make the existing call forwarding programme quiescent. If the subscriber subsequently attempts to activate a new call forwarding programme that contravenes an ODB category, the activation shall be denied and the subscriber informed of the denial.

questions.question: When transferring NITZ network name, time, DST and timezone information to an MS, what constraint applies to how this transfer uses network resources?
questions.reference_answer: Transfer of the relevant NITZ information shall not unduly consume scarce network resources.

questions.question: When a serving PLMN provides a network identity name to an MS using the default character set, what two forms of that name must it make available, and who chooses which one is used?
questions.reference_answer: The serving PLMN shall make both a "short" and a "long" name available to the MS when using the default character set. The MS shall be free to choose which of these names to use depending on its own characteristics and/or limitations, such as those of its display.

questions.question: A TFO call is handed over from one part of a network to another part that has not deployed TFO support. What must happen to the call?
questions.reference_answer: The call shall revert to normal operation once handed over into the part of the network that is not provisioned with TFO.

questions.question: Two GSM mobiles are in a mobile-to-mobile speech call using the same GSM speech coding standard. Must TFO be applicable, and which GSM speech coding standards must TFO support?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, TFO shall be applicable to all mobile-to-mobile speech calls where both parties use the same GSM speech coding standard, and TFO shall be supported for all of the GSM speech coding standards, i.e. Full Rate, Half Rate and Enhanced Full Rate.

questions.question: Why does TFO require a stricter timing requirement for reverting to normal operation than for applying TFO in the first place?
questions.reference_answer: There is a much stricter timing requirement on reverting to normal operation than on applying TFO because if TFO is enabled on only one side of a call (e.g. during a partial failure), the speech becomes unintelligible, so the network must detect and correct this condition rapidly.

questions.question: Network echo cancellers are normally used to remove hybrid echo in PSTN four-wire-to-two-wire conversions. Should they be used in mobile-to-mobile TFO calls, and why?
questions.reference_answer: No, these Network Echo Cancellers should not be used in mobile-to-mobile calls, since both terminals are already digital and the echo they are designed to remove does not arise in that scenario; they are only useful for mobile-to-PSTN calls.

questions.question: A MExE subscriber roams from her HPLMN into a VPLMN. Must she be able to access her normal MExE services there, and is service continuity across this kind of roaming guaranteed by the specification?
questions.reference_answer: Roaming MExE subscribers shall be able, as far as possible, to access their normal MExE services in their HPLMN, but service continuity when roaming depends on the availability of those services in the VPLMN and is outside the scope of the specification.

questions.question: MExE executables are graded into security domains. Which three domains must be supported, and is the untrusted "sandbox" itself counted as one of these domains?
questions.reference_answer: The three domains that shall be supported are the MExE Security Operator Domain (authorised by the HPLMN operator), the MExE Security Manufacturer Domain (authorised by the MExE UE manufacturer), and the MExE Security User Trusted Domain (written by user-trusted software developers and verified by organisations such as certification authorities). The sandbox in which untrusted MExE executables run is not considered to be one of these domains.

questions.question: Every MExE UE must support a minimal API regardless of its MExE Classmark. What is that minimal API called, and what does it consist of?
questions.reference_answer: The MExE UE shall support a core API known as the Core MExE API, the minimal set of API present on all MExE UEs, providing the MExE execution environment for applications and applets to run; it consists of generic and 3GPP-specific aspects.

questions.question: During eMLPP call set-up, pre-emption is required to free resources for a higher-priority call. What must the network do, and what happens once a precedence level has been set for a call?
questions.reference_answer: In case of pre-emption the network shall release the lowest lower-priority call and seize the resources needed to set up the higher-priority call. Once the precedence level is set for a call, it cannot be changed.

questions.question: A user selects an eMLPP precedence level for a call that is higher than her maximum authorised level. What must happen, and where is her maximum authorised precedence level stored?
questions.reference_answer: If the user selects a precedence level higher than her maximum authorised level, the maximum authorised precedence level shall be applied for the call instead. The maximum authorised precedence level shall be stored on the SIM/USIM, and the mobile station shall check that only an authorised level is used at call set-up.

questions.question: When an eMLPP call interworks with a network providing the ITU-T MLPP service, how must precedence levels A and B be mapped, and can other precedence levels change during that interworking?
questions.reference_answer: Precedence levels A and B shall be mapped to precedence level 0 when interworking with an MLPP network. The precedence level of a call, except for levels A and B, shall not be changed when interworking with networks providing MLPP.

questions.question: A subscriber with an eMLPP subscription for a priority level higher than the lowest requests registration of a default priority level that exceeds her maximum entitled level. What must the network do?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall reject this registration request, with an appropriate indication given to the subscriber.

questions.question: Can Mobile Number Portability be offered to a subscriber as a stand-alone service, and to which service TS12 is it explicitly not applicable?
questions.reference_answer: No, Mobile Number Portability cannot be offered as a stand-alone service. It applies to all teleservices (e.g. SMS, voice, fax), IP Multimedia services, and bearer services (e.g. data), except for TS12, which is the emergency call teleservice.

questions.question: After a Mobile Number Portability porting process completes, must the donor network retain the ported subscriber's subscription details, and which two networks remain involved in supporting the ported subscriber afterward?
questions.reference_answer: No; after the porting process is complete, the subscription details related to the ported DN on the donor network shall not be required and can be deleted. Only the number range owner network and the recipient network remain involved in the MNP/NAGNP solution for supporting service to the ported subscriber.

questions.question: In Mobile Number Portability, is the subscriber's IMSI/IMPI itself ported to the recipient network, and what must the recipient network do instead?
questions.reference_answer: No, the IMSI/IMPI shall not be ported. Instead, the recipient mobile network of the porting process shall issue a new IMSI/IMPI for the ported subscription.

questions.question: For an emergency location request in a region using ETSI standards, an IMEI is used to identify an unauthorized UE or a UE without a SIM/USIM. What must be indicated when this identification method is used?
questions.reference_answer: It shall be indicated that the use of IMEI-based identification is triggered by an emergency call.

questions.question: A target mobile user wants to hide her true identity from an LCS requestor and client. What kind of alias must be used, and what relationship must it have to her true identity?
questions.reference_answer: A unique alias identification must be used, having a one-to-one relationship to the true identity of the subscriber (or, for a Requestor alias, to the true identity of the requestor); the alias may be permanent or temporary, and the target mobile user shall be able to know her own alias.

questions.question: An LCS client includes an alias instead of the real identity of the Requestor in a location request. How does the target mobile user ultimately authorize that requestor?
questions.reference_answer: The target mobile user authorizes the requestor based on the requestor's true identity, after that identity has been decrypted in the requestor's operator's network.

questions.question: For a semi-autonomous UE-Based Location Calculation commercial service, if the network encrypts the location assistance information it broadcasts, what algorithm requirement applies?
questions.reference_answer: If the location assistance information is encrypted, a single common standardized encryption algorithm shall be used.

questions.question: ISDN offers two network options for handling Call Deflection while the served user's call is retained until the deflected-to user is informed. Which of the two options do PLMNs provide?
questions.reference_answer: PLMNs only provide network option b: the call is first removed from the served subscriber and then the connection to the deflected-to subscriber is established (rather than retaining the call to the served user until the deflected-to user is informed).

questions.question: A served mobile subscriber tries to invoke Call Deflection but the CD supplementary service cannot be provided to her. What must the network do, and can the network reject CD because the number of diversions has reached its limit?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall provide an indication to the mobile subscriber notifying her of the reason for failure. Yes, one of the listed possible causes for rejection is that the number of diversions has already reached the upper limit.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of successive Call Deflection diversions permitted for a single call, and can a network operator set a lower per-call limit?
questions.reference_answer: The upper limit is five diversions per call, counting all types of diversions. As a network operator option, the maximum number of diversions may instead be set anywhere in the range of one to five diversions per call.

questions.question: For a subscriber provided with a Translation Information Flag on a VPLMN supporting CAMEL phase 2, what must the network NOT do when the subscriber invokes Call Deflection?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall not check the validity of the deflected-to number, and shall not apply the CD interactions with Barring of all Outgoing International Calls (BOIC) or Barring of all Outgoing International Calls except those to the Home PLMN Country (BOIC-exHC).

questions.question: AMR Noise Suppression must not significantly increase channel activity when combined with DTX. In terms of the Voice Activity Factor measured with (w) and without (y) AMR NS active on noisy real-world signals, what relationship between w and y is required?
questions.reference_answer: For real-world signals, w (VAF with AMR NS active) is required not to be significantly greater than y (VAF without AMR NS active); any case where w is greater than y should be further investigated. w is also required to be less than the maximum of y and x (the clean-speech VAF).

questions.question: Where must it be possible to implement AMR Noise Suppression, and what form must the noise suppression specification itself take?
questions.reference_answer: It shall be possible to implement AMR Noise Suppression in the mobile station, operating on the uplink speech signal (implementation in the network on the downlink is for further study). The noise suppression specification shall be comprised of bit-exact fixed-point C code, with test vectors defined to verify operation.

questions.question: What is the required maximum initial convergence time T for AMR Noise Suppression, and how is that time interval used in subjective listening tests?
questions.reference_answer: T shall be a maximum of 2 seconds. In subjective testing, the first T seconds of each processed sample (with and without noise suppression) is deleted before presentation to listeners, on the assumption that this does not reduce intelligibility or introduce clipping; a subset of tests is also defined where this initial period is NOT removed, to test the subjective effect of the convergence period itself.

questions.question: Must the network be able to enable or disable the AMR Noise Suppression function, and does use of the feature in the network during a call impose any requirement on the mobile station's own use of it?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the network shall be able to enable or disable this optional noise suppression function both at call set-up and in-call. Use of the feature in the network during a call should not place any requirements on its use within the MS, and vice versa.

questions.question: A CAMEL CSE has finished issuing charging and event-arming instructions for an SMS set-up request. How many of the final delivery-control instructions (bar / continue / continue with modified information) may it then issue, and what must happen if it bars the SM delivery?
questions.reference_answer: The CSE shall issue one and only one of the final instructions: bar the SM delivery, continue the delivery, or continue the delivery with modified information. If the SM delivery is barred, the SMSC shall be informed.

questions.question: For a CAMEL-marked subscriber with mobility-management event notification set up, which two GPRS routeing-area update events (besides attach and the two detach types) trigger a notification to the CSE?
questions.reference_answer: Routeing area update of the MS to a different SGSN service area, and routeing area update of the MS within the same SGSN service area, both trigger a notification to the CSE (along with a network-initiated transfer to "MS not reachable for paging").

questions.question: A CAMEL-marked, CUG-subscribing subscriber receives a terminating call carrying CUG information, and the terminating CAMEL service tries to modify the called party number. If the called subscriber does NOT subscribe to CUG, what must the IPLMN do with the call?
questions.reference_answer: The IPLMN shall continue the call establishment to the modified called party number (rather than releasing the call, which is what happens only if the called subscriber does subscribe to CUG).

questions.question: Subscriber A calls mobile subscriber B, who has activated Conditional Call Forwarding to a destination in her home country, triggering Late Call Forwarding after the call has already failed once. Under Optimal Routing, how must the originating PLMN then route the call?
questions.reference_answer: The originating PLMN shall route the call directly to the forwarded-to party, rather than via HPLMN(B), because the Conditional Call Forward destination is in B's Home Country (or in the country where A is registered), which triggers Late Call Forwarding under Optimal Routing.

questions.question: Support of Optimal Routing lets calls be routed directly to a mobile subscriber's actual location instead of via her HPLMN. Who decides whether to actually optimise the routing of a given call, and can an HPLMN restrict this on a per-subscriber, per-call basis?
questions.reference_answer: The IPLMN handling the call decides whether or not to optimise the routing, taking into account information provided by the called mobile subscriber's HPLMN. As a network option, the HPLMN may permit or deny Optimal Routing for given subscribers on a per-call basis.

questions.question: For CLIR override, if a call originates in an ISDN/PLMN with no override category applicable but terminates in a different ISDN/PLMN where an override category does apply, can the calling line identity still be presented in the destination network?
questions.reference_answer: Yes. Because the rules and regulations of the destination network apply, a call with CLIR applied can still be overridden in the destination network even if the override category is not applicable in the originating network.

questions.question: When the CLIR supplementary service is invoked for an inter-network call, what must the originating network provide to the destination network, in addition to optionally the cause of no CLI?
questions.reference_answer: The originating network shall provide the destination network with a notification that the line identity of the calling party is not allowed to be presented to the called party.

questions.question: For COLR override between two ISDN/PLMNs, whose rules and regulations govern whether the override category applies?
questions.reference_answer: The rules and regulations of the originating network shall apply (unlike the CLIR override case, where it is the destination network's rules that govern).

questions.question: When the COLR supplementary service is invoked on an inter-network call, what must the destination network provide to the originating network?
questions.reference_answer: The destination network shall provide the originating network with a notification that the line identity of the connected party is not allowed to be presented to the calling party.

questions.question: A subscriber sends a Call Forwarding Busy deactivation request with no Basic Service Group information included. How broadly does the network apply that deactivation, and is the registered forwarded-to number data erased along with it?
questions.reference_answer: If no Basic Service Group information is included, the deactivation request applies to all Basic Service Groups. However, the registered forwarded-to-number information shall not be erased by deactivation, only by Erasure.

questions.question: Subscriber B is engaged in an active call with A when subscriber C's call triggers Call Waiting. If A or B terminates the active call, what must the network do for B while she can still accept C's waiting call within T2, and can B also use Call Hold instead to free the resources?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall continue to indicate ringing (or equivalent) towards subscriber C as for a normal call while B has not yet accepted; B can accept the call from C before T2 expires. Yes, B can also free the resources using the Call Hold supplementary service and then accept the waiting call from C before T2 expires.

questions.question: A served mobile subscriber has exactly one call on hold and no active call. What actions can she take with that held call, and can she receive an incoming call in this state without Call Waiting?
questions.reference_answer: She can retrieve the held call, set up another call, or disconnect the held call. She cannot receive a call in this state, except when using the Call Waiting supplementary service.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of calls that can be waiting at one time for a single mobile access under the Call Waiting supplementary service, per the base requirement, and can a network offer more?
questions.reference_answer: The maximum number of waiting calls at one time per mobile access is one, meaning no further calls are offered while a call is already waiting. As a network option this maximum may be set greater than one, as a possible future enhancement.

questions.question: In the Call Waiting supplementary service, what determines the length of timer T2 (the no-answer timeout), and within what range must it fall?
questions.reference_answer: The value of T2 is set at the service provider's discretion, within a range between 0.5 and 2 minutes.

questions.question: A served mobile subscriber has an active MultiParty call and a single call on hold, and asks the network to disconnect both. What must happen to any calls on hold in that case?
questions.reference_answer: All calls, even those on hold, shall be released.

questions.question: A subscriber with an active MultiParty call and a single held call requests a private communication to be established. Will the network accept this, and why?
questions.reference_answer: No, the network shall reject the request, because establishing a private communication in that state would result in an active call plus two calls on hold, which is not supported according to the Call Hold supplementary service; an indication is given to the subscriber with the reason for failure.

questions.question: If the radio path of a served mobile subscriber is permanently lost for any reason while she is in a MultiParty call, what must happen to that call?
questions.reference_answer: The MultiParty call shall be released.

questions.question: Can a served mobile subscriber control more than one MultiParty call at a time, and can MultiParty service be invoked if one of the two initial calls is already part of another MultiParty call?
questions.reference_answer: No to both: the served mobile subscriber cannot control more than one MultiParty call at a time, and it shall not be possible to invoke MultiParty service if either or both of the initial calls are already active parts of one or two other MultiParty calls.

questions.question: A caller tries to set up a MultiParty call to a subscriber whose Call Forwarding on Busy is active, and the forwarding condition is met. What happens to the forwarded-to subscriber?
questions.reference_answer: The forwarded-to subscriber will be alerted and can be added to the conference (the MultiParty call).

questions.question: A CUG subscriber has both a preferential CUG and the Outgoing Access capability, but outgoing calls are barred within that CUG. If she originates a call by entering that CUG's index without suppressing Outgoing Access, how is the call established?
questions.reference_answer: The call shall be established without any CUG information at all, i.e. as a normal call, because outgoing calls are barred within that CUG despite the OA capability not being suppressed.

questions.question: A CUG subscriber with a preferential CUG and Outgoing Access capability enters both a CUG index and a request to suppress the OA capability. Which CUG is used to establish the call?
questions.reference_answer: The call shall be established using the CUG index she provided (not the preferential CUG).

questions.question: A CUG subscriber roams into a PLMN that does not support CUG at all. For a basic service group that IS subject to CUG restrictions and for which she has no incoming access, are incoming calls to her allowed there?
questions.reference_answer: No, incoming calls shall not be allowed for basic service groups that are subject to CUG restrictions and for which the user does not have incoming access, even though the visited PLMN does not itself support CUG — the HPLMN must control the handling of roaming to enforce this restriction.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of Closed User Groups that an individual subscriber may be a member of?
questions.reference_answer: Each individual subscriber may be a member of a maximum of 10 CUGs.

questions.question: For the Advice of Charge supplementary service, when the MS must display the total accumulated charge, where must the SIM/USIM store the running cumulative unit value, and under what condition can that stored value be reset?
questions.reference_answer: The SIM/USIM shall store the running cumulative unit charge in the ACM. This value must be stored securely and shall not be capable of being interrupted, reset, or corrupted, except for resetting under control of the unblocking key.

questions.question: ISDN's UUS service 1 allows, as a network option, transfer of up to 32 octets of UUI. Is this option supported in PLMNs, and what must networks using the phase 1 or phase 2 standard do if they support UUS service 1 implicitly requested with 32 octets?
questions.reference_answer: No, this 32-octet network option shall not be supported in PLMNs. However, networks using the phase 1 or phase 2 standard that do support UUS service 1 implicitly requested with 32 octets shall apply the rules defined for interworking considerations in clause 8.

questions.question: A calling mobile subscriber includes UUI when originating a call, implicitly activating UUS service 1. Is the remote party required to send a response to this implicit activation, and can the remote party still include UUI in its call response?
