questions.reference_answer: No, when service 1 is implicitly activated the remote party is not required to send a response to the implicit activation request, but the remote party can still include UUI in the call response.

questions.question: UUS service 1 was explicitly requested with the option "UUS required" to a called subscriber who has Call Forwarding on No Reply active. What happens to the call if the no-reply condition timer expires?
questions.reference_answer: The call shall be released, because "UUS required" was requested and the no-reply timer expiring under CFNRy is incompatible with completing the UUS 1 exchange.

questions.question: Call forwarding on mobile subscriber busy is invoked due to a user-determined busy (UDUB) condition that is met after alerting has started. Which set of interaction rules then applies to the accompanying UUI and UUS request?
questions.reference_answer: The interactions defined for Call Forwarding on No Reply shall apply in this case (as opposed to the pre-alerting UDUB case, where the UUI and UUS request are simply forwarded with the call).

questions.question: A subscriber has chosen the subscription option "control of barring services by service provider" for Barring of Outgoing Calls. Can that subscriber herself activate or deactivate the barring, and does activating a barring program affect a call already in progress?
questions.reference_answer: No, if the subscriber has selected the "control by service provider" option, the supplementary service cannot be activated or deactivated by the subscriber; only the service provider can do so. Activation of barring of outgoing calls does not affect any current communication.

questions.question: A subscriber with password-based control of Barring of Incoming Calls sends a deactivation request without inserting any Basic Service code. How is that interpreted, and how many barring programs can be active at once for one basic service group?
questions.reference_answer: If no Basic Service code is inserted, it is interpreted as the group "All Basic Services". Only one barring program may be activated at a time for one basic service group; activating a new one deactivates an already active one.

questions.question: For a network-initiated USSD operation, what must the UE do if it cannot process the operation, and what if the alphabet indicated by the network is one the UE doesn't support?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall return an error indication to the node that originated the operation if it cannot process the operation. If the network's indicated alphabet is not supported by the UE, the UE shall inform the network.

questions.question: In a network-initiated USSD dialogue where the network explicitly indicates a response from the user is required, how is the next string the user enters treated, and what MMI capability must be provided to the user?
questions.reference_answer: The next string entered by the user shall be used as the response and is not interpreted according to normal MMI procedures. An MMI command shall be provided to allow the user to terminate the dialogue with a null response.

questions.question: Which service codes may PLMNs use for the internationally-standardized supplementary-service control message format ending in # SEND, besides the codes defined for PLMN-specific use?
questions.reference_answer: Only codes specified in TS 22.030, plus those defined for PLMN-specific use, may be used as the service code NN(N); all other values are reserved.

questions.question: Both subscriber A and subscriber B in an established call have subscribed to Explicit Call Transfer. Can they simultaneously invoke ECT to transfer the call to two different third parties, and is the network required to prevent this?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, both mobile subscribers can simultaneously transfer the call to different users, since simultaneous invocation is not prevented by the network (though this is not regarded as a normal situation, and the network cannot guarantee the indications supplied to the users will be sensible).

questions.question: The network cannot determine whether the connection resulting from an ECT request would still contain a subscriber able to terminate the call, e.g. due to interworking between different signalling system versions. What are the network's options in this case, and what mechanism might it use if it accepts the request anyway?
questions.reference_answer: As a network option, the request for ECT may be either accepted or rejected. If accepted, the network may employ other means to control the situation, such as time supervision, though the procedures for this are outside the scope of the specification.

questions.question: Subscriber A places a call that is forwarded to user C by Call Forwarding Unconditional, and user C is busy. Does subscriber A receive a CCBS-possible indication in this case?
questions.reference_answer: No, subscriber A shall not receive any CCBS-possible indication when the call has been forwarded via CFU and the destination user C is busy.

questions.question: A mobile-originating CAMEL-based service redirects a CCBS call to a different called party address than the one used for the initial call. What must the network do with the CCBS call and its corresponding request?
questions.reference_answer: The CCBS call shall be released by the network, and the corresponding CCBS request shall be automatically deactivated.

questions.question: Destination network B receives a CCBS request from originating network A while Barring of All Incoming Calls (BAIC) is active and operative for the relevant Basic Service Group at destination B. What must happen to that CCBS request?
questions.reference_answer: The CCBS request shall be rejected with an indication of short term denial.

questions.question: A subscriber has activated a CCBS request against destination B, and B's Barring of Incoming Calls when Roaming (BIC-Roam) then becomes active and operative when HPLMN B receives an interrogation to route the CCBS call. What must happen to that CCBS request?
questions.reference_answer: The specific CCBS request relating to that CCBS call shall be automatically deactivated.

questions.question: In the Follow Me feature, can a remote party be simultaneously registered to more than one initiating subscriber at a time, and can one initiating subscriber register Follow Me with respect to several remote parties at once?
questions.reference_answer: No, a remote party can be registered to only one initiating subscriber at a time, but the Follow Me feature may, at a given instant, be registered to an initiating subscriber with respect to several remote parties.

questions.question: The FM service supervisor performs a forced erasure of a subscriber's Follow Me registration toward a remote party. Must the initiating subscriber be informed, and must additional erasure information such as a password (when required by the operator) be encoded in any particular way?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the initiating subscriber whose registration has been erased shall be informed of the successful forced erasure by the network. Any operator-required additional information for erasure shall be coded as a USSD string with a length not exceeding 30 characters.

questions.question: Is the Follow Me feature applicable to Voice Group Services (TS 91/TS 92) in general, and is there any exception where a dispatcher could still use it?
questions.reference_answer: No, Follow Me is in general not applicable for Voice Group Services (TS 91, TS 92). However, a dispatcher may act as an initiating subscriber or a remote party for the Follow Me feature.

questions.question: A remote party subscriber wants to check her own Follow Me registration data stored in the network. Is she allowed to interrogate it herself, and what MSISDN does the network return in response?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, when the remote party corresponds to a subscriber, she shall be able to interrogate her own Follow Me data stored in the network. The network shall return the basic MSISDN of the initiating subscriber for which the remote party is registered to Follow Me.

questions.question: A called user has an override category set for name information under Calling Name Identification Presentation, while the calling party has activated CLIR. Which service normally takes precedence, and what changes when the called user has that override category?
questions.reference_answer: CLIR normally takes precedence over CNAP, meaning a privacy indication is shown instead of the calling name. But if the called user has an override category set for name information, the name information is presented to the called user despite CLIR being active.

questions.question: The override categories for CNAP's name information and for the line-identity information under TS 22.081 are kept separate. Whose responsibility is it to ensure the two override categories do not fall out of sync with each other?
questions.reference_answer: It is left to the CNAP service provider to ensure that no discrepancy occurs between the override category controlling the name information and the override category for the line identity information.

questions.question: The network fails to determine a caller's name information within its predefined time window for Calling Name Identification Presentation. What must be sent to the CNAP subscriber, and what purpose does the predefined time window serve?
questions.reference_answer: The CNAP subscriber shall be sent an indication that the name is unavailable. The predefined time is a network-dependent value chosen so that the called user may still receive the name in a timely manner prior to answering the call.

questions.question: A calling party has subscribed to CLIR. What effect does this have on Calling Name Identification Presentation for the called party, given that CNAP requires no action from the calling party to activate?
questions.reference_answer: If the calling party has subscribed to CLIR, then both the calling line identity and the calling name identity shall not be presented to the called party.

questions.question: A subscriber activates a Multiple Subscriber Profile CCBS request on a non-default profile and then moves to a network not supporting MSP Phase 2. If the CCBS recall matures while she is there, what happens to the CCBS request?
questions.reference_answer: The corresponding CCBS request shall be suspended until the subscriber next registers on a network supporting MSP Phase 2.

questions.question: Up to how many different profiles can be provisioned against a single subscriber using the Multiple Subscriber Profile feature, and must charges be tracked separately per profile?
questions.reference_answer: Up to four different profiles can be provisioned against a subscriber. Yes, the charges accrued for services shall be associated with the appropriate profile, allowing separate charging for each profile.

questions.question: A Multiple Subscriber Profile subscriber is already busy in a call under one profile. If a further incoming call arrives targeting a different profile of hers, is it accepted, and what supplementary services are unaffected by this rule?
questions.reference_answer: No, further incoming call attempts shall be rejected or treated as busy, even if they target a different profile than the one currently in a call. This does not prevent the normal operation of Call Waiting or Call Forwarding where applicable.

questions.question: In the Multiple Subscriber Profile feature, when a subscriber initiates a call without indicating a profile ID, which profile is used? And for mobile-terminating activities, how is the profile selected?
questions.reference_answer: If no profile ID is indicated for a mobile-originated call or short message, the registered profile is used (implicit selection). For mobile-terminating activities, the profile is selected according to the MSISDN addressed.

questions.question: In a Shared GERAN/UTRAN, besides balancing load individually per Participating Operator, what other load-balancing capability must the Hosting RAN Operator provide regarding the combined traffic of all Participating Operators?
questions.reference_answer: The Hosting RAN Operator shall provide the capability to perform load balancing on the combined traffic of all Participating Operators within the Shared GERAN or UTRAN, while maintaining the agreed shares of GERAN or UTRAN resources and managing Signalling and User traffic independently.

questions.question: 3GPP specifications must let a UE cope with multiple radio interfaces that may each provide different service capabilities. What two mechanisms must the specifications provide for this?
questions.reference_answer: The specifications shall provide a mechanism enabling a UE to adapt to different radio interfaces and determine the service capabilities available, and a mechanism enabling the UE to select radio interfaces capable of providing the appropriate service capabilities and to support mobility between multiple radio interfaces.

questions.question: Under the principle of phased service evolution, must services from a previous release continue to be supported in later releases, and why is this important from an end-user perspective?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, previous release services shall as a principle also be supported in following releases. This matters because continued support of legacy services is an important driver for established mobile users to stay with their existing operator while taking new services into use.

questions.question: Under an MNO/3rd-party OTT agreement for on-demand TV broadcast, what result information must the 3GPP network enable the MNO to report back to the 3rd party after delivering a TV service?
questions.reference_answer: The 3GPP network shall enable an MNO to inform a 3rd party of the result of delivering a TV service to a user, e.g. selected media format information, mode of content delivery (broadcast only, broadcast/unicast fall-back, consumption-based switching), QoE of content delivery, and cached content indication.

questions.question: During a multimedia call, an application requires synchronisation between some of its connections. If the UE undergoes a handover procedure, must that synchronisation be preserved, and is it acceptable for the access protocols to renegotiate connection characteristics on network initiative during the call?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the synchronisation shall not be lost during handover procedures. Connection characteristics may indeed be independently and dynamically re-negotiated on network initiative, for example due to a change of network load conditions or during a handover procedure.

questions.question: The PLMN must handle a wide range of IP traffic types for multimedia services. Must it support simultaneous IPv4 and IPv6 usage for a single bearer to the same PDN through the same APN, and can the operator restrict IPv4-only terminals from network access?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the PLMN shall support simultaneous IPv4 and IPv6 usage for a single bearer connecting to the same PDN through the same APN. The operator shall be able to control whether or not an IPv4-only terminal is allowed access to the network.

questions.question: A subscriber's IP session needs to continue when the UE hands over from one IP access network to another that supports a different IP version. Must service continuity be maintained in this case?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, service continuity of subscriber IP sessions shall be supported during UE handovers from one IP access network to another, regardless of whether the new IP access network supports the same version of IP as the old one.

questions.question: Under Automatic Roaming Agreements, a user wants service from a network with which neither she nor her home environment has any direct commercial agreement. How is this to be enabled, and what must fraud and cost control mechanisms ensure?
questions.reference_answer: This shall be enabled by interworking via trusted third parties, with each Home Environment interworking with one or more serving network operators under a negotiated commercial roaming agreement. Fraud and cost control mechanisms shall be used to ensure that charges incurred for 3GPP services do not exceed the credit limits set.

questions.question: A prepay subscriber's account for a specific service exhausts its credit while a chargeable session is ongoing. How quickly must the ongoing charging information related to that account be interrupted, and what must be checked before executing a requested prepay service in the first place?
questions.reference_answer: All ongoing charging information related to that prepay account shall be immediately interrupted, within a few seconds, as soon as the prepay credit exhausts or expires. Before executing the requested service, the prepay service shall check the subscriber's prepay account for coverage of the requested service charges.

questions.question: To guarantee a meaningful multi-prepay-account concept, how many different prepay accounts should be supported for a user at minimum?
questions.reference_answer: At least 2 different prepay accounts should be supported to guarantee a meaningful multi-prepay-account concept.

questions.question: For maritime communication between two vessels at sea, how is the minimum required communication range defined in relation to the vessels' antennas?
questions.reference_answer: The minimum communication range between vessels shall be equal to the maximum line-of-sight range between antennas mounted on the two vessels at sea or on inland waterways.

questions.question: For UAS security, what must the 3GPP system protect against with respect to UAS identities, and what must it support regarding regulatory requirements such as Lawful Intercept?
questions.reference_answer: The 3GPP system shall protect against spoofing attacks of the UAS identities, and shall support regulatory requirements, such as Lawful Intercept, for UAS traffic.

questions.question: Besides protecting UAS identities from spoofing, what must the 3GPP system protect regarding data transport between the UAS and the UTM, and what confidentiality protection must it support?
questions.reference_answer: The 3GPP system shall protect the transport of data between the UAS and UTM, and shall support confidentiality protection of identities related to the UAS and of personally identifiable information.

questions.question: When handing over multiple PDP contexts from UTRAN to GERAN and several remain candidates for handover, who decides which PDP context is maintained, and who makes that decision when the subscriber is roaming?
questions.reference_answer: It shall be an operator choice which PDP context is maintained. When the subscriber is roaming, this decision shall instead be taken by the serving network.

questions.question: In a UTRAN-to-GERAN Multicall handover, how many of the multiple simultaneous CS calls can be handed over?
questions.reference_answer: Only one call can be handed over in the case of a UTRAN-to-GERAN handover of a Multicall.

questions.question: If the technical implementation of the UTRAN necessitates a handover as a matter of normal operation, not related to the situations otherwise in scope of the handover service requirements, what must be true of the resulting service?
questions.reference_answer: Services shall in no way be degraded or adversely affected by such an implementation-necessitated handover.

questions.question: A UE-hosted application wants to react to a handover. What must the available service capability set be able to indicate to the application about that handover, and what negotiation should the service capabilities support?
questions.reference_answer: The service capability set shall be able to provide an indication that handover has occurred or could occur, along with information about the type of handover and the radio resources involved. The service capabilities should support QoS negotiation.

questions.question: Under the Multicall supplementary service, can more than one CS bearer be used for speech at the same time, and how must the network treat a call whose bearer capability information is unavailable, e.g. because it originated from a PSTN?
questions.reference_answer: No, only one CS bearer can be used for speech at any one time. If the bearer capability information is not available, the network shall, for multicall purposes, handle the call as telephony.

questions.question: Under the Multicall supplementary service, must it be possible to release each active CS call independently of the others, and must each CS call be able to use a dedicated bearer with independent traffic and performance characteristics?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: it shall be possible for each CS call to use a dedicated bearer of independent traffic and performance characteristics, and it shall be possible to release each active CS call independently of any other CS call.

questions.question: A mobile station is engaged in a speech call (including a held call) and does not have Call Waiting provisioned and activated. According to the Multicall busy definition, how must an incoming speech call be treated, regardless of whether further bearers happen to be available?
questions.reference_answer: The incoming speech call shall be regarded as encountering NDUB (Network Determined User Busy), irrespective of the further availability of bearers for the user, since Call Waiting is not provisioned and activated.

questions.question: A subscriber has one active CS call and one held call on the same bearer, and wants to split them onto separate bearers. Is this required to be possible, and within what limits?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible to create a new CS bearer and move one of the calls to it, resulting in both calls being active, within the limits set by the operator/user and within the capability of the terminal.

questions.question: The user profile for MMS lets a user maintain a "user-level blacklist" of addresses. How does this differ from an ODB blacklist, and what actions must the user be able to perform on it?
questions.reference_answer: The user-level blacklist lets the user decide from whom they do not want to receive messages by adding the corresponding address themselves, unlike an ODB blacklist. It shall be possible for the user to add, remove, and edit addresses in the user-level blacklist.

questions.question: An MMS service provider connects to a VASP. Must the MMS service provider be able to authenticate the VASP, be authenticated by it, and support encryption of the transport layer between them?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to all three: the MMS service provider shall be able to authenticate a connected VASP and shall be able to be authenticated by it, and the MMS shall support encryption of the transport layer between an MMS service provider and a VASP.

questions.question: For MMS notifications and acknowledgements, must a sender's delivery or read acknowledgement be sent unconditionally, or is it subject to some permission from the recipient?
questions.reference_answer: It is subject to the recipient's permission: the sender is acknowledged about successful or failed MM delivery, or about the MM being read/handled at the recipient terminal, only subject to the recipient permitting such an acknowledgement.

questions.question: If an MMS network based repository is supported, must the MMS be able to support a user request to forward a stored MM to another destination without first delivering it to that user?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the MMS shall be able to support a request from a user to forward one or more MMs stored in the network-based repository to another destination without being delivered first to that user.

questions.question: In the presence service, if a subscribed-watcher's subscription to a presentity's presence information is cancelled, must the watcher be informed, and can a presentity have a subscription denied while appearing to the watcher as granted?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: the presence service shall inform the subscribed-watcher if their watcher-subscription is cancelled, and it shall be possible for the presentity to configure the presence service to deny a subscription while appearing to the watcher as if it has been granted ("polite blocking").

questions.question: The home environment can act as both a supplier and a requester of presence information. Must the presence service enable interworking with external presence services in other PLMNs, the Internet, or LANs?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the presence service shall enable the network to present a consistent and interoperable support of presence, such that presence capability users can interwork with one or more other external presence services.

questions.question: Under VAS-SMS charging, when is charging only allowed to occur for a service that includes a status report?
questions.reference_answer: Charging only happens after the status report has been received by the SMSC.

questions.question: For Short Message Forwarding, what must be prevented regarding the forwarding chain itself, and can a service provider activate SM forwarding for a user without the recipient's approval?
questions.reference_answer: Infinite forwarding loops need to be prevented, and the maximum number of times an SM is forwarded should be limited. No, the service shall notify a recipient upon activation and only activate the service for the user upon his approval.

questions.question: A user sends a single Short Message to multiple destination addresses, with some addresses set to have their display information blocked. What must the other, non-blocked recipients receive, and must every recipient be able to reply to all original recipients?
questions.reference_answer: The recipients whose addresses are not blocked shall receive information on all recipients of the message. It shall be supported that each recipient of the message can send a message back to all recipients of the original message.

questions.question: For MBMS user mobility, if a user hands over to a target cell that offers the broadcast service she was already receiving, must she be able to continue receiving it there?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the user shall be able to continue receiving broadcast services throughout the broadcast service area, so in a handover to a target cell offering the same service, she should be able to continue receiving it there.

questions.question: For MBMS multicast mode, must it be possible to collect subscriber charging information for a user's roaming use of the multicast mode, on a per-multicast-service basis?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible to collect subscriber charging information, including roaming, for the use of the multicast mode and for the receipt of multicast data, on a per multicast service basis.

questions.question: An enterprise network authorized to support MPS wants to release an MPS for DTS session for a group of MPS-subscribed UEs while those UEs keep basic connectivity. Must the system support this, as an explicit request from the enterprise?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the system shall support means for an authorized enterprise network supporting MPS to explicitly request to release an MPS for DTS session or group of MPS for DTS sessions while maintaining basic connectivity to the MPS subscribed UE(s) or IoT device(s).

questions.question: An MPS for DTS session is not explicitly revoked by the Service User or an IoT device. Under what two conditions must the system in the RPLMN automatically revoke it?
questions.reference_answer: The system shall automatically revoke MPS upon UE detachment/deregistration (e.g., power down), or when all connections pertaining to the MPS for DTS session are released without an explicit release of that session. It shall also automatically revoke MPS when the maximum allowed duration for the session is reached.

questions.question: A terminating network cannot immediately assign the resources an incoming MPS session needs. What must happen to the MPS session request instead of simply being dropped?
questions.reference_answer: The MPS session request shall be queued and processed for the next available resource in accordance with the Service User's priority level and session arrival time; the network shall also support informing the calling Service User of the queued status.

questions.question: A Service User is using a UE without an MPS subscription and requests an MPS MMTEL video call. Can the system authenticate and authorize this, and what does the Service User provide as part of that process?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the system shall support means to authenticate and authorize such a request. As part of the process, the Service User provides MPS credentials specifically assigned for obtaining MPS from a UE without an MPS subscription, such as a calling card number, PIN, or security token.

questions.question: A CUG-restricted communication gets deflected via Communication Deflection to a new destination. Whose CUG information is sent to the deflected-to destination, and must the outgoing communication barring of the deflecting party be used to decide whether the deflection can occur?
questions.reference_answer: The CUG information sent to the "deflected-to" destination is the same CUG information of the originating party that was sent from the originating network. No, the outgoing communication barring information of the deflecting party shall not be used to determine whether the communication can be deflected.

questions.question: How many CUGs can a specific user be a member of under the CUG service described for IMS Multimedia Telephony, and must a subscription to a CUG apply to all communication services or can it be limited?
questions.reference_answer: A specific user may be a member of one or more CUGs. Subscription to a CUG shall be defined either for all communication services, or in relation to one, or to a list of communication services.

questions.question: For IMS Multimedia Telephony with Enhanced Voice, how does the required conversational quality compare against pre-Rel-12 3GPP wideband voice, and what is preferred when transcoding cannot be avoided?
questions.reference_answer: It should be possible to achieve significantly better service quality than both Rel-11 narrowband and wideband voice, and transmission efficiency should exceed that of the pre-Rel-12 wideband voice service. Transcoding should be avoided as much as possible; if it cannot be avoided, voice conversational quality degradation should be as limited as possible.

questions.question: A subscriber has an implicit Push Service subscription set up by a VASP on her behalf. From the Push service's point of view, what does the subscriber become, and for how long can the VASP use the Push Service to deliver content to her?
questions.reference_answer: From a Push service point of view the subscriber becomes a push recipient. The VASP shall be able to use the Push Service capabilities to deliver content to this push recipient for as long as the subscription remains valid.

questions.question: Can an operator withdraw the provision of the Push Service from a user, and can that withdrawal itself be general or pre-arranged, mirroring how provisioning works?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the operator shall be able to withdraw the provision of the Push service, and that withdrawal may be either general or pre-arranged.

questions.question: For Push Service security, must a Push Recipient be able to verify the identity of the Push Initiator, and must Push Initiators have any form of authorization with the Push Service Operator before using the service?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible for the Push Recipient to be assured of the identity of the Push Initiator. Push Initiators must have authorization, such as a service level agreement, with the Push Service Operator in order to use the Push Service.

questions.question: For MCPTT ambient listening, to how many parties in the call is audio transmitted, and what use cases is this feature intended for?
questions.reference_answer: For Ambient Listening, audio is only transmitted to one party in the call, i.e. a dispatcher or an authorized MCPTT User acting in a similar role. It is used for stolen MCPTT UEs, monitoring officers, officer safety, and particular operations where the MCPTT UE should not indicate what is happening.

questions.question: For an MCPTT call within one MCPTT system, what minimum average MOS-LQO must be achieved as measured by PESQ, and what is the corresponding minimum when the call interworks with a non-3GPP PTT system?
questions.reference_answer: Within one MCPTT system, the average MOS-LQO shall be greater than or equal to 3.0 as measured by PESQ (P.862/P.862.1). When the call involves interworking with other non-3GPP PTT systems, the average MOS-LQO shall be greater than or equal to 2.7 under the same measurement.

questions.question: In MCPTT priority processing, once a request for exclusive access to a resource is queued or granted, must the requesting party be informed of the outcome, and can they cancel the request while still queued?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the requesting party is informed (directly or indirectly) when the request is granted or denied, and each requestor can be notified of the position of the request in the queue and is allowed to cancel it while queued.

questions.question: In an off-network MCPTT Group call, two participants simultaneously request permission to transmit. Must the off-network Floor control functionality have a way to resolve this, and what indication must the member who IS allowed to transmit receive?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the off-network Floor control functionality shall have a mechanism for resolving simultaneous requests for permission to transmit within the same call. The member who is allowed to transmit shall be given an indication that they are allowed to transmit on their Selected MCPTT Group.

questions.question: If the Customized Alerting Tone (CAT) service cannot be played, e.g. the CAT system fails or the content has expired, what must the calling party experience instead?
questions.reference_answer: The calling party shall experience the traditional prompt tone instead of the CAT (and if a multimedia CAT specifically fails while roaming from 3G to 2G, a voice CAT may be played instead if possible).

questions.question: Subscriber A has activated the CAT service and calls subscriber B, who has not subscribed to or activated CAT, and B does not answer. What does A experience?
questions.reference_answer: Depending on A's settings, A will experience either CAT-A or the default alerting tone, followed by a 'no answer' indication once B's 'no answer' timer has expired.

questions.question: For CAT interworking across CS and IMS domains, if the calling party wants to copy the called user's CAT as her own, what two preconditions must be met?
questions.reference_answer: The called user must have enabled CAT sharing for that instance of CAT, and both users must be subscribers of the same HPLMN.

questions.question: For the Customized Ringback Signal (CRS) service, when the called party is roaming to another PLMN, must she still be able to experience the CRS set by the calling party?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, when roaming to another PLMN, the called party shall be able to experience the CRS set by the calling party (as well as the CRS she herself set).

questions.question: Called party B has activated both Communication Waiting and CRS, and is now busy with an incoming call from C. What does B experience, and how does this differ from a normal CRS playback?
questions.reference_answer: B experiences either the CRS service or the default communication waiting indication, depending on operator settings; if B experiences the CRS service, its audio information may be replaced by the default communication waiting tone in order to limit perturbation on the ongoing communication with C.

questions.question: For V2X security, subject to regional regulation and operator policy, what must the 3GPP system ensure to support pseudonymity and privacy of a UE using a V2X application?
questions.reference_answer: The 3GPP system shall support pseudonymity and privacy by ensuring that a UE identity cannot be tracked or identified by any other UE beyond a certain short time period required by the V2X application.

questions.question: For a UE supporting V2V or V2P applications, does 3GPP transport of the application messages require a valid subscription and authorization from a network operator, and is this transport provided whether or not the UE is served by E-UTRAN?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, 3GPP transport of V2V or V2P application messages requires the UE to have a valid subscription and authorization from a network operator, and this transport is provided for a valid subscriber whether the UE is served or not served by E-UTRAN.

questions.question: What is the maximum latency the E-UTRA(N) shall support for transferring messages between two UEs supporting a V2V/P application, directly or via an RSU, and what is the tighter latency figure that should apply for pre-crash sensing specifically?
questions.reference_answer: The maximum latency shall be 100 ms for general V2V/P message transfer. For pre-crash sensing usage specifically, the E-UTRA(N) should be capable of a maximum latency of 20ms.

questions.question: Must the E-UTRA(N) be able to achieve high reliability for V2X communication without relying on application-layer message retransmissions?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the E-UTRA(N) shall be able to support high reliability without requiring application-layer message retransmissions.

questions.question: Local IP Access lets IP-capable UEs connected via an H(e)NB reach devices on the same residential/enterprise IP network. Is data traffic for Local IP Access expected to traverse the mobile operator's core network, and what kind of traffic continues to traverse it regardless?
questions.reference_answer: No, data traffic for Local IP Access is expected not to traverse the mobile operator's network except for mobile operator network components located in the residential/enterprise premises. Signalling traffic will continue to traverse the mobile operator network regardless.

questions.question: If an H(e)NB supports the H(e)NB Hosting Party application on a UICC, what capability must that UICC application have regarding the H(e)NB's location, and what platform must the H(e)NB support for configuring it?
questions.reference_answer: The UICC application shall be able to acquire the geographical location of the H(e)NB. The H(e)NB shall support the use of the operator's UICC application management platform to configure the Hosting Party application.

questions.question: A UE in idle mode is evaluating cell reselection and finds a cell whose CSG identity is in its Allowed CSG List. What preference must the UE apply, once the cell reselection criteria are met?
questions.reference_answer: The UE in idle mode shall prefer to select the cell whose CSG Identity is in the UE's Allowed CSG List (or Operator CSG list), once the cell reselection criteria have been met.

questions.question: For the wireline compatibility of the Global Text Telephony standard, must a landline party's existing Text Telephone equipment be modified to interwork with it, and against which ITU recommendation must the standard be compatible?
questions.reference_answer: No, the landline party's Text Telephone equipment shall not need modifications or additions in order to be compatible and to achieve the desired error rate. The standard shall be compatible with equipment specified in ITU recommendation V.18 (including its annexes) and V.18 with V.61 for simultaneous voice and text.

questions.question: During a voice or video call, one party begins using the Global Text Telephony text feature. What effort must be made, and what is the default priority order among the possible text-conversation modes?
questions.reference_answer: An effort shall be made to establish text conversation, and it shall be possible to start text conversation during an already-established voice or video call by adding the text component. The default mode order, prioritising modes allowing simultaneous voice and text, shall be: IP Multimedia, CS Multimedia, data path text plus voice, voice path text.

questions.question: Must Global Text Telephony emergency calls be possible without a SIM/USIM module, in the same host environments where such calls are enabled for voice, and must supporting GTT for emergency calls come at the expense of normal emergency calls?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, GTT emergency calls shall be possible without the SIM/USIM module in the same host environments as such calls are enabled for voice. No, support of GTT service for emergency calls shall not jeopardise normal emergency calls.

questions.question: Under the IMS basic communication cases table, is Access-Network-to-Access-Network communication required to be supported on a per-network basis, and is Internal-Network-Resource-to-Access-Network communication also required?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, both are required: a network based on IMS shall support Access Network to Access Network communication, and Internal Network Resource to Access Network communication, as required basic communication cases per Table C.1.

questions.question: A local number or short code arrives at the HPLMN with a Local Context Indicator the HPLMN can interpret. What must the HPLMN do with it, and what must happen if the HPLMN is unable to resolve or route the received number?
questions.reference_answer: The HPLMN should interpret the short code to a globally routable URI or E.164 number according to the LCI value, and then correctly route the call. If the HPLMN is unable to resolve or route the received number, an error message shall be returned to the originating UE.

questions.question: For WebRTC IMS client access, in situations where the data communications do not traverse the operator network, does the media travel end to end without protocol conversion, and can it then be subject to different regulatory constraints than operator-traversing communications?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, in such situations WebRTC media travels end to end between two WebRTC IMS clients without any protocol conversion, and may then not be subject to the same regulatory constraints as communications that do traverse the operator network; end-to-end security may then be provided as an optional service enhancement.

questions.question: For the Packet Switched Streaming Service, must the number of implementations of each media type be minimized, and what consideration drives that requirement?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the number of implementations of each media type shall be kept to a minimum, considering the implementation impact on terminals, interoperability, content mobility, and backward compatibility.

questions.question: A PSS user has activated a streaming session and then receives a phone call. What must she be able to do with the streaming session, and what can she do after pausing it?
questions.reference_answer: The user shall have the possibility to pause the streaming session so she can decide whether she wants it to continue; after pausing, the user can choose to resume the streaming session.

questions.question: Must the PSS and MMS be able to interact with each other, and must the interfaces and protocols used between the PSS and other 3GPP multimedia delivery services be standardized?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible for the PSS to interact with the MMS and other 3GPP multimedia delivery services, and the interfaces and protocols used between them shall be standardized.

questions.question: Under the Generic User Profile, if a master component is located outside the home network, must the home operator be able to copy it into the home network?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the home operator shall be able to copy master components which are located outside the home network to the home network.

questions.question: For GUP network requirements, must the GUP interface be independent of the structure and semantics of the underlying data, and must GUP access support retrieving just a selected part of the profile rather than only the whole profile?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: the GUP Interface shall be independent of the structure and semantics of the data, and the GUP access mechanism shall support accessing either the whole profile data or a selected part of it.

questions.question: Does the 3GPP Generic User Profile specification mandate that any 3GPP service-specific data be part of the GUP, and what must still be specified to facilitate separate service-specific definitions?
questions.reference_answer: No, the specification does not mandate any 3GPP service-specific data to be part of the Generic User Profile. However, the common data types shall be specified to facilitate the separate work on service-specific definitions, e.g. for the user profile in HSS.

questions.question: For SRF-based automated voice services, is it possible to charge the user based on a free model subsidised by advertising revenue, and what population of subscribers must these services be available to?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, charging by a free model subsidised by advertising revenue from advertisement spots shall be possible. SRF-based automated voice services shall be available to both pre-paid and post-paid subscribers.

questions.question: Can a network operator permit or prevent access to a third-party SRF-based automated voice service, and on what two bases can the operator administer this authorization?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the network operator shall be able to permit or prevent access to a third-party service. The operator shall be able to administer the authorization of an SRF-based automated voice service on a user basis as well as on a service basis.

questions.question: Must the network be able to distinguish an SRF (speech recognition) session from a basic voice session, and for what purpose is this distinction given as an example?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible for the network to distinguish a SRF session from a basic voice session, for example for charging purposes.

questions.question: When adapting the distribution of an MBMS user service across access networks, can this adaptation in one access network affect the QoS of that MBMS user service in a different access network or a different part of the same access network?
questions.reference_answer: No, adaptation of the distribution of an MBMS user service to the QoS resources in one access network or part of an access network shall not affect the QoS of the MBMS user service in other access networks or other parts of the same access network.

questions.question: For MBMS pre-delivery verification, over what kind of connection must the UE inform the network of the start of services, and what type of previously stored bearer-specific information may this verification also carry to the BM-SC?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall provide a secure means of pre-delivery verification transmitted over a point-to-point connection to the home/visited network, which shall also support carrying previously stored bearer-specific non-real-time information, such as historic C/I measurements for the serving cell.

questions.question: For MBMS delivery verification, must this verification data be transmitted over a point-to-point connection, and can it be relayed onward to the service provider?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the UE shall provide the secure delivery verification over a point-to-point connection to the home/visited network, and this delivery verification may be relayed to the service provider.

questions.question: Under IMS Group Management, must each group have at least one group administrator at all times, and is the group administrator automatically also a group member?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, each group shall have at least one group administrator at all times, but the group administrator is not a group member by default.

questions.question: In IMS Group Management, must every group be assigned a globally unique group identifier, and who allocates that identifier?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, each group shall have a globally unique, addressable group identifier, which may be suggested by the group administrator when creating the group but is allocated by the IMS service provider.

questions.question: Under IMS Group Management, must it be possible to hide a group member's identifier (anonymity), and can each group member be associated with specific rights defining what actions they may perform?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: it shall be possible to hide the member identifier (anonymity), and each member shall be associated with rights that define which actions the member is allowed to perform.

questions.question: For group management security, must the group content and change notifications be protected against attacks such as eavesdropping, tampering, and replay, and must they only be supplied to authenticated and authorized users?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: it shall be possible to protect the request for group content and change notifications from attacks such as eavesdropping, tampering, and replay, and it shall only be possible for the group content and notifications to be supplied to authenticated and authorized users and applications.

questions.question: Under Personal Network access control, which UE has the access rights to register or deregister private UEs and Guest UEs?
questions.reference_answer: The UE nominated by the PN-User as the default UE for access control has the access rights to register/deregister private UEs and guest UEs.

questions.question: When a user has services from multiple operators available simultaneously and the same service is offered by more than one, which network shall the UE be prioritized to receive the subscribed service from, unless directed otherwise?
questions.reference_answer: Unless directed by the home operator's network, the UE shall be prioritized to receive subscribed services from the home operator's network.

questions.question: When the 5G system maintains service continuity as a user's serving network changes to a different operator's network offering the same service, what business precondition underlies this capability?
questions.reference_answer: A business agreement is required between the network operators for the 5G system to maintain service continuity with minimum interruption when switching between operators offering the same service.

questions.question: What maximum Time-To-First-Fix must the 5G system provide for its positioning services in general, and for which subset of positioning services must it additionally support a mechanism reaching a tighter TTFF?
questions.reference_answer: The 5G system shall be able to provide 5G positioning services with a TTFF less than 30 seconds, and for some 5G positioning services it shall additionally support mechanisms to provide a TTFF less than 10 seconds.

questions.question: What velocity accuracy and positioning service availability must the 5G system support for determining a UE's speed and 3D direction of travel?
questions.reference_answer: The 5G system shall support a mechanism to determine the UE's velocity with a positioning service availability of 99%, an accuracy better than 0.5 m/s for speed, and an accuracy better than 5 degrees for the 3-dimension direction of travel.

questions.question: Network diagnostics should be proactive rather than only reactive. What four capabilities should network diagnostics provide beyond simply detecting failures early?
questions.reference_answer: Network diagnostics should be able to accurately differentiate malfunctions/failures and evaluate their impact on the service/network, provide clear explanations about what happened, suggest corrective actions, and possibly perform those corrective actions automatically.

questions.question: For an MSGin5G application-to-point AOMT message used to control an IoT device (e.g. unlocking a shared bike), what latency property must the MSGin5G Service support given that these messages are time-sensitive?
questions.reference_answer: The AOMT messages are time-sensitive, so the MSGin5G Service needs to support low-latency delivery of AOMT messages.

questions.question: A UE that does not support the 3GPP MSGin5G message service at all wants to exchange messages using it. How can it still connect, and over which access types can that connection to the gateway occur?
questions.reference_answer: Such a UE can connect to the MSGin5G Service via an MSGin5G Gateway that translates between the MSGin5G Service and the non-3GPP message service. That connection to the gateway can be via 3GPP access or non-3GPP access, e.g. WLAN.

questions.question: For MSGin5G point-to-point messaging between different applications on a UE, what must the MSGin5G Service be able to determine about an incoming message so it can route it correctly?
questions.reference_answer: The MSGin5G Service needs to identify which application a message is to be delivered to, so it can route the message to the corresponding application server in the network and application client in the UE.

questions.question: For low-latency deterministic periodic multicast traffic supporting an intercom system with 1000 active UEs, what maximum downlink end-to-end latency and packet error rate must be met?
questions.reference_answer: The intercom system profile requires a downlink end-to-end latency of 7 ms and a packet error rate of 10^-4.

questions.question: For PWS Primary Notification, how much data is it expected to convey, and why does the specification keep it that small?
questions.reference_answer: The Primary Notification shall convey data small enough to be sent quickly on the network, typically a few bytes, to achieve quick information delivery for the imminent occurrence of an event like an earthquake or tsunami.

questions.question: In PWS security, if no regional or national regulatory requirement for integrity protection of Warning Notifications exists, what must the PWS-UE do with all Warning Notifications?
questions.reference_answer: There shall be no integrity protection of Warning Notifications in that case, and all Warning Notifications shall be presented to the PWS application on the PWS-UE.

questions.question: Can reception and presentation of a PWS Warning Notification to the user pre-empt an active voice or data session, and to which kinds of emergencies must Warning Notifications be limited?
questions.reference_answer: No, reception and presentation of Warning Notifications to the user shall not pre-empt an active voice or data session. Warning Notifications shall be limited to those emergencies where life or property is at imminent risk and some responsive action should be taken.

questions.question: Must PWS-capable UEs (PWS-UE) that are in idle mode be able to receive broadcast Warning Notifications, and are Warning Notifications processed in any particular order relative to each other?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, PWS-UEs in idle mode shall be capable of receiving broadcast Warning Notifications. Warning Notifications are processed by PWS on a first-in, first-out basis, subject to regulatory requirements.

questions.question: Under the Evolved Packet System, can a UE have simultaneously more than one active PDN connection exchanging traffic with more than one peer, and under what condition is this allowed?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the Evolved Packet System shall support a UE having simultaneously more than one active PDN connection exchanging traffic with more than one peer, when the network policies and user subscription allow it.

questions.question: Is a single application running on the UE required by the EPS to send and receive its traffic through multiple PDNs simultaneously?
questions.reference_answer: No, a single application running on the UE shall not be required to send and receive traffic through multiple PDNs.

questions.question: When a UE receives service via a non-3GPP access, must the PLMN providing that access be able to indicate to the UE the local availability of 3GPP access, and in what manner must this indication be given?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible for the PLMN that provides the non-3GPP access to indicate the local availability of 3GPP access to the UE, and this must be done in a secure manner, subject to the capabilities of the non-3GPP access network.

questions.question: For Indirect 3GPP Communication via an Evolved ProSe Remote UE, must the confidentiality and integrity of end-to-end data and signalling be comparable to the case of a direct 3GPP communication, and must lawful interception and PWS regulatory support be maintained regardless of access path?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: the 3GPP network shall ensure end-to-end confidentiality and integrity for an Indirect 3GPP Communication comparable to a direct 3GPP communication, and shall support regional or national regulatory requirements, such as lawful interception and PWS, independently of whether the UE accesses via direct or indirect 3GPP communication.

questions.question: For EPS Service Reachability, when a third party has placed an IP traffic-flow restriction, can that third party prohibit Service Reachability by intentionally blocking PLMN IP-based services, and must pre-existing EPS security be maintained?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the third party that placed the IP traffic-flow restriction shall be able to prohibit Service Reachability by intentionally blocking PLMN IP-based services, and pre-existing EPS security shall be maintained.

questions.question: In a combinational CS/IMS service, if media accepted by a user cannot be rendered simultaneously with the CS call, which type of speech and which type of video/image must be given preference?
questions.reference_answer: CS speech must be given preference over IMS speech/audio, while IMS video and images must be given preference over CS video.

questions.question: In a combinational service, if the calling party's CLI is restricted as a result of CLIR, what must the calling party's UE or the network ensure regarding an associated outgoing IMS session?
questions.reference_answer: The calling party's UE or the network shall ensure that the Public User Identity of the calling party is also restricted when establishing an outgoing IMS session associated with this CS call and when responding to an incoming IMS session associated with this CS call.

questions.question: Can an MCX Service Administrator limit the total number of MCX Service Groups an MCX User may be affiliated to simultaneously, and must an MCX User affiliate with a group before participating in that group's communications?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the MCX Service shall provide a mechanism for an MCX Service Administrator to limit the total number (Nc2) of MCX Service Groups an MCX User can be affiliated to simultaneously, and the MCX Service shall require that MCX Users affiliate with MCX Service Groups prior to participating in the communications of those groups.

questions.question: During MCX ambient listening, to how many parties is information transmitted, and is any indication given to the MCX User or people around them that the ambient listening is occurring?
questions.reference_answer: Information is only transmitted to one party in the communication, i.e. a dispatcher or authorized MCX User acting in a similar role. No, ambient listening is designed to give no indication to the MCX User or the people around them that it is happening.

questions.question: Must an MCX Service User be notified when their own request to transmit is removed from the MCX request queue, and can an authorised user (other than that user) also remove that request?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: an MCX Service User shall be notified when his request to transmit is removed from the MCX request queue, and the MCX Service shall provide a mechanism for an authorised user to remove another user's MCX request to transmit from the queue.

questions.question: If an MCX Emergency Group Communication occurs on a group that an MCX User is affiliated to, but that user is already in a Private Communication, must the user be notified of the Emergency Group Communication?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the MCX Service shall ensure that the MCX User is notified of the MCX Emergency Group Communication even though they are already in a Private Communication.

questions.question: In off-network MCVideo, at what point can a Participant cancel its request to transmit, and what must the MCVideo Administrator be able to configure regarding automatic termination of such requests?
questions.reference_answer: The MCVideo service, when operating off-network, shall provide a mechanism for a Participant to cancel its request to transmit at any stage, including before the request has been granted. The MCVideo service shall also provide a mechanism for the MCVideo Administrator to configure parameter(s) relating to the automatic termination of an off-network request to transmit.

questions.question: For MCVideo video material with evidentiary potential, must the service provide means for tamper DETECTION, and is tamper PROTECTION a mandatory or recommended capability?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the MCVideo service shall provide means for tamper detection for evidentiary video material. Tamper protection, by contrast, is only a should-level (recommended) requirement, not mandatory.

questions.question: In an MCVideo video conference, can a participant choose to disable video entirely and still use the video conferencing service, and can each participant choose a subset of received video streams while still hearing all audio streams?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: each participant shall be able to disable video and use the video conferencing service as a voice-only conference service, and each participant shall be able to choose and display a subset of video streams from other participants while continuing to receive audio streams from all participants.

questions.question: In off-network MCData, when a Participant's transmit time limit is reached, what must the Off-Network MCData Service do with that Participant's permission to transmit, and must the Participant be warned before the limit is reached?
questions.reference_answer: The Off-Network MCData Service shall remove the permission to transmit from that Participant once the transmit limit has been reached. Yes, it shall also provide an indication to the transmitting Participant a configurable amount of time before the limit is reached.

questions.question: Can an authorized person for an MCData user revoke, on demand, a previously granted authorization for that user to send IP data to a specific destination?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the MCData Service shall enable the authorized person to revoke such authorization on demand.

questions.question: For MCData off-network transmission override, how many levels must the priority hierarchy used for granting an override request contain at minimum?
questions.reference_answer: The priority hierarchy used for granting a request to override an active MCData transmission shall contain at least four (4) levels.

questions.question: For FRMCS CCTV offload from train to ground, which side initiates the offload, and under what condition can it start?
questions.reference_answer: The CCTV offload shall be initiated by the ground communication unit, once sufficient signal quality is available between the ground and mobile communication units.

questions.question: For FRMCS, can the transfer of CCTV archives be allowed to affect mission-critical communication?
questions.reference_answer: No, the transfer of CCTV archives shall not affect mission critical communication.

questions.question: A subscriber has Call Forwarding Unconditional active. If she then tries to activate Barring of all Incoming Calls, what happens?
questions.reference_answer: The activation of Barring of all Incoming Calls is denied, because Call Forwarding Unconditional is already active, and the mobile subscriber shall be informed of this supplementary service incompatibility.

questions.question: Under the Multimedia Telephony Service, if an appropriate bilateral agreement exists, can the home network instruct the visited network to play a network announcement or tone to the subscriber during a session? And is the UE allowed to locally render tones to indicate call diversion or queueing?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, given an appropriate bilateral agreement, the home network shall be able to instruct the visited network to play a network announcement or tone during a session. No, the UE shall not locally render tones to indicate diversion or queueing of calls.

questions.question: For 3GPP restricted local operator services, if a UE recognizes an origination attempt to such a service but has not received an indication from the serving system that these services are available, what must the UE do with the origination attempt?
questions.reference_answer: The UE shall block the origination attempt.

questions.question: For 3GPP restricted local operator services, if a UE explicitly requests network access solely to receive such services, is it put into limited service state?
questions.reference_answer: No, a UE explicitly requesting access to a network offering restricted local operator services, in order to receive them, shall not be put into limited service state.

questions.question: The IPLMN supports a lower CAMEL phase than the one negotiated between HPLMN and IPLMN, and the CSE determines a provisioned service will not operate correctly as a result. What actions can the CSE operator take?
questions.reference_answer: The CSE shall take such action as may be decided by the CSE operator, including denying the call request or handling the call using only the CAMEL capabilities negotiated between the HPLMN and the IPLMN.

questions.question: In off-network MCPTT, an MCPTT UE has no credentials for a specific MCPTT User and must still operate. Under what condition can it do so, and who defines the parameters (e.g. groups, priority, QoS) used for that temporary operation?
questions.reference_answer: An MCPTT UE without credentials of a specific MCPTT User can still operate in off-network mode if so configured by an MCPTT Administrator, who defines the specific parameters and attributes, such as groups, MCPTT Emergency behaviour, priority and QoS attributes, associated with a temporary MCPTT User Identity for that operation.

questions.question: For Disaster Condition support, must the 3GPP system be able to provide service to a Disaster Inbound Roamer everywhere in the network, or only within a specific region?
questions.reference_answer: Only within the specific region where the Disaster Condition applies — the 3GPP system shall be able to support provision of service to a Disaster Inbound Roamer only within that specific region.

questions.question: In a mobile-initiated USSD operation, what two indicators must the operation contain, and who decides the values selected for them?
questions.reference_answer: The mobile-initiated operation shall contain an alphabet indicator and a language indicator; the selection of values for these indicators is a matter for the user.

questions.question: A CUG subscriber has neither incoming-call-barred nor outgoing-call-barred restrictions within her CUGs. Upon receipt of a call setup attempt to or from her, what must the network check before establishing the call?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall check the validity of the CUG call setup attempt in conjunction with the access capabilities subscribed to, before attempting to establish the call to the required destination.

questions.question: Subscriber A has received a CCBS Recall and the network is awaiting her acceptance of it. Can subscriber A register in another location area at that moment?
questions.reference_answer: No, Subscriber A cannot register in another location area while having received a CCBS Recall and the network is awaiting her acceptance of it.

questions.question: For USSD messages that fall under Case a) (reserved for HPLMN use, e.g. 1X(Y) with X=0-4), if the serving network receives such a message from a visiting subscriber, what must it do with it?
questions.reference_answer: The serving network shall pass the USSD message directly to the HPLMN, because this case is reserved for HPLMN use.

questions.question: If the HLR receiving a mobile-initiated USSD operation does not support the alphabet indicated in it, what must happen?
questions.reference_answer: The HLR shall inform the UE that it does not support the indicated alphabet.

questions.question: An authorized MCPTT User ignores a Manual Commencement Private Call (with Floor control) request from another MCPTT User. Does the calling MCPTT User receive any indication of the reason for call failure?
questions.reference_answer: No, ignoring a Manual Commencement Private Call (with Floor control) results in no indication of the reason for call failure being sent to the calling MCPTT User.

questions.question: For CAMEL PDP-deactivation event monitoring, once the CSE has concluded issuing its instructions, how many of the final instructions (release the GPRS session, or continue processing) may it issue, and under what condition is releasing the GPRS session a valid instruction?
questions.reference_answer: The CSE shall send one and only one of the final instructions. Releasing the GPRS Session may only be given as an instruction if the PDP deactivation event is reported within a GPRS Session relationship.

questions.question: For the Advice of Charge service, if the charge information cannot be stored in the MS, what must happen to use of the telecommunications service?
questions.reference_answer: Use of the telecommunications service shall be prevented if the charge cannot be stored in the MS.

questions.question: For CAMEL call-establishment monitoring, when no relationship exists yet with a CSE for the call, and the CSE arms a mid-call DTMF event, to which network is the arming and detection of that event limited?
questions.reference_answer: The arming and detection of the mid-call DTMF event shall be limited to the VPLMN.

questions.question: Due to interworking problems, what must the service operator ensure regarding the combination of e-value sending and call-period control features in the same call for a subscriber with Enhanced CSE capability for Dialled Services?
questions.reference_answer: The service operator shall ensure that sending of e-values and call period control is not used by other services in the same call of that served subscriber.

questions.question: For Barring of All Incoming Calls, what happens to a call that has been forwarded to a subscriber who has this barring service active?
questions.reference_answer: Calls forwarded to that subscriber will be denied, just as any other incoming call to that subscriber would be.

questions.question: Under Call Forwarding Unconditional, if it is activated, does the network's behaviour depend on the state of the call termination?
questions.reference_answer: No, if Call Forwarding Unconditional is activated, calls are forwarded no matter what the condition of the termination is; the served mobile subscriber's ability to originate calls is unaffected.

questions.question: For the Push Service's privacy requirements, can an operator override a Push Recipient's privacy preferences, and under what condition?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, an operator shall at any time be able to override a Push Recipient's privacy preferences if required to do so by legal authorities.

questions.question: For GUP privacy control, does GUP authorization depend on who set the privacy rules for a given part of the GUP data?
questions.reference_answer: No, the GUP authorization shall be independent of who has set the privacy rules for each part of the GUP data; a generic mechanism shall ensure only data with a valid authority can be created, read, modified, or deleted.

questions.question: For GUP privacy, if lawful interception or another regulatory requirement applies, can GUP data still be delivered to authorities despite a user's privacy settings?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, lawful interception and other regulatory requirements may imply that GUP data is delivered to authorities despite the privacy settings.

questions.question: For CCBS deactivation, must the mobile subscriber be told whether her deactivation request succeeded, and what must happen to the network's stored references (queue entries, timers) to a deactivated CCBS request?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, subscriber A shall be informed that the deactivation is successful. Deactivation of a CCBS request shall result in all references to that request, i.e. entries in the A and B queues and timers, being removed from the network.

questions.question: For MExE Classmarks, must the use of MExE Classmarks be supported during capability negotiation between the MExE service provider and the MExE UE, and is a MExE Classmark the same thing as the existing UE Classmark?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the use of MExE Classmarks shall be supported during capability negotiation between the MExE service provider and the MExE UE. No, the MExE Classmark is distinct and unrelated to the existing UE Classmark.

questions.question: For Global Text Telephony general requirements, what must be standardised to ensure interoperability across different networks and terminals?
questions.reference_answer: An identified set of functionalities and protocols shall be standardised to ensure interoperability across networks and terminals in support of GTT.

questions.question: The Explicit Call Transfer (ECT) Consultative variant requires media sessions to already exist on both of the transferring party's communications before transfer. Is the ECT Consultative service required to apply only to IMS users?
questions.reference_answer: No, the service should be applicable independent of whether party B and party C are IMS users or not.

questions.question: Can a user (other than the PSAP) use Explicit Call Transfer on an emergency call, or on a call identified as a callback to an emergency call?
questions.reference_answer: No, the use of ECT on an emergency call, or a call identified as a callback to an emergency call, by a user that is not the PSAP, shall be precluded.

questions.question: For ECT Blind transfer, since the transferring party has not had prior communication with the third party, is the transfer result known in advance? What must be done for the transferring party regarding the establishment state?
questions.reference_answer: No, because the call towards the third party is blind, the result of the transfer is not knowable in advance. The transferring party should be informed of the establishment state of the transfer before being released from the communication.

questions.question: In service function management for network exposure, must the operator be able to manage service function chaining both when Hosted Services are provided by the operator itself and when they are provided by a third party?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the service function management shall be able to manage service function chaining for deployments where the Hosted Services are provided by the operator and for deployments where they are provided by a third party.

questions.question: During ECT invocation, can the two CS call parties who end up in speech connection after the transfer initiate IMS sessions associated with that CS call?
questions.reference_answer: No, because the two CS call parties have not exchanged Radio Network and Terminal capabilities with one another, nor are they aware of each other's Line Identification, they are not capable of initiating IMS sessions associated with the CS call.

questions.question: For the CSE-controlled call disconnection procedure, once the CSE has issued its instructions, how many of the final instructions may it issue, and what are the two options?
questions.reference_answer: The CSE shall issue one and only one final instruction: either continue the call processing (i.e. release the call), or continue the call processing with modified information.

questions.question: For CAMEL announcement and tones insertion, who is responsible for administering announcements by default, and under what condition can the VPLMN operator also administer them?
questions.reference_answer: The HPLMN operator is responsible for the administration of announcements by default. The VPLMN operator may also administer announcements if there is an appropriate bilateral agreement.

questions.question: For CAMEL announcement and tones insertion, must it be possible to play tones efficiently using local tone generators?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible to play tones efficiently using local tone generators.

questions.question: When a mobile subscriber does not completely specify which Call Forwarding on Mobile Subscriber Busy request is to be erased, what must the network do?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall reject the erasure request with an appropriate cause, since the subscriber has not completely specified which request is to be erased.

questions.question: Under Access Category rules, must Access Category 0 (MO signalling resulting from paging) ever be barred, regardless of Access Identity?
questions.reference_answer: No, Access Category 0 shall not be barred, irrespective of Access Identities.

questions.question: For the Call Waiting Multicall interaction, when the subscriber already has at least one ongoing call and a new terminating call is not speech, under what two conditions must Call Waiting be invoked?
questions.reference_answer: Call Waiting shall be invoked if the maximum number of bearers (Nbr) has been reached and Call Waiting is active and operative for at least one of the basic services currently in use.

questions.question: Under Multicall's interaction with Call Hold, when the maximum number of CS bearers has not been reached and a terminating call is indicated, must the subscriber still be able to accept it by applying Call Hold to an active speech call?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, irrespective of whether the maximum number of CS bearers (Nbr) is reached, she shall be able to accept the terminating call by applying Call Hold to an active speech call, making the bearer of the held call available to the new call.

questions.question: Under the Multicall supplementary service, what is the maximum number of held calls allowed per subscriber, regardless of the Multicall feature?
questions.reference_answer: There is no change to the maximum number of held calls allowed for Multicall: the maximum number of held calls is still 1 per subscriber.
