questions.question: For CFNRy invocation, if the limit of successive forwardings is reached and an additional forwarding is attempted, and the forwarded call then cannot be completed to the forwarded-to destination, what does the network do, and does the notification to the calling user reveal that the call had been forwarded?
questions.reference_answer: The network will clear the call towards the calling user with an indication that the call cannot be completed; this indication shall not include information that the call has been forwarded.

questions.question: For tandem call forwarding, to what range of values should the maximum number of tandem forwarding connections be limited, and why?
questions.reference_answer: The maximum number of tandem forwarding connections should be limited to a value between 1 and 5, in order to prevent infinite looping.

questions.question: For GPRS delay class 1 (Predictive) with SDU size 128 octets, what are the maximum mean transfer delay and the maximum 95-percentile delay?
questions.reference_answer: For delay class 1 at SDU size 128 octets, the maximum mean transfer delay is less than 0.5 seconds and the maximum 95-percentile delay is less than 1.5 seconds.

questions.question: Does the GPRS delay parameter include transfer delays incurred in external networks?
questions.reference_answer: No, the delay parameter defines the end-to-end transfer delay within the GPRS network(s) and does not include transfer delays in external networks.

questions.question: For MPS handover of a voice call from PS to CS, which specific call is transferred and given priority treatment in CS, and what happens to remaining non-MPS voice sessions still in PS?
questions.reference_answer: Only the active call, or if all calls are on hold then only the most recently active voice call, shall be transferred and receive priority treatment in CS. Any remaining non-MPS voice sessions in PS may be released.

questions.question: For MPS handover, must any remaining MPS data sessions still in PS be released when a voice call is handed over to CS?
questions.reference_answer: No, any remaining MPS sessions, such as MPS data, in PS shall not be released.

questions.question: MCPTT Emergency Private Calls (with Floor control) have pre-emptive priority over all other types of MCPTT calls, with three named exceptions. What are those exceptions?
questions.reference_answer: The exceptions are System Calls, MCPTT Emergency Group Calls, and other MCPTT Emergency Private Calls (with Floor control) — MCPTT Emergency Private Calls have pre-emptive priority over every other type of MCPTT call except those three.

questions.question: A CUG subscriber has a preferential CUG but no OA capability, and enters only a request to suppress the preferential CUG, without any CUG index. What happens to her call?
questions.reference_answer: The call shall be rejected, since she requested suppression of the preferential CUG without entering a CUG index and without OA capability.

questions.question: During the network subset personalisation process, if any of the pre-personalisation checks in clause 13 fail, what happens to the process?
questions.reference_answer: The personalisation process shall be terminated if any of the pre-personalisation checks fail.

questions.question: For the Multiple Subscriber Profile feature interacting with SMS, can the network indicate which profile was used for a mobile-terminated short message, and from which profile are all mobile-originated short messages sent by default?
questions.reference_answer: No, it will not be possible to indicate the profile used for the MT case. All MO short messages will be sent from the default profile, unless a registered or explicitly selected profile is used instead.

questions.question: For an MSP subscriber roaming in a network that does not support MSP Phase 2, from which profile are all mobile-originated short messages sent and charged?
questions.reference_answer: All MO short messages will be sent from and charged to the default profile while roaming in a network not supporting MSP Phase 2.

questions.question: For Call Forwarding Unconditional registration, is the network required to validate information related to the forwarded-to number?
questions.reference_answer: No, the network is not required to validate information related to the forwarded-to number.

questions.question: For CFNL, if user B activates communication forwarding not registered AFTER user A has already activated CCNL on user B, and a CCNL communication from A then encounters a not-logged-in condition at B, what two treatments are possible for that communication?
questions.reference_answer: Either the procedures of CCNL shall be applied, or the communication shall be forwarded as a normal communication.

questions.question: For GUP data transfer security, what must be true about the level of security applied to a transfer of User Profile data, relative to the data's confidentiality and the transfer's endpoints and routes?
questions.reference_answer: The secure mechanisms applied shall be appropriate to the level of confidentiality of the data, the endpoints of the transfer, and the routes available for the transfer of the data.

questions.question: For GUP data transfer, must it be possible for the consumer of data to detect whether the data has been tampered with during transmission?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, it shall be possible for the consumer of data to detect whether the data have been tampered with during transmission.

questions.question: Under CAMEL Call Party Handling, what is the minimum number of parties the IPLMN/VPLMN must support in a CPH group, and can one of these parties be a Specialised Resource Function?
questions.reference_answer: The IPLMN/VPLMN shall support at least 6 parties in a group, of which one may be a Specialised Resource Function.

questions.question: Under CAMEL Call Party Handling, is it required that a leg or group of legs be transferred between separate CPH configurations?
questions.reference_answer: No, it is not required to transfer a leg or a group of legs between separate CPH configurations.

questions.question: For CAMEL's change-of-basic-service event reporting, in which phase(s) of a call does the PLMN report basic service changes, even though the CSE can arm this event in various phases?
questions.reference_answer: The PLMN reports the basic service changes only in the active phase of the call.

questions.question: For MCX Service prioritization requirements, what must be established dynamically and in real-time regarding the relative priorities of MCX Service Group Communications and other traffic — for both transport and presentation?
questions.reference_answer: The MCX Service shall provide a mechanism to establish, dynamically and in real-time, the relative priorities of MCX Service Group Communications and other traffic, with respect to both transport and presentation.

questions.question: For MCX Service group membership lists, what identifier(s) must be used to reference each member when the list of currently affiliated members is provided?
questions.reference_answer: The list shall reference each member by MCX Service User ID and/or associated aliases.

questions.question: For MCX Group Regrouping, when MCX Service Groups with different security and priority levels are combined into a newly created temporary group, how many security levels and priority levels can the new temporary group have?
questions.reference_answer: The newly created temporary MCX Service Group can have only a single security level and a single priority level (along with a single floor control method and set of operational characteristics), even though the combined groups may have had different values.

questions.question: In off-network MCX Service Emergency Group Communication, what must an MCX UE that initiated the emergency communication be capable of transmitting to all other users in the communication?
questions.reference_answer: It shall be capable of transmitting its MCX Service User ID and an indication that it is an off-network MCX Service Emergency Group Communication to all other users.

questions.question: When an MCX UE transitions its off-network connection from a ProSe UE-to-UE relay to on-network operation for an ongoing communication, what must the MCX Service do regarding interruption?
questions.reference_answer: The MCX Service shall minimize the interruption to the ongoing MCX Service communication during that transition from off-network via a ProSe UE-to-UE relay to on-network operation.

questions.question: For MCData robot control latency requirements, what is the default control latency for an aerial unmanned vehicle, and for a terrestrial unmanned vehicle?
questions.reference_answer: The default control latency shall be under 50 ms for an aerial unmanned vehicle and under 400 ms for a terrestrial unmanned vehicle.

questions.question: For the MCData default priority scheme controlling robots, must the data exchanged for controlling the robot be capable of being pre-empted?
questions.reference_answer: No, the MCData Service default priority scheme shall ensure that data exchanged for controlling a robot has relevantly high priority among user data and cannot be pre-empted.

questions.question: For MCVideo robot control, what are the four minimum video control latency figures required for an aerial unmanned vehicle during take-off/landing, an aerial unmanned vehicle while flying, an aquatic/submarine unmanned vehicle, and a terrestrial unmanned vehicle moving at less than 120 km/h?
questions.reference_answer: Take-off/landing of an aerial vehicle: under 100 ms; flying aerial vehicle: under 300 ms; aquatic/submarine vehicle: under 500 ms; terrestrial vehicle under 120 km/h: under 400 ms.

questions.question: For MCVideo aerial unmanned vehicle support, what maximum altitude above the floor must be supported?
questions.reference_answer: The MCVideo service shall support aerial unmanned vehicles at an altitude of up to 150 meters above the floor.

questions.question: For UUS on Explicit Call Transfer, when calls are transferred by ECT, what must the network do with UUS services that were activated on either call prior to the ECT invocation, and is a specific notification sent to the involved subscribers about this?
questions.reference_answer: The network shall automatically deactivate any UUS services activated on either of the calls prior to the ECT invocation. No specific notification shall be sent to the involved subscribers about this deactivation.

questions.question: For IMS Multimedia Telephony media codec negotiation with a visited network, when the media plane is locally broken-out or broken-in within that visited network, who may instruct the visited network to perform transcoding?
questions.reference_answer: The home network may instruct the visited network to perform transcoding in this case.

questions.question: When end-to-end codec negotiation for IMS Multimedia Telephony fails, should transcoding be offered as a mandatory feature or only as an operator option?
questions.reference_answer: Transcoding should be provided only as an operator option when the codec negotiation fails, not as a mandatory feature.

questions.question: For PS-only subscriptions aimed at improving numbering resource efficiency, must a network operator be able to provide such subscriptions without assigning an MSISDN, and is remote UE configuration required to be supportable without an MSISDN?
questions.reference_answer: Yes to both: a network operator shall be able to provide PS-only subscriptions with or without assigning an MSISDN, and remote UE configuration shall be supported without the use of an MSISDN.

questions.question: When a user enters PIN or PIN2 on a UE, for how long may each entered digit be displayed to the user at most?
questions.reference_answer: Each entered digit should not be displayed to the user for longer than one second.

questions.question: For the vertical accuracy of LCS location estimates in Value Added Services, what is the approximate range the vertical accuracy may span, and what does the finer end of that range let the server resolve?
questions.reference_answer: The vertical accuracy may range from about three metres to hundreds of metres; the three-metre end of the range is fine enough to resolve a UE's position within one floor of a building.

questions.question: The MCX Service supports configuring how many MCX Service Group Communications an MCX UE can receive simultaneously, via parameter Nc4. Is a separate configurable limit, Nc5, provided for how many an MCX User (rather than the UE) can simultaneously receive?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, the MCX Service shall provide a separate mechanism to configure the number (Nc5) of MCX Service Group Communications to be simultaneously received by an MCX User, distinct from the UE-level limit Nc4.

questions.question: SM Deferred Delivery supports relative and absolute timing options. What must the relative-timing text convey, and what must the absolute-timing text convey instead?
questions.reference_answer: Relative timing text conveys how many more days, hours, and minutes shall pass before the message is delivered, while absolute timing text conveys the specific Date and Time for the message to be delivered.

questions.question: For BS 20 transparent digital interworking (regular mode), which fixed network user rates listed in the table use V.110 rate adaptation with UDI information transfer capability and are all marked as Supported across UTRAN, GERAN Iu mode, and GERAN A/Gb mode?
questions.reference_answer: All the listed rates from 0.3 kbit/s up to 38.4 kbit/s (0.3, 1.2, 2.4, 4.8, 9.6, 14.4, 19.2, 28.8, and 38.4 kbit/s) use Asynch access with UDI transfer capability and V.110 rate adaptation, and are marked Supported for UTRAN, GERAN Iu mode, and GERAN A/Gb mode.

questions.question: A user carries two SIMs in one handset (MUSIM) and needs to place an emergency call while one USIM is only in limited service. In what priority order must the UE pick a USIM to originate the call, and what must it avoid doing to that call once it starts?
questions.reference_answer: A MUSIM UE shall select a USIM to originate an emergency call in the following priority: first a USIM in normal service, then a USIM in limited service state. The MUSIM UE shall avoid interruptions of the emergency call procedure of one USIM by other services running on the other USIM.

questions.question: A user's device cannot reach any network directly but a nearby relay UE is available, and the user needs to reach emergency services. What must the remote UE try first, and once its emergency session gets through the relay, how must the network route it to a PSAP?
questions.reference_answer: Subject to local regulatory requirements, the UE shall first attempt to make an emergency session via any available network; only if it fails to find a network that allows emergency sessions shall it attempt an emergency session via a relay UE. Once established, the 5G system shall route the emergency session to an appropriate PSAP for the location of the remote UE, which can be in the same country as the remote UE or not.

questions.question: An authority wants to broadcast a short text alert to every device in a disaster area using the messaging service built for machine-type and IoT devices, rather than a phone call. What is the maximum end-to-end latency the service must support for delivering this broadcast, and who besides an authorized application server is allowed to trigger it?
questions.reference_answer: The MSGin5G Service shall support broadcasting a text or data message with end-to-end latency less than [500] ms. Besides an authorized application server, an authorized UE is also allowed to send a broadcast message to all UEs within a specific area configured according to application policy.

questions.question: Which specifications define the NR ARFCN information element, and what does it identify in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 9.3.1.181 (NGAP), TS 38.423 clause 9.2.2.19 (XnAP), and TS 38.473 clause 9.3.1.17 (F1AP) all define NR ARFCN, within NR Frequency Info, as a mandatory Integer giving the RF Reference Frequency per TS 38.104 clause 5.4.2.1 — the absolute frequency position of the reference resource block (Common RB 0, i.e. Point A) of the carrier, for a given direction (UL/DL/SUL) of a cell.

questions.question: Which service operation provides UE information for terminating domain selection of IMS voice, and what optional output can it return?
questions.reference_answer: Namf_MT_ProvideDomainSelectionInfo (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.4.3) provides UE information for terminating domain selection of IMS voice to the consumer NF. Optional output includes an indication of whether the UE supports IMS voice over PS session, the time stamp of the last radio contact with the UE, and the current RAT type.

questions.question: Which specifications describe the LOCATION REPORTING FAILURE INDICATION message, and what triggers the NG-RAN node to send it?
questions.reference_answer: Both TS 38.413 clause 8.12.2.2 (successful operation) and clause 8.12.1.3 (abnormal conditions) describe the LOCATION REPORTING FAILURE INDICATION message. The NG-RAN node sends it to the AMF when it cannot fulfil a LOCATION REPORTING CONTROL request -- for example if that message contains multiple Location Reporting Reference ID IEs set to the same value -- with an appropriate cause value, and the AMF takes action based on the indicated cause.

questions.question: Which specifications define the DL Scrambling Code information element, and what value does it carry in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.331 clause 10.3.6.36d defines DL Scrambling Code (inside HS-DSCH paging system information, FDD only) as an optional secondary scrambling code to apply for HS-DSCH/HS-SCCH, defaulting to the primary CPICH scrambling code. TS 25.423 clause 9.2.2.11 (RNSAP) and TS 25.433 clause 9.2.2.13 (NBAP) both define DL Scrambling Code as the scrambling code used by the radio link, an Integer(0..15) where 0 denotes the cell's primary scrambling code and 1-15 denote secondary scrambling codes.

questions.question: Which specifications define the UE Radio Capability information element, and what does it identify in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 9.2.1.27 (S1AP) and TS 36.423 clause 9.2.173 (X2AP) both define UE Radio Capability as a mandatory OCTET STRING containing the UERadioAccessCapabilityInformation message from TS 36.331 (or the -NB variant in S1AP). TS 38.413 clause 9.3.1.74 (NGAP) defines the same IE, containing either the UERadioAccessCapabilityInformation message from TS 38.331 or the -NB message from TS 36.331. In all three it conveys the UE's radio access capabilities to the network node.

questions.question: What request body attributes must an AF include to allocate or refresh MBS TMGI(s) via the Nnef_MBSTMGI_Allocation service operation, and which stage-2 operation does it correspond to?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.522 clause 4.4.29.2.2 describes the Nnef_MBSTMGI_Allocation request (HTTP POST with a TmgiAllocRequest body) that must include the afId attribute and the tmgiParams attribute (and suppFeat if feature negotiation applies); it corresponds to the stage-2 Nnef_MBSTMGI_Allocate service operation defined in TS 23.247.

questions.question: What does the Nnef_UEId_UeIdMappingGet operation retrieve, and what must the requester supply?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_UEId_UeIdMappingGet (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.27.3) gets the Ranging/SL Positioning UE identifier. It requires the GPSI or the Application Layer ID as input, and returns a Result plus the Application Layer ID or GPSI.

questions.question: Which two specifications describe the MOBILITY CHANGE REQUEST message used in the Mobility Settings Change procedure, and what does the receiving node evaluate?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 clause 8.3.8.2 and TS 36.300 clause 20.2.2.14 both describe the MOBILITY CHANGE REQUEST message, sent from one eNB (eNB1) to a peer eNB (eNB2) to negotiate handover trigger settings. Upon receipt, eNB2 evaluates whether the proposed handover trigger modification -- and, if included, the proposed SSB Offset value for a given SSB Area -- can be accepted, replying with MOBILITY CHANGE ACKNOWLEDGE if so.

questions.question: Which two specifications describe the MBMS SESSION UPDATE REQUEST message between the MME/MCE and eNB, and what does the eNB do upon receiving it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.444 clause 8.6.2 (M3AP, MME to MCE) and TS 36.443 clause 8.10.2 (M2AP, MCE to eNB) both describe the MBMS SESSION UPDATE REQUEST message. Per TS 36.443, on receiving it the eNB checks whether its cells are involved in the new MBMS Service Area (or, for SC-PTM, the new list of cell identities), updates its MBMS context and resources accordingly, joins or leaves the IP multicast group as needed, and then sends back an MBMS SESSION UPDATE RESPONSE message.

questions.question: What does the Naf_ProSe_DiscoveryAuthorizationResultUpdate service operation inform the AF of, and what identifiers must accompany a restricted-discovery revocation update?
questions.reference_answer: Naf_ProSe_DiscoveryAuthorizationResultUpdate (TS 23.304 clause 7.2.2.4) is used by the NF consumer to inform the AF of the revocation result following an update in authorization information. For discovery type "restricted" it requires the RPAUID, the Banned RPAUID, and the Banned PDUID as input, and returns a Result.

questions.question: Which specifications define UDRE Growth Rate, and what does it estimate in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.138 (RNSAP), TS 25.433 clause 9.2.1.125 (NBAP), and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.154 (PCAP) each define UDRE Growth Rate, inside the DGNSS Validity Period IE, as a mandatory enumerated field (growth rates 1.5 to 16) that estimates the growth rate of uncertainty (1-sigma) in the GNSS differential corrections provided in the DGPS/DGANSS Corrections IEs; the UDRE at the time given by the companion Time of Validity for UDRE Growth Rate field equals this growth rate times the UDRE value from the corrections IE.

questions.question: Which specifications define the UE CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message on the F1 and W1 interfaces, and what does it contain when a candidate SpCell is unacceptable?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.473 clause 8.3.1.3 (W1AP, ng-eNB-DU) and TS 38.473 clause 8.3.1.3 (F1AP, gNB-DU) both define the UE CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message, returned when the DU cannot establish the UE context or accept the requested SpCell. If the Candidate SpCell List IE was included in the request and the DU cannot accept the SpCell ID, it may include a Potential SpCell List IE in the failure message, ordered from most to least desired, for the CU to use in selecting a new SpCell.

questions.question: Which service operation does an AMF invoke to notify the MB-SMF's notification URI when it cannot deliver an N2 MBS session request to a NG-RAN node?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.527 clause 8.4.1.2 states that if an AMF receiving a Namf_MBSCommunication_N2MessageTransfer Request cannot send the N2 message to the indicated NG-RAN node (e.g. it has failed without restart), the AMF notifies this failure by sending a Namf_MBSCommunication_Notify request to the notification URI received in that request.

questions.question: Which specifications define the specificProblem attribute, and what does it qualify in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.111-2 clause 5.5.1 defines specificProblem as an AlarmInformation attribute that provides further qualification of an alarm beyond eventType. TS 28.532 clause 12.1.1.4.1a.9 references specificProblem as part of a generic PatchItem type used to modify managed-object attributes (including alarm-related ones). TS 32.412 clause 6.5.1 defines specificProblem, in the definition-and-legal-values table for alarm attributes, with the same role of further qualifying an alarm than eventType alone.

questions.question: Which LMF service operation lets a consumer NF subscribe to the status of a secure LCS-UP connection for a target UE, and what input does it require?
questions.reference_answer: Nlmf_Location_UPSubscribe (TS 23.273 clause 8.3.2.8) allows a consumer NF to subscribe about the status of a secure LCS-UP connection for a target UE. Required input is a Notification Target Address, Notification Correlation ID, and the UE identifier (SUPI); the optional input is the UE identifier (GPSI). Required output is a Subscription Correlation ID.

questions.question: Which service operation does a consumer NF use to request EPS Bearer IDs for a PDU session from the AMF, and which inputs must it include?
questions.reference_answer: Namf_Communication_EBIAssignment (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.13) requests a batch of EPS Bearer IDs for a PDU Session and can optionally indicate EBIs to release. Required inputs are SUPI, PDU Session ID, and the ARP list; the optional input is a Released EBI list.

questions.question: Which two specifications define the SGNB CHANGE CONFIRM message, and what does the MeNB include in it regarding data forwarding?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 clause 8.7.8.2 and TS 36.300 clause 20.2.2.26 both define the SGNB CHANGE CONFIRM message, sent by the MeNB to the en-gNB when it can perform the requested SgNB change. Per TS 36.423, for each E-RAB configured with the PDCP entity in the en-gNB, the MeNB may include the DL/UL Forwarding GTP Tunnel Endpoint IEs within the E-RABs To Be Released Item IE to request data forwarding for that bearer.

questions.question: Which specifications define a deregReason attribute, and in what deregistration context does each use it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.503 clause 6.2.6.2.5 defines deregReason, in the DeregistrationData type (used toward the AMF/SMF), as a mandatory DeregistrationReason string indicating why the UE/session is deregistered. TS 29.562 clause 6.1.6.2.13 defines deregReason, in its own DeregistrationData type for the IMS/HSS-like context, as a mandatory field indicating the reason for deregistration, alongside the IMPI and any associated/emergency-registered identities. TS 29.563 clause 6.3.6.2.2 defines deregReason, in the DeregistrationRequest type sent with the IMSI and optional GUAMI, as a mandatory DeregistrationReason string used by the HSS to decide whether a registered VLR should be cancelled.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Correlation ID information element, and what is it used for in each?
questions.reference_answer: The Correlation ID IE is defined in at least three specs with different roles: in TS 23.078 (CAMEL Phase 4, clause 4.6.2.13.2) it is an optional IE used by the gsmSSF to correlate dialogues from the initiating gsmSSF towards the gsmSCF with dialogues from the gsmSRF or an assisting gsmSSF towards the gsmSCF. In TS 29.171 (LCS, clause 7.4.28) it is a mandatory octet-string IE that identifies a specific location session, used to correlate a request/response pair with an ongoing location session in E-UTRAN and expected to be unique among concurrently active location sessions in an MME. In TS 33.128 (Lawful Interception, clause 5.3.1) it is a field of the LI_X2/LI_X3 message details (per ETSI TS 103 221-2) that shall contain the Correlation ID generated by the IRI-POI or as received in the relevant LI_X1 provisioning message.

questions.question: Which specifications define a Roaming number information element, and what is it used for in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.018 clause 8.2.2 (Send Routeing Info ack) defines Roaming number as a conditional E.164 number required to route the call to the visited MSC (VMSCB), present when the HLR received it via Provide Roaming Number ack and the call is not subject to early call forwarding. TS 23.018 clause 8.3.2 (Provide Roaming Number ack) defines it as the mandatory E.164 number itself, returned to allow routing the call to VMSCB. TS 23.079 clause 10.2.2 redefines the SRI ack for CCBS: Roaming number becomes conditional, present only for a basic-type interrogation when the HLR determines optimal-routeing charging requirements are met and the call is not forwarded. TS 52.008 clause 7.4 (HLR trace record content) lists Roaming number as a conditional trace field holding the roaming number returned from the serving VLR.

questions.question: Which specifications describe how SGNB RELEASE REQUEST is used inside EN-DC, one at the F1/gNB-DU level and one at the X2 level?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.401 clause 8.4.2.1 shows the SGNB RELEASE REQUEST message received by the gNB-CU from the MeNB, which then triggers the gNB-CU to send UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST and UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND to the gNB-DU to stop data transmission and release the UE context. TS 36.423 clause 8.7.9.2 defines the X2AP-level procedure: the MeNB sends SGNB RELEASE REQUEST to the en-gNB, which stops providing user data and, if it confirms the release, replies with SGNB RELEASE REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE.

questions.question: What alternative required inputs can be used to identify which ECS Address Configuration Information to delete via Nnef_ECSAddress_Delete?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Delete (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.4) accepts any one of: an AF-identifier; an S-NSSAI and DNN pair; the ECS Address Configuration Information itself; or an AF Transaction Id (which identifies the consumer's request for the information to be deleted). It returns a Result Indication.

questions.question: How does the values table for TP-Loop-Prevention (TP-LP) distinguish a forwarded/spawned SMS message from an original one?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.040 clause 9.2.3.28 defines TP-LP as a 1-bit field in the first octet of the SMS-Deliver/SMS-Status-Report. Value 0 means the message has not been forwarded and is not a spawned message (or the sending entity does not support setting this bit); value 1 means the message has either been forwarded or is a spawned message.

questions.question: What input does Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Delete require, and what does it let the consumer remove from the NSSF?
questions.reference_answer: Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Delete (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.16.3.6) lets an NF service consumer (e.g. AMF) delete the NSSAI availability information stored for it in the NSSF. It requires only the NF ID as input, with no required output.

questions.question: Which specifications define the trackingAreaList attribute, and what does it represent in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.510 clause 6.1.6.2.84 defines trackingAreaList, in the MlAnalyticsInfo type, as an optional array of TAIs representing the Area of Interest of an ML model; if omitted, the ML model applies to any TAI. TS 29.571 clause 5.4.4.74 defines trackingAreaList, in the SpatialValidityCond type, as a conditional array of TAIs to be included if available, listing the tracking area identities that condition applies to. TS 33.128 clause 7.3.3.2.62 defines trackingAreaList (as part of PresenceInfo, derived from TS 29.571) as a conditional SET OF TAI representing the list of tracking areas constituting the area of interest, when tracking areas are part of that area.

questions.question: Multiple service-enabler specs define an 'Application defined proximity range information' element for subscribing to dynamic information. Which specs define it, and what is it used for in each?
questions.reference_answer: The IE 'Application defined proximity range information' is a mandatory element defined identically in three service-enabler specs: TS 23.255 (UAS, clause 7.8.3.1), where it describes the range over which a host UAV's dynamic information is required when a UAS application server subscribes to host UAV dynamic information; TS 23.286 (V2X application enabler, clause 9.16.2.1), where it describes the range over which HD map dynamic information is required when a V2X application server subscribes at the VAE server; and TS 23.434 (VAL services, clause 9.3.2.9), where it describes the range over which UE(s) information is required when a VAL server requests UE(s) information from the Location Management server.

questions.question: Which operation creates a UE identifier mapping such as the GPSI-to-Application-Layer-ID mapping for Ranging/SL Positioning, and what does it return?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_UEId_UeIdMappingCreate (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.27.4) creates the UE identifier mapping information, e.g. the GPSI and Application Layer ID mapping for Ranging/SL Positioning. It requires the mapping information as input and returns a Result plus a Transaction Reference ID.

questions.question: Which specifications define a PLMN ID information element in the context of network slice / DNAI configuration, and what does it identify in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.435 clause 9.13.3.3 defines PLMN ID, in the Inter-PLMN slice modification notify message, as a mandatory field identifying the PLMN where the slice modification was performed. TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.3d defines PLMN ID, within AF-provided ECS Address Configuration Information, as the PLMN identifier to which that configuration information (target for a group of UEs or any UE) is applied. TS 23.700-48 clause 6.55.2.1 defines PLMN ID, in the DNAI/IP-range mapping table an AF provides to the 5GC, as indicating the PLMN in which the mapped target DNAI is supported.

questions.question: What does the Nnef_UEAddress_Get operation return, and what must the consumer provide to call it?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_UEAddress_Get (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.36.2) gets the UE's IP address (IPv4 address or IPv6 prefix). It requires the GPSI and the AF Identifier as input, and returns a Result plus the UE address.

questions.question: The Standardized 5QI-to-QoS-characteristics table from TS 23.501 clause 5.7.4 is reproduced or extended in several media-focused specs. Which specs reuse this 5QI table, and how does each one build on it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.925 (typical traffic characteristics of media services) reproduces the full Standardized 5QI-to-QoS-characteristics mapping table twice: in clause 7.2, as 'Table 7.2-1' embedded in the use-case collection template, so that a submitted media-service use case can be mapped to one or more of the listed 5QI values (1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,80,...); and again in clause 8.1.4 as 'Table 8.1.4-1', explicitly stated to be identical to TS 23.501's Table 5.7.4.1-1. TS 26.928 (extended reality/XR in 5G, clause 4.3.3) references the same TS 23.501 5.7.4 QoS model and its 5QI concept (including the note that the QoS Flow ID may equal the 5QI) as the basis for describing 5G QoS handling for XR traffic, without itself repeating the full table. TS 26.939 (5G live uplink streaming, clause 9.2.6.5) extends the mapping by defining NEW 5QI values (71-76 and others) for 'Live' Uplink Streaming, built on the same table structure (Resource Type, Default Priority Level, Packet Delay Budget, Packet Error Rate, Default Maximum Data Burst Volume, Default Averaging Window, Example Services) as TS 23.501's table.

questions.question: Which specifications describe the RAN CP RELOCATION INDICATION message, and what must the AMF do after authenticating the request it carries?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.3.8.2 describes the RAN CP RELOCATION INDICATION message, sent by the NG-RAN node to the AMF including a newly allocated RAN UE NGAP ID; the AMF authenticates the request using the NAS-level security information in the UL CP Security Information IE and, if successful, initiates the Connection Establishment Indication procedure including NAS-level security information in the DL CP Security Information IE. TS 33.512 clause 4.2.2.7 restates this same normative behaviour as a security test-case requirement.

questions.question: Which specifications define a Reporting interval information element, and what does it configure in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.435 clause 9.5.3.8 defines Reporting interval, in the VAL server policy usage reporting data subscribe request, as an optional field indicating the policy report data reporting interval requested by the VAL server from the NSCE server. TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.53 defines Reporting interval, within Periodical reporting criteria, as a mandatory Integer (in ms, from a fixed value set) giving the interval of periodical measurement reporting (or the maximum time for SI acquisition if configured for that). TS 26.501 clause 4.2.3 discusses reporting/service-access information for downlink media streaming where a reporting interval configures how often the UE reports service access/QoE information to the network.

questions.question: What does the Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageUnSubscribe service operation let a consumer NF do, and what must it supply as input?
questions.reference_answer: Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageUnSubscribe (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.6) lets an NF unsubscribe with the AMF to stop being notified of a particular N1 message type or a specific N2 information type about a UE. Required input is CN NF ID and N1 Message Type; there is no required output.

questions.question: Which specifications define the Primary CCPCH RSCP information element, and what does it measure in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.331 clause 10.3.7.54 defines Primary CCPCH RSCP (TDD only) as a mandatory Integer(0..91) per the P-CCPCH_RSCP_LEV mapping, with an optional DeltaPrimary CCPCH RSCP correction from Rel-5 onward. TS 25.423 clause 9.2.3.5 (RNSAP) and TS 25.433 clause 9.2.3.11A (NBAP) both define it as the Received Signal Code Power on the target cell's PCCPCH after despreading, referenced at the UE antenna connector (TS 25.225), encoded as Integer(0..91) per the mapping in TS 25.123.

questions.question: Which HSS service operation lets an NF consumer subscribe to monitoring event notifications, and what does the HSS return in response?
questions.reference_answer: Nhss_EE_Subscribe (TS 23.632 clause 6.1.5.1) requests the HSS to subscribe to monitoring event notifications (e.g. location change) per TS 23.682. Required input is IMSI, monitoring event type(s), and notification address; required output is a Result Indication and Subscription ID, with an optional Current State Not Available Indication.

questions.question: Which DCMF service operation lets a consumer NF create and reserve a media resource for IMS Data Channel media flow, and what output uniquely identifies that resource for later updates?
questions.reference_answer: Ndcmf_MRM_Create (TS 23.700-87 clause 6.20.3.1.2) lets the consumer NF request the DCMF to create and reserve a media resource to originate/terminate IMS Data Channel media flow, requiring the DCMF media specification as input. Required output includes a Result indication, DCMF resource identity, and Mb media resource information; the DCMF resource identity uniquely identifies the resource and is used as the reference when later updating (Ndcmf_MRM_Update) or deleting (Ndcmf_MRM_Delete) it.

questions.question: Which SBI service operation does the UDM invoke on the AMF to trigger a home-network-initiated primary authentication run, and in what situation is it used?
questions.reference_answer: The operation is Namf_HNAuthentication_Request, defined in TS 33.741 clause 5.2.2.1 as part of the home-network-triggered primary authentication procedure. The UDM sends the Namf_HNAuthentication_Request message to the AMF serving the UE, carrying the UE's SUPI, when the UDM decides to run a fresh primary authentication -- e.g. because it needs to send UPU or SoR data but cannot find a valid AUSF instance (no valid KAUSF), or because the AAnF needs to refresh KAKMA and has sent a request (via the AUSF/AAnF's own Nudm_HNAuthenticate-Request to the UDM) citing a cause for refresh. On receiving it, the AMF may reply with a Namf_HNAuthentication_acknowledge message and then starts the primary authentication procedure defined in TS 33.501.

questions.question: During mobile IAB-DU migration, which F1AP message does the source logical mobile IAB-DU send back to the source F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU to report the outcome of F1 setup with the target donor-CU, and what optional information can it carry?
questions.reference_answer: The message is MIAB F1 SETUP OUTCOME NOTIFICATION, an F1AP procedure message defined in TS 38.473 (clause 8.10.6.2 for the successful-operation behaviour, and clause 9.4.4 for its ASN.1 PDU definition). Per TS 38.401 (clause 8.23.3, step 4 of the mobile IAB-DU inter-CU migration procedure), the source logical mobile IAB-DU sends this message to the source F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU to inform it of the outcome of the F1 interface setup between the co-located target logical mobile IAB-DU and the target F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU; it may include a mapping between activated cells of the source and target logical mobile IAB-DUs, and, when migration is OAM-triggered, the gNB ID of the target F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU. Per TS 38.473 clause 8.10.6.2, upon receiving it (with the Activated Cells Mapping List or the Target F1 Terminating IAB-Donor gNB ID present) the gNB-CU shall take this into account for subsequent handover of connected UEs to the co-located target logical gNB-DU.

questions.question: During an EPS-to-5GS mobility LCS handoff, which parameter does the AMF provide to the GMLC as part of the Location_Response, and what is transferred alongside it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-71 clause 6.33.4, Table 6.33.4-1, shows that for EPS to 5GS mobility, the AMF provides the target AMF ID to the GMLC as part of the Location_Response, while the LCS context and LCS QoS mapping are transferred from EPS to 5GS.

questions.question: Which UDSF service operation starts a timer, and what optional inputs can accompany the start request?
questions.reference_answer: Nudsf_Timer_Start (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.14.3.2) lets an NF service consumer start a timer in the UDSF. Required input is the Timer ID and Time of expiry; optional inputs are a Notification Endpoint and Associated data, which can identify the purpose of the timer (e.g. a subscription that has timed out).

questions.question: Which specifications define CSG Identity, and what does it identify in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.331 clause 10.3.2.8 defines CSG Identity as a mandatory Bit string(27) IE (from Rel-8). TS 32.582 clause 6.1.1 lists CSG Identity among HNB Access Network related parameters, defining it as the CSG ID(s) to which the HNB belongs (referencing TS 22.011). TS 33.108 clause 10.5.1.1 discusses target actions such as E-UTRAN attach/detach reported via the REPORT record, where CSG-related identity is part of the location/cell reporting context for lawful interception.

questions.question: Which AMF service operation lets a consumer NF unsubscribe from delivery of a specific N2 information type, and what happens at the AMF when it is invoked?
questions.reference_answer: Namf_Communication_N2InfoUnSubscribe (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.9) is invoked by an NF to unsubscribe for delivery of a specific N2 information type. Required input is CN NF ID and the N2 information type to unsubscribe; the AMF then deletes the binding it held for that consumer NF for the requested information.

questions.question: Which two Time Synchronization APIs does TS 23.700-25 propose extending with Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Notify operations so an AF can request network timing synchronization status monitoring?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-25 clause 6.4.2.3 proposes extending the existing Ntsctsf_TimeSynchronization_Config and Ntsctsf_ASTI APIs with Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Notify operations so an AF can request monitoring of network timing synchronization status via the NEF or TSCTSF.

questions.question: Which specifications describe the X2 REMOVAL RESPONSE message, and what does the initiating eNB do after receiving it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.300 clause 20.2.2.18 and TS 36.423 clause 8.3.12.2 both describe the X2 REMOVAL RESPONSE message, sent by the receiving eNB2 to accept removal of X2 connectivity. After receiving it, the initiating eNB1 begins removing the TNL association towards eNB2 and may release all resources associated with that signalling connection; eNB2 may then release its own associated resources.

questions.question: Which specifications define Queue position info, and what does it report in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.281 clause 7.7.1.2.9 defines Queue position info as a mandatory field in the 'queue position info' information flow from the MCVideo transmission control server to the participant, giving the position of the queued transmit media request. TS 23.283 clause 10.5.2.14 (IWF queue position info) defines it as a mandatory field reporting the position of a queued floor request, exchanged between the IWF and the MCPTT floor control server. TS 23.379 clause 10.9.1.2.14 defines it analogously as a mandatory field from the MCPTT floor control server indicating the position of the queued floor request to the requesting UE (and optionally an authorized user).

questions.question: Which two GNSS constellations does the GNSSID enumeration list first, and where is this enumeration table defined?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.128 clause 7.3.3.2.54, Table 7.3.3.2.54-1, defines the GNSSID enumeration (derived from the GNSSID type in TS 29.572 clause 6.1.6.3.8). Its first two values are gPS(1) for GPS and galileo(2) for Galileo, followed by sBAS(3), modernizedGPS(4), qZSS(5), gLONASS(6), bDS(7), and nAVIC(8).

questions.question: Which specifications define the Redundant QoS Flow Indicator information element, and what does it indicate in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.483 clause 9.3.1.74, TS 38.413 clause 9.3.1.134 (NGAP), and TS 38.423 clause 9.2.3.118 (XnAP) all define the Redundant QoS Flow Indicator as a mandatory ENUMERATED(true, false) IE for a QoS flow as specified in TS 23.501: value 'true' indicates redundant transmission is requested for that QoS flow, and 'false' indicates redundant transmission is requested to be stopped if it was started.

questions.question: Which specifications define the EARFCN information element, and what does it identify in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 9.2.1.95 (S1AP) and TS 36.423 clause 9.2.26 (X2AP) both define EARFCN as a mandatory Integer giving the E-UTRA Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number that defines the carrier frequency used in a cell, per TS 36.104. TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.41D (RNSAP), within Neighbouring E-UTRA Cell Information, defines the CHOICE EARFCN Information (UL/DL EARFCN, or the EARFCN-Extended variant) identifying the uplink/downlink carrier frequency of a neighbouring E-UTRA cell, again referencing TS 36.104.

questions.question: What must a consumer supply to delete stored data from the UDSF via Nudsf_UnstructuredDataManagement_Delete?
questions.reference_answer: Nudsf_UnstructuredDataManagement_Delete (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.14.2.4) deletes data stored in the UDSF, e.g. when the AMF deletes context for an unregistered UE. It requires only the Data Identifier that uniquely identifies the data to be deleted, and returns a Result.

questions.question: For groupcast Ranging key requests, what identifies the target group, and what does the Nslpkmf_SLPKMFKeyRequest_GroupcastKey operation return?
questions.reference_answer: Nslpkmf_SLPKMFKeyRequest_GroupcastKey (TS 33.533 clause 7.2.3.2) requires an SLPGK ID and a Group Identifier as input (for broadcast operation, the Ranging/SL Positioning Application Identifier is used as the Group Identifier), and returns the SLPGK as required output.

questions.question: Which service operation does a CN NF invoke on the AMF to transfer a downlink N1 or N2 message towards the UE or AN, and what result indications can the AMF return?
questions.reference_answer: The operation is Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.7). The AMF's required output is a Result indication: if the UE is CM-IDLE the AMF returns "attempting to reach UE" while it triggers the network-triggered Service Request procedure, otherwise it indicates whether the N1 and/or N2 message was successfully transferred towards the UE/AN; on failure the AMF sets a cause value, and it may also provide redirection information or an estimated maximum wait time.

questions.question: Which three specifications describe the PWS CANCEL REQUEST message across the NG, F1 and W1 interfaces, and what does the receiving node do when the request cancels all warning messages?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.413 clause 8.9.2.2 (NGAP, AMF to NG-RAN node), TS 37.473 clause 8.5.2.2 (W1AP, ng-eNB-CU to ng-eNB-DU) and TS 38.473 clause 8.5.2.2 (F1AP, gNB-CU to gNB-DU) all describe the PWS CANCEL REQUEST message. If the Cancel-All Warning Messages Indicator IE is present in the request, the receiving DU/NG-RAN node stops broadcasting and discards all warning messages for the indicated area(s), rather than only the specific message identified by the Message Identifier and Serial Number IEs.

questions.question: Which SBI service operation lets the UDM cancel an ongoing deferred location request for a target UE, and what inputs/outputs does it define?
questions.reference_answer: The operation is Namf_Location_CancelLocation, defined in TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.5.5. It cancels an ongoing deferred location of a target UE for the consumer NF. Required inputs are the UE Identification (SUPI), a Notification Target address, and a Notification Correlation ID (no optional inputs); the required output is a Success/Failure indication (no optional outputs). TS 23.502 points to steps 4 and 10 of clause 6.3.3 of TS 23.273 for examples of its usage.

questions.question: Which service operation provides Ranging-related keying material for unicast communication, and what does it return?
questions.reference_answer: Nslpkmf_SLPKMFKeyRequest_UnicastKey (TS 33.533 clause 7.2.3.1) provides Ranging-related keying material for unicast communication. Required input is the Ranging/SL Positioning Application Identifier, SLPK ID, and KSLP freshness parameter 1; required output is KSLP and KSLP freshness parameter 2.

questions.question: The 'Floor priority' information element appears in floor-request information flows across several Mission Critical service specs. Which specs define it, and what does it convey in each?
questions.reference_answer: 'Floor priority' is a mandatory IE meaning 'priority of the request' in each case, carried in the floor-request information flow of three Mission Critical specs: TS 23.180 (common MC functional architecture, clause 10.5.3.2.1), in the IOPS floor request sent from a floor participant via the IOPS MC connectivity function; TS 23.283 (MC services interworking, clause 10.5.2.2), in the IWF floor request exchanged between the interworking function and the MCPTT floor control server; and TS 23.379 (MCPTT, clause 10.9.1.2.2), in the floor request sent from a floor participant to the MCPTT floor control server.

questions.question: Which specifications describe the UE RADIO CAPABILITY ID MAPPING procedure's response message, and which node answers the request?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.33 and TS 36.413 clause 8.19.2 both describe the UE RADIO CAPABILITY ID MAPPING RESPONSE message. The eNB initiates the procedure by sending UE RADIO CAPABILITY ID MAPPING REQUEST to the MME, and the MME answers with the UE RADIO CAPABILITY ID MAPPING RESPONSE, including the UE radio capability information that maps to the indicated capability ID.

questions.question: Which interfaces define the PSCell ID information element, and what does it represent in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 9.2.1.161 (S1AP) defines PSCell ID as part of Last Visited PSCell Information: an optional field (PSCell Information 9.2.1.141) present when SCG resources are configured, together with a mandatory Time Stay. TS 36.423 clause 9.2.142 (X2AP) defines PSCell ID as a mandatory NR CGI identifying the PSCell of the UE, used in the Location Information at SgNB IE. TS 38.413 clause 9.3.1.235 (NGAP) defines PSCell ID similarly inside Last Visited PSCell Information as an optional NG-RAN CGI present when SCG resources are configured, alongside Time Stay.

questions.question: What does the Nslpkmf_Discovery_MonitorAuthorize service operation return besides an authorization decision, and what security-capability input does it need?
questions.reference_answer: Nslpkmf_Discovery_MonitorAuthorize (TS 33.533 clause 7.2.2.2) lets the consumer NF obtain authorization from the SLPKMF for monitoring in the PLMN. Required input is the User Info ID, Ranging/SL Positioning Application Identifier, UE Role, and PC5 UE security capability. Required output is the chosen PC5 ciphering algorithm and discovery security materials; the optional output is a Discovery User Integrity Key (DUIK).

questions.question: Which specifications describe the MME CP RELOCATION INDICATION message, and what does the eNB do when it receives it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.3.13.2 and TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.31 both describe the MME CP RELOCATION INDICATION message, sent by the MME to the eNB for UEs using Control Plane CIoT EPS optimisation, to indicate that the UE's connection is being relocated to a new eNB. Upon reception, the (old) eNB terminates the delivery of NAS PDUs received from the MME and, per TS 36.300, initiates NAS Non Delivery Indication procedure(s) to report any non-delivered NAS PDUs.

questions.question: Which service operation lets a consumer search for timers stored in the UDSF, and what does it need to supply?
questions.reference_answer: Nudsf_Timer_Search (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.14.3.6) lets an NF service consumer search and retrieve timers matching a filter in the UDSF. It requires a Search filter as input (optionally a Filter), and returns a Result plus, optionally, the matching Timer Identity/Identities.

questions.question: In the F1AP mobile-IAB-DU inter-CU migration procedure, which message carries TA and PRACH resource information from the candidate gNB-DU up to the gNB-CU, and how does the gNB-CU use it?
questions.reference_answer: The message is the DU-CU TA INFORMATION TRANSFER message, defined as part of the DU-CU TA Information Transfer elementary procedure in TS 38.473 (F1AP, clause 9.4.4, ASN.1 for the DUCUTAInformationTransfer PDU carrying a TransactionID and a mandatory DUtoCUTAInformation-List). Per the inter-gNB-DU LTM procedure in TS 38.401 (clause 8.2.1.5, step 14), the candidate gNB-DU sends this message to the gNB-CU including the TA value(s) and associated PRACH resource information for the candidate cell; the gNB-CU then forwards that TA value and PRACH resource information to the source gNB-DU in the corresponding CU-DU TA INFORMATION TRANSFER message (step 15) so early TA acquisition can be prepared before the cell switch.

questions.question: What does the Namf_Communication_AMFStatusChangeSubscribe service operation let an NF do, and what must it supply?
questions.reference_answer: Namf_Communication_AMFStatusChangeSubscribe (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.14) lets an NF subscribe for AMF Status Change notification. The required input is one or more GUAMIs, which identify the AMF being tracked; there is no required output.

questions.question: Which specifications define a civicAddresses attribute, and what does it represent in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.122 clause 5.2.1.2.11 defines civicAddresses, in the LocationArea type (SCS/AS to SCEF), as an optional array(CivicAddress) identifying a list of civic addresses of the user where the UE is located. TS 29.503 clause 6.5.6.2.10 defines civicAddresses, in the LocationArea type, identically as an optional array of civic addresses identifying where the UE is located. TS 29.522 clause 5.33.5.2.6 defines civicAddresses, in the LadnServArea type, as a conditional array(CivicAddress) representing the LADN Service Area as a list of civic address(es), mutually exclusive with the geographicAreas/tais alternatives.

questions.question: In UTRAN's cell synchronisation scheme for introducing a late-entrant cell, which NBAP message triggers the transmission or measurement of cell synchronisation bursts, and what role does it play in the late-entrant procedure?
questions.reference_answer: The message is CELL SYNCHRONISATION INITIATION REQUEST. Per TS 25.433 (NBAP, clause 8.2.20.2), the CRNC sends it to the Node B over the Node B Control Port to configure transmission of cell synchronisation bursts (or SYNC_DL codes for 1.28Mcps TDD) and/or start measurement on them per the parameters given, and the Node B responds with CELL SYNCHRONISATION INITIATION RESPONSE if it can comply. Per TS 25.402 (synchronisation for UTRAN, clause 6.1.2.2.3), within the scheme for introducing new (late-entrant) cells into a synchronised RNS, this message is used twice: first to instruct the late-entrant cell to listen to the regular cell-sync-burst schedule of surrounding cells for frequency acquisition, and then to instruct the surrounding, already-synchronised cells to transmit a single common cell synchronisation burst that the late-entrant cell correlates against (within a +/-3 frame reception window) to determine system timing and adjust its own SFN.

questions.question: Which specification(s) describe the S-NODE RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE message, and which performance counter increments on its transmission?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.3.2.2 defines the S-NODE RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE message, sent by the M-NG-RAN node to the S-NG-RAN node to report whether the UE applied the requested reconfiguration (or the reason it was rejected), and it stops timer TXnDCoverall at the S-NG-RAN node. TS 28.552 clause 5.1.1.10.13 defines the DRB.EstabSuccDC counter, which increments on transmission of this same message, counting DRBs successfully set up in Dual Connectivity per mapped 5QI and per S-NSSAI.

questions.question: Which two specifications describe the X2AP MESSAGE TRANSFER message, and what is its purpose besides carrying another X2AP message?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.423 clause 8.5.1 and TS 36.300 clause 4.6.6.4 both describe the X2AP MESSAGE TRANSFER message. Besides indirectly transporting another X2AP message between two eNBs, it also allows an eNB to perform registration with an X2 GW: per TS 36.300, an (H)eNB can send an X2AP MESSAGE TRANSFER carrying a Source (H)eNB ID with no Target ID and no embedded X2AP message, purely so the X2 GW records the mapping of the eNB's Global eNB ID to its TNL address(es).

questions.question: Which specifications define the Ringing indication information element, and what does it convey in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.180 clause 10.5.2.2.3 (IOPS MCPTT ringing), TS 23.283 clause 10.4.1.4 (IWF ringing), and TS 23.379 clause 10.7.2.1.7 (MCPTT ringing) each define Ringing indication as an optional information element in the ringing information flow between MCPTT client/server (and, for TS 23.283, the IWF), conveying an indication to the calling party that the called party's device is ringing.

questions.question: What are the two possible values of the 3GPPPSDataOffStatus enumeration, and which clause table defines them?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.291 clause 6.1.6.3.13, Table 6.1.6.3.13-1, defines the 3GPPPSDataOffStatus enumeration with two values: ACTIVE, meaning 3GPP PS data off status is active, and INACTIVE, meaning it is inactive.

questions.question: Which specifications define the GANSS ID information element, and what does it identify?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.423 clause 9.2.1.119 (RNSAP), TS 25.433 clause 9.2.1.104 (NBAP), and TS 25.453 clause 9.2.2.130 (PCAP) each define GANSS ID as a mandatory IE that identifies a particular GANSS (GNSS), coded as defined in TS 25.331.

questions.question: Which specifications define an EES Endpoint information element, and what is it used for in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.558 clause 8.2.6, TS 23.700-98 clause 8.2.6, and TS 33.739 clause 6.4.2.1 all define EES Endpoint, in the EES Profile, as a mandatory field giving endpoint information (e.g. URI, FQDN, IP address) used to communicate with the EES; this is the information provided to the EEC so it can connect to the EES.

questions.question: Which service operation lets an NF consumer update ECS Address Configuration Information, and what optional parameters can accompany the request?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_ECSAddress_Update (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.37.3) lets the NF consumer request an update of ECS Address Configuration Information. Required input is the ECS Address Configuration Information; optional inputs are the AF-service-identifier, AF Transaction Id, DNN, and S-NSSAI. It returns a Result Indication.

questions.question: What is the Namf_Communication_ReleaseUEContext service operation used for during a handover, and what input does it require?
questions.reference_answer: Namf_Communication_ReleaseUEContext (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.12) is used by a source AMF to release the UE context in a target AMF during handover cancel procedures. It requires only the handle of the UE context as input, and its required output is a Cause.

questions.question: Which specifications define the LWIP ADDITION REQUEST message, and which two different network nodes can receive it from the eNB?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.463 clause 8.14.2 describes the LWIP ADDITION REQUEST sent by the eNB to the WT (to configure LWIP resources for the UE), while TS 36.300 clause 22B.2.2.13 describes the LWIP Addition Preparation procedure where the eNB sends the same LWIP ADDITION REQUEST message to the LWIP-SeGW to establish an LWIP bearer, which responds with LWIP ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE (or REJECT on failure).

questions.question: Which service operation does a consumer NF use to subscribe to direct UPF event exposure via an SMF, and what UE-level information can the request include?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-62 clause 6.16.3.2 describes that the consumer NF sends a subscription request to the SMF over the Nsmf_UPFAccessAuthorization_Create/Subscribe service operation, including its NF identity information, the UPF event exposure mode, exposure duration, and the information to be exposed; for UE-level requests it includes the UE IP address, UE ID (SUCI/GPSI), PDU session ID, and QFI.

questions.question: Which specifications define the RLF INDICATION message on the X2 interface, and what is its purpose?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.300 clause 20.2.2.12 and TS 36.423 clause 8.3.9.2 both define the RLF INDICATION message. Its purpose is to enable mobility robustness and radio link failure recovery improvement in E-UTRAN by passing information about a failure event over X2: eNB2 sends it to eNB1 after a re-establishment attempt or RLF report reception, optionally including a ShortMAC-I IE and the UE's RLF Report Container, to help eNB1 identify the UE and analyze the failure's root cause.

questions.question: What eDRX cycle length corresponds to code 0011 in the eDRX cycle table for GPRS-attached MS, and which clause defines that table?
questions.reference_answer: TS 45.002 clause 6.5.6a, Table 6.5.6a-1, lists the set of supported eDRX cycles for an MS in GPRS attached mode. eDRX cycle value 0011 corresponds to a cycle length of approximately 12.2 seconds (52 51-multiframes per eDRX cycle, 1024 eDRX cycles per hyperframe).

questions.question: What does the Nudm_MT_ProvideSRVCCInfo (Nudm_MT_Provide5GSRVCCInfo) operation provide to the HSS, and what optional outputs can it include?
questions.reference_answer: Nudm_MT_ProvideSRVCCInfo (TS 23.632 clause 6.2.3.4, the Nudm_MT_Provide5GSRVCCInfo operation) provides the UE's PS-to-CS SRVCC capability to the consumer NF (HSS), requiring only the SUPI as input. Required output is a Success/Failure indication; optional outputs are an indication of whether the UE supports SRVCC capability, whether the 5GS supports 5G-SRVCC, an STN-SR, and a C-MSISDN.

questions.question: During a 5GS-to-EPS handover with an ongoing MT-LR, which AMF service operation notifies the LMF that positioning must be aborted?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-71 clause 6.32.3.1 describes that the AMF invokes the Namf_Communication_N1MessageNotify service operation towards the LMF to indicate there is a Handover and that the ongoing positioning procedure is aborted (step C-2).

questions.question: Which specifications describe the SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message across the Xn and X2 interfaces, and what does it report?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.3.13.2 (Xn, S-NG-RAN node to M-NG-RAN node) and TS 36.423 clause 8.7.13.2 (X2, en-gNB to MeNB) both describe the SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message, used in dual connectivity to report the volume of data usage carried over the secondary RAT (NR) for the UE's PDU sessions/E-RABs, which the receiving node forwards on to the core network.

questions.question: Which specifications define the stateAfterObjectCreation assertion, and what must hold after object creation in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.532 clause 11.1.1.7.3.2, TS 32.412 clause 7.7.1.3.2, and TS 32.662 clause 7.4.1.3.2 all define the same stateAfterObjectCreation assertion identically: after an object of the IOC (Information Object Class) ManagedEntity is created, the number of instances of that IOC must equal N + 1, i.e. exactly one more instance than existed before creation.

questions.question: What input does the Nnef_UEId_UeIdMappingUpdate operation need before it can update a UE identifier mapping?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_UEId_UeIdMappingUpdate (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.27.5) updates the UE identifier mapping information (e.g. the GPSI/Application Layer ID mapping). It requires the Transaction Reference ID together with the GPSI and Application Layer ID mapping information, and returns an operation execution result indication.

questions.question: Which specifications define NEF API Charging Information, and how is it used in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.826 clause 5.1.5.19 (solution #1.19, IoT NEF charging information optimization) proposes NEF API Charging Information as part of a NIDD-based solution for optimizing charging for IoT NEF traffic, reducing CDR volume by limiting charging data to IoT-related events. TS 32.254 clause 6.2a.3.2 defines NEF API Charging Information as a mandatory field of the NEF charging CHF CDR record, holding the NEF-specific charging information defined in clause 6.3.1.4. TS 32.298 clause 5.1.5.0 describes the generic CHF-CDR record structure into which NF-specific fields such as NEF API Charging Information are concatenated for the relevant NF (here NEF).

questions.question: How does the NEF translate a UE's public IP address to a DNAI via the Nnef_IPtoDNAI_Get operation, and which NF does it query internally?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-48 clause 6.51.2.2 describes that the AF queries the NEF for IP-to-DNAI translation using Nnef_IPtoDNAI_Get Request (IP address(es)); the NEF then queries the UDR with Nudr_DM_Get Request (DNN, S-NSSAI, IP address(es)), formats the returned records into an IP-address-to-DNAI mapping table, and sends this mapping back to the AF in the Nnef_IPtoDNAI_Get response.

questions.question: How does an AF obtain a target DNAI via the Nnef_EASDeployment_Query service operation, and where might the NEF get that DNAI from?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.700-48 clause 6.52.2 describes that the AF invokes Nnef_EASDeployment_Query Request, providing EHE information (e.g. EAS IP address/range, FQDN(s), (L-)DNS server information), DNN(s), and optionally S-NSSAI(s); the NEF, after authorization, may determine the target DNAI from local configuration or obtain it from the UDR via Nudr_DM_Query Request/Response, then returns it to the AF in the Nnef_EASDeployment_Query Response.

questions.question: What does the UDSF do when Nudsf_Timer_Notify is invoked, and what input triggers it?
questions.reference_answer: Nudsf_Timer_Notify (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.14.3.4) is used by the UDSF to notify the NF service consumer about a timer expiry. It requires the Timer Identity as input and returns a Result.

questions.question: Which service operation lets an NF create a new user data record in the UDSF, and what optional inputs control when the data expires?
questions.reference_answer: Nudsf_UnstructuredDataManagement_Create (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.14.2.3) lets an NF service consumer insert a new user data record into the UDSF (e.g. AMF storing a registered UE's context). Required input is a Data Identifier and the Data; optional inputs are Validity time (after which the consumer is notified and the data removed) and a Notification Endpoint.

questions.question: Which three specifications describe the RACH INDICATION message across the F1, Xn and X2 interfaces, and what information does it convey?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.423 clause 8.3.20.2 (Xn, S-NG-RAN node to M-NG-RAN node), TS 38.473 clause 8.2.14.2 (F1, gNB-DU to gNB-CU) and TS 36.423 clause 8.3.17.2 (X2, en-gNB to MeNB) each describe the RACH INDICATION message. In all three it conveys information about one or more (successful) random-access procedures and the existence of a Random Access report at the UE, letting the receiving node fetch the RA report from the UE.

questions.question: Which specifications define the UE INACTIVITY NOTIFICATION message on the F1 and W1 interfaces, and what condition makes the DRB Activity IE mandatory in it?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.473 clause 8.3.6.2 (F1AP, gNB-DU) and TS 37.473 clause 8.3.6.2 (W1AP, ng-eNB-DU) both define the UE INACTIVITY NOTIFICATION message, sent by the DU to the CU. In both specs, if the DRB ID IE is included in the DRB Activity Item IE within the message, the DRB Activity IE shall also be included.

questions.question: Which specifications define the MME CONFIGURATION TRANSFER message, and what kind of information does it carry to the eNB?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.413 clause 8.16.2.1 and TS 36.300 clause 19.2.2.10a both define the MME CONFIGURATION TRANSFER message, sent by the MME to the eNB to request and/or transfer RAN configuration information, such as SON Configuration Transfer information (e.g. X2 TNL configuration, SON information requests/replies) and other relevant information.

questions.question: Which two specifications specify the DU-CU ACCESS AND MOBILITY INDICATION message, and what information does it carry from the gNB-DU to the gNB-CU?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.473 clause 8.11.2.2 and TS 38.401 clause 8.14.1.3 both describe the DU-CU ACCESS AND MOBILITY INDICATION message. It is sent by the gNB-DU to the gNB-CU and, per TS 38.401, is used to report DL LBT failure information related to mobility failures for a UE (collected after the gNB-CU requests such reporting); the gNB-CU takes the DL LBT Failure Information List IE, if included, into account for optimisation of mobility parameters.

questions.question: What does the Nnssaaf_AIW_Authenticate service operation do for network slice-specific authentication, and what must it carry as input for EAP authentication?
questions.reference_answer: Nnssaaf_AIW_Authenticate (TS 33.501 clause 14.4.2.2) lets the NSSAAF provide Authentication and Authorization service to the consumer NF by relaying EAP or EAP-TTLS inner method messages towards an AAA Server and performing the related protocol conversion. For EAP authentication, the initial authentication request requires the SUPI, while subsequent requests require the EAP message; required output includes the EAP message and authentication result, plus MSK and SUPI on success.

questions.question: Which specifications define an MBS listening status report information flow carrying MBS listening status, and what does that field indicate in each?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.289 clause 7.3.2.10 defines the MBS listening status report information flow (MC service client to MC service server, for broadcast and multicast MBS sessions) with MBS listening status as a mandatory field giving the listening status per MBS session ID. TS 23.434 clause 14.3.2.52 defines the equivalent NRM-client-to-NRM-server report with the same mandatory MBS listening status field. TS 23.783 clause 6.17.1.2.1 defines it for MC service client to MC service server reporting on broadcast MBS sessions identified by TMGI, again with MBS listening status as the mandatory per-TMGI broadcast listening status field.

questions.question: Which SLPKMF service operation authorizes a consumer NF to announce in the PLMN for Ranging/SL Positioning, and what input does it require?
questions.reference_answer: Nslpkmf_Discovery_AnnounceAuthorize (TS 33.533 clause 7.2.2.1) lets the consumer NF obtain authorization from the SLPKMF for announcing in the PLMN. Required input is the User Info ID, the Ranging/SL Positioning Application Identifier, and the UE Role; required output is the Authorization result.

questions.question: What does the Nnef_TrafficInfluence_Get operation retrieve, and which optional input parameters can narrow the request?
questions.reference_answer: Nnef_TrafficInfluence_Get (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.6.7.4A) gets the current traffic influence parameters, requiring only the AF Transaction Id. Optional inputs to narrow the request include the UE's IP or Ethernet address, GPSI, DNN, S-NSSAI, External Group Identifier, External Application Identifier or traffic filtering information, AF-Service-Identifier, and DNAI/routing profile pairs or N6 traffic routing information.

questions.question: What single input does Nlmf_Location_UPUnSubscribe need to cancel a secure LCS-UP connection status subscription?
questions.reference_answer: Nlmf_Location_UPUnSubscribe (TS 23.273 clause 8.3.2.10) lets a consumer NF unsubscribe from the status of a secure LCS-UP connection for a target UE. It requires only the Subscription Correlation ID as input, with no required output.

questions.question: What single identifier does Nhss_EE_Unsubscribe require to delete a monitoring event subscription at the HSS?
questions.reference_answer: Nhss_EE_Unsubscribe (TS 23.632 clause 6.1.5.2) requests the HSS to delete the subscription of a monitoring event. It requires only the Subscription ID as input, and returns an operation execution result indication.

questions.question: Which BSF service operation deletes an existing PCF binding for a PDU session, a UE, or an MBS session, and how is it invoked at the protocol level?
questions.reference_answer: Nbsf_Management_Deregistration (TS 29.521 clause 4.2.3.1) lets the NF service consumer delete an existing 'Individual PCF for a PDU Session Binding', 'Individual PCF for a UE Binding', or 'Individual PCF for an MBS Session Binding' resource at the BSF. It is invoked by issuing an HTTP DELETE request targeting the resource URI of the binding to be deleted.

questions.question: Which NSSF service operation lets an AMF unsubscribe from NSSAI availability change notifications, and what input identifies the subscription to cancel?
questions.reference_answer: Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability_Unsubscribe (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.16.3.5) lets an NF Service Consumer such as the AMF unsubscribe from a previously subscribed notification of NSSAI availability changes, Network Slice Replacement, or Network Slice Instance Replacement. It requires the Subscription Correlation ID as input.

questions.question: What is the Namf_Communication_N2InfoSubscribe service operation used for, and what does an NF have to provide when invoking it?
questions.reference_answer: Namf_Communication_N2InfoSubscribe (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.8) lets an NF subscribe with the AMF for delivery of information contained in a specific N2 message type. The required input is CN NF ID and the N2 information type to be subscribed; there is no required output.

questions.question: How does an NF stop receiving AMF Status Change notifications, and what identifier does that service operation require?
questions.reference_answer: It invokes Namf_Communication_AMFStatusChangeUnSubscribe (TS 23.502 clause 5.2.2.2.15) to unsubscribe from AMF Status Change notification. The required input is one or more GUAMIs, used to identify the AMF; there is no required output.

questions.question: In edge computing PFD management, which procedures put the NEF together with the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 4.18.2.2 (procedure for PFD management based on PFD Determination analytics) has the NWDAF notify or respond to the NEF (PFDF) with PFD Determination analytics, which the NEF (PFDF) compares against UDR-stored PFD information to decide whether to create/update/delete PFD information for the Application Identifier. TS 23.288 clause 6.16.4 (NWDAF-assisted PFD Determination) is the matching analytics-side procedure: the Consumer NF (NEF/PFDF) subscribes to the NWDAF for PFD Determination analytics, the NWDAF subscribes back to PFD notifications from the NEF (PFDF), and the NWDAF ultimately derives and notifies new/updated/deleted PFD information to the NEF (PFDF).

questions.question: In TR 23.700-08, which procedures for delivering hosting network selection and access information put the UDR and the NEF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TR 23.700-08 have the UDR and the NEF acting together in a step to deliver hosting network selection and access information. Clause 6.14.3 ("UE receives hosting network selection and access information from Localized service provider"): the hosting-network server, which may be the UDR, sends a Nudr_DM_Notify message to the NEF of the hosting network including the LSP ID and the Hosting Network Selection and Access Information, and the NEF then forwards it on (via Nnef_EventExposure_Notify) to the Local Service Provider App. Clause 6.43.3 ("Hosting network selection and access information transfer from hosting network to UE's home network"): the AF of the Localized service provider sends a notification of localized service registration to the UDR of the hosting network via the NEF of the hosting network, and the UDR sends a report of localized service registration back to the AF, with the UDR and NEF jointly relaying that registration/selection information toward the UE's home network.

questions.question: In ML Model lifecycle management with the ADRF, which procedures put the NWDAF and the MTLF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.288 clause 6.2B.5 describes NWDAF containing MTLF storing or updating ML Model(s) in the ADRF via Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest. Clause 6.2B.6 describes NWDAF containing MTLF deleting ML Model(s) from the ADRF via Nadrf_MLModelManagement_Delete. Clause 6.2B.7 describes NWDAF service consumers (containing MTLF or AnLF) retrieving ML Model(s) from the ADRF via Nadrf_MLModelManagement_RetrievalRequest, with NWDAF containing MTLF acting as the ADRF service consumer in the direct-retrieval branch. TR 23.700-81 clause 6.43.2 describes an alternate solution where the NWDAF containing MTLF stores the trained ML Model(s) and/or ML model information in the ADRF (optionally via DCCF) using the same Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest operation, and an NWDAF containing AnLF later retrieves the stored model.
