Clause 6.61.2.1 describes a further alternate solution where the NWDAF containing MTLF retrieves ML Model(s) from the ADRF on behalf of an NWDAF containing AnLF, adjusting filter information and, if it trains a new/further model, storing it back to the ADRF. In all five, the NWDAF instance running the MTLF logical function directly interacts with the ADRF in one step of the procedure.

questions.question: Which procedures put the RNC, the CN and the RANAP protocol in the same step for triggering a UTRAN-to-GSM intersystem handover?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.931 7.13.1.2 (Service Based Intersystem Handover): the CN initiates the radio access bearer with a RANAP Radio Access Bearer Assignment Request carrying the Service Handover IE, and based on that IE the RNC decides to hand over to GSM and sends a RANAP Relocation Required message to the CN. TS 25.931 7.13.1.3 (Directed Retry): the CN again initiates the bearer with a RANAP Radio Access Bearer Assignment Request, but the RNC responds with a RANAP Assignment Response failing the RAB setup and then sends RANAP Relocation Required with cause 'Directed Retry' to the CN.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the WT and the WLAN in the same step for modifying resources of an existing LWA bearer?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.300 22A.1.7.2 (WT Modification): either the eNB or the WT can initiate WT Modification to modify, establish or release bearer contexts for WLAN resources within the same WT; the eNB and WT exchange WT Modification Request/Confirm (or Required/Acknowledge) messages and the eNB reconfigures the UE's RRC connection if needed.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the NG and the AN in the same step for resuming the user plane connection of a PDU session after UE-triggered connection resume?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.502 5.2.2.3.25 (UE Triggered Connection Resume in RRC Inactive procedure): upon a notification that the UE is reachable, the NF service consumer (e.g. AMF) requests the SMF to resume the user plane connection of a PDU session, including N2 SM information such as the Path Switch Request Transfer received from the 5G-AN (NG interface), and the SMF replies with N2 SM information (Path Switch Response Transfer) to the 5G-AN if the resume succeeds.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AMF, the UDM, the TMSI and the GUAMI in the same step for AMF deregistration (purge)?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.503 5.3.2.4.2 (AMF deregistration for 3GPP access): the AMF sends a PATCH request to set the purgeFlag on the UDM's Amf3GppAccessRegistration resource; the UDM checks the received GUAMI against the stored GUAMI and, if it matches, sets the purge flag, otherwise the AMF may avoid freezing the UE's 5G-TMSI. TS 29.503 5.3.2.4.3 (AMF deregistration for non-3GPP access): the same PATCH/GUAMI-check/purge-flag/5G-TMSI logic applies to the AmfNon3GppAccessRegistration resource for non-3GPP access.

questions.question: For activating and deactivating SMS service authorization, which procedures put the AMF, the SMSF and the UDM in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 29.540 put the AMF, SMSF and UDM in the same step: clause 5.2.2.2.2 ('Activation of SMS service'), where the AMF sends an HTTP PUT to the SMSF to activate SMS for a UE and, if no UE Context for SMS yet exists, the SMSF registers itself with the UDM for the access type and retrieves subscription data; and clause 5.2.2.3.3 ('Removal of SMS service authorization over one of the access types'), where the AMF sends an HTTP PUT to deactivate SMS for one access type and the SMSF deregisters itself from the UDM for that access type.

questions.question: Which procedures put the LM server and the VAL server in the same step, for monitoring a vertical device's location against an area of interest?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.434 clause 9.3.11.2 (Monitoring VAL UE's location at a given location) shows the VAL server sending a Monitor Location Subscription Request to the LM server with the predetermined area of interest, and the LM server subscribing to UE location monitoring, periodically checking whether the VAL UE is inside or outside that area, and notifying the VAL server ('Notify Presence', 'Notify Absence' or 'Notify Mismatch Location') accordingly.

questions.question: In the number-of-UEs and number-of-PDU-sessions network slice admission control procedures, which procedures put the NSACF together with the SMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 4.2.11.4 (number of PDU Sessions per network slice availability check and update procedure) has the SMF anchoring the PDU session send Nnsacf_NSAC_NumOfPDUsUpdate_Request to the NSACF, which increases or decreases the stored PDU-session count for the S-NSSAI and returns a Result to the SMF. Clause 4.2.11.2a (hierarchical NSACF-based number-of-UEs check and update procedure) shows the same SMF/NSACF interaction pattern reused inside the hierarchical case: the request that reaches the (Primary) NSACF originates from the same anchor-SMF-triggered flow described in clause 4.2.11.2, with the SMF and NSACF acting together to update the UE/PDU-session admission counters.

questions.question: In the study on 5G timing resiliency and time-synchronization enhancements, which procedures put ASTI and TSCTSF in the same step for AF-requested access stratum timing synchronization?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-25 clause 6.7.3.2 ("Procedure for AF requested 5G access stratum timing synchronization with Requested Coverage Area") and clause 6.18.3.2 ("Procedure for subscription based control of access stratum time synchronization service with AF request") both put ASTI and TSCTSF in the same step: the TSCTSF activates or deactivates the 5G access-stratum time-synchronization (ASTI) service for the UE based on the AF request and, respectively, the UE's presence in the requested coverage area or the UE's Time Synchronization Subscription Data and PCF policy decision.

questions.question: In the study on system enhancements for Edge Computing phase 2, which solutions put HR (Home Routed session) and the EASDF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-48: clause 6.2.2 ("PDU Session Establishment Procedure for HR Session Breakout in VPLMN") has the AMF pass an HR Visited Session Breakout allowed indication to the V-SMF, which selects a V-SMF supporting UL-CL with V-EASDF interaction; clause 6.27.2 ("EAS discovery in VPLMN with dynamic setup of a LBO PDU Session") has the H-SMF set up an H-EASDF and DNS handling rules for the HR PDU Session before triggering the switch to a local-breakout PDU Session; clause 6.53.2 shows EAS discovery for that HR PDU Session with Session Breakout in the VPLMN, relying on the V-EASDF set up during establishment.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MBMS, the BM and the SC in the same step for the MBMS User Service initiation and termination lifecycle?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.346 5.3.1 (Initiation): the MBMS UE registers to the MBMS User Service and requests MBMS service keys if security is activated, then uses the MBMS activation procedure to activate the MBMS Bearer Service (the BM-SC receives the activation message unless MBMS Broadcast Mode is used, in which case activation is local to the UE). TS 26.346 5.3.2 (Termination): the MBMS UE deregisters and deregisters the security association if required, then uses the MBMS deactivation procedure to deactivate the Bearer Service when no other User Service still uses it (again with no message to the BM-SC in Broadcast Mode).

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF and the TMGI process in the same step, for creating or deleting an MBS session?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 7.1.1.2 (MBS Session Creation without PCC) shows the AF requesting TMGI allocation from the NEF/MBSF, which forwards the request to the MB-SMF and returns the allocated TMGI(s) to the AF; the NEF/MBSF also forwards the MBS session creation request that may reference a previously allocated TMGI. Clause 7.1.1.4 (MBS Session Deletion without PCC) shows the AF optionally requesting the NEF/MBSF to de-allocate the TMGI, with the NEF/MBSF forwarding the de-allocation request to the MB-SMF and relaying the response back to the AF.

questions.question: In the study on further enhancement for network automation, which solutions put the NWDAF, the AMF and the SMF together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-81: clause 6.11.2 ("Procedure for providing HPLMN load level analytics to VPLMN") has the V-NWDAF request Network Slice load level analytics from the H-NWDAF upon an AMF subscription/request; clause 6.24.2.2 ("Procedure for usage of Federated Learning in Abnormal Behaviour") has Client NWDAFs collect raw data from the SMF and the AMF respectively to train an Abnormal Classifier.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GMS and the MC service server in the same step for group regrouping using a preconfigured MC service group?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures in TS 23.280 clause 10.15.3 put the GMS and the MC service server together in the same step, since the MC service server is subscribed to the group configuration in the GMS and retrieves regroup-group configuration from it: clause 10.15.3.2.1 (preconfigured group regroup formation in a single MC system), clause 10.15.3.3.1 (preconfigured group regroup formation in multiple MC systems), clause 10.15.3.3.4 (preconfigured group regroup rejection in multiple MC systems), and clause 10.15.3.4.1 (adding a newly affiliated user to an in-progress preconfigured group regroup).

questions.question: Which procedure puts the AMF, the LMF and the SL positioning function in the same step for provisioning broadcast ciphering and integrity keys to a UE?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.893 6.22.2 (Solution details, broadcast protection key provision procedure): the LMF invokes Nlmf_Broadcast_CipheringKeyData Notify towards the AMF carrying SL Positioning broadcast Encryption/Integrity Keys (SPEK/SPIK) with validity periods and applicable tracking areas; the AMF stores them and later delivers applicable keys to the Target UE in the Registration Accept after the UE requests them in a Registration Request, deleting the key information once its validity period expires.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SEAF, the UDM and the AUSF in the same step for EAP-TLS based primary authentication?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.501 B.2.1.1 (Security procedures, EAP-TLS): the SEAF forwards the UE's SUCI to the AUSF via Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate; the AUSF requests authentication data from the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get, the UDM (SIDF) de-conceals the SUCI and selects EAP-TLS, and the SEAF then relays every subsequent EAP-TLS message between the UE and the AUSF until the AUSF derives KAUSF/KSEAF and the SEAF derives KAMF. TS 33.501 O.3 (Authentication procedure): for a non-5G-capable (N5GC) device registering via a W-AGF, the AMF/SEAF selects the AUSF and sends Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate Request; the AUSF requests data from the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get, the UDM selects EAP-TLS, and the SEAF relays every EAP-TLS message between the W-AGF/N5GC device and the AUSF until the AUSF derives the MSK and confirms the result to the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_ResultConfirmation.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the HMS and the HNB in the same step for transferring HNB configuration parameters during provisioning?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.467 6.1.4.1 (General): during the HNB Provisioning procedure the HMS transfers CN-level, RAN-level and RF-level configuration parameters to the HNB; if the HNB has auto-configuration capability, the HMS instead sends a list/range of values from which the HNB selects and returns a single value based on measured radio conditions, and the HMS may also supply control parameters for that auto-configuration process.

questions.question: Which procedures put the GMS and the IWF in the same step for subscribing to group configuration information between an MC system and its interworking function?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.283 clause 10.2.3 put the GMS and the IWF together in the same step, in opposite directions of subscription: clause 10.2.3.6 ('IWF subscribes to group configuration'), where the IWF subscribes to group configuration information stored in the group management server (GMS) of the primary MC system; and clause 10.2.3.8 ('MC system subscribes to group configuration'), where the group management server of the MC system instead subscribes to group configuration information stored in the IWF.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CSCF and the HSS in the same step for network-initiated IMS de-registration?
questions.reference_answer: Three de-registration procedures in TS 23.228 clause 5 put the S-CSCF and the HSS together in the same step: clause 5.3.1 (mobile-initiated de-registration), where the S-CSCF sends Cx-Put and the HSS clears or keeps the S-CSCF name and acknowledges with Cx-Put Resp; clause 5.3.2.1 (network-initiated de-registration on registration timeout), same Cx-Put/Cx-Put Resp exchange after the timers expire; and clause 5.3.2.2.1 (HSS-initiated administrative de-registration), where the HSS itself sends Cx-Deregister to the S-CSCF to start the de-registration.

questions.question: In TR 23.700-81, which procedures for roaming service experience analytics put the NWDAF and the PCF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TR 23.700-81 have the NWDAF and the PCF acting together in a step for cross-PLMN service experience analytics of a roaming UE. Clause 6.17.2 ("Procedure for providing VPLMN Service Experience analytics to HPLMN"): the H-PCF requests Service Experience analytics from the H-NWDAF, the H-NWDAF discovers and queries the V-NWDAF for the VPLMN-side analytics, and the H-NWDAF then returns the combined VPLMN+HPLMN analytics to the H-PCF, which may use it to update the UE's URSP/NSSP rules. Clause 6.37.2.1 ("Procedure for the service experience analytics subscription from H-NWDAF to V-NWDAF"): the PCF in the home network subscribes to service experience analytics for home-routed-roaming UEs via the H-NWDAF, the H-NWDAF subscribes onward to the V-NWDAF for the visited-network data, and after deriving the end-to-end analytics the H-NWDAF provides it back to the PCF, which may adjust QoS parameters accordingly.

questions.question: In the study on NWDAF Phase 3 enhancements, which procedures put NWDAF, FL and MTLF in the same step for federated learning directly between NWDAFs?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-81 clauses 6.51.2.1 ("Client NWDAF(s) Selection in Federated Learning Preparation Phase") and 6.21.2.3 ("FL operation between NWDAFs containing MTLF") both put NWDAF and FL in the same step: the Server NWDAF sends an Nnwdaf_MLPreparation_Request/Nnwdaf_MLModelTraining_Subscribe to Client NWDAF(s), which decide whether to join the FL process, run local training and return interim ML models, which the Server NWDAF aggregates. Clause 6.22.2 ("Federated learning group creation procedure") describes the same direct NWDAF-to-NWDAF FL mechanism from the group-formation angle: a Central NWDAF discovers candidate local NWDAFs via NRF, requests them to join the federated learning group for an Analytics ID, and the local NWDAFs reply whether they accept, forming the FL group used by the later training rounds.

questions.question: In the study on 5WWC phase 2 enhancements, which procedures put AMF and TNGF in the same step for switching a multi-access session's non-3GPP access path?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-53 clauses 6.8.3 (overall non-3GPP access switching), 6.16.3 (mobility-registration-based access switching) and 6.17.3 (traffic switching between two non-3GPP access paths) each put AMF and TNGF in the same step: the AMF sends an Initial (UE) Context Setup Request to the TNGF to establish or update the UE's connection over trusted non-3GPP access as part of switching the MA PDU Session's non-3GPP access path (from untrusted non-3GPP access, or between N3IWF and TNGF paths) to the TNGF.

questions.question: In the study on NWDAF Phase 3 enhancements, which solutions put NWDAF and ADRF in the same step for trained ML model storage and retrieval?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-81 clause 6.42.2.1 ("Procedure for trained ML model(s) storage in ADRF") and clause 6.42.2.2 ("Procedure for trained ML model(s) retrieval from ADRF") both put NWDAF (containing MTLF/AnLF) and ADRF in the same step: in 6.42.2.1 the NWDAF containing MTLF sends Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest to the ADRF and the ADRF may subscribe for ML model training updates back to the NWDAF; in 6.42.2.2 the NWDAF containing AnLF sends Nadrf_MLModelManagement_RetrievalRequest to the ADRF, which in turn discovers/queries the NWDAF containing MTLF and returns the model to the requesting NWDAF. Clause 6.43.2 ("Procedure of ML model storage in ADRF and ML model provision from ADRF") describes an alternate solution for the same storage-and-retrieval mechanism: the NWDAF containing MTLF stores the trained ML model(s) in the ADRF (optionally via DCCF) using the same Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest operation, registers the ML model profile, and an ML model consumer (NWDAF containing AnLF) later subscribes to and retrieves it. Clause 6.61.2.1 ("Procedure for ML model Retrieval From ADRF") describes a further alternate solution where the NWDAF containing MTLF retrieves ML model(s) from the ADRF on behalf of an NWDAF containing AnLF, adjusting filter information as needed, and may store a newly trained model back to the ADRF.

questions.question: During registration via untrusted non-3GPP access with N3IWF relocation, what message does the AMF send to N3IWF-1 to trigger the relocation, and how does N3IWF-2 know to route the resumed registration to the same AMF?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 23.700-17 clause 6.11.2.1, the AMF sends a N3IWF Relocation Command to N3IWF-1 that contains a Security Mode Control (SMC) Request message plus the address of N3IWF-2 and an AMF identity (e.g. GUAMI or IP address); N3IWF-1 forwards this to the UE. The UE then connects to N3IWF-2 and sends an IKE_AUTH request containing an EAP-Response/5G-NAS packet with the AMF identity received earlier; N3IWF-2 selects the same AMF based on that received AMF identity and forwards the SMC Complete message to the AMF inside a N3IWF Relocation Notify message, letting the AMF associate it with the existing UE context and resume the registration procedure.

questions.question: Which procedures put the IMS-ALG and the GW in the same step for Optimal Media Routeing session establishment?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.260 5.2.2.1.19.1 (IMS-ALG bypasses its local GW): the IMS-ALG allocates a local transport address at a GW then, once OMR selects the same IP realm as the incoming leg, de-allocates that GW so the local GW is bypassed. TS 32.260 5.2.2.1.19.2 (alternate IP realm is selected): the IMS-ALG interacts with a first GW and an alternate GW, then de-allocates the first GW and maintains the user-plane connection through the alternate GW when OMR selects a different realm.

questions.question: In TR 23.700-62, which procedures for UPF event exposure put the SMF, the PCF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TR 23.700-62 have the SMF, PCF and UPF acting together in a step for UPF event exposure toward TSN AF/TSCTSF. Clause 6.2.3.2 ("SMF based UPF event subscription"): the TSN AF/TSCTSF subscribes for TSN/TSC events via the PCF (Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Subscribe), the PCF issues a Npcf_SMPolicyControl_UpdateNotify to the SMF with updated policy/target-address information, and the SMF then sends Nupf_EventExposure_(Un)subscribe to the UPF so it reports TSC management information changes. Clause 6.2.3.3 ("Bridge information reporting"): during SM Policy Association Establishment the PCF detects a request related to TSN/TSC bridge integration and provides a policy control request trigger; the SMF relays this via the PCF to the TSN AF/TSCTSF, which subscribes for events, and the UPF exposure procedure of 6.2.3.2 is then invoked between UPF and TSN AF. Clause 6.17.3.1 ("Update/release UPF event exposure service subscription directly by UPF"): a consumer NF sends an update/release request directly to the UPF, and the UPF may report this to the SMF (or to the PCF via the SMF) so the SMF/PCF can decide what information to update or release before the UPF responds to the consumer NF.

questions.question: In the notify procedures the AMF uses towards the LMF for UE positioning, which procedures put the LMF and the NRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures in TS 29.518 put the LMF and the NRF in the same step, all describing how the AMF retrieves the LMF's NF profile from the NRF before delivering a notification: clause 5.2.2.3.5.3 (N1MessageNotify in the UE Assisted/UE Based Positioning Procedure), clause 5.2.2.3.5.5 (N1MessageNotify in LCS Event Report/Cancel Location/Periodic-Triggered Invoke procedures), clause 5.2.2.3.5.7 (N1MessageNotify in PRU Association/Disassociation procedures, where the AMF selects the LMF and retrieves its NF profile from the NRF), clause 5.2.2.3.6.3 (N2InfoNotify carrying NRPPa positioning parameters), and clause 5.2.2.4.4.2 (NonUeN2InfoNotify carrying network assistance data). In each case, if the N1/N2 notification URI is not already known, the AMF retrieves the LMF's NF profile from the NRF before sending the notification.

questions.question: Which procedures put the AF and the NWDAF in the same step across the Data Collection AF subscription, exposure and unsubscription lifecycle?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.531 5.3 (subscription): both the NWDAF and the Event Consumer AF discover the Data Collection AF via Nnrf_NFDiscovery and subscribe to events using Naf_EventExposure_Subscribe. TS 26.531 5.6 (data exposure): the Data Collection AF exposes events to the NWDAF and to the Event Consumer AF via Naf_EventExposure_Notify. TS 26.531 5.7 (unsubscription): the NWDAF and the Event Consumer AF each unsubscribe from the Data Collection AF via Naf_EventExposure_Unsubscribe.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SMF, the UUAA process and the USS in the same step, during session establishment?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.256 clause 5.2.3.2 (UUAA during PDU Session Establishment) shows the SMF invoking Nnef_Authentication_AuthenticateAuthorize for the USS-selected authentication/authorization of the UAV, then continuing the PDU Session Establishment once the USS returns the UUAA result. Clause 5.2.3.3 (UUAA during PDN connection establishment at Attach in EPS) shows the SMF+PGW-C retrieving subscription data, invoking the same UUAA procedure of clause 5.2.3.2 towards the USS, and updating the ACL in UPF+PGW-U once the USS-authorized result arrives. Clause 5.2.3.4 (UUAA using UE requested PDN connectivity procedure, for the scenario where UUAA-SM is not performed at Attach) shows the SMF+PGW-C likewise retrieving subscription data from the UDM+HSS and invoking UUAA Authentication/Authorization towards the USS during the UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure, configuring an ACL in the UPF+PGW-U until the USS-driven UUAA succeeds.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NRM server and the TMGI process in the same step, for pre-created session use or multicast session (de)activation in mission-critical group communication?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.434 clause 14.3.4A.2.2 (Use of pre-created MBS session) shows the NRM server initiating a TMGI allocation request either directly to the MB-SMF or indirectly via NEF, then using the allocated TMGI in the MBS session creation request. Clause 14.3.4A.5.2 (Multicast MBS session activation procedure) shows the NRM server sending an MBS session activation request indicating the TMGI to be activated, directly to the MB-SMF or via NEF/MBSF. Clause 14.3.4A.5.3 (Multicast MBS session deactivation procedure) shows the NRM server sending an MBS session deactivation request indicating the TMGI to be deactivated, again directly to the MB-SMF or via NEF/MBSF.

questions.question: In the study on Personal IoT Networks, which procedures put PCF and PEGC in the same step for QoS handling of PIN Element (PINE) communication?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-88 clauses 6.18.2 ("Procedures", non-3GPP delay budget) and 6.19.2.2 ("Procedures for QoS handling of PINE communication with 5GC via PEGC") both put PCF and PEGC in the same step: the PCF creates/updates PCC rules and provides QoS/delay-budget parameters that reach the PEGC via the SMF, and the PEGC may itself request a different non-3GPP delay budget or new QoS flow, which the PCF then re-evaluates.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SRNC and the SCCP protocol in the same step for establishing an inter-RNC signalling connection to request dedicated or common resources?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.420 4.5.1.3 (Establishment procedure initiated from the SRNC): the SRNC sends an SCCP Connection Request carrying a RADIO LINK SETUP REQUEST or ENHANCED RELOCATION REQUEST to the DRNC to request a dedicated DCH, and the DRNC replies with SCCP Connection Confirm or Connection Refusal (RNSAP procedures per TS 25.423). TS 25.420 4.5.1.3A (initiated from an RNC requesting common measurements or information): RNC1 sends an SCCP Connection Request carrying a COMMON MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST or INFORMATION EXCHANGE INITIATION REQUEST to RNC2, which replies with SCCP Connection Confirm or Refusal.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the FEC mechanism and the MBS Application Server in the same step for recovering a lost media object?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.517 6.2.4.6 (Object recovery procedure): using byte ranges recovered from the MBS AS, the MBSTF Client converts the received data into source symbols with ESIs, applies FEC decoding using the originally received symbols plus those recovered from the MBS AS, recovers the transmission object and its FDT metadata, and makes the recovered object available to the MBS-Aware Application via reference point MBS-7.

questions.question: In PCC congestion reporting, which procedures put the RCAF together with the PCRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.203 shows the RCAF and PCRF acting together in one step in four procedures: clause 7.3.1 (UE-initiated IP-CAN session termination), where step 20-21 has the PCRF send a Release context request to the RCAF using its stored identity, and the RCAF acknowledges and releases its context; clause 7.3.2 (GW/PCEF-initiated IP-CAN session termination), with the identical RCAF release-context step (21-22); clause 7.10.1 (RUCI reporting from RCAF to PCRF), where the RCAF sends non-aggregated or aggregated RAN User Plane Congestion Information reports and the PCRF allocates/returns a logical PCRF id; and clause 7.10.2 (PCRF-provided reporting restrictions), where the PCRF sends a Modify UE context request to the RCAF to set or remove reporting restrictions and the RCAF acknowledges and may resume RUCI reporting.

questions.question: For the Federated Learning registration, discovery, and maintenance procedures specified in TS 23.288 and its related stage-3/security procedures, which procedures put the NRF and the NWDAF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Five procedures put the NRF and the NWDAF in the same step for Federated Learning registration, discovery and maintenance: TS 23.288 clause 6.2C.2.1 ('Registration and Discovery procedure for Federated Learning'), where FL Server/Client NWDAF instances register their NF profiles (FL capability type, Analytics ID, etc.) with the NRF and the FL Server NWDAF discovers FL Client NWDAF(s) via the NRF; TS 23.288 clause 6.2C.2.3 ('Procedures for Maintaining Federated Learning Processes'), where the FL Server NWDAF gets the updated status of Client NWDAF(s) via NRF subscription/notification and discovers new candidate Client NWDAF(s) via the NRF during the execution phase; TS 29.552 clause 5.10.2.2 ('Preparation Procedure for Federated Learning'), where the FL Server/Client NWDAF instances register their NF profiles with the NRF and are discovered via the NRF; TS 29.552 clause 5.10.2.3 ('Procedure for Maintenance of Federated Learning Process'), where the FL Server NWDAF discovers new FL Client NWDAF(s) via the NRF during the FL execution phase; and TS 33.738 clause 6.17.2, which describes the high-level procedure for authorizing FL Server and FL Client NWDAFs that first register to the NRF with their FL-related information (Analytics ID, Interoperability ID, FL capability type, etc.) and later obtain access tokens from the NRF when reselecting Client NWDAFs.

questions.question: In the study on 5G timing resiliency and UPF-selection enhancements, which procedures put BSF and PCF in the same step for storing UPF information in the BSF?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-62 clauses 6.15.3.1.2 ("Procedure of UPF information in BSF") and 6.22.3.2 ("The consumer NF subscribes UPF change notification from the BSF by storing UPF ID and UE IP address in the BSF...") both put BSF and PCF in the same step: during PDU Session Establishment the SMF sends Npcf_SMPolicyControl_Update to the PCF with the UE IP address and UPF ID, and the PCF then sends Nbsf_Management_Register to the BSF to store that UPF/UE-IP mapping.

questions.question: In the study on architecture enhancements for a mobile base station relay, which procedures put AMF and IAB in the same step for cross-border roaming of the relay?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-05 clause 6.6.3.1 ("Signalling flow for roaming of mobile base station relay operating using IAB node integration procedure") and clause 6.6.3.2 ("...using inter-IAB-donor gNB mobility procedure") both put AMF and IAB (the IAB-UE / mobile base station relay) in the same step: the mobile base station relay (IAB-UE) sends a Registration Request to the VPLMN AMF, and the AMF checks with UDM whether MBSR operation is authorized before sending an MBSR-authorized indication back and letting the relay proceed with IAB node integration or inter-donor gNB mobility.

questions.question: In the study on converging fixed and mobile subscriber data management, which solutions put the UDM and the HSS FE together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.973: clause 6.2.3.1 ("Authentication and Registration") has the UDM interact with the HSS FE to retrieve authentication vectors from the EPS UDR and to relay Update/Cancel Location signalling for single registration; clause 6.2.3.2 ("IP address continuity of interworking without N26 from 5GS to EPS") has the UDM forward Update Location Request/Ack to the HSS FE, which handles it against the EPS UDR and returns the PGW-C+SMF FQDN; clause 6.2.3.3 ("T-ADS for IMS voice") has the UDM forward a T-ADS query to the HSS FE, which queries MME/SGSN and returns T-ADS information back through the UDM; clause 6.2.3.4 ("Supporting IMS related procedures") has the UDM identify IMS Cx/Dx/Sh requests and forward them to the HSS FE, which interacts with the EPS UDR and returns responses via the UDM; clause 6.2.3.6 ("MT SMS domain selection") has the UDM retrieve the SMSF address from the 5GS UDR and forward the MAP Send Routing Info for SM request to the HSS FE to obtain additional MT SMS routing addresses from the EPS side.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the CRNC and the CFN in the same step for updating the UE's timing advance value in CELL_FACH state?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.402 8.3.4.3.2 (UE with USCH Traffic in CELL_FACH state): the CRNC determines whether a new timing advance value is needed and, if so, includes the new value together with the CFN in which it takes effect in the next USCH allocation message (PHYSICAL SHARED CHANNEL ALLOCATION) to the UE, and also sends a user-plane control message with the CFN and updated timing advance to the Node B so it can adjust its physical-layer averaging.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF, the TSCTSF and the AF in the same step, for setting up or updating a session with required QoS?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.6 (Setting up an AF session with required QoS) shows the AF sending a Nnef_AFsessionWithQoS_Create request to the NEF, which then decides whether to forward the request via Ntsctsf_QoSandTSCAssistance_Create to the TSCTSF (which in turn talks to the PCF) or to contact the PCF directly; the trusted AF can also interact with the TSCTSF directly. Clause 4.15.6.6a (AF session with required QoS update procedure) mirrors the same three-party flow for an update: the AF sends Nnef_AFsessionWithQoS_Update to the NEF, which forwards to the same NF type (TSCTSF or PCF) it used at session establishment via Ntsctsf_QoSandTSCAssistance_Update.

questions.question: For indirect communication with delegated discovery, which procedures put the SCP and the NRF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures put the SCP and the NRF in the same step for indirect communication with delegated discovery: (1) TS 33.501 clause 13.4.1.3.2, 'Authorization and service invocation procedure, for indirect communication with delegated discovery', where the SCP requests an access token (Nnrf_AccessToken_Get) from the NRF on behalf of the NF Service Consumer and forwards the service request to the NF Service Producer; (2) TS 23.502 clause E.2, 'Delegated I-SMF discovery', where the SCP (optionally) sends an Nnrf_NFDiscovery Request to the NRF to discover SMF instances on behalf of the AMF, applying delegated SMF discovery to the PDU Session Establishment procedure; (3) TS 33.738 clause 6.6.2.3, where the NWDAF subscribes to the NRF (Nnrf_NFManagement_NFStatusSubscribe) for NF load/status changes using SCP-identified NF service consumers as part of collecting security log data via OAM; and (4) TS 33.875 clause 6.3.2.1, 'Access token request of SCP on behalf of an NF Service Consumer', which describes how the SCP uses a CCA to request an access token from the NRF for Scenario D (indirect communication with delegated discovery).

questions.question: In the network-assisted DAA procedure for two UAVs, what request does the USS send to the GMLC, and what does the GMLC do with the two resulting location results before reporting back to the USS?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 23.700-58 clause 6.2.3 (Option A), the USS, acting as AF/LCS client, sends a relative positioning request to the GMLC including the two UAV UE identities (GPSIs), a time slot, and a distance threshold. The GMLC obtains the location of UAV UE1 and UAV UE2 (using the GMLC-based procedure of TS 23.273 clause 6.1.2) at the scheduled time, calculates the relative positioning result from the two locations, checks it against the distance threshold, and reports the relative position result back to the USS within the given time slot.

questions.question: In the study on aligning 5GS support for enabling edge applications, which solutions put the ECSP and the OP (edge operator) together in the same step for edge node sharing?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-98: clause 7.44.2.3 ("EAS discovery for edge node sharing") has ECSP-1 and ECSP-2, under a service-level agreement, let EES-B request the list of registered EASs from partner Operator OP-A's EES-A; clause 7.45.2.2 ("EAS discovery Procedure") has the EES determine the EAS based on the desired ECSP of the UE and the ECSP of the EAS across OP A / OP B; clause 7.45.2.3 ("T-EAS discovery Procedure") has the T-EES determine the T-EAS the same way, using the EEC's home ECSP (identifying its OP).

questions.question: In EEC-authorized application context relocation, which procedures put the ACR, the EAS and the EES in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Two solutions in TS 33.739 put the ACR, the EAS and the EES in the same step for EEC-authorized application context relocation: clause 6.26.3 ('S-EAS decided ACR'), where the source EAS decides to trigger ACR, discovers the target EAS, and the source EES sends the target information notification to the EEC for authorization; and clause 6.26.4 ('S-EES executed ACR'), where the source EES itself detects and decides to execute ACR (triggered by a User Plane path change notification or EAS request) and coordinates with the EAS and EEC for authorization before relocating the EEC context.

questions.question: For authentication and authorization at the Nt DN-AAA server, which procedures put the SMF and the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Four procedures in TS 29.561 put the SMF and the UPF in the same step for DN-AAA authentication and authorization: clause 11.2.1 ('Authentication, Authorization and Accounting procedures in 5GC'), where the SMF sends a RADIUS Access-Request via the UPF to the DN-AAA server upon receiving an initial PDU session request; clause 11.2.1a ('...in EPC Interworking'), the same RADIUS flow when the SMF+PGW-C receives a Create Session Request from the MME; clause 12.2.1, the equivalent flow using Diameter DER/DEA messages in 5GC; and clause 12.2.1a, the Diameter variant for EPC interworking via SMF+PGW-C.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MAP protocol and the MSC in the same step for handling an inter-node handover or emergency-call location request?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.010 4.5 (Inter-MSC Handover): interworking rules govern whether new handover parameters are carried in the AN-APDU (same encapsulated protocol as the target radio access network interface) or in a MAP message (different encapsulated protocol, or parameters needed only by the target MSC) when transferred over the E-interface between MSCs. TS 32.271 5.2.3.3 (Network Induced Location Request): during an emergency call, the MSC (or SGSN) forwards the location request to the GMLC via a MAP Subscriber Location Report, which the GMLC acknowledges before transferring the location information to the LCS client.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the DN, the MOI and the NSI in the same step for intent-driven network slice delivering and assurance?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.836 6.4.2 (Procedure for intent driven approach for network slice service delivering and assurance): the MnS_Producer_for_Slice creates a concrete intent MOI for the consumer's expectation on a network slice, decides to create a new NSI or reuse an existing one, invokes procedures to deliver the corresponding network slice subnet(s), creates the MOI for NetworkSlice configured with the DN of the NetworkSliceSubnet MOI, and continuously monitors and reports intent fulfilment for the network slice.

questions.question: In the study on 5GS with satellite backhaul, which solutions put the GEO satellite and the SMF together with the UPF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-27: clause 6.4.2 ("Enabling GEO satellite edge computing via on-board UPF") has the AMF determine the GEO satellite ID serving the UE and pass it to the SMF, which sets up local switching via the on-board UPF; clause 6.6.2 ("High-level procedure for UPF-level N4 session solution") has the SMF create UPF-level N4 sessions and address mapping across on-board UPFs to support UE-UE local data switching over a GEO satellite backhaul.

questions.question: For location continuity during handover of an IMS emergency call, which procedures put the LRF and the GMLC in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 23.271 clause 9.4.5.4.2 (handover between 3GPP and 3GPP2 access types), the source SGSN/MME sends a Provide Subscriber Location response or Subscriber Location Report to the source GMLC carrying any location estimate obtained by the LRF-assigned session, and the target serving node sends a Subscriber Location Report to a target GMLC; the LRF and source/target location servers (including the GMLC) are then reconfigured. In clause 9.4.5.4.3 (E-UTRAN handover to WLAN) the source MME returns a Provide Subscriber Location response / Subscriber Location Report to the source GMLC and the LRF's source/target location servers are reconfigured. In clause 9.4.5.4.4 (WLAN handover to E-UTRAN, UTRAN or GERAN) the target MME or MSC server sends a Subscriber Location Report to a GMLC on the target side, which the GMLC acknowledges, and the LRF is again reconfigured together with the source/target location servers.

questions.question: In the study on satellite backhaul enhancements for non-public networks, which solutions put CAG and the DNN together in the same step for local-service access?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-08: clause 6.23.3 has the UE receive hosting-network selection and access information from the Localized Service Provider, tied to a DNN and CAG-based access; clause 6.32.3 ("Discovery and access local service via PNI-NPN") has the network provide, during Registration, a list of available local services together with the CAG identifiers and validity period for a given DNN-based service.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the AMF and the CHF in the same step for untrusted non-3GPP access registration charging?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.256 5.2.2.2.9 (Registration - Untrusted non-3GPP access - PEC charging): after NAS Registration Accept is sent via the N3IWF, the AMF sends a Charging Data Request[Event] to the CHF for the successful registration, and the CHF creates the CDR and acknowledges with a Charging Data Response.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the SMLC and the LMU in the same step for updating an ongoing uplink measurement?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.305 7.4.1.2 (Measurement Update): the E-SMLC informs the LMU of a change in the UE SRS transmission configuration during an ongoing SLmAP measurement reporting transaction by sending a Measurement Update, and the LMU continues UL RTOA measurements using the updated configuration.

questions.question: Which procedures put the CHF and the NSSAI in the same step for determining Network Slice charging duration by tenant?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.847 6.7.2.3 (Flow description): for NS actual duration charging based on SMF reporting, the CHF acting as UE CCS generates the UE CDR per S-NSSAI and reports each PDU session establishment/release Charging Data Request to the CHF acting as Tenant CCS, which generates CDRs the billing domain uses to derive the NS actual duration for the tenant. TS 32.847 6.7.4.3 (Flow description): for NS actual duration charging based on NWDAF performance collection, the CEF subscribes to PDU session count changes from the NWDAF and, once it determines the NS duration from the reported status, triggers a Charging Data Request to the CHF acting as Tenant CCS (configured with the S-NSSAI-to-Tenant-ID relationship), which counts the duration of the network slice for the tenant.

questions.question: Which procedures put the IWF and the LMR in the same step when an MC service client affiliates to or de-affiliates from a group defined in the LMR system?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.283 clause 10.1.2 put the IWF and the LMR-hosted group together in the same step: clause 10.1.2.4 ('Group affiliation to group defined in the LMR system'), where the MC service server sends an IWF group affiliation request to the IWF and receives an IWF group affiliation response confirming the LMR group affiliation; and clause 10.1.2.5 ('Group de-affiliation from a group defined in the LMR system'), where the MC service server sends an IWF group de-affiliation request to the IWF and receives the corresponding de-affiliation response.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF and the TSCTSF in the same step, for a required-QoS request targeting a group of devices?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.14 (Procedure for AF requested QoS for a UE or group of UEs not identified by a UE address) shows the NEF forwarding the group-addressed Nnef_AF_Request_QoS_Create request to the TSCTSF (step 4), and the TSCTSF replying to the NEF with the group members' relevant PDU Session information after resolving SUPIs via UDM (steps 5, 8), i.e. the NEF and TSCTSF interact directly in the same steps when the request targets a group by GPSI or External/Internal Group ID. TR 23.700-74 clause 6.22.3.1 (Procedure for provisioning of traffic characteristics and performance monitoring for a group) describes the TR draft solution version of the same mechanism: the NEF forwards Group ID, QoS parameters and Requested Alternative QoS Parameter Set(s) to the TSCTSF via Ntsctsf_QoSandTSCAssistance_Create, and the TSCTSF resolves the individual group members and replies to the NEF.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the MDA and the MDAS in the same step for the generic MDA analytics request and reporting workflow?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.104 11.1 (MDA request and reporting workflow): the MDAS Producer creates an MDARequest MOI for the MDAS Consumer, then per the requested reportingMethod (File/Streaming/Notification) subscribes to notifications or sets up a streaming connection with the reporting target; while the request is active the MDAS Producer keeps performing MDA and sends each MDA report to the reporting target using the selected reporting method.

questions.question: Which procedures put the I-CSCF and the HSS(-FE) in the same step when the I-CSCF sends a Cx-Query/Cx-Select-Pull (or equivalent Diameter query) to obtain the serving S-CSCF's name?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures put the I-CSCF/S-CSCF and the HSS together in the same step to resolve the serving S-CSCF: TS 23.228 clause 5.6.5.3 ('S-CSCF selection by I-CSCF for AS Originating call procedures'), where the I-CSCF queries the HSS for S-CSCF capabilities or the previously allocated S-CSCF name, and the S-CSCF then sends Cx-Put/Cx-Pull to store its name at the HSS; and TS 23.335 clause A.1.3 ('IMS re-registration flow example with Ud Query from HSS-FE'), where the I-CSCF sends Cx-Query/Cx-Select-Pull to the HSS(-FE), which fetches data from the UDR and returns the S-CSCF name.

questions.question: In 5G ProSe link security establishment via a UE-to-UE relay or for ranging, which procedures put a Direct Communication Request (DCR) and a Relay/Ranging Service Code (RSC) in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.740 clauses 6.3.2.1 and 6.4.2 show the 5G ProSe Source/Target UE sending a Direct Communication Request (DCR) containing the Relay Service Code (RSC) and an authorization token to the UE-to-UE Relay to establish PC5 security. Clause 6.7.2 shows the non-network-assisted variant, where the Source UE and UE-to-UE Relay exchange DCRs carrying a long-term credential ID and RSC. Clause 6.30.2.1 shows RSC/DCR used in security integrated into PC5 link establishment for discovery. TS 33.893 clauses 6.5.2.2.1 and 6.5.2.2.2 show the analogous DCR/RSC exchange for the Ranging service, between the Reference UE and Target UE (6.5.2.2.1) and between the Reference/Target UE and an Assistant UE (6.5.2.2.2).

questions.question: For layer-triggered mobility (LTM), which procedures put the gNB-CU and gNB-DU in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.401 clause 8.2.1.4 (Intra-gNB-DU LTM) shows the gNB-CU sending UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST messages to the gNB-DU to prepare candidate cells and later a CU-DU MOBILITY INITIATION REQUEST to trigger early synchronization/cell switch, with the gNB-DU forwarding RRC messages and reporting ACCESS SUCCESS. Clause 8.2.1.5 (Inter-gNB-DU LTM) shows the gNB-CU coordinating with both the source and candidate gNB-DUs via UE CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION and CU-DU/DU-CU CELL SWITCH NOTIFICATION and TA INFORMATION TRANSFER messages when the UE moves to another gNB-DU. Clause 8.2.1.6 (LTM with gNB-CU-UP change) shows the gNB-CU-CP performing LTM configuration with the gNB-DU (steps drawn from 8.2.1.5) while also setting up/modifying the bearer context in the gNB-CU-UP.

questions.question: In the study on ranging-based services and sidelink positioning, which procedures put GMLC and LMF in the same step for network-assisted sidelink positioning in network coverage?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-86 clauses 6.20.3.1 ("MT-LR procedure for Network assisted Sidelink positioning in Network Coverage case") and 6.20.3.2 ("MO-LR procedure for Network assisted Sidelink positioning in Network Coverage case") both put GMLC and LMF (UE1 LMF) in the same step: UE1 LMF sends a Provide Location Request to the GMLC for the Located UE (UE2), and the GMLC triggers UE2's own positioning procedure and returns UE2's location to UE1 LMF.

questions.question: In the study on enhancement of 5G UE Policy, which solutions put the SMF, the URSP and the DNN together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-85: clause 6.10.2.1 ("Network based URSP rules enforcement feedback") has the PCF find the serving SMF for a UE (with S-NSSAI/DNN) via UDM to verify URSP enforcement; clause 6.30.4 ("NWDAF providing analytics for URSP rules enforcement") has the PCF request URSP-enforcement analytics from the NWDAF, tied to the DNN/S-NSSAI, working with the SMF-served session context.

questions.question: Which procedures put the UP and the DRB together in the same step for activating user-plane security?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.501 6.6.2 (UP security activation mechanism, 5G): AS UP integrity protection and ciphering are activated per DRB as part of the RRC Connection Reconfiguration procedure; the gNB/ng-eNB signals the activation per DRB and both sides generate KUPint/KUPenc and start UP integrity protection and ciphering for the indicated DRBs. TS 33.401 7.3.4 (UP integrity protection activation mechanism, LTE): as part of the DRB addition via RRC Connection Reconfiguration, the eNB signals per-DRB UP integrity activation and both eNB and UE generate KUPint and start UP integrity protection for the indicated DRBs. TS 33.401 E.2.3 (SeNB encryption/decryption activation, dual connectivity): the MeNB forwards the UP integrity protection policy to the SeNB when offloading DRB(s); the SeNB activates UP integrity protection and ciphering per DRB and the UE derives KUPenc/KUPint and activates the same upon RRC reconfiguration. TS 33.401 E.3.3 (SgNB encryption/decryption/integrity protection activation, dual connectivity): the same per-DRB (and optionally per-SRB) UP security activation flow applies between the MeNB, SgNB and UE using KSgNB-UP-enc/KSgNB-UP-int.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SMF and the UPF in the same step when a PDU Session Anchor is added or removed via an intermediate SMF?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.502 clause 4.3 put the SMF and the UPF together in the same step: clause 4.3.5.5 ('Removal of additional PDU Session Anchor and Branching Point or UL CL'), where the SMF releases PSA1 via N4 and updates the UPF acting as Branching Point/UL CL; and clause 4.23.9.1 ('Addition of PDU Session Anchor and Branching Point or UL CL controlled by I-SMF'), where the I-SMF uses N4 to establish the new PDU Session Anchor 2 on a selected UPF and update the Branching Point/UL CL via N4.

questions.question: Which procedures put the UDM and the AUSF in the same step for triggering a re-authentication that refreshes the anchor key?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.741 5.6.2 (Solution details, UDM initiated primary authentication): the AUSF determines KAUSF needs refreshing (e.g. SoR/UPU counter wraparound) and sends a re-authentication request to the UDM, which checks operator policy and requests the serving AMF (SEAF) to initiate primary authentication. TS 33.741 5.7.2 (Solution details): the UDM sends a Re-Authentication Notification to the AMF, the SEAF invokes Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate towards the AUSF, the AUSF requests authentication data from the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get, and after the new KAUSF is generated the AUSF confirms the result to the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_ResultConfirmation.

questions.question: During N2/Xn handover of a PDU session, which procedures put the AMF, SMF, and access network in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.502 clause 5.2.2.2.4 (I-SMF Insertion, Change or Removal during Xn based Handover) shows the NF Service Consumer (e.g. AMF) requesting the I-SMF/SMF to create an SM context using N2 SM information from the target/source 5G-AN. Clause 5.2.2.3.15 (Connection Suspend procedure) shows the AMF requesting the SMF to suspend the user plane connection using N2 SM information received from the 5G-AN. Clause 5.2.2.3.4.2 (N2 Handover Preparation) shows the target AMF requesting the SMF to prepare the handover, exchanging N2 SM information carrying resource-setup/handover-request information to and from the target 5G-AN. Clause 5.2.2.3.4.3 (N2 Handover Execution) shows the target AMF requesting the SMF to complete the handover execution, using N2 SM information from the source/target 5G-AN.

questions.question: In TR 23.700-05, which procedures for positioning a UE served by a Mobile Base Station Relay (MBSR) put the MBSR and the LMF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TR 23.700-05 have the LMF and the MBSR acting together in a step. Clause 6.8.3 ("Positioning procedure for UE accessing via mobile base station relay"): the AMF invokes Nlmf_Location_DetermineLocation towards the LMF, and based on the MBSR indication the LMF obtains the MBSR's own location (via NRPPa signalling relayed by the mobile base station relay) to calculate the UE's location. Clause 6.15.3 ("Positioning Procedure for a UE with MBSR access"): a generalized positioning procedure (covering 5GC-MT-LR, 5GC-MO-LR, 5GC-NI-LR and deferred 5GC-MT-LR) where the AMF selects an LMF able to support MBSR-access location when it is aware the UE connects via an MBSR, and sends the location request to that LMF. Clause 6.7.3.1 ("MT_LR for UE served by a MBSR using TRP information request procedure"): the MBSR IAB-DU informs the Donor gNB-CU of its mobility, which is forwarded to the LMF together with the MBSR cell ID and permanent MBSR identity, so the LMF can treat the MBSR as a mobile TRP and later use this information when positioning the target UE.

questions.question: In the Send Routing Info for SM mapping via the IWF, what message does the IWF forward on to the HSS after receiving the SMS-GMSC's request, and what does it do with the resulting response?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.305 clause A.3.4.1, after the IWF receives a sendRoutingInfoForSM MAP V3 message from the SMS-GMSC, it sends an SRR (Send Routing Info Request) to the HSS (or SMS Router / IP-SM-GW). On receiving the SRA (Send Routing Info Answer) from the HSS, the IWF sends a sendRoutingInfoForSM Ack message back to the SMS-GMSC, and if the SRA contains information elements requiring an informServiceCentre message, the IWF also sends that message to the SMS-GMSC before closing the MAP dialog.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the AMF, the UDM and the SNPN in the same step for updating AMF registration information for 3GPP access?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.503 5.3.2.2.2 (AMF registration for 3GPP access): the AMF sends a PUT request to the UDM to update or create the UE's AMF registration information, including an 'ueSnpnSubscriptionInd' IE when the UE supports equivalent SNPNs and is served by an AMF in an equivalent SNPN of its subscribed SNPN; the UDM stores or replaces the registration data and returns 200 OK/204 No Content/201 Created, or 403 Forbidden if e.g. the UE registers in an SNPN using Credentials-Holder credentials it is not authorized to use.

questions.question: For UE-triggered policy provisioning, which procedures put the AMF and the PCF in the same step forwarding the UE Policy Container?
questions.reference_answer: Five UE-triggered policy provisioning procedures put the AMF and the PCF together in the same step: TS 23.256 clause 6.3.2.3 (UE triggered A2X Policy provisioning), TS 23.287 clause 6.2.4 and TS 23.700-86 clause 6.2.3.1.2 (UE triggered V2X Policy provisioning), and TS 23.304 clause 6.2.4 and TS 23.700-86 clause 6.2.3.2.2 (UE triggered ProSe/5G ProSe Policy provisioning). In each, the UE sends a UL NAS TRANSPORT message with a UE Policy Container to the AMF, and in the same step the AMF forwards it to the PCF via Namf_Communication_N1MessageNotify so the PCF can authorize and deliver the relevant policy.

questions.question: For gNB-CU-DU signalling during management-based MDT activation, which procedures put the MDT feature and the TCE in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 38.401 clause 8.13 put MDT and the TCE in the same step, one per split gNB unit: clause 8.13.2.2 ('Management based MDT Activation in gNB-CU-CP'), where the gNB-CU-CP checks MDT user consent and configures the Trace Session; clause 8.13.2.3 ('...in gNB-DU'), where the gNB-CU-CP forwards the Management based MDT PLMN List (and optionally a Polluted Measurement Indicator) to the gNB-DU via UE CONTEXT SETUP so the gNB-DU can flag affected measurements sent to the TCE; and clause 8.13.2.4 ('...in gNB-CU-UP'), the equivalent flow over BEARER CONTEXT SETUP for the CU-UP, again so the TCE can correlate and filter polluted measurements.

questions.question: In the UAE-layer-assisted change of USS, once the UAE server verifies a USS change request from the serving USS, how does it interact with the NEF to affect the user plane path, and what does it then forward to the UAE client?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 23.255 clause 7.6.2.3, after verifying the USS change request is authorized, the UAE server translates the change into a UP path change and interacts with the NEF as an AF to influence UP path routing (switching to the target DNAI), per the AF-influence-on-traffic-routing functionality of TS 23.502 clause 4.3.6.3, checking whether it can serve the target DNAI mapped to the target USS. The UAE server then forwards the USS change request to the UAE client, including the target USS information and updated Multi-USS policies, and the UAE client initiates communication with the target USS.

questions.question: Which procedures put the PF and the CDR in the same step for ProSe one-to-one direct communication charging?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.277 5.2.2.3.7 (event-based charging under coverage): the ProSe Function (PF) triggers a Charging Data Request[Event] to the CDF, which generates the CDR for both UEs' one-to-one direct communication. TS 32.277 5.2.2.3.10 (session-based charging under coverage): the PF triggers Charging Data Request[Start]/[Interim]/[Stop] to the CDF, which opens, updates and closes the CDR for the session accordingly.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the SMF and the RG in the same step when a 5G Residential Gateway hands its PDU session over between wireline and 3GPP access?
questions.reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.316 clause 7.6 put the SMF and the RG (5G-RG) together in the same step: clause 7.6.3.1 ('Handover of a PDU Session procedure from W-5GAN access to 3GPP access'), where the SMF releases resources over the source W-5GAN access for the 5G-RG's PDU Session while keeping the SM context with the AMF; and clause 7.6.4.1 ('Handover from 3GPP access/EPS to W-5GAN/5GC'), where the 5G-RG performs registration and PDU Session establishment with an existing-session indication via W-5GAN access, following the EPS-to-5GC-N3IWF handover procedure with the PGW-C+SMF.

questions.question: In the PDN GW initiated bearer modification procedure with bearer QoS update, what message does the PDN GW send to the Serving GW, and how does the Serving GW pass this on to the MME to reach the eNodeB and UE?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 23.401 clause 5.4.2.1, the PDN GW sends an Update Bearer Request (PTI, EPS Bearer Identity, EPS Bearer QoS, APN-AMBR, TFT, Maximum Packet Loss Rate) message to the Serving GW, which forwards the same Update Bearer Request to the MME. The MME builds a Session Management Request (with the QoS parameters, TFT, APN-AMBR, EPS Bearer Identity) and sends a Bearer Modify Request to the eNodeB, which maps the modified EPS Bearer QoS to the Radio Bearer QoS and signals an RRC Connection Reconfiguration message (carrying the Session Management Request) to the UE.

questions.question: Which procedures put the DSO and the MNO in the same step for coordinating an energy service outage and rapid recovery?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.318 A.2.2 (Coordinated Rapid Recovery and strategic outage plan Procedure): the DSO creates an OutageAndRecovery MOI at the MNO's MnS producer and subscribes to notifications, and the MNO notifies the DSO of attribute changes such as maxServiceDuration and answers the DSO's modify/query requests. TS 28.829 7.3.2.1.2 (Description): the DSO creates an MOI at the MNO holding outage/recovery timestamps and UPS backup information, the MNO notifies the DSO of attribute changes, and the DSO modifies and queries the UPS-related information via the MNO's MnS producer. TS 28.829 C.4.4 (Use case service flow): illustrates a power-cut incident where the DSO informs the MNO and the MNO may sustain the network on UPS for a limited time, but without standardized MNO-DSO coordination the DSO cannot use Smart Energy Services to accelerate recovery and must dispatch a technician instead. TS 22.867 5.18.3 (Service Flows): an ECC operator observes a power-line fault causing an outage; MNOs A and B, whose cellular nodes serving the recloser also lose power, inform the DSO operator (U) of the coincident outage and its UPS capacity so the DSO can coordinate remote recovery of the Distribution Automation asset.

questions.question: For DAA (Detect And Avoid) policy management between the UAS Application Enabler and its service consumer, which procedures put UAE and DAA in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.257 clauses 5.5.2.2.2/5.5.2.2.3/5.5.2.2.4 cover DAA Policy Creation/Update/Deletion (service consumer sends HTTP POST/PUT-PATCH/DELETE to the UAE Server), clause 5.5.2.3.2 covers the DAA Events Information Request (service consumer POSTs detected DAA events to the UAE Server), and clauses 5.5.2.4.2/5.5.2.4.3 cover the UAE Server notifying the service consumer of DAA Policy Configuration Completion Status and of DAA events, respectively.

questions.question: In the study on 5GC architecture enhancements for Time Sensitive Communication, which solutions put the UMIC and the PMIC together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-25: clause 6.11.3 ("Procedure for reserve the resource in TSN transport network") has NG-RAN send the uplink/downlink Port Management Information Container (PMIC/UMIC) in the N2 request to carry stream information for the CUC; clause 6.3.3 (timing synchronization resiliency and status reporting) reuses PDU session establishment enhanced for UPF timing resiliency, exposing timing synchronization capability that PMIC/UMIC information relies on.

questions.question: Which procedures put the NEF and the AF in the same step for subscribing to or unsubscribing from Member UE selection assistance?
questions.reference_answer: Two TS 23.502 clause 4.15.13 procedures put the NEF and the AF together in the same step for Member UE selection assistance: clause 4.15.13.1 ('Member UE selection assistance subscribe and update procedure'), where the AF subscribes to Member UE selection assistance by invoking a NEF service operation with its Member UE filtering criteria; and clause 4.15.13.7 ('Member UE selection assistance unsubscribe procedure'), where the AF sends Nnef_MemberUESelectionAssistance_unsubscribe (Subscription Correlation ID) and the NEF deletes the subscription(s) and responds with the operation execution result.

questions.question: In the study on further enhancements of Wireline-Wireless convergence, which solutions put the AMF and the TNGF together with the SSID in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-17: clause 6.10.2.1 ("Registration via trusted non-3GPP access with TNGF relocation") has the AMF trigger TNGF relocation during registration; clause 6.17.2 covers Registration and N3IWF/TNGF relocation so the AMF selects an N3IWF/TNGF supporting the requested S-NSSAIs, with SSID used for slice-aware WLAN selection; clause 6.19.2 has the UE select an SSID associated with the requested slices and the AMF process the resulting Registration Request, indicating TNGF selection based on slicing.

questions.question: In the enhanced network slicing study (TS 23.700-41), which procedures put the AMF and NSSF together in the same step of registration/slice selection handling?
questions.reference_answer: In TS 23.700-41 (study on enhanced support of network slicing), five candidate solutions show the AMF and the NSSF acting together in one step of registration or slice-selection handling: clause 6.10.2 (handling of a temporary S-NSSAI, where the AMF registers to the UDM and the validity timer for a temporary S-NSSAI can also be provided by the NSSF), clause 6.25.3 (UE registration/registration-update procedure, where the AMF decides the Registration Area and Allowed NSSAI with the help of UDM/NSSF), clause 6.26.3 (registration procedure impacts, where the AMF provides NSSAI information to the NSSF and creates Allowed/Secondary Allowed NSSAI based on NSSF input), clause 6.36.3 (registration with S-NSSAI having different reasons, where the AMF, or the NSSF, determines the Allowed NSSAI), and clause 6.42.3 (replacing an unavailable S-NSSAI, where the AMF, together with the NSSF via Nnssf_NSSelection_Get, determines and configures an alternative S-NSSAI).

questions.question: Which procedures put the IWF and the LMS in the same step for an event-triggered (unsolicited) location notification, or for using that notified location to answer a 'who is talking' query, between an MC system and an LMR system?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.283 clause 10.11 put the IWF and the LMS (via the MC service server) together in the same step: clause 10.11.4.2.2.1 (event-triggered location notification from the IWF in the LMR system to the LMS in the MC system), clause 10.11.4.2.2.2 (the reverse notification, from the LMS in the MC system to the IWF in the LMR system), and clause 10.11.3 ('Location of current talker'), where the MCPTT server checks the privacy policy of the current talking IWF user and provides that user's location, obtained via the IWF, to the MCPTT clients on the call.

questions.question: For IAB inter-donor-CU topology adaptation and backhaul recovery, which procedures put the IAB-donor-CU and gNB-DU in the same step involving a transport network layer (TNL) address?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.401 clause 8.17.2.1 (IAB Inter-CU topological redundancy procedure) shows the F1-terminating and non-F1-terminating IAB-donor-CUs exchanging IAB TRANSPORT MIGRATION MANAGEMENT messages and configuring new TNL addresses for the dual-connecting IAB-node's second path via the parent IAB-DU. Clause 8.17.3.1 (IAB inter-CU topology adaptation procedure) and 8.17.3.2 (with descendant IAB-node) show the source and target IAB-donor-CUs migrating an IAB-node's F1-C/F1-U TNL addresses across IAB-DUs during topology change. Clause 8.17.4 (IAB Inter-CU Backhaul RLF recovery) shows the recovering IAB-node's IAB-MT/IAB-DU reconnecting to a new IAB-donor-CU with reconfigured TNL addresses via the new parent IAB-DU. Clause 8.23.4 (Mobile IAB-node RLF recovery) reuses the same donor-CU/IAB-DU TNL-address migration steps from 8.17.3.1/8.17.4 for a mobile IAB-node.

questions.question: For the core-network SL-MO-LR and SL-MT-LR sidelink positioning procedures specified in TS 23.273, which procedures put the LMF and the LCS client role in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.273 put the LMF and the LCS Client/AF role in the same step for sidelink positioning: clause 6.20.1 ('Procedures of SL-MO-LR involving LMF'), where the AMF forwards the Ranging/Sidelink Positioning location results received from the LMF onward to the GMLC and to an AF or LCS Client if requested; clause 6.20.3 ('Procedures of SL-MT-LR involving LMF'), where an LCS Client or AF initiates the MT-LR request for a group of UEs that the LMF then processes and returns results for; and clause 6.20.4 ('Procedures of SL-MT-LR for periodic, triggered Location Events'), the periodic/triggered variant of 6.20.3 where the LCS Client or AF requests recurring sidelink location results serviced by the LMF.

questions.question: In AM and UE Policy Association handling with the PCF, which procedures put the AMF together with the CHF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 4.16.1.2 (AM Policy Association Establishment with new selected PCF) has the AMF establish the AM Policy Association while the PCF, if it determines the decision depends on policy-counter status, initiates Spending Limit Report Retrieval from the CHF before responding to the AMF. Clause 4.16.3.2 (AMF-initiated AM Policy Association Termination) has the AMF send Npcf_AMPolicyControl_Delete, after which the PCF unsubscribes from the CHF's policy counter status reporting if it had subscribed. Clause 4.16.11.1 (UE Policy Association Establishment) has the AMF establish the UE Policy Association with the (V-)PCF, and in the non-roaming case the (H-)PCF may interact with the CHF to decide UE policy based on spending limits, again via Spending Limit Report Retrieval.

questions.question: For EAS discovery via the EASDF in edge computing (TS 23.548), which procedures put the SMF together with the EASDF in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.548 shows the SMF and EASDF acting together in one step in four EAS-discovery procedures: clause 6.2.3.2.2 (EAS Discovery Procedure with EASDF), where the SMF selects the EASDF, invokes Neasdf_DNSContext_Create/Update towards it and receives DNS message reports back from it; clause 6.2.3.2.3 (EAS Discovery Procedure with Local DNS Server/Resolver), where the SMF may still invoke Neasdf_DNSContext_Delete on the EASDF when switching the UE to a Local DNS Server; clause 6.7.2.3 (EAS Discovery Procedure with V-EASDF for HR-SBO), where the V-SMF instructs the V-EASDF (the roaming counterpart of the SMF/EASDF pair) to construct and forward DNS queries/responses; and clause 6.7.2.5 (EAS discovery with V-EASDF/Local DNS Server using IP replacement for HR-SBO), where the V-SMF configures the V-EASDF and the VPLMN UPF with the IP-replacement DNS handling rules.

questions.question: Which procedures put the DAA function and the UAV in the same step, for detect-and-avoid support?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.255 clause 7.7.2.1.1 (DAA support management procedure) shows the UAS application specific server sending a DAA support management request identifying the UAV to the UAE server, which stores the DAA application policy and executes DAA configuration for that UAV. Clause 7.7.2.2.1 (DAA support involving UAVs with U2X support) shows the UAE client detecting nearby UAVs via U2X and sending DAA client event information about them to the UAE server. Clause 7.7.2.2.2 (DAA support involving UAVs without U2X support) shows the UAS application specific server determining nearby UAVs and sending DAA server event information, including their location, to the UAE server and client.

questions.question: In the charging flows for ProSe Direct Discovery, which procedures put the HPLMN and the VPLMN roles in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: Three message flows in TS 32.277 put the HPLMN and VPLMN ProSe Function roles in the same step: clause 5.2.2.1.2 (roaming/inter-PLMN Announce Request, where the VPLMN authorizes the UE to announce and the HPLMN charges the event), clause 5.2.2.1.4 (roaming Match Report, where the ProSe Function in HPLMN forwards the Match Report to the assigning PLMN and both HPLMN and VPLMN/other-PLMN generate charging records), and clause 5.3.2.2.2 (IEC/ECUR-mode roaming Announce Request, where the HPLMN requests authorization from the VPLMN's ProSe Function before responding to the UE, with OCS charging interactions on both sides).

questions.question: For registering an IP-SM-GW with the UDM, which procedures put the UDM and the IP-SM-GW in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TS 29.503 clause 5.3.2.2.7 (IP-SM-GW registration) shows the HSS sending a PUT request to the UDM to create or update the UE's IP-SM-GW registration, with the UDM responding '201 Created' or '200 OK' accordingly. Clause 5.3.2.5.11 (IP-SM-GW Registration Information Retrieval) shows an NF service consumer sending a GET request to the UDM to retrieve the UE's IP-SM-GW registration information, with the UDM responding '200 OK' including the registration data.

questions.question: In the study on multicast-broadcast services enhancement phase 3, which procedures put MBS, MBSF and AF in the same step for MBS session creation?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-47 clauses 6.27.3 ("Procedures", MBS session creation and multicast join enhancements) and 6.29.3 ("Procedures", MBS session creation for MOCN network sharing) both put MBS, MBSF and AF in the same step: the AF sends the MBS session-creation request (with TMGI allocation indication, service area, MOCN network-sharing indicator, etc.) to the NEF/MBSF, and the NEF/MBSF forwards it to the MB-SMF to reserve MBS session resources.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the SCG and the HO in the same step for an inter-MeNB handover that keeps the SeNB unchanged?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.300 10.1.2.8.8 (Inter-MeNB handover without SeNB change): the source MeNB includes the SCG configuration in the HandoverPreparationInformation sent to the target MeNB as part of the X2 Handover Preparation procedure, and the target MeNB forwards the SCG configuration to the UE in the handover command while the SeNB keeps the existing UE context.

questions.question: In the study on Ad hoc group communication for MCX services, which solutions put MC (mission critical service) and SDP together in the same step for group call setup?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-76: clause 7.1.3.1.1 ("Ad hoc group communication setup") has an authorized MC service user invite other MC service users into an ad hoc group communication with SDP negotiation for the session; clause 7.1.3.1.3 has the MC service server determine the participants list itself, based on criteria from the initiating MC service client, again negotiating SDP for the ad hoc session.

questions.question: In WIC registration to IMS based on web authentication, what does the eP-CSCF do with the security token received from the WIC before forwarding the REGISTER request, and which node ultimately responds with the 200 OK?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 23.228 clause U.2.1.3, when the eP-CSCF receives the REGISTER request from the WIC over the WSS connection, it validates the contents of the security token (issued earlier by the WAF/WWSF) and obtains the IMS identities being registered, then forwards the authorized REGISTER request into IMS to initiate authentication-less IMS registration using TNA procedures, indicating authentication has already been carried out. The S-CSCF responds with a 200 OK message, which the eP-CSCF then relays back to the WIC.

questions.question: Which procedures put the MN, the SN and the TEID in the same step for splitting a session across two tunnels in dual connectivity?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.340 10.14.1 (PDU Session Split at UPF during PDU session resource setup): the 5GC provides two UL TEID addresses on the NG-U interface, and the MN decides to split the PDU session using the SN Addition or MN-initiated SN Modification procedure, providing two DL TEID addresses and their associated QoS flows. TS 37.340 10.14.2 (during PDU session resource modify, 5GC initiated): the 5GC provides one additional UL TEID address, and the MN again uses SN Addition/Modification to set up the additional tunnel at the SN and provides the corresponding additional DL TEID address and QoS flows.

questions.question: Which procedures put the SRNC, the DRNC and the DCH in the same step for an unsynchronised transport channel bandwidth reconfiguration?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.931 7.14.2.2 (Bandwidth Increase): the SRNC decides no synchronised reconfiguration is needed and requests the DRNC to reconfigure the DCH via Radio Link Reconfiguration Request; both the DRNC's and the SRNC's own Node Bs allocate resources and confirm, then the SRNC sends RRC Transport Channel Reconfiguration to the UE. TS 25.931 7.14.2.3 (Bandwidth Decrease): the same SRNC-to-DRNC DCH reconfiguration request/response flow occurs, and the SRNC additionally initiates transport bearer modification of the Iub/Iur Data Transport Bearers using the ALCAP protocol.

questions.question: When an EES wants other EESes to know about a selected common EAS, how does it find out which other EES(s) serve the same EASID via the ECS, and what does a receiving EES do once it gets that declaration?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 23.700-98 clause 7.31.2.4 (and equivalently, steps 7-9 of clause 7.31.2.2), the EES contacts the ECS along with the EASID information of the selected common EAS to determine which other EES(s) serve the same EASID (per clause 8.8.3.3 of TS 23.558); the ECS provides endpoint information of the other EES(s) corresponding to the requested EASID. The EES then declares the selected common EAS to all determined EES(s) along with the Grouping required information and Group ID. A receiving EES stores the received selected common EAS information (with the Grouping required information/Group ID) and sends back an acknowledgement to the sending EES; the EAS(s) at a receiving EES are then notified about other common EASs via EDGE-3 notifications.

questions.question: Which procedure puts the PUR and the EPS in the same step for requesting and configuring a Pre-configured Uplink Resource?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.300 7.3d.2 (PUR Configuration Request and PUR configuration): the UE requests PUR configuration or release from the (ng-)eNB via PURConfigurationRequest, and when moving the UE to RRC_IDLE the (ng-)eNB includes the PUR configuration or release indication in the RRCConnectionRelease message, providing a PUR configuration ID for UEs using Control Plane CIoT EPS/5GS optimisations.

questions.question: In the study on 5G Timing Resiliency and TSC/URLLC enhancements, which solutions put the SMF and the Burst Arrival Time (BAT) together in the same step?
questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-25: clause 6.10.3 (QoS Flow establishment overview) has the SMF provide the TSCAI containing the Burst Arrival Time to NG-RAN and adjust it for 5GS time; clause 6.12.3 (cross layer scheduling optimization) has the TSCTSF provide a BAT window to the SMF, which determines the TSCAI for the QoS Flow based on it; clause 6.21.3 has the SMF receive the updated BAT offset via TSCAC from the TSNCF/CUC chain and update the QoS Flow's TSCAI.

questions.question: In the study on further enhancements to the 5G Multicast/Broadcast architecture, which solutions put the MBS session, NG and CM (connection management) together in the same step?
