questions.reference_answer: TR 23.700-47: clause 6.22.3.1 modifies the MBS session de-activation procedure so UEs stay in CM-CONNECTED/RRC_INACTIVE rather than the AMF deactivating over NG; clause 6.23.3 ("Multicast Session Activation Procedure") has the AMF page UEs across their registration areas, keeping CM-Connected UEs on NG-RAN; clause 6.4.3 ("Multicast Session Activation/Release Procedure") lets NG-RAN move group member UEs to RRC-INACTIVE (CM-CONNECTED) while the multicast MBS session stays active over NG.

questions.question: For self-healing IRP requirements, what must the IRPAgent support so the IRPManager can find out whether a self-healing operation succeeded or failed?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.541 clause 5.1 (REQ-SH-CON-003) states the IRPAgent shall support a capability allowing the IRPManager to know the success or failure result of self-healing.

questions.question: If MTC Provider information and/or AF ID are received in a request to create a 5G VN Group, what must the UDM check before allowing the operation?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.503 clause 5.6.2.3.2, if MTC Provider information and/or AF ID are received in the request to create a 5G VN Group, the UDM shall check whether the MTC Provider and/or the AF is allowed to perform this operation for the UE; otherwise, the UDM shall skip the MTC provider and/or AF authorization check.

questions.question: During which routing area updating procedures must an MS not request the use of power saving mode?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.008 clause 4.7.2.9, the MS shall not request the use of PSM during: an attach for emergency bearer services procedure; a routing area updating procedure for initiating a PDN connection for emergency bearer services; or a routing area updating procedure when the MS has a PDN connection established for emergency bearer services.

questions.question: When an SGSN fails and later receives an RA update request from an MS for which it has no MM context, how must it respond, and what must the MS then do to remain GPRS-attached?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.007 clause 11.0.1: if an RA update request is received from an MS for which no MM context exists, the SGSN shall reject the RA update with an appropriate cause; to remain GPRS-attached, the MS shall then perform a new GPRS attach and should (re-)activate PDP contexts.

questions.question: To enable IPv4 connectivity over Trusted WLAN Access, what server functionality must the TWAN support, and when does it deliver the IPv4 address to the UE if the UE requests it via DHCPv4?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.402 clause 16.1.5.2: the TWAN shall support DHCPv4 server functionality for IPv4 parameter configuration and address allocation; when the UE requests the IPv4 address via DHCPv4, the TWAN delivers the received IPv4 address to the UE within DHCPv4 signalling after the PMIPv6 or GTP tunnel is established between the TWAN and the PDN GW.

questions.question: When a subscriber's spending limit has reached a pre-set threshold, what must the system be able to trigger regarding QoS and access to IP services, and must the home network be able to enforce this for a roaming subscriber even without visited-network support?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.115 clause 4.5: the system shall be able to trigger a QoS downgrade and/or restrict access to one, several, or all IP services based on operator pre-defined thresholds; the home network shall be able to enforce spending limits for a roaming subscriber without dedicated support in the visited network.

questions.question: What must all NFs and the NRF support for authorization of NF service access using OAuth 2.0, and what role does the NRF play?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.500 clause 6.7.3, all NFs and the NRF shall support the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework with the 'Client Credentials' grant type as specified in clause 4.4 of IETF RFC 6749, except that there is no 'Authorization' HTTP request header in the access token request. The NRF shall act as the Authorization Server, providing 'Bearer' access tokens to NF service consumers to access services provided by NF service producers.

questions.question: When a 3GPP network needs to control traffic to a third-party server application because of congestion, what obligation does the network have towards traffic destined for other applications on that same server?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.101 clause 31.2.1: the 3GPP network shall be able to control (block/prioritize) traffic to a specific application on a third-party server or the server itself without affecting traffic to other applications on that server or to other third-party servers.

questions.question: For MDA-based handover optimization, what must the analytics output include besides the current statistics of gNB resource consumption?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.104 clause 7.2.5.2.3 (REQ-MOB_MDA-01/02) states that the MDA capability for handover optimization shall include providing the analytics output related to current statistics AND future predictions of both virtual resource consumption and radio resource consumption of the gNB.

questions.question: For End Marker packets constructed in the CP function, what must the CP function establish before it can forward those packets, and how must it set their source and destination IP addresses?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.244 clause 5.3.2, the CP function shall first establish (once) one standalone PFCP session not tied to any PDN connection, per UP function, for forwarding End Marker packets. It shall then construct the GTP-U End Marker packets with the destination IP address and TEID set according to the old F-TEID value, and a source IP address set according to the UP function's F-TEID value.

questions.question: What must the MCVideo service provide to an MCVideo User with respect to rejecting or ending a Private Communication?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.281 clause 5.3.1.4: the MCVideo service shall provide a mechanism for an MCVideo User to reject an MCVideo Private Communication, and a means by which an MCVideo User ends a Private Communication in which they are a Participant.

questions.question: When the HSS sends a P-CSCF-RestorationTrigger request to the UDM, what identity must the request contain, and how does the UDM confirm success?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.503 clause 5.3.2.8.2, the P-CSCF-RestorationTrigger request the HSS sends to the UDM shall contain the UE's identity, which shall be a SUPI. The UDM responds with '204 No Content' on success.

questions.question: For QoS flows requiring redundant transmission, what must the SMF instruct the PSA UPF to do about duplicated uplink packets, and how does the UPF identify duplicates?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.244 clause 5.24.2.4, for QoS flows requiring redundant transmission, the SMF shall instruct the PSA UPF to eliminate duplicated uplink packets based on their sequence numbers in the PDU Session Container extension header, by setting the EDRT flag and the FORW flag in the Apply Action IE of the FAR IE. The UPF then forwards only one copy and drops duplicates based on the sequence number.

questions.question: What must the N32-f interface be used for, and when is TLS-based forwarding used without any reformatting at the SEPPs?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.573 clause 4.2.3, the N32-f interface shall be used to forward the HTTP/2 messages of NF service producers and consumers in different PLMNs, through the SEPPs of the respective PLMNs. If TLS is the negotiated security policy between the SEPPs, the N32-f shall involve only forwarding of the HTTP/2 messages without any reformatting at the SEPPs and/or IPXs.

questions.question: Under Selected IP Traffic Offload (SIPTO), on what basis may a mobile operator enable or disable offload for a given UE, and can offload be applied selectively per defined IP network?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.101 clause 4.3.5.1: the mobile operator may enable/disable SIPTO on a per UE per defined IP network basis (e.g. based on tariff, subscription type); IP traffic to one defined IP network can be offloaded while traffic to others is not.

questions.question: At the IMS network-to-network interconnection point (IMS NNI), what must the IMS network and intermediate networks support regarding multiple peering points, and what may selection of a peering point be based on?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.228 clause 10.3: the IMS network and intermediate networks shall be able to support multiple peering points for interconnection to another IMS or intermediate network; NOTE 2 states selection of a peering point could be based on location, load balancing, or called party PUI.

questions.question: What must the receiving SEPP be able to reconstruct from the dataToIntegrityProtectAndCipher JSON array, and how does it know which original attribute each entry corresponds to?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 33.501 clause 13.2.4.3.2, dataToIntegrityProtectAndCipher is a JSON patch document (RFC 6902) containing all attribute values needing both encryption and integrity protection. The JSON array shall contain one entry per protected attribute value, and the index of each entry in the array is used to reference it within the dataToIntegrityProtect block, associating the encrypted value with its original attribute so the receiving SEPP can reassemble the original message.

questions.question: For a UE operating on a serving carrier under frame structure type 3, what RSSI measurement capability must the UE physical layer support, and how is the RSSI measurement period defined depending on whether DRX is used?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 36.133 clause 8.11.4.1, the UE physical layer shall be capable of performing RSSI measurements on one or more serving carriers operating under frame structure type 3 (if indicated by higher layers) and reporting them to higher layers, providing a single RSSI sample for each OFDM symbol within each configured RSSI measurement duration occurring at the configured periodicity. The RSSI measurement period corresponds to max(reportInterval, rmtc-Period) when no DRX is used, and max(reportInterval, rmtc-Period, DRX cycle length) when DRX is used.

questions.question: Under what conditions must the UE not use a locally stored P-CSCF address, and when must it clear all availability marks on its stored P-CSCF addresses?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.229 clause 5.1.9, the UE shall not use a locally stored P-CSCF address which is marked as unavailable when performing initial registration. The UE shall clear all availability marks on locally stored P-CSCF addresses if it performs a new P-CSCF discovery or is power-cycled.

questions.question: May a network operator define location-based service types beyond the standardized ones listed for privacy checking, and must those additional types be globally unique?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.071 clause 4.8.1.1: it shall be possible for the network operator/service provider to define additional, non-standardised service types, and these need not be globally unique.

questions.question: When the PartialPull feature is not supported by either side, what must the PCEF do to retrieve PFDs from the PFDF, and what must the PFDF include in a successful response?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.251 clause 4.4.1.1, the PCEF shall send an HTTP GET message to the PFDF to retrieve the PFDs for one or more application identifier(s) when the PartialPull feature is not supported in the PFDF and PCEF. On a successful pull, the PFDF shall provide all the PFDs of the specified application identifier(s) in the body of the HTTP response, and if caching time value(s) are configured for those application identifier(s), it shall also set the caching-time to those values in the response body. The PCEF must then install, update, or remove the received PFD(s) accordingly.

questions.question: Over the Iq interface used for e2ae RTP protection, what must happen to the keys' confidentiality, and what protection is mandatory if cryptographic protection is applied at all?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.328 clause 6.2.1.3.1 states that confidentiality of the keys sent over the Iq interface is required: the Iq interface shall be protected by NDS/IP, and if cryptographic protection is applied to the Iq interface then encryption shall be used.

questions.question: What must an MPS-subscribed IoT device be able to do when normal data service is degraded, with respect to invoking priority for data transmission service (MPS for DTS)?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.153 clause 9.3.2.1: the system shall support means for an IoT device with an MPS subscription to initiate an MPS for DTS session to an enterprise network supporting MPS, when normal data service is degraded.

questions.question: What must the MCPTT Service require of the called MCPTT User before an Automatic Commencement Private Call (with Floor control) audio transmission can proceed?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.179 clause 5.6.3 [R-5.6.3-013]: the MCPTT Service shall require that the called MCPTT UE acknowledge receipt of an Automatic Commencement Private Call (with Floor control) setup request before the audio transmission proceeds.

questions.question: Under MIMO dual-stream static orthogonal test conditions, what must the generated channel coefficients of the propagation channel satisfy?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.101 Annex B.2.6.3 states that the channel coefficients of the resulting propagation channel under MIMO dual-stream conditions shall be given by the specified generation method and associated with the transmitter and receiver ports as depicted, with the test setup not restricting implementation.

questions.question: If Barring of outgoing international calls except those directed to the home PLMN country is active, what happens when a subscriber tries to register an international forwarded-to number outside the HPLMN country as a call-forwarding-on-busy destination?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.082 clause 2.6.88.4: the registration of such an international forwarded-to number, as well as activation of call forwarding on mobile subscriber busy to it, is denied, and the mobile subscriber shall be informed of this supplementary service incompatibility.

questions.question: For an IMS multimedia emergency session enabled by the originating network, must the network deliver all media to a single IP PSAP, and what should it do if none of the requested media is successfully established?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.101 clause 10.4.2.3: the originating network shall deliver all media to the same IP PSAP throughout the duration of the IMS MES; if none of the requested media is successfully established, the IMS MES will fail and an IMS MES failure indication will be provided to the UE.

questions.question: What must the MCVideo service provide to allow an authorized MCVideo User such as a dispatcher to request an MCVideo UE to start transmitting video ('uplink pull')?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.281 clause 5.1.9.1.2 [R-5.1.9.1.2-001]: the MCVideo service shall provide a mechanism for an authorized MCVideo User (e.g. dispatcher) to request an MCVideo UE to transmit a video to the requester, another authorized party, or both.

questions.question: If a 5G-RG receives a REGISTRATION REJECT with 5GMM cause #77 over a wireline access network, what is it prevented from doing, and until when does that restriction last?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.501 clause 5.3.23, if a REGISTRATION REJECT, SERVICE REJECT, or DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message is received over a wireline access network with 5GMM cause #77 'wireline access area not allowed', the 5G-RG shall not access the 5GCN over that wireline access network until the 5G-RG is switched off, the UICC containing the USIM is removed, or the 5G-RG starts using another wireline access network.

questions.question: Must the system provide MPS treatment to a participant who joins an MMTEL video conference late, after MPS has already been activated for all other participants?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.153 clause 9.2.2.1: the system shall provide MPS for a late participant joining an MPS for MMTEL video conference after MPS was activated for all participants.

questions.question: During which mobility management procedures must a UE not request the use of power saving mode in EPS?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.301 clause 5.3.11, the UE shall not request the use of PSM during: an attach for emergency bearer services procedure; an attach procedure for initiating a PDN connection for emergency bearer services with attach type not set to 'EPS emergency attach'; a tracking area updating procedure for initiating a PDN connection for emergency bearer services; a tracking area updating procedure when the UE has a PDN connection established for emergency bearer services; or an attach for access to RLOS.

questions.question: For an IMS emergency session where the SUPI is unavailable or unauthenticated, what must the SMF include in the request it sends to the PCF?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.512 clause 4.2.2.9, if the SUPI is not available or unauthenticated, the SMF shall include the PEI within the 'pei' attribute and set the 'invalidSupi' attribute to 'true' in the HTTP POST message it sends to the PCF for the IMS emergency session PDU Session Establishment request.

questions.question: When the AMF determines that delivery of an N1 message has failed via NG-RAN paging, what must it include in the POST request body of the N1N2Transfer Failure Notification?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.518 clause 5.2.2.3.2, the AMF shall include the N1N2MessageTransfer request resource URI returned earlier in the N1N2MessageTransfer response, if any, otherwise a dummy URI, in the POST request body, along with N1/N2 message transfer cause information set as specified in clause 6.1.5.6.3.1.

questions.question: When an LMF invokes the NonUeN2MessageTransfer service operation, what must the POST request body contain besides the NRPPa-PDU IE?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.518 clause 5.2.2.4.1.6, the POST request body of NonUeN2MessageTransfer shall contain the NRPPa-PDU IE carrying Network Assistance Data generated by the LMF, together with the target NG-RAN node identifier(s), and shall also include the NF Instance Identifier of the NF Service Consumer (e.g. LMF) in the 'nfId' attribute.

questions.question: When a UE moves from RRC_INACTIVE to RRC_CONNECTED and the target gNB does not support the ciphering/integrity algorithms the UE was using, what must the target gNB do instead of resuming with those algorithms?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.501 clause 6.7.3.4 states that if the target gNB/ng-eNB does not support the received algorithms, or prefers different ones, it shall send an RRCSetup message on SRB0 to proceed as if the UE were in RRC_IDLE (a fallback procedure), after which the UE performs NAS-based RRC recovery and negotiates a suitable algorithm with the target gNB/ng-eNB via the AS SMC procedure.

questions.question: What mechanism must the MCPTT Service provide to an MCPTT Administrator regarding the number of simultaneous Group transmissions an MCPTT UE can receive in one group call in case of override?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.179 clause 5.5.2 [R-5.5.2-006]: the MCPTT Service shall provide a mechanism for an MCPTT Administrator to limit the total number (N5) of MCPTT Group transmissions that an MCPTT UE simultaneously receives in one MCPTT Group call in case of override.

questions.question: When Service Gap Control is active in the network, which NAS signalling connection releases does the network exclude from starting the SGC timer T3447?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.301 clause 5.3.17, after the UE transitions from EMM-CONNECTED to EMM-IDLE mode, the network starts SGC timer T3447 except when the UE was in EMM-CONNECTED mode due to: paging; attach requests without PDN connection request; or tracking area update requests without 'active' or 'signalling active' flag set.

questions.question: In the asynchronous balanced mode link procedures, why must the response time-out function duration differ between the two stations rather than be equal?
questions.reference_answer: TS 27.010 clause 5.4.5 states the duration of the time-out function (T1) in the two stations shall be unequal, in order to resolve contention situations.

questions.question: What TLS-related authentication mechanisms must the NAF Key Centre support, and under what condition must it additionally support USS?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 33.259 clause 4.4.5, the NAF Key Centre shall support TLS with certificate-based mutual authentication, TLS Extensions, and shared-key based mutual authentication using PSK-TLS as defined in TS 33.310 Annex E. If the NAF Key Centre is also offering its services to subscribers not subscribed to the operator hosting it, it shall support USS.

questions.question: For a shared RAN, what must the MOP's 3GPP management system allow an authorized consumer to determine about points of presence and shared cells?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.130 clause 5.1.1 (REQ-NS_GEN-CON-3/4) requires the 3GPP management system of the MOP to support a capability allowing its authorized consumer to know which POPs the shared resources belong to, and to configure which POPs share each cell.

questions.question: For the AAS BS equipment environmental requirements, from where must the applicable environmental conditions and classes be drawn?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.105 Annex A states the AAS BS equipment shall fulfil all requirements in the full range of environmental conditions for the relevant environmental class, and the environmental conditions and class shall come from the relevant IEC specifications (IEC 60721-3-3/60721-3-4) or the corresponding ETSI specifications (ETSI EN 300 019-1-3/1-4).

questions.question: How does the SGSN set the UE-AMBR when values are received from the HSS, versus when no values are received?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.060 clause 15.2.2: the SGSN shall set the UE-AMBR to the sum of the APN-AMBR of all active APNs, up to the subscribed UE-AMBR value; if no UE-AMBR values are received from the HSS, the SGSN shall set the UE-AMBR according to implementation-specific policies (e.g. a preconfigured maximum UE-AMBR).

questions.question: When a UE in 5GMM-IDLE mode receives an access attempt request from upper layers, what must the NAS layer do with the access identities and category before requesting access?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.501 clause 4.5.4.1, the NAS shall categorize the access attempt into access identities and an access category following subclause 4.5.2/4.5.2A and tables, and provide the applicable access identities and access category to the lower layers for the purpose of access control checking, before initiating the procedure to send the initial NAS message once the lower layers indicate the access attempt is allowed.

questions.question: If the EFOPLMNWLAN file on the USIM is present, how many operator-preferred PLMNs must it be possible to store at minimum, and how is priority order encoded among the entries?
questions.reference_answer: TS 31.102 clause 4.4.5.3 states that EFOPLMNWLAN shall be able to store at least the number of PLMNs specified in TS 24.234; the first PLMN entry in the file indicates the highest priority and the nth entry indicates the lowest, so priority is encoded purely by entry position.

questions.question: For handset UE positioning during audio testing, if the manufacturer-defined position (MECRP) is not provided and the handset lacks a traditional earpiece, what determination sequence must be followed to establish the ECRP?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.132 clause 5.1.1 states the ECRP determination order is: manufacturer-defined position (MECRP) if provided; else centre of the earpiece per ITU-T P.64 Annex E if a traditional earpiece exists; else, for non-traditional earpieces, a GUI showing optimal sound radiation location if provided, else an objective determination procedure per Annex H if possible, else a subjective determination by the test operator of the optimal holding position.

questions.question: In which cases does the UE use the default value of timer T3402 rather than a network-provided value?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.301 clause 5.3.6, the UE uses the default value of T3402 when: an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT is received without a specified value and the EPS update type is not 'periodic updating'; the network indicates the timer is 'deactivated'; the UE has no stored value; a new non-equivalent PLMN is entered and the tracking area updating fails with the attempt counter at 5; or a new non-equivalent PLMN is entered, attach fails, the attach attempt counter is 5, and no ATTACH REJECT was received from the new PLMN.

questions.question: During which attach or tracking area updating procedures must a UE supporting WUS assistance not include its UE paging probability information in EPS?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.301 clause 5.3.21, the UE shall not include its UE paging probability information during: an attach for emergency bearer services procedure; an attach procedure for initiating a PDN connection for emergency bearer services with attach type not 'EPS emergency attach'; a tracking area updating procedure for initiating a PDN connection for emergency bearer services; or a tracking area updating procedure when the UE has a PDN connection established for emergency bearer services.

questions.question: In BEST session initiation, if the BEST service is being used for key agreement only, what must the HSE additionally require from the UE beyond the normal implied confirmation?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.163 clause 4.3.2 states that normally a UE sending a UP message to the HSE or EAS is itself an implied confirmation of the BEST session start; however, if the BEST service is used for key agreement only, the HSE shall require the UE to send an EMSDP Session Start Confirmation, by setting the corresponding indicator in the EMSDP Session Start message.

questions.question: If the UE terminates the EAP-5G session by sending EAP-Response/5G-Stop to the N3IWF, what must the N3IWF do next, and what does the UE do once it receives the N3IWF's reply?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.502 clause 7.3.3.3, upon receiving an EAP-Response/5G-Stop message, the N3IWF shall complete the EAP-5G session by sending an EAP-Failure message to the UE. On reception of that EAP-Failure message, the UE shall delete any context related to the IKE SA without requiring an explicit INFORMATIONAL exchange carrying a Delete payload, as specified in IETF RFC 7296.

questions.question: What two information storage formats must a UE support for 'In Case of Emergency' (ICE) information on the UICC, and how many instances of a given format may the operator provision?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.101 Annex A.28: two formats shall be defined - phone number format (name and phone number) and free format; the mobile operator may provision zero, one or several instances of a given format on the UICC.

questions.question: In the attribute constraints for a RAN NRM fragment, under what condition does the nPNIdentityList support qualifier attribute become mandatory to be present?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.622 clause 4.3.60.3 states nPNIdentityList (support qualifier) shall be present only when both of these conditions are met: NR is supported, and several NPNs are supported in the RAN (per TS 38.331).

questions.question: Under NS_04N network signalling requirements, what is the spectrum emission limit for a UE, in the 0-160 kHz frequency offset range, and what measurement bandwidth applies?
questions.reference_answer: TS 36.102 clause 6.5A.3.3.2, Table 6.5A.3.3.2-1, states that when 'NS_04N' is indicated, for the +/-0-160 kHz frequency offset range the spectrum emission limit shall not exceed -2 dBm, measured with a 30 kHz measurement bandwidth.

questions.question: In the CCBS supplementary service, once the destination B idle guard timer (T8) expires and destination B is still idle, how must the network process a non-suspended CCBS request, and can requests be processed in parallel?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.093 clause 5.7: when T8 expires and destination B is still idle, the first non-suspended CCBS request shall be processed provided no entry is currently being processed; entries shall not be processed in parallel.

questions.question: While timer T3447 is running and the UE is in EMM-CONNECTED mode, under what conditions is the UE still allowed to send an UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.301 clause 5.6.4.4, while timer T3447 is running the UE shall not send an UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message while in EMM-CONNECTED mode unless one of these holds: the UE is configured to use access class 11-15 in the selected PLMN; the UE has a PDN connection for emergency bearer services established; or a network-initiated signalling message has been received.

questions.question: For TLS 1.2 profiling between network elements, what is the minimum Diffie-Hellman group size that must never be supported, and what elliptic curve size floor applies for ECDHE?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.210 clause 6.2.3 states that for DHE, Diffie-Hellman groups smaller than 2048 bits shall not be supported (groups of at least 4096 bits should be supported), and for ECDHE, elliptic curve groups of less than 256 bits shall not be supported, except curve25519, ed25519, and W-25519; secp256r1 (P-256) shall be supported.

questions.question: For single-RAT E-UTRA BS operation, in the 1 GHz to 12.75 GHz spurious emission frequency range, what is the maximum TRP level and what measurement bandwidth applies?
questions.reference_answer: TS 37.105 clause 10.7.4, Table 10.7.4-1, states that for the 1 GHz - 12.75 GHz frequency range, the TRP of any spurious emission shall not exceed -30 + X dBm (X = 9 dB unless regional regulation states otherwise), measured with a 1 MHz measurement bandwidth.

questions.question: Once NAS integrity protection has been activated between the UE and the AMF, under what condition, if any, is it allowed to switch to the NULL integrity algorithm?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.501 clause 6.4.3.2 states that once NAS integrity has been activated, it shall stay activated until the 5G security context is deleted in either the UE or the AMF, and it shall not be possible to change from a non-NULL integrity protection algorithm to the NULL integrity protection algorithm.

questions.question: For a mobile IAB-MT, which mandatory features must it support in addition to applying the same capabilities as a regular IAB-MT?
questions.reference_answer: TS 38.306 clause 4.2.15.1a states a mobile IAB-MT shall apply the same capabilities as IAB-MT unless indicated otherwise, and it is mandatory for the mobile IAB-MT to additionally support: acquisition of gNB-ID-Length from SIB1, cell barring based on mobileIAB-Support, and inclusion of mobileIAB-NodeIndication (all per TS 38.331).

questions.question: When a wild card APN is present in a UE's subscription context, what does this authorize the UE to do, and what must HSS/MME/S4 SGSN/AAA Server/Non-3GPP access nodes do when a PDN GW ID registration request arrives for an active APN not present in the subscription context?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.402 clause 13.4: the wild card APN authorizes the UE to connect to APNs not present in the subscription context; upon a PDN GW ID registration request for such an active APN, the nodes (HSS/MME/S4 SGSN/AAA Server/Non-3GPP access) shall store the PDN GW ID and the APN for the UE.

questions.question: When must a UE disable its E-UTRA capability, and what happens to its ability to access the 5GCN via E-UTRA if it supports both N1 mode and S1 mode?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.301 clause 4.5, the UE shall only disable the E-UTRA capability when in EMM-IDLE mode. When the UE supports both N1 mode and S1 mode, its capability to access the 5GCN via E-UTRA shall not be affected, regardless of whether the UE's E-UTRA capability is disabled or enabled.

questions.question: For 5G ProSe Direct Discovery charging, which three identifier substitutions must the 5G DDNMF make compared to the legacy ProSe Function's collected charging information?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.277 clause 5.1.2.1 states the 5G DDNMF shall collect the same charging information as the ProSe Function but with modifications: E-UTRAN is replaced by NG-RAN and E-UTRA is replaced with NR; the ECGI is replaced by NCGI; and corresponding 5GS identifiers replace EPS identifiers, e.g. SUPI instead of IMSI and GPSI instead of MSISDN.

questions.question: For cell selection criterion S detection in CELL_FACH, over how many measurement periods must the UE filter its P-CCPCH RSCP measurements, and what must the UE do once it decides it is out of service area?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.123 clause 5.4.3.4 states the UE shall filter P-CCPCH RSCP measurements used for cell selection criterion S evaluation over at least 3 measurement periods (TMeasurement_Period Intra); once the UE determines it is 'out of service area' (4 s of failing criterion S with no suitable new cell found), it shall initiate cell selection procedures for the selected PLMN.

questions.question: When an MCE fails, what must it do with the MBMS services affected by the failure, and within what timeframe?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.007 clause 15A.3: when an MCE fails, the MCE shall release all the MBMS services affected by the failure locally and towards E-UTRAN, either immediately or after a pre-configured time period if the corresponding MBMS bearer contexts are not re-established via any MME.

questions.question: A management service producer offers NF performance data file reporting. What two capabilities must it support for its authorized consumer, according to the requirements clause?
questions.reference_answer: TS 28.550 clause 5.2.2 (REQ-PDFR_NF-FUN-1/2) requires the management service producer for NF performance data file reporting to have the capability to send a notification about the NF performance data file being ready to its authorized consumer, and to have the capability to allow that authorized consumer to fetch the performance data file of the NF(s).

questions.question: In the Operator-Determined-Barring AVP, what data type is used and what does bit 8 represent?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.272 clause 7.3.30, the Operator-Determined-Barring AVP is of type Unsigned32, containing a bit mask indicating the services of a subscriber barred by the operator. Bit 8 means 'Barring of all outgoing international calls except those directed to the home PLMN country and Barring of all outgoing inter-zonal calls'.

questions.question: In the L-GW security requirements, why must the L-GW share the same secure backhaul link that the H(e)NB already established, rather than opening its own?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.320 clause 4.4.7 states the L-GW shall be tightly integrated with the H(e)NB and share the same security requirements: it shall use the same secure backhaul link established by the H(e)NB (clause 4.4.5) and the same secure H(e)MS link (clause 4.4.6); if the network allocates different IP addresses to the L-GW and H(e)NB, the backhaul link shall carry traffic to and from both addresses, and the L-GW shall be included in the H(e)NB's device integrity check and device validation.

questions.question: Before a serving PLMN or SNPN performs network slice-specific authentication and authorization, what must have already completed successfully, and how does the UE indicate its support for the feature?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.501 clause 4.6.2.4, the network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure shall not be performed unless the primary authentication and key agreement procedure (clause 5.4.1) has already successfully completed. The UE indicates its support for network slice-specific authentication and authorization via the 5GMM Capability IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.

questions.question: What must an SMF include when the 3GPP PS Data Off status of the UE is active during PDU session establishment, and what does the PCF then do to downlink IP flows?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.512 clause 4.2.2.8, if the SMF is informed that the 3GPP PS Data Off status of the UE is active, it shall include the '3gppPsDataOffStatus' attribute set to true within the SmPolicyContextData structure sent to the PCF. If the PCF receives this with accessType '3GPP_ACCESS', it shall configure the SMF to block downlink (and optionally uplink) IP flows not related to a service in the list of 3GPP PS Data Off Exempt Services.

questions.question: During a PFCP Association Setup procedure, how must a UPF that is configured for Inter-PLMN User Plane Security (IPUPS) indicate that support, and is IPUPS support restricted to specific UPFs?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.244 clause 5.27, during a PFCP Association Setup procedure, a UPF configured to be used for IPUPS shall indicate this with the UPF configured for IPUPS (UUPSI) flag. Any UPF can support the IPUPS functionality; it is not restricted, though in deployments where specific UPFs are designated, those reporting the UUPSI flag are selected to provide the IPUPS function.

questions.question: Through which signalling is the Access Point Name conveyed when a UE accesses EPC via S2b, versus via S2a with trusted WLAN in single-connection mode?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.302 clause 4.4.2, for access to EPC the APN is conveyed in the IKEv2 signalling during tunnel establishment when the S2b interface is used. When the UE accesses EPC via S2a using trusted WLAN access, the APN is conveyed in EAP-AKA' signalling for single-connection mode (SCM), or in WLAN Control Protocol (WLCP) signalling for multi-connection mode (MCM).

questions.question: In LCS privacy control, what is the minimum number of LCS clients and services per client that the privacy exception list of an LCS Server must be able to support?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.071 clause 6.4.3: the privacy exception list shall support a minimum of 20 LCS clients, and for each client it shall support a minimum of 10 services (max numbers determined by implementation constraints).

questions.question: What must an MCData user be able to choose to do with data from recently invited group communications?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.282 clause 6.2.2.2 [R-6.2.2.2-001]: an MCData user shall be able to choose to download data for any recently invited group communications.

questions.question: For the +CSIM generic SIM access command, what must the TE do with SIM information it receives, and is +CSIM support mandatory for the MT to implement?
questions.reference_answer: TS 27.007 clause 8.17 states the command <command> shall be sent to the SIM as-is by the MT, and the SIM <response> shall be sent back by the MT to the TA as-is; the TE shall take care of processing SIM information within the frame specified by GSM/UMTS. Implementation of +CSIM is Optional.

questions.question: What must a P-TMSI signature only be used for, and when must a used P-TMSI signature be deleted?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.008 clause 4.7.1.3, the P-TMSI signature is only used, in combination with a valid P-TMSI, by the MS for authentication and identification purposes in a subsequent attach, routing area update, or detach procedure; if the MS has no valid P-TMSI it shall not use it. Upon successful completion of the subsequent attach or routing area update procedure, or upon completion of an MS-initiated detach, the used P-TMSI signature shall be deleted.

questions.question: What must a NAF be able to do regarding acquisition and selection of shared key material from the BSF, including in the GBA_U case?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 33.220 clause 4.2.2, the NAF shall be able to locate and communicate securely with the subscriber's BSF, acquire shared key material established between the UE and BSF, acquire zero or more application-specific USSs from the HSS via the BSF, set the local validity condition of the shared key material per local policy, and check the lifetime and local validity condition of the key material. In the GBA_U case, the NAF shall be able to determine which key (Ks_ext_NAF, Ks_int_NAF, or both) to use via local policy or a key selection indication in the application-specific USS, with the USS indication overriding local policy when present.

questions.question: When a Service User hosts an MMTEL voice conference and invokes MPS to upgrade it, whose priority level determines the priority applied to all participants, and are there exceptions?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.153 clause 9.1.2.1 (NOTE 4): when MPS is invoked for all participants, the user priority level is based on the host MPS Service User, except where an individual participant used MPS to join with a higher user priority level, which is kept.

questions.question: When an SCP forwards a request carrying the 3gpp-Sbi-Max-Forward-Hops header with node type 'scp' and the value is zero, what must the SCP do?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.500 clause 6.10.10.2, if the value of the 3gpp-Sbi-Max-Forward-Hops header with node type 'scp' is zero, the SCP shall reject the request with the HTTP status code '502 Bad Gateway' and the protocol error 'MAX_SCP_HOPS_REACHED'; otherwise it shall decrement the value by 1 before forwarding the request.

questions.question: When the UP function needs to delete a PFCP session during Enhanced PFCP Association Release or after detecting a partial failure, what must it set the Report Type and the PSDBU flag to?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.244 clause 5.18.2, the UP function shall set the Report Type to 'USAR' if there is a non-zero usage report for the PFCP session, or to 'UISR' if there is none, and shall set the PSDBU flag to '1' in the last PFCP Session Report Request message sent for that session, to indicate to the CP function that the PFCP session is being deleted.

questions.question: When a ProSe-enabled UE uses ProSe Communication or an EPC Path established following ProSe Discovery, what categories of charging data must the 3GPP system be able to collect for that communication?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.115 clause 4.6: the system shall be able to collect charging data including activation/deactivation, initiation/termination, duration and amount of data transmitted/received, QoS (if via E-UTRAN), inter-operator communication, inter-operator signalling, and identification of UEs or groups involved.

questions.question: When two or more measurement granularity periods end at the exact same time, what must the network element do about generating measurement reports, rather than merging them into one?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.432 clause 5.1.1.1 states that in the event of two or more granularity periods ending at the same time, the NE shall generate one measurement report per granularity period (not one combined report) -- e.g. a NodeB with a 15-minute and a 5-minute granularity period generates two separate reports when their end times coincide.

questions.question: What must the MCData Service provide to an MCData User regarding the list of available recently invited data group communications they are affiliated to?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.282 clause 6.2.2.3 [R-6.2.2.3-001]: the MCData Service shall provide, periodically and on demand, to the MCData User the list of available recently invited data group communications for which they are affiliated.

questions.question: For TSCTSF charging triggers, when an AF request/subscribe is received, what category of reporting applies by default, and is the CHF allowed to change that category?
questions.reference_answer: TS 32.282 clause 5.2.1.2, Table 5.2.1.2.1 states that for the 'AF request/subscribe received' trigger condition, the default category is Immediate, and the CHF is Not Applicable for being allowed to change the category (i.e. it cannot be changed).

questions.question: What must the Evolved Packet System (EPS) ensure regarding confidentiality and integrity of ProSe communications compared to the existing 3GPP system?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.278 clause 9.4: the EPS shall ensure that the confidentiality and integrity of user data and network signalling over the ProSe Communication path is at a level comparable with that provided by the existing 3GPP system.

questions.question: What guidelines govern HTTP/2 connection and stream errors between NF services, and where are API-specific error responses defined?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.500 clause 5.2.4, HTTP/2 connection error and stream error shall be supported as specified in clause 5.4 of IETF RFC 9113. Guidelines for error responses to the invocation of APIs of NF services are specified in clause 4.8 of TS 29.501, while API-specific error responses are specified in the respective technical specifications.

questions.question: When an NF service consumer requests removal of the Authentication Result at the UDM, what must the UDM do on success?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.503 clause 5.4.2.3.3, on success the UDM shall return '204 No Content' and shall remove the Authentication result of the UE by completely replacing the individual AuthEvent resource.

questions.question: A UE supports multiple global GNSS constellations such as Galileo and GLONASS. What minimum performance requirement must it meet, according to the multi-constellation clause?
questions.reference_answer: TS 25.172 clause 4.7 states that UEs supporting multiple global constellations shall meet the minimum performance requirements for a combined scenario where each UE-supported constellation is simulated simultaneously.

questions.question: What must the network support regarding a user's ability to reject an incoming IMS session as 'user busy', and under what conditions can this indication apply when a session is offered to multiple contacts?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.228 clause 7.13: the network shall support a user's capability to reject an incoming IMS session with a 'user busy' indication; when offered to multiple contacts, the condition applies if none progress the session and one or more reject with 'user busy'.

questions.question: A UE supporting WUS assistance information must not include its UE paging probability information during which registration procedures?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.501 clause 5.3.24, the UE shall not include its UE paging probability information during: a registration procedure for initial registration for emergency services; initial registration for initiating an emergency PDU session; mobility and periodic registration update while the UE is in state 5GMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION-UPDATE for an emergency PDU session; or mobility and periodic registration update when the UE has an emergency PDU session established.

questions.question: What network layer addresses must a packet-domain subscriber identified by an IMSI be associated with as PDP addresses?
questions.reference_answer: TS 23.060 clause 14.5: a packet-domain subscriber identified by an IMSI shall have one or more network layer addresses (PDP addresses) conforming to the standard addressing scheme used, e.g. an IPv4 address, an IPv6 prefix, or both.

questions.question: What must a UE that supports IMS Multimedia Emergency Session (MES) also support, and how should it behave with respect to drawing attention to the user once an MES is initiated?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.101 clause 10.4.2.2: a UE supporting IMS MES shall also support IMS emergency voice calls, and once aware an IMS MES has been initiated the UE shall be able to (subject to user configuration) avoid drawing unnecessary attention to the user, confirming this to the user in as private a manner as reasonable.

questions.question: At most how many S-NSSAIs may each configured NSSAI set store in the UE, and what is the cap for the allowed NSSAI?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 24.501 clause 4.6.2.2, each configured NSSAI stored in the UE (including the default configured NSSAI) is a set composed of at most 16 S-NSSAIs, while each allowed NSSAI stored in the UE is a set composed of at most 8 S-NSSAIs.

questions.question: In CCBS handling, what must the network do if destination B rejects the CCBS call with UDUB (User Determined User Busy)?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.093 clause 6.5.1(d): if destination B rejects the CCBS call using UDUB, the CCBS request shall be automatically deactivated, and the network shall not offer subscriber A the opportunity to activate a CCBS request for this call again.

questions.question: When PMIP-based S5/S8 is used and the Serving GW receives a DHCPv6 Solicit message with an IA_PD option from the UE, what must the Serving GW do, and what must the PDN GW do once it gets the Proxy Binding Update?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 23.402 clause 4.7.6, the Serving GW shall support DHCPv6 relay agent functionality to intercept the related DHCPv6 message, and the DHCPv6 relay agent in the Serving GW shall relay the DHCPv6 Solicit message within the PMIPv6 tunnel to the PDN GW acting as a DHCPv6 server. Once the PDN GW receives the Proxy Binding Update carrying the delegated prefixes, it shall add the assigned prefix to the binding cache extended as specified in RFC 7148, then return the assigned prefix in the DMNP option carried by a PBA to the Serving GW.

questions.question: For the Media Session Handler's RAN-based metrics reporting, once a metrics configuration is received from the OAM, what must the Media Session Handler do with it, and what must it check before starting to report metrics for a media delivery session?
questions.reference_answer: TS 26.510 clause 5.6.3 states that when a metrics configuration is received, the Media Session Handler shall store this configuration and use it for all subsequent media delivery sessions; when a session starts, it shall determine whether metrics from this session shall be reported, based on the sample percentage, slice scope and streaming source filter specified in the stored configuration.

questions.question: What must the secure environment inside the eNB be able to do with sensitive data like long-term cryptographic secrets, and what access restriction applies to that data?
questions.reference_answer: TS 33.401 clause 5.3.5 requires the eNB's secure environment to support secure storage of sensitive data (e.g. long-term cryptographic secrets and vital configuration data) and the execution of sensitive functions such as en-/decryption of user data. Sensitive data used within the secure environment shall not be exposed to external entities, and only authorised access shall be granted to the data and functions within it.

questions.question: What criteria must a 3GPP system be able to base relay UE selection and reselection on?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.261 clause 6.9.2.4: selection/reselection may be based on traffic characteristics, subscriptions of relay and remote UE, capabilities/capacity/coverage, achievable QoS, power consumption, pre-pairing, the access type used, the 3GPP network connected to, overall power/performance optimization, and battery capabilities/lifetime.

questions.question: What must a 5G system be able to do for the HPLMN regarding a UE's temporary identifier and its subscriber identity?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.261 clause 8.5: the HPLMN shall be able to associate a temporary identifier to a UE's subscriber identity.

questions.question: When a SEPP receives an HTTP/2 message with a '3gpp-Sbi-Callback' header, how must it select the applicable data encryption and modification policy?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.573 clause 5.3.2.2, when the incoming HTTP/2 message has the '3gpp-Sbi-Callback' header, the SEPP shall select the data encryption and modification policy applicable for the specific notification type, identified by the header's value and the target PLMN, using the notification type list stored per clause 5.2.3.3.

questions.question: When the PCF provides a redirect instruction for a dynamic PCC rule and the 'redirectEnabled' attribute is initially provisioned, what value must it be set to, and what must the SMF instruct the UPF to do?
questions.reference_answer: Per TS 29.512 clause 4.2.6.2.4, the 'redirectEnabled' attribute shall be included and set to true when the redirect instruction is initially provisioned. If the 'redirectInfo' attribute is provided for a dynamic PCC rule, the SMF shall instruct the UPF to perform the requested redirection as defined in TS 29.244.

questions.question: If a transmitting MCData Group Member is notified that no other group members are affiliated, and does not terminate the request to transmit, what two options does the MCData Service have?
questions.reference_answer: TS 22.282 clause 6.2.2.4 [R-6.2.2.4-003]: the MCData Service may either terminate the permission to transmit, or allow the transmission to continue and store the transmitted data for a time-to-live and deliver invitations to receive to subsequent affiliating members.
